title: Construction Specifier Study Guide question bank

questions.question: In Division 00, the procurement requirements open with a heading numbered 00 10 00, which comes ahead of Instructions for Procurement. What is the MasterFormat title of that heading?

options.A: Advertisement for Bids
options.B: Bid Solicitation
options.C: Solicitation
options.D: Notice of Award
options.E: Invitation to Bid
options.F: Advertisements and Invitations

questions.explanation: The procurement requirements run 00 10 00 Solicitation, 00 20 00 Instructions for Procurement, 00 30 00 Available Information and 00 40 00 Procurement Forms and Supplements. Advertisements and Invitations (00 11 00), with the advertisement for bids and invitation to bid under it, is filed beneath Solicitation, so it is not the heading. Bid Solicitation is too narrow, because procurement also covers negotiated proposals and purchases.

questions.question: Which procurement-requirements heading, numbered 00 20 00, sits between Solicitation and Available Information and tells bidders or proposers the procedures they must follow?

options.A: Instructions for Procurement
options.B: Instructions to Bidders
options.C: Bidding Procedures
options.D: Supplementary Instructions
options.E: Procurement Definitions
options.F: Procurement Scopes

questions.explanation: Instructions for Procurement is the 00 20 00 heading that collects the procedures bidders or proposers must follow. Instructions to Bidders (00 21 13) is one document filed under it, and Supplementary Instructions, Procurement Definitions and Procurement Scopes are other titles beneath it (00 22 00, 00 23 00, 00 24 00), not the heading. The heading says procurement rather than bidding because it serves proposals as well as bids.

questions.question: The third procurement-requirements heading in Division 00 (00 30 00), after Instructions for Procurement, holds owner-furnished data such as subsurface investigations, surveys, and records of the existing site. What is its MasterFormat title?

options.A: Existing Conditions
options.B: Geotechnical Data
options.C: Available Information
options.D: Information Available to Bidders
options.E: Available Project Information
options.F: Preliminary Schedules

questions.explanation: Available Information (00 30 00) is the heading for data the owner makes available to bidders and proposers, such as geotechnical reports and existing-condition surveys. Available Project Information (00 31 00) and Preliminary Schedules are titles filed beneath it, and Existing Conditions is the title of Division 02. Information Available to Bidders describes the same content in bid-only wording but is not the MasterFormat title.

questions.question: The last procurement-requirements heading in Division 00, numbered 00 40 00, holds the forms that bidders or proposers fill in and submit, such as the bid form and the bid security form. What is its MasterFormat title?

options.A: Bid Forms & Supplements
options.B: Procurement Forms & Supplements
options.C: Procurement Substitution Procedures
options.D: Bid Security Forms
options.E: Proposal Forms
options.F: Representations and Certifications

questions.explanation: Procurement Forms and Supplements (00 40 00) is the heading for everything a bidder or proposer fills in and returns: bid forms, proposal forms, bid security and other supplements. Proposal Forms and Representations and Certifications are titles filed beneath it, and Procurement Substitution Procedures belongs under Instructions for Procurement. Bid Forms and Supplements is bid-only wording; the title says procurement because it covers proposals too.

questions.question: The contracting requirements in Division 00 open with heading 00 50 00, under which the owner-contractor agreement is filed. What is that heading's MasterFormat title?

options.A: Contracting Forms and Supplements
options.B: Agreement Forms
options.C: Project Forms
options.D: Contracting Definitions
options.E: Agreement Form Supplements
options.F: Notice of Award

questions.explanation: Contracting Forms and Supplements (00 50 00), often shortened to Contracting Forms, is the first contracting-requirements heading: under it sit the notice of award, the agreement forms, agreement form supplements such as allowance and unit price schedules, and the notice to proceed. Agreement Forms, Agreement Form Supplements and Notice of Award are titles filed beneath it. Project Forms (00 60 00) is the next heading, for bonds and certificates.

questions.question: Which contracting document is signed by both the owner and the contractor, binds them to its terms, and incorporates all the other contract documents by reference?

options.A: Owner-Contractor Contract
options.B: Notice of Award
options.C: Agreement
options.D: Letter of Intent
options.E: Notice to Proceed
options.F: Agreement Form Supplements

questions.explanation: The Agreement is the one instrument the owner and contractor both execute; it sets out their obligations and pulls the other contract documents in by reference. The contract itself is formed by all the contract documents together, so the signed agreement is only one part of it. A letter of intent or notice of award tells the selected bidder of the owner's decision, and a notice to proceed fixes the date work starts.

questions.question: Which contracting-requirements heading, numbered 00 60 00, holds the performance bond, the payment bond, certificates of insurance, and the forms used to administer the contract?

options.A: Contracting Forms and Supplements
options.B: Project Forms
options.C: Project Management Forms
options.D: Bond Forms
options.E: Certificates and Other Forms
options.F: Closeout Forms

questions.explanation: Project Forms (00 60 00) is the heading for forms that secure the contractor's performance, prove compliance, and support contract administration. Bond Forms, Certificates and Other Forms, and Closeout Forms are titles filed beneath it, not the heading. Contracting Forms and Supplements (00 50 00) is the separate heading for the agreement and the award and proceed notices.

questions.question: Among the project forms in the contracting requirements, which bond protects the owner when the contractor defaults, by having the surety finish the work or pay, up to the bond amount, for finishing it?

options.A: Warranty Bond
options.B: Maintenance Bond
options.C: Bid Bond
options.D: Performance Bond
options.E: Lien Bond
options.F: Retainage Bond

questions.explanation: A performance bond protects the owner against contractor default: the surety finishes the contract or funds its completion up to the penal sum. A bid bond protects the owner against withdrawal of a bid, so it is a procurement requirement filed with the procurement forms. Warranty and maintenance bonds cover defects after completion and are usually called for by individual specification sections.

questions.question: Which bond, normally furnished with the performance bond as a project form, guarantees that subcontractors, material suppliers, and others who furnish labor and materials to the project will be paid?

options.A: Maintenance Bond
options.B: Payment Bond
options.C: Bid Bond
options.D: Retainage Bond
options.E: Lien Bond
options.F: Special Bond

questions.explanation: The payment bond protects those who furnish labor, materials and services to the project: if the contractor does not pay them, the surety does. It usually accompanies the performance bond, which instead protects the owner if the contractor defaults. A bid bond secures a bid during procurement, and lien, retainage, maintenance and special bonds are other bond forms for narrower purposes.

questions.question: Among the project forms, after the performance and payment bonds, which item gives proof of the contractor's insurance coverage and of compliance with applicable laws and regulations?

options.A: Certificates
options.B: Insurance Requirements
options.C: Certificates of Occupancy
options.D: Affidavits
options.E: Schedule of Values
options.F: Representations and Certifications

questions.explanation: Certificates, such as certificates of insurance and of compliance with laws and regulations, are the project forms that prove the contractor has met those obligations. Insurance Requirements is an article of the supplementary conditions that states the coverage required, not the proof of it. Representations and Certifications are procurement forms submitted with a bid, and a certificate of occupancy is issued by the authority having jurisdiction near closeout.

questions.question: Which contracting-requirements heading, numbered 00 70 00, holds the general conditions and the supplementary conditions, the provisions that set the parties' basic rights, responsibilities, and relationships?

options.A: Terms and Conditions
options.B: Contracting Definitions
options.C: Conditions of the Contract
options.D: General Requirements
options.E: Contract Forms
options.F: Special Conditions

questions.explanation: Conditions of the Contract (00 70 00) is the heading for the written provisions that set the rights, responsibilities and relationships of the parties: the general conditions, adapted to the project by the supplementary conditions. Contracting Definitions is a title filed beneath it, and contract forms such as the agreement and bonds sit under other headings. General Requirements is Division 01, the administrative and procedural part of the specifications.

questions.question: Under Conditions of the Contract, which document holds the standard provisions that apply to almost every project and is usually a published form, such as AIA A201 or EJCDC C-700?

options.A: Contracting Definitions
options.B: Supplementary Conditions
options.C: Special Conditions
options.D: General Conditions
options.E: Terms and Conditions
options.F: General Requirements

questions.explanation: The general conditions (00 72 00) are the broadly applicable provisions of the contract, normally a standard form published by a professional association, such as AIA A201 or EJCDC C-700. The supplementary conditions modify them to fit one project. General Requirements is Division 01 of the specifications, which covers administrative and procedural requirements, not the conditions of the contract.

questions.question: What is the standard name of the document, filed under Conditions of the Contract right after the general conditions, that adapts the general conditions to one particular project by adding to, deleting from, or changing them?

options.A: Additional Conditions
options.B: Supplementary Conditions
options.C: Special Conditions
options.D: Modified Conditions
options.E: Supplementary Instructions
options.F: Agreement Form Supplements

questions.explanation: The supplementary conditions (00 73 00) amend the standard general conditions for one project, for example by setting its insurance requirements or wage rate requirements. Supplementary Instructions (00 22 00) amend the instructions to bidders during procurement, and agreement form supplements are schedules attached to the agreement. Names such as additional, modified or special conditions describe the idea but are not the standard term.

questions.question: The last heading of the contracting requirements, 00 90 00, gathers the documents that change the procurement and contract documents: addenda issued before the agreement is signed, requests and proposals pending during construction, and change orders issued afterward. What is its MasterFormat title?

options.A: Changes in the Work
options.B: Revisions, Clarifications & Modifications
options.C: Revisions and Amendments
options.D: Addenda and Change Orders
options.E: Record Clarifications and Proposals
options.F: Clarification and Modification Forms

questions.explanation: Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications (00 90 00) holds the actual changes in three groups: precontract revisions such as addenda, record clarifications and proposals, and record modifications such as change orders. Record Clarifications and Proposals is only the middle group, and Clarification and Modification Forms (00 63 00) are blank forms filed with the project forms. Addenda and Change Orders names just two of the documents.

questions.question: The specifications begin with a division that forms a subgroup of its own and states the administrative and procedural requirements that apply to all of the work. What are its number and title?

options.A: Div. 01 Special Requirements
options.B: Div. 01 General Requirements
options.C: Div. 01 Procurement Requirements
options.D: Div. 01 General Conditions
options.E: Div. 01 Administrative Requirements
options.F: Div. 01 Performance Requirements

questions.explanation: Division 01 General Requirements is the first subgroup of the specifications, and its requirements apply to every section in Divisions 02 through 49. Administrative Requirements (01 30 00) and Performance Requirements (01 80 00) are titles inside Division 01, not its name. General conditions, though similar in name, are part of the conditions of the contract in Division 00, as are the procurement requirements.

questions.question: Division 00 holds two groups of documents. What is the first group called, the one numbered 00 10 00 through 00 40 00 that sets out how prices will be solicited, whether the work is bid or negotiated?

options.A: Solicitation Requirements
options.B: Procurement Requirements
options.C: Pre-Bid Requirements
options.D: Bidding Requirements
options.E: Introductory Information
options.F: Procurement and Contracting Requirements

questions.explanation: Procurement requirements (00 10 00 to 00 40 00) are the documents that set out how pricing will be solicited: solicitation, instructions, available information, and forms. Procurement and Contracting Requirements is the title of all of Division 00, contracting requirements included. Bidding requirements is the narrower term for competitive bids only, and Introductory Information (00 01 00) is front matter such as the title page and table of contents.

questions.question: In MasterFormat, which division holds the procurement requirements, that is, the solicitation, the instructions for procurement, the available information, and the bid or proposal forms?

options.A: Division 00
options.B: Division 02
options.C: Division 01
options.D: Division 10
options.E: No division; MasterFormat numbers only the specifications
options.F: Division 00 or 01, at the specifier's choice

questions.explanation: Procurement requirements are placed in Division 00, Procurement and Contracting Requirements, at 00 10 00 to 00 40 00, and the contracting requirements follow in the same division. They are not specifications, but MasterFormat still gives them fixed numbers so that every project manual is arranged the same way. Division 01 General Requirements is the first division of the specifications.

questions.question: Which group in Division 00, numbered 00 50 00 through 00 90 00, holds the legal documents that set out the parties' rights and duties under the agreement and, unlike the procurement requirements, becomes part of the contract documents?

options.A: Agreement Requirements
options.B: General Requirements
options.C: Contracting Requirements
options.D: Contract Forms
options.E: Procurement and Contracting Requirements
options.F: Contracting Forms and Supplements

questions.explanation: Contracting requirements (00 50 00 to 00 90 00) are the legal documents of the contract: the agreement and its notices, the bonds and certificates, the general and supplementary conditions, and later revisions and modifications. Procurement and Contracting Requirements is the title of the whole of Division 00, and Contracting Forms and Supplements is only the first heading within the group. General Requirements is Division 01, which belongs to the specifications.

questions.question: The contracting requirements (the agreement, the bonds and certificates, the general and supplementary conditions, and addenda and modifications) are placed in which MasterFormat division?

options.A: Division 01
options.B: Division 10
options.C: Division 02
options.D: Division 00
options.E: Division 00 for the agreement and bonds, Division 01 for the conditions
options.F: No division; MasterFormat numbers only the specifications

questions.explanation: Contracting requirements share Division 00, Procurement and Contracting Requirements, with the procurement requirements, at 00 50 00 to 00 90 00; that includes the general and supplementary conditions at 00 72 00 and 00 73 00. Division 01 General Requirements is the first division of the specifications, not part of the contracting requirements. MasterFormat numbers these legal documents even though they are not specifications.

questions.question: What is the MasterFormat group called that runs from Division 01 through Division 49 and is divided into five subgroups?

options.A: Technical Specifications
options.B: Work Results
options.C: Procurement and Contracting Requirements
options.D: Specifications
options.E: General Requirements
options.F: Facility Construction

questions.explanation: MasterFormat has two groups: Procurement and Contracting Requirements (Division 00) and Specifications (Divisions 01 through 49). The Specifications Group is split into the General Requirements, Facility Construction, Facility Services, Site and Infrastructure, and Process Equipment subgroups, so those are parts of it, not its name. Technical specifications is a looser term for the work-result sections and leaves out Division 01.

questions.question: Which drawings are issued with the procurement documents and become contract documents when the agreement is signed, as the graphic counterpart of the specifications?

options.A: Coordination Drawings
options.B: Shop Drawings
options.C: Resource Drawings
options.D: Contract Drawings
options.E: Record Drawings
options.F: Measured Drawings

questions.explanation: Contract drawings are the graphic part of the contract documents, showing the extent, size and relationships of the work; they go out with the procurement documents and become binding when the agreement is executed. Resource drawings go out in the same set but are for information only and never become contract documents. Shop and coordination drawings are prepared by the contractor during construction, and record drawings document what was built.

questions.question: What is the standard name for the drawings that may be included with the procurement documents to show existing conditions or related construction for information only, and that do not become contract documents when the agreement is signed?

options.A: Resource Drawings
options.B: As-Built Drawings
options.C: Coordination Drawings
options.D: Schematic Drawings
options.E: Shop Drawings
options.F: Contract Drawings

questions.explanation: Resource drawings, such as drawings of an existing structure, inform bidders about existing conditions or related construction; they are the one part of the procurement documents that never becomes a contract document. Contract drawings go out in the same set but become binding at signing. As-built drawings document construction as completed, though an old set may be furnished as a resource drawing, and shop and coordination drawings are contractor submittals.

questions.question: What are the written or graphic documents called that clarify, revise, add to, or delete from the procurement documents before bids or proposals are received, and that become contract documents when the agreement is signed?

options.A: Addenda
options.B: Bulletins
options.C: Change Orders
options.D: Amendments
options.E: Clarification Notices
options.F: Supplemental Instructions

questions.explanation: Addenda are issued during procurement, typically before bids or proposals are received, to clarify or change the procurement documents; they are the main pre-contract revisions and become contract documents at signing. Change orders, written amendments and supplemental instructions are issued after the agreement is executed, and clarification notices are records of clarifications made during construction.

questions.question: Under Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications (00 90 00), which category covers changes made before the agreement is signed, namely addenda and, when they are permitted, bid or proposal revisions?

options.A: Pre-Award Changes
options.B: Pre-Bid Revisions
options.C: Pre-Contract Revisions
options.D: Bid Revisions
options.E: Changes to Bidding Requirements
options.F: Record Modifications

questions.explanation: Pre-contract revisions (MasterFormat 00 91 00, spelled Precontract Revisions) are everything revised before the agreement is executed: addenda, plus bid or proposal revisions where allowed. Bid Revisions is only one member of that category. Pre-Bid Revisions is too narrow, since the category is bounded by the signing of the agreement, not the bid date, and Record Modifications covers changes made after signing.

questions.question: Under Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications (00 90 00), which category covers documents that start a change or clarification but have not yet been made part of the contract by a formal modification?

options.A: Clarifications & Proposals
options.B: Bulletins & Proposals
options.C: Requests & Interpretations
options.D: RFIs & Submittals
options.E: Proposal Requests
options.F: Change Order Requests

questions.explanation: Clarifications and proposals are the requests and proposals that may lead to a change, such as requests for information, clarification notices, proposal requests and change order requests, until a formal modification incorporates them. Proposal requests and change order requests are individual documents within the category, not its name. Submittals are handled under Division 01 procedures and are not filed here.

questions.question: Under Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications (00 90 00), which category covers the changes to the work made after the agreement is signed, by change order, change directive, or minor change?

options.A: Contract Amendments
options.B: Post-Contract Revisions
options.C: Change Orders
options.D: Contract Modifications
options.E: Minor Changes in the Work
options.F: Construction Change Directives

questions.explanation: Contract modifications are the formal changes issued after the agreement is executed, at any time during the contract period: change orders, construction change directives and minor changes in the work. Each of those, like a written amendment, is one kind of modification, not the name of the category. Post-contract revisions mirrors the pre-contract category's name, but the standard term is contract modifications.

questions.question: What is the bound volume called that contains the procurement requirements, the contracting requirements, and the specifications, but not the drawings?

options.A: Project Manual
options.B: Contract Manual
options.C: Bidding Package
options.D: Specifications Book
options.E: Bidding Documents
options.F: Construction Documents

questions.explanation: The project manual is the written volume issued with the drawings; it holds the procurement requirements, contracting requirements and specifications. Calling it the specifications or spec book understates it, because the procurement and contracting documents in it are not specifications. Bidding documents and construction documents are wider sets that include the drawings as well.

questions.question: What is the general term for the full set issued to prospective contractors, whether the work will be bid, negotiated, or purchased: the procurement and contracting requirements, specifications, contract drawings, any resource drawings, and addenda?

options.A: Construction Documents
options.B: Solicitation Documents
options.C: Bidding Documents
options.D: Procurement Documents
options.E: Bidding Requirements
options.F: Request for Proposal

questions.explanation: Procurement documents are everything issued to obtain prices, and all of them except any resource drawings become contract documents once the agreement is signed. Bidding documents is the narrower term for competitive bidding, and bidding requirements are only the instructions and forms within the set. Construction documents is the umbrella for both the procurement documents and the contract documents.

questions.question: Once the owner and contractor sign the agreement, which set of documents binds them: the contracting requirements, specifications, contract drawings, addenda issued before signing, and modifications issued afterward?

options.A: Award Documents
options.B: Executed Documents
options.C: Contract Documents
options.D: Construction Documents
options.E: Record Documents
options.F: Contract Forms

questions.explanation: Contract documents are the subset of the procurement documents that becomes binding at signing, plus the modifications issued later; resource drawings are left out. Construction documents is the wider umbrella covering both procurement and contract documents, and contract forms such as the agreement and bonds are only part of the set. Record documents show the work as actually built.

questions.question: Which MasterFormat subgroup, with its full division range, follows Division 01 and holds divisions such as Existing Conditions, Concrete, Masonry, Openings, Finishes, and Conveying Equipment?

options.A: Div. 02-19 Building Construction
options.B: Div. 02-19 Shell and Interiors
options.C: Div. 02-19 Facility Construction
options.D: Div. 02-14 Facility Construction
options.E: Div. 02-19 Construction Materials
options.F: Div. 02-19 Special Construction

questions.explanation: The Facility Construction Subgroup runs from Division 02 Existing Conditions through Division 19; Division 14 Conveying Equipment is its last titled division and 15 through 19 are reserved for future expansion, so 02-14 is short. Shell and Interiors are UniFormat categories, and Special Construction is the title of Division 13, inside this subgroup.

questions.question: Which MasterFormat subgroup, with its full division range, holds Fire Suppression, Plumbing, HVAC, Electrical, Communications, and the other systems that serve a facility?

options.A: Div. 20-29 Building Services
options.B: Div. 21-28 Facility Services
options.C: Div. 20-29 Integrated Automation
options.D: Div. 20-29 Utilities
options.E: Div. 20-29 Facility Services
options.F: Div. 20-29 Equipment and Furnishings

questions.explanation: The Facility Services Subgroup covers Divisions 20 through 29: fire suppression, plumbing, HVAC, integrated automation, electrical, communications, and electronic safety and security, with Divisions 20, 24 and 29 reserved. Its range includes those reserved numbers, so 21-28 is wrong. Integrated Automation is Division 25 alone, and Utilities is Division 33 in the site and infrastructure subgroup.

questions.question: Which MasterFormat subgroup, with its full division range, holds earthwork, paving and site improvements, site utilities, transportation, and marine work, and is drawn on by every type of project for its civil work?

options.A: Div. 30-39 Building Sitework
options.B: Div. 30-39 Site & Infrastructure
options.C: Div. 31-35 Site & Infrastructure
options.D: Div. 30-39 Civil Work
options.E: Div. 30-39 Exterior Improvements
options.F: Div. 30-39 Earthwork & Utilities

questions.explanation: The Site and Infrastructure Subgroup is Divisions 30 through 39: Earthwork, Exterior Improvements, Utilities, Transportation, and Waterway and Marine Construction, with 30 and 36 through 39 reserved, so 31-35 is short. Civil work is what projects use it for, not its title; Exterior Improvements is Division 32 alone, and Building Sitework is a UniFormat category, not a MasterFormat subgroup.

questions.question: Which MasterFormat subgroup, with its full division range, holds the divisions for industrial process work, such as material processing and handling, process heating and cooling, pollution and waste control, and water and wastewater equipment?

options.A: Div. 40-49 Process Plant Construction
options.B: Div. 40-48 Process Equipment
options.C: Div. 40-49 Process Interconnections
options.D: Div. 40-49 Manufacturing Equipment
options.E: Div. 40-49 Electrical Power Generation
options.F: Div. 40-49 Process Equipment

questions.explanation: The Process Equipment Subgroup is Divisions 40 through 49, with 47 and 49 reserved; because 49 is part of the range, 40-48 is short. Process Interconnections is the title of Division 40 and Electrical Power Generation of Division 48, both inside the subgroup. Process plant construction describes the kind of project that uses these divisions, not the subgroup's title.

questions.question: Which two MasterFormat headings open the procurement requirements in Division 00, at 00 10 00 and 00 20 00, ahead of Available Information?

options.A: Solicitation
options.B: Advertisement for Bids
options.C: Invitation to Bid
options.D: Instructions for Procurement
options.E: Instructions to Bidders
options.F: Bidding Procedures

questions.explanation: The procurement requirements open with Solicitation (00 10 00) and Instructions for Procurement (00 20 00), followed by Available Information and Procurement Forms and Supplements. The advertisement for bids and invitation to bid are filed under Solicitation, and instructions to bidders is filed under Instructions for Procurement, so none of them is a heading. Bidding Procedures is not a MasterFormat title.

questions.question: After Solicitation and Instructions for Procurement, which two MasterFormat headings complete the procurement requirements, one for owner-furnished data such as geotechnical reports and one for the forms bidders or proposers submit?

options.A: Information Available to Bidders
options.B: Available Information
options.C: Existing Conditions
options.D: Bid Forms & Supplements
options.E: Procurement Forms & Supplements
options.F: Bid Security Forms

questions.explanation: Available Information (00 30 00) holds data the owner makes available, such as subsurface investigations and surveys, and Procurement Forms and Supplements (00 40 00) holds the bid or proposal forms, bid security and other submitted forms. Information Available to Bidders and Bid Forms and Supplements describe the same content in bid-only wording, but the titles say procurement because they also serve proposals. Existing Conditions is Division 02.

questions.question: Which two MasterFormat headings in the contracting requirements are 00 50 00, under which the owner-contractor agreement is filed, and 00 70 00, which holds the provisions setting out the parties' rights, responsibilities, and relationships?

options.A: Agreement Forms
options.B: Project Forms
options.C: Contracting Forms and Supplements
options.D: General Conditions
options.E: Terms and Conditions
options.F: Conditions of the Contract

questions.explanation: Contracting Forms and Supplements (00 50 00) holds the notice of award, the agreement forms and their supplements, and the notice to proceed; Conditions of the Contract (00 70 00) holds the general and supplementary conditions. Agreement Forms and General Conditions are titles filed beneath those headings, not the headings themselves. Project Forms (00 60 00) is the heading in between, for bonds and certificates.

questions.question: Which two contracting-requirements items are the document that the owner and contractor both sign, incorporating the other contract documents by reference, and the heading (00 60 00) that holds the performance bond, payment bond, and certificates?

options.A: Agreement
options.B: Owner-Contractor Contract
options.C: Notice of Award
options.D: Bond Forms
options.E: Project Forms
options.F: Project Management Forms

questions.explanation: The Agreement is the instrument executed by owner and contractor that binds them and brings in the other contract documents by reference; the contract itself is all of those documents together. Project Forms (00 60 00) is the heading for bonds, certificates and contract administration forms, with Bond Forms (00 61 00) filed beneath it. A notice of award tells a bidder the bid was accepted; it is not the signed agreement.

questions.question: Which two bonds are normally furnished as project forms in the contracting requirements and become contract documents, one protecting the owner if the contractor defaults and the other protecting those who furnish labor and materials?

options.A: Bid Bond
options.B: Performance Bond
options.C: Warranty Bond
options.D: Maintenance Bond
options.E: Lien Bond
options.F: Payment Bond

questions.explanation: The performance bond has the surety complete the work or fund its completion if the contractor defaults, and the payment bond assures that subcontractors and suppliers are paid; both become contract documents. A bid bond is a procurement requirement submitted with a bid. Warranty and maintenance bonds, when required, are usually called for in individual specification sections.

questions.question: Which two contracting-requirements items are the project form that proves insurance coverage and compliance with laws, and the last heading of the contracting requirements (00 90 00), which gathers addenda, pending clarifications, and contract modifications?

options.A: Insurance Requirements
options.B: Affidavits
options.C: Certificates
options.D: Revisions, Clarifications & Modifications
options.E: Changes in the Work
options.F: Addenda and Change Orders

questions.explanation: Certificates, such as certificates of insurance and of compliance with laws and regulations, are the last of the project forms after the bonds. Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications (00 90 00) closes the contracting requirements with precontract revisions, record clarifications and proposals, and record modifications. Insurance Requirements is a supplementary conditions article that states the coverage, not proof of it, and Addenda and Change Orders names only two of the documents.

questions.question: Which two documents are filed under Conditions of the Contract (00 70 00): one with broadly applicable provisions, usually a published form, and one that adapts those provisions to a particular project?

options.A: General Requirements
options.B: General Conditions
options.C: Special Conditions
options.D: Supplementary Conditions
options.E: Additional Conditions
options.F: Modified Conditions

questions.explanation: The general conditions (00 72 00) are the broadly applicable provisions, normally a standard form such as AIA A201 or EJCDC C-700, and the supplementary conditions (00 73 00) amend them for one project, for example with its insurance requirements. General Requirements is Division 01 of the specifications, not a condition of the contract. Additional, modified or special conditions describe the idea but are not the standard titles.

questions.question: Division 00 is divided into two groups of documents. Which two names identify them, the first covering 00 10 00 through 00 40 00 and the second 00 50 00 through 00 90 00?

options.A: Procurement Requirements
options.B: Bidding Requirements
options.C: Solicitation Requirements
options.D: General Requirements
options.E: Agreement Requirements
options.F: Contracting Requirements

questions.explanation: Procurement requirements (00 10 00 to 00 40 00) explain how prices will be solicited, and contracting requirements (00 50 00 to 00 90 00) are the legal documents of the contract, from the agreement to the modifications. Bidding requirements is the narrower term for competitive bidding only, since procurement also covers negotiation and purchasing. General Requirements is Division 01, the start of the specifications.

questions.question: Which two names belong to the written group of the project manual that follows the procurement and contracting requirements: the name of the group itself, and the title of Division 01, its first subgroup?

options.A: Div. 01 General Requirements
options.B: Div. 01 General Conditions
options.C: Div. 01 Administrative Requirements
options.D: Specifications
options.E: Technical Specifications
options.F: Work Results

questions.explanation: The written documents after Division 00 form the Specifications group, and its first subgroup is Division 01 General Requirements, followed by the four work-result subgroups in Divisions 02 through 49. General conditions belong to the conditions of the contract in Division 00, and Administrative Requirements is a title inside Division 01. Technical specifications usually means the work-result sections alone, without Division 01.

questions.question: Procurement documents can include two kinds of drawings: those that become contract documents when the agreement is signed, and those furnished only to show existing conditions, which never become contract documents. Which two standard category names identify them?

options.A: Coordination Drawings
options.B: Contract Drawings
options.C: Shop Drawings
options.D: Record Drawings
options.E: Resource Drawings
options.F: Schematic Drawings

questions.explanation: Contract drawings show the work to be built and become contract documents at signing; resource drawings, such as drawings of an existing building, inform bidders about existing conditions and stay outside the contract. Record drawings document construction as completed (an old record set may be furnished as resource drawings), and shop and coordination drawings are prepared by the contractor after award.

questions.question: Which two terms name the documents that revise the procurement documents before bids or proposals are received, and the category of requests and proposals that have not yet been incorporated into the contract by a formal modification?

options.A: Bulletins
options.B: Amendments
options.C: Addenda
options.D: Requests & Interpretations
options.E: RFIs & Submittals
options.F: Clarifications & Proposals

questions.explanation: Addenda revise the procurement documents during procurement and become contract documents at signing. Clarifications and proposals are requests for information, proposal requests and similar documents that may lead to a change but are not yet part of the contract. Amendments are written modifications made after the agreement is signed, and submittals are a Division 01 procedure, not a category of revisions, clarifications and modifications.

questions.question: Under Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications, which two categories sit on either side of the signing of the agreement: the one holding addenda issued before it, and the one holding change orders, change directives, and minor changes issued after it?

options.A: Pre-Contract Revisions
options.B: Pre-Award Changes
options.C: Pre-Bid Revisions
options.D: Post-Contract Revisions
options.E: Contract Modifications
options.F: Contract Amendments

questions.explanation: Pre-contract revisions cover everything revised before the agreement is executed, chiefly addenda and any permitted bid or proposal revisions, and contract modifications cover change orders, change directives and minor changes issued during the contract. Post-contract revisions and pre-award changes are not the standard category names, and a written amendment is one kind of modification, not the category.

questions.question: Which two terms name the bound written volume of procurement requirements, contracting requirements, and specifications, and the complete set issued to obtain prices, which adds the drawings and addenda and applies to bids, negotiated proposals, and purchases alike?

options.A: Bidding Package
options.B: Project Manual
options.C: Specifications Book
options.D: Bidding Documents
options.E: Solicitation Documents
options.F: Procurement Documents

questions.explanation: The project manual is the written volume: procurement requirements, contracting requirements and specifications, without the drawings. Procurement documents are the whole set used to obtain prices: the project manual plus contract drawings, any resource drawings and addenda. Specifications book understates the volume, because much of it is not specifications, and bidding documents is the narrower term for competitive bidding only.

questions.question: Which two terms name the set of documents that binds the owner and contractor once the agreement is signed, and the graphic part of that set?

options.A: Construction Documents
options.B: Award Documents
options.C: Contract Documents
options.D: Contract Drawings
options.E: Resource Drawings
options.F: Record Drawings

questions.explanation: Contract documents are the contracting requirements, specifications, contract drawings and addenda that become binding at signing, plus later modifications; contract drawings are their graphic part. Resource drawings are issued during procurement but never become contract documents, and record drawings document the finished work. Construction documents is the wider umbrella covering both procurement and contract documents.

questions.question: Which two MasterFormat subgroups, with their full division ranges, come between Division 01 General Requirements and the Site and Infrastructure Subgroup?

options.A: Div. 02-19 Building Construction
options.B: Div. 02-19 Facility Construction
options.C: Div. 02-14 Facility Construction
options.D: Div. 20-29 Facility Services
options.E: Div. 21-28 Facility Services
options.F: Div. 20-29 Building Services

questions.explanation: Facility Construction runs from Division 02 through 19 and Facility Services from Division 20 through 29. Each range includes its reserved divisions (15 through 19; 20, 24 and 29), so 02-14 and 21-28 cut them short. Building construction is a type of project, and building services sounds like a subgroup title but is not MasterFormat's.

questions.question: Which two MasterFormat subgroups, with their full division ranges, are the last two of the Specifications Group, after Facility Services?

options.A: Div. 30-39 Site & Infrastructure
options.B: Div. 30-39 Civil Work
options.C: Div. 31-35 Site & Infrastructure
options.D: Div. 40-49 Process Plant Construction
options.E: Div. 40-48 Process Equipment
options.F: Div. 40-49 Process Equipment

questions.explanation: Site and Infrastructure covers Divisions 30 through 39 and Process Equipment covers 40 through 49, each including its reserved divisions (30 and 36 through 39; 47 and 49), so 31-35 and 40-48 are short. Civil work and process plant construction describe the kinds of work these subgroups serve, not their titles.

questions.question: In the usual workflow for developing a project manual, the specifier starts by reviewing the owner-A/E agreement. What does the specifier prepare next, in step with schematic design?

options.A: Select master sections
options.B: Outline specifications
options.C: Prepare supplementary conditions
options.D: Preliminary project description
options.E: Draft new sections
options.F: Prepare bidding requirements

questions.explanation: A preliminary project description is the written partner of schematic design: it describes the project by systems and assemblies so it can be priced before products are chosen. Outline specifications follow in design development. Selecting master sections, drafting new sections, and preparing the supplementary conditions and bidding requirements come later, while the construction documents are produced.

questions.question: In the tripartite relationship of owner, A/E and contractor, the contractual relationship between the owner and the contractor is established by:

options.A: The executed owner-A/E professional agreement
options.B: An implied warranty of design from the A/E
options.C: The executed owner-contractor agreement
options.D: The general conditions of the contract alone
options.E: Third-party obligations through the A/E
options.F: A purchase order issued by the owner

questions.explanation: The tripartite relationship rests on two agreements: first the owner-A/E agreement, then the owner-contractor agreement, and it is the executed owner-contractor agreement that binds owner and contractor. The A/E and contractor have no contract with each other; the duties each owes the owner create only a third-party relationship between them. The general conditions form part of the construction contract but do not create it alone.

questions.question: In the facility life cycle, which stage comes immediately before construction?

options.A: Facility management
options.B: Construction documents
options.C: Procurement
options.D: Design
options.E: Project conception
options.F: Commissioning

questions.explanation: The facility life cycle runs from project conception through design, construction documents, procurement (bidding, negotiating or purchasing), construction, and facility management. Procurement is where the construction cost is set and the contract is awarded, so it sits between the construction documents and construction. Some delivery methods price the work earlier, but they follow the same general sequence of stages.

questions.question: Division 01 General Requirements is written broadly enough to apply to the specification sections in:

options.A: Divisions 02 through 19
options.B: Divisions 02 through 49
options.C: Divisions 00 through 49
options.D: The conditions of the contract
options.E: Divisions 01 through 49
options.F: The procurement requirements

questions.explanation: Division 01 expands on the administrative and procedural provisions of the conditions of the contract and is written to apply to every specification section in Divisions 02 through 49, so those requirements need not be repeated section by section. Divisions 02 through 19 is only the facility construction subgroup. Division 01 does not govern the conditions of the contract or the Division 00 procurement requirements.

questions.question: Administrative and procedural requirements form a three-tier hierarchy that gets more specific at each level. Which tier states its provisions in the BROADEST terms?

options.A: Division 01
options.B: General conditions
options.C: PART 1—GENERAL of each section
options.D: Section 01 10 00—Summary
options.E: PART 3—EXECUTION of each section
options.F: Section 01 30 00—Administrative Requirements

questions.explanation: The general conditions state provisions in broad terms and govern the other documents. Division 01 elaborates on them but is still written broadly enough to cover every specification section, and PART 1 of a section is the most specific, applying only to that section. Individual Division 01 sections such as Summary or Administrative Requirements belong to the middle tier, not the broadest.

questions.question: Which are characteristics of Division 01 General Requirements but NOT of the general conditions?

options.A: Definitions of the basic contract terms used throughout the documents
options.B: The legal relationships and obligations among the owner, A/E, and contractor
options.C: The rights and remedies of the parties in the event of default or dispute
options.D: Detailed, project-specific administrative and procedural requirements
options.E: Administrative governance of the other specification sections
options.F: Relatively static constants that allow published standard documents

questions.explanation: Division 01 is part of the specifications: it administratively governs the specification sections and holds the specific administrative and procedural requirements written for one particular project. The general conditions are broad contract provisions that define terms and set out the parties' relationships, rights and remedies; because their content is fairly constant from project to project, published standard forms can be used.

questions.question: A bid alternate that adds scope must be coordinated across the invitation to bid, the bid form and which Division 01 section?

options.A: 01 23 00 Alternates
options.B: 01 22 00 Unit Prices
options.C: 01 26 00 Contract Modification Procedures
options.D: 01 25 00 Substitution Procedures
options.E: 01 21 00 Allowances
options.F: 01 24 00 Value Analysis

questions.explanation: Section 01 23 00 Alternates identifies each alternate by number, describes the work it adds or changes and lists the sections affected, so it has to agree with the solicitation, the instructions and the bid form's price blank for each alternate. Unit prices, allowances, value analysis, substitutions and contract modifications each have their own Division 01 sections and do not define alternates.

questions.question: Which items are NOT among the standard components of an addendum?

options.A: Changes to prior addenda
options.B: The estimated cost effect of each change
options.C: Opening remarks and notice to bidders
options.D: To whom the addendum is issued
options.E: Name and address of the A/E
options.F: The owner's written approval of each change

questions.explanation: An addendum opens with its number and date, the project identification, the A/E's name and address, the recipients, and opening remarks with notice to bidders. Its changes follow in the same order as the project manual and drawings: prior addenda, procurement requirements, contracting requirements, specifications, then drawings. An estimated cost for each change and an owner approval block are not part of the standard format.

questions.question: In the three-party relationship of a construction surety bond, the principal is:

options.A: The owner
options.B: The surety
options.C: The contractor
options.D: The lender
options.E: The indemnitor
options.F: The architect

questions.explanation: A surety bond is a three-party arrangement. The contractor is the principal, the party with the primary obligation to perform; the owner is the obligee, for whose benefit the bond is written; and the surety guarantees the principal's obligations. A lender can be added as a second obligee on a dual obligee bond, but it is never the principal.

questions.question: Which coverage pays an injured employee's statutory benefits regardless of fault?

options.A: Workers' compensation
options.B: Employer's liability
options.C: Commercial general liability
options.D: Owner's and contractor's protective liability
options.E: Builder's risk
options.F: Professional liability

questions.explanation: Workers' compensation pays employees statutory benefits for job-related injuries whether or not anyone was at fault, and in return the employee cannot sue the employer for more. Employer's liability, part 2 of the same policy, covers the employer's liability to employees beyond what the compensation law imposes. Commercial general liability and owner's and contractor's protective liability answer claims by third parties.

questions.question: Who typically authors the conditions of the contract for a project?

options.A: The architect-of-record, while preparing the technical specifications
options.B: The specifier, by editing the firm's Division 01 master guide specification text
options.C: The owner or owner's attorney, frequently using a form such as AIA A201
options.D: The contractor, at the time of contract award and bond procurement
options.E: The owner's insurance adviser, while setting required coverages and limits
options.F: The construction manager, while organizing the separate bid packages

questions.explanation: The conditions of the contract are owner-provided legal documents: often a published standard form such as AIA A201, or standard conditions prepared by the owner's attorney or legal department. The specifier must review them before starting Division 00 or Division 01, and writes Division 01 to expand on them, but does not author them. The contractor, insurance adviser and construction manager do not write them either.

questions.question: Which items do NOT belong in an invitation to bid?

options.A: Instructions for preparing the bid
options.B: Bid security requirements
options.C: Project name and brief description
options.D: Time and place for receipt of bids
options.E: Owner's right to reject bids
options.F: Forms to use and copies to submit

questions.explanation: An invitation to bid should be brief and give only what contractors need to decide whether to obtain the documents: the project, when and where bids are received, the bid security required and the owner's right to reject bids. Anything needed to actually prepare a bid, such as how to fill in the bid and which forms and how many copies to submit, belongs in the instructions to bidders.

questions.question: Alternates listed on a bid form should:

options.A: Always be priced as a deduct from the base bid amount
options.B: Be renumbered on the bid form in order of expected cost
options.C: Match the alternate numbering and descriptions in Section 01 23 00
options.D: Override any conflicting description in the invitation to bid
options.E: Be described in full on the bid form instead of in Division 01
options.F: Match the item numbering in the Section 01 22 00 unit price list

questions.explanation: Section 01 23 00 Alternates identifies each alternate by number and describes its work, and the bid form provides a price blank for each one. Using the same numbers and titles in both, and in the agreement, keeps bids comparable and makes clear which work the owner accepts. Alternates can add or deduct, and their scope is described in Division 01, not on the bid form.

questions.question: When an addendum uses the narrative method to add text to an existing specification section, it should:

options.A: Reissue the entire affected section as a clean revised-page replacement set
options.B: State the revision in the transmittal cover letter instead of the body
options.C: Identify the section, article, and paragraph, then quote the new language
options.D: Reference the revision only by the project-manual page number affected
options.E: Mark the added text with clouds and delta symbols in the reissued section
options.F: List the change under the addendum's contracting-requirements heading

questions.explanation: In the narrative method each change is written out with enough of the original text or location to make it clear on its own: name the section, article and paragraph, then state the new wording. Reissuing the section with clouds and deltas is the revised-page method, and a cover letter, page number or wrong heading does not locate the change precisely.

questions.question: In the narrative method, each revision is described in the addendum text and no pages are reissued. This method is BEST suited for:

options.A: Edits that are issued after the contract is awarded
options.B: Wholesale revisions affecting many full specification sections
options.C: Replacement of several full revised drawing sheets
options.D: Small, surgical edits with clear paragraph references
options.E: Revisions marked with clouds and delta symbols on the page
options.F: Changes needing a CO-01 identifier in the header or footer

questions.explanation: The narrative method describes each change in words, quoting only as much of the original text as needed, which suits a few small edits that can be tied to a specific paragraph. When the changes are many or extensive, reissuing the revised pages or sheets usually communicates them better; clouds, deltas and identifiers such as CO-01 in the header or footer belong to that revised-page method.

questions.question: A bid form lists two alternates only by number ('Alternate 1' and 'Alternate 2'), each with a single price blank. Each alternate swaps a base-bid material for a different one, so its price could come in above or below the base bid. Section 01 23 00 gives each alternate's title and scope. Which changes would improve the bid form?

options.A: Show each alternate's title as well as its number
options.B: Have the specifier label each alternate as an add alternate
options.C: Keep only the numbers and refer bidders to Section 01 23 00 for titles
options.D: Show only the titles and drop the numbers
options.E: Let the bidder state whether each price is an add or a deduct
options.F: Have the owner decide add or deduct after bid opening

questions.explanation: Each alternate on the bid form should carry its title as well as its number, matching Section 01 23 00, so bidders cannot mistake which work they are pricing. When an alternate could cost more or less than the base, the bidder, not the specifier, should state whether the price is an add or a deduct. Labeling every alternate as an add in advance would be wrong for one that comes in below the base.

questions.question: Over the life of a project, the ability to influence its cost is GREATEST during which phase?

options.A: Bidding and the procurement phase of project work
options.B: Programming and the schematic design phase
options.C: Construction documents production phase
options.D: Construction phase, on the building site
options.E: Design development phase
options.F: Facility management phase

questions.explanation: The ability to influence project cost is highest at the start and falls as the project moves through each phase, because more players become involved and major changes become harder without raising the budget. Of these choices, programming and schematic design come earliest. By construction documents, bidding and construction most decisions are fixed, and facility management has the least influence of all.

questions.question: In design-bid-build delivery, which contractual relationship is absent by design?

options.A: Owner-A/E
options.B: Direct A/E-contractor
options.C: Contractor-subcontractor
options.D: Owner-contractor
options.E: A/E-consultant
options.F: Contractor-supplier

questions.explanation: In design-bid-build the owner holds two prime contracts, one with the A/E and one with the contractor. The A/E and the contractor have no contract with each other, only an administrative relationship that comes from their separate agreements with the owner. Consultant agreements, subcontracts and supplier purchase orders all exist beneath those prime contracts.

questions.question: In construction manager at risk (CMAR) delivery, which statements describe the construction manager?

options.A: Is hired by and contracts directly with the A/E for the work
options.B: Holds the subcontracts and assumes cost/schedule risk under a GMP
options.C: Acts only as the owner's advisor and so carries no contractual risk
options.D: Provides preconstruction services, such as budgeting, during design
options.E: Contracts with the owner for design-phase services only
options.F: Joins the owner and A/E in a single multi-party agreement

questions.explanation: The owner's agreement with a CMAR covers two stages: preconstruction services during design, such as budgeting, constructability reviews, scheduling and procurement, and then construction as the general contractor. As constructor, the CMAR holds the subcontracts and takes the cost risk under a guaranteed maximum price. It contracts with the owner, not the A/E, and unlike an advisor it carries real risk.

questions.question: In design-build delivery, the owner contracts with:

options.A: A separate A/E and a separate contractor
options.B: A construction manager, who hires the designers
options.C: Each trade contractor directly
options.D: A single entity for design and construction
options.E: The A/E and contractor in one multi-party agreement
options.F: A CM-Agent, who holds the trade contracts

questions.explanation: The defining feature of design-build is that the owner has a single agreement with one design-build entity for both design and construction. Separate owner-A/E and owner-contractor agreements belong to design-bid-build and CMAR, and a multi-party agreement among owner, A/E and contractor is typical of integrated project delivery.

questions.question: In integrated project delivery (IPD), the relationship among owner, A/E and contractor is typically:

options.A: A single design-build agreement holding both design and build
options.B: Two separate prime agreements managed independently of each other
options.C: A series of bilateral two-party agreements among the parties
options.D: A multi-party agreement with shared risk and shared reward
options.E: An agency agreement making a CM the owner's binding agent
options.F: A GMP agreement with a CM, plus a separate design contract

questions.explanation: Integrated project delivery is typically built on a multi-party agreement in which owner, A/E and contractor manage risk at the project level and share both risk and reward, instead of each protecting its own interests. A single design-build contract, independent prime agreements, a CM agency agreement and a GMP contract with a CM plus a separate design contract describe other delivery methods.

questions.question: Within a specification section, administrative requirements such as submittals belong in:

options.A: PART 2 PRODUCTS
options.B: PART 1 GENERAL
options.C: PART 3 EXECUTION
options.D: An appendix
options.E: Division 01 only
options.F: An ATTACHMENTS article

questions.explanation: PART 1 GENERAL holds the section's own administrative, procedural and temporary requirements, such as submittals and quality assurance, extending the general provisions of Division 01. PART 2 covers products and PART 3 covers installation and other site work. Division 01 sets the general submittal procedures, but the specific items each section requires are listed in that section's PART 1.

questions.question: Under the construction contract, a two-party warranty is an assurance between which parties?

options.A: Owner and A/E
options.B: Contractor and manufacturer
options.C: Owner and manufacturer
options.D: Owner and contractor
options.E: Contractor and subcontractor
options.F: Owner and guarantor

questions.explanation: A two-party warranty is the contractor's contractual promise to the owner that it will stand behind the work for a stated period. The manufacturer, subcontractors and the A/E are not parties to the construction contract. When a third party, a guarantor or surety, backs the obligation, the arrangement becomes a three-party guaranty instead.

questions.question: When a guaranty is added to the owner-contractor warranty, creating a three-party arrangement, who is the third party?

options.A: A guarantor or surety that answers if the principal fails to perform
options.B: The owner's lender holding the construction financing
options.C: The installing subcontractor that performed the work
options.D: The architect/engineer who prepared the documents
options.E: The owner's insurer providing builder's risk coverage
options.F: The commissioning agent who verifies the performance

questions.explanation: Legally, a guaranty is a separate contract in which a third party, the guarantor, takes on responsibility if the principal fails to perform, much as a surety does under a bond. A warranty, by contrast, is the principal's own promise. Installers, the A/E, lenders, insurers and commissioning agents are not parties to the guaranty.

questions.question: In a project manual organized by MasterFormat, Division 00 contains:

options.A: Existing-conditions surveys, demolition, and site-clearing requirements
options.B: General requirements applying in common to all of the technical divisions
options.C: Concrete, masonry, and the other primary structural work-result sections
options.D: Procurement and contracting requirements with the conditions of contract
options.E: Owner-furnished products and the commissioning of the completed facility
options.F: Facility services such as the plumbing, HVAC, and electrical work results

questions.explanation: Division 00 holds the procurement and contracting requirements: introductory information, solicitation, instructions for procurement, available information, procurement forms, agreement and bond forms, and the conditions of the contract. General requirements are Division 01, existing conditions are Division 02, concrete and masonry are Divisions 03 and 04, and plumbing, HVAC and electrical are in the facility services subgroup.

questions.question: Compared with the other written documents prepared as design progresses, an outline specification is best characterized as:

options.A: A brief, organized listing of products and systems keyed to MasterFormat numbers
options.B: A construction-phase administrative document issued only after the contract award
options.C: A precursor to shop drawings, prepared by the contractor for the A/E's review
options.D: A complete, contract-ready specification suitable for competitive bidding as-is
options.E: A description of systems and assemblies organized by UniFormat in schematic design
options.F: A compact, legally enforceable specification for projects of limited scope

questions.explanation: Outline specifications record early decisions on products, materials and quality, usually in design development, as brief sections organized by MasterFormat. Like preliminary project descriptions, which describe systems and assemblies by UniFormat during schematic design, they are less detailed and are not contract documents. Shortform and full-length specifications are the ones used as contract documents.

questions.question: OmniClass incorporates which formats as the basis of its tables?

options.A: MasterFormat
options.B: SectionFormat
options.C: UniFormat
options.D: PageFormat
options.E: PPDFormat
options.F: Uniform Drawing System

questions.explanation: OmniClass uses MasterFormat as the basis of its work results table and UniFormat as the basis of its elements table. SectionFormat and PageFormat sit under MasterFormat and govern the content of a section and the layout of a page, PPDFormat organizes a preliminary project description under UniFormat, and the Uniform Drawing System is part of the National CAD Standard.

questions.question: In the SectionFormat three-part structure, installation, on-site quality control and protection belong in:

options.A: PART 2 PRODUCTS, with the on-site products they apply to
options.B: Division 01, since they are common to all sections
options.C: PART 3 EXECUTION, which covers on-site activities
options.D: PART 1 GENERAL, as administrative requirements
options.E: PART 1 GENERAL, under Field [or] Site Conditions
options.F: PART 2 PRODUCTS, under Source Quality Control

questions.explanation: PART 3 EXECUTION covers work at the site: examination, preparation, installation, field quality control, adjusting, cleaning and protection. PART 2 covers products, including source quality control at the factory, and PART 1 covers administrative and procedural requirements such as field conditions. Division 01 holds only the general requirements common to all sections.

questions.question: A specifier cites each reference standard in a section by abbreviation and number only (for example, 'ASTM C150/C150M'), with no date or full organization name, and defines the organizations' abbreviations in Division 01. Under this approach, where are the reference standards themselves listed?

options.A: An appendix after Division 49
options.B: The general conditions in Division 00
options.C: The References article in PART 1 of each section
options.D: Section 01 42 00—References
options.E: The materials article in PART 2 of each section
options.F: Section 01 41 00—Regulatory Requirements

questions.explanation: Either way, each section lists its standards in the References article of PART 1; this approach only shortens the entries. Section 01 42 00 References then defines the abbreviations, can give the organizations' addresses, and states which edition applies, such as the one in effect when bids are received, but it does not list each section's standards.

questions.question: Specifying modes range from describing a whole project in descriptive terms to describing it only by statements of performance or human requirements. With which mode does the A/E keep the greatest control over the design?

options.A: A total project specified in descriptive terms
options.B: Descriptive specifying with performance criteria
options.C: A design-build statement based on UniFormat
options.D: Systems specified by general statements of performance
options.E: A major assembly specified as a self-contained component
options.F: A total project specified by human requirements alone

questions.explanation: At one end, the whole project is specified descriptively and the A/E defines every item; adding performance criteria, then specifying assemblies and systems by performance, gives the contractor more and more latitude. The narrower the performance specifying, the more control over configuration the A/E keeps. The broadest levels, general statements of performance or human requirements alone, are generally used only in design-build.

questions.question: A preliminary project description prepared during schematic design is organized by:

options.A: Trade contractor scope
options.B: SectionFormat three-part structure
options.C: UniFormat element categories
options.D: MasterFormat section numbers
options.E: UDS drawing disciplines
options.F: OmniClass product tables

questions.explanation: A preliminary project description is organized by UniFormat's systems and assemblies, which match early cost estimating and let the team describe the design before products are chosen. MasterFormat takes over in design development with the outline specifications, and SectionFormat organizes the contents of a single specification section.

questions.question: Construction information moves from UniFormat in the preliminary project description to MasterFormat in the outline specifications during which phase?

options.A: Schematic design
options.B: Programming
options.C: Design development
options.D: Construction documents
options.E: Procurement
options.F: Construction contract administration

questions.explanation: The change from UniFormat to MasterFormat usually comes in design development, when the preliminary project descriptions written in schematic design serve as a resource for the outline specifications. Schematic design is when the PPD itself is written. UniFormat eases the switch by cross-referencing MasterFormat Level 1 and 2 numbers.

questions.question: In the traditional organization of a drawing set, sheets are grouped:

options.A: By drawing type, then by discipline within each type
options.B: By discipline, then by drawing type within each discipline
options.C: By floor level, then by discipline within each level
options.D: Alphabetically by sheet title across all disciplines
options.E: By bid package, then by drawing type within each package
options.F: With all schedules together, then the other sheets by discipline

questions.explanation: A drawing set is traditionally grouped by discipline, such as civil, architectural, structural, mechanical and electrical, and within each discipline by drawing type, from general notes and plans through elevations, sections and details. Schedules stay with the discipline they belong to rather than being collected in one place.

questions.question: Which specifying method states the required results without dictating how to achieve them?

options.A: Proprietary (closed)
options.B: Descriptive
options.C: Reference standard
options.D: Performance
options.E: Proprietary (open)
options.F: Conventional specifying

questions.explanation: A performance specification states the required end result, the criteria for judging it and how compliance will be verified, leaving the contractor free to choose materials and methods that meet it. Descriptive specifying spells out materials and workmanship, proprietary specifying names products, and reference standard specifying works by citing a published standard rather than stating results.

questions.question: A typical outline specification entry consists of:

options.A: Step-by-step installation procedures carried over from PART 3
options.B: A section number and title with brief product descriptions
options.C: Cross-references to the bid form and instructions for each product
options.D: Full PART 1, PART 2, and PART 3 articles, only lightly edited
options.E: A UniFormat element number with assembly performance criteria
options.F: A schedule of products keyed to the drawing sheet numbers

questions.explanation: Outline specifications use MasterFormat section numbers and titles with short descriptions of the products, materials and assemblies chosen so far, often a page or less per section. When one is cut down from a full-length master, most of PART 1 and PART 3 is discarded except costly items such as mock-ups or field testing. UniFormat elements with performance criteria describe a preliminary project description instead.

questions.question: In the MasterFormat arrangement of Division 00, which order is correct?

options.A: Agreement, Invitation to Bid, Instructions to Bidders, Bid Form, Conditions
options.B: Invitation to Bid, Instructions to Bidders, Agreement, Bid Form, Conditions
options.C: Bid Form, Invitation to Bid, Instructions to Bidders, Agreement, Conditions
options.D: Invitation to Bid, Instructions to Bidders, Bid Form, Agreement, Conditions
options.E: Invitation to Bid, Bid Form, Instructions to Bidders, Agreement, Conditions
options.F: Instructions to Bidders, Invitation to Bid, Bid Form, Conditions, Agreement

questions.explanation: Division 00 runs from solicitation, including the invitation to bid (00 10 00), to instructions for procurement (00 20 00) and procurement forms such as bid forms (00 41 00), then to contracting forms such as agreement forms (00 52 00) and the conditions of the contract (00 70 00). Procurement items come before contracting items.

questions.question: Where should the full conditions for returning procurement documents and refunding document deposits be stated?

options.A: In the bid form, as a representation by each bidder
options.B: In the instructions to bidders, with at most a brief mention in the invitation
options.C: In Section 01 10 00 Summary
options.D: In the supplementary conditions
options.E: In the owner-contractor agreement
options.F: In the invitation to bid alone, since bidders read it first

questions.explanation: The instructions to bidders explain how documents are obtained and the conditions for returning them, including when they must come back and how deposits are refunded. Some A/Es also put this in the invitation, but invitations are often limited in size, so they should carry only the minimum and leave the full details to the instructions. Rules that apply only during procurement do not belong in Division 01 or the contract.

questions.question: Which information about the procurement documents belongs in an invitation to bid?

options.A: Instructions for modifying or withdrawing a submitted bid
options.B: The forms to use and the number of bid copies to submit
options.C: The procedure and deadline for requesting substitutions
options.D: Where the documents can be examined and how sets can be obtained
options.E: Guidance for pricing alternates and unit prices on the bid form
options.F: The insurance limits required by the supplementary conditions

questions.explanation: An invitation to bid gives contractors what they need to decide whether to get the documents, so it says where the documents can be examined, such as the A/E's office or plan rooms, and how sets can be obtained. How to prepare, submit, modify or withdraw a bid, the substitution procedure and pricing guidance belong in the instructions to bidders, and insurance limits belong in the conditions of the contract.

questions.question: During construction, a contractor asks to substitute a product. Under AIA A201, other than a minor change the architect authorizes, what is required before the contractor may make the substitution?

options.A: Only the architect's approval of its product data as a normal submittal
options.B: The owner's verbal approval at a progress meeting
options.C: Nothing, if the substitute meets the referenced standards
options.D: The architect's evaluation and the owner's consent, by change order or construction change directive
options.E: An addendum issued to all bidders
options.F: The surety's written consent

questions.explanation: AIA A201 lets the contractor make a substitution only after the architect evaluates it and the owner consents, with the change made by change order or construction change directive; the one exception is a minor change the architect authorizes. Ordinary submittal review covers the specified products, not replacements, and meeting reference standards or getting a verbal nod does not change the contract.

questions.question: An owner allows substitutions after the contract is awarded. Where should the specifier put the construction-phase procedures, including how long the architect has to ask for more information and to accept or reject a request?

options.A: Section 01 25 00 Substitution Procedures
options.B: Document 00 26 00 Procurement Substitution Procedures
options.C: Section 01 26 00 Contract Modification Procedures
options.D: Section 01 33 00 Submittal Procedures
options.E: Section 01 60 00 Product Requirements
options.F: Document 00 72 00 General Conditions

questions.explanation: Procedures for substitutions during construction, including the architect's review periods, belong in Section 01 25 00 Substitution Procedures; when the owner allows substitutions after award, this section should also limit how long after award requests will be considered. Document 00 26 00 covers substitutions during procurement, and the contract modification and submittal sections handle other actions, not requests to replace a specified product.

questions.question: A project's substitution section accepts substitutions for convenience only within 60 days after the notice to proceed. Substitutions for cause must be requested as soon as the need is found and at least 20 days before the related submittals are due to be prepared and reviewed. Five months after the notice to proceed, the specified window manufacturer announces it cannot deliver in time for the schedule. What should the contractor do?

options.A: Nothing; the 60-day window has closed, so the specified product must be used
options.B: Request a substitution for cause right away, at least 20 days before the window submittals are due
options.C: Submit the substitute window's data as the regular submittal, without a substitution request
options.D: Request a substitution for convenience, since keeping the schedule benefits the owner
options.E: Ask the architect to approve the substitute window through an RFI
options.F: Install a similar window and report the change at closeout

questions.explanation: A product that cannot be delivered in time is a project condition, so this is a substitution for cause; the 60-day limit applies only to substitutions for convenience. A request for cause goes in as soon as the need is known and early enough to be reviewed before the related submittals. Sending the substitute as an ordinary submittal or an RFI skips the substitution procedure.

questions.question: A project's substitution section says the architect will consider substitutions for convenience (changes the project does not need but that offer an advantage) only during the first 60 days after the notice to proceed. Four months after the notice to proceed, the contractor proposes a cheaper roofing membrane purely to save money. How should the architect handle the request?

options.A: Evaluate it anyway, since a cost saving benefits the owner
options.B: Treat it as a substitution for cause so that a later deadline applies
options.C: Approve it as a minor change in the Work
