options.D: Return it without action, since the window for convenience requests has closed
options.E: Answer it as a request for information
options.F: Accept it automatically if no decision is given within 15 days

questions.explanation: A cheaper membrane offered only to save money is a substitution for convenience: the project does not need it, it just offers an advantage. This project accepts such requests only within 60 days after the notice to proceed, so a request four months in is returned without action. Calling it a substitution for cause would misstate it, and a substitution is never accepted by silence.

questions.question: A contractor's substitution request names the substitute product but includes no comparison with the specified product and no product data. How should the architect respond?

options.A: Forward it to the owner for a decision without evaluating it
options.B: Mark it approved as noted and ask for the data later
options.C: Hold it until the review period runs out, after which it is approved by default
options.D: Return it without action, noting that the required comparison and data are missing
options.E: Research the product itself, since the A/E must show the substitute is not equal
options.F: Accept it if the substitute costs less than the specified product

questions.explanation: The party proposing a substitution must prove the substitute is comparable, so the request has to include the comparison and supporting data the procedures call for. A request without them cannot be evaluated and is returned without action, with the shortcoming noted. It is not approved by default when a review period passes, and the A/E does not do the requester's research or accept a product just because it is cheaper.

questions.question: During construction, a contractor wants to propose a substitution under the project's Section 01 25 00. Which form, as MasterFormat titles it, should it use?

options.A: 00 43 25 Substitution Request Form (During Procurement)
options.B: 00 63 13 Requests for Information Form
options.C: AIA Document G710, Architect's Supplemental Instructions
options.D: 00 63 25 Substitution Request Form (During Construction)
options.E: AIA Document G709, Work Changes Proposal Request
options.F: AIA Document G714, Construction Change Directive

questions.explanation: After award, a substitution request goes on the substitution request form for use during construction (00 63 25). The procurement-phase form (00 43 25) is for bidders before award, and the RFI form is for questions about the documents, not product changes. Supplemental instructions, proposal requests and construction change directives are issued by the architect or owner, not submitted by the contractor.

questions.question: A tiling section names a single product and makes no provision for comparable products or options. The contractor proposes a different manufacturer's tile only because it costs less; nothing about the project requires the change. Under substitution procedures that separate substitutions for cause from substitutions for convenience, this is a:

options.A: Comparable product submittal
options.B: Minor change in the Work
options.C: Substitution for cause
options.D: Substitution for convenience
options.E: Product option
options.F: Field order

questions.explanation: A substitution for convenience is a change the project does not require but that offers the contractor or owner an advantage, such as a lower price. A substitution for cause is forced by project conditions, such as a product no longer available in time or no longer meeting the code. Comparable products and options apply only where the specification allows them, and minor changes and field orders are issued by the architect.

questions.question: A contractor proposes replacing a specified product because the product can no longer satisfy a newly amended building code requirement. Under substitution procedures that separate substitutions for cause from substitutions for convenience, the proposal is a:

options.A: Substitution for convenience
options.B: Comparable product submittal
options.C: Substitution for cause
options.D: Value engineering proposal
options.E: Construction change directive
options.F: Minor change in the Work

questions.explanation: A substitution for cause is one required by project conditions, such as a specified product that is no longer available for the schedule or can no longer meet an amended code. A substitution for convenience is optional and offers an advantage the project does not need. A comparable product submittal assumes the specification already allows equivalents, and construction change directives and minor changes are issued by the architect or owner.

questions.question: Before starting a portion of the work, a contractor compares the documents and finds that a wall section conflicts with the door schedule. Under AIA A201, when and how should it report the conflict?

options.A: Within 48 hours of discovery, by telephone
options.B: Within 7 days of discovery
options.C: With the closeout documents, before final completion
options.D: Promptly on discovery, as a request for information in the form the architect requires
options.E: Within 15 days of discovery
options.F: At the next monthly progress meeting

questions.explanation: A201 has the contractor study and compare the documents before each portion of the work and report any error, inconsistency or omission it finds promptly, as a request for information in whatever form the architect requires; EJCDC C-700 likewise asks for such questions as soon as possible. Waiting a set number of days or for a meeting risks delay, and a contractor that fails to report can bear the resulting costs.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, how must the architect respond to the contractor's requests for information?

options.A: Within 3 days, the period A201 fixes for every RFI
options.B: Within 14 days, the same period as for submittals
options.C: Within 7 days, unless the owner extends the period
options.D: In writing, within any agreed time limits, or otherwise with reasonable promptness
options.E: Within 15 days, or the RFI is deemed answered in the contractor's favor
options.F: Only at the next progress meeting, in the meeting minutes

questions.explanation: A201 sets no fixed number of days: the architect responds to RFIs in writing within any time limits agreed upon, or otherwise with reasonable promptness, and may issue supplemental drawings and specifications. A specific response period, such as five working days, comes from the project's Division 01 section on requests for information (01 26 13), and an unanswered RFI is never deemed answered.

questions.question: A project's RFI procedures give the architect five working days to answer each RFI and say that if the architect asks for more information, the response time starts when the architect receives it. Two days after receiving an RFI, the architect asks the contractor for field measurements, which arrive four days later. When is the architect's answer due?

options.A: On the fifth working day after the RFI, regardless of the request
options.B: Three working days after the measurements arrive, the time left on the original clock
options.C: Five working days after the architect receives the measurements
options.D: Five working days after the contractor sends the measurements
options.E: Immediately, since the original period has already run out
options.F: Whenever the owner agrees to extend the period

questions.explanation: Under this rule, asking for more information restarts the clock: the architect's five working days run from the day the architect receives the measurements, not from the original RFI and not from the day the contractor sends them. Time used before the request does not carry over, so the full period applies again.

questions.question: Which contractor request is NOT a proper use of an RFI and would typically be returned without action?

options.A: A request for approval of a proposed substitution
options.B: A request to interpret an ambiguity between two detail callouts
options.C: A request to clarify a dimension missing from the drawings
options.D: A request to confirm which of two referenced standards governs
options.E: A request to resolve conflicting notes on two drawing sheets
options.F: A request to explain a discrepancy between a schedule and a plan

questions.explanation: RFIs are for questions about the contract documents: interpretations, missing information and clarifications, such as conflicting notes, a missing dimension or which standard governs. Asking approval of a substitution is not one of them; using an RFI to slip in a substitution, often after the substitution deadline has passed, is a known misuse, and such requests are returned so the substitution procedure is followed.

questions.question: Which statements about requests for information (RFIs) during construction are correct?

options.A: An RFI should not be used to pass the contractor's own duty to study the documents to the A/E
options.B: If the contractor thinks an RFI response adds cost, it may simply add the cost to its next payment application
options.C: An RFI response that does not change the contract documents needs no contract modification
options.D: The A/E may answer an RFI orally at the site, with no written response
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: The contractor may not use RFIs to shift its own duty to review the documents onto the A/E ({A}), and an answer that changes nothing in the contract documents needs no modification ({C}). A contractor that believes an answer adds cost or time must make a claim under A201 or a change proposal under C-700, not just bill it, and the A/E's response is given in writing.

questions.question: A subcontractor e-mails an RFI directly to the architect, bypassing the contractor. Under AIA A201's rules on communications, how should the architect handle it?

options.A: Log it and answer it along with the contractor's RFIs
options.B: Answer it directly to the subcontractor to save time
options.C: Return it without a response, since subcontractor questions must come through the contractor
options.D: Answer it only if it concerns shop drawings
options.E: Answer it within the normal response period if it arrived before the daily cutoff
options.F: Answer it once the A/E's consultant has reviewed it

questions.explanation: A201 routes communications with subcontractors and suppliers through the contractor, since neither the owner nor the A/E has a contract with them. An RFI sent straight to the architect by a subcontractor is therefore returned without a response; the question has to come through the contractor, who coordinates and submits it.

questions.question: A contractor needs the architect to interpret a conflict between a wall section and a door schedule. Which form, as MasterFormat titles it, should it submit?

options.A: 00 63 57 Change Order Request Form
options.B: 00 43 25 Substitution Request Form (During Procurement)
options.C: 00 63 25 Substitution Request Form (During Construction)
options.D: 00 63 13 Requests for Information Form
options.E: AIA Document G710, Architect's Supplemental Instructions
options.F: AIA Document G709, Work Changes Proposal Request

questions.explanation: Questions about what the contract documents mean go to the architect as requests for information, on the project's RFI form (00 63 13), a copy of which belongs in the project manual. Substitution request forms are for proposing different products, and a change order request seeks a change in contract sum or time. Supplemental instructions and proposal requests are issued by the architect, not submitted by the contractor.

questions.question: The project manual holds the written construction documents used to procure the construction contract and to build the project. Name the four kinds of documents it typically contains: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: The project manual holds the written construction documents used to procure the construction contract and to build the project. Which list names the four kinds of documents it typically contains?

options.A: Procurement requirements, contract forms, general requirements, technical specifications
options.B: Procurement requirements, contract forms, conditions of the contract, drawings
options.C: Procurement requirements, contract forms, conditions of the contract, specifications
options.D: Contract forms, conditions of the contract, specifications, drawings
options.E: Procurement requirements, contract forms, specifications, addenda
options.F: Procurement requirements, conditions of the contract, specifications, contract modifications

questions.explanation: A project manual typically contains the procurement requirements, the contract forms, the conditions of the contract and the specifications, and only the last group is actually specifications. The drawings are a separate, graphic part of the construction documents, and addenda and modifications are issued later to change the documents. Don't confuse this list with the arrangement of Division 00 into introductory information, procurement requirements and contracting requirements.

questions.question: Splitting a project manual into separate volumes is good practice once it runs past about 700 pages. Separate volumes may also be used for multiple-prime contract projects and for two kinds of documents issued after the manual itself: ____ and ____.

mc.question: Besides very long manuals and multiple-prime contract projects, separate project manual volumes may be used for which two kinds of documents issued after the manual itself?

options.A: Addenda
options.B: Shop drawings
options.C: Modifications
options.D: Record documents
options.E: Operation and maintenance data
options.F: Product data

questions.explanation: Addenda (issued before the contract is signed) and modifications (issued after) change the project manual, so they can be bound as separate volumes, as can the parts of a multiple-prime project. Shop drawings, product data, record documents and operation and maintenance data are contractor submittals, not documents the design team issues as part of the manual. The cover and table of contents list how many volumes there are and what each holds.

questions.question: In Division 00, the project title page, seals page, certifications page, table of contents, list of schedules and list of drawing sheets (00 01 01 through 00 01 20) make up which part of the division? ____

mc.question: In Division 00, the project title page, seals page, certifications page, table of contents, list of schedules and list of drawing sheets (00 01 01 through 00 01 20) make up which part of the division?

options.A: Procurement Requirements
options.B: Introductory Information
options.C: Contracting Requirements
options.D: Available Information
options.E: Procurement Forms and Supplements
options.F: General Requirements

questions.explanation: Division 00 opens with Introductory Information: the title, certifications and seals pages, the table of contents and the lists of drawing sheets and schedules. Procurement Requirements (00 10 00 to 00 40 00) and Contracting Requirements (00 50 00 to 00 70 00) follow it. Available Information is a procurement heading for items such as geotechnical data, and General Requirements is Division 01.

questions.question: In Division 00, the advertisement for bids, supplementary instructions to bidders, preliminary schedules, existing condition information, geotechnical data, bid forms and the bid security form (00 10 00 through 00 40 00) belong to which part of the division? ____

mc.question: In Division 00, the advertisement for bids, supplementary instructions to bidders, preliminary schedules, existing condition information, geotechnical data, bid forms and the bid security form (00 10 00 through 00 40 00) belong to which part of the division?

options.A: Contracting Requirements
options.B: Introductory Information
options.C: Procurement Requirements
options.D: Conditions of the Contract
options.E: Project Forms
options.F: General Requirements

questions.explanation: These are all Procurement Requirements, grouped under Solicitation, Instructions for Procurement, Available Information, and Procurement Forms and Supplements; they guide bidders and are not part of the contract documents. Contracting Requirements (00 50 00 to 00 70 00) hold the agreement, bond and certificate forms and the conditions of the contract, so Project Forms and Conditions of the Contract are headings inside that part.

questions.question: In Division 00, the agreement forms, bond forms, certificates and other forms, and the general and supplementary conditions (00 50 00 through 00 70 00) belong to which part of the division? ____

mc.question: In Division 00, the agreement forms, bond forms, certificates and other forms, and the general and supplementary conditions (00 50 00 through 00 70 00) belong to which part of the division?

options.A: Procurement Requirements
options.B: Conditions of the Contract
options.C: Introductory Information
options.D: Contracting Requirements
options.E: Procurement Forms and Supplements
options.F: General Requirements

questions.explanation: Contracting Requirements group Contracting Forms and Supplements (00 50 00), Project Forms (00 60 00) and Conditions of the Contract (00 70 00); unlike the procurement requirements, they become part of the contract. Conditions of the Contract is only one heading inside this part, so it does not take in the agreement and bond forms. Procurement Forms and Supplements hold the bid forms, which are procurement requirements.

questions.question: In MasterFormat's Specifications Group, Divisions 20 through 29 make up the ____ Subgroup.

mc.question: In MasterFormat's Specifications Group, which subgroup is made up of Divisions 20 through 29?

options.A: Facility Construction
options.B: Site and Infrastructure
options.C: Facility Services
options.D: Process Equipment
options.E: General Requirements
options.F: Procurement and Contracting Requirements

questions.explanation: The Specifications Group has five subgroups: General Requirements (Division 01), Facility Construction (02-19), Facility Services (20-29: fire suppression, plumbing, HVAC, electrical and the like), Site and Infrastructure (30-39) and Process Equipment (40-49). Facility Construction is the usual mix-up; it covers the building's construction divisions that come before the services. Procurement and Contracting Requirements is Division 00, a separate group.

questions.question: In the typical arrangement of a project manual by MasterFormat, Division 00 has three parts and is followed by Divisions 01 through 49. Name the four groups of documents in order: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: In the typical arrangement of a project manual by MasterFormat, Division 00 has three parts and is followed by Divisions 01 through 49. Which list names the four groups in order?

options.A: Procurement requirements, contract forms, conditions of the contract, specifications
options.B: Introductory information, procurement requirements, contracting requirements, specifications
options.C: Introductory information, bidding requirements, conditions of the contract, specifications
options.D: Introductory information, procurement requirements, contracting requirements, drawings
options.E: Introductory information, procurement requirements, general requirements, specifications
options.F: Procurement requirements, contracting requirements, general requirements, specifications

questions.explanation: Division 00 (Procurement and Contracting Requirements) is split into introductory information, procurement requirements and contracting requirements, and the specifications in Divisions 01 through 49 follow. The list that pairs procurement requirements with contract forms, conditions of the contract and specifications describes what a project manual contains, not this four-part arrangement. General requirements are Division 01, inside the specifications, and drawings are not part of the project manual.

questions.question: Before writing a section, the specifier gathers the project's requirements. One is the owner's intent to insure the structure through ____, because that makes the insurer's standards mandatory for the project.

mc.question: Before writing a section, the specifier gathers the project's requirements. The owner's intent to insure the structure through which organization makes that insurer's standards mandatory?

options.A: UL (Underwriters Laboratories)
options.B: NFPA
options.C: ASTM International
options.D: FM Global
options.E: ANSI
options.F: ICC

questions.explanation: FM Global is a commercial property insurer that also writes standards and tests products, so a building it insures must meet its standards, and the specifier needs to know that before writing. UL, NFPA, ASTM International, ANSI and ICC develop codes, standards or product certifications, but none of them is the owner's property insurer.

questions.question: Every product selection decision based on a product's suitability should be ____, and the A/E must either direct those decisions or be kept informed of them.

mc.question: Every product selection decision based on a product's suitability should be ____, and the A/E must either direct those decisions or be kept informed of them.

options.A: Deferred to the contractor's submittals
options.B: Left to the construction phase
options.C: Recorded
options.D: Approved by the authority having jurisdiction
options.E: Kept out of the specifications until bidding
options.F: Made by the product representative

questions.explanation: Each suitability-based product choice should be recorded, with the A/E either directing it or being told of it. Selection is a systematic, progressive compiling of information that begins in early design, so the record carries decisions forward into the specifications. Leaving choices to the contractor's submittals, the construction phase or a product representative takes them out of the design team's control.

questions.question: Product selection rests on evaluating each product against criteria drawn from the owner's requirements. Name the four broad factors considered in evaluating a product: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Product selection rests on evaluating each product against criteria drawn from the owner's requirements. Which list names the four broad factors considered in evaluating a product?

options.A: The product, the manufacturer, the installation, the warranty
options.B: The product, the supplier, the installation, the cost
options.C: The product, the manufacturer, the installation, the cost
options.D: The product, the manufacturer, the delivery time, the cost
options.E: The manufacturer, the installation, the cost, the reference standard
options.F: The product, the manufacturer, the maintenance, the cost

questions.explanation: The four broad factors are the product itself, its manufacturer, its installation and its cost. Warranty, maintenance, delivery time and reference standards are real considerations, but they are weighed within those four headings rather than replacing one of them. A supplier is not the manufacturer whose reliability and support are being judged.

questions.question: Name six common methods specifiers use to assemble and record specification information for a project: ____, ____, ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list names six common methods specifiers use to assemble and record specification information for a project?

options.A: Notes or email memoranda, product notebook, specification checklists, specification worksheets, preliminary project description, master guide specifications
options.B: Notes or email memoranda, manufacturers' product data, specification checklists, preliminary project description, outline specifications, shortform specifications
options.C: Product notebook, specification checklists, specification worksheets, preliminary project description, outline specifications, record drawings
options.D: Notes or email memoranda, product notebook, specification worksheets, preliminary project description, outline specifications, shortform specifications
options.E: Notes or email memoranda, product notebook, specification checklists, specification worksheets, preliminary project description, outline specifications
options.F: Notes or email memoranda, product notebook, specification checklists, shop drawings, preliminary project description, outline specifications

questions.explanation: The six methods are notes or email memoranda from the project A/E, the product notebook, specification checklists, specification worksheets, the preliminary project description (PPD) and outline specifications; a PPD or outline specification from an earlier phase can serve as a checklist. Master guide and shortform specifications are what the information gets written into, and product data, shop drawings and record drawings come from manufacturers or the contractor.

questions.question: Before any master guide section is edited or any original section is written for a project, the specifier must decide two basic things about the specifications: their ____ and their ____.

mc.question: Before any master guide section is edited or any original section is written for a project, which two basic decisions about the specifications must be made?

options.A: Their type
options.B: Their number of volumes
options.C: Their page layout
options.D: Their organization
options.E: Their bid date
options.F: Their printing method

questions.explanation: The type of specification and its organization are the basic procedural decisions made before any section is edited or written; EJCDC's Uniform Location of Subject Matter then helps decide where each subject belongs. Page layout follows a standard page format, and the number of volumes depends on the final page count, so those are production matters settled later. The bid date is a procurement matter.

questions.question: EJCDC's Uniform Location of Subject Matter gives a recommended primary and secondary location in the construction documents for each subject. Information placed in a secondary location should ____ rather than duplicate what the primary location states.

mc.question: EJCDC's Uniform Location of Subject Matter gives a recommended primary and secondary location for each subject. What should information placed in a secondary location do in relation to the primary location?

options.A: Supersede it
options.B: Supplement it
options.C: Repeat it word for word
options.D: Take precedence over it
options.E: Modify its intent
options.F: Replace it

questions.explanation: Secondary locations add detail to the requirement stated in the primary location; they never repeat or override it. Saying the same thing in two places invites conflicts when one copy is edited and the other is not, so each requirement is stated once in its primary location, secondary locations supplement it, and cross-references tie them together.

questions.question: Information collected for a specification section should be developed in the three-part ____, which keeps the presentation consistent while staying flexible enough for many kinds of projects.

mc.question: Information collected for a specification section should be developed in which three-part format, which keeps the presentation consistent across many kinds of projects?

options.A: MasterFormat
options.B: PageFormat
options.C: UniFormat
options.D: SectionFormat
options.E: OmniClass
options.F: Shortform specification

questions.explanation: SectionFormat arranges every section in three parts (PART 1—GENERAL, PART 2—PRODUCTS, PART 3—EXECUTION), with one requirement per article, paragraph or subparagraph so items can be changed without disturbing the rest. MasterFormat numbers and titles the sections, PageFormat sets the layout of each page, UniFormat and OmniClass are classification systems, and a shortform specification is a condensed kind of section, not a format.

questions.question: When the project is for a government agency, ____ methods of specifying are generally required, so the specifier must know this before starting to prepare the specifications.

mc.question: When the project is for a government agency, which kind of specifying is generally required?

options.A: Closed proprietary
options.B: Sole-source
options.C: Nonrestrictive
options.D: Brand-name-only
options.E: Exclusionary
options.F: Restrictive

questions.explanation: Public owners must keep bidding competitive, so they generally require nonrestrictive specifying, which can be built from descriptive, performance, reference standard or proprietary methods as long as several manufacturers can comply. Federal agencies in particular prohibit brand-name, sole-source and other restrictive or exclusionary requirements except in exceptional cases. Knowing this before writing matters because it limits the methods available.

questions.question: A project manual may use more than one method of specifying, but combining methods in a single product specification creates redundancy and can produce a ____ that cannot be resolved.

mc.question: Why should a specifier avoid combining methods of specifying, such as descriptive and proprietary, in a single product specification?

options.A: It shifts design responsibility to the contractor
options.B: It creates redundancy and can produce a conflict that cannot be resolved
options.C: It makes the specification closed proprietary
options.D: It requires a cash allowance in the bid
options.E: It breaks SectionFormat's three-part structure
options.F: It forces every bidder to submit a substitution request

questions.explanation: Two methods applied to one product state the same requirement twice in different terms, for example a named product plus descriptive requirements that the named product may not meet, and the result can be a conflict no one can resolve. Using different methods for different products in one project manual is fine. Combining methods does not by itself create an allowance, a substitution request or a closed specification.

questions.question: Good specification writing follows the four Cs of effective communication. Name them: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list names the four Cs of effective communication in specifications?

options.A: Clear, concise, consistent, complete
options.B: Clear, concise, correct, coordinated
options.C: Concise, correct, complete, coordinated
options.D: Clear, concise, correct, complete
options.E: Clear, consistent, correct, complete
options.F: Clear, correct, complete, comprehensive

questions.explanation: The four Cs are clear (simple, unambiguous sentences), concise (no unneeded words, but never at the cost of the other three), correct (accurate, exact words) and complete (nothing important left out). Coordinated is sometimes called a fifth C, and using terms consistently is a separate vocabulary rule, so neither replaces one of the four.

questions.question: Beyond the four Cs, specifications should also be ____ with all stakeholders, which is sometimes called the fifth C.

mc.question: Beyond the four Cs, what else should specifications be with all stakeholders, which is sometimes called the fifth C?

options.A: Consistent
options.B: Compatible
options.C: Concise
options.D: Correct
options.E: Coordinated
options.F: Comprehensive

questions.explanation: Coordination with all stakeholders is called the fifth C: the specifications have to fit with the drawings, the related sections and the consultants' work. Concise and correct are already two of the four Cs (with clear and complete), so they can't be the fifth. Consistent is a common wrong guess; it describes how terms are used, not this added C.

questions.question: Specifications should generally be written in the ____ mood, in which each sentence opens with the verb that defines the action, as in 'Spread adhesive with notched trowel.'

mc.question: In which grammatical mood should specifications generally be written, so that each sentence opens with the verb that defines the action?

options.A: Indicative
options.B: Imperative
options.C: Passive
options.D: Streamlined
options.E: Subjunctive
options.F: Interrogative

questions.explanation: The imperative mood puts the action verb first ('Install equipment plumb and level'), which keeps sentences short and easy to understand. The indicative mood needs 'shall' or 'will' in nearly every sentence and becomes wordy and monotonous, often in passive form ('Adhesive shall be spread...'). Streamlining is a separate technique, such as using colons in place of 'shall be' in lists, used along with the imperative; it is not a mood.

questions.question: Only the owner and the contractor sign the owner-contractor agreement, so every instruction in the specifications is directed to the ____.

mc.question: Only the owner and the contractor sign the owner-contractor agreement. To whom are all instructions in the specifications addressed?

options.A: The subcontractor for that trade
options.B: The owner
options.C: The A/E
options.D: The contractor
options.E: The supplier or manufacturer
options.F: The installer

questions.explanation: The specifications are part of the contract between owner and contractor, so their instructions go to the contractor, usually in the imperative mood without 'Contractor shall.' Subcontractors, suppliers and installers are not parties to that contract; the contractor decides who does which work. Where the owner or A/E must act, the text names them ('Owner will').

questions.question: 'Contractor shall' is normally left out in favor of the imperative mood. But 'The Contractor shall,' 'Owner will' and 'A/E will' may be used for clarity when the contractor and the owner or the A/E are both mentioned in the same ____ or ____.

mc.question: 'Contractor shall' is normally left out in favor of the imperative mood. Naming the parties ('The Contractor shall,' 'Owner will,' 'A/E will') is acceptable for clarity when two parties are mentioned in the same what?

options.A: Article
options.B: Section
options.C: Paragraph
options.D: Division
options.E: PART
options.F: Volume

questions.explanation: When one article or paragraph assigns duties to the contractor and also to the owner or A/E, naming each party avoids confusion about who does what. 'Will' has the same legal meaning as 'shall' but is treated as the less obligatory word, so it is used for the owner and A/E. Elsewhere, even within the same section or PART, the imperative addressed to the contractor stays the rule.

questions.question: Specifications don't assign work to trades. Under A201 §1.2.2, the way the Specifications are organized into divisions, sections and articles does not control the Contractor in dividing the Work among ____ or in deciding how much Work any trade performs.

mc.question: Under A201 §1.2.2, the organization of the Specifications into divisions, sections and articles does not control the Contractor in dividing the Work among whom?

options.A: Separate contractors
options.B: Subcontractors
options.C: The A/E's consultants
options.D: Testing agencies
options.E: Manufacturers
options.F: The Owner's own forces

questions.explanation: How the Work is split among subcontractors is the Contractor's decision, and MasterFormat sections are not meant to match a single trade. So write 'Wiring is specified in Section 26 05 19,' not 'the electrical subcontractor shall wire the unit.' Separate contractors are hired directly by the Owner, and the A/E's consultants write sections rather than perform the Work.

questions.question: Words in specifications should be chosen for precise meaning. Once a word has been chosen for a meaning, use it ____ throughout the specifications wherever that meaning is intended.

mc.question: Once a word has been chosen for a meaning in the specifications, how should it be used wherever that meaning is intended?

options.A: Interchangeably with its synonyms
options.B: Consistently
options.C: Sparingly, to avoid repetition
options.D: With a fresh definition each time
options.E: In capital letters
options.F: Alternately with its abbreviation

questions.explanation: Choose each word for its precise meaning, then use that same word every time the same meaning is intended. Switching to synonyms for variety, as ordinary prose encourages, makes the reader wonder whether a different meaning is meant, and specifications carry the force of a contract. A term is defined once, in the definitions, not each time it appears.

questions.question: A specifier should treat specifications from an earlier project as ____ only, rather than editing a copy of them for the new project.

mc.question: How should copies of an earlier project's specifications be used on a new project?

options.A: As the base text, edited for the new project
options.B: Only for reference
options.C: As the office master guide specification
options.D: As the new project's outline specifications
options.E: As the basis-of-design product list
options.F: In place of the product notebook

questions.explanation: Earlier project specifications are for reference only. A copied section may lack options, materials or standards the new project needs, may be out of date or name products no longer made, and may not reflect changes made by that project's addenda and modifications. Editing a maintained master guide specification is the sound way to produce new sections.

questions.question: Giving consultants and the others who write sections an early draft of ____ helps keep their sections from duplicating or omitting its requirements.

mc.question: Which document, sent in early draft form to consultants and the others who write sections, helps prevent overlapping requirements and omissions in their sections?

options.A: The bid form
options.B: The list of drawing sheets
options.C: Division 01—General Requirements
options.D: The geotechnical data
options.E: The construction schedule
options.F: The project cost estimate

questions.explanation: Division 01—General Requirements states the administrative and procedural requirements that apply to every section, so consultants who see an early draft can rely on it instead of writing their own versions or leaving things out. Their input for Division 01 is requested at the same time. Bid forms, geotechnical data, schedules and cost estimates don't set requirements for the consultants' sections.

questions.question: When the project's basic scope and requirements are established, the specifier prepares a list of ____, noting the ____ that goes with each and any related work specified in other sections.

mc.question: When the project's basic scope and requirements are established, what does the specifier list, and what does the list note for each entry?

options.A: Drawing sheets; scope of work
options.B: Section titles; scope of work
options.C: Section titles; construction cost
options.D: Products; manufacturers
options.E: Subcontractors; trade assignments
options.F: Specifying methods; reference standards

questions.explanation: The specifier lists the section titles with each section's scope of work and the related work specified elsewhere; the list coordinates the sections, helps prevent overlaps and omissions, and once finalized it can serve as the project manual's table of contents. It is organized by sections of work, not by subcontractor or trade. Products, manufacturers and costs are worked out later, within each section.

questions.question: When building the list of section titles for a project, the specifier can work through ____ as a checklist to be sure no required section is missing.

mc.question: When building the list of section titles for a project, which standard can the specifier work through as a checklist to be sure no required section is missing?

options.A: UniFormat
options.B: SectionFormat
options.C: MasterFormat
options.D: PageFormat
options.E: The product notebook
options.F: Uniform Location of Subject Matter

questions.explanation: MasterFormat's numbers and titles cover the common sections a project may need, so running through it catches missing sections. The proposed list is then compared with the master guide specification to see which sections can be edited from it and which must be written new. UniFormat organizes early descriptions by systems and assemblies, and SectionFormat and PageFormat govern a section's structure and page layout.

questions.question: When one section refers to another for coordination, cite the section number only, not ____ or page numbers, since those can change in later revisions.

mc.question: When one section refers to another for coordination, what should it avoid citing, along with page numbers, because they can change in later revisions?

options.A: Section numbers
options.B: Article numbers
options.C: Division numbers
options.D: Drawing sheet numbers
options.E: Reference standard designations
options.F: Addendum numbers

questions.explanation: Cross-references name the section number, which stays fixed, never article or page numbers, which shift whenever text is added or deleted. MasterFormat numbering is what makes this work: a section keeps the same number and title, so sections can be revised without renumbering the others. A division number is too broad to point to a specific requirement.

questions.question: When the proposed section title list is checked against the master guide specification's contents, watch for products or work that could end up specified in ____.

mc.question: When the proposed section title list is checked against the master guide specification's contents, watch for products or work that could end up specified in ____.

options.A: Division 00
options.B: More than one section
options.C: The general conditions
options.D: A cash allowance
options.E: A deductive alternate
options.F: The bid form

questions.explanation: The comparison flags products or work that could fall into more than one section so that each is specified once, and it marks which sections can be edited from the master and which must be written new. Duplicated requirements tend to drift apart and conflict. Allowances and alternates are pricing tools, and Division 00 and the general conditions don't specify products.

questions.question: When consultants such as mechanical, electrical, structural and civil engineers, or specialists in areas like roofing or door hardware, write some of the sections, the team needs special ____ so the specifications end up complete, compatible and consistent, with nothing duplicated or left out.

mc.question: When consultants and specialists write some of the sections, what does the team need so the specifications end up complete, compatible and consistent, with nothing duplicated or left out?

options.A: Value engineering
options.B: Commissioning
options.C: Delegated design
options.D: Coordination
options.E: A preconstruction meeting
options.F: Separate general requirements for each discipline

questions.explanation: Consultants often write their own sections because their disciplines seal their own documents, and specialists write sections such as roofing or hardware; that split calls for special coordination so the sections fit together without gaps or overlaps. The prime A/E keeps overall responsibility. Consultants should rely on the project's Division 01 rather than writing separate general requirements for their disciplines.

questions.question: The ____ should take responsibility for coordinating the specifications as a whole, including the sections written by engineering consultants and specialists.

mc.question: Who should take responsibility for coordinating the specifications as a whole, including the sections written by engineering consultants and specialists?

options.A: The contractor
options.B: The owner
options.C: The construction manager
options.D: Each engineering consultant, for its own sections
options.E: The prime A/E
options.F: The authority having jurisdiction

questions.explanation: The prime A/E is responsible for overall coordination of the specifications and should give consultants the project type, contract, formats, general conditions and Division 01 before they start. Each consultant coordinates its own sections with that framework but does not coordinate the whole. The contractor, owner and construction manager use the specifications but don't coordinate their preparation.

questions.question: Before consultants write any sections, the prime A/E should give them information on five subjects. Name them: ____, ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Before consultants write any sections, which five kinds of information should the prime A/E give them?

options.A: Type of project, type of contract, specification formats, general conditions, construction cost estimate
options.B: Type of project, type of contract, specification formats, owner's budget, Division 01 requirements
options.C: Type of project, type of contract, bid schedule, general conditions, Division 01 requirements
options.D: Type of project, type of contract, specification formats, general conditions, Division 01 requirements
options.E: Type of project, list of drawing sheets, specification formats, general conditions, Division 01 requirements
options.F: Type of contract, specification formats, general conditions, Division 01 requirements, bidders' qualifications

questions.explanation: Consultants need the type of project, the type of contract, the specification formats, the general conditions and, above all, the Division 01 requirements, and their own Division 01 input is requested at the same time. With that framework they can avoid putting administrative notes on their drawings or writing separate general requirements for their disciplines. Budgets, cost estimates, bid schedules and bidder information don't shape how their sections are written.

questions.question: The term ____ generally refers to precision and craftsmanship; it is often confused with quality, which reflects all of the requirements.

mc.question: Which term generally refers to precision and craftsmanship and is often confused with quality?

options.A: Quality assurance
options.B: Workmanship
options.C: Quality control
options.D: Tolerance
options.E: Performance
options.F: Execution

questions.explanation: Workmanship means precision and craftsmanship, with measurable properties that can be specified and checked through qualifications, tolerances and other quality assurance and quality control requirements. Quality is broader: it mirrors everything the requirements call for. Quality assurance and quality control are the means of securing and checking it, and a tolerance is one measure of workmanship.

questions.question: A well-known publication that controls workmanship, with measurable tolerances for joinery, surfaces and clearances and three grades (premium, custom and economy), is published jointly by AWMAC and the Woodwork Institute. Name it: ____.

mc.question: Which publication, issued jointly by AWMAC and the Woodwork Institute, controls workmanship with measurable tolerances for joinery, surfaces and clearances and with premium, custom and economy grades?

options.A: PS 1, Structural Plywood
options.B: PS 20, American Softwood Lumber Standard
options.C: North American Architectural Woodwork Standards (NAAWS)
options.D: TCNA Handbook for Ceramic Tile Installation
options.E: AWPA wood preservation standards
options.F: ASTM E2112 installation practice for windows and doors

questions.explanation: The North American Architectural Woodwork Standards (NAAWS) set measurable tolerances and premium, custom and economy grades for architectural woodwork, and the specifier selects the grade, which makes it a model of controlling workmanship by reference. PS 1 and PS 20 are product standards for plywood and softwood lumber, AWPA covers preservative treatment, ASTM E2112 covers window installation, and the TCNA Handbook covers tile installation.

questions.question: Workmanship falls into two main categories: workmanship in the ____ of products, and workmanship in their ____ at the project.

mc.question: Workmanship falls into two main categories. Which pair names them?

options.A: Design; installation
options.B: Manufacturing and fabrication; delivery and storage
options.C: Testing; inspection
options.D: Manufacturing and fabrication; application and installation
options.E: Delivery and storage; maintenance
options.F: Selection; warranty

questions.explanation: Workmanship covers the manufacturing and fabrication of products, specified in PART 2, and their application, installation or erection, specified in PART 3. Installation workmanship can matter as much as the product itself, which is why installer qualifications and mock-ups are used. Delivery and storage, testing and inspection, and warranties are other requirements, not categories of workmanship.

questions.question: A product's final characteristics, such as flatness, reflectivity and finish, result from the combination of its ____ and the ____ that goes into making it.

mc.question: A product's final characteristics, such as flatness, reflectivity and finish, result from the combination of which two things?

options.A: Materials; warranty
options.B: Cost; workmanship
options.C: Materials; workmanship
options.D: Color; texture
options.E: Reference standards; tolerances
options.F: Design; testing

questions.explanation: Materials have their own properties, but human and machine workmanship shape them: flatness and finish depend on the material's thickness and on fabrication techniques such as rolling or folding. Don't confuse the two. Fabricating a product in copper or stainless steel may be no different from fabricating it in carbon steel, so the material and the fabrication workmanship are separate requirements.

questions.question: Product and fabrication workmanship requirements are placed in PART ____ of a specification section.

mc.question: In which part of a specification section are product and fabrication workmanship requirements placed?

options.A: PART 1—GENERAL
options.B: PART 3—EXECUTION
options.C: PART 2—PRODUCTS
options.D: Division 01—General Requirements
options.E: The conditions of the contract
options.F: Section 01 45 00—Quality Control

questions.explanation: Each workmanship requirement goes under its proper heading: product and fabrication workmanship in PART 2—PRODUCTS, installation workmanship in PART 3—EXECUTION. Manufacturers' product data usually supply enough for PART 2, while installation needs closer attention. PART 1 holds the qualifications and submittals that support workmanship, not the fabrication requirements themselves.

questions.question: Installation workmanship requirements, often judged against a mock-up or field sample, are placed in PART ____ of a specification section.

mc.question: In which part of a specification section are installation workmanship requirements placed?

options.A: PART 2—PRODUCTS
options.B: PART 3—EXECUTION
options.C: PART 1—GENERAL
options.D: Division 01—General Requirements
options.E: The Warranty article
options.F: The drawings' general notes

questions.explanation: Installation (application or erection) workmanship belongs in PART 3—EXECUTION, while product and fabrication workmanship goes in PART 2—PRODUCTS. The installer's qualifications largely control the result, and a mock-up or field sample can set the acceptable level; the requirements for those qualifications and mock-ups themselves sit in PART 1 Quality Assurance.

questions.question: Workmanship requirements should be ____; avoid broad generalities such as 'best possible workmanship,' which contractors, subcontractors and suppliers can read many ways.

mc.question: How should workmanship requirements be stated?

options.A: As 'best possible workmanship'
options.B: As 'first-class' or 'high quality' work
options.C: In measurable terms
options.D: Left to the installer's judgment
options.E: Only on the drawings
options.F: Only through the warranty

questions.explanation: Workmanship has measurable properties, so state it in measurable terms: tolerances, referenced standards, qualifications, samples and tests that can be verified. Words like 'best' or 'first-class' mean different things to every contractor, subcontractor and supplier, so they can't be enforced. A warranty deals with failures after the fact and doesn't define the workmanship required.

questions.question: Six methods are commonly used to achieve the desired workmanship. Name them, a key word or two each: ____, ____, ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list names six common methods for achieving the desired workmanship?

options.A: Standards and codes, qualifications, trade association requirements, samples, tolerances, warranties
options.B: Standards and codes, qualifications, trade association requirements, samples, warranties, testing and inspection
options.C: Standards and codes, qualifications, trade association requirements, allowances, tolerances, testing and inspection
options.D: Standards and codes, qualifications, liquidated damages, samples, tolerances, testing and inspection
options.E: Standards and codes, retainage, trade association requirements, samples, tolerances, testing and inspection
options.F: Standards and codes, qualifications, trade association requirements, samples, tolerances, testing and inspection

questions.explanation: Desired workmanship is achieved by referring to standards and codes, setting qualifications for manufacturers, fabricators and installers, citing trade-association workmanship requirements, requiring samples as a basis for judging later work, specifying tolerances and performance or physical requirements, and setting testing and inspection requirements. Warranties, allowances, retainage and liquidated damages deal with remedies and payment, not with defining the workmanship.

questions.question: Selecting most of the many items specified for a project falls largely to the ____, and those choices drive the project's cost, so every stated requirement has economic consequences.

mc.question: Who largely selects the many items specified for a project, and so must weigh the economic impact of each requirement?

options.A: The owner
options.B: The contractor
options.C: The construction manager
options.D: The A/E
options.E: Product representatives
options.F: The subcontractors

questions.explanation: The A/E selects most specified items, so it must weigh the cost of each requirement and match grades to the use: the redwood for an entrance door pull need not be the same grade as a redwood edge strip at the parking lot. The owner sets requirements and may join the selection discussions, and product representatives supply information, but the specified choices are the A/E's.

questions.question: Specifying a specialized construction technique may be a poor choice when the project is in an area where ____ experienced in that technique are not available to do the work.

mc.question: Specifying a specialized construction technique may be a poor choice when the project is in an area where ____ experienced in that technique are not available to do the work.

options.A: Testing agencies
options.B: Skilled workers
options.C: Code officials
options.D: Product representatives
options.E: Design consultants
options.F: Sureties

questions.explanation: The availability of skilled workers in the project's area is a selection factor: a technique that local workers can't perform well puts the result at risk. The same thinking applies to product availability, custom colors with long lead times, and maintenance supplies and services. Testing agencies, code officials and product representatives support the work but don't perform it.

questions.question: Unless the contract says otherwise, five aspects of how the work is carried out are the contractor's sole responsibility, and the owner and A/E bear no responsibility for them: construction ____, ____, ____, ____ and ____.

mc.question: Unless the contract says otherwise, which five aspects of construction are the contractor's sole responsibility?

options.A: Means, methods, materials, sequences, procedures
options.B: Means, methods, techniques, tolerances, procedures
options.C: Means, methods, techniques, sequences, procedures
options.D: Means, design, techniques, sequences, procedures
options.E: Methods, techniques, sequences, procedures, quality standards
options.F: Means, methods, techniques, sequences, products

questions.explanation: Construction means, methods, techniques, sequences and procedures (often shortened to 'means and methods') are the 'how to' of building, and A201 makes the contractor solely responsible for them unless the documents give specific instructions. Materials, products, tolerances and quality standards are what the design team specifies; how the contractor achieves them is its own business.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700 §14.03.A, it is the ____'s obligation to assure that the Work is not defective.

mc.question: Under EJCDC C-700 §14.03.A, whose obligation is it to assure that the Work is not defective?

options.A: The Engineer's
options.B: The Owner's
options.C: The Contractor's
options.D: The Resident Project Representative's
options.E: The surety's
options.F: The testing agency's

questions.explanation: C-700 places the obligation for non-defective Work on the Contractor, which must also correct or replace defective Work and pay the costs it causes. The Engineer only has authority to decide whether Work is defective and to reject it, and the Owner or Engineer gives notice of defects they know about. Observing the Work does not shift the Contractor's obligation to anyone else.

questions.question: Under A201 §4.2.6 and EJCDC C-700, the ____ may reject Work that fails to conform to the Contract Documents, but that authority is not a duty owed to the contractor and does not give control of the Work.

mc.question: Under A201 §4.2.6 and EJCDC C-700, who may reject Work that fails to conform to the Contract Documents?

options.A: The Owner
options.B: The Architect (or the Engineer under C-700)
options.C: The Contractor
options.D: The construction manager
options.E: The surety
options.F: The testing agency

questions.explanation: The architect or engineer has authority to reject nonconforming Work, but using that authority (or not) creates no duty to the contractor and no responsibility for means and methods. The owner is the one party that can accept nonconforming Work, usually for a reduced Contract Sum; the A/E cannot. The contractor must correct rejected Work at its own expense.

questions.question: Under A201 §13.5.2, when the Architect, the Owner or public authorities require testing or inspection beyond what the Contract Documents call for, the cost is borne by the ____, unless the testing shows the Work fails to comply, in which case §13.5.3 puts all the resulting costs on the Contractor.

mc.question: Under A201 §13.5.2, who pays for testing or inspection that the Architect, the Owner or public authorities require beyond the Contract Documents, when the Work turns out to comply?

options.A: The Contractor
options.B: The Architect
options.C: The Owner
options.D: The testing agency
options.E: The surety
options.F: The authority having jurisdiction

questions.explanation: Testing the contract didn't require is extra, so the Owner pays for it when the Work passes. If the testing reveals Work that fails to comply, the Contractor pays all the costs that failure causes, including repeated tests and the Architect's added services. The Contractor does not pay simply because a test was ordered.

questions.question: Under A201 §12.3, instead of requiring removal and correction, the ____ may choose to accept Work that does not conform to the Contract Documents, with the Contract Sum reduced as appropriate and equitable.

mc.question: Under A201 §12.3, who may choose to accept Work that does not conform to the Contract Documents instead of requiring its correction?

options.A: The Architect
options.B: The Contractor
options.C: The construction manager
options.D: The Owner
options.E: The authority having jurisdiction
options.F: The surety

questions.explanation: Only the owner can accept nonconforming Work, and the Contract Sum is then reduced as appropriate and equitable, whether or not final payment has been made. The architect can reject Work but has no authority to accept Work that doesn't conform. The owner's acceptance also cannot excuse Work that violates a code requirement.

questions.question: Name the four Level 2 sections MasterFormat places under 01 40 00—Quality Requirements: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list names the four Level 2 sections MasterFormat places under 01 40 00—Quality Requirements?

options.A: Regulatory Requirements, References, Quality Assurance, Submittal Procedures
options.B: Regulatory Requirements, Quality Assurance, Quality Control, Testing and Inspecting Services
options.C: References, Quality Assurance, Quality Control, Product Requirements
options.D: Regulatory Requirements, References, Mockups, Quality Control
options.E: Regulatory Requirements, References, Quality Assurance, Quality Control
options.F: Regulatory Requirements, Definitions, Quality Assurance, Quality Control

questions.explanation: Under 01 40 00, MasterFormat lists 01 41 00 Regulatory Requirements, 01 42 00 References, 01 43 00 Quality Assurance and 01 45 00 Quality Control. Definitions, Mockups, and Testing and Inspecting Services are Level 3 titles beneath those, while Submittal Procedures (01 33 00) and Product Requirements (01 60 00) belong to other Division 01 groups.

questions.question: In MasterFormat, manufacturer, supplier, fabricator and installer qualifications, testing and inspecting agency qualifications, manufacturer's field services, field samples and mockups are all Level 3 sections under which Level 2 section of 01 40 00—Quality Requirements? ____

mc.question: In MasterFormat, manufacturer, supplier, fabricator and installer qualifications, testing and inspecting agency qualifications, manufacturer's field services, field samples and mockups are all Level 3 sections under which Level 2 section of 01 40 00—Quality Requirements?

options.A: 01 45 00—Quality Control
options.B: 01 43 00—Quality Assurance
options.C: 01 41 00—Regulatory Requirements
options.D: 01 42 00—References
options.E: 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures
options.F: 01 60 00—Product Requirements

questions.explanation: Qualifications, manufacturer's field services, field samples and mockups (01 43 13 through 01 43 39) fall under 01 43 00 Quality Assurance, which sets up quality before and during the work. 01 45 00 Quality Control holds the testing, inspecting and control procedures, including Contractor Quality Control (01 45 16.13). Regulatory Requirements covers codes, laws, rules, fees and permits.

questions.question: In MasterFormat's 01 40 00 group, testing laboratory services, plant inspection procedures, code-required special inspections, testing and inspecting services, and source and field procedures all fall under which Level 2 section? ____

mc.question: In MasterFormat's 01 40 00 group, testing laboratory services, plant inspection procedures, code-required special inspections, testing and inspecting services, and source and field procedures all fall under which Level 2 section?

options.A: 01 43 00—Quality Assurance
options.B: 01 41 00—Regulatory Requirements
options.C: 01 42 00—References
options.D: 01 45 00—Quality Control
options.E: 01 35 00—Special Procedures
options.F: 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures

questions.explanation: These are Level 3 sections 01 45 13 through 01 45 33 under 01 45 00 Quality Control, which covers testing and inspection of the work. Quality Assurance (01 43 00) is the tempting wrong pick: it holds qualifications, manufacturer's field services, field samples and mockups. Special inspector qualifications sit under Quality Assurance, but the special inspections themselves are Quality Control.

questions.question: Division 01 sections generally follow the order of SectionFormat's three parts, yet in most cases the bulk of their provisions belongs in PART ____.

mc.question: Division 01 sections generally follow the order of SectionFormat's three parts. In most cases, where does the bulk of their provisions belong?

options.A: PART 2—PRODUCTS
options.B: PART 3—EXECUTION
options.C: PART 1—GENERAL
options.D: The schedules at the end of PART 3
options.E: The Supplementary Conditions
options.F: Section 01 10 00—Summary

questions.explanation: Most Division 01 content is administrative and procedural (summary, price and payment, administrative requirements, quality assurance, temporary facilities), so it lands in PART 1—GENERAL. Only a few Division 01 sections align with PART 2 (product and performance requirements, source quality control) or PART 3 (field quality control, execution and closeout, life cycle activities).

questions.question: In PART 2—PRODUCTS, the ____ article includes tolerances that set a statistical range of acceptability for a product's properties before the product is incorporated into the project.

mc.question: Which PART 2—PRODUCTS article includes tolerances that set a statistical range of acceptability for a product's properties before the product is incorporated into the project?

options.A: Source Quality Control
options.B: Materials
options.C: Assembly or Fabrication
options.D: Finishes
options.E: Mixes
options.F: Accessories

questions.explanation: Assembly or Fabrication carries the tolerances a product must meet as it is made, before it reaches the project. Source Quality Control is the tempting wrong pick: it covers the tests, inspections and manufacturer services that check the product during manufacture, not the tolerances themselves. Tolerances for installed work go in PART 3.

questions.question: Four PART 3—EXECUTION articles relate to quality assurance and quality control. Name them: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list names the four PART 3—EXECUTION articles that relate to quality assurance and quality control?

options.A: Examination, preparation, installation, field or site quality control
options.B: Examination, cleaning, tolerances, field or site quality control
options.C: Installation, preparation, tolerances, field or site quality control
options.D: Examination, preparation, tolerances, protection
options.E: Examination, preparation, tolerances, field or site quality control
options.F: Examination, preparation, tolerances, source quality control

questions.explanation: Examination and Preparation are quality assurance steps that confirm conditions and surfaces are ready for the work, Tolerances set the acceptable deviation, and Field (or Site) Quality Control is the final verification and the basis for finding defective work. Installation, cleaning and protection are PART 3 articles too, but they carry out the work rather than assure or verify its quality, and Source Quality Control belongs in PART 2.

questions.question: A section requires the manufacturer's representative to visit the site, instruct the installer or the owner's personnel, and verify compliance with the manufacturer's instructions, with a field report as the submittal. These manufacturer's services are specified in PART ____.

mc.question: A section requires the manufacturer's representative to visit the site, instruct the installer or the owner's personnel, and verify compliance with the manufacturer's instructions, with a field report as the submittal. In which part of the section are these services specified?

options.A: PART 1—GENERAL
options.B: PART 2—PRODUCTS
options.C: PART 3—EXECUTION
options.D: The Warranty article of PART 1
options.E: The Supplementary Conditions
options.F: The owner-contractor agreement

questions.explanation: Site visits by the manufacturer's representative belong to PART 3's Field (or Site) Quality Control article, and the field report is the quality control submittal. PART 2 has its own Manufacturer Services paragraph, but it covers coordination at the source during manufacturing, such as special inspections at the plant; the visit to the site is the clue.

questions.question: Four kinds of requirements fall under PART 3's Field (or Site) Quality Control article. Name them: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list names the four kinds of requirements under PART 3's Field (or Site) Quality Control article?

options.A: Field or site tests, field or site inspections, non-conforming work, manufacturer's services
options.B: Field or site tests, field or site inspections, non-conforming work, warranty
options.C: Field or site tests, mock-ups, non-conforming work, manufacturer's services
options.D: Examination, field or site inspections, non-conforming work, manufacturer's services
options.E: Field or site tests, field or site inspections, adjusting, manufacturer's services
options.F: Field or site tests, field or site inspections, non-conforming work, closeout submittals

questions.explanation: Field or Site Quality Control covers field or site tests (soil compaction, load and compression tests), field or site inspections such as visual checks of joints and connections, non-conforming work and its correction, and manufacturer's services at the site. Mock-ups and examination are separate quality assurance steps, adjusting is its own PART 3 article, and warranties and closeout submittals belong in PART 1.

questions.question: Tests such as compression tests that verify a concrete mix design, and sieve analysis of aggregates, are specified in PART ____ of a section.

mc.question: In which part of a section are tests such as compression tests that verify a concrete mix design, and sieve analysis of aggregates, specified?

options.A: PART 3—EXECUTION
options.B: PART 2—PRODUCTS
options.C: PART 1—GENERAL
options.D: Geotechnical data in Division 00
options.E: The Supplementary Conditions
options.F: The Warranty article

questions.explanation: Tests that check a mix design or the materials themselves, such as sieve analysis of aggregates or test curves for switchgear, are source quality control tests in PART 2. Compression tests on concrete already placed are field tests in PART 3, so the mix-design context is what makes this PART 2. Geotechnical data is information made available to bidders, not a specification of tests.

questions.question: Three Division 01 groupings align with PART 2—PRODUCTS of SectionFormat. Name them: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which three Division 01 groupings align with PART 2—PRODUCTS of SectionFormat?

options.A: Product Requirements
options.B: Execution and Closeout Requirements
options.C: Performance Requirements
options.D: Quality Control (Field)
options.E: Quality Control (Source)
options.F: Temporary Facilities and Controls

questions.explanation: Division 01 is arranged to roughly follow SectionFormat: Product Requirements, Performance Requirements and Quality Control (Source) align with PART 2. Quality Control (Field), Execution and Closeout Requirements, and Life Cycle Activities align with PART 3, and administrative items such as Temporary Facilities and Controls align with PART 1.

questions.question: In SectionFormat, the Qualifications paragraph of PART 1's Quality Assurance article covers six kinds of parties. Name them: ____, ____, ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list names the six kinds of parties covered by the Qualifications paragraph of PART 1's Quality Assurance article?

options.A: Manufacturers, suppliers, fabricators, installers, testing agencies, licensed professionals
options.B: Manufacturers, suppliers, fabricators, installers, testing agencies, owner's representatives
options.C: Manufacturers, suppliers, fabricators, installers, inspectors, licensed professionals
options.D: Manufacturers, distributors, fabricators, installers, testing agencies, licensed professionals
options.E: Contractors, suppliers, fabricators, installers, testing agencies, licensed professionals
options.F: Manufacturers, suppliers, fabricators, sureties, testing agencies, licensed professionals

questions.explanation: Qualifications set the minimum expertise required of manufacturers, suppliers, fabricators, installers (or applicators and erectors), testing agencies and licensed professionals, such as design engineers employed by the contractor or manufacturer. Inspectors' qualifications matter for source inspections but are a separate requirement, and distributors, sureties and owner's representatives are not on the list.

questions.question: In SectionFormat, name the six subordinate titles directly under PART 1's Quality Assurance article: ____, ____, ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list names the six subordinate titles directly under PART 1's Quality Assurance article in SectionFormat?

options.A: Qualifications, certifications, regulatory agency sustainability approvals, warranty, mock-ups, field or site samples
options.B: Qualifications, certifications, regulatory agency sustainability approvals, source quality control, mock-ups, field or site samples
options.C: Qualifications, product data, regulatory agency sustainability approvals, preconstruction testing, mock-ups, field or site samples
options.D: Qualifications, certifications, regulatory agency sustainability approvals, preconstruction testing, mock-ups, field or site samples
options.E: References, certifications, regulatory agency sustainability approvals, preconstruction testing, mock-ups, field or site samples
options.F: Qualifications, certifications, coordination, preconstruction testing, mock-ups, field or site samples

questions.explanation: SectionFormat's Quality Assurance article lists Regulatory Agency Sustainability Approvals, Qualifications, Certifications (with Sustainability Standards Certifications beneath it), Preconstruction Testing, Field [or] Site Samples and Mock-ups. Product data, warranties, references and coordination have their own places in PART 1 (Submittals, Warranty, References, Administrative Requirements), and Source Quality Control is a PART 2 article.

questions.question: Within PART 1's Quality Assurance article, which subject covers procedures for posting bonds, recycling on the jobsite, limiting airborne pollution, submitting a procedures plan, and obtaining review and approval from authorities having jurisdiction? ____

mc.question: Within PART 1's Quality Assurance article, which subject covers procedures for posting bonds, recycling on the jobsite, limiting airborne pollution, submitting a procedures plan, and obtaining review and approval from authorities having jurisdiction?

options.A: Regulatory Requirements
options.B: Regulatory Agency Sustainability Approvals
options.C: Qualifications
options.D: Certifications
options.E: Preconstruction Testing
options.F: Mock-ups

questions.explanation: Regulatory Agency Sustainability Approvals gather the procedures and approvals that regulators require on environmental matters: bonds, jobsite recycling, airborne pollution limits, procedures plans and review by authorities having jurisdiction. Regulatory Requirements is the tempting wrong pick; it covers code compliance for items the contractor designs. Certifications verify that performance matches tested units or specified criteria.

questions.question: The quality-related submittals in PART 1's Submittals article generally respond to requirements specified in three articles of the section. Name them: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: The quality-related submittals in PART 1's Submittals article generally respond to requirements specified in which three articles of the section?

options.A: Quality Assurance
options.B: Administrative Requirements
options.C: Source Quality Control
options.D: Delivery, Storage, and Handling
options.E: Field or Site Quality Control
options.F: Warranty

questions.explanation: Quality assurance and quality control submittals answer what the Quality Assurance article (PART 1), Source Quality Control (PART 2) and Field or Site Quality Control (PART 3) require, such as qualification statements, test reports and manufacturer reports. Administrative Requirements is the tempting wrong pick: it deals with quality through preinstallation meetings, but the quality submittals respond to the three articles that set quality requirements.

questions.question: Name the four subordinate titles of SectionFormat's PART 1 Administrative Requirements article: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list names the four subordinate titles of SectionFormat's PART 1 Administrative Requirements article?

options.A: Coordination, progress meetings, sequencing, scheduling
options.B: Allowances, preinstallation meetings, sequencing, scheduling
options.C: Coordination, preinstallation meetings, sequencing, scheduling
options.D: Coordination, preinstallation meetings, warranty, scheduling
options.E: Coordination, preinstallation meetings, sequencing, references
options.F: Coordination, preinstallation meetings, sequencing, unit prices

questions.explanation: Administrative Requirements holds Coordination, Preinstallation Meetings, Sequencing and Scheduling for the section's work; preinstallation meetings for complex installations are its main quality content. Allowances and unit prices belong to Price and Payment Procedures, references to the References article, and warranties to their own article. Progress meetings are project-wide and are specified in Division 01.

questions.question: In a section's quality assurance requirements, ____ describe the obligation to comply with codes for items the contractor designs, including the requirements of authorities having jurisdiction.

mc.question: In a section's quality assurance requirements, which subject describes the obligation to comply with codes for items the contractor designs, including the requirements of authorities having jurisdiction?

options.A: Regulatory Agency Sustainability Approvals
options.B: Qualifications
options.C: Regulatory Requirements
options.D: Reference Standards
options.E: Certifications
options.F: Preconstruction Testing

questions.explanation: Regulatory Requirements state the code obligations, including those of authorities having jurisdiction, for items the contractor designs. Regulatory Agency Sustainability Approvals is the tempting wrong pick: it covers bonds, jobsite recycling, pollution limits and agency approval of procedures. In the current SectionFormat outline, a Regulatory Requirements title also appears under the product description in PART 2.

questions.question: Soil compaction testing of fill placed at the site is specified in PART ____ of the earthwork section.

mc.question: In which part of the earthwork section is soil compaction testing of fill placed at the site specified?

options.A: PART 1—GENERAL
options.B: PART 2—PRODUCTS
options.C: Geotechnical data in Division 00
options.D: PART 3—EXECUTION
options.E: The Warranty article
options.F: The Supplementary Conditions

questions.explanation: Soil compaction, load and compression tests on in-place work are field or site tests under PART 3's Field (or Site) Quality Control article, even when samples taken at the site are tested elsewhere. PART 2 tests check materials or mix designs at the source, and the geotechnical data in Division 00 is information for bidders, not a testing requirement.
