questions.question: The sections that build on particular administrative and procedural provisions of the conditions of the contract, and that apply broadly to the work of every other section, make up ____.

mc.question: Which part of the project manual builds on particular administrative and procedural provisions of the conditions of the contract and applies broadly to the work of every other section?

options.A: Division 00—Procurement and Contracting Requirements
options.B: The Supplementary Conditions
options.C: Division 01—General Requirements
options.D: The General Conditions
options.E: PART 1—GENERAL of each section
options.F: Division 02—Existing Conditions

questions.explanation: Division 01—General Requirements expands on the administrative and procedural provisions of the conditions of the contract and applies to Divisions 02 through 49, so those requirements are stated once instead of in every section, which would invite conflicts and omissions. Requirements unique to one section stay in that section. The general and supplementary conditions set the contract terms that Division 01 builds on.

questions.question: Division 01 expands on the administrative and procedural provisions of the conditions of the contract, which consist of the ____ conditions and the ____ conditions.

mc.question: Division 01 expands on the administrative and procedural provisions of the conditions of the contract. Which two documents make up the conditions of the contract?

options.A: General requirements
options.B: General conditions
options.C: Agreement
options.D: Supplementary instructions to bidders
options.E: Supplementary conditions
options.F: Instructions to bidders

questions.explanation: The conditions of the contract (00 70 00) are the general conditions (00 72 00), a standard form such as AIA A201 or EJCDC C-700, and the supplementary conditions (00 73 00), which modify them for the specific project. Division 01, the General Requirements, expands on both but is a separate part of the project manual, and the instructions to bidders and their supplements are procurement requirements, not contract conditions.

questions.question: By definition in the AIA, EJCDC and ConsensusDocs general conditions, the ____ are not part of the contract documents, so provisions stated only there cannot be enforced while the construction contract is being administered.

mc.question: By definition in the AIA, EJCDC and ConsensusDocs general conditions, which of these is not part of the contract documents, so that provisions stated only there cannot be enforced during contract administration?

options.A: Contracting requirements
options.B: Supplementary conditions
options.C: Procurement requirements
options.D: Division 01 general requirements
options.E: Addenda
options.F: Contract drawings

questions.explanation: The standard general conditions exclude the procurement requirements (00 10 00 through 00 40 00, such as the instructions to bidders and bid form) from the contract documents. Items that apply only during procurement, such as bid security or the bid opening date, belong there; anything that must bind the contractor belongs in the contract documents, such as Division 01. Contracting requirements, supplementary conditions, addenda and drawings are all contract documents.

questions.question: A masonry section sets an allowance that covers only buying and delivering the facing brick, at a stated price per thousand; the labor to install the brick, overhead and profit are included in the contract sum. Under AIA A201's allowance provisions, this is a ____ allowance.

mc.question: A masonry section sets an allowance that covers only buying and delivering the facing brick, at a stated price per thousand; the labor to install it, overhead and profit are included in the contract sum. Under AIA A201's allowance provisions, which type of allowance is this?

options.A: Quantity allowance
options.B: Cash allowance
options.C: Installation allowance
options.D: Contingency allowance
options.E: Testing and inspecting allowance
options.F: Time allowance

questions.explanation: The allowance articles of A201, ConsensusDocs 200 and EJCDC C-700 provide cash allowances: sums in the contract sum that cover only the cost of materials or equipment delivered to the site, including taxes, while installation, handling, overhead and profit are carried in the contract sum separately. A quantity allowance instead names a quantity of work, furnished and installed, and an installation allowance would cover the labor this one leaves out.

questions.question: A carpet section's allowance has bidders include 200 square yards of a specified sheet carpet, purchased, delivered and installed, with the contract sum adjusted if the area actually needed differs. This is a ____ allowance.

mc.question: A carpet section's allowance has bidders include 200 square yards of a specified sheet carpet, purchased, delivered and installed, with the contract sum adjusted if the area actually needed differs. Which type of allowance is this?

options.A: Cash allowance
options.B: Contingency allowance
options.C: Quantity allowance
options.D: Installation allowance
options.E: Time allowance
options.F: Testing and inspecting allowance

questions.explanation: A quantity allowance states an amount of work (here, square yards of carpet, furnished and installed) that bidders include in their prices, usually paired with a unit price so the contract sum can be adjusted to the quantity actually installed; MasterFormat numbers it 01 21 29. A cash allowance instead states a dollar amount, which under the standard general conditions covers only materials delivered to the site.

questions.question: Master guide specification systems are a good source of detailed examples of Division 01 sections. Four of them are AIA's ____ (published by Deltek), Deltek's ____, BSD's ____, and DoD/NASA's ____.

mc.question: Which list correctly completes this statement: four master guide specification systems that give detailed examples of Division 01 sections are AIA's ____ (published by Deltek), Deltek's ____, BSD's ____, and DoD/NASA's ____?

options.A: MasterSpec; SpecText; SpecLink; MasterFormat
options.B: MasterSpec; SpecText; SpecLink; Unified Facilities Guide Specifications
options.C: MasterFormat; SpecText; SpecLink; Unified Facilities Guide Specifications
options.D: MasterSpec; SectionFormat; SpecLink; Unified Facilities Guide Specifications
options.E: MasterSpec; SpecText; UniFormat; Unified Facilities Guide Specifications
options.F: MasterSpec; SpecText; OmniClass; UniFormat

questions.explanation: MasterSpec (AIA, published by Deltek), SpecText (Deltek) and SpecLink (BSD) are the full-length commercial master guide specifications based on US products and standards, and the Unified Facilities Guide Specifications are the federal DoD/NASA masters. MasterFormat, SectionFormat, UniFormat and OmniClass are classification and format standards that organize specifications; they are not master specification text to edit.

questions.question: General administrative and procedural requirements form a three-tier hierarchy, each tier more specific than the one before. Name the three tiers, from broadest to most specific: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: General administrative and procedural requirements form a three-tier hierarchy. Which list gives the tiers in order, from broadest to most specific?

options.A: General conditions; Division 01; PART 1 of each specification section
options.B: Supplementary conditions; Division 01; PART 2 of each specification section
options.C: General conditions; supplementary conditions; PART 3 of each specification section
options.D: Procurement requirements; Division 01; PART 1 of each specification section
options.E: Agreement; general conditions; Division 01
options.F: General conditions; Division 01; PART 3 of each specification section

questions.explanation: The general conditions state administrative and procedural provisions broadly; Division 01 elaborates on them but stays broad enough to apply to every section; and PART 1 (General) of each section states requirements for that section only. Testing shows the pattern: the general conditions say tests may be required, Division 01 sets the laboratory procedures, and each section names the actual tests. PART 2 and PART 3 cover products and execution, not procedures.

questions.question: Provisions that are general in nature and suit almost any project, that professional associations publish as standardized forms, and that define the basic rights, responsibilities and relationship of the owner and contractor are the ____.

mc.question: Which document contains provisions that are general in nature and suit almost any project, is published by professional associations as a standardized form, and defines the basic rights, responsibilities and relationship of the owner and contractor?

options.A: Supplementary conditions
options.B: General requirements (Division 01)
options.C: Master guide specifications
options.D: General conditions
options.E: Instructions to bidders
options.F: Supplementary instructions to bidders

questions.explanation: The general conditions, such as AIA A201 or EJCDC C-700, are standard forms with wide applicability that set out the parties' basic rights, responsibilities and risk allocations and how the contract is administered. The supplementary conditions then modify them to fit one project, and together the two make up the conditions of the contract; Division 01 and master guide specifications are specifications, not contract conditions.

questions.question: The Division 01 sections, together called the General Requirements, specify five kinds of requirements. Name them: ____, ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: The Division 01 sections, together called the General Requirements, specify five kinds of requirements. Which list names the five kinds?

options.A: Administrative; procurement; temporary facilities and controls; performance; life cycle activities
options.B: Administrative; procedural; temporary facilities and controls; contracting; life cycle activities
options.C: Administrative; procedural; temporary facilities and controls; performance; life cycle activities
options.D: Bidding; procedural; temporary facilities and controls; performance; life cycle activities
options.E: Administrative; procedural; temporary facilities and controls; performance; technical specifications for individual products
options.F: Administrative; procedural; insurance and bonds; performance; life cycle activities

questions.explanation: Division 01 covers administrative and procedural requirements (contract administration, submittals, communication and quality control), temporary facilities and controls (used by the contractor only during construction, then removed), performance requirements, and life cycle activities such as commissioning, operation, maintenance and decommissioning. Procurement and contracting requirements, insurance and bonds belong in Division 00, and product-specific technical requirements belong in Divisions 02-49.

questions.question: AIA A101 is a standard form of agreement between owner and contractor; its companion AIA A201 (EJCDC's counterpart is C-700) is a standard form of the ____.
answers: general conditions of the contract for construction

mc.question: AIA A101 is a standard form of agreement between owner and contractor. Its companion, AIA A201 (EJCDC's counterpart is C-700), is a standard form of which document?

options.A: Supplementary conditions
options.B: Instructions to bidders
options.C: General conditions
options.D: Owner-architect agreement
options.E: General requirements (Division 01)
options.F: Performance bond

questions.explanation: A201 is the General Conditions of the Contract for Construction and C-700 the Standard General Conditions of the Construction Contract; both are filed in Division 00 under 00 72 00. Project-specific changes to them go in the supplementary conditions (00 73 00), not in Division 01. Instructions to bidders are a separate form (AIA A701), and the owner-architect agreement is B101.

questions.question: Except for a single statement giving Division 01 its authority, the ____ should not make general references to Division 01, and they should neither repeat the general conditions nor stray into topics that belong in Division 01.

mc.question: Except for a single statement giving Division 01 its authority, which document should not make general references to Division 01, repeat the general conditions, or stray into Division 01 topics?

options.A: Supplementary instructions to bidders
options.B: Agreement form supplements
options.C: Instructions to bidders
options.D: Supplementary conditions
options.E: General conditions
options.F: Bid form

questions.explanation: The supplementary conditions modify the general conditions for one project. Beyond a statement establishing Division 01's authority they need no general references to it (references to specific Division 01 sections are optional aids), and they should not restate the general conditions or cover topics Division 01 handles; coordinating the two avoids conflicts, omissions and duplication. Instructions to bidders and their supplements govern only procurement.

questions.question: Contracting requirements have a fourth heading besides contracting forms, project forms and conditions of the contract: 00 90 00—Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications. Name the three Level 2 titles MasterFormat 2020 places under it: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which three Level 2 titles does MasterFormat 2020 place under 00 90 00—Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications?

options.A: Precontract Revisions
options.B: Contract Modification Procedures
options.C: Record Clarifications and Proposals
options.D: Clarification and Modification Forms
options.E: Record Modifications
options.F: Closeout Forms

questions.explanation: Under 00 90 00 come 00 91 00 Precontract Revisions (addenda and bid or proposal revisions made before the agreement is signed), 00 93 00 Record Clarifications and Proposals (record copies of RFIs, clarification notices and proposal requests) and 00 94 00 Record Modifications (record copies of change orders, directives and field orders). Contract Modification Procedures is a Division 01 section (01 26 00), and the blank forms are Project Forms (00 63 00).

questions.question: Name the four Level 2 titles MasterFormat 2020 places under 00 60 00—Project Forms: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list gives the four Level 2 titles MasterFormat 2020 places under 00 60 00—Project Forms?

options.A: Bond Forms, then Certificates and Other Forms, then Clarification and Modification Forms, then Agreement Forms
options.B: Bid Forms, then Certificates and Other Forms, then Clarification and Modification Forms, then Closeout Forms
options.C: Bond Forms, then Certificates and Other Forms, then Clarification and Modification Forms, then Closeout Forms
options.D: Bond Forms, then Representations and Certifications, then Clarification and Modification Forms, then Closeout Forms
options.E: Bond Forms, then Certificates and Other Forms, then Notice of Award, then Notice to Proceed
options.F: Agreement Forms, then Bond Forms, then Certificates and Other Forms, then Closeout Forms

questions.explanation: Project Forms holds the blank forms the contract uses: Bond Forms (00 61 00, such as performance and payment bond forms), Certificates and Other Forms (00 62 00, such as insurance certificate, schedule of values and payment application forms), Clarification and Modification Forms (00 63 00, such as RFI, field order and change order forms) and Closeout Forms (00 65 00, such as the certificate of substantial completion). Bid forms are procurement forms, and agreement forms and notices fall under 00 50 00.

questions.question: In MasterFormat, the Notice of Award (00 51 00), Agreement Forms (00 52 00), Agreement Form Supplements (00 54 00) and Notice to Proceed (00 55 00) fall under 00 50 00—____.

mc.question: In MasterFormat, the Notice of Award (00 51 00), Agreement Forms (00 52 00), Agreement Form Supplements (00 54 00) and Notice to Proceed (00 55 00) fall under which Level 2 heading?

options.A: 00 40 00 Procurement Forms and Supplements
options.B: 00 60 00 Project Forms
options.C: 00 50 00 Contracting Forms and Supplements
options.D: 00 70 00 Conditions of the Contract
options.E: 00 20 00 Instructions for Procurement
options.F: 00 90 00 Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications

questions.explanation: 00 50 00 Contracting Forms and Supplements holds the documents that form the contract itself: the notice of award, the agreement forms (such as AIA A101 or EJCDC C-520), agreement supplements such as allowance and unit price schedules, and the notice to proceed. Bid forms are Procurement Forms and Supplements (00 40 00), bonds and certificates are Project Forms (00 60 00), and the general and supplementary conditions are Conditions of the Contract (00 70 00).

questions.question: The document the owner and contractor sign that binds them to its terms, sets out their relationship and obligations to each other, and incorporates all the other contract documents by reference is the ____.

mc.question: Which document, signed by the owner and contractor, binds them to its terms, sets out their relationship and obligations, and incorporates all the other contract documents by reference?

options.A: General conditions
options.B: Notice of award
options.C: Bid form
options.D: Agreement
options.E: Notice to proceed
options.F: Performance bond

questions.explanation: The agreement (for example AIA A101 or EJCDC C-520, filed under 00 52 00 Agreement Forms) is the legal instrument both parties execute; it states the contract price and times and identifies the other contract documents, which it incorporates by reference, and Division 01 supplements some of its provisions. The bid form is only the bidder's offer, and the notice of award and notice to proceed are separate contracting forms issued around it.

questions.question: The bond under which, if the contractor defaults or fails to perform, the surety must either finish the work as the contract requires or pay, up to the bond's penal sum, for its completion is the ____.

mc.question: Which bond requires the surety, if the contractor defaults or fails to perform, either to finish the work as the contract requires or to pay, up to the penal sum, for its completion?

options.A: Payment bond
options.B: Bid bond
options.C: Performance bond
options.D: Maintenance bond
options.E: Lien bond
options.F: Retainage bond

questions.explanation: The performance bond protects the owner against the contractor's failure to complete the work: the surety finishes the contract or funds its completion up to the penal amount. The payment bond instead guarantees that subcontractors and suppliers are paid, and the bid bond is bid security used only during procurement. Performance and payment bond requirements belong in the supplementary conditions; maintenance or warranty bonds are usually called for by individual sections.

questions.question: The bond guaranteeing that subcontractors, suppliers and others who furnish labor, materials or services for the project will be paid is the ____.

mc.question: Which bond guarantees that subcontractors, suppliers and others who furnish labor, materials or services for the project will be paid?

options.A: Performance bond
options.B: Payment bond
options.C: Bid bond
options.D: Maintenance bond
options.E: Retainage bond
options.F: Certificate of insurance

questions.explanation: A payment bond (also called a labor and material payment bond) guarantees payment to those who supply labor, materials and services to the project. The performance bond instead guarantees that the contract will be completed, and the bid bond secures the bid during procurement. Performance and payment bonds are contract documents whose requirements go in the supplementary conditions, while bid bond information goes in the procurement requirements.

questions.question: Two kinds of certificates commonly included in the project forms are the certificate of ____, which shows the contractor carries the required coverage, and the certificate of ____ with applicable laws and regulations.

mc.question: Two kinds of certificates commonly included in the project forms are the certificate of ____, showing the contractor carries the required coverage, and the certificate of ____ with applicable laws and regulations. Which two words complete the statement?

options.A: Insurance
options.B: Substantial completion
options.C: Payment
options.D: Compliance
options.E: Warranty
options.F: Completion

questions.explanation: Project forms include certificates of insurance, showing the coverage the contract requires, and certificates of compliance with applicable laws and regulations. MasterFormat files the certificate of insurance form under 00 62 00 Certificates and Other Forms (00 62 16) and the certificate of compliance form with the closeout forms (00 65 13). Certificates of substantial completion and of completion record the progress of the work, not coverage or legal compliance.

questions.question: People often call the bound book that goes with the set of ____ 'the specifications', but the specifications are only one part of it; the more accurate name for the book is the project manual.

mc.question: The bound book that goes with the set of ____ is often wrongly called 'the specifications'; the more accurate name for it is the project manual. Which term fills the blank?

options.A: Contract drawings
options.B: Procurement forms
options.C: Record documents
options.D: Submittals
options.E: Addenda
options.F: Operation and maintenance data

questions.explanation: The project manual is the book that accompanies the contract drawings: it collects the procurement requirements, contracting forms, conditions of the contract, Division 01 and the technical specifications. The specifications are only one part of it, which is why calling the whole book 'the specifications' is inaccurate. Submittals, record documents and operation and maintenance data are produced later, during construction and closeout.

questions.question: Contract documents, the written and graphic documents prepared by the A/E and design team, typically include four things. Name them: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list gives the four things the contract documents typically include?

options.A: Procurement requirements; contract drawings; specifications; addenda
options.B: Contracting requirements; contract drawings; specifications; addenda (pre-contract revisions)
options.C: Contracting requirements; contract drawings; specifications; resource drawings
options.D: Contracting requirements; contract drawings; submittals; addenda
options.E: Contracting requirements; contract drawings; specifications; shop drawings
options.F: Procurement requirements; contract drawings; specifications; resource drawings

questions.explanation: Contract documents are the part of the procurement documents that become the contract: the contracting requirements (00 50 00 through 00 90 00, such as the agreement and conditions), the contract drawings, the specifications and pre-contract revisions (addenda). The procurement requirements and any resource drawings do not become contract documents, and submittals such as shop drawings come later from the contractor and are not contract documents either.

questions.question: Name the six documents that make up the procurement documents: ____, ____, ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list names the six procurement documents?

options.A: Procurement requirements; contracting requirements; contract drawings; specifications; resource drawings; addenda
options.B: Procurement requirements; contracting requirements; contract drawings; specifications; record drawings; addenda
options.C: Procurement requirements; contracting requirements; contract drawings; specifications; resource drawings; change orders
options.D: General requirements; contracting requirements; contract drawings; specifications; resource drawings; addenda
options.E: Procurement requirements; contracting requirements; contract drawings; submittals; resource drawings; addenda
options.F: Procurement requirements; contract drawings; specifications; resource drawings; addenda; shop drawings

questions.explanation: The procurement documents are the procurement requirements (00 10 00 through 00 40 00), the contracting requirements (00 50 00 through 00 90 00), the contract drawings, the specifications, any resource drawings, and pre-contract revisions (addenda). When the owner and contractor reach agreement, all but the resource drawings become contract documents (and the standard general conditions also exclude the procurement requirements). Record drawings, change orders and submittals arise only after award.

questions.question: Division 01 schedules a quantity allowance of 250 linear feet of corridor partition. So that the contract sum can be adjusted if the quantity actually installed differs, the bid form asks bidders for ____ for that item.

mc.question: Division 01 schedules a quantity allowance of 250 linear feet of corridor partition. What does the bid form ask bidders for, so the contract sum can be adjusted if the quantity actually installed differs?

options.A: Alternates
options.B: Unit prices
options.C: Cash allowances
options.D: Contingency allowances
options.E: A schedule of values
options.F: A stipulated sum

questions.explanation: Quantity allowances are paired with unit prices: bidders price the work per unit (each, or per linear foot), the allowance sets the quantity included in the contract sum, and the unit price adjusts the sum when the measured quantity differs. Alternates are separately priced options the owner may accept, and an alternate based on these quantities must also reference the unit prices. A schedule of values supports payment applications, not quantity adjustments.

questions.question: The standard EJCDC form for a work change directive is EJCDC ____.

mc.question: Which EJCDC document is the standard form for a work change directive?

questions.explanation: EJCDC C-940 is the Work Change Directive form: it orders a change before price and times are agreed, and a change order follows once the value of the change is established. C-941 is the EJCDC Change Order, C-700 the Standard General Conditions, C-520 an owner-contractor agreement, C-620 the application for payment, and C-200 the guide to instructions to bidders. EJCDC has no standard field order form.

questions.question: Under ConsensusDocs, the ____ formalizes changes in the work, adjusts the contract time and price, is also used to accept substitutions, and needs only the owner's and contractor's signatures (standard form ConsensusDocs 202).

mc.question: Under ConsensusDocs, which document formalizes changes in the work, adjusts the contract time and price, is also used to accept substitutions, and needs only the owner's and contractor's signatures?

options.A: Interim directive
options.B: Written amendment
options.C: Change order
options.D: Construction change directive
options.E: Work change directive
options.F: Field order

questions.explanation: The ConsensusDocs change order (form ConsensusDocs 202) records an agreed change in the work with its time and price adjustment, is also how substitutions are accepted, and is signed only by the owner and contractor. The interim directive, signed by the owner alone, directs work before price or time is agreed. Construction change directives (AIA), and work change directives and field orders (EJCDC), belong to other contract families.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700, an engineer's field order is binding on owner and contractor. If the contractor thinks the field order warrants more money or time, what must it submit before doing the affected work? A ____.

mc.question: Under EJCDC C-700, a field order is binding on the owner and contractor. If the contractor thinks a field order warrants an adjustment in contract price or times, what must it submit before doing the affected work?

options.A: A Claim
options.B: A Change Proposal
options.C: A Change Order
options.D: A Work Change Directive
options.E: A Request for Information
options.F: An Application for Payment

questions.explanation: In C-700 a Change Proposal is the contractor's written request for an adjustment in contract price or times, and it must be submitted before the contractor proceeds with field-order work it thinks deserves one. A Claim is the later step, used to contest the engineer's decision on a Change Proposal. Change orders and work change directives formalize or order the change itself; they are not the contractor's request.

questions.question: When an AIA A201 contractor receives a construction change directive, it must promptly ____ with the changed work and tell the architect whether it agrees with the directive's method for adjusting the contract sum or time.

mc.question: Under AIA A201, what must the contractor do on receiving a construction change directive?

options.A: Stop the affected work until the owner, contractor and architect sign a change order
options.B: Promptly proceed with the change and tell the architect whether it agrees with the adjustment method
options.C: Submit a proposal and wait for the architect to accept it before starting the change
options.D: Sign the directive before starting, since the directive is not valid without the contractor's signature
options.E: File a claim and suspend the affected work until the claim is resolved
options.F: Ask the owner to reissue the change as an order for a minor change in the work

questions.explanation: A construction change directive orders the change before the owner and contractor agree on price or time, so the contractor must go ahead promptly and state whether it agrees with the proposed adjustment method. If it agrees and signs, the agreement is recorded as a change order; if not, the work still goes on and the architect determines the adjustment. The directive is valid with only the owner's and architect's signatures.

questions.question: Owner-furnished, contractor-installed (OFCI) products are listed in Division 01, in either Section 01 10 00—Summary or Section ____.

mc.question: Owner-furnished, contractor-installed (OFCI) products are listed in Division 01, in either Section 01 10 00—Summary or which other section?

options.A: 01 65 00 Product Delivery Requirements
options.B: 01 73 00 Execution
options.C: 01 62 00 Product Options
options.D: 01 64 00 Owner-Furnished Products
options.E: 01 66 00 Product Storage and Handling Requirements
options.F: 01 12 00 Multiple Contract Summary

questions.explanation: The OFCI list goes in 01 10 00 Summary or 01 64 00 Owner-Furnished Products, and the section used should also state the owner's and contractor's responsibilities; if 01 64 00 is used, the list sits there and is cross-referenced in Summary. Section 01 73 00 Execution covers the basic requirements for installing products, including owner-furnished ones, but refers back to 01 64 00 rather than listing them.

questions.question: Mockups are specified in two places: the general requirements for mockups, including integrated mockups, go in Division ____, and the mockups needed for particular work go in the sections of Divisions ____.

mc.question: When coordinating Division 01 with the other sections, where are mockups specified?

options.A: Division 01 only
options.B: Divisions 02-49 only
options.C: Division 01 and Divisions 02-49
options.D: Division 00 and Division 01
options.E: Division 00 and Divisions 02-49
options.F: Division 01 and the supplementary conditions

questions.explanation: Division 01 (Section 01 43 39 Mockups, under 01 43 00 Quality Assurance) sets the general requirements for mockups, including integrated mockups that combine the work of several sections. Each product section in Divisions 02-49 then states its own mockup requirements and cross-references 01 43 39 instead of repeating it. Division 00 holds procurement and contracting requirements, not quality requirements.

questions.question: Because insurance amounts vary from project to project, the proper place for them, when the general conditions do not provide for them, is the ____; with AIA documents they go in an insurance attachment to the owner-contractor agreement instead.

mc.question: Because insurance amounts vary from project to project, where do they properly go when the general conditions do not provide for them (and no AIA insurance attachment to the agreement is used)?

options.A: General conditions
options.B: Supplementary conditions
options.C: Instructions to bidders
options.D: Section 01 10 00 Summary
options.E: Bid form
options.F: Section 01 41 00 Regulatory Requirements

questions.explanation: The standard AIA, EJCDC and ConsensusDocs general conditions contain no insurance dollar amounts, so project-specific amounts go in the supplementary conditions (00 73 16 Insurance Requirements), or with AIA documents in an attachment to the agreement. The owner supplies the coverage amounts, ideally after consulting its insurance advisor, and the A/E inserts them. Insurance is a contract condition, so it does not belong in Division 01 or in the procurement documents.

questions.question: Routine procedures for shop drawings, product data and samples are specified in Division 01 Section ____, while the specific items that must be submitted are identified in each section of Divisions 02-49.

mc.question: Routine procedures for shop drawings, product data and samples are specified in which Division 01 section, while each section of Divisions 02-49 identifies the specific items to be submitted?

options.A: 01 31 00 Project Management and Coordination
options.B: 01 33 00 Submittal Procedures
options.C: 01 32 00 Construction Progress Documentation
options.D: 01 78 00 Closeout Submittals
options.E: 01 43 00 Quality Assurance
options.F: 01 26 00 Contract Modification Procedures

questions.explanation: Section 01 33 00 Submittal Procedures sets the routine for every submittal: the submittal schedule, formats, number of copies, and handling of shop drawings, product data and samples. Each section's PART 1 submittals article then lists exactly what to submit for that work. Closeout Submittals (01 78 00) covers end-of-project items such as operation and maintenance data, warranties and record documents.

questions.question: Substitution procedures for the construction stage go in Section 01 25 00—Substitution Procedures; the substitution procedures that apply during procurement go in Division 00, document ____.

mc.question: Substitution procedures for the construction stage go in Section 01 25 00—Substitution Procedures. Which Division 00 document holds the substitution procedures that apply during procurement?

options.A: 00 22 00 Supplementary Instructions
options.B: 00 26 00 Procurement Substitution Procedures
options.C: 00 21 00 Instructions
options.D: 00 25 00 Procurement Meetings
options.E: 00 63 25 Substitution Request Form (During Construction)
options.F: 00 24 00 Procurement Scopes

questions.explanation: MasterFormat gives procurement-stage substitutions their own Division 00 document, 00 26 00 Procurement Substitution Procedures, coordinated with 01 25 00 for the construction stage; if one set of procedures serves both stages, the procurement requirements must refer to 01 25 00. The substitution request form used during construction is a project form (00 63 25), not a procurement procedure.

questions.question: Field offices, hoists and scaffolding, vehicular access and parking, dust and noise barriers, and project identification signs are all specified in sections under Division 01's 01 50 00—____.

mc.question: Field offices, hoists and scaffolding, vehicular access and parking, dust and noise barriers, and project identification signs are all specified under which Level 2 heading of Division 01?

options.A: 01 70 00 Execution and Closeout Requirements
options.B: 01 30 00 Administrative Requirements
options.C: 01 50 00 Temporary Facilities and Controls
options.D: 01 60 00 Product Requirements
options.E: 01 10 00 Summary
options.F: 01 40 00 Quality Requirements

questions.explanation: 01 50 00 Temporary Facilities and Controls runs from Temporary Utilities (01 51 00) through Construction Facilities such as field offices, Construction Aids such as hoists and scaffolding, Vehicular Access and Parking, and Temporary Barriers and Enclosures, to Project Identification (01 58 00). These items serve the contractor only during construction and are removed when no longer needed; specifying them in Division 01 makes them contract requirements.

questions.question: A masonry veneer section's Mockups article states that the brick veneer is to be built as part of the integrated exterior mockup. When coordinating the specifications, which Level 3 Division 01 section under 01 43 00 Quality Assurance should it cross-reference? Section ____.

mc.question: A masonry veneer section's Mockups article says the brick veneer is to be built as part of the integrated exterior mockup. Which Level 3 Division 01 section, under 01 43 00 Quality Assurance, should it cross-reference?

questions.explanation: Section 01 43 39 Mockups, the last Level 3 section under 01 43 00 Quality Assurance, specifies mockups, including integrated exterior mockups that bring several sections' work together in one assembly. The masonry section states its own mockup needs and cross-references 01 43 39 rather than repeating it. Nearby numbers are 01 43 36 Field Samples, 01 43 33 Manufacturer's Field Services, 01 43 23 Installer Qualifications and 01 43 26 Testing and Inspecting Agency Qualifications.

questions.question: Documents, written or drawn, that change the procurement documents before bids or proposals are opened, whether by clarifying, revising, adding or deleting information or by changing an earlier document of the same kind, are called ____.

mc.question: What are the written or graphic documents called that change the procurement documents before bids or proposals are opened, by clarifying, revising, adding or deleting information (or changing an earlier one of their kind)?

options.A: Change orders
options.B: Addenda
options.C: Requests for information
options.D: Supplemental instructions
options.E: Bid revisions
options.F: Field orders

questions.explanation: Addenda are issued during procurement, normally before bids or proposals are opened and in time for bidders to price the changes, and they modify the procurement documents or previous addenda. Once the agreement is executed, changes are made by contract modifications such as change orders instead. Bid revisions change a bidder's own bid, not the documents, and requests for information are questions, not changes.

questions.question: Procurement and contract documents are modified by two means: addenda, issued before bids or proposals are received (sometimes up until the agreement is signed), and ____, issued after the agreement is executed.

mc.question: Procurement and contract documents are modified by two means: addenda, issued before bids or proposals are received (sometimes up until the agreement is signed), and which documents, issued after the agreement is executed?

options.A: Supplementary conditions
options.B: Requests for information
options.C: Bid revisions
options.D: Change orders
options.E: Substitution requests
options.F: Notices to proceed

questions.explanation: Addenda change the documents during procurement (AIA allows them until the agreement is executed, EJCDC only until bids are received); after execution, change orders modify the contract. Neither should be relied on to fix poorly prepared documents. Supplementary conditions are part of the original contract, and requests for information and substitution requests lead to changes only once a modification is issued.

questions.question: The A/E helps the owner develop a procurement strategy for the project. Name the three conditions the plan weighs when choosing between a general contractor, multiple contractors and different delivery methods: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: When the A/E helps the owner develop a procurement strategy (a general contractor, multiple contractors, or another delivery method), which three conditions does the plan weigh?

options.A: Local practices
options.B: The A/E's preferred specifying method
options.C: The local labor market
options.D: The edition of MasterFormat in use
options.E: The chances of unfavorable site conditions
options.F: The number of drawing sheets

questions.explanation: The procurement plan looks at local practices, the local labor market, and the chances of unfavorable site conditions, and uses them to judge whether one general contractor, multiple contractors, or another delivery method suits the project. Documentation choices such as the specifying method or MasterFormat edition have no bearing on that decision. Whatever the plan, no change procedure substitutes for clear, complete, coordinated documents.

questions.question: Addenda and change orders are the proper means of handling changes that arise, but they should not be relied on to fix badly prepared ____ and ____.

mc.question: Addenda and change orders are the proper means of handling changes that arise, but which two things should they not be relied on to fix when badly prepared?

options.A: Shop drawings
options.B: Drawings
options.C: Bids
options.D: Project manuals
options.E: Submittals
options.F: Record documents

questions.explanation: Changes do arise, and addenda (before the agreement) and change orders (after it) are how they are handled, but using them to patch up drawings and project manuals that were poorly prepared in the first place is bad practice; nothing replaces clear, concise, correct, complete and coordinated documents. Shop drawings, submittals, bids and record documents are prepared by others and are not what addenda and change orders exist to modify.
questions.source: limits of addenda and change orders

questions.question: The narrative method describes changes to procurement and contract documents in words, rather than reissuing revised pages or sheets. Name the three criteria to observe when using it: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which three criteria should be observed when using the narrative method to describe changes to procurement and contract documents?

options.A: Accuracy
options.B: Brevity
options.C: Completeness
options.D: Clarity
options.E: Consistency
options.F: Cross-references

questions.explanation: Narrative changes should observe brevity (give only enough to make the change clear, without oversimplifying), clarity (repeat enough of the original text that each change explains itself), and cross-references (state a change once, then refer to it wherever it applies). Accuracy, brevity and clarity are instead the three qualities of good specification writing style, so accuracy is the usual mix-up.

questions.question: In the revised-page method, the change is made in the specification section or drawing sheet itself, marked with a revision method such as clouds or delta symbols, and the section or sheet is then ____, possibly with the revision date and an identifier such as CO-01 in its header or footer.

mc.question: In the revised-page method, the change is made in the specification section or drawing sheet itself and marked with a revision method such as clouds or delta symbols. What then happens to the section or sheet?

options.A: It is reissued, often with the revision date and an identifier such as CO-01 in its header or footer
options.B: It is kept on file while a separate narrative statement describes the change
options.C: It is held for the record documents and distributed only at closeout
options.D: It is returned to the contractor as a shop drawing for approval
options.E: It is withdrawn from the set and replaced by a request for information
options.F: It is marked void and kept out of the contract documents

questions.explanation: The revised-page method edits the section or sheet itself, marks the edits with clouds, deltas, strikethrough or similar identifiers, and reissues it, often dated and tagged (for example CO-01 or Change Order No. 1). When there are many changes, or changes of certain kinds, this can communicate better than the narrative method, which leaves the original pages alone and describes each change in words.

questions.question: Rather than answer a bidder's question orally, the A/E should say that an addendum will be issued promptly, because most instructions to bidders state that oral interpretations are not ____.

mc.question: Why should the A/E tell a bidder that an addendum will be issued promptly instead of giving an oral interpretation?

options.A: An oral answer would void the bidder's bid bond
options.B: Instructions to bidders bar the A/E from answering bidder questions at all
options.C: Most instructions to bidders state that oral interpretations are not binding
options.D: An oral answer automatically becomes part of the contract documents when the agreement is signed
options.E: Oral answers may be given only at the pre-bid meeting
options.F: Answers to bidder questions are issued as change orders after award

questions.explanation: Oral instructions should be avoided even if a written addendum is meant to follow: typical instructions to bidders say oral interpretations are not binding, and the general conditions normally require every contract modification to be written. Bidders' questions are answered by addendum during procurement; change orders come only after the agreement is executed.

questions.question: Since the main purpose of addenda is to change the procurement documents, many of those changes result from ____ raised by bidders or proposers.

mc.question: Since the main purpose of addenda is to change the procurement documents, many of those changes result from what, raised by bidders or proposers?

options.A: Claims
options.B: Change order requests
options.C: Questions
options.D: Applications for payment
options.E: Shop drawing submittals
options.F: Closeout submittals

questions.explanation: Many addenda answer questions raised by bidders or proposers; others add requirements (including changes in the extent of work), correct errors or omissions, change the time, date or place for receiving bids, or add qualified products and approved substitutions. Claims, change order requests, payment applications and submittals all arise during construction, after the agreement, when changes are made by contract modification rather than addendum.

questions.question: References to addenda, how they are issued, and other pertinent facts about them appear in four documents. Name them: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list names the four documents that refer to addenda, how they are issued, and other facts about them?

options.A: Instructions for procurement; bid form; notice to proceed; conditions of the contract
options.B: Advertisement for bids; bid form; agreement; conditions of the contract
options.C: Instructions for procurement; bid form; agreement; conditions of the contract
options.D: Instructions for procurement; performance bond; agreement; conditions of the contract
options.E: Instructions for procurement; bid form; agreement; Section 01 10 00 Summary
options.F: Notice of award; bid form; agreement; Division 01 general requirements

questions.explanation: Addenda are tied into the documents by references in the instructions for procurement (their administrative requirements and method of issue), the bid or proposal form (where bidders acknowledge receiving them), the agreement (which lists the addenda among the contract documents), and the conditions of the contract (which define them). Notices of award and to proceed, bonds and Division 01 do not govern addenda.

questions.question: A minor addendum can sometimes go out as late as ____ days before bids or proposals are due without causing hardship for bidders or proposers.

mc.question: What is the latest a minor addendum can sometimes be issued before bids or proposals are due, without causing hardship for bidders or proposers?

options.A: 24 hours before
options.B: 7 days before
options.C: 4 days before
options.D: 10 days before
options.E: 14 days before
options.F: 21 days before

questions.explanation: Addenda must reach bidders with enough time to price them, but a minor one can sometimes still go out four days ahead of the due date. A significant change arriving late may instead justify postponing the bid opening. Don't confuse this with the deadlines for bidder questions: AIA A701 asks for them at least 7 days before receipt of bids and EJCDC C-200 recommends 10 days.

questions.question: Addenda should be numbered ____, and where separate contracts are to be awarded, each contract gets its own ____ of addenda numbers.

mc.question: How should addenda be numbered when separate contracts are to be awarded?

options.A: Consecutively, with a separate series of numbers for each contract
options.B: Consecutively, with one combined sequence shared by all the contracts
options.C: By date of issue, with a separate set of numbers for each contract
options.D: By the specification section affected, in one list for all contracts
options.E: By drawing sheet number, restarting for each contract
options.F: Alphabetically, with letters shared by all the contracts

questions.explanation: Number addenda consecutively, and when separate contracts will be awarded, give each contract its own series of addendum numbers, which keeps each contract's addenda in an unbroken sequence. Where feasible, a simple numbering system for the items inside each addendum also makes later cross-referencing easier. A single sequence shared by every contract, or numbering by date or section, does not follow this practice.

questions.question: AIA A201 treats addenda as instruments issued before the agreement is executed. EJCDC C-700 instead defines addenda as instruments issued before ____.

mc.question: AIA A201 treats addenda as instruments issued before the agreement is executed. EJCDC C-700 instead defines addenda as instruments issued before what?

options.A: Execution of the agreement
options.B: Issuance of the notice of award
options.C: Receipt (opening) of bids
options.D: Issuance of the notice to proceed
options.E: The pre-bid meeting
options.F: Award of the contract

questions.explanation: EJCDC C-700 ends addenda when bids are received or opened, reflecting public work, where the procurement documents often may not be changed between bid opening and execution of the agreement. AIA A201, like ConsensusDocs 200, allows addenda up to execution of the agreement, so a private owner can negotiate adjustments to a bid by addendum. After execution, either family uses contract modifications.

questions.question: The value of the work should decide whether a change is made: non-critical changes that affect neither cost nor time may be left out of addenda and deferred until the ____ is executed.

mc.question: Non-critical changes that affect neither cost nor time may be left out of addenda. Until when may they be deferred?

options.A: Until bids are opened
options.B: Until the agreement is executed
options.C: Until the notice to proceed is issued
options.D: Until substantial completion
options.E: Until the first application for payment
options.F: Until the preconstruction conference

questions.explanation: Whether to issue an addendum should depend on the value of the work involved: for non-critical changes that affect neither cost nor time, it can be better to wait and handle them once the agreement is executed, and many small changes can be dealt with in brief statements. Changes that do affect cost or time belong in an addendum issued early enough for every bidder to price them.

questions.question: When a significant change can only be made by a last-minute addendum, the owner should be told and, where possible, the ____ should be put off.

mc.question: When a significant change can only be made by a last-minute addendum, the owner should be told and, where possible, what should be put off?

options.A: The notice of award
options.B: The pre-bid meeting
options.C: The bid opening date
options.D: The notice to proceed
options.E: Execution of the agreement
options.F: The advertisement for bids

questions.explanation: Hasty last-minute addenda made of a few inadequate statements should be avoided. When a significant late change is unavoidable, tell the owner and, if possible, move the bid opening date so bidders have time to price it; a minor addendum, by contrast, can sometimes go out as late as four days before bids are due. The same guidance applies to addenda in a proposal process.

questions.question: Instructions to bidders set time limits for bidder questions. EJCDC C-200 recommends submitting them at least 10 days before bid opening; AIA A701 stipulates at least ____ days before the date of receipt of bids.

mc.question: Instructions to bidders set time limits for bidder questions. EJCDC C-200 recommends at least 10 days before bid opening. How many days before the date of receipt of bids does AIA A701 stipulate?

options.A: At least 3 days
options.B: At least 4 days
options.C: At least 7 days
options.D: At least 14 days
options.E: At least 21 days
options.F: At least 30 days

questions.explanation: Standard instructions to bidders set deadlines for submitting questions and substitution requests: AIA A701 requires at least seven days before the date for receipt of bids, and EJCDC C-200 recommends at least ten days before bid opening. Four days is a different figure: how late a minor addendum may sometimes still be issued.

questions.question: Addenda issued electronically should be produced in a format that prevents modification, such as ____.

mc.question: Addenda issued electronically should be produced in a format that prevents modification. Which format is the usual example?

options.A: Editable word-processing file
options.B: Native CAD drawing file
options.C: PDF (portable document format)
options.D: Spreadsheet file
options.E: BIM model file
options.F: Plain email message text

questions.explanation: Bidders often forward addenda to sub-bidders on tight schedules, so addenda should be easy to reproduce or electronic, and electronic copies should be in a format with security features that prevent changes after distribution, such as PDF. Word-processing, spreadsheet, CAD and BIM files are easily edited, so a recipient could alter an addendum without anyone noticing.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, the instrument that orders a change in the work before the owner and contractor have reached agreement on adjusting the contract sum or contract time is a ____.

mc.question: Under AIA A201, which instrument orders a change in the work before the owner and contractor have agreed on adjusting the contract sum or time?

options.A: Change order
options.B: Order for a minor change in the work
options.C: Construction change directive
options.D: Work change directive
options.E: Interim directive
options.F: Field order

questions.explanation: The architect prepares the construction change directive (AIA G714) and the owner and architect sign it; it directs the change, and the contractor must perform it while the adjustment is worked out. A change order requires agreement on the change, sum and time, and a minor change involves no adjustment at all. Work change directives (EJCDC) and interim directives (ConsensusDocs) serve the same purpose in other contract families.

questions.question: An AIA A201 construction change directive is signed by only two parties: the ____ and the ____. The contractor's signature is not required.

mc.question: Under AIA A201, which two parties sign a construction change directive when it is issued?

options.A: Owner
options.B: Contractor
options.C: Surety
options.D: Architect
options.E: Subcontractor
options.F: Building official

questions.explanation: A201 defines the construction change directive as a written order that the architect prepares and the owner and architect sign, so it takes effect without the contractor's agreement, and the contractor must carry out the change. The contractor signs only if it agrees with the adjustment, and that agreement is then recorded as a change order. A change order itself needs the owner's, contractor's and architect's signatures.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700, a written order issued by the engineer for minor changes in the work that involve no change in the contract price or contract times, needing neither an executed change order nor the owner's signature, is a ____.

mc.question: Under EJCDC C-700, what is the engineer's written order for minor changes in the work that involve no change in contract price or times and need neither an executed change order nor the owner's signature?

options.A: Work change directive
options.B: Field order
options.C: Change order
options.D: Minor change in the work
options.E: Change Proposal
options.F: Construction change directive

questions.explanation: In EJCDC C-700 the field order is the engineer's written order for minor changes that leave contract price and times unchanged; it binds owner and contractor without an executed change order or the owner's signature, and EJCDC publishes no standard form for it. The AIA counterpart is the minor change in the work (issued on G710, Architect's Supplemental Instructions); a work change directive is signed by the owner and leads to a change order once the change's value is set.

questions.question: A contract modification changes part of the original contract rather than replacing it. Name the three kinds of change a modification can make to portions of the contract documents: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which three kinds of change can a contract modification make to portions of the contract documents?

options.A: Adding
options.B: Replacing the entire contract
options.C: Deleting
options.D: Rebidding the affected work
options.E: Correcting
options.F: Reissuing the complete set of contract documents

questions.explanation: A contract modification adds to, deletes from, or corrects portions of the contract documents. It changes the original contract in some way, often by substituting for one part of it, but it never replaces the contract as a whole, and it does not require rebidding the work or reissuing the full set of documents.

questions.question: In a standard addendum, after the opening remarks and notice to bidders or proposers, the changes are grouped in five parts, following the order of the project manual and drawings. Name them: changes to ____, ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: In a standard addendum, after the opening remarks and notice to bidders or proposers, the changes are grouped in five parts. Which list names them in order?

options.A: Prior addenda; procurement requirements; contracting requirements; specifications; drawings
options.B: Prior addenda; procurement requirements; contracting requirements; specifications; record documents
options.C: Prior addenda; procurement requirements; general requirements; specifications; drawings
options.D: Prior addenda; bid forms; contracting requirements; specifications; drawings
options.E: Change orders; procurement requirements; contracting requirements; specifications; drawings
options.F: Prior addenda; procurement requirements; contracting requirements; submittals; drawings

questions.explanation: An addendum opens with its number and date, project identification, the A/E's name and address, the recipients, and opening remarks with a notice to bidders or proposers. The changes then follow in project-manual order: prior addenda, procurement requirements, contracting requirements, specifications (in section sequence, including approved substitutions), and drawings (in sheet sequence). Division 01 changes fall under specifications.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, a change order states the parties' agreement on three things. Name them: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Under AIA A201, a change order states the parties' agreement on which three things?

options.A: The change in the work
options.B: The amount of retainage to be withheld
options.C: The amount of any adjustment in the contract sum
options.D: The method of binding dispute resolution
options.E: The extent of any adjustment in the contract time
options.F: The architect's additional compensation

questions.explanation: An A201 change order (AIA G701) is drawn up by the architect and signed by all three parties, recording agreement on the change in the work, the amount of any contract sum adjustment, and the extent of any contract time adjustment; sum and time can be changed only this way. If agreement on sum or time is missing, a construction change directive is used instead.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, which three parties sign a change order? ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Under AIA A201, which three parties sign a change order?

options.A: Surety
options.B: Owner
options.C: Contractor
options.D: Subcontractor
options.E: Architect
options.F: Building official

questions.explanation: Because an A201 change order records agreement on the change, the contract sum and the contract time, the architect prepares it and the owner, contractor and architect all sign it. A construction change directive needs only the owner's and architect's signatures, and an order for a minor change in the work can be issued by the architect alone. Sureties and subcontractors are not parties to the owner-contractor contract.

questions.question: When the contractor signs a construction change directive to show it agrees with the proposed method of adjusting the contract sum or time, that agreement should be recorded as a ____.

mc.question: When the contractor signs a construction change directive to show it agrees with the proposed method of adjusting the contract sum or time, how should that agreement be recorded?

options.A: As an order for a minor change in the work
options.B: As a written amendment
options.C: As a change order
options.D: As architect's supplemental instructions
options.E: As a claim
options.F: As a work change directive

questions.explanation: Under A201, a construction change directive signed by the contractor shows its agreement, which takes effect immediately and is recorded as a change order (G701). If the contractor disagrees, it must still perform the work, and the architect usually determines the method and amount of adjustment from reasonable expenditures plus an allowance for overhead and profit. Minor changes and supplemental instructions are for changes with no sum or time adjustment.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, the architect may order, without the owner's signature, a change that involves no adjustment to the contract sum or time and is consistent with the intent of the contract documents. What does A201 call this type of change (not the form used to issue it)? A ____.

mc.question: Under AIA A201, the architect may order, without the owner's signature, a change that involves no adjustment to the contract sum or time and is consistent with the intent of the contract documents. What does A201 call this type of change (not the form used to issue it)?

options.A: Construction change directive
options.B: Minor change in the work
options.C: Architect's supplemental instructions
options.D: Field order
options.E: Change order
options.F: Written amendment

questions.explanation: A201 lets the architect order minor changes in the work, changes that adjust neither the contract sum nor the time and are consistent with the documents' intent; they are made by written order and bind owner and contractor without the owner's signature. Architect's Supplemental Instructions (G710) is the form usually used to issue them, not the name of the change. EJCDC's equivalent is the field order.

questions.question: The procedures for initiating and processing contract modifications belong in which Division 01 section? Section ____.

mc.question: The procedures for initiating and processing contract modifications belong in which Division 01 section?

options.A: 01 25 00 Substitution Procedures
options.B: 01 31 00 Project Management and Coordination
options.C: 01 26 00 Contract Modification Procedures
options.D: 01 33 00 Submittal Procedures
options.E: 01 29 00 Payment Procedures
options.F: 00 63 00 Clarification and Modification Forms

questions.explanation: Section 01 26 00 Contract Modification Procedures sets how modifications are requested and processed, the forms to use, and the data needed to substantiate claims for time and cost, kept consistent with the agreement and the general and supplementary conditions. It is also where the architect names any document other than G710 used for minor changes. Substitution Procedures (01 25 00) covers product substitutions, and 00 63 00 holds the blank forms.

questions.question: Issuing contract document modifications promptly and in an orderly way keeps ____ and ____ to a minimum.

mc.question: Why should contract document modifications be issued in a timely and orderly fashion?

options.A: To give the surety time to approve each change
options.B: To minimize delays and added costs
options.C: To let the contractor bill for changed work before doing it
options.D: So that changes need not appear in the record documents
options.E: So that the owner's signature is not needed
options.F: To spare the architect from evaluating the contractor's proposals

questions.explanation: Timely, orderly modifications minimize delays and added costs: a change started early leaves time to consider proposals and alternatives and reach a mutually acceptable change without disrupting progress. Modifications can usually stay concise by referring to attachments that detail the changes and their cost breakdowns. Speed does not remove the need for the proper signatures or for recording the change.

questions.question: Name the three recognized ways to modify the contract documents when using AIA A201: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which three are the recognized ways to modify the contract documents when using AIA A201?

options.A: Change order
options.B: Work change directive
options.C: Construction change directive
options.D: Field order
options.E: Minor change in the work
options.F: Interim directive

questions.explanation: A201 recognizes the change order (AIA G701), the construction change directive (G714) and the order for a minor change in the work (usually issued on G710, Architect's Supplemental Instructions). Work change directives and field orders are EJCDC C-700 terms (C-700 adds a fourth method, the written interpretation or clarification), and the interim directive is the ConsensusDocs counterpart of the construction change directive.

questions.question: The standard AIA form for ordering minor changes in the work, AIA G710, is titled ____.

mc.question: The standard AIA form for ordering minor changes in the work, AIA G710, has which title?

options.A: Construction Change Directive
options.B: Work Changes Proposal Request
options.C: Architect's Supplemental Instructions
options.D: Change Order
options.E: Field Order
options.F: Supplementary Instructions to Bidders

questions.explanation: AIA G710, Architect's Supplemental Instructions, is the form the architect uses to issue minor changes in the work, which need no owner signature because they do not change the contract sum or time. The other AIA change forms are G701 Change Order, G709 Work Changes Proposal Request and G714 Construction Change Directive; Supplementary Instructions to Bidders is a procurement document, and field orders belong to EJCDC.

questions.question: The standard AIA form for a construction change directive is AIA Document ____.

mc.question: Which AIA document is the standard form for a construction change directive?

questions.explanation: AIA G714 is the Construction Change Directive form. Its neighbors are G701 Change Order, G709 Work Changes Proposal Request (asking the contractor to price a proposed change), G710 Architect's Supplemental Instructions (minor changes) and G702, the contractor's application for payment; EJCDC's work change directive form is C-940.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700, a written directive signed by the owner on or after the contract's effective date, ordering additions, deletions or revisions in the work, responding to differing subsurface or physical conditions, or addressing emergencies, is a ____.

mc.question: Under EJCDC C-700, what is the written directive, signed by the owner and issued on or after the contract's effective date, that orders additions, deletions or revisions in the work, responds to differing subsurface or physical conditions, or addresses emergencies?

options.A: Field order
options.B: Change order
options.C: Construction change directive
options.D: Work change directive
options.E: Interim directive
options.F: Change Proposal

questions.explanation: The EJCDC work change directive (form C-940) orders the change before its value is settled; it may or may not affect contract price or times, but it is evidence that the change will later be incorporated in a change order. A field order covers only minor changes with no price or time change, and the construction change directive (AIA) and interim directive (ConsensusDocs) are the counterparts in other contract families.

questions.question: Name the four recognized ways to change the contract documents when using EJCDC C-700: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list gives the four recognized ways to change the contract documents when using EJCDC C-700?

options.A: Change order; construction change directive; field order; engineer's written interpretation or clarification
options.B: Change order; work change directive; field order; engineer's written interpretation or clarification
options.C: Change order; work change directive; minor change in the work; engineer's written interpretation or clarification
options.D: Change order; work change directive; field order; interim directive
options.E: Change order; work change directive; field order; written amendment
options.F: Addendum; work change directive; field order; engineer's written interpretation or clarification

questions.explanation: EJCDC C-700 recognizes four methods: the change order (C-941), the work change directive (C-940), the field order (no standard EJCDC form), and the written interpretation or clarification issued by the engineer. AIA A201 recognizes only three (change order, construction change directive, minor change in the work), ConsensusDocs uses the interim directive and written amendment, and addenda change documents only before the contract.

questions.question: Under ConsensusDocs 200, the written order, signed only by the owner, that directs the contractor to perform work before agreement on an adjustment to contract time or price (and also directs work the owner believes is not a change) is the ____.

mc.question: Under ConsensusDocs 200, what is the written order, signed only by the owner, that directs the contractor to perform work before agreement on an adjustment to contract time or price, and also directs work the owner believes is not a change?

options.A: Change order
options.B: Written amendment
options.C: Construction change directive
options.D: Interim directive
options.E: Work change directive
options.F: Field order

questions.explanation: ConsensusDocs 200 recognizes three ways to change the contract: the change order (ConsensusDocs 202, signed by owner and contractor), the interim directive (ConsensusDocs 203, signed by the owner alone) and the written amendment. The interim directive does the job that AIA's construction change directive and the EJCDC and DBIA work change directives do in those contract families.

questions.question: ConsensusDocs 200 counts the written amendment as a way to change the contract, yet it provides no standard form for it and does not treat it as a formal change document. The only place its general conditions mention it is the clause on the ____ of the contract documents.

mc.question: ConsensusDocs 200 counts the written amendment as a way to change the contract but provides no standard form for it. Where in its general conditions is the written amendment mentioned?

options.A: In the changes provisions, beside the interim directive
options.B: In the definitions of the contract documents
options.C: In the order of precedence of the contract documents
options.D: In the claims and disputes provisions
options.E: In the insurance and bonds provisions
options.F: In the payments and completion provisions

questions.explanation: The written amendment appears in ConsensusDocs 200 only in the order-of-precedence clause, where written amendments are listed along with change orders, and no standard form exists for it. Its formal change documents are the change order (ConsensusDocs 202) and the interim directive (ConsensusDocs 203). A document recording changes that a later change order will formalize describes a work change directive, not a written amendment.

questions.question: Name the three ways ConsensusDocs 200 provides for changing the contract documents: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which three methods of changing the contract documents does ConsensusDocs 200 recognize?

options.A: Change order
options.B: Construction change directive
options.C: Interim directive
options.D: Field order
options.E: Written amendment
options.F: Work change directive

questions.explanation: ConsensusDocs 200 provides the change order (ConsensusDocs 202, signed by owner and contractor), the interim directive (ConsensusDocs 203, signed by the owner alone and used to direct work before price or time is agreed) and the written amendment, which has no standard form. Construction change directive is the AIA name for the directive tool, work change directive is the EJCDC and DBIA name, and the field order is EJCDC's minor-change document.

questions.question: DBIA Document No. 535, the general conditions between owner and design-builder, provides three ways to change the contract documents. Name them: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which three ways of changing the contract documents does DBIA Document No. 535 recognize?

options.A: Construction change directive
options.B: Change order
options.C: Interim directive
options.D: Work change directive
options.E: Field order
options.F: Minor changes

questions.explanation: DBIA 535 recognizes the change order (DBIA 500D2, signed by owner and design-builder), the work change directive (DBIA 500D5, which orders a change before price or time is agreed) and minor changes, which the design-builder may make if they do not materially or adversely affect design, quality, performance or workmanship and the owner is promptly told in writing. Interim directive is the ConsensusDocs term, construction change directive the AIA term, and field order the EJCDC term.

questions.question: The A/E issues a document that describes proposed changes and asks the contractor to propose how much the contract sum, the contract time, or both should change. It is informational only: it neither directs the contractor to carry out the changes nor halts work in progress. This document is a ____.

mc.question: The A/E issues a document that describes proposed changes and asks the contractor to propose how much the contract sum, the contract time, or both should change. It is informational only: it neither directs the contractor to carry out the changes nor halts work in progress. This document is a ____.

options.A: construction change directive
options.B: change order
options.C: change order proposal request
options.D: request for information
options.E: work change directive
options.F: Architect's Supplemental Instructions

questions.explanation: A change order proposal request (AIA G709, Work Changes Proposal Request, or similar) prices a possible change: the contractor answers with a proposed adjustment of sum, time or both, and once terms are agreed the A/E writes the change order. A construction change directive or work change directive, by contrast, orders the work before the price is agreed, and the change order is the signed final agreement.

questions.question: The standard change order forms are AIA Document ____ and EJCDC ____.

mc.question: Which pair names the standard change order forms of AIA and EJCDC, in that order?

options.A: AIA G714; EJCDC C-940
options.B: AIA G701; EJCDC C-941
options.C: AIA G701; EJCDC C-940
options.D: AIA G710; EJCDC C-942
options.E: AIA G709; EJCDC C-941
options.F: AIA G714; EJCDC C-941

questions.explanation: AIA G701 and EJCDC C-941 are the change order forms, and in both systems the contract sum or price and the contract time change only by written change order. The look-alike numbers belong to other tools: G714 is the AIA construction change directive, C-940 the EJCDC work change directive, G710 the Architect's Supplemental Instructions and C-942 the field order, both used for minor changes.

questions.question: Under DBIA general conditions, when the owner directs a change by work change directive before the price or time adjustment is agreed, both parties must negotiate in ____ toward an agreement, which is then recorded in a change order.

mc.question: Under DBIA general conditions, when the owner directs a change by work change directive before price or time is agreed, how must the owner and design-builder negotiate the adjustment that a change order later records?

options.A: Through binding arbitration
options.B: Through mediation
options.C: Before a dispute review board
options.D: In good faith
options.E: Through the initial decision maker
options.F: Through litigation

questions.explanation: DBIA's general conditions oblige the owner and design-builder to bargain in good faith toward agreement after a work change directive, and the final cost and time are then written into a change order. The directive itself is signed by the owner, and by the design-builder when it accepts. Mediation, arbitration, a dispute review board and an initial decision maker are ways to resolve disputes, not the standard of negotiation the clause sets.

questions.question: A DBIA change order (Document No. 500D2) records changes in scope, price and time and must be signed by the ____ and the ____.

mc.question: Whose signatures does a DBIA change order (Document No. 500D2) require?

options.A: Owner and architect
options.B: Design-builder and architect
options.C: Owner and engineer
options.D: Owner and construction manager
options.E: Owner and design-builder
options.F: Design-builder and surety

questions.explanation: Under DBIA documents only the two contracting parties sign the change order: the owner and the design-builder, recording the change in scope and the adjustments to contract price and time. ConsensusDocs change orders likewise need only owner and contractor. AIA and EJCDC change orders add a third signature, the architect's or engineer's, recommending the change.

questions.question: AIA, EJCDC, ConsensusDocs and DBIA documents all hold that only the ____ has the authority to execute (authorize) a change order.

mc.question: AIA, EJCDC, ConsensusDocs and DBIA documents all hold that only the ____ has the authority to execute (authorize) a change order.

options.A: architect/engineer (A/E)
options.B: contractor
