options.C: owner
options.D: construction manager
options.E: design-builder
options.F: initial decision maker

questions.explanation: Executing a change order means authorizing it, and that power belongs to the owner alone in all four document families. The A/E signs to recommend the change and the contractor signs to accept it, but neither signature authorizes it. In design-build the design-builder also signs, yet only as the party accepting the change.

questions.question: Only the owner executes (authorizes) a change order, and the contractor signs it to show acceptance. The A/E signs it to show that the A/E is ____ the change.

mc.question: Only the owner executes (authorizes) a change order, and the contractor signs it to show acceptance. The A/E signs it to show that the A/E is ____ the change.

options.A: authorizing
options.B: accepting
options.C: certifying
options.D: recommending
options.E: approving
options.F: verifying

questions.explanation: Each signature on a change order means something different: the owner authorizes the change, the contractor accepts it, and the A/E recommends it, and EJCDC assigns the same three roles to owner, contractor and engineer. The A/E cannot authorize or approve the change, because only the owner executes change orders; certifying is what the architect does for applications for payment.

questions.question: The ____ sets out uniform acquisition policies and procedures that apply to every executive agency of the federal government.

mc.question: The ____ sets out uniform acquisition policies and procedures that apply to every executive agency of the federal government.

options.A: Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS)
options.B: Buy American Act
options.C: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR)
options.D: WBDG Federal Facility Criteria
options.E: Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC)
options.F: Davis-Bacon Act

questions.explanation: The Federal Acquisition Regulation is the primary document of the Federal Acquisition Regulations System, which also includes agency regulations that implement or supplement it, and federal contract conditions, whatever their title, are based on it. The Unified Facilities Guide Specifications and Criteria are design and specification guidance, and the Buy American and Davis-Bacon Acts are individual statutes contracts must obey.

questions.question: Federal contract conditions do not carry titles like AIA A201 or EJCDC C-700. Name the four titles federal documents might carry instead: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Federal contract conditions do not carry titles like AIA A201 or EJCDC C-700. Which list gives four titles they might carry instead?

options.A: General Conditions, General Standards, Special Provisions, Contract Clauses
options.B: General Provisions, Supplementary Conditions, Special Provisions, Contract Clauses
options.C: General Provisions, General Standards, Instructions to Bidders, Contract Clauses
options.D: General Provisions, General Standards, Special Provisions, Contract Clauses
options.E: General Provisions, General Standards, Special Provisions, General Requirements
options.F: General Conditions, Supplementary Conditions, Special Provisions, Contract Clauses

questions.explanation: Federal documents may be called Contract Clauses, General Provisions, General Standards or Special Provisions, and however they are titled, all are based on the FAR. General Conditions and Supplementary Conditions are the private-sector names used with AIA and EJCDC documents, Instructions to Bidders is a procurement document, and General Requirements is the title of Division 01 of the specifications.

questions.question: The stated vision of the Federal Acquisition Regulations System is to deliver the ____ product or service to the customer in a timely way, while keeping the public's trust and meeting public policy objectives.

mc.question: The stated vision of the Federal Acquisition Regulations System is to deliver the ____ product or service to the customer in a timely way, while keeping the public's trust and meeting public policy objectives.

options.A: lowest price
options.B: highest quality
options.C: domestically produced
options.D: best value
options.E: commercially available off-the-shelf
options.F: sole-source

questions.explanation: The FAR System's vision is timely delivery of best-value products and services while keeping public trust and meeting public policy objectives, with acquisition participants working as an empowered team. Best value weighs cost, quality and timeliness together, so neither lowest price nor highest quality alone is the goal. Domestic production and off-the-shelf items are separate rules, not the vision.

questions.question: Name the four guiding principles of the Federal Acquisition Regulations System: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list gives the four guiding principles of the Federal Acquisition Regulations System?

options.A: Award to the lowest responsible bidder; fulfill public policy objectives; minimize administrative operating costs; act with integrity, fairness and openness
options.B: Satisfy the customer; fulfill public policy objectives; use only domestically produced materials; act with integrity, fairness and openness
options.C: Satisfy the customer; fulfill public policy objectives; minimize administrative operating costs; act with integrity, fairness and openness
options.D: Satisfy the customer; fulfill public policy objectives; minimize administrative operating costs; specify brand-name products wherever practical
options.E: Satisfy the customer; maximize the use of military specifications; minimize administrative operating costs; act with integrity, fairness and openness
options.F: Award to the lowest responsible bidder; use only domestically produced materials; minimize administrative operating costs; act with integrity, fairness and openness

questions.explanation: The FAR System commits to satisfying the customer in cost, quality and timeliness, keeping administrative operating costs down, doing business with integrity, fairness and openness, and fulfilling public policy objectives. Lowest-bid award, domestic-only materials, brand names and military specifications are not among them; federal policy in fact restricts brand names and ranks military specifications last among reference standards.

questions.question: Three bodies share the job of preparing, issuing and maintaining the FAR. Name them: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which three bodies jointly prepare, issue and maintain the FAR?

options.A: Secretary of Defense
options.B: Comptroller General of the United States
options.C: General Services Administration (GSA)
options.D: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
options.E: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)
options.F: Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)

questions.explanation: The Secretary of Defense, the administrators of the General Services Administration and NASA jointly prepare, issue and maintain the FAR. The Comptroller General has a right of access to contractor records, and agencies such as the Army Corps of Engineers or HUD apply the FAR and may publish regulations that supplement it, but they do not issue it.

questions.question: Under the FAR, the group that includes the government's technical, supply and procurement representatives, the customers they serve, and the contractors that furnish the products and services is called the ____.

mc.question: Under the FAR, the group that includes the government's technical, supply and procurement representatives, the customers they serve, and the contractors that furnish the products and services is called the ____.

options.A: contracting activity
options.B: project team
options.C: Federal Acquisition Regulations System
options.D: design team
options.E: acquisition team
options.F: Federal Supply Service

questions.explanation: The acquisition team is everyone in the acquisition process: government technical, supply and procurement people, the customers they serve, and the contractors, and the FAR vision asks them to work as a team empowered to decide within their areas. The contracting activity is the office the head of the contracting activity runs, and the Federal Acquisition Regulations System covers the regulations and government contracting staff, not contractors.

questions.question: Under the FAR, the official who manages an agency's contracting activity, and who is a contracting officer by virtue of that position, is the ____.

mc.question: Under the FAR, the official who manages an agency's contracting activity, and who is a contracting officer by virtue of that position, is the ____.

options.A: termination contracting officer (TCO)
options.B: head of the contracting activity (HCA)
options.C: Comptroller General
options.D: agency's project manager
options.E: GSA administrator
options.F: Secretary of Defense

questions.explanation: The head of the contracting activity (HCA) manages the contracting activity and holds contracting officer authority simply by holding that post. A termination contracting officer settles terminated contracts, the agency's project manager resolves conflicting review comments on a design, and the Comptroller General, the GSA administrators and the Secretary of Defense are high officials who do not run an agency's contracting office.

questions.question: Under the FAR, contracting officers have authority to do three things with contracts, along with making the related determinations and findings. Name them: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Under the FAR, which three things do contracting officers have authority to do with contracts?

options.A: Enter into contracts
options.B: Prepare the project specifications
options.C: Administer contracts
options.D: Bind the government beyond their delegated authority
options.E: Terminate contracts
options.F: Revise the Federal Acquisition Regulation

questions.explanation: Contracting officers may enter into, administer or terminate contracts, and they make the determinations and findings that go with those acts; only they may sign contracts for the United States. They bind the government only as far as the authority delegated to them in writing. The A/E prepares the specifications, and DOD, GSA and NASA maintain the FAR itself.

questions.question: Under FAR Part 43, only contracting officers may execute contract modifications. The kind of modification used to make administrative changes, issue change orders and issue termination notices, as opposed to recording negotiated equitable adjustments, is a ____ modification.

mc.question: Under FAR Part 43, only contracting officers may execute contract modifications. The kind of modification used to make administrative changes, issue change orders and issue termination notices, as opposed to recording negotiated equitable adjustments, is a ____ modification.

options.A: bilateral
options.B: negotiated
options.C: administrative
options.D: unilateral
options.E: equitable
options.F: definitized

questions.explanation: FAR contract modifications are either bilateral or unilateral. Unilateral ones cover administrative changes, change orders, changes permitted under clauses other than the Changes clause, and termination notices, and the Changes clause lets the contracting officer make unilateral changes within the contract's scope. Bilateral ones record negotiated equitable adjustments, definitize letter contracts and capture other agreed changes, so negotiated, equitable and definitized all point to the bilateral kind. Administrative names only one of the unilateral uses, not a kind of modification.

questions.question: When a federal contractor receives a change order, it may not stop work; it has an obligation to ____ (except that in cost-reimbursement or incrementally funded contracts it need not go past the limits of the Limitation of Cost or Limitation of Funds clauses).

mc.question: When a federal contractor receives a change order, it may not stop work; it has an obligation to ____ (except that in cost-reimbursement or incrementally funded contracts it need not go past the limits of the Limitation of Cost or Limitation of Funds clauses).

options.A: negotiate an equitable adjustment first
options.B: initiate a claim
options.C: suspend the affected work
options.D: proceed
options.E: request a bilateral modification
options.F: seek the A/E's recommendation

questions.explanation: A federal change order binds the contractor at once: it must comply and keep working, which is the obligation to proceed, limited only by the Limitation of Cost or Limitation of Funds clauses in cost-reimbursement or incrementally funded contracts. The price is settled afterward, and only if the contractor and government cannot agree on the equitable adjustment may the contractor consider a claim.

questions.question: Under FAR Part 46 (Quality Assurance), agencies must make sure that no contract prevents the government from performing ____.

mc.question: Under FAR Part 46 (Quality Assurance), agencies must make sure that no contract prevents the government from performing ____.

options.A: audits
options.B: commissioning
options.C: inspections
options.D: value engineering
options.E: design reviews
options.F: terminations

questions.explanation: FAR Part 46 has agencies make sure contracts carry the inspection and quality requirements the government needs, that tendered supplies and services meet the contract, that government quality assurance happens before acceptance, and that no contract bars the government from performing inspections. Audit access comes from a separate access-to-records clause, and commissioning, value engineering and design reviews are not on this list.

questions.question: Under FAR 46.7, a warranty clause may not restrict the government's rights under an inspection clause with respect to three things. Name them: ____, ____, ____.
answers: gross mistakes that amount to fraud

mc.question: Under FAR 46.7, which three matters stay protected by the government's inspection-clause rights no matter what a warranty clause says?

options.A: Latent defects
options.B: Normal wear and tear
options.C: Fraud
options.D: Damage from improper maintenance
options.E: Gross mistakes amounting to fraud
options.F: Liquidated damages for late completion

questions.explanation: However a warranty clause is written, it cannot cut back the government's inspection-clause rights for latent defects, fraud, or gross mistakes amounting to fraud. A warranty's job is to set out each side's rights and duties for defective items and to encourage quality work. Wear and tear and poor maintenance are things warranties commonly exclude, and liquidated damages deal with delay, not defects.

questions.question: Under FAR 46.7, using a warranty in a government contract is not ____; a warranty's benefits must be in proportion to what it costs the government.

mc.question: Under FAR 46.7, using a warranty in a government contract is not ____; a warranty's benefits must be in proportion to what it costs the government.

options.A: optional
options.B: permitted
options.C: mandatory
options.D: enforceable after government acceptance
options.E: allowed in construction contracts
options.F: subject to a cost-benefit test

questions.explanation: Warranties in government contracts are optional: one is used only when its benefits are worth its cost to the government. When a warranty is used, it gives the government a contractual right to have defects corrected even after acceptance, for a stated time, use or event. Saying warranties are not permitted, not enforceable after acceptance or not allowed in construction contracts gets the rule backward.

questions.question: Under FAR 49.4, when the government ends all or part of a contract because the contractor has failed, or is expected to fail, to meet its contract obligations, the action is termination for ____.

mc.question: Under FAR 49.4, what is it called when the government ends all or part of a contract because the contractor has failed, or is expected to fail, to meet its contract obligations?

options.A: Termination for convenience
options.B: Termination for default
options.C: Suspension of the work
options.D: Liquidated damages
options.E: Equitable adjustment
options.F: Bilateral modification

questions.explanation: Termination for default rests on the contractor's actual or expected failure to perform; the government owes nothing for work not yet delivered and can recover advance and progress payments made for it. Termination for convenience needs no contractor failure, only the contracting officer's finding that ending the work serves the government. Private-sector documents call the default case termination for cause.

questions.question: Under FAR 49.502, the contracting officer may end all or part of a contract upon deciding that doing so is in the government's best interest, and the government pays only for services rendered up to the effective date. This is termination for ____.

mc.question: Under FAR 49.502, the contracting officer may end all or part of a contract upon deciding that doing so is in the government's best interest, paying only for services rendered up to the effective date. What is this called?

options.A: Termination for default
options.B: Termination for cause
options.C: Suspension of the work
options.D: Termination for convenience
options.E: Liquidated damages
options.F: Equitable adjustment

questions.explanation: Termination for convenience lets the government stop work whenever the contracting officer finds that doing so serves its interest, with no fault by the contractor; a Notice of Termination states the extent and effective date, and payment covers only services rendered until then. Termination for default, and its private-sector counterpart termination for cause, depend on the contractor's failure to perform, and a suspension only pauses the work.

questions.question: To end a federal contract for the government's convenience, the contracting officer delivers a document to the contractor stating how much of the contract is terminated and when the termination takes effect. This document is a ____.

mc.question: To end a federal contract for the government's convenience, the contracting officer delivers a document to the contractor stating how much of the contract is terminated and when the termination takes effect. This document is a ____.

options.A: Notice to Proceed
options.B: Notice of Award
options.C: change order
options.D: Notice of Termination
options.E: justification and approval
options.F: Certificate of Substantial Completion

questions.explanation: The contracting officer terminates by delivering a Notice of Termination that describes the extent of the termination and its effective date; the government then pays only for services rendered up to that date. A Notice of Award accepts a bid and a Notice to Proceed starts the contract times, so both belong to the start of a contract, and a change order alters the work rather than ending it.

questions.question: Under FAR Part 49, terminations are generally settled by one of three methods or a mix of them. Name them: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Under FAR Part 49, which three methods are generally used, alone or combined, to settle a terminated contract?

options.A: Negotiated agreement
options.B: Binding arbitration
options.C: Termination contracting officer (TCO) determination
options.D: Mediation
options.E: Costing out under Standard Form (SF) 1034
options.F: Litigation in a court of competent jurisdiction

questions.explanation: A terminated federal contract is settled by negotiated agreement, by determination of the termination contracting officer (TCO), by costing out under Standard Form 1034, or by a combination of these, and the TCO should seek a fair, prompt negotiated settlement whenever possible. Mediation, arbitration and litigation are ways to resolve disputes, as in AIA's documents, not the settlement methods FAR Part 49 lists.

questions.question: Under FAR 970.5232-3 (Access to Records and Reports), the contractor must retain the books, records and reports the contract requires for at least ____ after final payment and the closing of all pending matters.

mc.question: Under FAR 970.5232-3 (Access to Records and Reports), the contractor must retain the books, records and reports the contract requires for at least ____ after final payment and the closing of all pending matters.

options.A: one year
options.B: two years
options.C: three years
options.D: five years
options.E: seven years
options.F: ten years

questions.explanation: The access-to-records clause requires an acceptable cost accounting system, access to pertinent records for the owner, federal agencies and the Comptroller General so the government can audit and examine them, and retention of those records for at least three years after final payment once pending matters are closed. One year is the familiar private-sector correction period after substantial completion, which has nothing to do with record retention.

questions.question: FAR 970.5232-3 requires the contractor to give access to records pertinent to the contract so that the government can do four things with the information. Name them: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: FAR 970.5232-3 requires the contractor to give access to records pertinent to the contract. Which list gives the four things that access lets the government do with the information?

options.A: Auditing, examining, excerpting and retaining
options.B: Auditing, certifying, excerpting and transcribing
options.C: Approving, examining, excerpting and transcribing
options.D: Auditing, examining, publishing and transcribing
options.E: Auditing, examining, excerpting and transcribing
options.F: Auditing, examining, certifying and retaining

questions.explanation: The access clause lets the government audit, examine, make excerpts of and transcribe the contractor's books, documents, papers and records that bear directly on the contract, and the owner, federal agencies and the Comptroller General all share that access. Retaining the records for at least three years after final payment is the contractor's own duty, not a government right, and the clause gives no right to publish, certify or approve them.

questions.question: The FAR 25.2 requirement, based on a federal statute, that limits the construction materials a federal contractor may use to domestically produced ones is called ____.

mc.question: The FAR 25.2 requirement, based on a federal statute, that limits the construction materials a federal contractor may use to domestically produced ones is called ____.

options.A: Davis-Bacon Act
options.B: Trade Agreements Act
options.C: preference for American shipping
options.D: Buy American
options.E: Anti-Kickback Act
options.F: Contract Work Hours Standards

questions.explanation: Buy American, a federal statute applied through FAR 25.2, restricts construction materials to domestically produced ones through a two-part test of US manufacture plus domestic component content, with an exception for commercially available off-the-shelf items. The Davis-Bacon Act sets wage rates and the American-shipping preference covers transport; like Buy American they are social value provisions, but they do not govern where materials come from.

questions.question: Under the Buy American test for construction materials as standard specifying guidance states it, a material made in the United States that is not wholly or mostly iron or steel qualifies only if its domestic components cost more than ____ percent of the cost of all its components. (For iron or steel materials, foreign iron and steel must be under 5 percent of the cost.)

mc.question: Under the Buy American test for construction materials as standard specifying guidance states it, a material made in the United States that is not wholly or mostly iron or steel qualifies only if its domestic components cost more than ____ of the cost of all its components.

options.A: 5 percent
options.B: 25 percent
options.C: 40 percent
options.D: 55 percent
options.E: 85 percent
options.F: 95 percent

questions.explanation: The test has two parts: the material must be manufactured in the United States, and, unless it is mainly iron or steel, the cost of its domestic components must be more than 55 percent of total component cost. Iron and steel materials face a stricter rule, foreign iron and steel under 5 percent of cost, so 5 and 95 percent belong to that case. The FAR thresholds are revised from time to time, so confirm the current figure on a real project.

questions.question: Buy American makes an exception for material that sells in large quantities on the open market and is offered to the government unchanged, in the same form the public buys it. Such material is a ____ item, a narrower category than a commercial item in general.

mc.question: What does Buy American call material that sells in large quantities on the open market and is offered to the government unchanged, in the same form the public buys it?

options.A: A commercial item description (CID)
options.B: A commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) item
options.C: A basis-of-design product
options.D: A brand-name or equal product
options.E: A standard product
options.F: Foreign material approved by the government

questions.explanation: A commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) item is sold in substantial quantities commercially and offered to the government unmodified, in its commercial form, and such items are excepted from the Buy American domestic-content test. A commercial item description is a GSA document describing acceptable commercial products, not an exemption. Other foreign material needs the contractor's request and a government decision.

questions.question: ____ is often the common link between federal and private-sector specifications: most agencies organize their guide specifications by it, though their section numbers and titles sometimes differ from the current edition.

mc.question: ____ is often the common link between federal and private-sector specifications: most agencies organize their guide specifications by it, though their section numbers and titles sometimes differ from the current edition.

options.A: SectionFormat
options.B: MasterFormat
options.C: PageFormat
options.D: UniFormat
options.E: OmniClass
options.F: National CAD Standard

questions.explanation: MasterFormat links federal and private-sector specifications because most agencies use its numbers and titles to organize their guide specifications, even if some lag the current edition or depart from it on purpose. SectionFormat governs the arrangement inside each section, PageFormat the page layout, and UniFormat organizes by systems and assemblies rather than by work results.

questions.question: Most federal government guide specifications follow ____ for the structure within each section, even though their paragraph numbering may not use the alphanumeric arrangement PageFormat prefers.

mc.question: Most federal government guide specifications follow ____ for the structure within each section, even though their paragraph numbering may not use the alphanumeric arrangement PageFormat prefers.

options.A: MasterFormat
options.B: PageFormat
options.C: UniFormat
options.D: SectionFormat
options.E: OmniClass
options.F: National CAD Standard

questions.explanation: SectionFormat sets the three-part structure inside a section, and most government guide specifications conform to it; where they depart is paragraph numbering, since some agencies use a legal style of Arabic numerals instead of PageFormat's alphanumeric arrangement. MasterFormat organizes the sections themselves rather than their contents, and PageFormat governs page layout and numbering, the very place federal practice may differ.

questions.question: Instead of PageFormat's alphanumeric paragraph arrangement, some federal agencies number paragraphs and subparagraphs with Arabic numerals only (1.1, 1.1.1, 1.1.2.1), a numbering style known as ____ style.

mc.question: Instead of PageFormat's alphanumeric paragraph arrangement, some federal agencies number paragraphs and subparagraphs with Arabic numerals only (1.1, 1.1.1, 1.1.2.1), a numbering style known as ____ style.

options.A: alphanumeric
options.B: outline
options.C: Roman numeral
options.D: legal
options.E: streamlined
options.F: narrative

questions.explanation: Legal style numbers every paragraph and subparagraph with Arabic numerals joined by points, such as 1.1, 1.1.1 and 1.1.2.1, and some agencies use it in place of PageFormat's alphanumeric arrangement. Alphanumeric is the PageFormat arrangement itself, Roman numerals are discouraged in specifications, and streamlined, outline and narrative describe ways of writing specifications, not paragraph numbering.

questions.question: In almost every situation, federal agencies ____ specifying products by brand name, by manufacturer's name, or by any other proprietary or restrictive requirement.

mc.question: In almost every situation, federal agencies ____ specifying products by brand name, by manufacturer's name, or by any other proprietary or restrictive requirement.

options.A: require
options.B: encourage
options.C: prohibit
options.D: prefer
options.E: permit
options.F: recommend

questions.explanation: Federal agencies prohibit brand names and other restrictive product requirements in almost all cases, so that competition is unlimited and standard products and current models meet the project's needs. Brand names are allowed only under narrow exceptions, such as matching an existing system or listing at least three acceptable products while allowing others, which is why permit, prefer and encourage all misstate the rule.

questions.question: On a federal project, the procurement and construction phases of the contract are administered by the ____, a role the A/E would normally play in the private sector.

mc.question: On a federal project, the procurement and construction phases of the contract are administered by the ____, a role the A/E would normally play in the private sector.

options.A: architect/engineer (A/E)
options.B: initial decision maker
options.C: contracting officer
options.D: resident project representative
options.E: authority having jurisdiction
options.F: Comptroller General

questions.explanation: Under federal general conditions a contracting officer, either a military officer or a civilian government employee, administers the procurement and construction phases, so the A/E has less authority than on private work. The government is also owner and chief regulator, and local code officials have no jurisdiction on federal property. The initial decision maker and resident project representative are AIA and EJCDC roles.

questions.question: Federal contract provisions meant to help particular industries and special interest groups, such as wage rates, preference for American shipping, affirmative action, use of small businesses and the Buy American Act, are called ____ regulations.

mc.question: Federal contract provisions meant to help particular industries and special interest groups, such as wage rates, preference for American shipping, affirmative action, use of small businesses and the Buy American Act, are called ____ regulations.

options.A: labor standards
options.B: acquisition
options.C: quality assurance
options.D: general provisions
options.E: social value
options.F: accessibility

questions.explanation: Social value regulations use federal contracts to support particular industries and interest groups; besides those named, they include accessibility standards, labor standards, environmental rules and the use of businesses owned by minorities and women. Labor standards and accessibility standards are single members of the group, not its name, and General Provisions is one possible title for federal contract conditions.

questions.question: Federal projects settle contract disputes differently from the private sector. These methods usually do not directly affect the specifications, but they significantly affect the ____.

mc.question: Federal projects settle contract disputes differently from the private sector. These methods usually do not directly affect the specifications, but they significantly affect the ____.

options.A: technical specifications
options.B: product selection
options.C: contract administration
options.D: drawings
options.E: A/E selection
options.F: bid security

questions.explanation: Dispute-settlement methods are one of the ways federal general conditions differ from private ones, and their weight falls on contract administration, which the contracting officer runs, rather than on the specifications. Because the disputes process lives in the contract conditions, it usually leaves the technical sections, product selection and drawings untouched. Other federal differences include the contracting officer in place of the A/E and the government acting as both owner and primary regulator.

questions.question: Because the federal government buys no commercial insurance for its buildings or their contents, it is described as ____.

mc.question: Because the federal government buys no commercial insurance for its buildings or their contents, it is described as ____.

options.A: the primary regulating authority
options.B: an additional insured
options.C: self-insuring
options.D: indemnified by its contractors
options.E: bonded through a surety
options.F: covered by builder's risk insurance

questions.explanation: A self-insuring owner carries its own losses instead of buying commercial insurance, which is why federal guide specifications may be stricter than private ones on fire protection, safety, security and the durability of components and construction. The government is also the primary regulating authority, but that describes its code role, not how it covers losses. Additional insured status and builder's risk are forms of commercial insurance, and a surety bond backs the contractor's performance, not the owner's buildings.

questions.question: By prohibiting brand names and proprietary requirements, federal agencies aim to encourage ____ competition suited to the type and requirements of the work.

mc.question: By prohibiting brand names and proprietary requirements, federal agencies aim to encourage ____ competition suited to the type and requirements of the work.

options.A: limited
options.B: unlimited
options.C: prequalified
options.D: qualifications-based
options.E: domestic
options.F: negotiated

questions.explanation: The aim is unlimited competition suited to the work, using standard products and current models, and specifications should state only the government's actual minimum needs in a way that invites the widest practicable competition. Prequalification and qualifications-based selection narrow the field of bidders or proposers, and any domestic preference comes from Buy American, not from the brand-name rule.

questions.question: Local building code authorities have no jurisdiction on federal property, but local authorities having jurisdiction do have jurisdiction over ____ that federal agencies lease.

mc.question: Local building code authorities have no jurisdiction on federal property, but local authorities having jurisdiction do have jurisdiction over ____ that federal agencies lease.

options.A: federal property
options.B: private property
options.C: military facilities
options.D: GSA-owned buildings
options.E: National Park Service land
options.F: Postal Service-owned buildings

questions.explanation: On federal property local building code authorities have no jurisdiction, although other federal agencies may, and federal guide specifications may depart from or exceed local codes. Privately owned property that a federal agency leases is different: there the local authorities having jurisdiction keep their jurisdiction. Military facilities, GSA-owned buildings and park land are all federal property.

questions.question: To remove any chance that naming a brand in a federal specification will limit competition, the agency's contracting authority should add a two-word phrase after the brand name: ____.

mc.question: To remove any chance that naming a brand in a federal specification will limit competition, the agency's contracting authority should add a two-word phrase after the brand name: ____.

options.A: no substitutions
options.B: or approved equal
options.C: basis of design
options.D: or equal
options.E: salient characteristics
options.F: minimum requirements

questions.explanation: Whenever a federal specification names a brand, the agency's contracting authority should follow it with the two words 'or equal' so that equivalent products can compete. 'No substitutions' would close the specification, which federal policy avoids. A basis-of-design product is only a reference point, and salient characteristics are the features an equal product must match, not the phrase that opens the specification.

questions.question: Because the federal government is self-insuring, its guide specifications may set stricter requirements than the private sector does in four areas. Name them: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Because the federal government is self-insuring, its guide specifications may be stricter than private-sector ones in which four areas?

options.A: Fire protection, safety, security and energy efficiency
options.B: Fire protection, accessibility, security and durability
options.C: Acoustics, safety, security and durability
options.D: Fire protection, safety, aesthetics and durability
options.E: Energy efficiency, safety, accessibility and durability
options.F: Fire protection, safety, security and durability

questions.explanation: Since the government absorbs its own losses, its guide specifications may demand more than private ones for fire protection, safety, security, and the durability of components and construction, all of which reduce the risk of loss. Accessibility is a social value requirement, and energy efficiency, acoustics and aesthetics are design goals; none of them is the self-insurance reason for stricter federal requirements.

questions.question: Federal specifications may use brand names only under four exceptions. Name each by its key idea: ____, ____, ____, ____.
answers: no other feasible way to describe

mc.question: Which list gives the four exceptions under which federal specifications may use brand names?

options.A: No other feasible way to describe the essential characteristics; matching an existing system; names used only to set minimum salient characteristics; two acceptable products listed, with no others permitted
options.B: No other feasible way to describe the essential characteristics; the owner's preferred manufacturer; names used only to set minimum salient characteristics; at least three acceptable products listed, with others permitted
options.C: The product is the lowest-priced option; matching an existing system; names used only to set minimum salient characteristics; at least three acceptable products listed, with others permitted
options.D: No other feasible way to describe the essential characteristics; matching an existing system; names used only to set minimum salient characteristics; at least three acceptable products listed, with others permitted
options.E: No other feasible way to describe the essential characteristics; matching an existing system; the product is a basis-of-design selection; at least three acceptable products listed, with others permitted
options.F: The A/E's past experience with the product; matching an existing system; the product is a basis-of-design selection; at least three acceptable products listed, with others permitted

questions.explanation: Brand names are allowed only when there is no other feasible way to describe essential characteristics (a paint color, a stone's appearance, a high-technology product's performance); when new work must match an existing system; when a statement says the names only set minimum salient characteristics and equal products are allowed; or when at least three acceptable products are listed and others are permitted. Owner preference, low price, a basis-of-design choice or two listed products do not qualify.

questions.question: When a federal agency extends or connects to an existing system and must buy the matching brand, it prepares a ____ document to procure that one brand, often with technical input from the A/E.

mc.question: When a federal agency extends or connects to an existing system and must buy the matching brand, it prepares a ____ document to procure that one brand, often with technical input from the A/E.

options.A: substitution request
options.B: request for information (RFI)
options.C: justification and approval (J&A)
options.D: commercial item description (CID)
options.E: change order proposal request
options.F: Notice of Award

questions.explanation: Matching an existing system is one of the few cases where a federal agency may buy a specific brand, and the agency documents it with a justification and approval to procure that one brand, with the A/E often supplying technical input. A substitution request works the other way, asking to use something other than the specified product, and a commercial item description describes acceptable commercial products generically.

questions.question: In federal work, a specification that limits the contractor to one product, identified by brand name and model number, is the exception: it is used only when no other product can do the job, and only with the A/E's technical justification, which the agency approves or rejects. Of the four specifying methods, this is the ____ specification.

mc.question: In federal work, a specification that limits the contractor to one product, identified by brand name and model number, is used only when no other product can do the job and only with the A/E's technical justification. Which of the four specifying methods is it?

options.A: Descriptive
options.B: Performance
options.C: Reference standard
options.D: Proprietary
options.E: Generic
options.F: Sole-source

questions.explanation: Naming one product by brand and model is proprietary specifying, one of the four methods along with descriptive, performance and reference standard. Federal specifications are normally generic, so a proprietary requirement needs the A/E's technical justification and the agency's approval. Sole source describes the result, a single supplier that may take advantage of its position, rather than a specifying method.

questions.question: Government construction specifications draw on four classifications of reference standards. In order of preference, name them: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list gives the four classifications of reference standards for government construction, in order of preferred use?

options.A: Private-sector standards, commercial item descriptions, federal specifications, proprietary specifications
options.B: Building codes, commercial item descriptions, federal specifications, military specifications
options.C: Private-sector standards, commercial item descriptions, federal specifications, military specifications
options.D: Private-sector standards, manufacturers' literature, federal specifications, military specifications
options.E: Private-sector standards, commercial item descriptions, agency guide specifications, military specifications
options.F: Manufacturers' standards, commercial item descriptions, Unified Facilities Guide Specifications, military specifications

questions.explanation: The preferred order runs from private-sector standards to commercial item descriptions (CIDs), then federal specifications, and last military specifications. Government policy favors non-government standards from bodies such as ASTM, NFPA and ANSI, and many federal specifications are being replaced by them or by CIDs. Building codes, manufacturers' literature, proprietary specifications and agency guide specifications are not among the four classes.

questions.question: Federal regulations (41 CFR 101-28) define a simplified, indexed description of available commercial products the government finds acceptable, written in terms of their function or performance. This document is a ____.

mc.question: Federal regulations (41 CFR 101-28) define a simplified, indexed description of available commercial products the government finds acceptable, written in terms of their function or performance. This document is a ____.

options.A: federal specification
options.B: military specification (MIL-SPEC)
options.C: private-sector standard
options.D: guide specification
options.E: commercial item description (CID)
options.F: commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) item

questions.explanation: A commercial item description (CID) is a short, indexed GSA document that describes acceptable commercial products by function or performance and often references ASTM, ANSI and other industry standards. CIDs rank second in preferred use, after private-sector standards and ahead of federal and military specifications. A COTS item is a product sold commercially in unmodified form, not a document that describes products.

questions.question: Commercial item description (CID) documents are issued and controlled by the ____.

mc.question: Commercial item description (CID) documents are issued and controlled by the ____.

options.A: Department of Defense (DOD)
options.B: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)
options.C: General Services Administration (GSA)
options.D: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
options.E: ASTM International
options.F: Comptroller General of the United States

questions.explanation: The GSA issues and controls CIDs, and its Federal Supply Service also issues federal specifications and standards. Military specifications come from the Department of Defense, ASTM International is a private-sector standards developer whose standards CIDs often reference, and the Comptroller General's role in federal contracts is access to contractor records, not standards.

questions.question: By definition, a ____ contract is with a single source, so the brand-name item is identified, and its justification completed, before that contract is awarded. (Give the contract type, not just 'single-source'.)

mc.question: By definition, a ____ contract is with a single source, so the brand-name item is identified, and its justification completed, before that contract is awarded.

options.A: multiple-award
options.B: cost-reimbursement
options.C: letter
options.D: requirements
options.E: incrementally funded
options.F: fixed-price

questions.explanation: A requirements contract, also called a single-award contract, is with one source, so the need for that source's brand-name item is settled before the primary contract is awarded and the brand-name justification must be finished first. A multiple-award contract offers products from many sources, so its justification comes later, when an order is placed. Cost-reimbursement, letter and fixed-price describe pricing or form, not the number of sources.

questions.question: Under a multiple-award contract, which offers buyers products from many sources, the need for one manufacturer's brand-name item, and its justification, are settled at the time of the ____, not when the multiple-award contract is placed.

mc.question: Under a multiple-award contract, which offers buyers products from many sources, the need for one manufacturer's brand-name item, and its justification, are settled at the time of the ____, not when the multiple-award contract is placed.

options.A: contract award
options.B: bid opening
options.C: solicitation
options.D: order
options.E: final payment
options.F: contract closeout

questions.explanation: A brand name appearing on a multiple-award contract does not mean it is the only such item available, so the need for one manufacturer's brand is fixed, and justified, when the order is placed. With a requirements contract the single source is known up front, so the justification is completed before that contract is awarded. Either way, the justification happens when the brand-name requirement is determined.

questions.question: Federal specifications and standards are issued by the GSA's ____ and cover a wide range of items the federal government uses, including some construction products.

mc.question: Which body issues federal specifications and standards, which cover a wide range of items the federal government uses, including some construction products?

options.A: The Department of Defense
options.B: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
options.C: ASTM International
options.D: The GSA Federal Supply Service
options.E: The National Institute of Building Sciences
options.F: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration

questions.explanation: Federal specifications (FED) and federal standards (FED-STD) come from the GSA Federal Supply Service and cover many kinds of items the government buys, only some of them construction products; they rank third in preferred use. The Department of Defense issues military specifications, and ASTM International is one of the private-sector developers whose standards are replacing many federal specifications.

questions.question: Federal specifications and standards usually appear as references within PART ____ of a specification section.

mc.question: Within which part of a specification section do federal specifications and standards usually appear as references?

options.A: PART 3—EXECUTION
options.B: The bid form
options.C: PART 2—PRODUCTS
options.D: The supplementary conditions
options.E: The instructions to bidders
options.F: The drawing schedules

questions.explanation: Federal specifications describe products, so they are cited in PART 2—PRODUCTS, usually with the class or grade of the product stated, since most are classification documents. PART 3 covers execution of the work, and the bid form, instructions to bidders, supplementary conditions and drawing schedules are not where a section's product requirements are written.

questions.question: A federal client's master guide specifications number and title some sections differently from the current MasterFormat. Whose numbers and titles is the A/E usually expected to use? Those defined by the ____.

mc.question: A federal client's master guide specifications number and title some sections differently from the current MasterFormat. Whose numbers and titles is the A/E usually expected to use?

options.A: Those of the current MasterFormat edition
options.B: Those of the A/E's office master specification
options.C: Those defined by the client agency
options.D: Those of the specification software publisher
options.E: Those chosen by the contractor
options.F: Those required by the local authority having jurisdiction

questions.explanation: Where an agency's specifications differ from MasterFormat, the A/E normally follows the agency's own section numbers and titles. Many agencies developed their own guide specifications for their needs, and the more those differ from the A/E's office master, the more time the project specifications take. Using current MasterFormat numbers or the office master instead would put the documents out of step with the agency.

questions.question: Most federal specifications set requirement levels for the product they describe and grade it by its physical and functional characteristics, which makes them ____ documents.

mc.question: Most federal specifications set requirement levels for the product they describe and grade it by its physical and functional characteristics, which makes them ____ documents.

options.A: performance
options.B: proprietary
options.C: classification
options.D: guide
options.E: outline
options.F: procurement

questions.explanation: Most federal specifications are classification documents: they set requirement levels and sort a product into classes or grades by its physical and functional characteristics, so a specifier citing one usually has to name the class or grade wanted. Military specifications are organized the same way, by type and quality classes. Performance specifications state required results instead, and proprietary ones name products.

questions.question: When military specifications would be used in non-military construction, current Department of Defense policy is to convert them to ____ standards or federal specifications.

mc.question: When military specifications would be used in non-military construction, current Department of Defense policy is to convert them to ____ standards or federal specifications.

options.A: military
options.B: proprietary
options.C: private-sector
options.D: agency-unique
options.E: local building code
options.F: foreign government

questions.explanation: Military specifications describe products for military needs, either items unique to the military or commercial products modified for it, and they rank last in preferred use. For non-military construction DOD converts them to private-sector standards, such as those of ASTM, NFPA or ANSI, or to federal specifications. Proprietary or agency-unique requirements would run against federal policy favoring non-government standards.

questions.question: Military specifications (MIL-SPEC), which describe the physical and operational characteristics of products used for military needs, are issued by the ____.

mc.question: Military specifications (MIL-SPEC), which describe the physical and operational characteristics of products used for military needs, are issued by the ____.

options.A: General Services Administration (GSA)
options.B: Department of Defense (DOD)
options.C: GSA Federal Supply Service
options.D: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)
options.E: ASTM International
options.F: National Institute of Building Sciences (NIBS)

questions.explanation: The US Department of Defense issues military specifications, which cover items made only for the military as well as commercial items adapted for military use and are organized by type and quality classes. The GSA issues commercial item descriptions, and its Federal Supply Service issues federal specifications and standards. ASTM International is a private-sector standards developer.

questions.question: When a federal agency supplies its own procurement and contracting requirements and the A/E writes the rest of the specifications, the content of ____ may differ greatly from the same division prepared for a private-sector project.

mc.question: When a federal agency supplies its own procurement and contracting requirements and the A/E writes the rest of the specifications, which division's content may differ greatly from the same division prepared for a private-sector project?

options.A: Division 02—Existing Conditions
options.B: Division 03—Concrete
options.C: Division 01—General Requirements
options.D: Division 08—Openings
options.E: Division 09—Finishes
options.F: Division 26—Electrical

questions.explanation: Division 01 expands on the administrative and procedural provisions of the conditions of the contract, so when the agency supplies its own procurement and contracting documents, a federal Division 01 can look very different from a private-sector one, and the A/E must learn the agency's procedures before writing it. Technical divisions such as Concrete or Finishes specify the work itself rather than building on the contract conditions.

questions.question: One item to settle when negotiating the A/E's fee for a federal project: will the agency furnish the ____ documents, or must the A/E write them?

mc.question: One item to settle when negotiating the A/E's fee for a federal project: will the agency furnish the ____ documents, or must the A/E write them?

options.A: reference
options.B: shop drawing
options.C: front-end
options.D: record
options.E: operation and maintenance
options.F: warranty

questions.explanation: Fee negotiation for federal work should settle whether the agency supplies the front-end documents, meaning the procurement and contracting requirements, or the A/E must write them, along with the guide specifications' form, the number of reviews and copies, review times, page format and typeface. Reference standards raise a different question, whether the agency provides copies or pays for them. Shop drawings, record documents, O&M data and warranties come from the contractor.

questions.question: The number of agency reviews affects the A/E's fee. During design, the agency often wants reviews at four milestones. Name them: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: During design of a federal project, at which four milestones does the agency often want specification reviews?

options.A: 30 percent, 60 percent, 90 percent and final completion
options.B: 30 percent, 50 percent, 90 percent and substantial completion
options.C: Schematic design, design development, construction documents and bidding
options.D: 35 percent, 50 percent, 95 percent and final completion
options.E: 30 percent, 50 percent, 90 percent and final completion
options.F: 15 percent, 50 percent, 75 percent and final completion

questions.explanation: Agencies often review the specifications at 30 percent (a section list or outline specifications), 50 percent (marked-up guide specifications or a rough draft), 90 percent (a resubmittal or final draft) and final completion (the final typed copy), after which the agency advertises for bids. The milestones are percentages of design rather than private-sector phase names, and the last is final completion, not substantial completion, which is a construction milestone.

questions.question: Federal agency guide specifications must be edited for each project. They are usually written for ____ construction, so they may need considerable changes for repair or rehabilitation projects.

mc.question: Federal agency guide specifications must be edited for each project. They are usually written for ____ construction, so they may need considerable changes for repair or rehabilitation projects.

options.A: renovation
options.B: tenant improvement
options.C: new
options.D: design-build
options.E: fast-track
options.F: phased

questions.explanation: Agency guide specifications are guides written mostly for new construction, so the A/E must edit them for each project and may have to rework them heavily for repair or rehabilitation. Where they lack coverage, the A/E supplies material in a form the agency approves. Renovation and tenant improvement work need the most editing rather than being what the guides assume, and design-build, fast-track and phased describe delivery or scheduling, not the type of construction.

questions.question: Many federal agencies issue their own guide specifications to A/E firms. The agency noted for using a commercially available master guide specification system instead is the ____.

mc.question: Many federal agencies issue their own guide specifications to A/E firms. Which agency is noted for using a commercially available master guide specification system instead?

options.A: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE)
options.B: Naval Facilities Engineering Command (NAVFAC)
options.C: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)
options.D: Veterans Administration (VA)
options.E: General Services Administration (GSA)
options.F: United States Postal Service (USPS)

questions.explanation: The GSA uses a commercially available master guide specification system rather than one written by the government. The Army Corps of Engineers, NAVFAC, the Air Force Civil Engineer Center and NASA instead publish the Unified Facilities Guide Specifications jointly, distributed through the WBDG Federal Facility Criteria and edited with NASA's SpecsIntact software.

questions.question: The WBDG Federal Facility Criteria, which grew out of a study of problems in publishing federal master guide specifications for construction, started out as the ____.

mc.question: The WBDG Federal Facility Criteria, which grew out of a study of problems in publishing federal master guide specifications for construction, started out as the ____.

options.A: Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS)
options.B: SpecsIntact
options.C: Construction Criteria Base (CCB)
options.D: Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC)
options.E: Federal Supply Service
options.F: National CAD Standard

questions.explanation: The online WBDG Federal Facility Criteria began as the Construction Criteria Base (CCB), created after a study of the trouble agencies had publishing their master guide specifications. Today it distributes the Unified Facilities Guide Specifications, the SpecsIntact software and other agencies' criteria, such as DOD's Unified Facilities Criteria, so those are its contents rather than its origin.

questions.question: Name the four purposes of the WBDG Federal Facility Criteria: ____, ____, ____, ____.
answers: decrease overlap and conflicts among criteria
improve dissemination of master guide specifications

mc.question: Which list gives the four purposes of the WBDG Federal Facility Criteria?

options.A: Improve construction quality; reduce overlap and conflicts among criteria; speed new technology into construction; lower A/E design fees
options.B: Improve construction quality; replace private-sector standards with federal ones; speed new technology into construction; improve dissemination of master guide specifications
options.C: Lower construction costs; reduce overlap and conflicts among criteria; speed new technology into construction; improve dissemination of master guide specifications
options.D: Improve construction quality; reduce overlap and conflicts among criteria; certify federal specifiers; improve dissemination of master guide specifications
options.E: Lower construction costs; reduce overlap and conflicts among criteria; certify federal specifiers; enforce local building codes
options.F: Improve construction quality; reduce overlap and conflicts among criteria; speed new technology into construction; improve dissemination of master guide specifications

questions.explanation: The WBDG Federal Facility Criteria exists to improve construction quality, cut overlap and conflict among criteria, bring new technology into construction faster, and spread master guide specifications and other design and construction documents more widely, putting information in users' hands quickly and cheaply. It does not set fees, certify people, enforce local codes or replace private-sector standards, which federal policy in fact favors.

questions.question: The free automated system NASA created for developing construction project specifications, in which UFGS and NASA specifications are formatted for editing and embedded notes are deleted at printing, is ____.

mc.question: The free automated system NASA created for developing construction project specifications, in which UFGS and NASA specifications are formatted for editing and embedded notes are deleted at printing, is ____.

options.A: MasterSpec
options.B: SpecLink
options.C: SpecsIntact
options.D: SpecText
options.E: Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS)
options.F: Construction Criteria Base (CCB)

questions.explanation: SpecsIntact, short for 'specifications kept intact,' is NASA's free software for editing UFGS and NASA guide specifications: it checks references and submittals, generates submittal lists, renumbers paragraphs, builds tables of contents and strips the embedded editing notes when printing. MasterSpec, SpecText and SpecLink are commercial master guide specification systems, and the UFGS are the specifications it edits, not the software.

questions.question: The Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS) are published through a joint effort of four organizations. Name them: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: The Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS) are published through a joint effort of which four organizations?

options.A: US Army Corps of Engineers, Naval Facilities Engineering Command, General Services Administration, NASA
options.B: US Army Corps of Engineers, Naval Facilities Engineering Command, Air Force Civil Engineer Center, NASA
options.C: General Services Administration, Naval Facilities Engineering Command, Air Force Civil Engineer Center, NASA
options.D: US Army Corps of Engineers, Naval Facilities Engineering Command, Air Force Civil Engineer Center, Department of Veterans Affairs
options.E: US Army Corps of Engineers, Department of Housing and Urban Development, Air Force Civil Engineer Center, NASA
options.F: US Army Corps of Engineers, National Park Service, General Services Administration, NASA

questions.explanation: The UFGS are produced jointly by four federal bodies: NAVFAC (the Naval Facilities Engineering Command), the Army Corps of Engineers, NASA and the Air Force Civil Engineer Center; they are distributed through the WBDG Federal Facility Criteria together with the SpecsIntact editing software. Other federal agencies, such as the General Services Administration, HUD and Veterans Affairs, handle their specifications in their own ways and are not UFGS publishers.

questions.question: Through the WBDG Federal Facility Criteria, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) provides ____ standards along with NIST criteria.

mc.question: Through the WBDG Federal Facility Criteria, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) provides NIST criteria along with which documents?

options.A: Unified Facilities Criteria
options.B: Federal Green Construction Guide for Specifiers
options.C: Voluntary product standards
options.D: Standards for the Treatment of Historic Properties
options.E: FEMA design guides
options.F: Accessibility guidelines and standards

questions.explanation: On the WBDG Federal Facility Criteria, NIST supplies voluntary product standards alongside its own NIST criteria. Each other agency listed there contributes something different: the Department of Defense the Unified Facilities Criteria, EPA the green construction guide for specifiers, the National Park Service its standards for treating historic properties, the US Access Board its accessibility guidelines, and Homeland Security the FEMA design guides.

questions.question: On the WBDG Federal Facility Criteria, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) design guides and documents are provided under the ____.

mc.question: On the WBDG Federal Facility Criteria, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) design guides and documents are provided under which federal department?

options.A: Department of Defense
options.B: Department of Homeland Security
options.C: Department of the Interior
options.D: Department of Housing and Urban Development
options.E: Department of Transportation
options.F: Department of Veterans Affairs

questions.explanation: FEMA is part of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), so the WBDG Federal Facility Criteria lists the FEMA design guides and documents under DHS. The Department of Defense appears there for its Unified Facilities Criteria, and the Department of the Interior is the parent of the National Park Service, whose historic-preservation standards are listed separately.

questions.question: When editing an agency's master guide specification, the entire section, not just the ____ text, should be read and edited.

mc.question: Which guideline applies when editing an agency's master guide specification for a project?

options.A: Keep the index at the front of each section in the issued specification.
options.B: Leave the editing notes in the issued text for the contractor's guidance.
options.C: Read and edit the entire section, not just the bracketed text.
options.D: Keep every standard the master lists in the References article.
options.E: Keep the master's revision notations and other identification markings.
options.F: Leave proofreading to the agency's reviewers.

questions.explanation: Agency master guide specifications are only guides, so the whole section must be read against the project, not just the choices in brackets: make every selection, fill every blank and check the text around them. The other guidelines run the opposite way: incorporate and then remove editing notes, trim References to the standards still cited, delete the master's identification markings and its index, and proofread instead of relying on agency reviewers.

questions.question: When editing an agency's master guide specification, paragraphs should not be selected by ____ alone.

mc.question: When editing an agency's master guide specification, paragraphs should not be selected on the basis of which feature alone?

options.A: Their paragraph number
options.B: Their editing note
options.C: Their title
options.D: Their revision notation
options.E: Their bracketed choices
options.F: Their cited reference standards

questions.explanation: A paragraph's title names only its subject; the requirements written beneath it may or may not fit the project, so each paragraph has to be read before it is kept or deleted. Editing notes, by contrast, exist to guide these choices, and their applicable requirements should be worked into the text, while bracketed choices and cited standards are things the editor must resolve, not shortcuts for selecting paragraphs.

questions.question: Four types of specifications are meant for use by bidders, proposers and contractors, unlike preliminary project descriptions and outline specifications: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which four types of specifications are meant for use by bidders, proposers and contractors, as opposed to preliminary project descriptions and outline specifications?

options.A: Narrative, sheet, shortform and full-length specifications
options.B: Narrative, sheet, outline and full-length specifications
options.C: Narrative, sheet, shortform and performance specifications
options.D: Preliminary project descriptions, sheet, shortform and full-length specifications
options.E: Narrative, master guide, shortform and full-length specifications
options.F: Outline, sheet, shortform and proprietary specifications

questions.explanation: The four types meant for bidders, proposers and contractors are narrative, sheet, shortform and full-length specifications, each with its own content and format. Preliminary project descriptions and outline specifications are early design documents, master guide specifications are office or agency starting texts, and performance and proprietary are methods of specifying rather than types of specification documents.

questions.question: Ranked from least to most detailed, the written descriptions of a project fall into two groups: documents that are not contract documents and documents that are. The two less detailed ones, which are not contract documents, are ____ and ____.

mc.question: Ranked by level of detail, which two written documents are the less detailed ones that are not contract documents?

options.A: Drawing notes
options.B: Preliminary project descriptions
options.C: Shortform specifications
options.D: Outline specifications
options.E: Full-length specifications
options.F: Sheet specifications

questions.explanation: Preliminary project descriptions and outline specifications record early design decisions to help the design progress and support cost estimates; neither is meant to serve as a contract document. Drawing notes, shortform specifications and full-length specifications are all contract documents, from brief notes on the drawings to a complete project manual, and sheet specifications printed on the drawings are likewise issued for bidding and construction.

questions.question: Outline specifications, which record the A/E's early decisions on materials, products and general level of quality, are usually prepared during the ____ phase.

mc.question: Outline specifications, which record the A/E's early decisions on materials, products and general level of quality, are usually prepared during which phase?

options.A: Schematic design
options.B: Construction documents
options.C: Design development
options.D: Pre-design
options.E: Procurement
options.F: Construction

questions.explanation: Outline specifications usually belong to design development, when materials and products are being actively selected, and they help advance the design and update cost estimates. They are used earlier, in schematic design, only when the owner asks for them or the A/E knows the building type well; the preliminary project description is the usual schematic design document, and the full specifications follow in construction documents.

questions.question: A shortform master guide specification still uses the three-part SectionFormat, but with no more than ____ levels of paragraphs under each article.

mc.question: A shortform master guide specification still uses the three-part SectionFormat. At most, how many levels of paragraphs should it use under each article?

options.A: One
options.B: Two
options.C: Three
options.D: Four
options.E: Five
options.F: Six

questions.explanation: A shortform format keeps the three-part SectionFormat headings as organizing markers but limits each article to two paragraph levels, so the brief descriptions stay easy to read. A third level is tolerated now and then for lists of items but is best avoided, which makes three the tempting wrong answer; deeper nesting defeats the purpose of a short form.

questions.question: Before writing a section, the specifier needs two kinds of information: the specific project requirements (from the owner, the drawings, the PPD, codes), and ____ about the products and construction methods (from manufacturers, trade associations, standards organizations).

mc.question: Before writing a section, the specifier needs the specific project requirements plus a second kind of information about the products and construction methods, drawn from manufacturers, trade associations and standards organizations. What is that second kind called?

options.A: Shop drawings
options.B: Record documents
options.C: Reference materials
options.D: Procurement requirements
options.E: Addenda
options.F: Closeout submittals

questions.explanation: The second kind of information is reference material about the products and methods in the section being written: manufacturers' product data and guide specifications, trade association literature and reference standards. Shop drawings, closeout submittals and record documents come from the contractor during and after construction, and procurement requirements and addenda govern bidding, so none of them can inform a section before it is written.

questions.question: When a basis-of-design product is named, the definition of the term, and how comparable products will be accepted if they are permitted, belongs in Division ____.

mc.question: When a basis-of-design product is named, where should the definition of the term, and how comparable products will be accepted if they are permitted, be stated?

options.A: Division 00 instructions for procurement
options.B: Division 01 General Requirements
options.C: The supplementary conditions
options.D: The agreement form
options.E: PART 2 of each product section
options.F: The drawing general notes

questions.explanation: The definition of basis-of-design products, and the rules for accepting comparable products where they are allowed, apply across the whole project, so they are stated once in Division 01 General Requirements. Repeating them in PART 2 of every product section breaks the principle of saying it once and in the right place, and the agreement, supplementary conditions and procurement instructions are not where product requirements for the work are defined.

questions.question: Name UniFormat's four Level 1 categories lettered A through D: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list gives UniFormat's Level 1 categories lettered A through D, in order?

options.A: Substructure, Superstructure, Interiors, Services
options.B: Foundations, Shell, Interiors, Services
options.C: Substructure, Shell, Interiors, Services
options.D: Substructure, Exterior Vertical Enclosures, Interiors, Services
options.E: Substructure, Shell, Interiors, Equipment and Furnishings
options.F: Substructure, Shell, Conveying, Services

questions.explanation: After an unlettered Project Description, UniFormat's Level 1 categories run Substructure, Shell, Interiors and Services; the later lettered categories cover equipment and furnishings, special construction and demolition, and building sitework, with Z General last. Foundations, Superstructure, Exterior Vertical Enclosures and Conveying are Level 2 classes inside those categories, not Level 1 categories.

questions.question: UniFormat divides each Level 1 category into classes by separating it into the parts that compose it, a method information specialists call ____.

mc.question: UniFormat divides each Level 1 category into classes by separating it into the parts that compose it. What do information specialists call this method of classifying?

options.A: Faceted classification
options.B: Composition
options.C: Indexing
options.D: Decomposition
options.E: Pure classification
options.F: Cross-referencing

questions.explanation: Breaking a category down into the parts that make it up is called decomposition; in UniFormat it yields Level 2 classes such as A10, Level 3 classes such as A1010, and Level 4 entries with two more digits after a decimal point. Faceted and pure classification describe the multifaceted structure of OmniClass and Uniclass, a different kind of system, and composition is the reverse of breaking a whole into its parts.

questions.question: UniFormat can organize three kinds of information in the early stages of a facility's life cycle: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which three things can UniFormat be used to organize in the early stages of a facility's life cycle?

options.A: Preliminary project descriptions
options.B: Identification of the details within a set of drawings
options.C: Preliminary cost estimates
options.D: Procurement and contracting documents
options.E: Drawing detail filing
options.F: Contractor's shop drawing submittals

questions.explanation: UniFormat arranges information by systems and assemblies, which suits preliminary project descriptions, preliminary cost estimates and an office's library of drawing details, since a detail usually shows an assembly of many materials. It is meant for filing details internally, not for identifying the details in a project's drawing set; procurement and contracting documents take MasterFormat Division 00 numbers, and shop drawings are a construction-phase submittal.

questions.question: When elemental (systems and assemblies) performance specifications are included in a project manual, they go in Section ____, in an order taken from UniFormat's categories.

mc.question: When elemental (systems and assemblies) performance specifications are included in a project manual, which MasterFormat section holds them, in an order taken from UniFormat's categories?

options.A: 01 42 00 References
options.B: 01 60 00 Product Requirements
options.C: 01 40 00 Quality Requirements
options.D: 01 80 00 Performance Requirements
options.E: 01 35 00 Special Procedures
options.F: 01 10 00 Summary
