questions.explanation: Section 01 80 00 Performance Requirements is MasterFormat's place for elemental performance specifications, arranged by UniFormat categories so that system requirements can be stated without naming products. 01 60 00 Product Requirements holds general product rules, 01 40 00 Quality Requirements groups quality assurance and quality control, and 01 42 00 References is where reference standard organizations and abbreviations can be defined.

questions.question: Name the four methods of specifying: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list names the four methods of specifying?

options.A: Descriptive, prescriptive, reference standard, proprietary
options.B: Descriptive, performance, prescriptive, proprietary
options.C: Prescriptive, performance, reference standard, proprietary
options.D: Descriptive, performance, reference standard, nonrestrictive
options.E: Descriptive, performance, reference standard, proprietary
options.F: Narrative, performance, reference standard, proprietary

questions.explanation: The four methods are descriptive, performance, reference standard and proprietary, and a single section may combine several of them. Prescriptive is not a fifth method but a label for specifications that fix products and processes rather than results; nonrestrictive is a goal that public owners require and any method can serve, and narrative is a type of specification document.

questions.question: Two of the four specifying methods are always prescriptive, specifying products and processes rather than results: ____ and ____.

mc.question: Which two specifying methods are always prescriptive, specifying products and processes rather than results?

options.A: Descriptive and performance
options.B: Proprietary and reference standard
options.C: Descriptive and proprietary
options.D: Performance and reference standard
options.E: Descriptive and reference standard
options.F: Performance and proprietary

questions.explanation: Descriptive specifying spells out the materials and workmanship, and proprietary specifying names the products, so both fix the means and leave the results unstated, which is what prescriptive means. Reference standard specifying can serve either prescriptive or performance specifications, depending on the standard cited, and performance specifying states the required results and leaves the means to the contractor.

questions.question: Proprietary specifications come in two forms, distinguished by how they handle substitutions: ____ proprietary and ____ proprietary.

mc.question: Proprietary specifications come in two forms, distinguished by how they handle substitutions. Which two words name those forms, each followed by 'proprietary'?

options.A: Sole-source
options.B: Closed
options.C: Nonrestrictive
options.D: Open
options.E: Or-equal
options.F: Prescriptive

questions.explanation: A closed proprietary specification names one product, or several as options, and generally bars substitutions; an open proprietary specification names products but lets bidders propose substitutions for the A/E to approve. Sole source describes a product only one supplier can provide, 'or equal' is a phrase sometimes added after product names, and nonrestrictive is a public-agency requirement, so none of them names one of the two forms.

questions.question: There are three forms of open proprietary specification: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which three are forms of open proprietary specification?

options.A: Requested alternates
options.B: Optional products
options.C: Proposed substitutions
options.D: Cash allowances
options.E: Controlled substitutions
options.F: Single named product

questions.explanation: Open proprietary specifications let other products in three ways: requested alternates (alternate products named in the specifications and priced on the bid form), proposed substitutions (none named, but bidders may offer substitutes with the cost difference) and controlled substitutions (named products, with substitutions under Section 01 25 13). Optional products and a single named product are closed forms that bar substitutes, and cash allowances are a pricing device.

questions.question: Besides a citation of the applicable requirements (unless the whole standard applies), a complete reference standard designation includes four items: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Besides a citation of the applicable requirements (unless the whole standard applies), which four items make up a complete reference standard designation?

options.A: Issuing organization's name, standard number, standard title, issue date
options.B: Issuing organization's name, standard number, standard title, website address
options.C: Issuing organization's name, standard number, issue date, website address
options.D: Standard number, standard title, issue date, testing laboratory
options.E: Issuing organization's name, standard title, issue date, approving authority
options.F: Issuing organization's name, standard number, standard title, adopting code

questions.explanation: A designation has to set each standard apart from all the others: the issuing organization's name, the standard's number, its title and its date of issue, plus the applicable requirements when only part of it applies. Website addresses may be added to the PART 1 References list for convenience but are not part of the designation, and the date matters because standards are revised periodically.

questions.question: When a descriptive specification is used, the burden of performance is assumed by the ____.

mc.question: When a descriptive specification is used, who assumes the burden of performance?

options.A: The contractor
options.B: The owner
options.C: The A/E (architect/engineer)
options.D: The manufacturer
options.E: The installer
options.F: The testing agency

questions.explanation: A descriptive specification tells the contractor exactly what to provide, such as a concrete mix by its proportions, so if work built exactly as described fails to perform, the A/E who wrote the description bears the responsibility. Under a performance specification the contractor must achieve the stated result, which is why the contractor is the tempting but wrong answer here.

questions.question: A standard approved by its sponsoring organization but still awaiting final approval by its membership is listed as ____; authorities having jurisdiction usually don't accept such standards.

mc.question: A standard that its sponsoring organization has approved but that still awaits final approval by its membership is listed as what?

options.A: Voluntary
options.B: Adopted
options.C: Withdrawn
options.D: Tentative
options.E: Mandatory
options.F: Superseded

questions.explanation: A tentative standard has passed its sponsor but not the final approval of its members or other stakeholders, so it reflects current thinking but has no official status; authorities having jurisdiction usually reject it and the A/E should cite it with caution. Voluntary describes reference standards in general, as opposed to mandatory codes, and adopted describes a standard that a code has taken in.

questions.question: To make a proprietary specification nonrestrictive, public agencies usually require a minimum of ____ brand names followed by 'or equal', plus the item's salient characteristics.

mc.question: To make a proprietary specification nonrestrictive, public agencies usually require at least how many brand names followed by 'or equal', plus the item's salient characteristics?

options.A: Two
options.B: Three
options.C: Four
options.D: Five
options.E: One
options.F: Six

questions.explanation: Public agencies usually ask for at least three brand names with 'or equal' and the item's salient characteristics, which gives a basis for judging whether another product is equal. Naming a single product is closed specifying, and simply deleting the brand name while copying the manufacturer's listed qualities still produces a closed proprietary specification dressed up as a performance specification.

questions.question: An alternate is something named in the documents for which alternative pricing is requested; something requested to replace a specified item is a ____.

mc.question: An alternate is something named in the documents for which alternative pricing is requested. What is something requested to replace a specified item called?

options.A: Alternate
options.B: Allowance
options.C: Unit price
options.D: Product option
options.E: Substitute
options.F: Basis-of-design product

questions.explanation: A substitute is a product someone asks to use in place of the one specified, while an alternate is named in the documents and priced separately, usually on the bid form; the two terms are often confused. Allowances and unit prices are pricing methods, and product options are choices the documents already permit, so none of them replaces a specified item by request.

questions.question: Adding 'or equal' after proprietary names is redundant when the project manual contains a comprehensive Section ____.

mc.question: Adding 'or equal' after proprietary names is redundant when the project manual contains which comprehensive section?

options.A: 01 62 00 Product Options
options.B: 01 25 13 Product Substitution Procedures
options.C: 01 60 00 Product Requirements
options.D: 01 42 00 References
options.E: 01 26 00 Contract Modification Procedures
options.F: 01 23 00 Alternates

questions.explanation: When Section 01 25 13 Product Substitution Procedures fully covers the limits on substitutions, the contractor's representations and how to request one, adding 'or equal' after every product name only repeats it; the rule is to say it once and in the right place. Product Options and Product Requirements deal with choices among specified products and general product rules, not with requests to substitute.

questions.question: At least ____ days should be allowed between the deadline for substitution requests during bidding and publication of the addendum that accepts them.

mc.question: At minimum, how many days should be allowed between the deadline for bidders' substitution requests and publication of the addendum that accepts them?

options.A: One
options.B: Five
options.C: Seven
options.D: Ten
options.E: Three
options.F: Fourteen

questions.explanation: The A/E sets the deadline for substitution requests, and at least three days should separate it from the addendum that tells all bidders which substitutions were accepted, so each request gets proper consideration. Ten days is the tempting wrong answer: a typical instructions-to-bidders clause asks for written requests at least 10 days before the bid date, which is a different interval.

questions.question: Division 00 document 00 31 32, which gives the information needed to specify sections such as waterproofing, earthwork and pavements, is titled ____.

mc.question: Division 00 document 00 31 32 gives the information needed to specify sections such as waterproofing, earthwork and pavements. What is its title?

options.A: Existing Condition Information
options.B: Survey Information
options.C: Geotechnical Data
options.D: Preliminary Schedules
options.E: Existing Hazardous Material Information
options.F: Environmental Assessment Information

questions.explanation: 00 31 32 Geotechnical Data reports subsurface conditions, which drive the requirements for waterproofing, earthwork and pavements. Its neighbors under 00 31 00 Available Project Information cover other subjects: 00 31 13 Preliminary Schedules for phasing, 00 31 19 Existing Condition Information, 00 31 21 Survey Information and 00 31 26 Existing Hazardous Material Information.

questions.question: Specifications define qualitative requirements and usually leave to the drawings information such as ____ (how many of each item), form and location.

mc.question: Specifications define qualitative requirements. Which kind of information do they usually leave to the drawings, along with form and location?

options.A: Physical properties
options.B: Installation methods
options.C: Quality control provisions
options.D: Quantity
options.E: Performance requirements
options.F: Standards of workmanship

questions.explanation: Drawings show how much there is, what shape it takes and where it goes, while specifications describe the quality of what is provided. A vapor retarder may simply be noted on the drawings while the specifications set its perm rating, its physical properties, how it is installed and its quality control, so properties, methods, performance and workmanship all belong in the specifications. The two documents complement each other rather than overlap.

questions.question: Specifications describe work results, not just products. Carpet, for example, is the product; the work result is ____.

mc.question: Specifications describe work results, not just products. Carpet is a product; which term names the corresponding work result?

options.A: Carpet tile
options.B: Sheet carpet
options.C: Carpeting
options.D: Carpet cushion
options.E: Resilient flooring
options.F: Entrance flooring

questions.explanation: A specification describes the result of applying labor and skill to products, so the product carpet becomes the work result carpeting, which is also the MasterFormat title 09 68 00 Carpeting. Carpet tile, sheet carpet and carpet cushion are products, and resilient or entrance flooring are different work results. Because MasterFormat is organized by work results, one product can appear in several divisions.

questions.question: If drawing notes say 'concrete pavers', a switch to brick means changing several notes plus the specifications; the drawings should instead use the generic note ____ so only the specifications change.

mc.question: If drawing notes say 'concrete pavers', a switch to brick means changing several notes plus the specifications. Which generic note should the drawings use instead, so that only the specifications change?

options.A: Brick pavers
options.B: Stone paving
options.C: Rigid paving
options.D: Unit pavers
options.E: Flexible paving
options.F: Precast concrete pavers

questions.explanation: Drawings should identify a material generically and leave its description to the specifications, so a note reading unit pavers covers concrete, brick or stone pavers and survives a change of material. Brick, stone or precast concrete pavers are specific materials that would force more drawing revisions, and rigid and flexible paving are different kinds of pavement altogether. Fewer detailed notes also mean fewer conflicts between drawings and specifications.

questions.question: EJCDC 1910-16, a reference that gives the recommended primary and secondary locations for each subject in the construction documents, is titled ____.

mc.question: EJCDC 1910-16 is a reference that gives the recommended primary and secondary locations for each subject in the construction documents. What is its title?

options.A: Uniform Drawing System
options.B: Standard General Conditions of the Construction Contract
options.C: Owner's Instructions Concerning Bonds and Insurance for Construction
options.D: Uniform Location of Subject Matter
options.E: National CAD Standard
options.F: Owner's Instructions to the Architect

questions.explanation: Uniform Location of Subject Matter (also published as EJCDC N-122 and AIA A521) tells the specifier where each subject belongs, with primary and secondary locations and suggested cross-references; what goes in a secondary location supplements the primary one rather than repeating it. The Uniform Drawing System is part of the National CAD Standard for drawings, and C-700 and C-052 are EJCDC's general conditions and owner's bond and insurance instructions.

questions.question: When schedules are placed in the specifications, they go at the end of PART 3 or in the section numbered XX ____ of each division.

mc.question: When schedules are placed in the specifications rather than on the drawings, they go at the end of PART 3 or in which section number of each division?

questions.explanation: Each division reserves its XX 06 00 number for schedules, such as 08 06 00 Schedules for Openings or 09 06 00 Schedules for Finishes, and a section's own schedules can also sit at the end of PART 3. The neighboring numbers have other uses: XX 01 00 operation and maintenance, XX 03 00 conservation treatment, XX 05 00 common work results and XX 08 00 commissioning.

questions.question: The conditions of the contract, the contracting forms and the procurement requirements bound into a project manual are not specifications; they are usually prepared by, or in coordination with, the owner, the owner's legal counsel and the owner's ____.

mc.question: The conditions of the contract, contracting forms and procurement requirements in a project manual are usually prepared by, or with, the owner, the owner's legal counsel and which other advisor to the owner?

options.A: Specifier
options.B: Construction manager
options.C: Insurance advisor
options.D: Cost estimator
options.E: Commissioning agent
options.F: Lender

questions.explanation: Division 00 documents such as the bidding requirements, contract forms and contract conditions set legal and financial terms, so they come from the owner's side: the owner, the owner's legal counsel and the owner's insurance advisor. That is why the whole book is better called a project manual than the specifications. The A/E coordinates these documents but should never act as insurance advisor or set insurance limits.

questions.question: Of the Division 00 documents, 00 70 00 ____ has the most influence on preparing the Division 01 sections.

mc.question: Which Division 00 document has the most influence on preparing the Division 01 sections?

options.A: Preliminary Schedules
options.B: Geotechnical Data
options.C: Instructions for Procurement
options.D: Agreement Forms
options.E: Bond Forms
options.F: Conditions of the Contract

questions.explanation: Division 01 sections expand on the administrative and procedural provisions of 00 70 00 Conditions of the Contract (the general and supplementary conditions), so that document shapes the General Requirements most and can also affect PART 1 and PART 3 of some sections. Preliminary Schedules help plan phasing and Geotechnical Data informs earthwork and waterproofing sections, but neither drives Division 01.

questions.question: The supplementary conditions, which modify the general conditions to fit a specific project, are Division 00 document number ____.

mc.question: The supplementary conditions, which modify the general conditions to fit a specific project, carry which Division 00 number?

questions.explanation: Within the Conditions of the Contract (00 70 00), number 00 72 00 holds the general conditions, which apply to almost any project, and 00 73 00 holds the supplementary conditions that adjust them for this one; 00 71 00 is Contracting Definitions. The nearby numbers 00 52 00 Agreement Forms, 00 62 00 Certificates and Other Forms and 00 43 00 Procurement Form Supplements are forms, not conditions.

questions.question: Besides the general SUBMITTALS article, SectionFormat's PART 1 has four submittal article titles: ____ submittals, ____ submittals, ____ submittals, ____ submittals.

mc.question: Besides the general SUBMITTALS article, which four submittal article titles appear in SectionFormat's PART 1?

options.A: Action, informational, closeout and sustainable design submittals
options.B: Action, shop drawing, closeout and maintenance material submittals
options.C: Action, informational, closeout and maintenance material submittals
options.D: Product data, informational, closeout and maintenance material submittals
options.E: Action, informational, delegated design and maintenance material submittals
options.F: Action, quality assurance, closeout and maintenance material submittals

questions.explanation: SectionFormat sorts submittals into ACTION SUBMITTALS and INFORMATIONAL SUBMITTALS (product data, shop drawings, samples, certificates, reports and the like), CLOSEOUT SUBMITTALS (maintenance contracts, operation and maintenance data, warranty and record documentation) and MAINTENANCE MATERIAL SUBMITTALS (spare parts, extra stock, tools). Shop drawing, delegated design and sustainable design submittals are subordinate titles inside those articles, and quality assurance is a separate PART 1 article.

questions.question: Closeout submittals typically need no action by the A/E, and maintenance material submittals need no A/E action other than ____.

mc.question: Maintenance material submittals need no action by the A/E other than what?

options.A: Approval or rejection
options.B: Responsive action
options.C: Confirmation of receipt
options.D: Review for conformance with the design concept
options.E: Certification of compliance
options.F: Distribution to the consultants for review

questions.explanation: Maintenance material submittals are the spare parts, extra stock and tools turned over to the owner, so the A/E simply confirms they were received. Responsive action, such as approving or rejecting and reviewing for conformance with the design concept, belongs to action submittals like shop drawings, product data and samples; informational and closeout submittals are grouped so that no responsive action is expected.

questions.question: Under SectionFormat's MAINTENANCE MATERIAL SUBMITTALS article, the three subordinate titles are ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which three subordinate titles appear under SectionFormat's MAINTENANCE MATERIAL SUBMITTALS article?

options.A: Spare Parts
options.B: Maintenance Contracts
options.C: Extra Stock Materials
options.D: Operation and Maintenance Data
options.E: Tools
options.F: Warranty Documentation

questions.explanation: MAINTENANCE MATERIAL SUBMITTALS covers physical items handed to the owner: spare parts, extra stock materials such as ceiling tiles, flooring and paint, and tools. The article states their type and quantity, while their characteristics are specified in PART 2. Maintenance contracts, operation and maintenance data and warranty documentation are paperwork, listed under CLOSEOUT SUBMITTALS instead.

questions.question: SectionFormat says to state the type and quantity of special tools for the Owner under maintenance material submittals, but to describe the tools themselves in PART 2 under the article ____.

mc.question: SectionFormat says to state the type and quantity of special tools for the Owner under maintenance material submittals. Under which PART 2 article are the tools themselves described?

options.A: Materials
options.B: Finishes
options.C: Accessories
options.D: Source Quality Control
options.E: Owner-Furnished Products
options.F: Mixes

questions.explanation: Tools such as special wrenches, gauges and circuit setters, which the owner's own tool kit would not include, are specified in PART 2 under ACCESSORIES, the article for accessory products like fasteners, adhesives and flashings. Owner-Furnished Products covers items the owner supplies, the reverse situation, and spare parts and extra stock are described in PART 2 with the product itself.

questions.question: Three PART 1 articles deal specifically with quality: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which three PART 1 articles deal specifically with quality?

options.A: Administrative Requirements
options.B: Source Quality Control
options.C: Submittals
options.D: Field Quality Control
options.E: Quality Assurance
options.F: Examination

questions.explanation: In PART 1, quality is handled by Administrative Requirements (coordination and preinstallation meetings), Submittals (quality assurance and quality control submittals) and Quality Assurance (qualifications, certifications, preconstruction testing and mock-ups). Source Quality Control is a PART 2 article for testing at the plant or shop, while Field Quality Control and Examination are PART 3 articles for the site.

questions.question: Under SectionFormat's PART 1 article WARRANTY [OR] BOND, the three subordinate titles are ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which three subordinate titles appear under SectionFormat's PART 1 article WARRANTY [OR] BOND?

options.A: Warranty Documentation
options.B: Manufacturer Warranty
options.C: Maintenance Contracts
options.D: Special Warranty
options.E: Bonds
options.F: Extended Correction Period

questions.explanation: WARRANTY [OR] BOND holds Manufacturer Warranty, Special Warranty and Extended Correction Period; the basic correction period is defined in the general conditions, so extending it may also call for an edit to the supplementary conditions. Warranty Documentation, Maintenance Contracts and Bonds are subordinate titles under CLOSEOUT SUBMITTALS, which covers the paperwork delivered at the end of the job.

questions.question: Testing and inspection done away from the site, at the plant, mill, factory or shop where a product is made or fabricated, is specified in the PART 2 article ____.

mc.question: Testing and inspection done away from the site, at the plant, mill, factory or shop where a product is made or fabricated, is specified under which article?

options.A: Field Quality Control
options.B: Quality Assurance
options.C: Preconstruction Testing
options.D: Source Quality Control
options.E: Assembly or Fabrication
options.F: Examination

questions.explanation: Testing and inspection at the source, meaning the manufacturer's or fabricator's own facility, is specified in PART 2 under SOURCE QUALITY CONTROL, next to the products being made. FIELD [OR] SITE QUALITY CONTROL in PART 3 covers tests and inspections of installed work, Examination checks conditions before installation, and Quality Assurance with its Preconstruction Testing subordinate is a PART 1 article.

questions.question: The North American Architectural Woodwork Standards (NAAWS), published jointly by AWMAC and the Woodwork Institute, control workmanship with measurable tolerances for joinery, surfaces and clearances in three grades: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: The North American Architectural Woodwork Standards (NAAWS) control woodwork workmanship with measurable tolerances. Which three grades does the specifier choose among?

options.A: Premium, standard, economy
options.B: Premium, custom, economy
options.C: Premium, custom, commercial
options.D: Select, custom, economy
options.E: Best, better, good
options.F: Architectural, custom, economy

questions.explanation: NAAWS, from AWMAC and the Woodwork Institute, sets measurable tolerances for joinery, surfaces and clearances in premium, custom and economy grades, and the specifier must pick the grade for each item. Measurable grades like these are the point: wording such as 'best possible workmanship' cannot be enforced, because 'best' means different things to different readers.

questions.question: Full-size erected assemblies used for testing and observation and to set the standard by which workmanship will be judged, with their location and extent shown on the drawings, are ____.

mc.question: What are the full-size erected assemblies called that are used for testing and observation, set the standard by which workmanship will be judged, and have their location and extent shown on the drawings?

options.A: Field samples
options.B: Samples
options.C: Mock-ups
options.D: Preconstruction testing
options.E: Shop drawings
options.F: Delegated design submittals

questions.explanation: Mock-ups are full-size assemblies built for testing and observation that become the benchmark for judging the finished work; they are specified under QUALITY ASSURANCE in PART 1. Field samples are smaller trial applications of finishes and coatings at the site, samples are submitted pieces of the actual products, and preconstruction testing is a separate quality assurance requirement, not a built assembly.

questions.question: Under SectionFormat's PART 3 article CLOSEOUT ACTIVITIES, the two subordinate titles are ____ and ____.

mc.question: Which two subordinate titles appear under SectionFormat's PART 3 article CLOSEOUT ACTIVITIES?

options.A: Systems Startup
options.B: Demonstration
options.C: Adjusting
options.D: Training
options.E: Waste Management
options.F: Protection

questions.explanation: CLOSEOUT ACTIVITIES holds Demonstration, where the installer or manufacturer shows that equipment operates properly, and Training of the owner's personnel in operation and maintenance, coordinated with Section 01 79 00 Demonstration and Training. Systems Startup, Adjusting and Protection are separate PART 3 articles, and Waste Management is a subordinate title under CLEANING.

questions.question: Before consultants prepare any of their sections, two things should be made available to them: the ____ and the ____ sections.

mc.question: Before consultants prepare any of their sections, which two things should be made available to them?

options.A: The instructions for procurement and the Division 01 sections
options.B: The conditions of the contract and the outline specifications
options.C: The preliminary project description and the Division 01 sections
options.D: The conditions of the contract and the Division 01 sections
options.E: The agreement form and the office master guide specifications
options.F: The conditions of the contract and the cost estimate

questions.explanation: Consultants need the conditions of the contract and the Division 01 sections before they write, so their sections are coordinated and neither repeat nor omit general requirements; their input to Division 01 is requested at the same time. The prime A/E stays responsible for coordinating every consultant's sections, and documents such as outline specifications or the cost estimate do not set those project-wide requirements.

questions.question: Any A/E firm may retain an outside specifier on a project-by-project basis, such as a member of SCIP, which stands for ____.

mc.question: Any A/E firm, whatever its size, may hire an outside specifications consultant on a project-by-project basis or for all its projects. Members of which organization provide this kind of service?

options.A: Construction Specifications Canada
options.B: National Institute of Building Sciences
options.C: American Institute of Architects
options.D: Engineers Joint Contract Documents Committee
options.E: Specifications Consultants in Independent Practice
options.F: Design-Build Institute of America

questions.explanation: SCIP, Specifications Consultants in Independent Practice, is the organization of independent specification consultants that any firm may retain for one project or for all of them. Otherwise a firm produces its own specifications through a principal in a small office, a full-time specifier in firms of roughly 20 to 70 people, or a specifications department in a large firm; the other organizations listed publish standards or contract documents rather than supplying consultants.

questions.question: In the most effective writing sequence for a specification section, PART ____ is most frequently written first.

mc.question: In the most effective writing sequence for a specification section, which portion is most frequently written first?

options.A: PART 1 GENERAL
options.B: PART 3 EXECUTION
options.C: PART 2 PRODUCTS
options.D: The SUMMARY article
options.E: The SUBMITTALS article
options.F: The schedules attached after END OF SECTION

questions.explanation: Writing usually starts with PART 2 PRODUCTS, then PART 3 EXECUTION, then a return to PART 2 to confirm the products suit the installation and to add secondary materials. PART 1 GENERAL comes last, because its articles, such as Summary, Submittals, Quality Assurance and Warranty, can only be written accurately once the products and execution are settled.

questions.question: The list of section titles, used to coordinate the sections and prevent overlaps or omissions, can in its final form become the project manual's ____.

mc.question: The list of section titles, used to coordinate the sections and prevent overlaps or omissions, can in its final form become which part of the project manual?

options.A: List of Drawing Sheets
options.B: Summary of Work
options.C: Project Title Page
options.D: List of Schedules
options.E: Schedule of Values
options.F: Table of Contents

questions.explanation: The section title list, built with MasterFormat as a checklist and shared with the owner and design team, grows into the project manual's table of contents, and cross-checking the sections against it is part of quality control before issue. The List of Drawing Sheets and List of Schedules are other introductory documents, Summary of Work describes the project's scope, and the schedule of values is the contractor's payment breakdown.

questions.question: Although drafts should go out early, as a general rule the sections of Divisions 02 through 49 are written before the Division ____ sections are finalized.

mc.question: Drafts of certain sections go out early for review, yet as a general rule those sections are finalized only after the sections of Divisions 02 through 49 have been written. Which sections are they?

options.A: Outline specifications
options.B: Division 01 General Requirements sections
options.C: Preliminary project descriptions
options.D: Office master guide specifications
options.E: Consultants' mechanical and electrical sections
options.F: The specifications notebook

questions.explanation: Division 01 General Requirements is drafted early and sent to consultants so overlaps and omissions are caught, but it is finalized after the sections of Divisions 02 through 49 are written, so its general provisions match what the technical sections actually need. Outline specifications and preliminary project descriptions come earlier in design, and office master guide specifications are firm-wide texts, not project sections.

questions.question: Name SectionFormat's three PARTs: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list gives SectionFormat's three PARTs, in order?

options.A: General, Materials, Execution
options.B: General, Products, Execution
options.C: Administrative Requirements, Products, Execution
options.D: General, Products, Installation
options.E: Summary, Products, Execution
options.F: Scope, Materials, Workmanship

questions.explanation: PART 1 GENERAL covers the section's own administrative, procedural and temporary requirements, extending Division 01; PART 2 PRODUCTS covers the products, materials, equipment, mixes, fabrications, systems and assemblies; PART 3 EXECUTION covers installation or application, preparation, and cleaning and protection afterward. Summary and Administrative Requirements are articles within PART 1, and materials and installation are topics inside PARTS 2 and 3.

questions.question: MasterFormat's Specifications Group has five subgroups: ____, ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which list gives the five subgroups of MasterFormat's Specifications Group, in order?

options.A: General Requirements, Facility Construction, Facility Services, Site and Infrastructure, Procurement and Contracting Requirements
options.B: Existing Conditions, Facility Construction, Facility Services, Site and Infrastructure, Process Equipment
options.C: General Requirements, Facility Construction, Mechanical and Electrical, Site and Infrastructure, Process Equipment
options.D: General Requirements, Shell and Interiors, Facility Services, Site and Infrastructure, Process Equipment
options.E: General Requirements, Facility Construction, Facility Services, Site and Infrastructure, Process Equipment
options.F: General Requirements, Facility Construction, Facility Services, Exterior Improvements, Process Equipment

questions.explanation: The Specifications Group runs General Requirements (Division 01), Facility Construction (02 to 19), Facility Services (20 to 29), Site and Infrastructure (30 to 39) and Process Equipment (40 to 49). Procurement and Contracting Requirements is the other group, holding Division 00; Existing Conditions and Exterior Improvements are division titles, and Shell and Interiors are UniFormat categories.

questions.question: MasterFormat organizes its numbers and titles into two groups: the ____ Group and the ____ Group.

mc.question: MasterFormat organizes its numbers and titles into two groups. What are they?

options.A: Procurement Requirements Group and Contracting Requirements Group
options.B: Procurement and Contracting Requirements Group and Specifications Group
options.C: Bidding Requirements Group and Specifications Group
options.D: General Requirements Group and Technical Specifications Group
options.E: Facility Construction Group and Facility Services Group
options.F: Procurement and Contracting Requirements Group and General Requirements Group

questions.explanation: MasterFormat's Procurement and Contracting Requirements Group (Division 00) holds introductory, procurement and contracting documents, which are not specifications, and its Specifications Group (Divisions 01 through 49) holds the administrative requirements and the physical work. General Requirements, Facility Construction and Facility Services are subgroups within the Specifications Group, and procurement and contracting share a single group rather than having one each.

questions.question: MasterFormat is typically updated on a ____ cycle, so the specifier should keep track of changes to its numbers and titles.

mc.question: MasterFormat is typically updated on what cycle, so the specifier should keep track of changes to its numbers and titles?

options.A: Annual
options.B: Biannual (twice a year)
options.C: Biennial (every two years)
options.D: Triennial (every three years)
options.E: Five-year
options.F: Ten-year

questions.explanation: MasterFormat is normally revised on a biennial cycle, every two years, so numbers and titles can change from one edition to the next and office masters need to keep up. Biannual sounds alike but means twice a year, and annual or longer cycles do not match the usual revision schedule.

questions.question: MasterFormat's Specifications Group spans Divisions 01 through 49; Divisions 02 through 49, all but General Requirements, are commonly called the ____ specifications.

mc.question: MasterFormat's Specifications Group spans Divisions 01 through 49. What are Divisions 02 through 49, all but General Requirements, commonly called?

options.A: Front-end specifications
options.B: General specifications
options.C: Technical specifications
options.D: Performance specifications
options.E: Procurement specifications
options.F: Supplementary specifications

questions.explanation: Divisions 02 through 49 describe the physical work and are known as the technical specifications, while Division 01 General Requirements applies broadly to all of them and Division 00 holds documents rather than specifications. 'Front end' is an informal name some people give Divisions 00 and 01, and it is better replaced by the division names themselves.

questions.question: When a section doesn't need one of its PARTs, SectionFormat keeps that PART's number and title followed by the words ____, to show it was omitted on purpose.

mc.question: When a section doesn't need one of its PARTs, SectionFormat keeps that PART's number and title followed by which words, to show it was omitted on purpose?

options.A: Not Applicable
options.B: Reserved
options.C: Not Used
options.D: Intentionally Left Blank
options.E: Deleted
options.F: Omitted

questions.explanation: An unneeded PART is not deleted: its number and title stay, followed by 'Not Used', so readers know the omission was deliberate and the three-part structure stays intact. 'Reserved' is MasterFormat's label for division numbers not yet assigned, and phrases such as 'Not Applicable' or 'Intentionally Left Blank' are not the SectionFormat convention.

questions.question: Attachments, added after END OF SECTION for convenience or clarity, are of four kinds: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which four kinds of items can be attached after END OF SECTION for convenience or clarity?

options.A: Schedules, tables, illustrations and forms
options.B: Schedules, tables, drawings and forms
options.C: Schedules, tables, illustrations and product data
options.D: Shop drawings, tables, illustrations and forms
options.E: Schedules, photographs, illustrations and forms
options.F: Schedules, tables, details and reports

questions.explanation: Schedules, tables, illustrations and forms may follow END OF SECTION, which always comes before them, and the related PART should refer to them. A schedule is a titled grouping with at least three columns of related information, and a table is a simple list or chart of related items; drawings, product data and reports are separate documents, not section attachments.

questions.question: Written formats come in two types. SectionFormat, PageFormat and PPDFormat are compositional formats, giving guidelines for preparing documents; OmniClass, UniFormat and MasterFormat, which structure information so it can be stored and retrieved, are ____ formats.

mc.question: SectionFormat, PageFormat and PPDFormat are compositional formats. What type of format are OmniClass, UniFormat and MasterFormat, which classify construction information so it can be stored and retrieved?

options.A: Compositional
options.B: Faceted
options.C: Narrative
options.D: Taxonomical
options.E: Procedural
options.F: Descriptive

questions.explanation: Taxonomical formats such as OmniClass, UniFormat and MasterFormat classify construction information so it can be stored consistently and found again. Compositional formats such as SectionFormat, PageFormat and PPDFormat instead give guidelines for arranging text within a document. Faceted describes the structure of OmniClass alone, and narrative and descriptive name a type of specification and a specifying method, not types of format.

questions.question: PageFormat lists three mandatory section-identification items for the header or footer of every page: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which three section-identification items does PageFormat make mandatory in the header or footer of every page?

options.A: Section number
options.B: Project name
options.C: Section title
options.D: Issue date
options.E: Page number
options.F: File name

questions.explanation: Every page must carry the section number, section title and page number so it can be identified even when it is separated from the rest. Total pages, author name and file name are optional section items, and the project name, location, number and issue date belong to the project identification group placed in the other header or footer area.

questions.question: PageFormat's preferred location for page numbers is at the ____ edge of the page, in the header or footer.

mc.question: Where does PageFormat prefer page numbers to be placed?

options.A: At the bound edge, in the header or footer
options.B: Centered in the footer
options.C: At the unbound edge, in the header or footer
options.D: Centered in the header
options.E: In the gutter, beside the binding
options.F: In the side margin, beside the first line of text

questions.explanation: Page numbers belong at the unbound edge, the edge away from the binding, where they are easiest to see while flipping through a printed project manual; the section number, section title and project name go there too. Less important items such as author or file name can sit at the bound edge, and header and footer data is kept at the margins rather than centered unless it is the only item on the line.

questions.question: PageFormat says ____-point fonts are usually considered the smallest readable size.

mc.question: PageFormat says fonts of what point size are usually considered the smallest readable size?

options.A: 8 point
options.B: 9 point
options.C: 10 point
options.D: 11 point
options.E: 12 point
options.F: 14 point

questions.explanation: PageFormat requires no particular font, but it treats 10 point as the smallest size that most readers can comfortably read. It also favors serif typefaces for body text and sans serif for titles and headings, recommends one font throughout the project manual, and notes that smaller fonts need shorter lines to stay readable.

questions.question: In PageFormat, the extra space added at the bound edge of each page to allow for binding is called the ____.

mc.question: In PageFormat, what is the extra space added at the bound edge of each page to allow for binding called?

options.A: Margin
options.B: Indent
options.C: Header
options.D: Gutter
options.E: Unbound edge
options.F: Justification

questions.explanation: The gutter is extra width at the bound edge, added on top of the normal margin when a binding would otherwise hide the text. A margin is the ordinary blank space next to every edge of the page, an indent is a temporary left margin within a paragraph, and the unbound edge is the opposite side of the page, where page numbers go.

questions.question: PageFormat says ____ should be avoided entirely in specification text, since it may conflict with formats that identify modifications such as strikeout.

mc.question: Which text treatment does PageFormat say to avoid entirely in specifications, because it may conflict with formats that mark modifications such as strikeout?

options.A: Boldface
options.B: Underlining
options.C: Italics
options.D: Capitalization
options.E: Indentation
options.F: Two-column layout

questions.explanation: Underlining is ruled out because revision marking already uses underlines and strikeout to show changes, so underlined text could be mistaken for an edit. Emphasis should come from capitalization, spacing and punctuation; bold or italic may help navigation in Part and Article titles but should not carry meaning, and indented outline levels and a two-column layout are accepted layout tools.

questions.question: PageFormat page numbers start at 1 in each section and consist of the section number followed by a ____ and the sequential page number within the section.

mc.question: PageFormat page numbers start at 1 in each section. What separates the section number from the sequential page number?

options.A: Period
options.B: Colon
options.C: Slash
options.D: Hyphen
options.E: Comma
options.F: Semicolon

questions.explanation: A page number such as 08 71 00 - 3 combines the section number, a hyphen with a space on each side, and the page within that section, so any page can be referenced exactly. Numbering restarts at 1 in each section because one continuous sequence through the whole project manual would make revisions harder.

questions.question: A revision log (project name and number, section number and title, and a brief description of each change) should be archived for use in updating the ____, to capture lessons learned.

mc.question: A revision log listing the project, the section and a brief description of each change should be archived for use in updating what, to capture lessons learned?

options.A: Project record documents
options.B: Office master guide specifications
options.C: Addenda
options.D: Specifications notebook
options.E: Section title list
options.F: Closeout submittals

questions.explanation: Archived revision logs let a firm feed each project's changes back into its office master guide specifications, so the next project starts from better text. The revised specifications themselves are distributed and archived in a neutral, secured format such as PDF; record documents and closeout submittals belong to the construction contract, and addenda are revisions issued during bidding, not a source for updating masters.

questions.question: In every MasterFormat division, the Level 2 number XX 01 00 holds operation and maintenance and XX 08 00 holds commissioning; XX 05 00 holds ____.

mc.question: In every MasterFormat division, XX 01 00 holds operation and maintenance and XX 08 00 holds commissioning. What does the Level 2 number XX 05 00 hold?

options.A: Schedules
options.B: Conservation treatment for period work
options.C: Common work results
options.D: General requirements
options.E: Performance requirements
options.F: Product requirements

questions.explanation: MasterFormat reserves the same Level 2 numbers in every division for the same kinds of sections: XX 01 00 operation and maintenance, XX 05 00 common work results, XX 06 00 schedules and XX 08 00 commissioning, so 09 05 00 is Common Work Results for Finishes. Schedules sit one number higher at XX 06 00 and conservation treatment of period work at XX 03 00, while general, product and performance requirements are Division 01 titles.

questions.question: For a project issued in multiple work packages, the preferred approach is the ____ method, in which each new package adds to and revises the documents issued before, rather than the standalone method.

mc.question: For a project issued in multiple work packages, which method is preferred, in which each new package adds to and revises the drawings and specifications issued before?

options.A: Standalone method
options.B: Cumulative method
options.C: Narrative method
options.D: Revised-page method
options.E: Fast-track method
options.F: Multiple-prime method

questions.explanation: In the cumulative method each work package builds on the earlier ones, so the documents grow toward one comprehensive contract set and revisions stay manageable. In the standalone method every package is complete and separate, which makes each scope easy to see but means revisions must be tracked package by package. The narrative and revised-page methods are ways of writing changes, and fast-track is a scheduling technique.

questions.question: For version-control file names of issued specifications, a consistent naming protocol can use the optional yyyy-mm-dd date convention prescribed by ISO ____.

mc.question: Which standard prescribes the optional yyyy-mm-dd date convention that can be used in version-control file names for issued specifications?

options.A: ISO 9000
options.C: ISO 8601
options.F: ASTM C150

questions.explanation: ISO 8601 is the international standard for representing dates and times, and its optional yyyy-mm-dd form gives file names a consistent date stamp for version control. Revisions should be issued and archived in a neutral format such as PDF, with protection against unauthorized changes. ISO 9000 covers quality management, ISO 55000 asset management, ISO 12006 the frameworks for classifying construction information, and ASTM C150 portland cement.

questions.question: Specifications can be written in two grammatical moods: the imperative, which should generally be used throughout, and the ____ mood, which needs 'shall' or 'will' and tends toward wordiness.

mc.question: Specifications can be written in two grammatical moods. One opens each sentence with the verb ('Spread adhesive with notched trowel') and should generally be used throughout. Which is the other, which needs 'shall' or 'will' and tends toward wordiness?

options.A: Imperative
options.B: Passive
options.C: Indicative
options.D: Streamlined
options.E: Descriptive
options.F: Narrative

questions.explanation: The indicative mood states requirements with 'shall' or 'will' ('Adhesive shall be spread with notched trowel'), which adds words and monotony and stretches 'shall', traditionally meaning 'has a duty to', onto things that have no duties. The imperative puts the verb first and is preferred. 'Passive' names a voice rather than a mood, and streamlined text is a form that drops words, not a mood.

questions.question: Good specification writing style is characterized by three qualities: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Good specification writing style is characterized by which three qualities?

options.A: Accuracy, completeness, clarity
options.B: Clarity, conciseness, completeness
options.C: Accuracy, brevity, completeness
options.D: Accuracy, brevity, clarity
options.E: Brevity, clarity, consistency
options.F: Correctness, conciseness, clarity

questions.explanation: Good style rests on accuracy, brevity and clarity, which come from short, simple declarative or imperative sentences and plain words; long, stilted sentences whose meaning could change with one misplaced comma work against all three. Lists that bring in completeness, consistency or correctness borrow from the separate four Cs of communication (clear, concise, correct, complete), which is a different list.

questions.question: In specification language, 'party' is kept for those who sign the contract; to include persons or companies that did not sign it, such as subcontractors, the generic term ____ is used.

mc.question: In specification language, 'party' is kept for those who sign the contract. Which generic term should be used to include persons or companies that did not sign it, such as subcontractors?

options.A: Party
options.B: Signatory
options.C: Entity
options.D: Subcontractor
options.E: Separate contractor
options.F: Claimant

questions.explanation: A party is a signer of the contract, such as the owner and the contractor in the owner-contractor agreement. When a requirement must also reach subcontractors and others in the construction process who never signed, the generic word 'entity' is used. 'Signatory' means the same as party, while 'subcontractor', 'separate contractor' and 'claimant' each name only one kind of participant.

questions.question: In specifications, 'balance' is used only when writing about money; for 'that which is left over' the preferred word is ____.

mc.question: In specifications, 'balance' is used only when writing about money. Which word is preferred for 'that which is left over'?

options.A: Quantity
options.B: Remainder
options.C: Amount
options.D: Surplus
options.E: Difference
options.F: Balance

questions.explanation: Paired words are kept apart so each has one meaning: 'balance' is for money and 'remainder' for what is left over. 'Amount' and 'quantity' form a separate pair (money versus numbers, length, area or volume), and looser words such as 'surplus' or 'difference' do not carry the intended meaning. Once a word is chosen, it should be used the same way throughout the specifications.

questions.question: Abbreviations in contract documents should be limited to ____ or fewer letters, and short words should not be abbreviated when that saves only a character or two.

mc.question: Abbreviations in contract documents should be limited to how many letters at most?

options.A: Three
options.B: Four
options.C: Five
options.D: Six
options.E: Seven
options.F: Eight

questions.explanation: Abbreviations should have five letters or fewer, belong mainly on drawings and schedules where space is tight, must be defined on the drawings or in Division 01, and must match between drawings and specifications; when in doubt, spell the word out. Abbreviating a short word to save one or two characters only adds confusion.

questions.question: Where two spellings are equally correct (gage or gauge, catalog or catalogue), the ____ spelling is preferred in contract documents.

mc.question: Where two spellings are equally correct (gage or gauge, catalog or catalogue), which spelling is preferred in contract documents?

options.A: The longer spelling
options.B: The British spelling
options.C: The shorter spelling
options.D: A simplified spelling such as 'thru'
options.E: The spelling the manufacturer uses
options.F: The more formal spelling

questions.explanation: When the office's standard dictionary accepts two spellings, contract documents use the shorter one: gage, catalog, molding, facia. Brevity must not turn into substandard spelling, though, so shortcuts such as 'thru' for 'through' are avoided. Naming one dictionary as the office standard keeps spelling correct and consistent across the documents.

questions.question: Division 00's Procurement Requirements (00 10 00 through 00 40 00) consist of four Level 2 groups: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which four Level 2 groups make up the Procurement Requirements in Division 00 (00 10 00 through 00 40 00)?

options.A: Solicitation; Instructions for Procurement; Available Information; Conditions of the Contract
options.B: Solicitation; Instructions for Procurement; Available Information; Procurement Forms and Supplements
options.C: Advertisement for Bids; Instructions for Procurement; Available Information; Procurement Forms and Supplements
options.D: Solicitation; Notice of Award; Available Information; Procurement Forms and Supplements
options.E: Solicitation; Instructions for Procurement; Geotechnical Data; Procurement Forms and Supplements
options.F: Solicitation; Instructions for Procurement; Project Forms; Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications

questions.explanation: Procurement Requirements run 00 10 00 Solicitation, 00 20 00 Instructions for Procurement, 00 30 00 Available Information and 00 40 00 Procurement Forms and Supplements. Contracting Requirements follow from 00 50 00, so Notice of Award, Project Forms and Conditions of the Contract belong there, while Advertisement for Bids and Geotechnical Data are lower-level titles inside Solicitation and Available Information.

questions.question: In Division 00, the Contracting Requirements (00 50 00 through 00 90 00) fall under four headings: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which four headings make up the Contracting Requirements in Division 00 (00 50 00 through 00 90 00)? (Listed alphabetically.)

options.A: Available Information; Conditions of the Contract; Contracting Forms and Supplements; Project Forms
options.B: Bond Forms; Conditions of the Contract; Contracting Forms and Supplements; Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications
options.C: Conditions of the Contract; Procurement Forms and Supplements; Project Forms; Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications
options.D: Contracting Forms and Supplements; Instructions for Procurement; Project Forms; Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications
options.E: Conditions of the Contract; Contracting Forms and Supplements; Project Forms; Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications
options.F: Contracting Forms and Supplements; General Requirements; Project Forms; Solicitation

questions.explanation: Contracting Requirements group 00 50 00 Contracting Forms and Supplements (the agreement), 00 60 00 Project Forms (bonds and certificates), 00 70 00 Conditions of the Contract (general and supplementary conditions) and 00 90 00 Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications. Procurement Forms and Supplements, Instructions for Procurement and Available Information belong to the Procurement Requirements, and Bond Forms is a title inside Project Forms.

questions.question: Procurement documents comprise procurement requirements, contracting requirements, contract drawings, specifications, resource drawings and addenda. When the agreement is signed, the two that do not become contract documents are ____ and ____.

mc.question: When the owner and contractor sign the agreement, most procurement documents become contract documents. Which two do not?

options.A: Contracting requirements
options.B: Procurement requirements
options.C: Contract drawings
options.D: Resource drawings
options.E: Specifications
options.F: Addenda

questions.explanation: Contract documents are the contracting requirements (00 50 00 through 00 90 00), the contract drawings, the specifications and the addenda issued before the contract. The procurement requirements, such as the solicitation and instructions to bidders, serve only the bidding stage, and resource drawings (for example, record drawings of an existing building) are issued for information only and stay out of the contract.

questions.question: Name the titles of MasterFormat Divisions 21, 22 and 23, in that order: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: What are the titles of MasterFormat Divisions 21, 22 and 23, in that order?

options.A: Fire Suppression; Plumbing; Electrical
options.B: Plumbing; Heating, Ventilating, and Air-Conditioning; Electrical
options.C: Fire Suppression; Integrated Automation; Heating, Ventilating, and Air-Conditioning
options.D: Fire Suppression; Plumbing; Heating, Ventilating, and Air-Conditioning
options.E: Electronic Safety and Security; Plumbing; Heating, Ventilating, and Air-Conditioning
options.F: Fire Suppression; Plumbing; Integrated Automation

questions.explanation: The Facility Services subgroup opens with Division 21 Fire Suppression, 22 Plumbing and 23 Heating, Ventilating, and Air-Conditioning (HVAC), then continues with 25 Integrated Automation, 26 Electrical, 27 Communications and 28 Electronic Safety and Security. Divisions 20, 24 and 29 are reserved, so Electrical is 26, not 23.

questions.question: MasterFormat's five titled divisions in the 30s, Divisions 31 through 35, are, in order: ____, ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: What are the titles of MasterFormat Divisions 31 through 35, in order?

options.A: Earthwork; Exterior Improvements; Utilities; Transportation; Waterway and Marine Construction
options.B: Earthwork; Exterior Improvements; Utilities; Transportation; Process Interconnections
options.C: Existing Conditions; Exterior Improvements; Utilities; Transportation; Waterway and Marine Construction
options.D: Earthwork; Planting; Utilities; Transportation; Waterway and Marine Construction
options.E: Earthwork; Exterior Improvements; Electrical; Transportation; Waterway and Marine Construction
options.F: Earthwork; Exterior Improvements; Utilities; Conveying Equipment; Waterway and Marine Construction

questions.explanation: The Site and Infrastructure subgroup holds Division 31 Earthwork, 32 Exterior Improvements, 33 Utilities, 34 Transportation and 35 Waterway and Marine Construction, with 30 and 36 through 39 reserved. Every project draws its civil work from this 30-series. Existing Conditions is Division 02, Conveying Equipment is 14, Planting is a title inside Division 32, and Process Interconnections opens the 40s.

questions.question: In specifications, 'provide' means to ____ and ____, complete and ready for the intended use.

mc.question: In specifications, 'provide' means to do which two things, complete and ready for the intended use?

options.A: Furnish and deliver
options.B: Furnish and install
options.C: Install and test
options.D: Coordinate and install
options.E: Design and install
options.F: Purchase and store

questions.explanation: 'Furnish' means to supply and deliver to the site ready for installation, 'install' means to put in position for service or use, and 'provide' means both, leaving the work complete and ready for use. 'Furnish and deliver' describes furnishing alone. Because the three words carry contract meaning, their definitions belong in the supplementary conditions or in Division 01.

questions.question: In SectionFormat and PageFormat terms, a Division is a standard category of construction specifications and the framework for project specifications; MasterFormat defines ____ of them.

mc.question: SectionFormat and PageFormat define a Division as a standard category of construction specifications. How many Divisions does MasterFormat define?

questions.explanation: MasterFormat numbers 50 divisions, 00 through 49, which together form the framework for organizing project specifications. Only 35 of them carry titles today; the rest, such as 20, 24, 29, 30 and 36 through 39, are reserved for future use. Counting just the titled divisions, or taking the highest number, 49, gives the wrong total.

questions.question: Because specifications are legal documents, formal punctuation applies, including the ____ comma: a comma follows every item in a series, even the one just before 'and' or 'or', as in 'clean walls, floors, and ceilings'.

mc.question: Because specifications are legal documents, formal punctuation applies. Which practice puts a comma after every item in a series, including the one before the conjunction, as in 'clean walls, floors, and ceilings'?

options.A: Streamlined form
options.B: The and/or construction
options.C: The Oxford comma
options.D: A colon at the end of a parent paragraph
options.E: Hierarchical indentation
options.F: A period after each list item

questions.explanation: Specifications are legal documents, so they follow formal punctuation and are written so that dropping or moving a mark cannot change the meaning. The Oxford (serial) comma goes after every item in a series, including the one before 'and' or 'or'. Colons and end periods govern paragraphs and lists rather than items in a series, and 'and/or' should be avoided altogether.

questions.question: In streamlined specification text, which puts the subject first, a ____ is understood to stand for 'shall', 'shall be' or 'shall comply with'.

mc.question: In streamlined specification text, which puts the subject first, which punctuation mark is understood to stand for 'shall', 'shall be' or 'shall comply with'?

options.A: Comma
options.B: Period
options.C: Colon
options.D: Slash
options.E: Parentheses
options.F: Hyphen

questions.explanation: Streamlining lists products, materials and standards with the subject first, then a colon, then the requirement, as in 'Portland Cement: ASTM C150, Type I'. A statement in Division 01 or the supplementary conditions should explain that the colon implies 'shall', 'shall be' or 'shall comply with' and that the imperative text is addressed to the Contractor.

questions.question: Apart from perspectives and isometrics, which digital models now produce easily, most design and construction drawings fall into five drawing types: ____, ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Apart from perspectives and isometrics, which five drawing types make up most design and construction drawings?

options.A: Plans, elevations, sections, details, legends
options.B: Plans, elevations, sections, shop drawings, schedules
options.C: Plans, elevations, title sheets, details, schedules
options.D: Plans, key plans, sections, details, schedules
options.E: Sketches, elevations, sections, details, schedules
options.F: Plans, elevations, sections, details, schedules

questions.explanation: Most drawing sets are built from plans, elevations, sections, details and schedules, each suited to showing a different kind of condition. Perspectives and isometrics, once kept for presenting design concepts, can now be generated easily from a digital model. Key plans, legends and title sheets are supporting views within the set, and shop drawings come from the contractor, not the design team.

questions.question: The AIA CAD Layer Guidelines define four data fields within a layer name: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which four data fields make up a layer name under the AIA CAD Layer Guidelines?

options.A: Discipline designator, major group, minor group, sheet number
options.B: Discipline designator, major group, minor group, status
options.C: Discipline designator, drawing type, minor group, status
options.D: Sheet number, major group, minor group, status
options.E: Discipline designator, major group, title block, status
options.F: Discipline designator, drawing type, sheet number, status

questions.explanation: A layer name strings together the discipline designator (such as architectural or structural), the major group (a building system such as walls), the minor group (which refines the major group) and the status (new, existing, temporary, not in contract or a phase). Sheet numbers come from sheet identification under the Uniform Drawing System, and drawing types or title blocks are handled with optional added identifiers, not the four basic fields.

questions.question: Besides the NIBS foreword, introduction and administration, the U.S. National CAD Standard consists of four parts: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Besides the NIBS foreword, introduction and administration, which four parts make up the U.S. National CAD Standard?

options.A: AIA CAD Layer Guidelines; Uniform Drawing System; BIM Implementation; MasterFormat
options.B: AIA CAD Layer Guidelines; UniFormat; BIM Implementation; Plotting Guidelines
options.C: OmniClass; Uniform Drawing System; BIM Implementation; Plotting Guidelines
options.D: AIA CAD Layer Guidelines; Uniform Drawing System; BIM Implementation; Plotting Guidelines
options.E: AIA CAD Layer Guidelines; Uniform Drawing System; SectionFormat; Plotting Guidelines
options.F: AIA CAD Layer Guidelines; Uniform Drawing System; MasterFormat; UniFormat

questions.explanation: The NCS, administered by the buildingSMART alliance of the National Institute of Building Sciences, combines the AIA CAD Layer Guidelines, the Uniform Drawing System, BIM Implementation and the Plotting Guidelines. MasterFormat, UniFormat and keynotes can be inserted into the Uniform Drawing System, but they, like OmniClass and SectionFormat, are separate standards rather than parts of the NCS.

questions.question: A small, symbolic view showing where a portion of the project sits within the whole, used with a larger-scale plan that presents only part of the project, is a ____.

mc.question: What is the small, symbolic view called that shows where a portion of the project sits within the whole, used with a larger-scale plan that presents only part of the project?

options.A: Match line
options.B: Key plan
options.C: Location map
options.D: Site plan
options.E: Title sheet
options.F: Enlarged floor plan

questions.explanation: A key plan is a small non-scaled view that shows how the part drawn on a sheet relates to the whole project, and it can also mark where sections or elevations are taken without sending the reader back to the full plan. A match line marks where a drawing continues on another sheet, and the location map on the title sheet places the project itself.

questions.question: Schedules, key plans, isometrics, perspectives and title sheets are typical ____ views, as opposed to plans, elevations and sections.

mc.question: Schedules, key plans, isometrics, perspectives and title sheets are typical examples of which kind of view?

options.A: Scaled
options.B: Enlarged
options.C: Non-scaled
options.D: Half-size
options.E: Large-scale
options.F: Detail

questions.explanation: Every view on a drawing is either scaled or non-scaled. Plans, elevations and sections are scaled views and should carry both a numeric and a graphic scale, since half-size prints are common on site. Schedules, key plans, isometrics, perspectives and title sheets are non-scaled, laid out in whatever way best presents their information.

questions.question: Drawings that the contractor prepares to fit together all the trades' requirements in a congested space, such as a small ceiling cavity shared by HVAC, plumbing, fire protection and electrical work, are ____ drawings.

mc.question: What are the drawings called that the contractor prepares to fit together all the trades' requirements in a congested space, such as a small ceiling cavity shared by HVAC, plumbing, fire protection and electrical work?

options.A: Shop drawings
options.B: Record drawings
options.C: Coordination drawings
options.D: Resource drawings
options.E: Supplemental drawings
options.F: Construction drawings

questions.explanation: Coordination drawings are prepared by the contractor during construction so the HVAC, plumbing, fire protection, electrical and telecommunications work in a tight space can be fitted together. Shop drawings show how one product will be fabricated and installed, record drawings are contract drawings marked up to show what was actually built, and supplemental drawings are issued by the architect/engineer to clarify or change the documents.

questions.question: In public work, regulations usually require the solicitation to be published as a legal notice addressed to all qualified bidders. The solicitation then takes the form of an ____, rather than an invitation to bid, which goes only to bidders the owner selects.

mc.question: In public work, regulations usually require the solicitation to be published as a legal notice addressed to all qualified bidders. What form does the solicitation then take?

options.A: Invitation to bid
options.B: Request for proposal
options.C: Advertisement for bids
options.D: Request for qualifications
options.E: Notice of award
options.F: Instructions to bidders

questions.explanation: When law or policy requires public notice, the solicitation is an advertisement for bids, published in newspapers or on project or government websites and open to every qualified bidder. In private work the legal notice is usually skipped and an invitation to bid goes only to selected contractors. Requests for proposal and for qualifications belong to the competitive proposal process, and the notice of award is the owner's acceptance of a bid.

questions.question: The invitation to bid should be short and simple and leave out detailed requirements. Information a bidder needs to actually prepare and submit a bid belongs in the ____.

mc.question: The invitation to bid should be short and simple and leave out detailed requirements. Where does the information a bidder needs to actually prepare and submit a bid belong?

options.A: Bid form
options.B: Advertisement for bids
options.C: Supplementary conditions
options.D: Instructions to bidders
options.E: Owner-contractor agreement
options.F: General conditions

questions.explanation: The instructions to bidders run longer than the solicitation because they tell bidders how to prepare and submit a bid and state the conditions that will govern the award. The invitation or advertisement only announces the project, and the bid form is the document the bidder fills in, not the place for the rules. The agreement and the conditions govern the contract after award.

questions.question: To curb bid shopping on some public works, prequalified subcontractors send their prices directly to the owner rather than through the prime contractor. This arrangement is a ____.

mc.question: To curb bid shopping on some public works, prequalified subcontractors send their prices directly to the owner rather than through the prime contractor. What is this arrangement called?

options.A: Bid listing
options.B: Bid security
options.C: Bid depository
options.D: Prequalification of bidders
options.E: Competitive proposal
options.F: Request for qualifications

questions.explanation: Bid shopping is a bidder revealing one subcontractor's price to squeeze a lower one from another. A bid depository counters it by having prequalified subcontractors file their prices with the owner, independent of the prime contractor. Bid listing, where bidders name their subcontractors in the bid, is a different control and can hamper the contractor if a listed firm will not sign a subcontract.

questions.question: The bid form is typically not a contract document, but the price, unit prices, alternate prices and completion time from the successful bid are carried into the ____.

mc.question: The bid form is typically not a contract document. Into which document are the price, unit prices, alternate prices and completion time from the successful bid carried?

options.A: General conditions
options.B: Owner-contractor agreement
options.C: Supplementary conditions
options.D: Instructions to bidders
options.E: Schedule of values
options.F: Performance bond

questions.explanation: Because the bid form usually stays outside the contract, the figures that matter from the winning bid (contract price, unit prices, accepted alternates and time of completion) are written into the owner-contractor agreement, which is a contract document. For the same reason, a liquidated damages amount must appear in the agreement or the conditions, and only once, rather than only on the bid form.

questions.question: Five Division 01 groupings align with SectionFormat PART 1—GENERAL: ____, ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which five Division 01 groupings align with SectionFormat PART 1—GENERAL? (Listed alphabetically.)

options.A: Administrative Requirements; Price and Payment Procedures; Product Requirements; Summary; Temporary Facilities and Controls
options.B: Administrative Requirements; Execution and Closeout Requirements; Price and Payment Procedures; Quality Assurance; Summary
options.C: Administrative Requirements; Performance Requirements; Quality Assurance; Summary; Temporary Facilities and Controls
options.D: Price and Payment Procedures; Quality Assurance; Quality Control; Summary; Temporary Facilities and Controls
options.E: Administrative Requirements; Life Cycle Activities; Price and Payment Procedures; Quality Assurance; Temporary Facilities and Controls
options.F: Administrative Requirements; Price and Payment Procedures; Quality Assurance; Summary; Temporary Facilities and Controls

questions.explanation: Division 01 mirrors the three parts of a section. Summary, Price and Payment Procedures, Administrative Requirements, Quality Assurance, and Temporary Facilities and Controls match PART 1—GENERAL; Product Requirements, Performance Requirements and source quality control match PART 2—PRODUCTS; field quality control, Execution and Closeout Requirements, and Life Cycle Activities match PART 3—EXECUTION.

questions.question: Bid bond information belongs in the procurement requirements, while the requirements for performance and payment bonds should be stated in the ____.

mc.question: Bid bond information belongs in the procurement requirements. Where should the requirements for performance and payment bonds be stated?

options.A: Instructions to bidders
options.B: Bid form
options.C: General conditions
options.D: Supplementary conditions
options.E: Advertisement for bids
options.F: Section 01 29 00—Payment Procedures

questions.explanation: A bid bond matters only during bidding, so it is a procurement requirement; performance and payment bonds are part of the contract, and the supplementary conditions state what is required for them. The architect/engineer should get the bond information from the owner early enough to put it in the project manual. On AIA projects much of the bond and insurance detail now sits in the A101 attachment titled Insurance and Bonds.

questions.question: Non-practitioners often call Division 00 and Division 01 the "____" documents, a term specifiers avoid in favor of the division names themselves.

mc.question: Non-practitioners often call Division 00 and Division 01 by a nickname that specifiers avoid in favor of the division names. Which term is it?

options.A: Project manual
options.B: Front end
options.C: Technical
options.D: Bidding
options.E: Contract
options.F: Procurement

questions.explanation: Divisions 00 and 01 are non-technical, and people outside specification writing often lump them together as 'front end' documents; the recommended practice is to call them Division 00 and Division 01. Before writing either, the specifier must review the owner's proposed agreement and conditions of the contract. The project manual is the whole bound volume, and procurement, contract and bidding documents are defined sets, not nicknames.

questions.question: The basic requirements for the contractor's options in selecting among specified products, without making a substitution, go in Section 01 62 00—____.

mc.question: Which Division 01 section, numbered 01 62 00, covers the contractor's options in selecting among specified products, including the rules for deciding whether products are equivalent?

options.A: Substitution Procedures
options.B: Product Requirements
options.C: Product Options
options.D: Common Product Requirements
options.E: Owner-Furnished Products
options.F: Product Delivery Requirements
