questions.explanation: Section 01 62 00—Product Options sets the general rules for the contractor's choices among the products the documents already allow, including how to decide whether products are equivalent. A proposal to use a product that is not specified is a substitution and goes through Section 01 25 00—Substitution Procedures, and 01 60 00 Product Requirements is the broad title over the product sections.

questions.question: When the work in the project manual and drawings will be done under more than one contract (for example, multiple-prime contracts), the contracts and the scope of each are described in Section 01 12 00—____.

mc.question: Which section, numbered 01 12 00, describes the contracts and the scope of each when the work will be done under more than one contract, such as multiple-prime contracts?

options.A: Summary of Work
options.B: Multiple Contract Summary
options.C: Work Restrictions
options.D: Project Management and Coordination
options.E: Owner-Furnished Products
options.F: Special Procedures

questions.explanation: Section 01 12 00—Multiple Contract Summary is used when the work is split among several contracts, as with multiple-prime contracts, construction management and some design-build projects; it identifies each contract, its scope and any owner-furnished items. A single-contract project uses 01 11 00—Summary of Work, and coordination duties among the contractors are assigned in 01 31 00—Project Management and Coordination.

questions.question: Record documents, warranties, spare parts, and operation and maintenance data are specified in Section 01 78 00—____, while the procedures for substantial and final completion and the punch list go in Section 01 77 00—Closeout Procedures.

mc.question: Section 01 77 00—Closeout Procedures covers the steps to substantial and final completion. What is the title of Section 01 78 00, which covers record documents, warranties, spare parts, and operation and maintenance data?

options.A: Submittal Procedures
options.B: Demonstration and Training
options.C: Closeout Submittals
options.D: Facility Maintenance
options.E: Execution and Closeout Requirements
options.F: Starting and Adjusting

questions.explanation: Section 01 78 00—Closeout Submittals specifies what is handed over at the end of the job (record documents, warranties, spare parts, and operation and maintenance data), along with how many copies and in what form. Section 01 77 00 covers the procedures for reaching completion, 01 79 00 covers demonstration and owner training, and 01 33 00 covers submittals during construction.

questions.question: MasterFormat places seven sections under 01 20 00—Price and Payment Procedures. Besides 01 29 00—Payment Procedures, give the exact titles of the other six, 01 21 00 through 01 26 00: ____, ____, ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Besides 01 29 00—Payment Procedures, which list gives the titles of 01 21 00 through 01 26 00 under 01 20 00—Price and Payment Procedures, in order?

options.A: Allowances; Unit Prices; Alternates; Value Engineering; Substitution Procedures; Contract Modification Procedures
options.B: Allowances; Unit Prices; Alternates; Value Analysis; Product Options; Contract Modification Procedures
options.C: Allowances; Schedule of Values; Alternates; Value Analysis; Substitution Procedures; Contract Modification Procedures
options.D: Allowances; Unit Prices; Alternates; Value Analysis; Substitution Procedures; Contract Modification Procedures
options.E: Allowances; Unit Prices; Alternates; Value Analysis; Substitution Procedures; Change Orders
options.F: Allowances; Unit Prices; Requests for Information; Value Analysis; Substitution Procedures; Contract Modification Procedures

questions.explanation: The 01 20 00 group runs 01 21 00 Allowances, 01 22 00 Unit Prices, 01 23 00 Alternates, 01 24 00 Value Analysis, 01 25 00 Substitution Procedures and 01 26 00 Contract Modification Procedures, then 01 29 00 Payment Procedures. Value Engineering (01 24 13), Requests for Information (01 26 13), Change Orders (01 26 63) and Schedule of Values (01 29 73) are narrower titles inside these sections, and Product Options is 01 62 00.

questions.question: Under A201 §3.8.2, an allowance covers only the cost of materials and equipment delivered to the site plus required taxes, less trade discounts. The contractor's unloading and handling, labor, installation, overhead and profit for allowance items are included in the ____ but not in the allowance.

mc.question: Under A201 §3.8.2, an allowance covers only the cost of materials and equipment delivered to the site plus required taxes, less trade discounts. Where are the contractor's unloading and handling, labor, installation, overhead and profit for allowance items included?

options.A: In the allowance amount itself
options.B: In a markup added to the allowance when it is spent
options.C: In the Contract Sum, but not in the allowance
options.D: In the Owner's contingency allowance
options.E: In the unit prices
options.F: In a Change Order issued after the allowance item is installed

questions.explanation: Unless the documents say otherwise, an allowance pays only for the delivered materials and equipment and their taxes; the contractor's handling, labor, installation, overhead and profit for that work are already in the Contract Sum. When the actual cost differs from the allowance, a Change Order adjusts the Contract Sum by the difference. EJCDC C-700 13.02 says the same, using the term Contract Price.

questions.question: Besides cash allowances, EJCDC C-700 13.02 provides for an Owner's ____ allowance, which is for the sole use of the Owner to cover unanticipated costs.

mc.question: EJCDC C-700 13.02 provides for an Owner's allowance that is reserved for the Owner's sole use to cover unanticipated costs. What kind of allowance is it?

options.A: Cash allowance
options.B: Quantity allowance
options.C: Contingency allowance
options.D: Time allowance
options.E: Installation allowance
options.F: Testing and inspecting allowance

questions.explanation: An Owner's contingency allowance, if the contract includes one, belongs to the Owner alone and covers costs nobody anticipated. A cash allowance, by contrast, covers specified materials and equipment delivered to the site plus taxes, with the contractor's handling, labor, overhead and profit already in the Contract Price. Before final payment a Change Order adjusts the Contract Price to the actual amounts for allowance work.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700 13.03, after reviewing its preliminary findings with the contractor, the ____ determines the quantities and classifications of Unit Price Work actually performed.

mc.question: Under EJCDC C-700 13.03, who determines the actual quantities and classifications of Unit Price Work the contractor has performed?

options.A: Owner
options.B: Contractor
options.C: Engineer
options.D: Resident Project Representative
options.E: Owner and Contractor by mutual agreement
options.F: Independent testing laboratory

questions.explanation: The Engineer makes the determination after going over its preliminary findings with the contractor, and its written decision is final and binding unless corrected for changed facts or better data. The estimated quantities in the Agreement are not guaranteed; they serve to compare bids and set an initial Contract Price, and payment follows actual quantities. A Resident Project Representative only assists the Engineer at the site.

questions.question: Alternates on the bid form may be either ____ or ____, with a blank provided for each, and each one must be fully described in Section 01 23 00—Alternates.

mc.question: Alternates requested on the bid form, each fully described in Section 01 23 00, may be of which two kinds?

options.A: Cash or quantity
options.B: Additive or deductive
options.C: Lump sum or unit price
options.D: Fixed or percentage
options.E: Mandatory or voluntary
options.F: Stipulated or negotiated

questions.explanation: An alternate either adds work and cost to the base bid or deducts them, so the bid form gives a blank for each alternate's price, Section 01 23 00 defines exactly what each one includes, and the instructions to bidders explain how to price them. Alternates complicate bidding and can raise prices, so they should be few. Cash and quantity describe allowances, and fixed or percentage describe fees.

questions.question: Under A201 §7.3.4, if quantities originally contemplated are materially changed so that applying the agreed unit prices would cause ____ to the Owner or Contractor, the applicable unit prices are equitably adjusted.

mc.question: Under A201 §7.3.4, agreed unit prices are equitably adjusted when quantities change so much that applying them would cause what to the Owner or Contractor?

options.A: Undue hardship
options.B: Substantial inequity
options.C: A material breach
options.D: Consequential damages
options.E: Unreasonable delay
options.F: Liquidated damages

questions.explanation: A201 lets either party have unit prices adjusted when a Change Order or Construction Change Directive changes the planned quantities so much that the original prices would be substantially inequitable. EJCDC C-700 uses a two-part test instead: the quantity must differ materially and significantly from the estimate, and the contractor's unit costs must have changed materially and significantly as a result.

questions.question: When the contractor disagrees with a Construction Change Directive's pricing method and the Architect determines the adjustment under A201 §7.3.7, costs are limited (unless the Contract Documents say otherwise) to five categories: ____, ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: When the Architect determines a Construction Change Directive adjustment under A201 §7.3.7, which five cost categories are allowed (unless the Contract Documents say otherwise)?

options.A: Labor; materials, supplies and equipment; hand tools; bond and insurance premiums, permit fees and taxes; added supervision and field office personnel
options.B: Labor; materials, supplies and equipment; rental of machinery and equipment; bond and insurance premiums, permit fees and taxes; principal office expenses
options.C: Labor; materials, supplies and equipment; rental of machinery and equipment; contingency; added supervision and field office personnel
options.D: Financing costs; materials, supplies and equipment; rental of machinery and equipment; bond and insurance premiums, permit fees and taxes; added supervision and field office personnel
options.E: Labor; materials, supplies and equipment; rental of machinery and equipment; bond and insurance premiums, permit fees and taxes; added supervision and field office personnel
options.F: Labor; small tools; rental of machinery and equipment; bond and insurance premiums, permit fees and taxes; added supervision and field office personnel

questions.explanation: Under §7.3.7 the Architect prices the change from reasonable expenditures and savings, allowing labor (with payroll taxes, benefits and workers' compensation), materials, supplies and equipment, rental of machinery and equipment except hand tools, bond and insurance premiums with permit fees and taxes, and added supervision and field office personnel, plus overhead and profit as the Agreement sets. Principal office expenses, financing and contingencies are not on the list.

questions.question: When a Construction Change Directive adjusts the Contract Sum, A201 §7.3.3 bases the adjustment on one of three agreed methods (failing those, the Architect determines it under §7.3.7): ____, ____, ____.
answers: cost of the work plus a fee

mc.question: Which three agreed methods can A201 §7.3.3 use to set the Contract Sum adjustment in a Construction Change Directive (failing those, the Architect determines it under §7.3.7)?

options.A: Itemized lump sum; unit prices; guaranteed maximum price
options.B: Itemized lump sum; allowances; cost plus a fixed or percentage fee
options.C: Guaranteed maximum price; unit prices; cost plus a fixed or percentage fee
options.D: Itemized lump sum; schedule of values; liquidated damages
options.E: Schedule of values; unit prices; guaranteed maximum price
options.F: Itemized lump sum; unit prices; cost plus a fixed or percentage fee

questions.explanation: The three agreed bases are a properly itemized lump sum backed by enough data to evaluate it, unit prices stated in the Contract Documents or agreed later, and cost determined as the parties agree plus a mutually acceptable fixed or percentage fee. If the contractor does not respond or disagrees, the Architect sets the adjustment from reasonable expenditures and savings. A guaranteed maximum price and a schedule of values describe the contract sum, not ways to price a change.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700 7.05, when an item is specified by naming one or more proprietary items, the specification is intended to establish four characteristics required: ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Under EJCDC C-700 7.05, naming one or more proprietary items in a specification is intended to establish which four characteristics of the item required?

options.A: Type, function, appearance, cost
options.B: Type, performance, appearance, quality
options.C: Manufacturer, function, appearance, quality
options.D: Type, function, durability, quality
options.E: Type, function, appearance, warranty
options.F: Type, function, appearance, quality

questions.explanation: Naming proprietary items sets the type, function, appearance and quality the owner requires. Unless the specification says no 'or equal' is allowed, the contractor may ask the Engineer to accept another item, which qualifies only if it is at least equal in materials, quality, durability, appearance and strength, performs the same function, and adds no cost or time. An item that fails can still be proposed as a substitute under 7.06.

questions.question: Under A201 §3.4.2, except for minor changes authorized by the Architect, the contractor may make substitutions only with the consent of the ____, after evaluation by the Architect and in accordance with a Change Order or Construction Change Directive.

mc.question: Under A201 §3.4.2, apart from minor changes the Architect authorizes, whose consent does the contractor need to make a substitution, after the Architect's evaluation?

options.A: Architect
options.B: Owner
options.C: Initial Decision Maker
options.D: Surety
options.E: Authorities having jurisdiction
options.F: Subcontractor who installs it

questions.explanation: A substitution changes what the Owner is buying, so A201 requires the Owner's consent, given after the Architect has evaluated the proposal and documented by Change Order or Construction Change Directive. The Architect evaluates but cannot approve a substitution alone; on its own authority it can order only minor changes that involve no change in Contract Sum or Contract Time.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700 7.05, the Engineer is the sole judge of whether a proposed item is an "or-equal," and neither approval nor denial of an or-equal request results in any change in the ____.

mc.question: Under EJCDC C-700 7.05, what is the effect of the Engineer's approval or denial of an 'or-equal' request?

options.A: The Owner receives a credit for any savings
options.B: The Contract Price does not change
options.C: The savings are split equally between Owner and Contractor
options.D: The Contractor is reimbursed for preparing the supporting data
options.E: The cost difference is added by Change Order
options.F: A denial can be appealed as a Claim

questions.explanation: An or-equal is, by definition, an item at least equal to the named one that adds no cost or time, so C-700 says neither approval nor denial changes the Contract Price. The contractor pays for the supporting data, the Engineer alone judges acceptability, and a denial is final and cannot be appealed. An item that does not qualify can instead be proposed as a substitute under 7.06, which has its own criteria and review.

questions.question: Under A201 §7.3.8, the credit the contractor allows the Owner for a deletion or change that results in a net decrease in the Contract Sum is the ____, as confirmed by the Architect.

mc.question: Under A201 §7.3.8, how is the credit figured that the contractor gives the Owner for a deletion or change that reduces the Contract Sum?

options.A: Estimated cost
options.B: Value shown in the schedule of values
options.C: Actual net cost, as confirmed by the Architect
options.D: Original bid amount
options.E: Replacement cost
options.F: Cost plus overhead and profit

questions.explanation: For a deletion or other change that lowers the price, the Owner's credit is the contractor's actual net cost, confirmed by the Architect, not an estimate or the value carried in the schedule of values. When one change both adds and credits related work, overhead and profit are figured only on the net increase, if there is one.

questions.question: Under A201 §3.12.8, the Architect's approval of a submittal does not relieve the contractor of responsibility for a deviation from the Contract Documents unless the contractor specifically told the Architect ____ about the deviation when submitting it, and the Architect gave written approval to that specific deviation (or a Change Order or Construction Change Directive authorized it).

mc.question: Under A201 §3.12.8, the Architect's approval of a submittal relieves the contractor of a deviation from the Contract Documents only if the contractor flagged the deviation at the time of submittal in what way?

options.A: Orally
options.B: In writing
options.C: Through the Owner
options.D: At the next progress meeting
options.E: Through the subcontractor who prepared it
options.F: By telephone

questions.explanation: The contractor stays responsible for deviations, and for errors or omissions in submittals, unless it pointed out the deviation in writing when it submitted, and then either the Architect approved that specific deviation in writing as a minor change or a Change Order or Construction Change Directive authorized it. On resubmittals, too, the contractor must call out in writing any revisions the Architect did not ask for.

questions.question: Under A201 §4.2.7, the Architect reviews shop drawings, product data and samples only to check that they conform with the information given and the ____ expressed in the Contract Documents.

mc.question: Under A201 §4.2.7, the Architect reviews shop drawings, product data and samples only for conformance with the information given and what else expressed in the Contract Documents?

options.A: Construction means and methods
options.B: Dimensions and quantities
options.C: Design concept
options.D: Safety precautions
options.E: Installation instructions
options.F: Performance of equipment and systems

questions.explanation: The Architect's review is limited: it checks submittals against the information in the Contract Documents and the design concept they express. It does not verify dimensions and quantities, installation instructions or equipment performance, which stay the contractor's responsibility, and it does not approve safety precautions or construction means and methods. Submittals themselves are not Contract Documents.

questions.question: Within 10 days after the Effective Date of the Contract, EJCDC C-700 2.03 requires the contractor to submit three preliminary schedules to the Engineer: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Within 10 days after the Effective Date of the Contract, which three preliminary schedules does EJCDC C-700 2.03 require the contractor to submit to the Engineer?

options.A: Progress Schedule; Schedule of Submittals; Unit Prices Schedule
options.B: Progress Schedule; Certificates of Insurance; Schedule of Values
options.C: Safety Program; Schedule of Submittals; Schedule of Values
options.D: Progress Schedule; Schedule of Submittals; Schedule of Values
options.E: Progress Schedule; Schedule of Submittals; Certificates of Insurance
options.F: Safety Program; Certificates of Insurance; Schedule of Values

questions.explanation: The contractor submits a preliminary Progress Schedule (start and finish of the stages of the Work, with any Milestones), a preliminary Schedule of Submittals and a preliminary Schedule of Values that adds up to the Contract Price. They are reviewed at a conference at least 10 days before the first Application for Payment, and no progress payment is made until acceptable schedules are in. Certificates of insurance and safety programs are handled under other paragraphs.

questions.question: The law governing contracts for the sale of goods between buyers and sellers, adopted in every state except Louisiana, is Article ____ of the Uniform Commercial Code.

mc.question: Which article of the Uniform Commercial Code governs contracts for the sale of goods between buyers and sellers and has been adopted in every state except Louisiana?

options.A: Article 1
options.B: Article 2
options.C: Article 2A
options.D: Article 3
options.E: Article 4
options.F: Article 9

questions.explanation: Article 2 (Sales) is the UCC article that governs purchasing contracts for movable goods, covering how contracts are formed, the obligations of seller and buyer, performance, breach and remedies; contracts mainly for services fall outside it. Each state adopts the UCC separately, so details vary, and Louisiana has not adopted Article 2. Other articles deal with matters such as negotiable instruments and secured transactions.

questions.question: When A201 §3.12.10 requires professional design services of the contractor, they must be provided by a properly licensed design professional whose ____ and ____ appear on all drawings, calculations, specifications, certifications and submittals that professional prepares.

mc.question: When A201 §3.12.10 requires professional design services of the contractor, what must appear on every drawing, calculation, specification, certification and submittal the licensed design professional prepares?

options.A: Signature and date
options.B: Signature and seal
options.C: Name and license number
options.D: Seal and license number
options.E: Initials and date
options.F: Firm name and address

questions.explanation: Delegated design must come from a properly licensed design professional whose signature and seal appear on everything that professional prepares. The Owner and Architect must spell out all the performance and design criteria the design has to meet, and the Architect then reviews the signed and sealed submittals only for conformance with the design concept, relying on the professional's work.

questions.question: A railing section delegates the structural design to a professional engineer engaged by the contractor. PART 1 asks for a delegated-design submittal signed and sealed by that engineer, and PART 2 includes an article, commonly titled ____, that holds the 'Delegated Design' paragraph and the loads the railing must withstand.

mc.question: A railing section delegates the structural design to a professional engineer engaged by the contractor, and PART 1 asks for a signed and sealed delegated-design submittal. In PART 2, which article commonly holds the 'Delegated Design' paragraph and the loads the railing must withstand?

options.A: Regulatory Requirements
options.B: Source Quality Control
options.C: Performance Requirements
options.D: Materials
options.E: Fabrication
options.F: Manufacturers

questions.explanation: When design is delegated, the section must say what is delegated and state the criteria, usually in a PART 2 performance requirements article (SectionFormat lists it as Performance/Design Criteria): engage a qualified professional engineer, then the structural loads the design must resist. PART 1 requires the delegated-design submittal, signed and sealed by that engineer, and anything not delegated, such as the finish, is specified in the usual way.

questions.question: A construction bond is a three-party agreement. Name the three parties: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: A construction bond is a three-party agreement. Which three parties does it bind?

options.A: Principal, surety, claimant
options.B: Principal, indemnitor, obligee
options.C: Principal, surety, obligee
options.D: Named insured, surety, obligee
options.E: Principal, insurer, obligee
options.F: Indemnitee, surety, claimant

questions.explanation: The principal (the contractor) stays primarily liable for the bonded obligation and must indemnify the surety; the surety (the bonding company) is only secondarily liable, much like a cosigner on a note; and the obligee (the owner) is the party the bond protects. Unlike an insurer, a surety expects to be repaid by the principal. A claimant is someone seeking payment under a payment bond, not a party to it.

questions.question: Construction projects use three basic types of bonds (the first a procurement requirement, the other two contract documents): ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Which three basic types of bonds are used on construction projects (one a procurement requirement, the other two contract documents)?

options.A: Bid bond, performance bond, maintenance bond
options.B: Bid bond, warranty bond, payment bond
options.C: Lien bond, performance bond, payment bond
options.D: Bid bond, performance bond, payment bond
options.E: Bid bond, performance bond, retainage bond
options.F: Maintenance bond, warranty bond, payment bond

questions.explanation: The three basic bonds are the bid bond, a procurement requirement that protects the owner if the selected bidder fails to sign the contract, and the performance and payment bonds, contract documents that protect the owner against contractor default and unpaid subcontractors and suppliers. Warranty or maintenance bonds, when needed, are usually called for in individual specification sections, and lien and retainage bond forms serve special purposes.

questions.question: A basic commercial general liability policy has an exclusion known as XCU. Removing it covers claims arising from the three hazards the letters stand for: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: A basic commercial general liability policy has an exclusion known as XCU. Which three hazards do the letters stand for?

options.A: Excavation, collapse, underground property damage
options.B: Explosion, contamination, underground property damage
options.C: Explosion, collapse, utility interruption
options.D: Explosion, collapse, underground property damage
options.E: Excavation, contamination, utility interruption
options.F: Explosion, pollution, underground property damage

questions.explanation: XCU stands for explosion, collapse and underground property damage. Deleting the exclusion is advisable when the work carries those risks, because it restores coverage for blasting, for structures that collapse when excavation or removal of shoring takes away their support, and for underground damage caused by mechanical excavation. Excavation is the cause behind two of the hazards, not one of the letters.

questions.question: A surety's agent usually proves authority to sign a bond for the surety with a ____, and the procurement instructions should require a copy to be attached to the executed bond.

mc.question: What document usually proves that an agent is authorized to sign a bond on behalf of the surety?

options.A: Consent of surety
options.B: Certificate of insurance
options.C: Power of attorney
options.D: Indemnity agreement
options.E: Notarized affidavit
options.F: Treasury listing of acceptable sureties

questions.explanation: A power of attorney names the agent who may bind the surety, so a copy should be filed with the signed bond; EJCDC C-700 likewise requires a bond signed by an agent or attorney-in-fact to come with a certified copy of that authority. A consent of surety approves final payment, the indemnity agreement runs between principal and surety, and the federal Treasury listing shows which sureties are acceptable.

questions.question: Most payment bonds require remote claimants, such as sub-subcontractors, to notify the contractor in writing that they have not been paid within ____ days after they last furnished labor or material to the project.

mc.question: Most payment bonds require remote claimants, such as sub-subcontractors, to give the contractor written notice of nonpayment within how many days after they last furnished labor or material?

options.A: 21 days
options.B: 30 days
options.C: 60 days
options.D: 90 days
options.E: 120 days
options.F: 180 days

questions.explanation: Remote claimants, who have no contract with the contractor, typically must give written notice within 90 days of last furnishing labor or material. The notice protects a contractor that has already paid its first-tier subcontractor from paying again for that subcontractor's unpaid suppliers. Claimants must also sue within a fairly short period, and only labor and material for the bonded project are covered.

questions.question: Subsurface investigations, surveys, existing-condition records and hazardous-material reports furnished to bidders are grouped in the procurement requirements as ____. They are for preparing bids and are not part of the contract documents.

mc.question: Subsurface investigations, surveys, existing-condition records and hazardous-material reports furnished to bidders are grouped in the procurement requirements under which heading?

options.A: Existing Conditions
options.B: Instructions for Procurement
options.C: Available Information
options.D: Procurement Forms and Supplements
options.E: Supplementary Conditions
options.F: Record Documents

questions.explanation: MasterFormat 00 30 00 Available Information holds the reports and data the owner furnishes for bidders' use. It is issued with a disclaimer, is not a contract document, and does not relieve bidders of their own investigations; its recommendations, such as a geotechnical compaction test, may even differ from the specifications. Division 02 Existing Conditions specifies work on existing construction, not bidding information.

questions.question: Most commercial general liability policies are written on the ____ basis: coverage is fixed by when the damaging event happened, so the policy need not still be in force when the claim is made.

mc.question: On which basis are most commercial general liability policies written, so that coverage depends on when the damaging event happened and the policy need not still be in force when the claim is made?

options.A: Claims-made
options.B: Occurrence
options.C: Completed value
options.D: Reporting
options.E: Named peril
options.F: All-risk

questions.explanation: Under occurrence-basis coverage, the policy in force when the damage happened responds even if the claim comes years later; it is the usual form and protects the owner better. A claims-made policy covers only if insurance stays in force continuously from the event to the claim, which is hard to ensure after the contractor leaves, so it is seldom used for construction. Completed value, reporting, named peril and all-risk describe property insurance.

questions.question: Builder's risk insurance is written in one of two forms: ____ (written for the project's anticipated value when finished, and used on most projects) or ____ (revised regularly, usually with each payment application, as the insured value grows).

mc.question: Builder's risk insurance comes in two forms: one written for the project's anticipated value when finished and used on most projects, and one revised regularly, usually with each payment application, as the insured value grows. Which pair names them in that order?

options.A: Completed value; claims-made
options.B: Completed value; reporting
options.C: All-risk; reporting
options.D: Replacement cost; reporting
options.E: Occurrence; claims-made
options.F: Named peril; all-risk

questions.explanation: The completed value form insures the anticipated finished value from the start and is required by AIA and EJCDC documents. The reporting form starts at the actual value and is raised at each report, so premiums track the insured value, but a missed report can leave the owner underinsured. Named peril and all-risk describe which perils are covered, and occurrence and claims-made describe liability policies.

questions.question: Contract documents should require that the owner and the A/E be named ____ under the contractor's liability coverage. This extends the policy's benefits for the contractor's operations to them but does not cover their own errors or omissions.

mc.question: Contract documents should require that the owner and the A/E be listed on the contractor's liability policy in which role, giving them the policy's benefits for the contractor's operations but not covering their own errors or omissions?

options.A: Named insureds
options.B: Additional insureds
options.C: Obligees
options.D: Indemnitees
options.E: Claimants
options.F: Principals

questions.explanation: As additional insureds, the owner and A/E share the contractor's coverage for the contractor's operations; the insurer does not broaden the policy, and the contractor remains the named insured. Their own acts, errors or omissions are covered only by their professional liability policies, and this endorsement is no substitute for owner's protective liability insurance, which usually gives greater coverage.

questions.question: Under A201 §9.8.4, the Certificate of Substantial Completion establishes the responsibilities of the Owner and Contractor for six things: ____, ____, ____, ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: Under A201 §9.8.4, the Certificate of Substantial Completion establishes the Owner's and Contractor's responsibilities for which six things?

options.A: Security, maintenance, heat, utilities, damage to the Work, warranties
options.B: Security, cleaning, heat, utilities, damage to the Work, insurance
options.C: Security, maintenance, heat, utilities, damage to the Work, insurance
options.D: Security, maintenance, heat, utilities, retainage, insurance
options.E: Punch list, maintenance, heat, utilities, damage to the Work, insurance
options.F: Security, maintenance, commissioning, utilities, damage to the Work, insurance

questions.explanation: The Architect's Certificate of Substantial Completion fixes the date of Substantial Completion, divides responsibility between Owner and Contractor for security, maintenance, heat, utilities, damage to the Work and insurance, and sets the time for finishing the items on the attached list. Warranties are not on that list; they start on the date of Substantial Completion unless the Certificate says otherwise.

questions.question: Under A201 §9.10.4, making final payment waives the Owner's Claims except those arising from three things: ____, ____, ____.
answers: failure of the Work to comply

mc.question: Under A201 §9.10.4, making final payment waives the Owner's Claims except those arising from which three things?

options.A: Unsettled liens and claims; failure of the Work to comply with the Contract Documents; liquidated damages
options.B: Unsettled liens and claims; failure of the Work to comply with the Contract Documents; terms of special warranties
options.C: Unsettled liens and claims; consequential damages; terms of special warranties
options.D: Concealed conditions; failure of the Work to comply with the Contract Documents; terms of special warranties
options.E: Concealed conditions; consequential damages; liquidated damages
options.F: Unsettled liens and claims; concealed conditions; liquidated damages

questions.explanation: Final payment ends the Owner's Claims except for liens, Claims, security interests or encumbrances arising from the Contract that are still unsettled; failure of the Work to comply with the Contract Documents; and the terms of special warranties the documents require. On the other side, a contractor that accepts final payment waives all claims except those already made in writing and still identified as unsettled.

questions.question: Name the three steps a Claim passes through under A201 Article 15: ____, ____, ____.

mc.question: In order, which three steps does a Claim pass through under A201 Article 15?

options.A: Negotiation; mediation; binding dispute resolution
options.B: Initial decision; dispute review board; binding dispute resolution
options.C: Initial decision; mediation; dispute review board
options.D: Negotiation; dispute review board; arbitration
options.E: Initial decision; mediation; binding dispute resolution
options.F: Initial decision; negotiation; dispute review board

questions.explanation: A Claim first goes to the Initial Decision Maker (the Architect unless the Agreement names someone else); mediation is then a condition precedent to binding dispute resolution, which is arbitration or litigation as chosen in the Agreement. Industry guidance calls this a step dispute resolution process. Negotiation and dispute review boards can help settle disputes, but neither is a required step under A201.

questions.question: A201 §15.1.6 is a mutual waiver of ____ damages: the Owner gives up claims for lost rental income, financing and business losses, and the Contractor gives up principal office expenses and profit other than anticipated profit on the Work.

mc.question: A201 §15.1.6, under which the Owner gives up claims for lost rental income, financing and business losses and the Contractor gives up principal office expenses and profit beyond that on the Work, is a mutual waiver of which kind of damages?

options.A: Liquidated
options.B: Consequential
options.C: Actual
options.D: Punitive
options.E: Incidental
options.F: Compensatory

questions.explanation: In §15.1.6 the Owner and Contractor waive consequential damages against each other: the Owner's lost use, income, profit, financing and reputation, and the Contractor's principal office costs, lost financing and business, and profit other than anticipated profit on the Work. The waiver applies even after termination, but it does not block liquidated damages where the Contract Documents provide for them.

questions.question: AIA A201 requires Claims to be initiated within 21 days. Under EJCDC C-700 ¶12.01, a Claim must be delivered directly to the other party promptly, and in no event later than ____ days after the start of the event giving rise to it.

mc.question: AIA A201 requires Claims to be initiated within 21 days. Under EJCDC C-700 ¶12.01, what is the latest a Claim may be delivered to the other party, counted from the start of the event giving rise to it?

options.A: 7 days
options.B: 10 days
options.C: 14 days
options.D: 21 days
options.E: 30 days
options.F: 60 days

questions.explanation: EJCDC C-700 requires a Claim to reach the other party promptly and no later than 30 days after the event starts (or within 30 days of an Engineer's decision on a Change Proposal that is being appealed), with a copy to the Engineer for information. The 21-day limit belongs to AIA A201, which counts from the event or from when the claimant first recognizes the condition, whichever is later.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700 ¶4.01, if no Notice to Proceed is given, the Contract Times start to run on the ____ day after the Effective Date of the Contract.

mc.question: Under EJCDC C-700 ¶4.01, if no Notice to Proceed is given, on which day after the Effective Date of the Contract do the Contract Times start to run?

options.A: 7th day
options.B: 10th day
options.C: 21st day
options.D: 30th day
options.E: 60th day
options.F: 90th day

questions.explanation: Without a Notice to Proceed, C-700 starts the Contract Times on the 30th day after the Effective Date; a Notice to Proceed may be given at any time within those 30 days. The Times never start later than the 60th day after Bid opening or the 30th day after the Effective Date, whichever is earlier, so the 60th day is an outer limit, not the default. No Work may be done at the Site before the Times start.

questions.question: Under AIA A201 §9.8.2, when the Work is substantially complete, the punch list (a comprehensive list of work still to be finished or corrected before final payment) is prepared and submitted by the ____.

mc.question: Under AIA A201 §9.8.2, who prepares and submits the punch list, the comprehensive list of work still to be finished or corrected before final payment, when the Work is substantially complete?

options.A: Architect
options.B: Contractor
options.C: Owner
options.D: Construction manager
options.E: Subcontractors
options.F: Commissioning authority

questions.explanation: Under A201 the Contractor prepares the list and submits it to the Architect, who then inspects to decide whether the Work is substantially complete; leaving an item off the list does not relieve the Contractor of finishing it. The Architect's part is the inspection, not the list (under EJCDC C-700, by contrast, the Engineer attaches a punch list to the preliminary certificate). Section 01 77 00—Closeout Procedures specifies the procedure.

questions.question: Under AIA A201 §9.3.1, the Contractor submits each Application for Payment to the Architect at least ____ days before the date established for the progress payment. The Architect then has seven days to certify payment or give reasons for withholding.

mc.question: Under AIA A201 §9.3.1, at least how many days before the date established for each progress payment must the Contractor submit its Application for Payment to the Architect?

options.A: 7 days
options.B: 14 days
options.C: 10 days
options.D: 21 days
options.E: 30 days
options.F: 60 days

questions.explanation: A201 requires each itemized Application for Payment, prepared from the schedule of values, at least ten days before the progress payment date. Seven days is the Architect's period: within seven days of receiving the application, the Architect either issues a Certificate for Payment or tells the Owner and Contractor in writing why certification is withheld. Fourteen and 21 days are other A201 time limits.

questions.question: Industry guidance recognizes five project delivery methods: ____, ____, ____, ____ and ____.

mc.question: Which list names the five recognized project delivery methods?

options.A: Design-bid-build, construction manager at risk, design-build, owner-build, integrated project delivery
options.B: Design-bid-build, construction manager as agent, design-build, owner-build, integrated project delivery
options.C: Design-bid-build, construction manager at risk, design-build, program management, integrated project delivery
options.D: Design-bid-build, construction manager at risk, design-build, owner-build, construction manager as advisor
options.E: Design-bid-build, multiple-prime contracting, design-build, owner-build, integrated project delivery
options.F: Fast-track, construction manager at risk, design-build, owner-build, integrated project delivery

questions.explanation: The five delivery methods are design-bid-build (with competitive bid, competitive proposal and negotiated options), construction manager at risk, design-build, owner-build and integrated project delivery. Construction manager as agent, construction manager as advisor and program management are management options used alongside a delivery method, not methods themselves; fast-track is a scheduling technique, and multiple-prime is a way of dividing the construction contracts.

questions.question: Design-bid-build delivery has three options, which differ mostly in how the project is procured: ____, ____ and ____.

mc.question: Which three are the options of the design-bid-build delivery method?

options.A: Competitive bid
options.B: Bridging documents
options.C: Competitive proposal
options.D: Construction manager as advisor
options.E: Negotiation
options.F: Fast-track scheduling

questions.explanation: Design-bid-build can be procured by competitive bid (the baseline), by competitive proposal, where proposers submit extra documents so the owner can choose the best-qualified contractor and may still negotiate the final price, or by negotiation. Bridging documents is one of the design-build options, construction manager as advisor is a management option, and fast-track is a scheduling technique.

questions.question: Design-build entities take six forms, classified by the kind of firm that provides the primary services: ____, ____, ____, ____, ____ and ____.

mc.question: Which list names the six variations of design-build, classified by the kind of firm that provides the primary services?

options.A: Pure, designer-based, constructor-based, developer-based, bridging, single-purpose entity
options.B: Pure, designer-based, constructor-based, turnkey, joint venture, single-purpose entity
options.C: Competitive proposal, designer-based, constructor-based, developer-based, joint venture, single-purpose entity
options.D: Pure, designer-based, constructor-based, developer-based, joint venture, single-purpose entity
options.E: Pure, bridging, constructor-based, developer-based, joint venture, turnkey
options.F: Pure, designer-based, owner-build, developer-based, joint venture, single-purpose entity

questions.explanation: The six forms are pure design-build (one integrated firm with in-house design and construction staff), designer-based (the architect/engineer subcontracts the builder), constructor-based (the contractor subcontracts the architect/engineer), developer-based, joint venture, and single-purpose entity (a corporation or LLC formed only to deliver the project). Bridging and competitive proposals are design-build options and turnkey describes the extent of services, not the kind of firm; owner-build is a separate delivery method.

questions.question: When a design-build contract also covers services such as buying and financing the land, buying and installing specialized furnishings and equipment, building commissioning and facility management, so that one entity provides everything the owner needs to make the new facility ready for occupancy and use, the contract could be considered a ____ contract.

mc.question: A design-build contract that also covers land purchase and financing, specialized furnishings and equipment, commissioning and facility management, so one entity delivers a facility ready to occupy, could be considered what kind of contract?

options.A: Bridging
options.B: Single-purpose entity
options.C: Turnkey
options.D: Program management
options.E: Integrated project delivery
options.F: Construction manager at risk

questions.explanation: When design-build adds services beyond design and construction, such as land acquisition and financing, furnishings and equipment, commissioning or facility management, the contract may be called turnkey: one entity hands the owner a facility ready to use. It is still design-build delivery; turnkey describes the extent of services. Bridging is a design-build option that gives the owner more control of design, and a single-purpose entity is a form of design-build firm.

questions.question: On a fast-tracked construction manager at risk project, a distinct portion of the work that subcontractors price separately, such as underground utilities, structure, elevators, mechanical or electrical work, is called a ____; these are bid in the order in which each portion can start on site.

mc.question: On a fast-tracked construction manager at risk project, what is a distinct portion of the work (such as underground utilities, structure or elevators) that subcontractors price separately, released in the order each portion can start on site?

options.A: Alternate
options.B: Allowance
options.C: Unit price
options.D: Separate contract
options.E: Bid package
options.F: Addendum

questions.explanation: With fast-tracking, the construction manager at risk and the architect/engineer schedule the documents so separate bid packages (also called work packages) can be issued and bid in a logical sequence, letting early work start before the documents are finished. A bid package is a portion of the construction manager's own work bid by subcontractors, not a separate prime contract, and it is not an alternate, which is optional work the owner may accept or reject.

questions.question: When the documents are complete enough (at the end of design development or partway through construction documents), the construction manager at risk accepts the risk for the cost of the work by proposing a not-to-exceed ____.

mc.question: When the documents are complete enough, what not-to-exceed figure does the construction manager at risk propose, taking on the risk for the cost of the work?

options.A: Stipulated sum
options.B: Guaranteed maximum price
options.C: Cost of the work plus a fee
options.D: Unit price
options.E: Cash allowance
options.F: Owner's contingency

questions.explanation: The construction manager at risk proposes a guaranteed maximum price (GMP): if the scope does not materially change and its pricing assumptions hold, the project will cost no more than that amount. The construction manager pays any excess, and savings below it are credited to the owner or shared. A stipulated sum is a fixed price rather than a ceiling on cost, and cost of the work plus a fee has no ceiling unless a GMP is added.

questions.question: When a construction manager at risk brings a major subcontractor in during design to help the design team through consultation, without the subcontractor taking responsibility for the design, the subcontractor is providing ____ services.

mc.question: A major subcontractor brought in by the construction manager at risk during design, to advise the design team without taking responsibility for the design, is providing what kind of services?

options.A: Delegated design
options.B: Design-build
options.C: Constructability review
options.D: Design-assist
options.E: Value analysis
options.F: Commissioning

questions.explanation: A design-assist subcontractor takes the architect/engineer's design parameters, develops more detailed designs and cost alternatives, and helps prepare the construction documents, but the design stays the architect/engineer's responsibility. Delegated design is different: the contractor is made responsible for designing a component and retains a licensed design professional to do it. Under design-build, all design responsibility rests with the design-builder.

questions.question: The principles of integrated project delivery are grouped as contractual principles (ones that can be written into contracts) and behavioral principles (choice-based, but needed to optimize the project). Name the three behavioral principles: ____, ____ and ____.

mc.question: Which three are the behavioral principles of integrated project delivery (choice-based, but needed to optimize the project)?

options.A: Mutual respect and trust
options.B: Shared financial risk and reward
options.C: Willingness to collaborate
options.D: Collaborative decision-making
options.E: Open communications
options.F: Early involvement of key participants

questions.explanation: The behavioral principles are mutual respect and trust, willingness to collaborate, and open communications: no contract can require them, but the project depends on them. Shared financial risk and reward, early involvement of key participants and collaborative decision-making are contractual principles, because they can be written into the agreement. Multi-party agreements, BIM, lean methods and co-location are the catalysts.

questions.question: Besides its contractual and behavioral principles, integrated project delivery has four catalysts: ____, ____, ____ and ____.

mc.question: Which list names the four catalysts of integrated project delivery?

options.A: Multi-party agreements, BIM, shared financial risk and reward, team co-location
options.B: Liability waivers, BIM, lean design and construction, team co-location
options.C: Multi-party agreements, fiscal transparency, lean design and construction, team co-location
options.D: Multi-party agreements, BIM, lean design and construction, early involvement of key participants
options.E: Collaborative decision-making, open communications, lean design and construction, team co-location
options.F: Multi-party agreements, BIM, lean design and construction, team co-location

questions.explanation: The catalysts are multi-party agreements, building information modeling (BIM), lean design and construction, and co-locating the team: tools and arrangements that make integration work. Shared financial risk and reward, liability waivers, fiscal transparency, early involvement of key participants and collaborative decision-making are contractual principles, and open communications is a behavioral principle, so none of them is a catalyst.

questions.question: The owner usually provides the information about contract procedures, and AIA Document ____, Owner's Instructions to the Architect, is the form for obtaining it (Part A for the construction contract, Part B for bidding procedures).

mc.question: Which AIA document, Owner's Instructions to the Architect, collects the owner's information on the construction contract (Part A) and bidding procedures (Part B)?

questions.explanation: AIA G612 gathers the owner's instructions on the construction contract, insurance and bonds, and bidding procedures, which shape the procurement and contracting documents and the specifying methods. The other forms serve later or different purposes: G701 is the Change Order, G702 the Application and Certification for Payment, G710 Architect's Supplemental Instructions, G714 the Construction Change Directive, and A201 the general conditions.

questions.question: When a construction manager at risk or integrated project delivery project issues its contract documents as multiple work packages, Division 01 may be issued as a ____ package that all later work packages reference, so it need not be republished with each package; a later package that needs a Division 01 revision carries that change.

mc.question: On a construction manager at risk or IPD project issued as multiple work packages, how can Division 01 be handled so it need not be republished with every package?

options.A: Repeat the complete Division 01 in every work package
options.B: Issue it once as a stand-alone package that later work packages reference
options.C: Issue with each package only the Division 01 sections that apply to it
options.D: Move its requirements into the supplementary conditions
options.E: Hold it until the last work package and issue it by addendum
options.F: Put its requirements in the general notes on the drawings

questions.explanation: Whether a construction manager at risk or IPD project is issued as one set or as work packages, the same Division 01 requirements govern, so Division 01 can go out once as a stand-alone package that later packages reference; if a later package needs a Division 01 change, that package carries the revision. Issuing only the applicable Division 01 sections with each package is the approach for multiple-prime bid/proposal packages under a construction manager as advisor or agent.

questions.question: With multiple-prime contracts under a construction manager as advisor or agent, the conditions of the contract issued with the various bid/proposal packages should be ____, which means preparing them early, in time for the first package.

mc.question: With multiple-prime contracts under a construction manager as advisor or agent, how should the conditions of the contract be handled across the bid/proposal packages?

options.A: Each package gets conditions tailored to that contract's scope
options.B: They go out only with the packages they apply to, like allowances or testing sections
options.C: They are issued once with the first package, and later packages omit them
options.D: Identical conditions go with every package, so they must be ready in time for the first package
options.E: They are prepared last, after every package's scope is known
options.F: They are issued by addendum after the packages are awarded

questions.explanation: Every prime contractor must work under identical conditions of the contract, so they go out with every bid/proposal package, and because the first package already needs them they must be prepared early. Tailoring by package is the rule for Division 01, not for the conditions: sections such as allowances, alternates or testing laboratory services are issued only with the packages they concern.

questions.question: On a multiple-prime project, unless some contractual entity is given responsibility and authority for coordination, the ____ may end up assuming the responsibility to coordinate between the prime contracts.

mc.question: On a multiple-prime project, if no contractual entity is assigned responsibility and authority for coordination, who may end up assuming it?

options.A: Architect/engineer
options.B: Construction manager
options.C: Program manager
options.D: General contractor
options.E: Specialty contractor
options.F: Owner

questions.explanation: On multiple-prime work, whoever organizes the documents (the architect/engineer, construction manager or owner-builder) has to set out how the work is split among the contracts and coordinated. If no one is given that responsibility and authority, it can fall to the owner, who holds every prime contract. The architect/engineer or construction manager coordinates only when assigned to, and there is no general contractor to do it.

questions.question: A program manager can serve the owner in two ways. In an administrative role, the program manager works within the owner's project staff and cannot bind the owner; in a ____ role, it works independently of that staff and can bind the owner.

mc.question: A program manager can serve the owner in an administrative role, within the owner's staff and unable to bind the owner, or in what other role, independent of that staff and able to bind the owner?

options.A: Advisory
options.B: Leadership
options.C: Representative
options.D: Consulting
options.E: Supervisory
options.F: Oversight

questions.explanation: In the leadership role the owner empowers the program manager to act as its agent and make decisions that bind the owner; in the administrative role it supports the owner's staff without that authority. Either way the program manager contracts only with the owner and acts as an extension of the owner's staff. Serving as the owner's representative without decision-making power describes the administrative role, not the leadership role.

questions.question: On an owner-build project, where the owner provides its own construction services, the construction documents may concentrate mainly on the information needed to obtain ____.

mc.question: On an owner-build project, where the owner provides its own construction services, the construction documents may concentrate mainly on the information needed to obtain what?

options.A: Competitive bids
options.B: Construction financing
options.C: Permits
options.D: Performance and payment bonds
options.E: Builder's risk insurance
options.F: Product warranties

questions.explanation: Owner-build documents are structured like those for other delivery methods and may be prepared in-house or by an independent architect/engineer. Because the owner performs the construction itself, they may concentrate on the information the authorities having jurisdiction need to issue permits, rather than on instructing an outside contractor. Bids, bonds, insurance and financing are not that stated focus.

questions.question: Systems, assemblies and materials are evaluated against four project components: ____, ____, ____ and ____.

mc.question: Which list names the four project components that systems, assemblies and materials are evaluated against?

options.A: Project requirements and design intent; the project drawings; code requirements; material cost
options.B: Project requirements and design intent; manufacturer competition; code requirements; constructability and construction sequence
options.C: Project requirements and design intent; the project drawings; code requirements; constructability and construction sequence
options.D: The owner's budget; the project drawings; code requirements; constructability and construction sequence
options.E: Project requirements and design intent; the project drawings; material durability; constructability and construction sequence
options.F: Project requirements and design intent; product availability; energy efficiency; constructability and construction sequence

questions.explanation: Each system, assembly or material is checked for compliance with the project requirements and design intent, consistency with the drawings, compliance with code requirements, and compatibility with the intended constructability and construction sequence. The aim is to confirm which available products apply and that different products and systems work together. Cost, availability, durability and energy performance matter in product selection, but they are not these four components.

questions.question: Goods that various manufacturers can produce uniformly and consistently with the same predetermined quality are called a ____; a material becomes one when it is specified without naming a manufacturer, so that any manufacturer's material is acceptable.

mc.question: What are goods called that various manufacturers can produce uniformly and consistently to the same predetermined quality, as a material becomes when it is specified without naming a manufacturer?

options.A: Material
options.B: Standard product
options.C: Proprietary product
options.D: Assembly
options.E: Commodity
options.F: Equipment

questions.explanation: A commodity is a good that many manufacturers make to the same predetermined quality, so any of them will do; a material becomes a commodity once it is specified without naming a manufacturer. A material is the substance itself, converted from a raw state; a standard product is one manufacturer's regular, stocked line; and a proprietary product is often unique, with no functional equivalent.

questions.question: An attribute is a characteristic of product performance, and it has three essential considerations: ____, ____ and ____.

mc.question: Which three are the essential considerations of a product performance attribute?

options.A: Requirements
options.B: Tolerances
options.C: Criteria
options.D: Warranties
options.E: Tests
options.F: Reference standards

questions.explanation: Each attribute is defined by requirements (the desired results, usually stated qualitatively), criteria (measurable or observable performance levels for a requirement) and tests (the means of verifying conformance with each criterion). For a ceiling's surface burning characteristics, for example, the requirement is flame spread, the criterion a rating under 25, and the test ASTM E84. Reference standards and tolerances may support these, but they are not the three considerations.

questions.question: The project schedule has two basic influences on product selection: ____ and ____.

mc.question: Which two are the basic influences that the project schedule has on product selection?

options.A: Design delivery
options.B: Project budget
options.C: Product delivery
options.D: Regulatory requirements
options.E: Sustainability rating system
options.F: Project program

questions.explanation: Design delivery: an accelerated design may leave too little time to evaluate products, limiting the documents to products already known and leading to more substitution requests and higher prices. Product delivery: a product that cannot be made and delivered between submittal approval and the date it is needed on site is not a viable choice. The budget, codes, sustainability goals and program also influence selection, but not through the schedule.

questions.question: As the design concept develops and the aesthetic design is still fluid, products should first be identified only as ____ products, because it is too early to spend much effort selecting the actual products to be specified.

mc.question: While the design concept is developing and the aesthetic design is still fluid, how should products first be identified?

options.A: As proprietary products
options.B: As custom products
options.C: As basis-of-design products
options.D: As sole-source products
options.E: As standard products
options.F: As generic products

questions.explanation: Early in design, while the form is still changing, products are identified generically, because evaluating and choosing actual products would waste effort on decisions likely to change. Each product's attributes are then evaluated against the project's criteria as the design develops. Naming proprietary, custom, basis-of-design or sole-source products comes later, if at all.

questions.question: Drawings should not define the work of specific subcontractors or trades, but they may indicate four things, each of which must also be covered in the correct Division 01 section: ____, ____, ____ and ____.
answers: work by owner or separate contract

mc.question: Drawings should not define the work of specific trades. Which list names the four things they may indicate, each also covered in the correct Division 01 section?

options.A: Limits of work; extent of alternates; construction phasing areas; work of specific subcontractors
options.B: Limits of work; proprietary product names; construction phasing areas; work by the owner or by separate contract
options.C: Detailed material descriptions; extent of alternates; construction phasing areas; work by the owner or by separate contract
options.D: Limits of work; extent of alternates; proprietary product names; work of specific trades
options.E: Limits of work; extent of alternates; construction phasing areas; work by the owner or by separate contract
options.F: Extent of alternates; construction phasing areas; detailed material descriptions; work of specific subcontractors

questions.explanation: Drawings may show limits of work, the extent of alternates, construction phasing areas, and work the owner or a separate contractor will perform, while the written requirements for each go in the right Division 01 section. They should not split the work among subcontractors or trades, and drawing notes should stay generic: detailed material descriptions and proprietary product names belong in the specifications.

questions.question: Proprietary product information should not appear on the drawings unless a ____ proprietary specification restricts the choice to one product; otherwise, accepting a substitution could mean revising every proprietary reference by addendum or contract modification.

mc.question: Proprietary product names may appear on the drawings only when which kind of specification restricts the choice to one product?

options.A: Open proprietary specification
options.B: Closed proprietary specification
options.C: Or-equal specification
options.D: Descriptive specification
options.E: Performance specification
options.F: Reference standard specification

questions.explanation: Drawing notes stay generic even when the specifications name products. Only a closed proprietary specification, which allows one product and no substitutions, justifies naming the product on the drawings; under an open proprietary or or-equal specification another product may be accepted, and every product name on the drawings would then need revising by addendum or modification. Descriptive, performance and reference standard specifications do not name products at all.

questions.question: To keep materials from needing frequent replacement and becoming costly maintenance items, architects/engineers should evaluate material ____ within the project's interior conditions, especially for materials that take heavy wear, such as flooring.

mc.question: To keep high-wear interior materials such as flooring from needing frequent replacement and becoming costly maintenance items, which property should be evaluated within the project's interior conditions?

options.A: Energy efficiency
options.B: Indoor air quality
options.C: Durability
options.D: Noise control
options.E: Flame spread
options.F: Initial cost

questions.explanation: A product unsuited to the interior climate can deteriorate and shorten the building's useful life, so material durability is judged against the actual interior conditions, especially for high-wear surfaces like flooring. Energy efficiency, air quality and noise are other interior factors to evaluate, but they do not address how often a material must be replaced, and a low initial cost can be outweighed by frequent replacement.

questions.question: A model building code becomes an enforceable code for a jurisdiction only once it is formally ____ by the local authority having jurisdiction, which may take only portions of it and modify them.

mc.question: What must the local authority having jurisdiction do with a model building code before it becomes enforceable there?

options.A: Publish it under the jurisdiction's own name
options.B: Obtain an evaluation report for it
options.C: Formally adopt it, in whole or in part
options.D: Have it approved by the model code-writing organization
options.E: Reference it in the project specifications
options.F: Wait for the next edition to be issued

questions.explanation: A model code such as the International Building Code has no force on a project until a local authority having jurisdiction formally adopts it; the authority may adopt only parts of it and modify them, and then enforces the adopted version. The model code-writing organization develops and publishes the code, but only adoption by the jurisdiction gives it legal force.

questions.question: Model code-writing organizations evaluate building materials and products, and when one complies with the model code they issue a document showing its acceptance, called an ____. Building officials may rely on it, but it does not guarantee local approval.

mc.question: When a model code-writing organization finds that a product complies with the model code, what document does it issue to show the product's acceptance?

options.A: Test report
options.B: Product data
options.C: Certificate of compliance
options.D: Evaluation report
options.E: Environmental Product Declaration
options.F: Manufacturer's instructions

questions.explanation: Manufacturers submit samples, product information and test reports, and if the product complies with the model code the organization issues an evaluation report showing its acceptance. Anyone can consult these reports and many authorities require them, but they do not guarantee approval by the local building official, and some jurisdictions run their own evaluation programs. A test report is only one piece of evidence submitted for that evaluation.

questions.question: A review of the design to find out whether it is practical to build with the means, methods and products available when construction is planned, within the owner's budget and the project's time requirements, is a ____.

mc.question: What is a review of the design that checks whether it is practical to build with the means, methods and products available at the time of construction, within the owner's budget and schedule?

options.A: Value analysis
options.B: Plan review
options.C: Cost estimate
options.D: Life cycle cost analysis
options.E: Constructability review
options.F: Commissioning review

questions.explanation: A constructability review, best done by someone experienced in building similar projects, finds parts of the design that would be difficult or impractical to build and recommends more practical options. Cost is weighed only as it affects practicality, so it is not a cost estimate, and it differs from value analysis, which seeks the best life cycle value. Plan review is the authority having jurisdiction's check of the documents.

questions.question: A constructability review is advised in six situations: ____, ____, ____, ____, ____ and ____.
answers: site with unusual challenges or constraints

mc.question: Which list names the six situations in which a constructability review is advised?

options.A: Innovative or unusual design techniques; unfamiliar project components; an unfamiliar location; a site with unusual challenges or constraints; specific budget constraints; a large number of alternates
options.B: Innovative or unusual design techniques; unfamiliar project components; a public owner; a site with unusual challenges or constraints; specific budget constraints; specific time constraints
options.C: Multiple-prime contracts; unfamiliar project components; an unfamiliar location; a site with unusual challenges or constraints; specific budget constraints; specific time constraints
options.D: Innovative or unusual design techniques; unfamiliar project components; an unfamiliar location; a site with unusual challenges or constraints; a negotiated contract; specific time constraints
options.E: Innovative or unusual design techniques; a closed proprietary specification; an unfamiliar location; a design-build delivery method; specific budget constraints; specific time constraints
options.F: Innovative or unusual design techniques; unfamiliar project components; an unfamiliar location; a site with unusual challenges or constraints; specific budget constraints; specific time constraints

questions.explanation: A constructability review is recommended when the design uses innovative or unusual techniques, unfamiliar components are being considered, the project will be built in an unfamiliar location, the site poses unusual challenges or constraints, or the budget or schedule is specifically constrained. A public owner, multiple-prime or negotiated contracts, many alternates, a closed proprietary specification and design-build delivery are not on that list. The review works best once details are developed but before the construction documents are final.

questions.question: Incorporating reference standards saves the architect/engineer from writing lengthy text, but it carries six liabilities. Name them (a key word each is enough): ____, ____, ____, ____, ____, ____.
answers: inadequate standards coexist with stringent ones

mc.question: Incorporating reference standards saves writing lengthy text but carries six liabilities. Which list names them?

options.A: Inadequate standards coexist with stringent ones; duplication and contradiction; embedded options; consensus-based development; undesired requirements; different editions enforced by different AHJs
options.B: Inadequate standards coexist with stringent ones; duplication and contradiction; incorporation by number and title; minimum requirements; undesired requirements; different editions enforced by different AHJs
options.C: Inadequate standards coexist with stringent ones; duplication and contradiction; embedded options; minimum requirements; undesired requirements; different editions enforced by different AHJs
options.D: Inadequate standards coexist with stringent ones; duplication and contradiction; embedded options; minimum requirements; undesired requirements; publication by trade associations
options.E: Listing in the model codes; duplication and contradiction; embedded options; minimum requirements; undesired requirements; different editions enforced by different AHJs
options.F: Inadequate standards coexist with stringent ones; shorter specification text; embedded options; minimum requirements; consensus-based development; different editions enforced by different AHJs

questions.explanation: The six liabilities are that inadequate standards exist alongside stringent ones, standards can duplicate or contradict the contract documents, they contain embedded options, they generally set only minimum requirements, they may contain unwanted requirements, and different authorities having jurisdiction may enforce different editions with conflicting requirements. Consensus development, publication by trade associations, listing in codes and incorporation by number are simply facts about standards, and shorter text is the benefit.

questions.question: Categories, classes or groups within a reference standard from which the applicable properties must be selected, such as the 10 cement types in ASTM C150, are called ____; if the architect/engineer does not choose, the choice falls to the contractor, who can be expected to pick the least expensive.

mc.question: What are the categories, classes or groups within a reference standard called, such as the 10 cement types in ASTM C150, from which the specifier must choose or else leave the choice to the contractor?

options.A: Alternates
options.B: Embedded options
options.C: Allowances
options.D: Exceptions
options.E: Minimum requirements
options.F: Undesired requirements

questions.explanation: Embedded options are choices built into a standard, such as the cement types in ASTM C150, and the specifier must identify and select the right one to prevent discrepancies. Left unselected, the choice passes to the contractor, who can reasonably be expected to pick the cheapest. Alternates and allowances are pricing devices in the procurement documents, and exceptions are the specifier's stated departures from a standard.

questions.question: If a reference standard is not compatible with other project requirements or contains duplications or contradictions, the architect/engineer must choose between citing it and defining ____ to it, or writing its own requirements into the specifications instead.

mc.question: If a reference standard conflicts with other project requirements or contains duplications or contradictions, the architect/engineer must choose between citing it and defining ____ to it, or writing its own requirements into the specifications instead. Which term fills the blank?

options.A: Alternates
options.B: Allowances
options.C: Addenda
options.D: Exceptions
options.E: Substitutions
options.F: Tolerances

questions.explanation: A standard must be read and understood before it is cited; if it clashes with other requirements or duplicates them, the specifier either cites it with stated exceptions or writes original requirements instead. A blanket statement that the more stringent requirement governs cannot be relied on to resolve every conflict. Addenda, alternates, allowances and substitutions are procurement and change tools, not ways of modifying a standard.

questions.question: A frequently cited example of a reference standard that covers contractor-owner and contractor-subcontractor relationships, and uses 'owner' and 'contract documents' in a different sense from the general conditions, is the ____ Code of Standard Practice.

mc.question: Which organization's Code of Standard Practice covers contractor-owner and contractor-subcontractor relationships and uses 'owner' and 'contract documents' differently from the general conditions?

options.A: ACI
options.B: ASTM
options.C: NFPA
options.D: APA
options.E: ANSI
options.F: AISC

questions.explanation: The American Institute of Steel Construction (AISC) Code of Standard Practice addresses relationships among owner, contractor and subcontractors and gives 'owner' and 'contract documents' meanings that differ from the general conditions. Once referenced, its duplicated statements become part of the specifications, so wording that departs from the conditions of the contract or Division 01 creates ambiguity and possible disputes. ACI, ASTM and NFPA standards are referenced too, but this example is AISC's.
