questions.question: The architect/engineer could state that when a reference standard conflicts with the specifications or with another referenced standard, the more ____ requirements apply, but such a statement cannot be relied on to handle every conflict.

mc.question: A specifier may state that when a reference standard conflicts with the specifications or with another referenced standard, the more ____ requirements apply, though such a statement cannot be relied on for every conflict. Which word fills the blank?

options.A: Recent
options.B: Stringent
options.C: Detailed
options.D: Economical
options.E: Lenient
options.F: General

questions.explanation: The specifier may add a clause that the more stringent requirements apply when a standard conflicts with the specifications or another standard, but such a clause cannot settle every conflict. The specifier still has to identify duplications, modify the references to remove contradictions, and exclude provisions that clash with other requirements. Newer, more detailed or cheaper requirements are not the test that clause uses.

questions.question: Four cost estimating methods are used during design, from the quickest and least accurate to the most accurate: ____, ____, ____ and ____.

mc.question: Which list gives the four design-phase cost estimating methods in order, from the quickest and least accurate to the most accurate?

options.A: Order of magnitude, unit of measure, assemblies/systems, life cycle cost
options.B: Unit of measure, order of magnitude, value analysis, unit price
options.C: Historical cost data, unit of measure, assemblies/systems, unit price
options.D: Order of magnitude, published cost data, assemblies/systems, unit price
options.E: Unit price, assemblies/systems, unit of measure, contingency
options.F: Order of magnitude, unit of measure, assemblies/systems, unit price

questions.explanation: Order of magnitude uses cost per unit of occupancy, such as per bed or per seat (about 20 to 25 percent accuracy); unit of measure uses cost per square or cubic foot (15 to 20 percent); assemblies/systems prices assembled construction, often in UniFormat (about 10 percent); and unit price takes off quantities from the completed construction documents, usually in MasterFormat (3 to 5 percent). Life cycle cost and value analysis evaluate options, and historical or published data are sources for estimates, not methods.

questions.question: A unit price estimate, built from a complete quantity takeoff of the finished construction documents, is the most accurate estimating method; it is usually accurate within ____ percent of the actual cost.

mc.question: A unit price estimate, built from a complete quantity takeoff of the finished construction documents, is usually accurate within what range of the actual cost?

options.A: 3 to 10 percent
options.B: About 10 percent
options.C: 3 to 5 percent
options.D: 15 to 20 percent
options.E: 20 to 25 percent
options.F: Within 1 percent

questions.explanation: A unit price estimate lists every material, component and cost item from the completed construction documents, so it is the most accurate, typically within 3 to 5 percent, and the most time-consuming. Assemblies/systems estimates are accurate to about 10 percent, unit of measure estimates 15 to 20 percent, and order of magnitude estimates 20 to 25 percent. A 3-to-10-percent figure is a typical construction-phase contingency, not an estimate's accuracy.

questions.question: Life cycle costs are the expected expenses of a project, or of a particular material, piece of equipment or system, and they include five things: ____, ____, ____, ____ and ____.

mc.question: Which list names the five kinds of expense that life cycle costs include for a project, material, piece of equipment or system?

options.A: Design, construction, financing, maintenance, and resale, demolition or salvage
options.B: Site acquisition, construction, operation, maintenance, and resale, demolition or salvage
options.C: Design, construction, operation, maintenance, and legal fees
options.D: Design, construction, operation, maintenance, and resale, demolition or salvage
options.E: Design, financing, operation, maintenance, and salvage
options.F: Design, construction, operation, insurance, and resale, demolition or salvage

questions.explanation: Life cycle cost totals the cost of owning a project or component: design, construction, operation, maintenance (including replacement), and resale, demolition or salvage at the end of its life. Financing, site acquisition, legal fees and insurance are project budget costs, but they are not the five life cycle categories. Value analysis is a separate process that uses life cycle costs to compare options.

questions.question: Life cycle costs rest on the total cost of ____ over a long period of time, not just the initial cost of construction.

mc.question: Life cycle costs reflect the total cost of what over a long period, rather than only the initial cost of construction?

options.A: Construction
options.B: Operation
options.C: Acquisition
options.D: Ownership
options.E: Financing
options.F: Replacement

questions.explanation: Life cycle cost covers what the owner will actually pay to build, operate and maintain the project over its life, so it rests on the total cost of ownership. Construction (first cost), operation and replacement are each only part of that total, and acquisition or financing describe how the owner obtains or pays for the asset. Judged this way, an option that costs more to build can still be cheaper to own.

questions.question: An asset's useful life can end when it is no longer profitable, or when it has deteriorated so far that the cost of maintaining it exceeds the cost of ____.

mc.question: An asset's useful life can end when it is no longer profitable, or when it has deteriorated so far that maintaining it costs more than what?

options.A: Repairing it
options.B: Replacing it
options.C: Operating it
options.D: Demolishing it
options.E: Renovating it
options.F: Insuring it

questions.explanation: An asset's life ends economically when it stops being profitable, or physically when upkeep would cost more than replacing it. Physical life is projected from historic data on similar projects, and economic life from regularly updated accounting data. Repair and renovation are forms of upkeep, not the alternative that maintenance cost is weighed against.

questions.question: The service life of a building is defined by three factors: ____, ____ and ____.

mc.question: Which three factors define the service life of a building?

options.A: Functional working life
options.B: Economic life
options.C: Technical service life
options.D: Physical life
options.E: Design working life
options.F: Warranty period

questions.explanation: Functional working life is how long the building can still meet its users' demands, even with repairs or adaptations; technical service life is how long it performs to its architectural, structural, mechanical and electrical requirements; design working life is the period it is assumed to serve its intended purpose before major repairs or adaptations are needed. Economic and physical life are used in life cycle cost forecasting, not these three factors.

questions.question: A value analysis workshop follows five phases, in order: ____, ____, ____, ____ and ____.

mc.question: Which list gives the five phases of a value analysis workshop in order?

options.A: Information, evaluation (analysis), speculation (creative), validation, presentation
options.B: Programming, speculation (creative), evaluation (analysis), development, presentation
options.C: Information, speculation (creative), evaluation (analysis), development, presentation
options.D: Information, speculation (creative), verification, development, presentation
options.E: Information, speculation (creative), evaluation (analysis), development, implementation
options.F: Speculation (creative), information, development, evaluation (analysis), validation

questions.explanation: In the information phase the architect/engineer presents the design and the owner's objectives and definition of value are set; speculation generates as many ideas as possible; evaluation discards weak ideas; development turns the best into priced, workable solutions; and presentation delivers a written report with recommendations. Validating the program and verifying the budget are goals of the workshop, not phases.

questions.question: ____ International is a professional association dedicated to promoting value analysis; it advocates a value analysis workshop that can be held at any point during design and construction.

mc.question: Which professional association is dedicated to promoting value analysis and advocates a value analysis workshop that can be held at any point during design and construction?

options.A: ASTM International
options.B: International Code Council
options.C: SAVE International
options.D: American Society for Quality Control
options.E: International Facility Management Association
options.F: National Institute of Building Sciences

questions.explanation: SAVE International promotes value analysis and proposes workshops in which experienced, multidisciplinary teams study alternative concepts, materials and methods without compromising the project's function. ASTM International develops standards, the International Code Council develops model codes, and the International Facility Management Association serves facility managers; none of them is the value analysis society.

questions.question: The most effective way to perform value analysis on a design is with a ____ team of stakeholders and participants who can each contribute to the evaluation, which takes a high level of cooperation among them.

mc.question: What kind of team is the most effective way to perform value analysis on a design, drawing on stakeholders and participants who can each contribute?

options.A: Independent third-party
options.B: In-house
options.C: Single-discipline
options.D: Multidisciplinary
options.E: Owner-only
options.F: Contractor-led

questions.explanation: Value analysis works best with a multidisciplinary team of stakeholders and participants, each bringing a different perspective on the most effective design for the owner's requirements, which demands a high level of cooperation. A review by one discipline or one party alone loses those perspectives. Timing matters as well: the earlier value analysis happens in design, the more effective and less disruptive it is.

questions.question: Legally, a separate contract by a third party, much like a surety bond, under which that party takes on responsibility if the principal fails to perform, is a ____.

mc.question: Legally, what is a separate contract by a third party, much like a surety bond, in which that party takes on responsibility if the principal fails to perform?

options.A: Warranty
options.B: Express warranty
options.C: Guaranty
options.D: Extended warranty
options.E: Indemnification
options.F: Implied warranty

questions.explanation: The law distinguishes the two terms: a guaranty is a third party's separate promise to answer if the principal fails, while a warranty is the principal's own assurance that it will take on stipulated responsibilities for completed work. So a manufacturer warrants its material, and the contractor gives a third-party guaranty for that material plus a warranty for its own installation workmanship. Indemnification is a promise to hold another party harmless from claims and losses.

questions.question: The two basic types of special warranty used on construction projects are ____ warranties and ____ warranties.

mc.question: Which two are the basic types of special warranty used on construction projects?

options.A: Extended warranties
options.B: Express warranties
options.C: Purchase warranties
options.D: Implied warranties
options.E: Full warranties
options.F: Limited warranties

questions.explanation: Extended warranties cover both products and workmanship; purchase warranties cover products only. The warranties specified for construction are usually extended warranties written into the individual specification sections. Express and implied describe how a warranty arises (written terms versus the law and the transaction), and full and limited describe how complete its coverage is.

questions.question: An exclusion limits the applicability of a warranty, whereas a ____ must be satisfied for the warranty to take effect; if it goes unmet, the warranty is void.

mc.question: An exclusion limits the applicability of a warranty. What must be satisfied for a warranty to take effect at all, so that failing it voids the warranty?

options.A: A disclaimer
options.B: A remedy
options.C: A limitation
options.D: The correction period
options.E: A condition
options.F: An endorsement

questions.explanation: A condition is a requirement that must be met for the warranty to apply; if it is not, the whole warranty is void. A roofing warranty, for example, may make proper use and adequate maintenance conditions rather than exclusions, letting the manufacturer refuse coverage even for a failure unrelated to the unmet condition. A disclaimer denies responsibility, and a remedy is what the warrantor must provide when the warranty applies.

questions.question: Standard general conditions from AIA, EJCDC and ConsensusDocs make no provision for extended warranties, so an extended warranty must be specified in ____ of the product's specification section.

mc.question: Standard AIA, EJCDC and ConsensusDocs general conditions make no provision for extended warranties. Where must an extended warranty be specified?

options.A: In PART 2—PRODUCTS of the product's specification section
options.B: In PART 1—GENERAL of the product's specification section
options.C: In PART 3—EXECUTION of the product's specification section
options.D: In the supplementary conditions
options.E: In the owner-contractor agreement
options.F: In the instructions to bidders

questions.explanation: The standard general conditions already give a one-year correction period, so one-year warranties need not be specified, but an extended warranty exists only if the specifications require it, in PART 1—GENERAL of the section for that product. PART 2 describes the products themselves and PART 3 their installation, and product-specific warranty terms belong with the product, not in the supplementary conditions or the agreement.

questions.question: Under AIA A201 §3.5, the Contractor's warranty excludes remedy for damage or defect caused by five things: ____, ____, ____, ____ and ____.
answers: alterations not executed by the Contractor

mc.question: Under AIA A201 §3.5, which list names the five causes of damage or defect that the Contractor's warranty excludes?

options.A: Abuse; alterations not executed by the Contractor; concealed or unknown conditions; improper operation; normal wear and tear
options.B: Hazardous materials; alterations not executed by the Contractor; improper or insufficient maintenance; improper operation; normal wear and tear
options.C: Abuse; acts of separate contractors; improper or insufficient maintenance; improper operation; normal wear and tear
options.D: Abuse; alterations not executed by the Contractor; improper or insufficient maintenance; delays caused by the Owner; normal wear and tear
options.E: Abuse; alterations not executed by the Contractor; improper or insufficient maintenance; improper operation; concealed or unknown conditions
options.F: Abuse; alterations not executed by the Contractor; improper or insufficient maintenance; improper operation; normal wear and tear and normal usage

questions.explanation: A201 §3.5 excludes remedy for damage or defects caused by abuse, alterations to the Work not executed by the Contractor, improper or insufficient maintenance, improper operation, and normal wear and tear and normal usage. Concealed or unknown conditions, hazardous materials, Owner delays and separate contractors are dealt with in other A201 provisions, not in this warranty exclusion. The one-year correction period is a separate obligation from this warranty.

questions.question: Under the Uniform Commercial Code, two warranties are implied in every sale of goods unless the sale documents clearly state they do not apply: the implied warranty of ____ and the implied warranty of ____.

mc.question: Under the Uniform Commercial Code, which two warranties are implied in every sale of goods unless the sale documents clearly state they do not apply?

options.A: Implied warranty of merchantability
options.B: Express warranty
options.C: Implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose
options.D: Full warranty
options.E: Limited warranty
options.F: Extended warranty

questions.explanation: Merchantability means the goods are of fair, average quality and suitable for the ordinary uses of such goods; fitness for a particular purpose arises when the seller knows the buyer's specific purpose and the buyer relies on the seller's skill to choose suitable goods. An express warranty is any written warranty, and full, limited and extended describe a warranty's coverage, so none of them is implied by the sale itself.

questions.question: An express warranty may consist of three things: ____, ____ and ____.

mc.question: Which three things may make up an express warranty under the Uniform Commercial Code?

options.A: An affirmation of fact or promise about the goods, such as a performance claim
options.B: The seller's knowledge of the buyer's particular purpose
options.C: A description of the goods, such as drawings or specifications
options.D: Goods passing without objection in the trade
options.E: A sample or model that the bargain is based on
options.F: Adequate packaging and labeling

questions.explanation: An express warranty can be an affirmation of fact or promise about the goods (such as a performance claim), a description of the goods (photos, drawings or specifications), or a sample or model that forms part of the basis of the deal; any written warranty is express. Passing without objection in the trade and adequate packaging and labeling are tests of the implied warranty of merchantability, and reliance on the seller's knowledge of the buyer's purpose creates the implied warranty of fitness.

questions.question: A written warranty that does not satisfy every minimum standard of a full warranty, for example one limited to labor or to materials for a stated period, is a ____ warranty.

mc.question: What is a written warranty called that does not satisfy every minimum standard of a full warranty, such as one covering only labor or only materials for a stated period?

options.A: Full warranty
options.B: Express warranty
options.C: Implied warranty
options.D: Limited warranty
options.E: Extended warranty
options.F: Purchase warranty

questions.explanation: A limited warranty falls short of at least one of the minimum standards of a full warranty, for example by covering only labor or only materials, or only for a stated time. A full warranty covers both labor and materials, and the warrantor must remedy a defect within a reasonable time and without charge. Because the Uniform Commercial Code sets no time limit, manufacturers limit the period themselves.

questions.question: Post-occupancy evaluations, which become the baseline for the ongoing facility evaluation program, are best performed ____ months after initial occupancy.

mc.question: When are post-occupancy evaluations, the baseline for the ongoing facility evaluation program, best performed?

options.A: Within 30 days after initial occupancy
options.B: 9 to 12 months after initial occupancy
options.C: At the end of the one-year correction period
options.D: 3 to 6 months after initial occupancy
options.E: 18 to 24 months after initial occupancy
options.F: Before final completion

questions.explanation: Post-occupancy evaluations are best done three to six months after initial occupancy, and they set the baseline for the ongoing facility evaluation program. They help the facility manager find nonconforming work and warranty items missed before occupancy, gather users' feedback on needed modifications, plan future projects and anticipate maintenance needs. The other timings are not the recommended window.

questions.question: Under AIA A201 §12.2.2, if any Work is found not in accordance with the Contract Documents within one year after the date of ____ (or after the commencement of warranties, or under the terms of a special warranty), the Contractor must correct it promptly after written notice from the Owner.

mc.question: Under AIA A201 §12.2.2, the one-year period for correcting nonconforming Work runs from the date of what?

options.A: Final completion
options.B: Final payment
options.C: Substantial Completion
options.D: Commencement of the Work
options.E: Final inspection by the Architect
options.F: Execution of the Agreement

questions.explanation: The one-year correction period runs from the date of Substantial Completion of the Work or a designated portion, from a separate warranty commencement date set under §9.9.1, or as a special warranty provides. It is not tied to final completion or final payment, corrective work does not extend it, and it does not limit the Contractor's other obligations or its general warranty.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700 ¶7.06, the Contractor's application for a substitute must certify three things about the proposed item: ____, ____ and ____.

mc.question: Under EJCDC C-700 ¶7.06, which three things must the Contractor's application certify about a proposed substitute item?

options.A: Adequately perform the functions and achieve the results the general design calls for
options.B: Be at least equal in quality, durability, appearance and strength
options.C: Be similar in substance to the item specified
options.D: Cause no increase in cost to the Owner or in the Contract Times
options.E: Be suited to the same use as the item specified
options.F: Have a proven record of performance and responsive service

questions.explanation: For a substitute, C-700 asks the Contractor to certify that the item will adequately perform the functions and achieve the results of the general design, be similar in substance to the specified item, and be suited to the same use. Being at least equal in quality and appearance, adding no cost or time, and having a proven service record are the stricter or-equal tests of ¶7.05. A substitute application also states any effect on Contract Times and itemizes costs or credits.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700 ¶7.05, no 'or-equal' item may be ordered or installed until the Engineer determines it is an 'or-equal', which will be evidenced by an approved ____ or other written communication.

mc.question: Under EJCDC C-700 ¶7.05, the Engineer's determination that a proposed item is an 'or-equal' is evidenced by an approved what, or other written communication?

options.A: Field Order
options.B: Change Order
options.C: Work Change Directive
options.D: Change Proposal
options.E: Addendum
options.F: Shop Drawing

questions.explanation: An or-equal is accepted through the normal submittal process, by an approved Shop Drawing or other written communication; the Contractor pays for the supporting data, and neither approval nor denial changes the Contract Price. A substitute is different: the Engineer's acceptance is evidenced by a Field Order or a proposed Change Order that accounts for the substitution and its effects on Contract Price or Contract Times.

questions.question: The procedures that guard against construction defects and departures from the contract documents before and during the work, including submittals, certifications and other actions that confirm proposed products and services meet the contract requirements, are called ____.

mc.question: What are the procedures called that guard against defects and departures from the contract documents before and during the work, through submittals, certifications and similar actions?

options.A: Quality control
options.B: Quality assurance
options.C: Field quality control
options.D: Source quality control
options.E: Construction observation
options.F: Testing and inspection

questions.explanation: Quality assurance is preventive: submittals, certifications and similar steps taken before and during the work to make sure the proposed products and services will meet the requirements. Quality control evaluates completed work for conformance, through testing and inspection of installed work; field and source quality control are the specification articles for those tests. The contractor's quality assurance begins with its site visit to learn the conditions.

questions.question: Quality control at one step of a process becomes quality assurance for the next: a slump test, for instance, controls the quality of concrete still in the mixer while assuring the quality of that concrete before it is placed. The American Society for Quality Control calls this a quality ____.

mc.question: Quality control at one step of a process becomes quality assurance for the next, as when a slump test checks concrete in the mixer and assures the concrete about to be placed. What does the American Society for Quality Control call this?

options.A: A quality management system
options.B: Third-party certification
options.C: A quality loop or quality spiral
options.D: Field quality control
options.E: Source quality control
options.F: Testing and inspection

questions.explanation: Raw material suppliers, manufacturers and fabricators each run quality control on their own step, and that control becomes part of the quality assurance for the step that follows, a chain the American Society for Quality Control calls a quality loop or quality spiral. A quality management system such as ISO 9000 is a framework for a firm's internal procedures, and field or source quality control names where tests are performed.

questions.question: Submittals that the architect/engineer must review and respond to, by approving them, approving them as noted, asking for revision and resubmittal, or rejecting them, are ____ submittals.

mc.question: Which submittals require the architect/engineer to respond by approving, approving as noted, requesting revision and resubmittal, or rejecting them?

options.A: Informational submittals
options.B: Closeout submittals
options.C: Maintenance material submittals
options.D: Action submittals
options.E: Delegated design submittals
options.F: Sustainable design submittals

questions.explanation: Action submittals need a responsive action: the architect/engineer reviews them and approves, approves as noted, asks for revision and resubmittal, or rejects. Informational submittals, such as test reports and qualification statements, verify that work meets the quality requirements and are mostly kept as a record without action. SectionFormat lists all submittals in one list, leaving the architect/engineer to decide which are action and which are informational.

questions.question: When permanent building systems and equipment, such as HVAC, electrical systems and elevators, are first put into operation, the process is called ____; the systems must operate properly before substantial completion can be reached.

mc.question: What is the first operation of permanent building systems and equipment, such as HVAC, electrical systems and elevators, called?

options.A: Commissioning
options.B: Testing, adjusting, and balancing
options.C: Start-up
options.D: Demonstration and training
options.E: Substantial completion
options.F: Closeout

questions.explanation: Start-up is the first operation of permanent systems such as HVAC, electrical systems and elevators; it is scheduled and coordinated under Division 01, follows the manufacturers' written instructions, and must succeed before substantial completion. Testing, adjusting and balancing come after start-up, and demonstration and training instruct the owner's staff. Commissioning is the broader quality-focused process that verifies systems meet the owner's project requirements.

questions.question: Two words used in construction contract administration differ in meaning: to ____ implies a less focused look, where simply noticing or seeing is enough, whereas to inspect implies a careful, critical evaluation of what is in place.

mc.question: Which word, used in construction contract administration, implies a less focused look in which simply noticing or seeing is enough, in contrast to inspect?

options.A: Examine
options.B: Review
options.C: Observe
options.D: Verify
options.E: Supervise
options.F: Monitor

questions.explanation: To observe means noticing or seeing what is there, without the careful, critical evaluation that inspect implies, and those who administer the contract or manage the project need to use each word with its intended meaning. Examine and verify suggest checking closely, like inspect, and to supervise means directing the work, which A201 assigns to the Contractor.

questions.question: There are three types of commissioning: ____, ____ and ____.

mc.question: Which three are the types of commissioning?

options.A: Total project commissioning
options.B: Recommissioning
options.C: Systems and equipment commissioning
options.D: Decommissioning
options.E: Building envelope commissioning
options.F: Testing, adjusting, and balancing

questions.explanation: Total project commissioning (also called total facility or building commissioning) runs from project conception through facility use, documents the owner's project requirements and includes the other two types. Systems and equipment commissioning tests, adjusts and trains operators for specific systems, and building envelope commissioning oversees the exterior envelope, fenestration, waterproofing and roofs. Testing, adjusting and balancing is one activity within commissioning, and decommissioning shuts a facility down.

questions.question: The commissioning process begins with the commissioning authority documenting the ____, the basis of the design proposed to meet them, and how the components, assemblies and systems will work together.

mc.question: What does the commissioning authority document first, at the start of the commissioning process, before the design team explains how it will be met?

options.A: Basis of design
options.B: Commissioning plan
options.C: Commissioning specifications
options.D: Owner's project requirements
options.E: Project program
options.F: Sequence of operations

questions.explanation: Commissioning starts with the commissioning authority documenting the owner's project requirements; the design team then develops the basis of design to explain how those requirements will be met, and the commissioning plan, developed later, details how they will be verified. Commissioning specifications set the performance benchmarks, tests and turnover requirements, and the sequence of operations is part of what the basis of design describes.

questions.question: A printed project manual should be split into separate volumes once it exceeds about how many pages?
questions.explanation: Good practice is to divide a printed project manual into separate volumes once it passes about 700 pages, because thicker sets are impractical to bind as one book. No rule sets a hard limit; 700 is the usual binding threshold, and the cover and table of contents should say what each volume contains.

questions.question: A basis-of-design product is best described as:

options.A: An alternate priced separately on the bid form
options.B: A set of measurable performance criteria with no product named
options.C: The single named product allowed, with every substitution barred
options.D: A named product that sets the minimum any substitute must meet
options.E: A product defined only by citing an industry reference standard
options.F: A product the owner furnishes for the contractor to install

questions.explanation: A basis-of-design product is named to set the type, function, dimensions, appearance and quality that any comparable product must match, so other makers can still compete. Barring every substitute describes a closed proprietary specification, and a separately priced option on the bid form is an alternate, not a quality benchmark.

questions.question: Which organizing format provides a sound basis for a practical project coordination checklist?

options.A: UniFormat
options.B: SectionFormat
options.C: MasterFormat
options.D: OmniClass
options.E: PageFormat
options.F: Uniform Drawing System

questions.explanation: A coordination checklist lists materials, systems and products section by section, so that items noted on the drawings are not left out of the specifications, and MasterFormat supplies exactly that section structure. UniFormat organizes by building element and suits early design descriptions; SectionFormat and PageFormat govern the inside and the layout of a single section.

questions.question: Coatings applied to a product at the shop or factory are specified in:

options.A: PART 1 Submittals of product data and samples
options.B: PART 3 Application and installation procedures
options.C: PART 2 Finishes for the product itself
options.D: Division 09 finish sections exclusively
options.E: PART 2 Accessories furnished with the product
options.F: PART 3 Field [or] Site Quality Control

questions.explanation: Shop and factory finishes are part of the product, so they go in the Finishes article of PART 2—PRODUCTS, which covers primer materials, finish materials and shop finishing methods. PART 3 covers work done at the site, and a Division 09 section would not cover a coating the manufacturer applies before delivery.

questions.question: A project must reach a stated sustainability rating, and the means and methods to get there are left to the contractor. Which section applies?

options.A: Section 01 35 63—Sustainability Certification Project Requirements
options.B: Section 01 33 29—Sustainable Design Reporting
options.C: Section 01 81 13—Sustainable Design Requirements
options.D: Section 01 78 53—Sustainable Design Closeout Documentation
options.E: Section 01 35 66—Sustainability Certification Project Procedures
options.F: Section 01 81 19—Indoor Air Quality Requirements

questions.explanation: When the goal is simply to reach a particular rating and the contractor decides how, the place is Section 01 81 13—Sustainable Design Requirements. Sections 01 35 63 and 01 35 66 are for projects pursuing specific points through a rating system, and the reporting and closeout sections handle paperwork, not the performance goal.

questions.question: Which is NOT a project delivery method?

options.A: Owner-build
options.B: Fast-track
options.C: Integrated project delivery
options.D: Construction manager at risk
options.E: Design-bid-build
options.F: Design-build

questions.explanation: Fast-track is a scheduling technique, not a delivery method: it overlaps design, procurement and construction so early work can start before the whole design is finished, and several delivery methods can use it. The recognized delivery methods are design-bid-build, construction manager at risk, integrated project delivery, design-build and owner-build.

questions.question: Which of the following are NOT among the items a specification revision log should capture?

options.A: Owner's or A/E's project number
options.B: Section number and title
options.C: Name of the person who made each change
options.D: Brief description of the changes
options.E: Project name
options.F: Reference standards cited in the section

questions.explanation: A revision log archived for updating the office master records the project name, the owner's or A/E's project number, the section number and title, and a short description of each change. It does not need the name of the person who made each edit or a list of the reference standards cited; the project number is easy to overlook, but it belongs on the log.

questions.question: Procurement and contracting requirements in MasterFormat are located in:

options.A: Division 01
options.B: Division 00
options.C: Division 02
options.D: Section 01 21 00
options.E: Section 01 10 00
options.F: Section 00 01 10

questions.explanation: MasterFormat places the procurement and contracting requirements in Division 00, the Procurement and Contracting Requirements Group. Its items, such as the bid form, agreement and conditions, are documents rather than specifications; Division 01 starts the Specifications Group with the General Requirements.

questions.question: A government agency project generally requires which specifying approach?

options.A: Nonrestrictive
options.B: Reference standard only
options.C: Performance only
options.D: Closed proprietary
options.E: Descriptive only
options.F: Exclusionary

questions.explanation: Government agency projects generally require nonrestrictive specifying so that several manufacturers can compete, and the specifier needs to know this before writing begins. Closed proprietary specifying is the opposite, and a nonrestrictive specification can still be written with descriptive, performance or reference standard methods, so no single method is mandated.

questions.question: Adding 'or equal' after every proprietary name is redundant when the project manual includes:

options.A: A comprehensive Section 01 25 13
options.B: A complete Section 01 42 00
options.C: A substitution page on the bid form
options.D: At least three named products per item
options.E: A complete Section 01 60 00
options.F: A product options paragraph in PART 2

questions.explanation: A comprehensive Section 01 25 13—Product Substitution Procedures states the rules for proposing and judging substitutes once, for the whole project, so repeating 'or equal' after each name adds nothing. That is the 'say it once and in the right place' principle; Section 01 42 00 covers references, and a substitution page on the bid form only lists what bidders propose.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, shop drawings, product data, and samples are:

options.A: Contract Documents once the architect approves them
options.B: Contract Documents only for delegated-design work
options.C: Not Contract Documents, even when approved
options.D: Modifications once the contractor stamps them
options.E: Contract Documents once the owner accepts them
options.F: Part of the Drawings once incorporated in the Work

questions.explanation: Under A201, shop drawings, product data and samples are not Contract Documents, whether or not they are approved. They show how the Contractor proposes to meet the information and design concept in the Contract Documents, so review does not turn them into contract requirements or Modifications. EJCDC C-700 takes the same position.

questions.question: An A/E expects to ask the AHJ for a code interpretation at a meeting. Which statements are correct?

options.A: The supporting information should be sent to the AHJ to review ahead of the meeting.
options.B: The meeting may require design drawings, product literature, material ratings, and product certifications.
options.C: Product representatives should send interpretation information straight to the AHJ rather than to the A/E.
options.D: Only the product representative may present the interpretation request to the AHJ.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: Both {A} and {C}

questions.explanation: When an interpretation is expected, the A/E sends the supporting information to the AHJ in advance so it can be reviewed before the meeting, and the meeting may call for drawings, references, product literature, material ratings and certifications. Product representatives route their information through the A/E rather than straight to the code official, and nothing limits the request to the rep presenting it.

questions.question: Specifying 'ASTM C150, Type I Portland cement' is an example of which specification method?

options.A: Descriptive method
options.B: Performance method
options.C: Reference standard method
options.D: Closed proprietary method
options.E: Open proprietary method
options.F: Basis-of-design method

questions.explanation: Citing ASTM C150, Type I sets the cement's requirements by pointing to an established industry standard instead of writing them out, which is reference standard specifying. No brand is named, so it is not proprietary, and it neither describes properties in the specifier's own words (descriptive) nor states an end result to be verified (performance).

questions.question: Estimated quantities for unit price items are stated in the:

options.A: General conditions
options.B: Bid or proposal form
options.C: Instructions to bidders
options.D: Affected Division 02-49 sections
options.E: Section 01 22 00, Unit Prices
options.F: Schedule of values

questions.explanation: Estimated quantities for unit price items are stated on the bid or proposal form, where they give every bidder the same basis and let the owner compare bids. The Division 01 unit price section lists each item with its unit and method of measurement but does not repeat the quantities, and the schedule of values is the contractor's payment breakdown.

questions.question: To keep the documents consistent, revision identifiers in the specifications should be coordinated with which documents?

options.A: The bid form and bid tabulation
options.B: The revisions shown on the drawings
options.C: The submittal and RFI logs
options.D: The schedule of values
options.E: The addenda issued to bidders
options.F: The project manual table of contents

questions.explanation: Revision identifiers in the specifications, such as revision numbers, delta symbols and clouds, should match those used on the drawings and in addenda and modifications, so a change reads the same way in every contract document. Logs, pricing forms and the table of contents track or list information but are not where revisions are marked.

questions.question: Which agreement should the specifier review first when developing the project manual?

options.A: Owner-Contractor Agreement
options.B: Surety bond agreement
options.C: Owner-A/E Agreement
options.D: Subcontractor agreements
options.E: A/E-Consultant Agreement
options.F: Owner-Construction Manager Agreement

questions.explanation: Among the first tasks in preparing a project manual is reviewing the Owner-A/E Agreement, which defines the A/E's services and so what the specifier must deliver. The Owner-Contractor Agreement and general conditions are reviewed after that, when they are available; subcontracts and surety bonds are the contractor's arrangements.

questions.question: The International Building Code is published by the:

options.A: International Conference of Building Officials (ICBO)
options.B: National Fire Protection Association (NFPA)
options.C: Building Officials and Code Administrators (BOCA)
options.D: International Code Council (ICC)
options.E: International Association of Plumbing and Mechanical Officials (IAPMO)
options.F: American National Standards Institute (ANSI)

questions.explanation: The International Building Code is published by the International Code Council, which also publishes the IECC, IFC, IRC and the other International codes. NFPA writes model codes of its own that jurisdictions can adopt, such as NFPA 101 and NFPA 5000, and ANSI coordinates standards, but neither publishes the IBC.

questions.question: What organizational system should outline specifications use?

options.A: PPDFormat numbering and structure
options.B: OmniClass numbering structure
options.C: MasterFormat numbering structure
options.D: UniFormat numbering structure
options.E: UDS sheet numbering structure
options.F: Bid package numbering structure

questions.explanation: Outline specifications are organized by MasterFormat numbers and titles so they match the organization of the final project manual as closely as possible. UniFormat organizes by building element, as in a preliminary project description, and SectionFormat only guides the order of information inside each outline section.

questions.question: Which term names the written volume that holds the procurement requirements, the contract forms, the conditions of the contract, and the specifications?

options.A: Specifications
options.B: Procurement requirements
options.C: Contract documents
options.D: Project manual
options.E: Construction documents
options.F: Conditions of the contract

questions.explanation: The project manual is the written part of the construction documents, put together for procuring the construction contract and for building the project, and it holds all four of those parts. Specifications, procurement requirements and conditions are only components of it, and contract documents and construction documents also include the drawings.

questions.question: Streamlining in specifications most often refers to:

options.A: Combining PART 1 and PART 2 into one article
options.B: Removing all administrative requirements text
options.C: Using a colon in place of "shall be" in lists
options.D: Eliminating reference standards from sections
options.E: Writing each sentence in the indicative mood
options.F: Listing products by brand with "or equal"

questions.explanation: Streamlining lists products, materials and standards with the subject first, then a colon, as in 'Aggregate: ASTM C33'; the colon stands in for 'shall be' or 'shall comply with.' A statement in Division 01 or the supplementary conditions explains the convention. It trims wording; it does not delete requirements or merge parts.

questions.question: When schedules are placed within a specification section, where are they conventionally located?

options.A: At the end of PART 3 — EXECUTION
options.B: At the end of PART 1 — GENERAL
options.C: In an appendix at the back of the project manual
options.D: At the end of PART 2 — PRODUCTS
options.E: At the beginning of PART 3 — EXECUTION
options.F: At the beginning of PART 2 — PRODUCTS

questions.explanation: Schedules placed in a specification section, such as hardware or sealant schedules, go at the end of PART 3—EXECUTION. They are not really execution requirements; they sit there for convenience. Schedules covering materials from several sections belong on the drawings or in a separate section instead.

questions.question: Specifying "3000 psi concrete strength at 28 days" is an example of which method?

options.A: Performance
options.B: Open proprietary
options.C: Descriptive
options.D: Reference standard
options.E: Closed proprietary
options.F: Basis of design

questions.explanation: Requiring 3000 psi strength at 28 days states the end result and a measurable test for compliance while leaving the mix design to the contractor, which is performance specifying. A descriptive specification would spell out the mix proportions and materials, and a reference standard specification would cite an industry standard.

questions.question: During construction, a contractor proposes a substitute product. Under AIA A201, what must happen before the contractor may use it?

options.A: Architect approval of it as a shop drawing submittal
options.B: Owner consent after Architect evaluation, by Change Order or CCD
options.C: Architect finding it equal, at no change in the Contract Sum
options.D: Owner consent after Architect evaluation, issued as an addendum
options.E: Architect consent after Owner evaluation, by Change Order or CCD
options.F: Architect determination after evaluation, issued as a field order

questions.explanation: Under A201 §3.4.2 the Contractor may substitute only with the Owner's consent, after the Architect has evaluated the proposal, and by Change Order or Construction Change Directive, minor changes excepted. An addendum modifies the procurement documents before the contract is signed, so it is the wrong instrument once construction is under way.

questions.question: In the usual sequence of product research and evaluation, what comes right after identifying the type of product required?

options.A: Compile a preliminary list of products and makers
options.B: Compare product quality, availability, and costs
options.C: Establish the desired performance and design criteria
options.D: Obtain budget quotes from product representatives
options.E: Summarize product quotes for the cost estimate
options.F: Draft the preliminary project description

questions.explanation: Product research runs in order: identify the type of product, set its requirements from the desired performance and design criteria, research and compare candidate products, and finally compile a preliminary list of products and manufacturers that meet the design and code requirements. Comparing quality and cost is the third step, and the list comes last.

questions.question: Which of the following are NOT typical closeout submittals?

options.A: Final survey
options.B: Extra stock materials
options.C: Maintenance contracts
options.D: Qualification statements
options.E: Manufacturer reports
options.F: Spare parts

questions.explanation: Typical closeout submittals are maintenance contracts, operation and maintenance data, the final survey, warranties, project record documents, spare parts and extra stock materials. Qualification statements and manufacturer reports are informational submittals made during the work; the final survey surprises many, but it is a closeout item.

questions.question: Reference standards are typically developed by:

options.A: Model code-writing organizations
options.B: Federal and state regulatory agencies
options.C: Local authorities having jurisdiction
options.D: Industry associations and societies
options.E: Ecolabel program administrators
options.F: Federal procurement agencies

questions.explanation: Reference standards are voluntary documents created and maintained by associations, societies, institutes and manufacturer or installer groups involved with the products, not by government agencies. Model code bodies adopt them by reference because those groups have done research and testing the code writers cannot match.

questions.question: EJCDC C-700 cuts off addenda earlier than AIA A201 does. The earlier cutoff reflects:

options.A: The use of field orders for changes before award
options.B: The engineer's loss of authority once bids are opened
options.C: The rule that an opened bid is itself a binding contract
options.D: Public-works limits on changing documents after bid opening
options.E: A private owner's freedom to negotiate until the agreement is signed
options.F: Jurisdictions that allow negotiation with the lowest responsible bidder

questions.explanation: EJCDC C-700 defines addenda as issued before bids are received, while A201 lets them run until the Agreement is executed. The earlier cutoff suits public works, where rules may forbid changing the procurement documents once bids are opened; A201's later cutoff suits a private owner who may negotiate up to signing. Field orders are post-award minor changes, not a procurement tool.

questions.question: Cleaning substrates and protecting in-place conditions before installation belong in which article?

options.A: PART 3 Examination of the existing substrates and conditions
options.B: PART 2 Fabrication and source assembly
options.C: PART 1 Field [or] Site Conditions
options.D: PART 3 Preparation of surfaces to receive work
options.E: PART 3 Protection of completed installations
options.F: PART 3 Cleaning and waste management

questions.explanation: The PREPARATION article of PART 3 covers readying the surface, area or site for the section's products: protecting in-place conditions, surface preparation such as cleaning the substrate, and demolition or removal. Examination only verifies that conditions are acceptable, and the Cleaning and Protection articles deal with the finished installation afterward.

questions.question: On a federally funded public project, which specification method is generally restricted?

options.A: Reference standard
options.B: Descriptive
options.C: Performance
options.D: Proprietary
options.E: Commercial item description
options.F: Non-restrictive

questions.explanation: The federal government and many public authorities restrict proprietary, exclusionary specifications except in exceptional circumstances and call for non-restrictive specifications instead. Descriptive, performance and reference standard methods can all be written non-restrictively, as long as several manufacturers can meet them.

questions.question: When a design-builder contracts out the construction, which procurement option does it most often use?

options.A: Competitive bid option
options.B: Competitive proposal option
options.C: Qualifications-based selection
options.D: Negotiation option
options.E: Best value: fees option
options.F: Best value: total cost option

questions.explanation: A design-builder that hires a separate contractor for the construction may use any of the design-bid-build procurement options, but most choose negotiation because they tend to work with contractors they already have relationships with. Competitive bidding stays available but is not the usual choice in that situation.

questions.question: Where should a copy of the standardized RFI form be placed?

options.A: In the A/E's office files, filled out from calls
options.B: In the supplementary conditions, as a contract form
options.C: In the instructions to bidders only
options.D: In the project manual, for the contractor's use
options.E: In Section 01 33 00, with the submittal forms
options.F: In the procurement form supplements, for bidders

questions.explanation: A standardized RFI form, with room for the question and for the A/E's answer, should be bound into the project manual and given to the contractor to use during construction. Placing it in the project manual makes every request arrive in the same format; it is not a bidding form or a submittal form.

questions.question: Which reference standard issue is the warning that citing two or more standards for the same product can let their requirements clash and make an inferior product more likely?

options.A: Duplication and conflict
options.B: Availability
options.C: Optional provisions
options.D: Applicability
options.E: Design criteria
options.F: Reduced conflict and duplication

questions.explanation: Duplication and conflict is the issue: when two or more standards cover one product, the requirements of one can contradict another, which opens the door to an inferior product. 'Reduced conflict and duplication' sounds similar but is an advantage of standards, credited to ANSI's coordination; applicability and optional provisions are separate issues.

questions.question: Why must each design consultant be aware of the specifications production schedule?

options.A: To coordinate addenda and substitution responses after bid opening
options.B: To draft the conditions of the contract for their portion
options.C: To ensure the A/E receives every section on time and complete
options.D: To invoice the owner directly for their coordination work
options.E: To set the bid date for their portion of the work
options.F: To produce the document packages the CM identifies

questions.explanation: Most consultants write the sections for their own part of the project, so each must know the production schedule and the delivery dates for its documents. That way the A/E receives every section on time and nothing is missing when the set goes to the owner; consultants do not set bid dates or draft the conditions of the contract.

questions.question: Which of these are ecolabels?

options.A: UL fire-resistance listing
options.B: Model code evaluation report
options.C: FSC Chain of Custody Certification
options.D: ASTM E84 Class A rating
options.E: CRI Green Label Plus
options.F: Life cycle assessment

questions.explanation: Ecolabels are marks on product packaging that let buyers quickly spot products meeting specific environmental performance criteria; examples are CRI Green Label Plus, UL GREENGUARD, FSC Chain of Custody Certification and Green Seal. A UL fire-resistance listing or an ASTM E84 rating marks fire performance, and a life cycle assessment is an analysis method, not a label.

questions.question: Which statements about the specifier's role in product and material coordination are correct?

options.A: The specifier should serve as the default coordinator of products and materials
options.B: The specifier alone decides which products are specified
options.C: The specifier is the last line of defense on intended use and compatibility
options.D: The specifier usually selects products before the designers detail them
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: The specifier is the default coordinator of products and materials and the last line of defense that each is used as intended and works with adjacent materials. That role does not make the specifier the only one deciding which products are used, and selection is usually led by the A/E and design team rather than made by the specifier ahead of the design.

questions.question: An office master's section template should follow which formats?

options.A: MasterFormat and UniFormat
options.B: SectionFormat and PageFormat
options.C: UniFormat and PageFormat
options.D: OmniClass and UniFormat
options.E: MasterFormat and SectionFormat
options.F: OmniClass and PageFormat

questions.explanation: A master section template should follow SectionFormat for the arrangement of articles within each section and PageFormat for the layout of each page, so every new section starts out consistent. MasterFormat supplies section numbers and titles and UniFormat organizes by building element, so neither governs what a template looks like inside.

questions.question: Which Division 01 groupings align with PART 3—EXECUTION of SectionFormat?

options.A: Quality Control (Source)
options.B: Quality Assurance
options.C: Quality Control (Field)
options.D: Performance Requirements
options.E: Temporary Facilities and Controls
options.F: Life Cycle Activities

questions.explanation: Division 01 mirrors SectionFormat's three parts. Quality Control (Field), Execution and Closeout Requirements, and Life Cycle Activities align with PART 3; Product Requirements, Performance Requirements and Quality Control (Source) align with PART 2; and Quality Assurance and Temporary Facilities and Controls align with PART 1.

questions.question: Which pairings of a reference standard with the category of standard it represents are correct?

options.A: ASTM E2112, installation of exterior windows, doors and skylights: workmanship standard
options.B: NFPA 13, installation of sprinkler systems: installation standard
options.C: ASTM E119, fire tests of building construction and materials: performance standard
options.D: ACI 318, building code requirements for structural concrete: product standard
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: ASTM E2112 is classed as a workmanship standard, even though its title says installation, and NFPA 13 is an installation standard. ASTM E119 is a test method standard, not a performance standard (ASTM F1487 for playground equipment is a performance example), and ACI 318 is a design standard, not a product standard like APA PS-1 for plywood.

questions.question: Which project conditions call for full-length specification sections?

options.A: High liability risk
options.B: No installation involved
options.C: Result matters more than method
options.D: Design still fluid
options.E: Larger, more complex project
options.F: Limited scope of work

questions.explanation: Full-length sections suit larger, more complex projects and projects with high liability risk. Limited-scope work suits shortform specifications, a design that is still fluid calls for outline specifications, a need where the result matters most calls for performance specifying, and goods with no installation call for purchasing specifications.

questions.question: Why are last-minute design changes the most likely cause of discrepancies between drawings and specifications?

options.A: Addenda issued late in bidding do not become contract documents
options.B: An addendum fixes a duplicated requirement in one place but not the other
options.C: Late changes are drawn, and the specifications override the drawings
options.D: Bidders price the original documents instead of the addenda
options.E: Changes in early packages are not carried into later packages
options.F: Bidders' differing interpretations are turned into change orders

questions.explanation: When a requirement appears in both the drawings and the specifications, an addendum making a last-minute change can fix it in one place and miss the other, leaving a conflict. That is why each requirement is stated once, in the right place. Addenda do become contract documents, and change orders come afterward, as a result of the conflict.

questions.question: A design is over budget, and the team revisits its value analysis decisions. Which actions are appropriate?

options.A: Re-evaluate earlier product choices for savings that keep quality
options.B: Evaluate a new set of material and product solutions
options.C: Adjust the objectives and criteria to create new evaluation criteria
options.D: Choose cheaper products without regard to other project criteria
options.E: {A}, {B} and {C}
options.F: Both {A} and {B}

questions.explanation: When a design runs over budget, the team can revisit earlier choices for savings that keep quality, evaluate a new set of material and product solutions, and adjust the objectives and criteria to form new evaluation criteria. Buying cheaper products regardless of other project objectives is not value analysis, which weighs quality, performance, budget and schedule together.

questions.question: What is the main drawback of commercial master guide specifications?

options.A: They become outdated unless vigilantly maintained
options.B: They contain far more than a project needs
options.C: Their proprietary language needs editing for competitive bids
options.D: They do not follow MasterFormat numbers and titles
options.E: They save time only on nearly identical projects
options.F: Their product information is unreliable

questions.explanation: Commercial master guide specifications are regularly updated, but they hold far more information than any one project needs, so extensive editing is necessary. Going out of date is the weakness of an office master that is not maintained, and proprietary language needing edits is the drawback of manufacturer-furnished guide specifications.

questions.question: Requirements for CPM or Gantt scheduling belong in which section?
questions.explanation: Section 01 32 00—Construction Progress Documentation is where a critical path method (CPM) network schedule with updates, or the simpler Gantt method, is required, along with long-lead items and milestone dates. Section 01 33 00 covers submittal procedures, 01 31 19 project meetings, and 01 32 33 photographic documentation.

questions.question: Why are electronic formats useful for distributing addenda?

options.A: Owners need them for the record documents
options.B: Bidders must forward them to sub-bidders quickly
options.C: They need no acknowledgment on the bid form
options.D: AHJs require electronic copies for plan review
options.E: They show the A/E's tracked changes to bidders
options.F: Some formats can block changes after distribution

questions.explanation: Bidders often have to pass addenda on to sub-bidders on short notice, and electronic distribution makes that fast. Formats such as PDF can also carry security settings that stop anyone from altering the document once it is issued. Bidders still acknowledge addenda on the bid form, and issued addenda show final text, not tracked edits.

questions.question: Using BIM clash detection with the rest of the design team minimizes which of the following?

options.A: Shop drawing and submittal reviews during construction
options.B: The number of specification sections each discipline writes
options.C: Substitution requests received during bidding
options.D: Time-consuming coordination meetings
options.E: Budget variances that require corrective action
options.F: Costly construction changes in the field

questions.explanation: BIM clash detection finds where elements from different disciplines collide, and working through it with the whole design team cuts down on time-consuming meetings and costly changes in the field. It does not replace submittal review during construction, and budget variances are a cost-control matter.

questions.question: Which statements about consultants hired directly by the owner are correct?

options.A: Commissioning agents and security advisers are typical examples
options.B: They are employed by the A/E under the design contract
options.C: Specifications should cover the contractor's duties in working with them
options.D: A construction manager acting as advisor is one of them
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: Owners regularly hire their own consultants, such as commissioning agents, security advisers and construction managers acting as advisors. When those consultants deal with the contractor during construction, the specifications should state the contractor's responsibilities for working with them. They are the owner's consultants, not people the A/E employs under its design contract.

questions.question: Which organization coordinates standards development to reduce duplication and conflict?

options.A: ANSI
options.B: ASCE
options.C: ASTM
options.D: UL
options.E: ICC
options.F: CSA

questions.explanation: ANSI, the American National Standards Institute, coordinates standards development and adopts and promotes standards written by its accredited members, which reduces duplication and conflict between standards. ASTM and UL develop standards themselves and the ICC writes model codes; none of them plays that coordinating role.

questions.question: Revisions issued during procurement to modify the bidding documents are:

options.A: Construction change directives
options.B: Field orders
options.C: Change orders
options.D: Addenda
options.E: Substitution requests
options.F: Requests for information

questions.explanation: Addenda are written instruments issued during procurement, usually before bids are opened, to clarify, revise or delete information in the procurement documents or in earlier addenda. Change orders, construction change directives and field orders modify the contract after it is signed, and an RFI is a question, not a revision.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700, a field order is:

options.A: Signed by the owner; orders a change before price or time is set
options.B: Issued by the engineer; interprets the documents without changing the Work
options.C: Signed by owner and contractor; adjusts the price or times
options.D: Issued by the engineer; orders a minor change with no price or time change
options.E: Issued by the architect; orders a minor change with no price or time change
options.F: Signed by the owner and engineer; orders a minor change with no price change

questions.explanation: EJCDC C-700 defines a field order as the engineer's written order requiring minor changes in the Work that do not change the Contract Price or Contract Times, and it needs no owner signature. An owner-signed order issued before price or time is agreed is a work change directive, and a written interpretation clarifies without changing the Work.

questions.question: A candidate product fails one applicable code requirement but meets every other project requirement. How should the A/E treat it?

options.A: Include it as an alternate for bidders to price
options.B: Include it if the owner accepts the risk in writing
options.C: Include it if its warranty covers code-related failures
options.D: Exclude it from the project
options.E: Include it as an allowance for the owner to decide
options.F: Include it if it meets a different referenced standard

questions.explanation: A product that does not comply with an applicable code or safety rule, or with any other specified standard, should be left out of the project. Code compliance is what screens out products that create unreasonably hazardous conditions, so owner acceptance, a warranty, alternate pricing or a different standard cannot cure the failure.

questions.question: A project has one roof system, a loose-laid ballasted EPDM membrane. How should the drawings label it?

options.A: Roof membrane
options.B: Ballasted EPDM membrane
options.C: EPDM roofing, see specifications
options.D: Manufacturer's name and product number
options.E: Roofing Type A
options.F: Single-ply EPDM roofing

questions.explanation: Drawing notes should identify a material without describing it, so a project's only roof system is labeled simply 'roof membrane' and the specifications describe the ballasted EPDM. Describing the system on the drawings invites conflicts, a general 'see specifications' note is a cross-reference to avoid, and lettered types are needed only when there is more than one membrane.

questions.question: Safeguarding finished installations from damage until acceptance is most appropriately specified in:

options.A: PART 2 Source Quality Control testing
options.B: PART 3 Protection of completed work
options.C: PART 1 Delivery, Storage, and Handling
options.D: Division 01 Quality Requirements
options.E: PART 3 Preparation of in-place conditions
options.F: PART 3 Cleaning during and after the work

questions.explanation: Protecting finished work from damage until the owner accepts it is specified in the PROTECTION article of PART 3—EXECUTION. Protecting in-place conditions and surrounding surfaces before installation goes under Preparation, and delivery, storage and handling in PART 1 deals with products before they are installed.

questions.question: Under A201, the architect reviews shop drawings and other submittals only for the limited purpose of:

options.A: Approving the contractor's means, methods, sequences, and safety precautions
options.B: Determining the accuracy and completeness of all dimensions and quantities shown
options.C: Substantiating the contractor's installation and equipment-performance instructions
options.D: Checking conformance with information given and the design concept
options.E: Approving each assembly of which a reviewed item is a component
options.F: Confirming the adequacy of the delegated designer's certifications

questions.explanation: Under A201 §4.2.7 the Architect reviews submittals only to see whether they conform to the design concept and the information given in the Contract Documents. The review does not verify dimensions and quantities, substantiate installation or performance instructions, or approve means, methods, sequences and safety precautions, which remain the Contractor's responsibility.

questions.question: Administrative and procedural requirements specific to a section belong in:

options.A: PART 2—PRODUCTS
options.B: PART 3—EXECUTION
options.C: PART 1—GENERAL
options.D: Division 01
options.E: Section 01 30 00 only
options.F: The supplementary conditions

questions.explanation: PART 1—GENERAL holds the administrative, procedural and temporary requirements that apply only to that section. It extends Division 01 and should supplement it without repeating it; requirements common to all sections belong in Division 01 itself, while PART 2 and PART 3 cover products and execution.

questions.question: In the EJCDC procurement documents, the party that furnishes the Goods to the owner is the:

options.A: Vendor
options.B: Supplier
options.C: Goods contractor
options.D: Seller
options.E: Buyer
options.F: Manufacturer

questions.explanation: EJCDC purchasing documents call the manufacturer or vendor that furnishes the Goods the Seller, and the owner the Buyer. 'Goods contractor' is a generic term for that party, not EJCDC's, and in EJCDC documents a supplier, vendor or manufacturer is a party holding a subcontract under a prime construction contractor.

questions.question: Which of the following should take part in the coordination meeting held as the project design stage begins?

options.A: The specifier preparing the project manual sections
options.B: The CAD or BIM drafters producing the drawings
options.C: The selected construction inspector or testing agent
options.D: The owner's commissioning agent
options.E: The product representatives for the basis-of-design products
options.F: The authority having jurisdiction's plan reviewer

questions.explanation: The coordination meeting held as design begins brings together the A/E, its consultants, the CAD or BIM drafters and the specifier, the people who will produce the drawings and the project manual. Inspectors, testing agents, commissioning agents, product representatives and code reviewers are not part of that design-team meeting.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the substitution review process under Section 01 25 00?

options.A: To determine whether a proposed product is equivalent to the specified product
options.B: To document the basis for an automatic extension of the contract time
options.C: To establish the unit price adjustment when quantities differ from estimates
options.D: To transfer responsibility for product selection from the A/E to the contractor
options.E: To set procedures for the owner's selection of products under cash allowances
options.F: To set the participants, schedule and reports for a value analysis study

questions.explanation: Section 01 25 00—Substitution Procedures sets the basic requirements for considering the contractor's substitution proposals, including the rules and procedures for judging whether a proposed product is equivalent to the one specified. Unit prices, allowances and value analysis have their own sections, and accepting a substitute does not hand product selection to the contractor.

questions.question: When should compiling product selections and evaluations begin?

options.A: As soon as early sketches are available
options.B: When design development drawings are issued
options.C: When the outline specifications are drafted
options.D: When construction documents are nearly complete
options.E: When the owner approves schematic design
options.F: When the project manual is assembled for bidding

questions.explanation: Product decisions, evaluations of equivalent products and local availability should be recorded systematically and progressively, starting as soon as the first design drawings or sketches exist. Waiting for design development, outline specifications or late construction documents means decisions made along the way go unrecorded.

questions.question: On a single-prime project, who determines how the work is divided among subcontractors and trades?

options.A: The owner, through Division 01
options.B: The A/E, through the arrangement of sections
options.C: The A/E, through notes on the drawings
options.D: The contractor
options.E: The construction manager, through bid packages
options.F: The subcontractors, by the scopes they bid

questions.explanation: On a single-prime project, the contractor decides how to divide the work among subcontractors and trades. MasterFormat section titles and their arrangement are not scopes of work and do not assign work to trades, and the drawings should not try to define the work of particular subcontractors either.

questions.question: To keep references to alternates consistent throughout the construction documents, the A/E should:

options.A: Identify each alternate by number only, without a title
options.B: Let each consultant designate alternates in its own sections
options.C: Describe alternates only in Section 01 23 00 and the bid form
options.D: Share each alternate's designation and title with the team
options.E: Identify each alternate by title only, without a number
options.F: Describe only what each alternate adds, not the base bid

questions.explanation: Each alternate should get both a designation, such as Alternate No. 1, and a descriptive title, and those designations, titles and contents should go to every design team member so all references match. A number alone is easy to confuse, and each affected section should also say it is affected and refer to Section 01 23 00.

questions.question: Which statements about a requirement stated only in the instructions to bidders are correct?

options.A: It is not enforceable during administration of the construction contract
options.B: Under A201 it is outside the Contract Documents unless the Agreement enumerates the Instructions to Bidders
options.C: It becomes a Contract Document once repeated in an addendum issued before execution
options.D: It binds the Contractor because A201 counts the Contractor's bid among the Contract Documents
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: AIA, EJCDC and ConsensusDocs general conditions all leave procurement requirements out of the contract documents, so a provision stated only in the instructions to bidders cannot be enforced during construction. A201 §1.1.1 excludes the Instructions to Bidders, the bid and the bidding portions of addenda unless the Agreement lists them, so repeating the requirement in an addendum does not make it binding.

questions.question: Which statements about closed proprietary specifications are correct?

options.A: They can name one product or several products as options.
options.B: They do not allow substitutions.
options.C: They must name at least three products to be valid.
options.D: They name one product followed by 'or equal.'
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: A closed proprietary specification may name a single product or several products as options, but either way substitutions are not allowed. Naming at least three products is the point where competition may be achieved, not a validity rule, and adding 'or equal' makes it an open proprietary specification.

questions.question: When is value analysis most efficient and effective?

options.A: At the end of construction documents
options.B: After bids show the actual prices
options.C: Early in the design process
options.D: During construction, through substitutions
options.E: At pricing, while competition still applies
options.F: During procurement, through addenda

questions.explanation: Value analysis is most efficient and effective early in design, when a change touches fewer related decisions. The later it happens, the more it disrupts the design and schedule and the less value is kept; simple changes are still possible at pricing, and during construction both cost and schedule are most at risk.

questions.question: SectionFormat's three parts, in order, are:

options.A: PRODUCTS, EXECUTION, GENERAL
options.B: GENERAL, PRODUCTS, EXECUTION
options.C: SUMMARY, PRODUCTS, EXECUTION
options.D: GENERAL, EXECUTION, PRODUCTS
options.E: GENERAL, PRODUCTS, INSTALLATION
options.F: SUMMARY, MATERIALS, EXECUTION

questions.explanation: Every section is arranged PART 1—GENERAL, PART 2—PRODUCTS, PART 3—EXECUTION. Writing products first, then execution, then general is the recommended writing sequence, not the order of the parts, and Summary is an article inside PART 1, not a part.

questions.question: Estimated unit price quantities listed on the bid form are best described as:
