options.A: Guaranteed minimum quantities for which the contractor will be paid in full
options.B: Estimates used to compare bids; payment is for work actually performed
options.C: Cash allowances included in the contract sum for the listed unit-price items
options.D: Maximum quantities that the contractor is contractually barred from exceeding
options.E: Fixed quantities that the owner has no right to increase or decrease
options.F: Final quantities, so no change order adjusts the contract sum for them

questions.explanation: The quantities listed on the bid form are only estimates of the work shown; they let the owner compare bids and fix the contract sum. The contractor is paid for the work actually performed and measured, the owner may raise or lower quantities within a stated maximum, and the final sum is adjusted by change order to the actual quantities.

questions.question: Which simple forms are recommended for recording questions about the specifications during procurement?

options.A: Substitution request form (during procurement)
options.B: Substitution request log
options.C: Request for information form
options.D: Communication record
options.E: Communication log
options.F: Substitution request form (during construction)

questions.explanation: A communication record and a communication log are simple, effective tools for capturing bidders' questions about the specifications during procurement, and every answer must then go out in writing, usually by addendum. Substitution request forms and logs track proposed substitutes, and the RFI form is the tool for questions during construction.

questions.question: When the A/E begins product research, the product representative is often consulted to determine:

options.A: The project's construction budget
options.B: The AHJ's code interpretation
options.C: The final product selection
options.D: Product details and product viability
options.E: The owner's project requirements
options.F: The project's construction schedule

questions.explanation: At the start of research, the A/E often consults the product representative to learn product details and whether the product is viable for the use. The representative is an information resource; the A/E makes the final selection, often with the owner and design team, and only the AHJ can give a code interpretation.

questions.question: Codes applicable to a project:

options.A: Vary between states and between local jurisdictions
options.B: Are set by each state and applied the same in every city
options.C: Are the latest model code editions the ICC has published
options.D: Are chosen by the A/E to suit the project type
options.E: Are model codes adopted in full, without amendment
options.F: Are enforced by the ICC, which writes them

questions.explanation: Applicable codes differ from state to state and between local jurisdictions; a city may even adopt codes different from those of its county. A model code becomes enforceable only when the authority having jurisdiction adopts it, so the edition in force is the adopted one, not simply the newest ICC edition, and the A/E does not choose it.

questions.question: Which items should the office master list of section numbers and titles designate for each section?

options.A: The subcontractor pricing anticipated for the work covered by the section
options.B: The construction sequencing and milestone dates affecting the section
options.C: The owner's preferred manufacturers to be named within the section
options.D: The individual responsible for preparing and updating the section
options.E: The order of priority for completing the section if it is unfinished
options.F: The reference standards to be cited in the section's Part 2 articles

questions.explanation: An office master list of section numbers and titles records, for each section, a short description of its work and related work, its status, the dates of first preparation and latest revision, the person responsible for preparing and updating it, and the priority for finishing incomplete sections. Pricing, sequencing, preferred makers and reference standards are project or section content.

questions.question: Which statements about prescriptive specifying are correct?

options.A: Descriptive specifying is used for prescriptive specifications.
options.B: Proprietary specifying is used for prescriptive specifications.
options.C: Reference standard specifying can be used only for prescriptive specifications.
options.D: Performance specifications specify the means as well as the results.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: Prescriptive specifications state the products and processes rather than the results, and both the descriptive and proprietary methods are used to write them. Reference standard specifying can serve both prescriptive and performance specifications, and performance specifications state results without prescribing the means.

questions.question: The procedure for requests for information belongs in which Division 01 section?

options.A: Section 01 32 00—Construction Progress Documentation
options.B: Section 01 25 00—Substitution Procedures
options.C: Section 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures
options.D: Section 01 26 00—Contract Modification Procedures
options.E: Section 01 29 00—Payment Procedures
options.F: Section 01 24 00—Value Analysis

questions.explanation: Section 01 26 00—Contract Modification Procedures provides the method for the contractor or owner to ask for clarification of work that is not described or detailed well enough, and for the A/E to answer without changing the contract sum or time. MasterFormat places 01 26 13 Requests for Information under it; an RFI is not a submittal.

questions.question: When engineering consultants write sections of the project manual, the prime A/E should:

options.A: Leave coordination to each consultant for its own discipline
options.B: Bind each consultant's sections as a separate volume
options.C: Assume responsibility for overall coordination
options.D: Have each consultant write a Division 01 for its discipline
options.E: Assign overall coordination to the owner's representative
options.F: Leave coordination to the contractor's submittal reviews

questions.explanation: The prime A/E should take responsibility for overall coordination of the specifications, including sections written by engineering consultants and specialists. Leaving coordination to each consultant, or having each write its own Division 01, produces separate general requirements that conflict with one another.

questions.question: OmniClass is best described as:

options.A: A standardized page-layout convention for printed specification sections
options.B: A multi-table classification framework for the entire built environment
options.C: A commercial specification-writing software platform used by specifiers
options.D: A classification scheme limited to building elements, similar to UniFormat
options.E: A work-results numbering system that replaced MasterFormat outright
options.F: A standard for arranging the information within each specification section

questions.explanation: OmniClass is a classification framework of many tables, based on ISO standards, for organizing every kind of construction information about the built environment over its whole life cycle. It incorporates MasterFormat as its work results table and UniFormat as its elements table rather than replacing them.

questions.question: Who should be the default coordinator of products and materials?

options.A: The A/E's project manager
options.B: The specifier
options.C: The project designer
options.D: The contractor
options.E: The designated coordinator
options.F: The product representative

questions.explanation: The specifier is the default coordinator of products and materials, the last check that they are used as intended and work with adjacent materials. The A/E's project manager holds ultimate responsibility for coordinating the construction documents as a whole and may name a designated coordinator, which is a different role.

questions.question: Putting common administrative requirements in Division 01, rather than repeating them in every section, follows which principle?

options.A: Write broadly enough to apply to all sections
options.B: Use the same format in every section
options.C: Specify by reference standard where possible
options.D: Say it once and in the right place
options.E: State it at two levels of detail
options.F: Be clear, concise, correct and complete

questions.explanation: Division 01 follows the principle 'say it once and in the right place': requirements stated once there apply to every technical section, while repeating them throughout would invite conflicts and omissions. Writing broadly is how Division 01 reaches all sections, not the principle itself, and the four Cs describe good writing, not where information goes.

questions.question: An RFI is appropriately used when:

options.A: An item of work is insufficiently described or detailed in the contract documents
options.B: The contractor seeks to add scope and a corresponding increase in the contract sum
options.C: The contractor is preparing its periodic application for payment for completed work
options.D: A product substitution is proposed by the contractor after the contract is awarded
options.E: The contractor wants the architect's approval of its means and methods
options.F: The contractor asks for coordination information already shown in the documents

questions.explanation: An RFI asks the A/E to clarify an item of work that is not described or detailed well enough in the contract documents, and the answer should not change the contract sum or time. Added scope with added cost goes through the change process, substitutions follow substitution procedures, and information already shown needs no clarification.

questions.question: Besides raising construction cost, overspecifying Division 01 can:

options.A: Turn Division 01 provisions into procurement requirements
options.B: Shift design liability from the A/E to the contractor
options.C: Override the general conditions wherever the two conflict
options.D: Create excess obligations for the contract administrator
options.E: Make Division 01 provisions part of the agreement
options.F: Relieve the contractor of control over means and methods

questions.explanation: Division 01 administrative requirements and temporary facilities carry direct and indirect costs, so overspecifying them can raise construction cost needlessly and load excess obligations on whoever administers the construction contract. It does not shift design liability, change which document governs, or turn Division 01 into procurement requirements.

questions.question: Products are built to tolerate only certain project conditions, which the specifier compares with the site before selecting one. Which of these is NOT one of those conditions?

options.A: Manufacturer's financial stability
options.B: Frequency of use
options.C: Space constraints
options.D: Security, vandalism, or theft concerns
options.E: Atmospheric pressure
options.F: Owner's or manufacturer's maintenance program

questions.explanation: The conditions a product must withstand include its installed location, temperature, humidity, wind and sun, seismic risk, atmospheric pressure, chemical exposure, interior or exterior use, space constraints, frequency of use, security concerns and the maintenance program. A manufacturer's financial stability matters when choosing a source, but it is not a site condition.

questions.question: On a CMAR project, who prepares the procurement documents for each subcontract?

options.A: The A/E, as part of its basic services
options.B: The owner's procurement staff
options.C: The construction manager
options.D: The A/E, with the construction manager's review
options.E: The owner's attorney or legal department
options.F: The A/E, as one set for all packages

questions.explanation: Under construction manager at risk, the A/E does not prepare procurement documents; the construction manager prepares them for each subcontract it plans to issue. The A/E still works with the construction manager on the drawings and specifications that go into each package, so the packages carry the information they need.

questions.question: Two standards both define functional requirements for the same product, but they differ. What does this redundancy make especially important?

options.A: Citing both standards so either may be used
options.B: Knowing which standard the specs cite and what each covers
options.C: Citing only the more recent of the two standards
options.D: Having the manufacturer certify against both standards
options.E: Citing whichever standard the manufacturer prefers
options.F: Letting the AHJ pick one of the standards at plan review

questions.explanation: Codes and standards often overlap, and two standards for the same product can differ a great deal, so the A/E must know which aspects the compliance evaluation covers and which standard the specifications actually cite. Citing both, or whichever one the manufacturer prefers, could let a product that meets only the weaker one qualify.

questions.question: In the MasterFormat section number 03 20 00, what does the third pair of digits (00) represent?

options.A: Level 2 number
options.B: Level 3 number
options.C: Level 4 number
options.D: Division
options.E: Subgroup number
options.F: Group number

questions.explanation: MasterFormat numbers are built from three pairs of digits: the first pair is the Level 1 division (03, Concrete), the second pair is Level 2 (20), and the third pair is Level 3 (00). An optional fourth pair can be added for Level 4; groups and subgroups are not identified by these digits.

questions.question: Which Division 01 section lists every alternate and describes what the base bid and each alternate include?
questions.explanation: Section 01 23 00—Alternates lists every alternate proposed for the project and describes what the base bid includes and what each alternate includes. Section 01 21 00 is Allowances, 01 22 00 Unit Prices, 01 24 00 Value Analysis, 01 25 00 Substitution Procedures and 01 26 00 Contract Modification Procedures.

questions.question: MasterFormat Division 23 covers which work result?

options.A: Plumbing systems, piping, and fixtures
options.B: Communications, data, and signal systems
options.C: Electrical power, lighting, and distribution
options.D: Heating, ventilating, and air-conditioning
options.E: Fire suppression systems and sprinklers
options.F: Integrated automation and building controls

questions.explanation: Division 23 is Heating, Ventilating, and Air-Conditioning, in the Facility Services Subgroup. Its neighbors, easy to confuse with it, are Division 21 Fire Suppression, 22 Plumbing, 25 Integrated Automation, 26 Electrical and 27 Communications.

questions.question: When a product representative helps the design team with a specific product, how is that product often specified?

options.A: As a sole-source product
options.B: As an owner-preferred product
options.C: As an allowance item
options.D: As a basis-of-design product
options.E: As an alternate
options.F: As a comparable product

questions.explanation: When a product representative helps the design team with a particular product, that product is often named as the basis of design. Division 01 should then define basis-of-design products and how comparable products will be accepted, which keeps the specification from becoming sole-source.

questions.question: Which delivery method is most commonly associated with project descriptions written as performance specifications?

options.A: Construction Manager at Risk
options.B: Owner-Build
options.C: Design-Bid-Build
options.D: Design-Build
options.E: Integrated Project Delivery
options.F: Design-Negotiate-Build

questions.explanation: Project descriptions for design-build are a typical place for performance specifying: the owner states the required results and how they will be verified, and the design-builder, who completes the design, chooses the means. Performance specifying gives the flexibility to accept any solution that delivers the same result.

questions.question: When reviewing project requirements, which shortcomings of master and proprietary guide specifications must the specifier watch for?

options.A: They may not address local project conditions
options.B: They may lack reference standards for listed products
options.C: They may not follow section format and page layout
options.D: They may offer no options for products and materials
options.E: They may contain references that do not apply
options.F: They may not allow editing to suit the project

questions.explanation: Local conditions and governing codes must be reviewed because proprietary and master guide specifications may fail to address local project conditions or may carry references that do not apply. Guide specifications exist to standardize formats and offer product options, and they are meant to be edited for each project.

questions.question: When the work is split among several prime contracts, the contracts and the scope of each are identified in:

options.A: Section 01 11 00—Summary of Work
options.B: Section 01 14 00—Work Restrictions
options.C: Section 01 31 00—Project Management and Coordination
options.D: Section 01 12 00—Multiple Contract Summary
options.E: Section 01 11 16—Work by Owner
options.F: Section 01 11 19—Purchase Contracts

questions.explanation: Section 01 12 00—Multiple Contract Summary is used when the work is done under more than one contract; it identifies the contracts, the scope of each, and each party's coordination duties. Section 01 11 00—Summary of Work describes work under a single contract, and 01 31 00 covers coordination procedures, not each contract's scope.

questions.question: How is product evaluation during design best characterized?

options.A: A progressive evaluation over several design phases
options.B: A single evaluation made when specifications are drafted
options.C: An evaluation made once the contractor's submittals arrive
options.D: An evaluation made once, at the end of schematic design
options.E: A one-time product decision made by the owner in programming
options.F: An evaluation made after the drawings and specifications are done

questions.explanation: Product evaluation is progressive and multi-phased: it starts in schematic design with conceptual decisions about the primary products and continues as detailed information is gathered and checked in later design phases. Drawings and specifications are developed after a product is found to comply, so evaluation is not a single event.

questions.question: On a performance bond, which party remains primarily liable to perform the bonded contract?

options.A: The surety
options.B: The obligee
options.C: The principal
options.D: The claimant
options.E: The indemnitor
options.F: The bonding agent

questions.explanation: On a performance bond the principal, the contractor, remains primarily liable to perform the bonded contract and must indemnify the surety for any loss. The surety, like a cosigner on a note, is only secondarily liable once the principal defaults, and the obligee is the owner the bond protects.

questions.question: Who has the responsibility to enforce consistent terminology and abbreviations across the construction documents?

options.A: The contractor
options.B: The specifier
options.C: The A/E
options.D: Each consultant for its own discipline
options.E: The owner
options.F: The CAD or BIM drafters

questions.explanation: The A/E is responsible for enforcing consistent terminology and abbreviations across the construction documents. Inconsistent terms usually spread through reused old details and poorly edited specifications; the specifier and consultants help keep terms aligned, but enforcement across the whole set rests with the A/E.

questions.question: Why should consultants avoid general notes on their drawings about administrative matters?

options.A: Drawings are not contract documents, so the notes cannot be enforced
options.B: Administrative notes must be sealed by the prime A/E, not the consultant
options.C: Bidders price only the specifications, so the notes would be ignored
options.D: They belong in Division 01, and repeating them invites conflicts
options.E: Consultants are not permitted to write any specification sections
options.F: Notes on the drawings would take precedence over the specifications

questions.explanation: Administrative matters and contract terms belong in Division 01 and the other contract documents. When consultants put such general notes on their drawings, each discipline ends up with its own general requirements, which invites conflicts. Drawings are contract documents, so enforceability is not the reason.

questions.question: During the construction documents phase, documents are typically reviewed for coordination at which completion stages?

options.A: 25 and 75 percent
options.B: 50 and 90 percent
options.C: 75 and 95 percent
options.D: 90 and 100 percent
options.E: 60 and 100 percent
options.F: 50 and 75 percent

questions.explanation: Construction documents are typically checked for coordination at the 50 percent and 90 percent completion stages, after the schematic design and design development reviews. At each milestone, interim specification sections and consultant drawings are gathered and checked within and between disciplines and against the project manual.

questions.question: Which statements about precedence between the drawings and specifications are correct?

options.A: Precedence statements in the project manual are not recommended
options.B: The conditions should state that the A/E makes a documented interpretation
options.C: The conditions should state that the specifications govern over the drawings
options.D: A precedence listing may be prepared for bidding purposes only
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: Because drawings and specifications complement each other, setting an order of precedence in the project manual is not recommended. The conditions of the contract should say only that the A/E makes a documented interpretation when the two conflict, and a precedence list may be prepared for bidding purposes only, if needed. A clause saying the specifications govern is exactly what to avoid.

questions.question: For the fast-track technique to work, what must be clearly delineated?

options.A: The critical path for each trade
options.B: The scope of work for each activity
options.C: The retainage for each contract
options.D: The allowances in each package
options.E: The milestone dates for each package
options.F: The long-lead items for each trade

questions.explanation: Fast-track overlaps design and construction so one activity can start while later ones are still being designed or procured, and it works only if the scope of work for each activity is clearly delineated. That defined scope, issued as a work package, is what gets priced, permitted and built; milestones and long-lead items matter but do not define the packages.

questions.question: Before consultants start writing their sections, the prime A/E should give them which of the following?

options.A: The conditions of the contract
options.B: The drawings, but none of the Division 00 documents
options.C: The owner's project budget and cost targets
options.D: The final addenda and post-bid clarifications
options.E: The Division 01 General Requirements sections
options.F: Substitution requests received from bidders

questions.explanation: Before consultants write any sections, they need the conditions of the contract and the Division 01 General Requirements sections, so they can coordinate with them and avoid duplications and omissions; their input to Division 01 is requested at the same time. Addenda and bidders' substitution requests come later, during procurement.

questions.question: Cross-references within the project manual should reference:

options.A: Only the article title
options.B: Section number and page number
options.C: Section number, article, and paragraph
options.D: Section number only
options.E: Section title only
options.F: Division and article numbers

questions.explanation: Cross-references to other sections should point to the section number, not to article, paragraph or page numbers. Those numbers shift as the specifications are revised, so a reference to them can end up pointing to the wrong place, while the section number stays fixed.

questions.question: Why should equipment such as pumps or valves be identified on the drawings by short generic names or coded symbols, such as 'PRV-1'?

options.A: To satisfy MasterFormat section-numbering rules that apply to drawings
options.B: To simplify drawing changes by keeping descriptions in the specs
options.C: To assist the AHJ in enforcing code provisions during the plan review
options.D: To prevent contractors from proposing any unauthorized substitutions
options.E: To reduce discrepancies among drawings and with the specifications
options.F: To let the drawn outline serve as the detailed fabrication drawing

questions.explanation: Keeping detailed descriptions in the specifications means a change can be made by revising only the specifications, and fewer written changes on the drawings mean fewer chances for discrepancies among drawings and between drawings and specifications. Generic notes make an accepted substitution easier to absorb, and the drawn item should be only a representative outline.

questions.question: During which design phase are outline specifications most typically prepared?

options.A: Programming
options.B: Construction documents
options.C: Schematic design
options.D: Design development
options.E: Procurement
options.F: Construction

questions.explanation: Outline specifications fit best in design development, when materials and products are being actively selected. They may be prepared earlier, in schematic design, if the owner requires it or the A/E knows the building type well, and they can set the quality level used to establish a guaranteed maximum price.

questions.question: On a typical project, who makes the final selection of products?

options.A: The owner
options.B: The contractor
options.C: The A/E
options.D: The product representative
options.E: The supplier
options.F: The authority having jurisdiction

questions.explanation: The A/E typically makes the final product selection, either alone or after discussions with the design team, owner and contractor. The contractor makes the choice only when performance-based documents or several listed products leave it open after award, and product representatives supply information but do not decide.

questions.question: Which of the following belong in Section 01 14 00—Work Restrictions?

options.A: Procedures for special facility types such as hospitals
options.B: Barriers protecting the owner's occupants and spaces
options.C: Temporary access and parking for construction
options.D: Owner-required working hours for the contractor's operations
options.E: The advance notice, in days, the owner needs before work in occupied areas
options.F: Temporary utility sources and service connections for the work

questions.explanation: Section 01 14 00 is limited to restrictions on the contractor's use of the premises, such as the owner's required working hours and how many days' notice must be given before work in occupied areas. Barriers protecting the owner's occupancy go in 01 56 00, access and parking in 01 53 00 and 01 55 00, procedures for special facility types in 01 35 00, and utility sources in 01 18 00.

questions.question: How is a reference standard normally incorporated into a specification?

options.A: By paraphrasing its requirements
options.B: By binding a copy into the project manual
options.C: By copying its text into PART 2
options.D: By citing its developer, number, and title
options.E: By naming a manufacturer that complies
options.F: By stating 'as required by code'

questions.explanation: A reference standard is normally incorporated by citing its developer, number and title or other common designation, which makes its provisions part of the specifications as if written out. Copying or binding in the full text is avoided because standards are usually copyrighted, and naming a complying manufacturer is proprietary specifying, not use of the standard.

questions.question: Which principle for locating information in the contract documents guards against duplication?

options.A: Clear, concise, correct, and complete
options.B: Specify by reference wherever possible
options.C: Each discipline specifies its own work
options.D: Say it once and in the right place
options.E: Back-coordinate changes into earlier packages
options.F: Share product decisions at the earliest phase

questions.explanation: The principle for placing information in the contract documents is 'say it once and in the right place.' Stating each requirement once avoids duplications that later turn into discrepancies. 'Clear, concise, correct and complete' describes good writing, not where information goes, and specifying by reference is a method, not a location rule.

questions.question: When specifications are performance-based or list several acceptable products, who often makes the final product selection?

options.A: The owner, during programming
options.B: The specifier, during construction documents
options.C: The A/E, during design development
options.D: The contractor, after contract award
options.E: The A/E, during submittal review
options.F: The product representative, during bidding

questions.explanation: When the documents are performance-based or list several acceptable products, the contractor may make the final selection after the contract is awarded. The A/E and owner may not learn which product was chosen until submittals arrive during construction, unless bidders must list their key products with the bid.

questions.question: Most sustainability standards summarize a product's environmental impact using:

options.A: A life cycle assessment
options.B: A life cycle cost analysis
options.C: A single-attribute test
options.D: An ecolabel rating
options.E: A Health Product Declaration
options.F: A Safety Data Sheet

questions.explanation: Most sustainability standards rely on a life cycle assessment to sum up a product's environmental impact and compare it with similar products. A life cycle cost analysis measures money over time, not environmental impact, and ecolabels are separate marks on packaging that signal a product meets set criteria.

questions.question: On a project issued in multiple bid packages, a modification issued in an early package must be:

options.A: Back-coordinated into the packages issued before it
options.B: Incorporated into every later package
options.C: Held until the final package is issued
options.D: Issued again as a change order after award
options.E: Sent only to the bidders on that early package
options.F: Left for the contractor to carry into later work

questions.explanation: On a project issued in multiple packages, a modification issued in an early package must be carried into every later package. Back-coordination works in the other direction: when a later package changes something, the earlier packages must be updated to match.

questions.question: MasterFormat is organized by:

options.A: Functional elements
options.B: Systems and assemblies
options.C: Project life cycle phases
options.D: Work results
options.E: Products and materials
options.F: Trades and subcontracts

questions.explanation: MasterFormat organizes construction information by work results, the construction practices that come from combining products and methods. Organizing by functional elements, that is systems and assemblies, is UniFormat's approach, and MasterFormat's divisions are not meant to assign work to particular trades.

questions.question: The most effective writing sequence within a single specification section is:

options.A: PART 1, then PART 2, then PART 3
options.B: PART 2, then PART 3, then PART 1
options.C: PART 3, then PART 2, then PART 1
options.D: PART 1, then PART 3, then PART 2
options.E: PART 2, then PART 1, then PART 3
options.F: PART 3, then PART 1, then PART 2

questions.explanation: The most effective sequence is to write PART 2—PRODUCTS first, then PART 3—EXECUTION, then check PART 2 again, and write PART 1—GENERAL last. Leaving PART 1 for the end lets its submittals, quality assurance and warranty articles reflect the products and methods actually chosen; the writing order differs from the order of the parts.

questions.question: Which statements about delegated design under AIA A201 are correct?

options.A: The owner and architect specify all performance and design criteria the services must satisfy
options.B: The delegated professional's signature and seal appear on the calculations and shop drawings
options.C: The architect reviews the delegated submittals to confirm the design's structural adequacy
options.D: The contractor is responsible for the adequacy of the criteria the documents specify
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: Under A201 §3.12.10, the Owner and Architect must specify all the performance and design criteria the delegated services must meet, and the licensed professional who performs them signs and seals the drawings, calculations and other submittals. The Architect reviews those only for conformance with information given and the design concept, and the Contractor is not responsible for the adequacy of the specified criteria.

questions.question: What is the overall objective of product research and selection?

options.A: Find the products with the lowest life cycle cost
options.B: Find the highest-quality products available
options.C: Find suitable products that maximize owner value
options.D: Find code-compliant products at the lowest cost
options.E: Find the products with the shortest lead times
options.F: Find products the owner and contractor prefer

questions.explanation: The overall aim of product research and selection is to find suitable products that meet the project's goals while giving the owner the most value. Life cycle cost, first cost and top quality are each one measure of value, but none of them alone is the objective.

questions.question: An authority having jurisdiction (AHJ) is BEST described as:

options.A: A federal agency that writes the model building code and adopts it for every U.S. jurisdiction
options.B: A manufacturer-led trade group that develops the reference standards that codes cite by number
options.C: A private rating laboratory that tests products and then certifies the firms that install them
options.D: An organization, agency, or department with control over an aspect of construction in its area
options.E: A model code-writing organization, such as the ICC, that develops and maintains building codes
options.F: The design professional of record, who interprets the codes that apply to the project design

questions.explanation: An authority having jurisdiction is any organization, agency or department with control over some aspect of construction in the area it is responsible for. A model code writer such as the ICC publishes codes, but they are enforceable only once a jurisdiction adopts them, and the design professional applies the codes without having that authority.

questions.question: Final revisions to the project manual are best distributed in:

options.A: Manufacturer's proprietary format
options.B: Paper copies only
options.C: Native specification source files
options.D: A neutral format such as PDF
options.E: Word-processing files with tracked changes
options.F: Native files named with a yyyy-mm-dd date

questions.explanation: Revisions are best issued and archived in a neutral format, for example PDF, or posted online, with security that keeps the documents from being changed by unauthorized means. Native or editable files can be altered, and a yyyy-mm-dd date convention is a file-naming practice for version control, not a distribution format.

questions.question: Particular attention during document coordination should be given to coordinating Division 01 with:

options.A: The available project information
options.B: The drawing sheet index
options.C: The instructions to bidders
options.D: The conditions of the contract
options.E: The geotechnical report
options.F: The owner's design manual

questions.explanation: Division 01 expands on the administrative provisions of the general conditions, so the fit between Division 01 sections and the conditions of the contract deserves special attention. Checking that each document is correct on its own is not the same as making sure it agrees with the other parts.

questions.question: During procurement, how should a response to a bidder's substitution request be issued?

options.A: By change order
options.B: By RFI response
options.C: By supplemental instruction
options.D: By addendum
options.E: By contract modification
options.F: By verbal reply at the prebid meeting

questions.explanation: During procurement, every response to a question or substitution request must be in writing, typically by addendum, so all bidders receive it; a verbal answer without written confirmation is improper. Change orders, contract modifications and supplemental instructions apply once a contract exists, and RFIs are a construction-phase tool.

questions.question: When an A/E begins researching products, before narrowing to a final choice, which of the following are among the primary factors to consider?

options.A: Sourcing
options.B: Product representative
options.C: Contractor's subcontractor list
options.D: Warranty requirements
options.E: Compatibility with other selected products
options.F: Bidders' product lists

questions.explanation: The primary research factors are the economic implications of each choice, industry conditions and availability, sourcing, code requirements, suitability for project conditions, the product representative, and applicable product standards. Compatibility with other selected products and warranty requirements are weighed later, in the final selection, and bidders' product lists arrive only with the bids.

questions.question: Which are NOT benefits of using a master guide specification?

options.A: Lower bid prices from contractors
options.B: Reduced exposure to liability
options.C: Reduced delays in project development
options.D: Expanded decision-making capability
options.E: Minimized repetitive work
options.F: Shorter construction duration on site

questions.explanation: A master guide specification reduces liability exposure by cutting errors and omissions, expands the A/E's choices with a wide range of options, avoids delays by letting specifications be produced alongside the drawings, and frees staff from repetitive work. Its savings are in the A/E's own production time, not in bid prices, and the delays it avoids are in design, not in construction on site.

questions.question: Standard agreement forms published by AIA or EJCDC should be included in the project manual:

options.A: As the actual forms, bound in
options.B: By document number only
options.C: Only after the contract is awarded
options.D: In Division 01 with the general requirements
options.E: By title and edition date in the TOC
options.F: As attachments to the instructions to bidders

questions.explanation: Standard agreement forms should be bound into the project manual as the actual forms rather than included by reference only. Binding in the real form removes the risk of pointing bidders to an incorrect or outdated edition, which is exactly what a reference by document number or title can do.

questions.question: When reviewing project requirements, the specifier prepares a preliminary table of contents by identifying needed sections from:

options.A: MasterFormat
options.B: OmniClass
options.C: SectionFormat
options.D: UniFormat
options.E: PageFormat
options.F: Uniform Drawing System

questions.explanation: While reviewing project requirements, the specifier drafts a preliminary table of contents by picking the MasterFormat sections needed to cover the project's scope. SectionFormat and PageFormat govern the inside and the layout of each section, and UniFormat organizes by building element for early descriptions.

questions.question: A submersible sewage pump cannot operate within the design's flow range and total dynamic head. The A/E should:

options.A: Add a performance warranty
options.B: Require startup testing
options.C: Allow bidders to propose equals
options.D: Select a different pump
options.E: Require manufacturer site inspections
options.F: Require more detailed shop drawings

questions.explanation: The A/E should confirm the manufacturer recommends a product for the intended use and check its documented properties and limits against the design criteria. A pump that cannot run within the required flow range and total dynamic head should simply not be specified; a warranty, startup testing or bidder equals do not cure the mismatch.

questions.question: Which drawing notes follow recommended practice?

options.A: Firestop at penetration, see Section 07 84 00
options.B: Manhole cover and frame, see specifications
options.C: Refer to specifications for sealant types and colors
options.D: Roof membrane Type A, see roofing specifications
options.E: Unit pavers
options.F: Acme Model 400 power roof ventilator

questions.explanation: Drawing notes should be generic, identifying a material without describing it, so 'unit pavers' is right: a later switch from concrete to brick pavers changes only the specifications. General cross-references such as 'see specifications' should be avoided, but citing a specific section number is acceptable, and proprietary names belong on drawings only when a closed proprietary specification allows just one product.

questions.question: Substitutions are allowed both during bidding and after award. How should the procurement requirements handle bidding-phase substitutions?

options.A: Leave them to the supplementary conditions
options.B: Repeat the full Section 01 25 00 text in the instructions
options.C: Route bidding-phase requests through the RFI process
options.D: Refer to Section 01 25 00 as the basis for the process
options.E: Accept them only by addendum after bid opening
options.F: Cover them in Section 01 26 00 modification procedures

questions.explanation: When substitutions are allowed both during procurement and after award, one Section 01 25 00 can govern both, and the procurement requirements must refer to it as the basis for the bidding-phase process. Procurement requirements should point to Division 01 sections by number and title rather than repeat them, and RFIs handle clarifications, not substitutions.

questions.question: What can make a specialized construction technique inappropriate for a project?

options.A: Few skilled workers in the project area
options.B: No prior AHJ approval of the technique
options.C: No manufacturer guide specification
options.D: A longer construction schedule
options.E: Limited local maintenance supplies
options.F: Custom colors with longer lead times

questions.explanation: A specialized construction technique may be a poor choice where workers skilled in it are not available in the project's area. Custom colors and maintenance supplies are separate product-evaluation factors, and prior AHJ approval or a manufacturer guide specification does not decide whether local trades can do the work.

questions.question: When consultants prepare their own specification sections, the prime A/E should do which of the following?

options.A: Have the owner approve each consultant's sections independently
options.B: Defer Division 01 coordination to each consultant
options.C: Allow each consultant to set their own format
options.D: Assume responsibility for overall specification coordination
options.E: Give consultants the Division 01 requirements before they write sections
options.F: Have each consultant write general requirements for its discipline

questions.explanation: The prime A/E should take on overall coordination of the specifications and give consultants the project type, contract, formats, general conditions and especially the Division 01 requirements before they write any sections. Letting each consultant set its own format or write general requirements for its discipline produces the conflicting requirements this is meant to prevent.

questions.question: A 'Basic Requirements' section placed in an individual technical division is:

options.A: Recommended where one discipline writes the whole division
options.B: Recommended for requirements common to that division
options.C: Not recommended, since it may conflict with Division 01
options.D: Acceptable if Division 01 cross-references it
options.E: Required where several disciplines write the divisions
options.F: Acceptable for requirements unique to one section

questions.explanation: A 'Basic Requirements' or 'Special Provisions' section inside a technical division is not recommended because it can conflict with Division 01. Requirements common to several sections, even when one discipline writes the whole division, belong in Division 01, and requirements unique to one section go in that section.

questions.question: Which of the following should Section 01 25 00—Substitution Procedures specify?

options.A: Procedures for replacing a separate prime contractor
options.B: Qualifications of the testing laboratory
options.C: Duties of the commissioning authority
options.D: Procedures for substituting a specified installer
options.E: Rules for deciding whether products are equivalent
options.F: Participants and reports for a value analysis study

questions.explanation: Section 01 25 00 sets the basic requirements for considering the contractor's substitution proposals, including the rules and procedures for deciding whether products are equivalent, plus the requirements and procedures for substituting a specified installer. Testing laboratory qualifications belong with quality requirements, commissioning duties with commissioning, and value analysis studies in 01 24 00.

questions.question: One recommended way to relay product information to the specifier is to:

options.A: Route product information through a set person, such as the PM
options.B: Share product decisions only at milestone coordination meetings
options.C: Let any team member send product decisions directly to the specifier
options.D: Have the specifier collect product decisions from each consultant
options.E: Note each product decision in detail on the drawings for the specifier
options.F: Carry product decisions over from a previous project's specifications

questions.explanation: A sound protocol has all product information reach the specifier through designated people, such as the project manager or project A/E, so the specifier works from one consistent set of decisions. Letting any team member send decisions directly invites contradictions, and waiting for milestone meetings or having the specifier chase each consultant leaves no single, controlled channel.

questions.question: Under ConsensusDocs 200, a substitution accepted after the agreement is executed is formalized by:

options.A: An interim directive
options.B: An owner's written order
options.C: A written amendment
options.D: A change order
options.E: A field order
options.F: A construction change directive

questions.explanation: ConsensusDocs uses the change order (ConsensusDocs 202) to formalize changes in the work, adjust contract time and price, and accept substitutions; only the owner and contractor sign it. The interim directive orders work before price or time is agreed, and the owner's written order is the ConsensusDocs form for minor changes, so neither formally accepts a substitution.

questions.question: How many days before receipt of bids does AIA A701 require bidder questions to be submitted?

options.A: At least 14 days
options.B: At least 10 days
options.C: At least 4 days
options.D: At least 7 days
options.E: At least 15 days
options.F: At least 21 days

questions.explanation: AIA A701, Instructions to Bidders, has bidders submit questions no later than seven days before the bids are received. Ten days is the period EJCDC C-200 recommends, and four days is how late a minor addendum can sometimes go out without hardship, not a deadline for bidder questions.

questions.question: UniFormat is best suited to organizing construction information by:

options.A: Trades and subcontractors
options.B: Procurement requirements
options.C: Work results
options.D: Systems and assemblies
options.E: Spaces and their functions
options.F: Products and materials

questions.explanation: UniFormat arranges information by the physical parts of a facility, called systems and assemblies, each defined by the function it performs rather than by the products it contains. Organizing by work results, products and materials is the MasterFormat view, and neither system is arranged by trades or by spaces.

questions.question: Which statements about guide specification sources are correct?

options.A: AIA/Deltek MasterSpec is a commercially available full-length master
options.B: The Unified Facilities Guide Specifications are a commercial subscription product
options.C: Deltek SpecText is a commercially available full-length master
options.D: Most commercial master specifications are based on MasterFormat numbers and titles
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: AIA/Deltek MasterSpec, Deltek SpecText and BSD SpecLink are commercially produced full-length master guide specifications, and most commercial masters are built on MasterFormat section numbers and titles, so {F} is correct. The Unified Facilities Guide Specifications are a government system published jointly by the Army Corps of Engineers, NAVFAC, the Air Force and NASA, not a commercial subscription product.

questions.question: The shop drawing format and the number of copies to submit are specified in:

options.A: Section 01 31 00—Project Management and Coordination
options.B: Section 01 32 00—Construction Progress Documentation
options.C: Section 01 78 00—Closeout Submittals
options.D: Section 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures
options.E: Section 01 77 00—Closeout Procedures
options.F: Section 01 43 00—Quality Assurance

questions.explanation: Section 01 33 00 covers the submittal schedule, shop drawings, product data and samples, including the shop drawing format (prints, reproducibles or electronic files) and how many copies to submit and to keep for the owner. Section 01 78 00 handles closeout items such as record documents and warranties, and 01 32 00 handles progress schedules, daily reports and photographs.

questions.question: If a contractor delivers concrete meeting a descriptive specification's mix proportions but the concrete fails to reach 3000 psi, who is responsible?

options.A: The contractor, for not meeting strength
options.B: The A/E, who assumed the burden of performance
options.C: The owner, for accepting the design
options.D: The ready-mix supplier, for non-conforming product
options.E: The testing agency, for not rejecting the mix
options.F: The contractor's concrete subcontractor

questions.explanation: When a descriptive specification is used, the A/E carries the burden of performance. If only the mix proportions were specified and the concrete followed them, the 3000 psi strength was implied but never required, so the contractor cannot be held responsible. The supplier and testing agency delivered or checked what was described, not a strength.

questions.question: Industry guidance on the FAR Buy American test says a construction material that is not wholly or predominantly iron or steel must have domestic components costing more than what share of the cost of all its components?

options.A: 95 percent
options.B: 50 percent
options.C: 75 percent
options.D: 55 percent
options.E: 5 percent
options.F: 45 percent

questions.explanation: The two-part test requires the material to be manufactured in the United States and, for materials not wholly or predominantly iron or steel, domestic components costing more than 55 percent of all components. For iron or steel materials the test instead keeps foreign iron and steel under 5 percent, which is where 95 percent tempts. Later FAR amendments raise the 55 percent threshold in steps, so check the current clause on a real project.

questions.question: In specifications, the word "shall" traditionally is used in connection with acts required of:

options.A: The contractor
options.B: The A/E
options.C: The manufacturer
options.D: The owner
options.E: The subcontractor
options.F: The commissioning agent

questions.explanation: Shall is the imperative used for work the contractor is required to do. Will is treated as the less obligatory word and is used for acts required of the owner or the A/E, which is why those choices tempt. Subcontractors and manufacturers are not parties to the owner-contractor agreement, so the instructions are addressed to the contractor.

questions.question: Wind load calculations for a project site are made according to:

options.A: ASTM E119
options.B: ACI 350
options.C: ASCE/SEI 7
options.D: ASTM E84
options.E: TMS 602
options.F: NFPA 70

questions.explanation: Wind loads for a site are calculated under ASCE/SEI 7, the standard that sets minimum design loads for buildings and other structures and that building codes adopt by reference. ASTM E119 covers fire tests of building construction, ASTM E84 covers surface-burning characteristics such as flame spread, and ACI 350 covers environmental engineering concrete structures.

questions.question: In what order should the A/E evaluate products?

options.A: Smaller components first, then the larger systems they form
options.B: Major systems and subsystems first, then smaller components
options.C: In the sequence the work will be installed on site
options.D: Each system and component on its own, in any order
options.E: In MasterFormat number order, starting with Division 02
options.F: Owner-selected finishes first, then the systems behind them

questions.explanation: Some products affect how others perform and limit later choices, so the A/E should look at the major systems and subsystems before anything else. Smaller components are then judged on quality, performance and compatibility with the selections already made. Starting with small parts, or following the installation sequence, risks choosing components that do not suit the system they end up in.

questions.question: Which statements about outline specifications are correct?

options.A: They record the A/E's early design decisions.
options.B: They are not intended for use as contract documents.
options.C: They are organized by UniFormat systems and assemblies.
options.D: They become legally enforceable once bound into the project manual.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: Outline specifications record the A/E's early decisions on materials, products and the general level of quality, and they are not meant to be used as contract documents, so {E} is correct. They are organized by MasterFormat, not UniFormat, and the compact specification that is legally enforceable is the shortform specification, not the outline.

questions.question: Under A201, the contractor is not required to provide professional design services unless:

options.A: The contract documents specifically call for such professional services
options.B: The architect requests the services in writing after reviewing submittals
options.C: The delegated portion exceeds a stated dollar threshold in the agreement
options.D: The contractor voluntarily retains a design professional for those services
options.E: The architect's consultant declines to design that portion of the work
options.F: The portion falls outside the architect's own licensed discipline

questions.explanation: A201 does not require the contractor to provide services that amount to the practice of architecture or engineering unless the contract documents specifically call for them on a portion of the Work, or the contractor needs them for its own construction means and methods. A later written request from the architect, a dollar threshold or the contractor's own choice to hire a designer does not create that duty.

questions.question: For the dates in version-control file names, which optional convention is recommended?

options.A: mm-dd-yyyy
options.B: dd-mm-yyyy
options.C: yyyy-mm-dd
options.D: yy-mm-dd
options.E: yyyy-dd-mm
options.F: mm-dd-yy

questions.explanation: A consistent file-naming protocol for version control can use the optional yyyy-mm-dd convention of ISO 8601, which puts year, month and day in that order. The common US order, mm-dd-yyyy, and the day-first orders used elsewhere are not the convention ISO 8601 prescribes.

questions.question: Which of these do manufacturers' websites generally provide about their products?

options.A: Installed-cost estimates
options.B: AHJ approval letters
options.C: Certificates of Occupancy
options.D: Safety Data Sheets
options.E: Environmental Product Declarations
options.F: Project shop drawings

questions.explanation: Manufacturer websites typically offer installation instructions, datasheets, catalogs, Safety Data Sheets, Environmental and Health Product Declarations, test and evaluation reports, details and BIM objects, and guide specifications. Shop drawings are prepared for a specific project, certificates of occupancy and approvals come from the AHJ, and installed costs depend on project conditions, which is why product representatives are asked for them.

questions.question: Statements of precedence among the contract documents are not recommended because the documents are:

options.A: Independent
options.B: Complementary
options.C: Hierarchical
options.D: Sequential
options.E: Prioritized
options.F: Duplicative

questions.explanation: The contract documents are complementary, each completing the others, so a project manual statement ranking their precedence is not recommended. The conditions of the contract should say only that the A/E makes a documented interpretation when drawings and specifications conflict. A precedence listing may be prepared for bidding purposes only, which is why calling the documents hierarchical or prioritized is wrong.

questions.question: The main risk of specifying the same item in both descriptive and performance terms is that:

options.A: The contractor must satisfy both sets, which raises the cost
options.B: The bidder may comply with only the lesser requirement
options.C: The A/E is relieved of the burden of performance
options.D: The item can no longer be bid competitively
options.E: The described product becomes a closed proprietary item
options.F: The stated performance criteria override the mix proportions

questions.explanation: Describing an item and also stating its required performance, such as giving a concrete mix by proportions and by strength, sets the two up to conflict. The bidder may then be able to meet only the lesser of the two requirements. Doing this does not force compliance with both sets, and it does not by itself make the item proprietary or noncompetitive.

questions.question: Which work-package version-control approach progresses toward a single comprehensive set of contract documents?

options.A: Sequential method
options.B: Revised-page method
options.C: Cumulative method
options.D: Standalone method
options.E: Narrative method
options.F: Fast-track method

questions.explanation: In the cumulative method each new work package adds revised drawings and specifications to those already issued, so the packages build toward one comprehensive set and revisions stay manageable; it is preferred for that reason. In the standalone method every package is complete and separate, with revisions tracked separately. Narrative and revised-page methods describe how individual changes are issued, not how packages accumulate.

questions.question: Which specification method describes the required end result and the criteria for verifying it, without limiting means?

options.A: Reference standard
options.B: Descriptive
options.C: Closed proprietary
options.D: Performance
options.E: Open proprietary
options.F: Basis of design

questions.explanation: A performance specification states the end result required, gives measurable criteria for confirming that it was achieved, and avoids unnecessary limits on how the result is reached. A descriptive specification instead spells out the properties and workmanship, while proprietary and basis-of-design methods rely on named products.

questions.question: Which of the following are typically the owner's responsibility to provide?

options.A: The construction progress schedule
options.B: Coordination drawings
options.C: The geotechnical report
options.D: Delegated-design calculations
options.E: Surveys of the site's physical characteristics and utility locations
options.F: Shop drawings and product data

questions.explanation: Owners typically furnish the geotechnical report, which is included or referenced in Division 00 as available project information, and A201 has the owner furnish surveys of the site's physical characteristics, legal limitations and utility locations. Progress schedules, coordination drawings, delegated-design calculations, shop drawings and product data all come from the contractor's side.

questions.question: In value analysis, which of the following establish the price parameters for products?

options.A: Product delivery time
options.B: Budget requirements
options.C: Quality requirements
options.D: Time allotted for value analysis
options.E: Maintenance costs
options.F: Product availability

questions.explanation: In value analysis, budget requirements and maintenance costs are what set the price limits for products and so shape the A/E's budget decisions. Delivery time, availability and the time allowed for the analysis are schedule considerations, and quality is weighed in its own right, so none of these sets the price parameters.

questions.question: Which are reasons for an A/E to meet with the AHJ before applying for permits?

options.A: To get a local interpretation of the proposed design
options.B: To negotiate the permit fees and inspection schedule
options.C: To have the AHJ review the specifications for completeness
options.D: To obtain the AHJ's list of approved manufacturers
options.E: To request a modification from the code requirements
options.F: To have the AHJ adopt a newer model code edition

questions.explanation: An A/E may meet the AHJ ahead of the permit application to learn how the local officials read the code as it applies to a proposed design, or when it is asking for a modification from code requirements. Such meetings may call for drawings, product literature and ratings to support the request. Negotiating fees, a completeness review of the specifications and adopting a newer code are not their purpose.

questions.question: For many projects, which may be a better measure of value than initial capital cost?

options.A: Life cycle cost
options.B: Installed cost
options.C: Operating cost
options.D: Maintenance cost
options.E: Replacement cost
options.F: Repair cost

questions.explanation: Initial capital cost is not always the deciding factor; for many projects the life cycle cost, which accounts for repair and replacement over the product's life, is the better gauge of value. Operating and maintenance costs are only parts of life cycle cost, and installed cost is still a first cost.

questions.question: An A/E specifies the same grade of redwood for an entrance door pull and for an edge strip along the parking lot paving. What principle does this overlook?

options.A: Use one grade throughout for consistency
options.B: Avoid wood at exterior paving edges
options.C: Specify grades that suit each use
options.D: Specify the higher grade where in doubt
options.E: Prefer domestic wood to imported wood
options.F: Avoid grades with long lead times

questions.explanation: A material used for different purposes should not automatically get the same grade. Choose the grade each part of the project actually needs and avoid costly requirements for items that are not critical, such as a paving edge strip. Using one grade throughout, or the higher grade whenever in doubt, adds cost without benefit.

questions.question: Which statements about reusing a previous project's specification sections are correct?

options.A: Previous project specifications should be used only for reference.
options.B: An old project's sections may omit changes later issued by addendum or modification.
options.C: Copied sections may be edited for a new project if the same contractor is used.
options.D: Copying a previous project's sections is required by industry standards.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: Previous project specifications should serve as reference only and should not be edited into a new project's sections, so {E} is correct. An old section may lack needed options, materials or standards, the product may be gone, and the copy may not show the addenda and modifications issued on that project. Using the same contractor changes none of this, and no standard requires copying.

questions.question: Which statements describe ways product representatives can support the design team?

options.A: They identify comparable competitor products so sections are equitable
options.B: They approve contractor substitution requests on the owner's behalf
options.C: They propose alternative technology to cut costs without losing quality
options.D: They review draft sections to confirm all needed components are specified
options.E: {A}, {B} and {D}
options.F: {A}, {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: Product representatives can propose alternative design or construction technology that cuts cost without giving up quality, review draft sections to confirm every needed component is specified, and help identify comparable competing products so sections are equitable, so {F} is correct. Approving substitution requests is not their role; the A/E evaluates substitutions under the contract.

questions.question: Under AIA A201 and ConsensusDocs 200, which statements about cash allowances are correct?

options.A: The allowance covers materials and equipment delivered to the site, including taxes
options.B: The contractor's installation costs, overhead and profit are included in the contract sum
options.C: The contractor must contract with whomever the owner designates, without objection
options.D: The allowance also covers unloading and handling the items at the site
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: Under both A201 and ConsensusDocs 200, a cash allowance pays only for the materials and equipment delivered to the site, taxes included, so {E} is correct. The contractor's labor, unloading and handling at the site, installation, overhead and profit are carried in the contract sum unless the documents say otherwise, which rules out the handling statement. The contractor may also refuse, on reasonable objection, to contract with a party the owner designates.

questions.question: Field tests are specified in PART 3. Under which PART 1 article are the field quality-control reports the contractor must submit listed?

options.A: Closeout Submittals
options.B: Quality Assurance
options.C: Action Submittals/Informational Submittals
options.D: Administrative Requirements
options.E: Maintenance Material Submittals
options.F: Field [or] Site Conditions

questions.explanation: SectionFormat lists Field [or] Site Quality Control reports among the action and informational submittals in PART 1, alongside product data, test reports and certificates. Quality Assurance sets prerequisites such as qualifications and mock-ups but is not where test reports are submitted, and closeout and maintenance material submittals come at the end of the project.

questions.question: A roofing warranty excludes damage from gusts of 55 mph or more, but the code design gust is 85 mph. What is the best A/E response?

options.A: Accept it, since warranty terms do not affect code compliance
options.B: Seek a warranty covering code-level winds, or another product
options.C: Add a clause that the more stringent requirement governs
options.D: Accept it, since design-level winds rarely occur in service
options.E: Accept it if its exclusion is raised to 70-mph gusts
options.F: Accept it if the warranty period is extended to offset it

questions.explanation: The A/E should confirm that warranty terms are consistent with code requirements; a warranty that stops at 55 mph gusts does not cover winds the roof must be designed to resist. Many manufacturers will not negotiate warranty terms, so the owner may need another product with an acceptable warranty. A 'more stringent governs' clause cannot rewrite a manufacturer's warranty, and raising the exclusion to 70 mph still falls short of 85-mph gusts.

questions.question: A contractor receives an A201 construction change directive but disagrees with its method for adjusting the contract sum. The contractor:

options.A: Proceeds at the price it proposed
options.B: May stop the changed work until a change order is signed
options.C: Proceeds only after its surety consents
options.D: Proceeds; the architect then sets the adjustment
options.E: Proceeds; the owner then sets the adjustment
options.F: Proceeds; the initial decision maker sets the adjustment

questions.explanation: On receiving a construction change directive, the contractor must promptly proceed with the change and tell the architect whether it agrees with the stated method of adjustment. If it disagrees, the architect determines the adjustment from reasonable expenditures and savings, with an allowance for overhead and profit on an increase. The contractor may not stop the work, and neither the owner nor the initial decision maker sets the amount at this stage.

questions.question: Geotechnical data and existing-condition reports are typically located in:

options.A: The supplementary conditions
options.B: PART 1 of the earthwork section
options.C: Division 01 general requirements
options.D: Division 00 available information
options.E: Division 02 subsurface investigation
options.F: The instructions for procurement

questions.explanation: Existing condition information (00 31 19) and geotechnical data (00 31 32) are Division 00 documents under 00 30 00, Available Information. They are furnished so bidders can prepare bids and they inform sections such as earthwork and waterproofing, but they are not part of the contract documents and are not written into those sections.

questions.question: Shop drawings, product data, and samples are categorized in SectionFormat as:

options.A: Source quality-control submittals from the plant
options.B: Maintenance material submittals such as extra stock
options.C: Closeout submittals delivered at project completion
options.D: Action submittals and informational submittals
options.E: Quality assurance items such as mock-ups and field samples
options.F: Administrative requirements such as preinstallation meetings

questions.explanation: In SectionFormat, shop drawings, product data and samples fall under the PART 1 article Action Submittals/Informational Submittals, together with certificates, test reports and delegated design submittals. Closeout submittals hold items such as warranties and record documents, maintenance material submittals hold spare parts and extra stock, and mock-ups and field samples are Quality Assurance items.

questions.question: Approved substitutions made before bid opening are typically incorporated by means of:

options.A: An RFI response
options.B: A change order
options.C: A field order
options.D: An addendum
options.E: A supplemental instruction
options.F: A written amendment

questions.explanation: Before bids are opened, the procurement documents are changed by addendum, and adding qualified products or approved substitutions is one of the standard uses of addenda. Change orders, field orders and supplemental instructions are construction-phase tools used after the agreement is signed, and an RFI response only interprets the documents.

questions.question: What is the objection to using 'and/or' in specifications?

options.A: Is reserved for clauses in the conditions of the contract
options.B: Always means 'and,' so the 'or' is redundant
options.C: Lets the contractor decide whether it means 'and' or 'or'
options.D: Needs a comma before it when it ends a series
options.E: Must first be defined in the supplementary conditions
options.F: Lets the A/E decide its meaning when interpreting

questions.explanation: And/or is a shortcut borrowed from legal and business writing, and in a specification it lets the contractor decide whether the requirement means 'and' or 'or.' Write whichever word is intended. The term is not reserved for the conditions of the contract, and the problem is that it hands the choice to the contractor, not to the A/E.

questions.question: A final survey is classed as which type of submittal?

options.A: Closeout
options.B: Informational
options.C: Action
options.D: Maintenance material
options.E: Quality assurance
options.F: Delegated design

questions.explanation: Closeout submittals are what the contractor hands over at the close of the project: the final survey, warranties, record documents, O&M data, maintenance contracts, spare parts and extra stock. A final survey can look informational, but it is delivered at closeout and is specified with the other closeout submittals in Section 01 78 00.

questions.question: Archived specification files should have security features to:

options.A: Keep bidders and sub-bidders from viewing earlier drafts
options.B: Limit file access to the A/E's own staff
options.C: Prevent the owner from editing the record set
options.D: Prevent changes by means other than those designated
options.E: Lock file names to the ISO 8601 date convention
options.F: Keep the revision log hidden from the owner

questions.explanation: Revised specifications should go out and be archived in a neutral format such as PDF, protected by security that stops the contract documents from being altered except by the means expressly designated for changes. The aim is controlled change of the record, not hiding drafts from bidders, limiting access to the A/E's staff or keeping the owner out.

questions.question: Why should the actual agreement form be bound into the project manual rather than included by reference?

options.A: It removes the risk of citing a wrong or outdated form
options.B: Forms included only by reference are unenforceable
options.C: It lets the A/E edit the agreement terms more easily
options.D: It makes the supplementary conditions unnecessary
options.E: Standard forms may not be cited in a project manual
options.F: It gives the agreement precedence over the drawings

questions.explanation: Owners often use standard agreement forms published by professional organizations, but the actual form should be bound into the project manual rather than cited by reference. Binding it in removes the chance of pointing to a wrong or out-of-date form. The reason is accuracy: forms included by reference are not unenforceable, and binding them in does not make the supplementary conditions unnecessary.

questions.question: Which practice perpetuates inconsistent terminology in construction documents?

options.A: Reusing details and specifications from past projects without careful editing
options.B: Having consultants write the sections for their own disciplines
options.C: Listing drawing abbreviations on the drawings instead of in the specifications
options.D: Using generic notes on the drawings instead of product names
options.E: Using an edited abbreviation list tailored to the project
options.F: Reviewing drawing and specification terms with the design team

questions.explanation: Inconsistent terms are carried forward by habits such as reusing old drawing details without thought and lightly editing a past project's specifications, which is why the A/E must enforce consistent terminology. Listing drawing abbreviations on the drawings, using a project-tailored abbreviation list and keeping drawing notes generic are recommended practices, not causes.

questions.question: Which statements about the three-tier hierarchy for testing and submittals are correct?

options.A: The general conditions establish that testing may be required
options.B: Division 01 states who selects the testing laboratory and who pays
options.C: Section 01 33 00 identifies the specific items needing shop drawings
options.D: The individual sections give only the broad testing procedures
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: Requirements get more specific at each tier: the general conditions establish that testing may be required, and Division 01 sets broad procedures such as who selects the laboratory and who pays, so {E} is correct. Routine submittal procedures are in Division 01, but the specific items needing shop drawings or samples are named in the individual sections, which also state the particular tests rather than broad procedures.

questions.question: Which method describes modifications in writing, observing brevity, clarity, and cross-references?

options.A: Standalone method
options.B: Narrative method
options.C: Revised-page method
options.D: Cumulative method
options.E: Strikethrough method
options.F: Revision-number method

questions.explanation: In the narrative method, changes are described in words, kept brief, made clear by quoting enough of the original wording that each change explains itself, and stated once with cross-references elsewhere. The revised-page method reissues the changed section or sheet instead, and the standalone and cumulative methods manage work packages.

questions.question: When a basis-of-design product is named and equivalent products are allowed, what should the specifier document?

options.A: Only the manufacturer's name and model number
options.B: The salient characteristics that define equivalency
options.C: Manufacturer's complete proprietary marketing language
options.D: Pricing data for proposed substitutions
options.E: Proof of comparability furnished by each bidder
options.F: The single source that will supply the product

questions.explanation: The named product sets the standard, but other products can be judged equivalent only if the specification states the salient characteristics, such as type, function, dimensions, appearance and quality, that equivalence is measured against. Deleting the brand and copying the maker's literature word for word yields a closed proprietary specification in disguise, and a bare name and model number gives the A/E nothing to compare.

questions.question: Tolerances for a product's properties before it is incorporated into the project are specified in:

options.A: PART 2, Assembly or Fabrication
options.B: PART 3, Installation
options.C: PART 3, Field [or] Site Quality Control
options.D: PART 1, Quality Assurance
options.E: PART 2, Source Quality Control
