options.F: PART 3, Examination

questions.explanation: The PART 2 Assembly or Fabrication article holds tolerances that set the acceptable range for a product's properties before it is built into the project. PART 3 Installation has its own Tolerances title, but it limits deviation in the installed work, and Source Quality Control covers testing and inspection at the plant.

questions.question: Division 01 sections should be written broadly enough to apply to the work of which divisions?

options.A: Divisions 01 through 33
options.B: Divisions 02 through 33
options.C: Divisions 02 through 49
options.D: Divisions 00 through 49
options.E: Divisions 02 through 48
options.F: Divisions 01 through 49

questions.explanation: Division 01 expands on the conditions of the contract and is worded broadly enough to govern every section in Divisions 02 through 49, so common requirements are not repeated section by section. Division 00 holds the procurement and contracting requirements, which sit outside what Division 01 governs, and Division 49 is the last division of the Specifications Group.

questions.question: A team compares three mechanical systems on size, noise, and performance, and prices the total cost of owning each over 30 years. What are the 30-year figure and the overall comparison called?

options.A: Life cycle cost; value analysis
options.B: Value analysis; life cycle cost
options.C: Life cycle cost; constructability review
options.D: Order of magnitude estimate; value analysis
options.E: Life cycle cost; facility condition assessment
options.F: Unit price estimate; value analysis

questions.explanation: Life cycle cost is what the owner can expect to pay to construct, operate and maintain an item over time, while value analysis compares options to find the best value. A value analysis of mechanical systems can include a life cycle cost for each one, so the two are related but different processes. A constructability review checks buildability, and order of magnitude and unit price figures are first-cost estimates.
questions.source: life cycle cost and value analysis

questions.question: In practice, IPD's construction documentation works most like which approach?

options.A: Design-bid-build issued as one bid package
options.B: CM as advisor with multiple-prime contracts
options.C: CMAR with fast-track scheduling and work packages
options.D: Design-build based on the owner's bridging documents
options.E: Owner-build with specialty contractor packages
options.F: Design-bid-build using the negotiated option

questions.explanation: Whatever its contract arrangement, integrated project delivery runs much like CMAR with fast-track scheduling: documentation is staggered into separate work packages, and the contractor may prepare each package's procurement requirements while working with the A/E. CM as advisor also staggers packages, but that construction manager is not the contractor, and design-bid-build issues complete documents for a single bid.

questions.question: A common approach to the project manual table of contents is to:

options.A: Have the contractor compile it from the bid set after award
options.B: Generate it early and keep it current through production
options.C: Omit it on small projects with few sections
options.D: Let the printer compile it from the bound sections
options.E: Number its pages straight through the whole manual
options.F: Place it in Division 01 with Section 01 10 00

questions.explanation: One common approach is to start the table of contents early in design and maintain it throughout production, using it to organize the work. Before publication, checking the manual against it is part of quality control. Leaving it for the contractor or the printer to compile after the sections are done gives up that control.

questions.question: Product representatives usually prefer to compete against:

options.A: Low-cost competing products
options.B: Unlisted competing products
options.C: Imported competing products
options.D: Qualified competing products
options.E: Domestic competing products
options.F: Custom competing products

questions.explanation: Few projects name only one manufacturer, so product representatives should be ready to name other qualified competitors. They generally would rather go up against qualified products than face potentially cheap but inferior ones. Low-cost competition is exactly what they hope to avoid, and whether a rival is imported, domestic or custom is not the point.

questions.question: Under the negotiated option of design-bid-build, when is the project manual usually completed?

options.A: Before negotiations, so the contractor prices complete documents
options.B: After negotiations start, which often begin in early design
options.C: Before schematic design, to help select the contractor
options.D: Never, because outline specifications become the contract
options.E: During bidding, through addenda to the outline specifications
options.F: Before proposals, as the basis of the request for proposals

questions.explanation: With the negotiated option, the project manual is usually compiled and finished after negotiations have begun in the early design phases. Negotiations often rest on outline specifications and design development drawings that lead to a guaranteed maximum price, and the complete documents then finalize the design, obtain permits and establish actual prices. The outline specifications never become the contract.

questions.question: Section 01 33 00 should give the A/E minimum review times covering:

options.A: The first submittal only
options.B: Every resubmittal until approval
options.C: The first submittal and two resubmittals
options.D: The first submittal and one resubmittal
options.E: One resubmittal only, after a rejection
options.F: The first submittal and the closeout submittals

questions.explanation: Submittal review is part of the lead time that sets when procurement must start, so Section 01 33 00 should tell the contractor the minimum time the A/E needs for the first submittal and one resubmittal. Covering only the first submittal understates the time needed, and promising time for every resubmittal is open-ended.

questions.question: Where should a definition of basis-of-design products and acceptance of comparable products be included?

options.A: On the drawings
options.B: In the supplementary conditions
options.C: In Division 01
options.D: In each affected Division 02-49 section
options.E: In the instructions for procurement
options.F: In the general conditions

questions.explanation: When basis-of-design products are used, Division 01 should define the term and state how comparable products, if allowed, will be accepted. Stating it there says it once for every section; repeating it in each Division 02-49 section would duplicate a general requirement and break the say-it-once principle.

questions.question: Which statements about shortform specifications are correct?

options.A: They are legally enforceable contract documents.
options.B: They should use the three-part SectionFormat headings.
options.C: They are organized by UniFormat systems and assemblies.
options.D: They usually suit construction management multiple-prime projects best.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: Unlike outline specifications and preliminary project descriptions, a shortform specification is a legally enforceable contract document, and the three-part SectionFormat headings should be used to organize it, so {E} is correct. It is a condensed full-length specification, organized by MasterFormat rather than UniFormat, and for multiple-prime construction management projects full-length specifications are usually more suitable.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700, who pays the engineer's charges for evaluating a contractor's proposed substitute?

options.A: The owner, unless the substitute is rejected
options.B: The contractor, but only if the substitute is approved
options.C: The owner, as part of the engineer's basic services
options.D: The contractor, whether or not the substitute is approved
options.E: The contractor, but only for changing the Contract Documents
options.F: The engineer, as the sole judge of the substitute's acceptability

questions.explanation: Under C-700 the contractor reimburses the owner for the engineer's reasonable charges for evaluating each substitute the contractor proposes, whether or not the engineer approves it. If the substitute is accepted, the contractor also pays for the engineer's changes to the contract documents, and it supplies all supporting data at its own expense. The engineer judges acceptability but does not absorb the cost.

questions.question: What is evaluating products for constructability and sequence meant to produce?

options.A: A trade assignment for each MasterFormat section
options.B: A confirmation that the design is within budget
options.C: A coordinated, workable construction sequence
options.D: A confirmation that products comply with codes
options.E: A confirmation of consistency with the drawings
options.F: A confirmation that products meet the design intent

questions.explanation: This evaluation coordinates design, product evaluation and construction so that the result is a construction sequence that meets the project requirements, using the overall schedule, major equipment and delivery dates. MasterFormat titles do not assign work to trades, and code compliance and budget are separate parts of product evaluation.

questions.question: By submitting shop drawings under A201, the contractor represents that it has:

options.A: Waived its right to claim additional contract time arising from the submittal
options.B: Obtained pre-approval of any product substitutions contained in the submittal
options.C: Reviewed them, verified field measurements, and coordinated them with the work
options.D: Transferred responsibility for the design's adequacy to the architect of record
options.E: Left the checking of dimensions and quantities to the architect's review
options.F: Obtained the owner's approval of each item before submitting it

questions.explanation: By submitting shop drawings, product data and samples, the contractor represents under A201 that it has reviewed and approved them, determined and verified materials and field measurements, and checked and coordinated them with the Work and the contract documents. Submitting does not shift design responsibility to the architect, leave dimension checking to the architect's review, or waive time claims.

questions.question: Which describes a generic product rather than a specific one?

options.A: Class 150 ductile iron pipe for a sewer force main
options.B: Ductile iron pipe for a sewer force main
options.C: One maker's ductile iron pipe for a sewer force main
options.D: 8-inch ductile iron pipe for a sewer force main
options.E: Push-on-joint ductile iron pipe for a sewer force main
options.F: Cement-lined ductile iron pipe for a sewer force main

questions.explanation: A generic product names only the product type and its use, such as ductile iron pipe for a sewer force main, and it must be settled before specific products are researched. Adding a size, pressure class, lining, joint type or reference standard turns it into a specific product, and naming one maker narrows it further.

questions.question: Which of the following should Section 01 22 00—Unit Prices include?

options.A: The contractor's allowable overhead-and-profit mark-up on unit-price work
options.B: Who is responsible for measuring the actual unit-price quantities
options.C: The minimum insurance limits the contractor must carry for unit-price work
options.D: The total contract sum to be carried for all unit-price line items combined
options.E: A reference to the unit price schedule incorporated into the agreement
options.F: The cash allowance amounts carried for each of the unit-price items

questions.explanation: Section 01 22 00 sets out unit price procedures and measurement for payment: who measures the actual quantities, how that is administered and coordinated, and a reference to the unit price schedule in the agreement. Overhead, profit and taxes are already included in each unit price, insurance limits belong in the supplementary conditions, and cash allowances are in Section 01 21 00.

questions.question: ASTM C150 covers 10 cement types. If the A/E does not specify one, the selection is:

options.A: Made by the AHJ during plan review
options.B: Made by the testing laboratory
options.C: Left to the contractor
options.D: Defaulted to Type I by the standard
options.E: Made by the cement manufacturer
options.F: Defaulted to the most stringent type

questions.explanation: Many standards contain embedded options, such as the cement types in ASTM C150, and each is a choice the A/E must make. If no type is specified, the choice passes to the contractor, who will likely pick the cheapest option. The standard does not default to a type, and the AHJ, laboratory and manufacturer do not make the selection.

questions.question: What is the aim of value analysis?

options.A: Forecasting the total cost of owning a facility
options.B: Cutting first cost, chiefly by reducing project size
options.C: Confirming the design can be built in sequence
options.D: Finding alternatives that enhance life cycle value
options.E: Assigning a cost to every maintenance activity
options.F: Comparing budgeted and actual expenditures

questions.explanation: Value analysis, also called value engineering or value management, evaluates a design to find alternative methods, systems or materials that benefit the project by enhancing its life cycle value. Using it only to cut construction cost is problematic, and owners rarely accept a smaller project to save money. Forecasting the total cost of ownership is life cycle costing, which a value analysis may use as an input.

questions.question: Sustainability consultant input often crosses all disciplines. Who should coordinate it?

options.A: The prime A/E
options.B: The owner's commissioning agent
options.C: The sustainability consultant
options.D: The mechanical engineer
options.E: The owner
options.F: The construction manager as advisor

questions.explanation: The prime A/E is responsible for the overall coordination of the specifications, and because sustainability input can touch every discipline, coordinating it falls to the prime A/E too. The sustainability consultant supplies the input but does not coordinate the other disciplines, and the owner, commissioning agent and mechanical engineer do not hold that role.

questions.question: What rule governs how product installation and workmanship information is assembled and recorded?

options.A: Notes filed by SectionFormat part
options.B: A communication record form for each product
options.C: Folders organized by UniFormat element
options.D: None; develop methods that work for you
options.E: Notebooks organized by MasterFormat division
options.F: A log of every email from the project A/E

questions.explanation: There are no set rules for assembling and recording installation and workmanship information; each specifier develops methods that work. Common approaches include compiled notes, a log of the project A/E's emails, a notebook or folders by MasterFormat division, and checklists, but these are options, not a rule. A communication record documents an understanding reached in a conversation, not workmanship data.

questions.question: A section names a basis-of-design product and lists two other manufacturers. The contractor submits a product by one of the listed manufacturers. How is it handled?

options.A: As a comparable product submittal under product requirements
options.B: As a substitution for convenience under Section 01 25 00
options.C: As a substitution for cause, since it is not the basis of design
options.D: As a request for interpretation, since equivalence is unclear
options.E: As a procurement substitution under Document 00 26 00
options.F: As a deviation requiring a Construction Change Directive

questions.explanation: A substitution is a request to replace a product the contract documents require, but a listed manufacturer is already permitted, so its product is submitted as a comparable product under the Division 01 product requirements, which define the basis of design and how comparable products are accepted. Substitution procedures, before or after award, are for unlisted products, and nothing here calls for an interpretation or a directive.

questions.question: Which of the following are liabilities of incorporating reference standards?

options.A: They generally set only minimum requirements
options.B: They can contain embedded options
options.C: They spare the A/E from writing lengthy text
options.D: AHJs may enforce different editions of them
options.E: {A}, {B} and {D}
options.F: Both {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: Citing standards saves the A/E from writing long text, but it brings liabilities: standards generally set only minimum requirements, they can contain embedded options, AHJs may enforce different editions, and they can duplicate, contradict or add unwanted requirements, so {E} is correct. Sparing the A/E lengthy writing is the benefit of citing standards, not a liability.

questions.question: When issuing multiple work packages under CMAR, Division 01 is best handled by:

options.A: Issuing it as a stand-alone package later packages reference
options.B: Issuing a full copy of Division 01 within each separate work package
options.C: Issuing the work packages with Division 01 omitted entirely
options.D: Issuing each subcontract with a CM-rewritten Division 01 set
options.E: Issuing it only with the final package, after all revisions
options.F: Placing it in Division 00 with the CM's subcontract forms

questions.explanation: With multiple work packages, Division 01 can be issued once as a stand-alone package that every later package references, so it does not have to be republished each time; any revision goes out with the package that needs it. A full copy in each package invites conflicting versions, and omitting Division 01 or holding it for the final package leaves early packages without general requirements.

questions.question: When CM-Advisor/Agent is used on a multiple-prime project, the A/E typically:

options.A: Issues only outline specifications to each separate prime
options.B: Produces one combined package covering all of the trades
options.C: Produces construction document packages identified by the CM
options.D: Delegates Division 01 general-requirements drafting to each prime
options.E: Produces construction document packages identified by each prime
options.F: Produces document packages identified by its own consultants

questions.explanation: When a construction manager as advisor or agent runs a multiple-prime project, the A/E usually produces construction document packages that the CM identifies, so the packages line up with the separate prime contracts and the fast-track schedule. The individual primes and the A/E's consultants do not define the packages, and one combined package would not suit separate contracts.

questions.question: When fast-tracking under the CM as advisor/agent method with multiple-prime contracts, the A/E's document preparation time will most likely:

options.A: Remain the same as it would for a single-prime design-bid-build
options.B: Be eliminated entirely, since the CM prepares all the documents
options.C: Decrease, because the overall project schedule is made shorter
options.D: Increase, even though the overall project schedule is reduced
options.E: Decrease, since the CM prepares the procurement documents
options.F: Increase only when a single-prime contract is used instead

questions.explanation: Fast-tracking shortens the overall project, but the A/E usually needs more time to prepare documents, because they are staggered into separate bid packages released at different times. That holds with multiple-prime or single-prime contracts. The CM may prepare the procurement documents, yet that does not shorten the A/E's work on the construction documents.

questions.question: Earthwork is covered in MasterFormat Division:
questions.explanation: Division 31, Earthwork, sits in the Site and Infrastructure Subgroup with Division 32, Exterior Improvements, and Division 33, Utilities. Division 02 is Existing Conditions, Division 34 is Transportation and Division 35 is Waterway and Marine Construction.

questions.question: Version control of the specifications should begin when?

options.A: When the construction contract is awarded
options.B: When the AHJ issues the building permit
options.C: When the first addendum is issued
options.D: When the project team formally accepts them
options.E: When AHJ plan review of the documents begins
options.F: When the first change order is issued

questions.explanation: Version control should begin once the project team formally accepts the specifications and continue through the AHJ's plan review, procurement and construction, so that everyone works from the latest version and can see what changed. Starting at the permit, the first addendum or contract award misses the revisions made during plan review.

questions.question: Which MasterFormat division covers Openings, such as doors and windows?
questions.explanation: Division 08, Openings, covers doors and frames, entrances, storefronts, curtain walls, windows, skylights, hardware and glazing. Division 06 is Wood, Plastics, and Composites, Division 07 is Thermal and Moisture Protection, Division 09 is Finishes and Division 10 is Specialties.

questions.question: Which are ways manufacturers can demonstrate a commitment to product quality?

options.A: Staffing local product representatives
options.B: Publishing guide specifications
options.C: Submitting products for code evaluation
options.D: Training and certifying installers
options.E: Imposing a stricter company standard
options.F: Paying reps to write specifications

questions.explanation: Manufacturers can show a commitment to quality by training and certifying, licensing or approving the companies that install their products, and by imposing a company standard stricter than the commonly used industry standard; some also join consensus standards with other makers. Staffing local representatives, publishing guide specifications and seeking code evaluation are services or approvals, not commitments to a higher quality level.

questions.question: Preliminary project descriptions are usually prepared during which phase?

options.A: Programming
options.B: Design development
options.C: Schematic design
options.D: Construction documents
options.E: Procurement
options.F: Construction

questions.explanation: Preliminary project descriptions are written during schematic design and organized by UniFormat systems and assemblies. In design development they become a resource for the outline specifications, which is when written information switches to MasterFormat; that switch is why design development tempts, but the PPD already exists by then.

questions.question: When the contract documents require delegated design, the delegated designer's calculations and shop drawings must bear:

options.A: The architect's seal, as designer of record
options.B: The manufacturer's certification in place of a seal
options.C: The contractor's approval stamp in place of a seal
options.D: The seal and signature of the professional who prepared them
options.E: The owner's written acceptance in place of a seal
options.F: The seal of the architect's structural consultant

questions.explanation: When the contract documents call for delegated design, A201 has the contractor obtain it from a properly licensed design professional, whose signature and seal must appear on every drawing, calculation, certification and shop drawing that professional prepares. The architect does not seal the delegated work, and a contractor's stamp, a manufacturer's certification or the owner's acceptance cannot stand in for that seal.

questions.question: Which statements about when addenda become part of the documents are correct?

options.A: When issued, addenda become part of the contract documents
options.B: Portions affecting the contract documents join them once the agreement is executed
options.C: Portions affecting the contract documents join them when bids are opened
options.D: Under A201, portions relating to bidding requirements become Contract Documents
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: Both {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: When issued, addenda become part of the procurement documents; only the portions that affect the contract documents join them, and only once the agreement is executed. A201 likewise counts addenda issued before execution among the Contract Documents but leaves out their portions that relate to bidding requirements. So addenda do not join the contract documents on issue or at bid opening.

questions.question: When converting a full-length master guide specification into an outline specification, the specifier should focus on:

options.A: PART 3—EXECUTION installation steps
options.B: Reference standards only
options.C: PART 2—PRODUCTS
options.D: PART 1—GENERAL administrative requirements
options.E: PART 1 mock-ups and installation warranties
options.F: PART 3 field quality control testing

questions.explanation: When no commercial outline master is available, convert a full-length master by discarding most of PART 1 and PART 3 and concentrating on PART 2, keeping what establishes basic product and installation quality. Cost-driving items such as mock-ups, installation warranties and field testing may be kept, but they are exceptions rather than the focus, and most reference standards are removed.

questions.question: Basic requirements for the contractor's installation of owner-furnished products belong in:

options.A: Section 01 64 00—Owner-Furnished Products
options.B: Section 01 10 00—Summary
options.C: Section 01 65 00—Product Delivery Requirements
options.D: Section 01 73 00—Execution
options.E: Section 01 66 00—Product Storage and Handling Requirements
options.F: Section 01 11 16—Work by Owner

questions.explanation: Section 01 73 00, Execution, specifies the basic requirements for installing new, pre-purchased and owner-furnished products, and refers to Section 01 64 00 for the owner-furnished products' characteristics. Section 01 64 00 itself covers the administrative side: those characteristics plus coordination, scheduling and receiving. The delivery and storage sections deal with handling, not installation.

questions.question: Final coordination before issuance should include verifying which of the following?

options.A: That a precedence listing is bound into the project manual
options.B: That product representatives have approved their sections
options.C: That the contractor has reviewed the documents for constructability
options.D: That all schedules are consistent
options.E: That previously noted inconsistencies and errors have been corrected
options.F: That the agreement form is included by reference only

questions.explanation: Final coordination before issuance confirms that previously noted inconsistencies, errors and inaccuracies were corrected, that the documents are complete (checking both the project manual and drawing tables of contents), and that all schedules agree. Precedence listings are discouraged, product representatives review draft sections during design rather than approve them, and agreement forms should be bound in, not included by reference.

questions.question: On a multiple-prime project, what does each prime contract have?

options.A: Its own drawings and project manual
options.B: One shared manual with its own drawings
options.C: Shared drawings with its own manual
options.D: A shared set with its own bid form
options.E: One shared set of drawings and manual
options.F: Its own Division 01 in a shared manual

questions.explanation: In a multiple-prime arrangement the owner procures separate contracts, and each one gets its own set of drawings and its own project manual covering that contractor's portion of the work. A single-prime contract, by contrast, typically needs only one set of drawings and one project manual.

questions.question: MasterFormat Division 01 covers:

options.A: Contracting requirements
options.B: General requirements
options.C: Existing conditions
options.D: Procurement requirements
options.E: Conditions of the contract
options.F: Available information

questions.explanation: Division 01, General Requirements, is the first division of the Specifications Group and the only one in its General Requirements Subgroup. Procurement and contracting requirements, including the conditions of the contract and available information, are Division 00 documents, and Existing Conditions is Division 02.

questions.question: Which document modifies the fixed, standardized provisions of AIA A201 for a specific project?

options.A: The bid form and bid schedule
options.B: The owner-contractor agreement
options.C: Supplementary conditions
options.D: Division 01 General Requirements
options.E: Instructions to bidders
options.F: Supplementary instructions to bidders

questions.explanation: Supplementary conditions modify the constants in the general conditions for a particular region or project; they are written for each project and take precedence over the general conditions. Division 01 expands on the conditions of the contract without modifying them, and the agreement and bidding documents serve other purposes.

questions.question: Section 01 29 00 specifies requirements for the contractor's submittal of which of the following?

options.A: The schedule of values
options.B: Shop drawings and product data
options.C: Closeout submittals and warranties
options.D: Substitution requests
options.E: Applications for payment
options.F: Requests for information

questions.explanation: Section 01 29 00, Payment Procedures, governs how the contractor submits the schedule of values and its applications for payment, including the forms or software, copies and timing for each. Shop drawings belong in Section 01 33 00, closeout submittals in 01 78 00, substitution requests in 01 25 00 and RFIs under 01 26 00.

questions.question: Specifications obtained from product manufacturers should be:

options.A: Bound separately at the back of the project manual as supplementary data
options.B: Reviewed and edited to remove biases and proprietary content where needed
options.C: Rejected outright as inherently unsuitable for any project specification section
options.D: Incorporated verbatim to preserve the manufacturer's stated technical accuracy
options.E: Cited by title in the PART 1 References article in place of section text
options.F: Accepted as written once the product representative has reviewed them

questions.explanation: Manufacturer-furnished guide specifications save research and writing time, but they must be reviewed for bias toward the maker's product and for accuracy, and their proprietary language usually needs editing for competitively bid projects. Using them verbatim, or accepting them once a representative has looked at them, skips that review, while rejecting them outright throws away useful technical data.

questions.question: Each Division 02-49 section affected by an alternate should:

options.A: State that it is affected and refer to Section 01 23 00
options.B: Describe the full scope of the alternate in PART 1
options.C: List the alternate's add or deduct amount in PART 1
options.D: Leave out alternate products until the owner selects them
options.E: Refer bidders to the bid form for the alternate's description
options.F: Leave alternate coordination to the consultant who wrote it

questions.explanation: Each section affected by an alternate should include a paragraph saying so and refer to Section 01 23 00, Alternates, which describes what the base bid and each alternate include. Restating the alternate's full scope or price in the section would duplicate Section 01 23 00 and the bid form, and the alternate's products must still be specified so bidders can price them.

questions.question: What is usually written early in design to record basic product and material choices while the design is still evolving?

options.A: Shortform specifications
options.B: Outline specifications
options.C: Full-length specifications
options.D: Performance specifications
options.E: Purchasing specifications
options.F: Master guide specifications

questions.explanation: Outline specifications are written early in the design process to state basic product and material requirements at a time when the design can still change. Shortform specifications are condensed contract specifications for limited-scope work, full-length specifications describe the work in detail for construction, and a master guide specification is the template that sections are edited from.

questions.question: The imperative mood is preferred in specifications because it:

options.A: Eliminates the need for punctuation within numbered lists
options.B: Uses the word "shall" with every sentence in the section
options.C: Allows indirect instructions to the owner and the contractor
options.D: Places the action verb first, producing a concise directive
options.E: Assigns the owner's duties through the word "will"
options.F: Repeats "Contractor shall" so the duty is always clear

questions.explanation: The imperative mood opens the sentence with the verb that defines the action, giving a short, clear directive such as 'Install equipment plumb and level.' Because all instructions are addressed to the contractor, 'Contractor shall' is generally left out; shall and will appear only where the owner or A/E is named alongside the contractor.

questions.question: Which warranty term is generally the LEAST reliable basis for comparing two warranties?

options.A: Duration alone
options.B: Exclusions and limitations
options.C: Manufacturer's financial backing
options.D: Whether labor is covered
options.E: Remedies and their limits
options.F: Conditions for keeping it valid

questions.explanation: Duration is the most commonly specified and compared warranty term, but it may be one of the least important. If the A/E specifies only a duration, there is no basis for rejecting a warranty that meets it but is unacceptable in its exclusions, remedies, coverage or conditions. Those other terms decide whether the owner is actually protected.

questions.question: Where are the requirements and procedures for requesting substitutions best specified?

options.A: In the supplementary conditions
options.B: In the owner-contractor agreement
options.C: In each technical section, after the named products
options.D: In Division 01, Section 01 25 00
options.E: In Division 01, Section 01 26 00
options.F: In Division 01, Section 01 33 00

questions.explanation: Substitution requirements and procedures belong in Division 01, in Section 01 25 00, Substitution Procedures (or 01 25 13 for products), which sets the limits, the contractor's representations and how to request and submit. With a comprehensive section there, adding 'or equal' after each product name is redundant. Section 01 26 00 covers contract modifications and 01 33 00 covers submittals.

questions.question: Which statements about how drawings and specifications should relate are correct?

options.A: They should complement each other without overlaps or gaps
options.B: Critical requirements should be repeated in both so neither is missed
options.C: A drawing note may refer to a specific specification section
options.D: General 'see specifications' notes help readers find requirements
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: Well-prepared drawings and specifications fit together like a jigsaw puzzle, with no overlaps or gaps, and a drawing note may point to a specific section, such as 'see Section 07 84 00,' so {E} is correct. Repeating critical requirements in both invites discrepancies when only one copy gets revised, and general 'see specifications' notes are to be avoided.

questions.question: When should a reference standard be reviewed and its content understood?

options.A: When the contractor submits compliance data
options.B: Before it is cited in the specifications
options.C: Only if the AHJ questions its edition
options.D: During the final coordination review
options.E: When the AHJ adopts a new edition of it
options.F: After bids reveal any conflicts with it

questions.explanation: Review a reference standard and understand its content and purpose before citing it; once cited, its provisions become part of the specifications as if written out, along with any conflicts and embedded options. If it does not fit the project, the A/E can take exceptions to it or write original requirements instead. Waiting for submittals, bids or the AHJ is too late.

questions.question: MasterFormat sections are intended to correspond to:

options.A: A single drawing detail
options.B: A work result
options.C: A single trade or subcontract
options.D: A UniFormat element
options.E: A single product or material
options.F: A single drawing discipline

questions.explanation: A MasterFormat section is a portion of a division that specifies a work result, and sections are not meant to match a single trade or subcontract; how the contractor divides the work among trades is its own decision. A single product or drawing detail is narrower than a work result, and UniFormat elements are systems and assemblies, a different classification.

questions.question: Which statements about where procurement-stage provisions belong are correct?

options.A: Bid security requirements belong in the procurement requirements
options.B: Performance and payment bond requirements belong in the supplementary conditions
options.C: Document acquisition and cost belong in the procurement requirements
options.D: Bid opening dates belong in Section 01 10 00—Summary
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: Bid security, document acquisition and cost, and bid opening dates apply only during procurement, so they go in the procurement requirements, not in Division 01. Performance and payment bond requirements belong in the supplementary conditions. That makes {F} correct; placing bid opening dates in Section 01 10 00 is the error.

questions.question: Which AIA document is used for minor changes in the work that do not require an adjustment in contract sum or time?

options.A: AIA G701, Change Order, signed by all parties
options.B: AIA G710, Architect's Supplemental Instructions
options.C: AIA G612, Owner's Instructions to the architect
options.D: AIA G714, Construction Change Directive
options.E: AIA G709, Work Changes Proposal Request
options.F: A written amendment signed by both parties

questions.explanation: AIA G710, Architect's Supplemental Instructions, is the standard form for minor changes: instructions or interpretations that do not adjust the contract sum or time and are consistent with the documents' intent. A minor change needs no owner signature. A change order (G701) or construction change directive (G714) is used when the sum or time may change.

questions.question: Where may door schedules and finish schedules appropriately be placed?

options.A: In the bid form
options.B: In the general conditions
options.C: On the drawings
options.D: In the shop drawings
options.E: In the specifications
options.F: In the outline specifications

questions.explanation: The US National CAD Standard recommends schedules in the drawing set, but schedules built as databases or spreadsheets can go in either the drawings or the specifications, and the A/E picks whichever is more practical and economical. Shop drawings are contractor submittals, outline specifications are not contract documents, and the bid form and general conditions do not hold schedules.

questions.question: A preliminary project description describes a two-sided structural-sealant curtain wall on aluminum framing under UniFormat B2010.40, Fabricated Exterior Wall Assemblies. Using UniFormat's cross-reference to MasterFormat, in which section is it specified?
questions.explanation: UniFormat's cross-reference places this system in Section 08 44 00, Curtain Wall and Glazed Assemblies, which includes the Level 3 section 08 44 13, Glazed Aluminum Curtain Walls. 07 42 00 is Wall Panels, 08 41 00 is Entrances and Storefronts, 08 45 00 is Translucent Wall and Roof Assemblies and 08 46 00 is Window Wall Assemblies.

questions.question: The purpose of the coordination process is summed up as:

options.A: Managing dependencies between activities
options.B: Eliminating changes during construction
options.C: Assigning responsibility for errors and omissions
options.D: Controlling cost through budget thresholds
options.E: Detecting clashes between discipline models
options.F: Enforcing consistent terminology and abbreviations

questions.explanation: Coordination makes project delivery more valuable and efficient by handling how project tasks and parties depend on one another, summed up as managing dependencies between activities. Setting budget thresholds and corrective actions is cost management, a separate function, and clash detection or consistent terminology are only pieces of coordination, not its purpose.

questions.question: Which statements about reference standards are correct?

options.A: Reference standards in themselves are voluntary.
options.B: Some codes and regulations adopt reference standards.
options.C: Model code bodies do more research and testing than reference standards developers.
options.D: Reference standards often set quality at a minimum level.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: Reference standards are voluntary in themselves, unlike codes and regulations, though some codes and regulations adopt them, and they often set quality only at a minimum level, so {F} is correct. Model code bodies rely on reference standards precisely because they cannot match the research and testing that the standards developers carry out.

questions.question: What is the main drawback of office master guide specifications?

options.A: Their product information is unreliable
options.B: They can become outdated unless vigilantly maintained
options.C: Their proprietary language needs editing for competitive bids
options.D: They contain far more than a project needs
options.E: Very few projects are identical, so editing takes longer
options.F: They lack the firm's vetted office knowledge

questions.explanation: An office master holds the firm's vetted knowledge, but it can go out of date unless someone maintains it vigilantly. Carrying far more content than a project needs is the drawback of commercial masters, proprietary language needing edits is the drawback of manufacturer-furnished specifications, and editing out text that does not apply is the drawback of reusing previous project specifications.

questions.question: When products from multiple manufacturers appear similar and meet the design intent, who determines the acceptable degree of variance in their characteristics?

options.A: The owner
options.B: The A/E
options.C: The product representative
options.D: The contractor
options.E: The manufacturer
options.F: The authority having jurisdiction

questions.explanation: Products from different makers that look alike and meet the design intent still differ in their characteristics. Deciding how much variance can be allowed while still meeting the design intent is the A/E's job, along with confirming that products satisfy the design criteria, codes and standards. The contractor may make the final selection, but only within the limits the A/E sets.

questions.question: Which statements about cash allowances under AIA A201 and ConsensusDocs 200 are correct?

options.A: The allowance covers materials and equipment delivered to the site, including taxes
options.B: Installation, handling, overhead and profit are in the contract sum, not the allowance
options.C: The contractor must contract with any supplier the owner designates, without objection
options.D: ConsensusDocs says the sum may be adjusted where A201 says it will be
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: A201 and ConsensusDocs 200 both limit the cash allowance to materials and equipment delivered to the site, taxes included, and carry the contractor's labor, unloading, handling, installation, overhead and profit in the contract sum. A201 says the contract sum will be adjusted by change order for the cost difference, while ConsensusDocs says it may be, so {F} is correct. The contractor need not contract with a designated party it reasonably objects to.

questions.question: Manufacturer guide specifications must be reviewed carefully for:

options.A: Copyright limits on editing
options.B: Product bias and accuracy
options.C: MasterFormat numbering errors
options.D: Units of measurement
options.E: Product pricing and lead times
options.F: Sales territory restrictions

questions.explanation: Manufacturer guide specifications relieve the A/E of some research and writing, but they must be checked for bias toward one product and for whether they state the needed information accurately. Dropped into a project unedited, they can bring proprietary requirements, 'no substitutions' clauses and set values that shut out comparable products. Pricing, lead times and numbering are not the main concern.

questions.question: A product under consideration has a long lead time. What should the A/E evaluate?

options.A: Whether its shop drawings can be waived
options.B: Whether it should become an alternate
options.C: Whether it can be carried as an allowance
options.D: Whether it fits the project schedule
options.E: Whether it can be listed as a unit price
options.F: Whether a substitution should be invited

questions.explanation: Delivery and availability are schedule factors in evaluating products, so for a long-lead item the A/E checks how its schedule fits the project schedule; if needed, it can then be procured early. Making it an alternate, an allowance or a unit price does not answer the schedule question, and waiving shop drawings would not shorten fabrication or shipping.

questions.question: Which statements about UCC Article 2 are correct?

options.A: It covers sales of movable goods
options.B: Contracts for goods costing more than $5,000 must be in writing
options.C: It covers contracts primarily for services, such as an installation check
options.D: The price must be fixed in the contract for it to be enforceable
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: UCC Article 2 governs sales of movable goods, so contracts mainly for services, including a supplier's technical assistance or installation check, fall outside it. Contracts for goods over $500, not $5,000, must be in writing to be enforceable, and the UCC lets the parties leave terms such as price open to be settled later.

questions.question: When a piece of information appears in both the drawings and the specifications, the recommended practice is to:

options.A: Place it in the location most likely to be read
options.B: Say it once and in the right place
options.C: Repeat it in both locations for emphasis
options.D: Put it only on the drawings
options.E: Put it only in the specifications
options.F: Let a precedence statement govern it

questions.explanation: The governing principle is to say it once and in the right place, so each requirement appears in either the drawings or the specifications, not both. Repeating it for emphasis invites discrepancies when an addendum corrects one copy and misses the other. Neither document is always the right home, and a precedence statement is not the fix.

questions.question: Off-site (shop) fabrication is typically beneficial when:

options.A: Field conditions are better controlled than shop conditions
options.B: The assembled item is too large to ship to the site
options.C: Shop conditions allow better control before delivery
options.D: Field labor is the only construction resource available
options.E: Connections must be cut to final dimensions in the field
options.F: A short schedule calls for a more expensive manufacturer

questions.explanation: When part of a product's work can be done in a shop, where conditions are easier to control, before delivery, choosing that product often benefits the owner, provided it can still be shipped after fabrication. Steel beams and columns, for example, are fabricated off-site with connections cut before they reach the site. An item too large to ship is the exception, not the reason.

questions.question: Shortform specifications are LEAST appropriate for:

options.A: A design-negotiate-build with a familiar contractor
options.B: A design-build delivery project
options.C: A small interior tenant improvement
options.D: A construction management multiple-prime project
options.E: A simple single-prime contract project
options.F: An owner-build delivery project

questions.explanation: Multiple-prime contracts under construction management bring coordination complications, so unless a shortform specification is written specifically to handle them, full-length specifications usually work better. Shortforms suit negotiated work with a familiar contractor, design-build, owner-build, small tenant improvements and simple single-prime projects.

questions.question: Which are NOT among the four common sources of prewritten guide specification text?

options.A: Contractor-furnished specifications
options.B: Commercial master guide specifications
options.C: Manufacturer-furnished specifications
options.D: Office master guide specifications
options.E: Previous project specifications
options.F: Reference standard specifications

questions.explanation: The four sources commonly compared are commercial master guide specifications, office master guide specifications, manufacturer-furnished specifications and previous project specifications. Contractors do not furnish guide text, and reference standards are cited within specifications rather than serving as a source of section text.

questions.question: What decides whether the revised-page method may communicate changes better than the narrative method?

options.A: The number and type of changes
options.B: The project delivery method in use
options.C: Whether the change comes during bidding or construction
options.D: Whether the owner or the contractor requested it
options.E: The number of bidders who must receive it
options.F: The cost of the change to the contract sum

questions.explanation: Whether reissuing revised pages works better than describing changes in words depends on how many changes there are and what kind they are. Both methods can be used for addenda and for later modifications, so the phase of the project, who asked for the change, its cost and the delivery method do not decide it.

questions.question: In specification practice, what is a communication record form used for?

options.A: To request a substitution during bidding
options.B: To log incoming substitution requests
options.C: To confirm a verbal understanding in writing
options.D: To request an interpretation during construction
options.E: To record a change in the contract sum or time
options.F: To request a product be accepted as equivalent

questions.explanation: A communication record confirms in writing an understanding reached in a phone call or meeting, is copied to the parties and filed, and a companion communication log lists the questions received. Substitution requests, RFIs and change orders each have their own forms, so they are not what a communication record is for.

questions.question: A firm's office master section for flush wood doors lists five manufacturers and standardizes book-matched veneer. Which conditions call for revising the master itself?

options.A: The last project closed out with no claims
options.B: A client wants slip matching on its next projects
options.C: The firm is opening an office in another state
options.D: One listed manufacturer bought another listed one
options.E: Doors are warping from installation before the HVAC runs
options.F: A regional door manufacturer is near a new office

questions.explanation: Revise a master when its text is wrong for every project: two listed manufacturers are now one company, so the list is out of date, and doors warping because they are installed before the HVAC system is running is a recurring problem the text should address. One client's request for slip matching is a project edit, and a new office calls for checking whether the master suits that region, not rewriting it.

questions.question: Under the revised-page method, how is a change to the project manual or drawings issued?

options.A: The section or sheet is changed with revision marks and reissued
options.B: Each change is described in writing, expressed once and cross-referenced
options.C: Each later package adds revised documents to those issued earlier
options.D: Each package is issued complete, with its revisions tracked separately
options.E: The change is confirmed on a Communication Record sent to all parties
options.F: Only the changed paragraphs are issued, and no section is reissued

questions.explanation: In the revised-page method the change is made directly in the specification section or drawing sheet, marked with a revision identifier such as clouds or delta symbols, and the section or sheet is reissued, often with the revision date and an identifier such as CO-01 in the header or footer. Describing each change in words is the narrative method, and adding to or keeping separate earlier packages are the cumulative and standalone work-package methods.

questions.question: A master section's Part 3 says only to install doors in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. How should the specifier view this?

options.A: Usually required wording for performance sections
options.B: May be inadequate; add project-specific requirements
options.C: Usually sufficient, since the manufacturer controls installation
options.D: Generally prohibited, since it delegates the design
options.E: Adequate, since installation is the contractor's means and methods
options.F: Adequate once the instructions are bound into the project manual

questions.explanation: Requiring installation per the manufacturer's instructions may be enough in some cases, but the team should identify project-specific requirements to add for clarity. Any added text must be checked so it does not conflict with the manufacturer's instructions or other requirements. Treating the phrase as always sufficient, always required or prohibited misses the need for that project review.

questions.question: After a phone call about a wall that leaves too little room for the specified lockers, the architect sends the contractor a communication record directing the wall to be moved. The record says it will be taken as complete and accurate unless the recipient objects in writing within seven days. The contractor never responds and builds the wall in its original location. Who is responsible?

options.A: The contractor
options.B: The architect
options.C: The architect and contractor equally
options.D: The owner
options.E: The locker subcontractor
options.F: The specifier

questions.explanation: The architect confirmed the resolution in writing, copied the parties and gave seven days to object. By staying silent, the contractor accepted the record, so building the wall in the original location is its responsibility. Had the architect never put the call in writing, the architect and contractor would likely have shared the blame, which is why written confirmation of verbal understandings matters.

questions.question: Liquidated damages usually accrue when the contractor fails to achieve which milestone on time?

options.A: Certificate of occupancy
options.B: Beneficial occupancy
options.C: Substantial completion
options.D: Final completion
options.E: Partial occupancy
options.F: Final acceptance

questions.explanation: Liquidated damages fix an agreed amount for the owner's loss from inexcusable delay, and they are usually deducted when the contractor fails to reach substantial completion within the stipulated time or by a stated date. Final completion comes later and is not the usual trigger, and occupancy milestones are not what the damages measure.

questions.question: When a fire-resistance-rated assembly is required, the specifications should coordinate with:

options.A: The IBC table for the required hourly rating
options.B: A listed design chosen by the contractor with the same rating
options.C: Any listed design that provides the required rating
options.D: The specific tested design that matches the construction
options.E: The product representative's proposed alternative assembly
options.F: The manufacturers already named in the specification section

questions.explanation: Fire-resistance-rated construction relies on a tested assembly made of specifically listed products, and deviations from those listed products are generally not allowed. The specified products must therefore match the particular tested design indicated for the construction. Another listed design with the same hourly rating uses different products, so it is not interchangeable, and neither the contractor nor a representative can swap one in.

questions.question: Asbestos and lead abatement will be part of the work. How should it be specified?

options.A: Refer the demolition section to Document 00 31 26 for removal
options.B: Add Division 02 remediation sections for asbestos and lead
options.C: Place a general note on the demolition drawings citing the reports
options.D: Attach the hazardous material reports to the agreement
options.E: Show the abatement on the drawings as work not in the contract
options.F: Specify the abatement in Section 01 35 43, Environmental Procedures

questions.explanation: When abatement is part of the contract work it has to be specified, so add Division 02 remediation sections such as 02 82 00, Asbestos Remediation, and 02 83 00, Lead Remediation, and revise the demolition section to match. Document 00 31 26, Existing Hazardous Material Information, is available information for bidders rather than a contract document, so pointing to it does not put abatement in the contract.

questions.question: Listing both the basis-of-design product name and its product number is:

options.A: Unnecessary, because the drawing schedule identifies the product
options.B: Recommended, because it makes submittal review easier
options.C: Discouraged, because it makes the specification proprietary
options.D: Required only when no comparable products are listed
options.E: Discouraged, because it duplicates the product data submittal
options.F: Recommended, because it removes the need for comparable products

questions.explanation: Giving both the basis-of-design product name and its number makes submittals easier to review, especially when the contractor submits a product other than the basis of design. The contractor also needs to know the exact product to price the installation, such as fasteners and backing, so a drawing schedule alone is not enough, and naming a basis of design does not by itself close the specification.

questions.question: Which of the following are recommended when listing alternates in Section 01 23 00 and on the bid form?

options.A: Label each alternate as an add or a deduct so bidders know which way the price moves
options.B: Label only the alternates that remove scope as deducts
options.C: Have the bidder indicate whether its alternate price adds or deducts
options.D: Have the A/E assign add or deduct after the bids are opened
options.E: Identify each alternate by its title as well as its number
options.F: Describe what each alternate includes and leave the base bid to the drawings

questions.explanation: The bidder, not the specifier, states whether each alternate price is an add or a deduct, so the bid form should ask for it. Each alternate also needs a title as well as a number so references stay consistent throughout the documents. Section 01 23 00 should describe what both the base bid and each alternate include, rather than leaving the base bid to the drawings.

questions.question: At the final check before issuance, the toilet accessory schedule conflicts with the toilet room elevations. The A/E should:

options.A: Add a note that the schedule governs the elevations
options.B: Leave it for the contractor to raise as an RFI
options.C: Add a precedence listing to Division 01
options.D: Correct the conflict before the documents are issued
options.E: Correct the conflict by addendum during bidding
options.F: Move the schedule from the drawings to the project manual

questions.explanation: Final coordination before issuance includes verifying that all schedules are consistent and that noted errors are corrected, so a known conflict should be fixed before the documents go out. Precedence notes are not recommended, an RFI leaves bidders to read the conflict differently and can lead to change orders, and a later addendum is the very fix the final check exists to avoid.

questions.question: The owner wants separate pricing for one specific floor tile product. Which Division 01 section is edited?

options.A: Section 01 22 00—Unit Prices
options.B: Section 01 21 00—Allowances
options.C: Section 01 23 00—Alternates
options.D: Section 01 29 00—Payment Procedures
options.E: Section 01 26 00—Contract Modification Procedures
options.F: Section 01 25 00—Substitution Procedures

questions.explanation: A separate price for one named product is an alternate, so the bid form gets a space for it, Section 01 23 00, Alternates, describes it, and the tiling section notes that it is affected. A unit price pays a rate for quantities that are uncertain, and an allowance carries a sum for a selection not yet made.

questions.question: An owner sets a minority business enterprise (MBE) participation goal for a new office building. Which documents are edited?

options.A: A Division 00 MBE form and the supplementary conditions
options.B: Section 01 60 00 and Section 01 80 00
options.C: The bid form alone, where bidders list a percentage
options.D: Each technical section, trade by trade
options.E: Section 01 81 13 and the LEED checklist
options.F: The agreement form and the general conditions

questions.explanation: An MBE goal is a procurement and contracting matter, so edit Division 00: an MBE certification form (00 62 39) and the supplementary conditions, where MasterFormat places equal employment opportunity and MBE requirements (00 73 36 and 00 73 39). The Division 01 product and performance sections and the technical sections do not carry such goals.

questions.question: The construction, review, and use of mockups as standards for installed work belong in which Division 01 group?

options.A: 01 40 00—Quality Requirements
options.B: 01 30 00—Administrative Requirements
options.C: 01 60 00—Product Requirements
options.D: 01 70 00—Execution and Closeout Requirements
options.E: 01 50 00—Temporary Facilities and Controls
options.F: 01 80 00—Performance Requirements

questions.explanation: The 01 40 00 Quality Requirements group covers managing and reporting quality, including building, reviewing and using mock-ups and field samples as standards for installed work, testing laboratory qualifications and payment for tests; MasterFormat lists 01 43 39, Mockups, under Quality Assurance there. The administrative, product and execution groups handle other matters.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, a contractor believes the architect's response to its RFI involves additional cost. What must the contractor do?

options.A: Make a Claim as provided in A201 Article 15
options.B: Submit a second RFI asking for the cost adjustment
options.C: Proceed, since the RFI response itself adjusts the contract sum
options.D: Stop work until the owner signs a change order
options.E: Submit a substitution request under Section 01 25 00
options.F: Wait for the architect to issue a change order

questions.explanation: A201 says that if the contractor believes clarifications or instructions the architect issues in answer to its RFIs involve extra cost or time, it must make a Claim under Article 15. An RFI answer interprets the documents but does not change the contract sum, and RFIs are for questions, not for requesting adjustments. The contractor must start the process rather than wait for a change order.

questions.question: Which of these contractor requests are improper uses of an RFI?

options.A: A request for approval of a proposed substitution
options.B: A request to clarify an insufficiently detailed item
options.C: A request for an increase in the contract sum
options.D: A question about dimensions that conflict between two drawings
options.E: A request for information missing from a door schedule
options.F: A request to interpret an ambiguous specification paragraph

questions.explanation: RFIs are for questions that arise from interpreting the documents, from missing information or from a need for clarification. A substitution sent as an RFI is often an attempt to get around the substitution deadline and belongs in the substitution procedures, and a request for more money belongs in the claim or change process. Conflicting dimensions, missing schedule data and ambiguous wording are exactly what RFIs are for.

questions.question: The local code does not adopt a particular reference standard. How does that standard become a project requirement?

options.A: By its publication as an ANSI standard
options.B: By the manufacturer's claim of compliance
options.C: By reference in the project specifications
options.D: By listing in a code's appendices
options.E: By an evaluation report for the product
options.F: By its citation in a manufacturer's guide spec

questions.explanation: Reference standards are voluntary until a code adopts them or the project specifications incorporate them by citing the developer's name, number and title; once cited, their requirements become part of the contract. ANSI status, a manufacturer's claim, an evaluation report, a code appendix the jurisdiction has not adopted or a manufacturer's guide specification binds no one on the project.

questions.question: Which statements about sustainability requirements are correct?

options.A: LEED and Green Globes are voluntary sustainability programs.
options.B: An owner may require compliance with a voluntary sustainability program as a programming provision.
options.C: Adopting the IBC by itself requires projects to earn a LEED rating.
options.D: A jurisdiction may provide sustainability as a code path alternative, such as adopting the IgCC.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: LEED and Green Globes are voluntary programs, an owner may make compliance with one a programming requirement, and a jurisdiction may build sustainability into its adopted code or offer it as a code path alternative, such as adopting the IgCC, so {F} is correct. Adopting the IBC by itself does not require a project to earn a LEED rating.

questions.question: In a High Velocity Wind Zone subject to hurricanes, exterior windows and doors must:

options.A: Meet impact criteria or have impact protection
options.B: Have aluminum rather than steel frames
options.C: Be fixed and inoperable
options.D: Be triple-glazed for thermal performance
options.E: Have galvanized steel frames and hardware
options.F: Be shuttered only where they face the ocean

questions.explanation: In a High Velocity Wind Zone subject to hurricanes, exterior parts of the building must pass the impact test criteria or be shielded by an external protection device that does, so windows and doors need impact-rated units or impact protection. Aluminum frames are often chosen on a coast because they resist salt-spray corrosion, which is a durability choice, not the wind requirement.

questions.question: Which of the following are construction-related powers of the jurisdiction that adopts a building code?

options.A: Writing the model code it later enforces
options.B: Interpreting provisions of the adopted code
options.C: Inspecting only after substantial completion
options.D: Approving the A/E's specifications before bidding
options.E: Condemning buildings not in compliance
options.F: Updating the model code about every three years

questions.explanation: The agency that adopts a code becomes the local authority for issuing permits and certificates of occupancy, interpreting the code's provisions, enforcing it by granting or withholding approvals, inspecting new and altered buildings, and condemning buildings that do not comply. Writing the model code and revising it every three years or so is the work of model code organizations such as the ICC, not of the jurisdiction that adopts it.

questions.question: For the low-slope roof of a two-story office building near the Gulf Coast, which membrane color is best?

options.A: White, to reduce solar heat gain
options.B: Black, to dry faster after rain
options.C: Black, to hide dirt and staining
options.D: Gray, to balance heat gain and glare
options.E: Black, to resist hail and storm damage
options.F: Tan, to suit the local aesthetic conditions

questions.explanation: Products must suit the exterior conditions at the site, and on the Gulf Coast intense sun and heat are among the most important. A white, reflective membrane turns sunlight away and cuts solar heat gain, which lowers cooling loads. A black membrane absorbs that heat, and quicker drying, hiding dirt, or storm resistance do not outweigh heat gain in this climate; gray gives up much of the reflectance.

questions.question: When is a constructability review best performed?

options.A: After details develop, before CDs are finalized
options.B: At the end of schematic design, before details exist
options.C: After bids arrive, using the low bidder's input
options.D: During construction, as shop drawings are reviewed
options.E: After CDs are finalized, as a last quality check
options.F: During programming, when site constraints emerge

questions.explanation: A constructability review is most useful once the details are developed enough to evaluate, but before the construction documents are finalized, so its recommendations can be worked in with little disruption to the design schedule. At the end of schematic design there is too little detail to judge, and after the documents are final or bids are in, every change costs time and money. The review asks whether the design can practically be built, not what it costs.

questions.question: A ceiling product is evaluated for surface-burning characteristics with three statements: flame spread; a rating under 25 on a scale of 0 to 100; and ASTM E84. In performance terms, what role does 'a rating under 25' play?

options.A: Requirement
options.B: Criterion
options.C: Test
options.D: Attribute
options.E: Performance characteristic
options.F: Reference standard

questions.explanation: Performance specifying breaks each attribute into requirements, criteria, and tests. The requirement is the desired result (limited flame spread), the criterion is the measurable or observable level that satisfies it (a rating under 25), and the test is how conformance is verified (ASTM E84). The attribute is the characteristic being addressed, surface-burning characteristics, not the number.

questions.question: Which of the following are NOT among the four Cs of specification writing?

options.A: Consistent
options.B: Correct
options.C: Concise
options.D: Clear
options.E: Complete
options.F: Coordinated

questions.explanation: Specification language follows the four Cs: clear, concise, complete, and correct. Consistency and coordination with the drawings both matter in a project manual, but neither is one of the four Cs, which is why those two are the ones that do not belong.

questions.question: Which of these are sources of project-requirements information rather than product reference material?

options.A: Trade association handbooks
options.B: Manufacturers' guide specifications
options.C: Detailed cost estimate
options.D: Commercial master guide specifications
options.E: Outline specifications prepared earlier
options.F: Specifications from similar past projects

questions.explanation: Before editing a section, the specifier gathers two kinds of information. Project requirements come from this project: the owner's requirements, the drawings, a preliminary project description or outline specification prepared earlier, the detailed cost estimate, and the governing codes. Reference material describes products and methods in general, which is what trade association handbooks, manufacturers' guide specifications, commercial masters, and specifications from past projects provide.

questions.question: In SectionFormat, 'Preconstruction Testing' is a subordinate title under:

options.A: PART 3, Examination
options.B: PART 1, Quality Assurance
options.C: PART 2, Source Quality Control
options.D: PART 3, Field [or] Site Quality Control
options.E: PART 1, Administrative Requirements
options.F: PART 1, Field [or] Site Conditions

questions.explanation: SectionFormat lists Preconstruction Testing under the Quality Assurance article in PART 1, together with qualifications, certifications, and field samples and mock-ups. Its near twin, Preinstallation Testing, sits under Examination in PART 3, and testing at the plant or shop belongs to Source Quality Control in PART 2.

questions.question: Which is NOT a closeout submittal?

options.A: Delegated design submittals
options.B: Project record documents
options.C: Spare parts
options.D: Sustainable design closeout documentation
options.E: Maintenance contracts
options.F: Warranties

questions.explanation: Delegated design submittals are action or informational submittals reviewed while the work is under way, not documents turned over at the end. Closeout submittals typically include maintenance contracts, operation and maintenance data, the final survey, warranties, project record documents, spare parts and extra stock, and sustainable design closeout documentation.

questions.question: As a general rule, when should the Division 01 sections be finalized?

options.A: Before any technical section is started
options.B: After the Divisions 02–49 sections are written
options.C: When the drawings reach design development
options.D: After the owner's final review
options.E: Before consultants begin writing their sections
options.F: After bids are received and addenda issued

questions.explanation: Division 01 sections should be drafted as early as possible and circulated for review, but as a general rule the sections of Divisions 02 through 49 are written first and Division 01 is finalized after them. Drafting early is not the same as finishing early; waiting until after bids and addenda is too late, because the project manual must be complete before procurement.

questions.question: Standard agreement forms (such as AIA A101) should appear in the project manual:

options.A: As actual bound or sample copies for bidders to review the contract terms
options.B: Only after award of the contract, included in the conformed record set
options.C: Only when the owner specifically directs the A/E to reproduce the documents
options.D: By reference to the document number only, to avoid using an outdated form
options.E: Listed by title and edition in Section 01 42 00—References only
options.F: Summarized in the instructions to bidders in place of the full form

questions.explanation: Standard agreement forms should be included in the project manual as actual bound or sample copies, not by reference only. A real copy lets bidders review the contract terms they will be asked to sign, and binding it in also removes the risk of pointing to an incorrect or outdated edition, which is exactly the risk a by-reference citation creates.

questions.question: A specification reads 'reinforcing bars: ASTM A615, Grade 60.' This is which specification method?

options.A: Descriptive method
options.B: Reference standard method
options.C: Performance method
options.D: Closed proprietary method
options.E: Open proprietary method
options.F: Basis-of-design method

questions.explanation: Citing an industry standard such as ASTM A615, Grade 60, to set the product's properties is reference standard specifying: the standard carries the detailed requirements instead of the section text. A descriptive specification would spell out those properties in the section itself, and a performance specification would state the results required rather than a product standard.

questions.question: A specification reads: 'Zim tile manufactured by Zimbo Inc.' Which classification BEST applies?

options.A: Proprietary
options.B: Descriptive
options.C: Performance
options.D: Reference standard
options.E: Non-restrictive
options.F: Cash allowance

questions.explanation: Naming a specific manufacturer and product identifies the item by brand, which makes this a proprietary specification; with no 'or equal' or substitution language it is a closed proprietary one. Descriptive and performance specifications describe properties or required results without naming a product, and a reference standard specification relies on an industry standard.

questions.question: Coordination of drawings and specifications is the primary responsibility of:

options.A: The construction manager
options.B: Each consultant for their own discipline only
options.C: The owner's representative
options.D: The prime A/E
options.E: The contractor's project manager
options.F: The lead specialty consultant

questions.explanation: The prime A/E is responsible for overall coordination of the drawings and specifications, including the portions prepared by engineering and specialty consultants. Each consultant prepares its own part, but someone has to coordinate across disciplines, and that duty falls to the prime A/E rather than the owner, the construction manager, or the contractor.

questions.question: An invitation calls for sealed bids at a stated office by a stated time; mailed bids go to the same address. May a bidder email its bid?

options.A: Yes, if the email arrives before the deadline
options.B: No, because sealed bids must reach the stated office
options.C: Yes, if a signed original follows by mail
options.D: No, because bids must be delivered in person
options.E: Yes, if the bid is sent as a password-protected file
options.F: Yes, because mailed and emailed bids are treated alike

questions.explanation: Bids may be submitted only by the methods the procurement documents allow. This invitation allows sealed bids delivered to the stated office, by hand or by mail, for public opening, so an emailed bid is not an accepted method no matter when it arrives. Delivery in person is not the only method either, since mailed bids are allowed.

questions.question: EJCDC C-200 recommends that bidders submit questions at least how many days before the bid opening?

options.A: 7 days
options.B: 10 days
options.C: 14 days
options.D: 15 days
options.E: 4 days
options.F: 21 days
