questions.explanation: EJCDC C-200, EJCDC's suggested instructions to bidders, recommends that bidders' questions arrive no later than 10 days before bids are opened. Seven days is AIA A701's deadline for questions, and four days is how late a minor addendum can sometimes be issued without hardship to bidders.

questions.question: A project's RFI procedures allow the architect five days to respond to each RFI and state that RFIs received after 1:00 p.m. count as received on the next working day. Working days are Monday through Friday. An RFI reaches the architect at 3:00 p.m. on a Friday. When is it considered received?

options.A: That Friday, when it arrived
options.B: Monday, the next working day
options.C: Saturday, the next calendar day
options.D: Whenever the architect logs it
options.E: Tuesday, two working days later
options.F: On the date its response is due

questions.explanation: The cutoff rule decides it: an RFI that arrives after 1:00 p.m. counts as received on the next working day, and since Saturday is not a working day, that is Monday. The five-day response period then runs from Monday. The cutoff moves only the start of the clock; it does not change the response allowance, and the date the architect logs the RFI has no effect.

questions.question: In a large gathering room, speech is hard to understand because of reverberation. Which products would best fix this?

options.A: Acoustical panels on the walls
options.B: High-performance acoustical ceilings
options.C: Acoustical batts inside the wall cavities
options.D: High-performance insulating glazing
options.E: Hard, smooth, easily cleaned wall finishes
options.F: Ultraviolet tints on the room's windows

questions.explanation: Reverberation is sound bouncing around the room off hard surfaces, so the fix is fewer hard surfaces and more absorptive ones, such as acoustical wall panels and high-performance acoustical ceilings. Batts inside the wall cavities and insulating glazing reduce sound passing through walls and windows from outside, which is a different problem, and hard, smooth finishes make reverberation worse.

questions.question: When the owner requests it, the A/E reproduces the approved project manual and drawings in enough sets for procurement and for what other purpose?

options.A: Funding approvals by financial institutions
options.B: The contractor's insurance underwriting
options.C: Each subcontractor's shop drawing work
options.D: Marketing the completed project
options.E: Archiving by the A/E for version control
options.F: The surety's review for bonding

questions.explanation: When the owner asks, the A/E reproduces the approved project manual and drawings in enough sets for procurement and for funding approvals by financial institutions; further copies go to each project team member and to regulatory agencies for permits. Shop drawings, insurance underwriting, and bonding are not among the purposes these sets serve.

questions.question: Which of the following does builder's risk insurance cover?

options.A: The structure under construction
options.B: The contractor's tools and construction equipment
options.C: A subcontractor's equipment only while it is being installed
options.D: Bodily injury to third parties at the site
options.E: Materials and equipment to be incorporated into the project
options.F: Mobile equipment such as cranes and backhoes

questions.explanation: Builder's risk is property insurance written for a building under construction: it covers the structure itself and the materials and equipment that are or will become part of the project. The contractor's own tools and construction equipment, including cranes and backhoes, need separate coverage; an installation floater covers a subcontractor's materials during installation; and bodily injury to third parties is a liability risk, not property damage.

questions.question: PageFormat establishes which of the following for the printed project manual?

options.A: The crosswalk between MasterFormat and UniFormat
options.B: Placement of headers, footers, and page numbers
options.C: The three-part GENERAL/PRODUCTS/EXECUTION organization
options.D: The standard article titles within each PART
options.E: Margins and the arrangement of paragraph levels
options.F: The sequence of sections in the table of contents

questions.explanation: PageFormat gives guidelines for margins, line spacing, headers and footers, page numbering, section numbers and titles, and how Parts, Articles, Paragraphs, and subparagraphs are arranged on the page. The three parts and their standard article titles come from SectionFormat, and the order of sections in the table of contents comes from MasterFormat.

questions.question: When the owner furnishes products for the contractor to install, Section 01 64 00 should do which of the following?

options.A: Specify purchasing the products through the contractor's suppliers
options.B: Specify paying for the products through a cash allowance
options.C: Specify warranting the products against manufacturing defects
options.D: Specify procedures for coordinating, scheduling, and receiving the products
options.E: Specify the basic requirements for installing, applying, and erecting them
options.F: List the owner-furnished products, cross-referenced in Section 01 10 00

questions.explanation: Section 01 64 00, Owner-Furnished Products, states the essential characteristics of the products the owner supplies, specifies how they are coordinated, scheduled, and received so their condition is acceptable on delivery, and holds the list of owner-furnished products, which Section 01 10 00 cross-references. The basic requirements for installing them belong in Section 01 73 00, Execution, and the products come from the owner, not through the contractor's suppliers or a cash allowance.

questions.question: On a federally funded construction project, the Davis-Bacon Act requires the contractor to:

options.A: Meet the Department of Labor's wage determinations
options.B: Pay all workers at least the federal minimum wage
options.C: Pay the rates in the state's public-works wage law
options.D: Hire only union-affiliated labor for covered work
options.E: Pay the wage rates the A/E sets in the specifications
options.F: Pay rates fixed by a labor stabilization agreement

questions.explanation: Federally funded projects must meet the U.S. Department of Labor's wage requirements under the Davis-Bacon Act, whose wage determinations are set by work classification for each project jurisdiction. Those rates closely track local union wage and benefit scales, but the act does not require union labor. State wage laws govern state public contracts, and the A/E does not set wage rates.

questions.question: Which of the following does the UCC implied warranty of merchantability require of the goods?

options.A: Fit for the ordinary uses of goods of that kind
options.B: Fit for a particular purpose the seller knew the buyer had
options.C: Backed by a written warranty from the seller
options.D: Free of any security interest unknown to the buyer
options.E: Adequately contained, packaged, and labeled
options.F: Free of defects for one year after delivery

questions.explanation: Under the UCC, merchantable goods pass without objection in the trade, are fit for the ordinary uses of goods of their kind, are properly contained, packaged, and labeled, and match the promises on the label. Fitness for a particular purpose the seller knew about is the separate, second implied warranty; any written warranty is an express warranty; and freedom from unknown liens or security interests is the warranty of title.

questions.question: A ConsensusDocs change order requires the signatures of:

options.A: The owner and the contractor only
options.B: The owner, the contractor, and the A/E
options.C: The owner only
options.D: The contractor and the A/E only
options.E: The owner and the A/E only
options.F: The owner, the contractor, and the surety

questions.explanation: The ConsensusDocs 202 change order needs only the owner's and the contractor's signatures. Under AIA A201, the architect prepares the change order and all three parties, owner, contractor, and architect, sign it, while the ConsensusDocs 203 interim directive needs only the owner's signature, so the other combinations borrow from those forms.

questions.question: On an owner-build project, how are Division 01 tasks a general contractor would normally handle, such as temporary utilities, testing, and traffic control, accomplished?

options.A: Assigned to the A/E under contract administration
options.B: Deleted from Division 01, since no general contractor is retained
options.C: Assigned to specialty contractors or done otherwise
options.D: Covered by the owner's builder's risk insurance
options.E: Assigned to a CM-Agent who holds the trade contracts
options.F: Waived unless the authority having jurisdiction requires them

questions.explanation: When the owner acts as builder there is no general contractor to provide traffic control, temporary utilities and facilities, testing, and inspections, but the tasks still have to be done. The owner must decide how, typically by making them the responsibility of the individual specialty contractors or by arranging them some other way. They are not deleted or waived, and they do not become part of the A/E's contract administration.

questions.question: What most reliably distinguishes a construction manager as agent from a construction manager as advisor?

options.A: Whether the CM guarantees a maximum price
options.B: Whether the CM's decisions bind the owner
options.C: Whether the CM holds the trade contracts
options.D: Whether the CM gives preconstruction advice
options.E: Whether the CM contracts only with the owner
options.F: Whether the CM is at risk for construction defects

questions.explanation: A CM-Agent acts as the owner's agent and can make decisions that bind the owner, within the authority the agreement delegates; a CM-Advisor may offer many of the same services but only advises and cannot bind the owner. Both contract only with the owner, neither holds trade contracts or guarantees a maximum price, and both can give preconstruction advice, so those features do not tell them apart.

questions.question: PPDFormat is most accurately described as the format for:

options.A: Postoccupancy Performance Data submitted by the contractor at closeout
options.B: Project Procurement Documents binding and distribution requirements
options.C: Project Manual page headers, footers, margins, and numbering layout
options.D: Preliminary Project Descriptions prepared during early design phases
options.E: Preliminary Project Phases listed in the Division 00 available information
options.F: Preliminary Project Schedules issued with the procurement documents

questions.explanation: PPDFormat is the standard for organizing the written design information in a preliminary project description, the description of a project prepared in the early design phases and arranged by UniFormat's systems and assemblies, ahead of the outline specifications. Page layout belongs to PageFormat, and PPD does not stand for procurement documents, project phases, or schedules.

questions.question: Citations of reference standards (such as ASTM C150) most appropriately appear in which SectionFormat article?

options.A: PART 1 - REFERENCES
options.B: PART 1 - SUMMARY of work
options.C: PART 3 - EXECUTION
options.D: PART 2 - PRODUCTS
options.E: PART 1 - QUALITY ASSURANCE
options.F: PART 2 - SOURCE QUALITY CONTROL

questions.explanation: The full designation of each standard cited in a section goes in the References article of PART 1, along with abbreviations and definitions. PART 2 and PART 3 can then refer to the standard by its number alone, which saves space and puts all the section's standards in one list for gathering reference material. Quality Assurance and Source Quality Control state requirements and testing, not the list of standards.

questions.question: Preinstallation meeting requirements specific to a section are most appropriately specified in:

options.A: PART 3, Examination
options.B: PART 1, Quality Assurance
options.C: PART 1, Administrative Requirements
options.D: PART 1, Summary
options.E: PART 1, Field [or] Site Conditions
options.F: PART 1, Delivery, Storage, and Handling

questions.explanation: SectionFormat places Preinstallation Meetings under Administrative Requirements in PART 1, with coordination, sequencing, and scheduling; the article is used when a complex installation needs coordination and understanding among several participants. Quality Assurance covers qualifications, certifications, field samples, and mock-ups, not meetings, and general project meetings belong in Division 01.

questions.question: Requirements for a product's packaging and its protection at the site before installation are specified under:

options.A: PART 2, Materials
options.B: PART 3, Protection
options.C: PART 1, Delivery, Storage, and Handling
options.D: PART 3, Installation
options.E: PART 1, Field [or] Site Conditions
options.F: PART 1, Maintenance Material Submittals

questions.explanation: Delivery, Storage, and Handling in PART 1 covers delivery and acceptance requirements, storage and handling requirements, and packaging, so it governs the product from shipment until it is built in. The Protection article in PART 3 covers the work after installation, and Field or Site Conditions covers the ambient and existing conditions the installation needs.

questions.question: Acceptable ambient air temperature for installation is most appropriately specified in:

options.A: PART 1 - FIELD/SITE CONDITIONS
options.B: PART 1 - QUALITY ASSURANCE
options.C: PART 2 - PRODUCTS
options.D: PART 3 - EXECUTION (Preparation)
options.E: PART 3 - EXECUTION (Examination)
options.F: PART 1 - DELIVERY, STORAGE, AND HANDLING

questions.explanation: In SectionFormat, the Field [or] Site Conditions article in PART 1 covers ambient conditions and existing conditions, so the temperature range required during installation is stated there. Examination and Preparation in PART 3 describe actions taken at the site, such as checking substrates and preparing surfaces, not the environmental limits the work needs.

questions.question: Section-specific extended guarantee requirements (beyond Division 01 closeout) are specified in:

options.A: Division 01 only, with no section-level guarantee statements
options.B: PART 3 - EXECUTION under the closeout activities article
options.C: PART 1 - WARRANTY of the technical section itself
options.D: PART 2 - PRODUCTS under the performance article
options.E: PART 1 - CLOSEOUT SUBMITTALS, as warranty documentation
options.F: The supplementary conditions in Division 00

questions.explanation: A special or extended warranty that applies to one section's work goes in the Warranty article in PART 1 of that technical section, whose subordinate titles include manufacturer warranty, special warranty, and extended correction period. Closeout Submittals only calls for the warranty documents to be turned in, and Division 01 sets the general closeout procedures, not section-specific guarantees.

questions.question: A specifier joins a 300 SF MRI-suite renovation in an urgent-care facility that stays open during construction. The imaging room has stringent shielding and infection-control requirements. Which form of specification fits?

options.A: Outline specifications
options.B: Performance specifications only
options.C: Shortform specifications
options.D: Full-length specifications
options.E: Purchasing specifications
options.F: Specifications placed on the drawings

questions.explanation: The form of specification depends on the project's complexity and liability risk, not its floor area. A small MRI renovation with stringent shielding and infection-control requirements, in a facility that stays open, is complex and high-risk, so full-length sections fit. The small footprint tempts toward shortform, but shortform suits limited-scope, lower-risk work, and outline specifications are an early-design tool.

questions.question: An interior-only office upfit with a limited scope of work and no exterior envelope, roofing or waterproofing is being built by a contractor that has done five similar fit-outs for the same tenant at other locations. Which form of specification fits?

options.A: Outline specifications
options.B: Full-length specifications
options.C: Shortform specifications
options.D: Purchasing specifications
options.E: Performance specifications
options.F: Preliminary project descriptions

questions.explanation: Shortform specifications suit limited-scope projects that need less detail than full-length sections, and work with no exterior envelope, roofing, or waterproofing can be built from more streamlined documents; a contractor experienced with this tenant's fit-outs lowers the risk further. Full-length sections are for larger, complex, or high-liability projects, and outline specifications and preliminary project descriptions are early-design documents, not contract specifications.

questions.question: When the result matters most and optional solutions that meet the same requirements are welcome, which specifying method fits?

options.A: Performance
options.B: Descriptive
options.C: Reference standard
options.D: Proprietary
options.E: Open proprietary
options.F: Purchasing

questions.explanation: When the result matters most, performance specifications state the required results and how they will be verified, leaving room for any solution that achieves them. Descriptive, reference standard, and proprietary methods each fix more of the product itself, and purchasing specifying is for buying goods with no installation.

questions.question: The work is limited to delivering goods, with no construction or installation. Which approach fits?

options.A: Shortform specifications and a single-prime contract
options.B: Performance specifications and a design-build contract
options.C: Purchasing specifications and a purchasing contract
options.D: Outline specifications and a purchase order
options.E: Purchasing specifications and a single-prime contract
options.F: Full-length specifications and a purchasing contract

questions.explanation: When the work is only the delivery of goods, with no construction or installation, purchasing specifications and a purchasing contract are appropriate. Single-prime and design-build contracts are construction contracts, and outline, shortform, and full-length specifications are written for construction projects, so pairing either with a goods-only purchase does not fit.

questions.question: Fast-track scheduling usually has what effect on overall document preparation time?

options.A: Unchanged, since only the sequence changes
options.B: Shorter, since each package is smaller
options.C: Shorter, as the project schedule shortens
options.D: Longer, though the project schedule shortens
options.E: Longer, and the project schedule lengthens too
options.F: Shorter, since documents come in bursts

questions.explanation: Fast-track and multiple-prime techniques can shorten the overall project schedule, but document preparation usually takes longer, because the documents are produced in staggered bid packages, each prepared in a burst of effort and coordinated with the others. Smaller packages do not add up to less total effort, which is why the owner-A/E agreement should allow adequate fees for the extra time.

questions.question: In Section 01 32 00, how are CPM and Gantt scheduling matched to projects?

options.A: CPM for fast-track only; Gantt for single-prime only
options.B: CPM for complex work; Gantt for straightforward work
options.C: Gantt for complex work; CPM for straightforward work
options.D: Either one, regardless of the project's complexity
options.E: Gantt for multiple-prime work; CPM for single-prime work
options.F: CPM for long-lead items; Gantt for milestone dates

questions.explanation: Section 01 32 00, Construction Progress Documentation, should call for critical path method (CPM) network analysis, with updating, on complex projects and the simpler Gantt bar chart method where the work is straightforward. The section should also identify long-lead items and milestone dates, but those are things the schedule tracks, not a basis for choosing the method.

questions.question: The construction contract was signed before the A/E came on board, and the owner is a public entity. What should the specifier expect of the general and supplementary conditions?

options.A: They are superseded by Division 01
options.B: They may not be open to modification
options.C: They are controlled by the contractor
options.D: They must be redrafted to the office master
options.E: They are modified by supplementary conditions
options.F: They stay open to change until bids are due

questions.explanation: When the construction contract was executed before the A/E joined, its general and supplementary conditions may no longer be available for modification, and public entities may have conditions that cannot be modified at all. The specifier reviews them and writes Division 01 to fit them; Division 01 expands on the conditions but never supersedes them, and the specifier cannot simply redraft them to the office master.

questions.question: Which documents does the A/E send to both the owner and the consultants for review while producing the project manual?

options.A: The proposed conditions of the contract
options.B: The bid form and instructions to bidders
options.C: The geotechnical report and property survey
options.D: The final compiled project manual
options.E: The draft Division 01 sections
options.F: The executed Owner-Contractor Agreement

questions.explanation: While preparing the project manual, the A/E sends the proposed conditions of the contract and the draft Division 01 sections to both the owner and the consultants for review, since the technical sections build on them. The Owner-Contractor Agreement is something the specifier reviews rather than circulates, and the project manual is compiled and reproduced only at the end.

questions.question: During procurement, an A/E wants a written trail of bidders' questions and of substitution requests. Which pairing of tools fits?

options.A: RFI forms for the questions; the submittal log for the substitution requests
options.B: Field orders for the questions; construction change directives for the substitutions
options.C: Communication records and a communication log for the questions; a substitution request log for the substitutions
options.D: Notes of phone calls answered verbally; the bid tabulation for the substitutions
options.E: Draft addenda for the questions; change orders for the substitutions
options.F: Meeting minutes for the questions; supplemental instructions for the substitutions

questions.explanation: During procurement, a communication record documents each question about the documents and a communication log tracks them all, while a substitution request log tracks each request and its outcome so the whole team, including the owner, can follow it. Answers go out in writing, by addendum, never verbally. RFIs, submittals, field orders, change orders, change directives, and supplemental instructions are tools for construction, once a contract exists.

questions.question: Why is PDF useful when distributing revised documents?

options.A: It is the one format every AHJ requires
options.B: It adds delta symbols to revised text automatically
options.C: It shows every editor's tracked changes to recipients
options.D: It can prevent modification after distribution
options.E: It lets bidders forward their edits to sub-bidders
options.F: It records the revision date in each section footer

questions.explanation: Electronic formats let revisions such as addenda reach bidders and sub-bidders quickly, and some, such as PDF, have security features that keep a document from being modified after it is distributed. Tracked changes are a feature of editing software, revision marks such as deltas are applied by the A/E, and no single format is required by every AHJ.

questions.question: Under the narrative method, what does the cross-references criterion require?

options.A: Cite the drawing sheet beside every specification change
options.B: Give only enough information to make the change clear
options.C: Express a change once, then refer to it where needed
options.D: Repeat enough original text to make each change clear
options.E: Refer readers to the drawings instead of the addendum
options.F: Explain related drawing changes in a separate bulletin

questions.explanation: In the narrative method of describing modifications, the cross-references criterion means stating a change only once and then referring to it wherever else it applies; when a specification change also affects the drawings, all the related changes are explained in the same addendum. Repeating enough original text to make each change self-explanatory is the clarity criterion, and giving only enough information to make the change clear is brevity.

questions.question: Each work package is complete and separate, covering only its own scope, with revisions tracked separately. Which approach is this, and what is its drawback?

options.A: Revised-page; requires reissuing every full section
options.B: Standalone; harder to manage as packages multiply
options.C: Narrative; relies too heavily on prose descriptions
options.D: Cumulative; contradicts earlier-released packages
options.E: Standalone; makes each package's extent harder to see
options.F: Cumulative; harder to manage as packages multiply

questions.explanation: In the standalone method, each work package is a complete, separate set of drawings and specifications for its own scope. That makes each package's extent easy to see, but because revisions must be tracked package by package, it grows harder to manage as more packages are issued. The cumulative method, where each package adds to the earlier ones, is preferred because it builds toward one complete set of documents.

questions.question: A firm's office master is based on VA or HUD guide specifications. How should the A/E treat those documents?

options.A: Update them each time a commercial release arrives
options.B: Avoid them, since private work cannot use agency text
options.C: Rewrite them as the firm's permanent office standard
options.D: Make only project-specific edits to them
options.E: Make long-term changes so the master stays current
options.F: Use them unedited, since agency text is mandatory

questions.explanation: When an office master is based on agency guide specifications such as the VA's or HUD's, the A/E does not make long-term changes to those documents; it makes only the edits a particular project needs. The agency maintains the text, so rewriting it as the firm's permanent standard or updating it like a commercial subscription is not the A/E's role, and the text is still edited for each project rather than used as is.

questions.question: What is the main drawback of reusing a previous project's specifications?

options.A: Few projects are identical, so editing out content is slow
options.B: Its proprietary language needs editing for competitive bidding
options.C: The text becomes outdated without vigilant maintenance
options.D: The product information is unreliable
options.E: It contains far more than any project requires
options.F: It runs only in a proprietary software application

questions.explanation: A previous project's specifications save time only when the new project is identical, and very few are, so stripping out content that does not apply can take longer than it saves. Proprietary language that needs editing is the drawback of manufacturer-furnished specifications, too much content is the commercial master's, and text that goes stale without upkeep is the office master's.

questions.question: Manufacturer-furnished specifications have reliable product information. What is their main drawback?

options.A: Proprietary language needs editing for competitive bids
options.B: They contain far more content than the project needs
options.C: Few projects are identical, so editing out text takes time
options.D: They can become outdated unless vigilantly maintained
options.E: They lack the firm's vetted office knowledge
options.F: They seldom follow MasterFormat numbers and titles

questions.explanation: Manufacturer-furnished guide specifications carry reliable product information, but they are written around the manufacturer's own products, so their proprietary language must be edited out for a competitively bid project. Containing far more than a project needs is the commercial master's drawback, going stale without upkeep is the office master's, and slow editing of non-applicable text is the previous project specification's.

questions.question: Which source of guide specifications is generally the most effective and efficient for an A/E firm?

options.A: Manufacturer-furnished guide specifications
options.B: A commercial master, used as published
options.C: A set pre-edited to the firm's main project types
options.D: The most recent similar project's specifications
options.E: The owner's guide specifications for the project
options.F: Text written from scratch for each project

questions.explanation: The most effective and efficient source is a set of specifications already edited to suit the firm's principal project types and requirements, so each project starts close to what it needs. Manufacturer-furnished, commercial, and previous-project sources each carry drawbacks, such as proprietary language, excess content, or text that must be stripped out, and writing from scratch every time gives up the benefit of prewritten text.

questions.question: Why does an office master list leave gaps in Level 3 and Level 4 section numbering?

options.A: Record the date of initial preparation and the latest revision of each section
options.B: Allow the later addition of other sections needed for a specific project
options.C: Distinguish edited sections from unedited sections for novice users
options.D: Reserve numbers for procurement and contracting documents in Division 00
options.E: Set the order of priority for completing incomplete or unedited sections
options.F: Leave room for a brief description of the related work in other sections

questions.explanation: The office master list assigns each section a MasterFormat number and title, leaving gaps in the Level 3 and Level 4 numbering so that sections a particular project needs can be added later in their proper place. Revision dates, development status, and the priority for finishing unedited sections are separate entries on the list, and Division 00 numbering has nothing to do with the gaps.

questions.question: An office master's Level 2 section would be too broad and unwieldy because it covers too many product types. What should the firm do?

options.A: Combine the work into a related Level 2 section
options.B: Write the whole division as one section
options.C: Write several Level 3 sections in its place
options.D: Use a single Level 4 section for all the products
options.E: Write it as a shortform Level 2 section instead
options.F: Postpone it until a project needs the section

questions.explanation: When a Level 2 section would cover too many product types or grow unwieldy, several narrower Level 3 sections can be written in its place. A single section for a whole division can work on small projects, but that makes the scope broader, not narrower, and neither a lone Level 4 section nor a shortform version fixes an over-broad scope.

questions.question: When an office master starts from a commercial master, a checklist of edited and unedited sections guards against what?

options.A: Conflicts between owner guide specifications and the firm's standard practice
options.B: Inconsistent revision identifiers between the specifications and the drawings
options.C: The permanent deletion of paragraphs that may be needed on future projects
options.D: Novices assuming that unedited sections are acceptable for use as-is
options.E: Outdated reference standards remaining in the commercial master's text
options.F: Duplicate sections or omitted sections in the office master list

questions.explanation: Starting an office master from a commercial master saves time, but the firm should keep a checklist showing which sections it has edited to suit its practice and which it has not, so that inexperienced staff do not assume an unedited section is ready to use. Outdated standards and missing or duplicate sections are real concerns, but they are handled by maintenance and by the master list, not by this checklist.

questions.question: Which statements about editing master guide specifications are correct?

options.A: In database masters, paragraphs that don't apply are unselected rather than deleted
options.B: In word-processor masters, paragraphs that don't apply are deleted unless track changes is on
options.C: Instructional notes should give direction, guidance and notice of required decisions
options.D: Cloud-based systems typically let the specifier edit the master sections in place
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: In word-processor masters, paragraphs and articles that do not apply are deleted unless track changes is on; in database masters they are never permanently deleted, only unselected. Instructional notes should give direction, guidance, and notice of the decisions the specifier must make. That makes {F} correct. Cloud-based systems typically do not let the specifier edit the master sections; selected sections are copied into a project file instead.

questions.question: A firm wants a shortform master for each of its common project types. From what is it best developed?

options.A: An expanded preliminary project description
options.B: A full-length master guide specification
options.C: Industry reference standards
options.D: Sections written from scratch
options.E: An existing project specification
options.F: The design development outline specifications

questions.explanation: A shortform specification can be produced several ways, such as building up a project description, revising another project's specification, working from reference standards, or writing from scratch, but the recommended way is to develop it from a full-length master guide specification. A separate shortform master can then be kept for each common project type, such as residential, light commercial, or tenant improvement.

questions.question: In a cloud-based master specification system, how is a project section created?

options.A: The specifier selects sections, and copies are added to a project file
options.B: The specifier exports the master to a word processor to edit offline
options.C: The system locks the project file until the AHJ approves the sections
options.D: The specifier edits the master in place, then restores it from a backup
options.E: The specifier unselects paragraphs directly in the cloud master sections
options.F: The system generates each section automatically from the BIM model

questions.explanation: Cloud-based master specification software typically does not allow the master sections themselves to be edited. The specifier selects the sections the project needs, and copies are added automatically to a project file, where they are edited while the master stays intact. Unselecting paragraphs is how a database master excludes content inside a section, not how a project section is created in the cloud.

questions.question: What final review is recommended before project specifications are distributed?

options.A: Confirm paragraphs carried from the master are unedited
options.B: Confirm each bidder has acknowledged every addendum
options.C: Have the AHJ stamp each section for code approval
options.D: Compare the project section text with the master text
options.E: Check each section against the outline specifications
options.F: Post the files to the project website for comment

questions.explanation: Before distribution, comparing each project section's text with the master text, or reviewing the changes tracked against the master, confirms that all applicable content was kept and unneeded content removed. Confirming that master paragraphs are unedited misses the point, since master text must be edited to suit the project, and addendum acknowledgments and AHJ review are separate steps.

questions.question: Which information never appears in project specifications, so it is kept out of the master text but must be retrievable from it?

options.A: Lists of acceptable manufacturers and their products named within the products article
options.B: Editing notes, instructional commentary, and option-handling guidance for the editing A/E
options.C: Detailed cost data and the actual wording of trade-association and referenced standards
options.D: Submittal requirements and quality-assurance provisions repeated from Division 01 sections
options.E: Color, pattern and texture choices that are too numerous to list as options in the master
options.F: Project-specific engineering design data that changes with each project's requirements

questions.explanation: Some information essential to specifying never appears in project specifications, notably detailed cost data and the full text of trade-association and other referenced standards. It is kept out of the master text, but the master system should let the specifier retrieve it quickly, for example through hyperlinks in the text or notes. Colors and project design data are also left out of the master, but they do appear in project specifications.

questions.question: Which statement correctly applies the definitions of project stakeholders and participants?

options.A: The owner is a participant, while architects, engineers, and suppliers are stakeholders
options.B: Only the contractor is a stakeholder; everyone else is a participant
options.C: The owner is a stakeholder, while architects, engineers, and suppliers are participants
options.D: Stakeholders and participants are interchangeable terms for all project team members
options.E: The owner and architect are stakeholders, while engineers and suppliers are participants
options.F: Stakeholders act in only a portion of the process; participants act in a major portion

questions.explanation: Stakeholders are actively involved in a major portion of project delivery and have an interest, such as investment, operations, or reputation, that the finished facility may affect; the owner is the typical stakeholder. Participants take part in only a portion of the process and have indirect interests, as architects, engineers, and suppliers do. The terms are not interchangeable, and the 'portion' distinction runs the other way.

questions.question: In the standard model of project delivery, the people on a project are organized into which four teams?

options.A: Owner Team, A/E Team, General Contractor Team, and Subcontractor Team
options.B: Owner Team, Design Team, Contractor Team, and Facility Management Team
options.C: Client Team, Design Team, Construction Team, and Vendor Team
options.D: Owner Team, Design Team, Contractor Team, and Supplier Team
options.E: Owner Team, Design Team, Contractor Team, and Consultant Team
options.F: Owner Team, Consultant Team, Contractor Team, and Supplier Team

questions.explanation: The people who plan, design, and build a project are organized into four teams, each unique to that project: the Owner Team, the Design Team, the Contractor Team, and the Supplier Team. Facility managers belong to the owner's side and consultants to the design team, so neither forms a separate team of its own.

questions.question: In the facility life cycle, which stage immediately follows design?

options.A: Construction
options.B: Project conception
options.C: Construction documents
options.D: Procurement
options.E: Facility management
options.F: Design development

questions.explanation: The facility life cycle runs from project conception to design, construction documents, procurement, construction, and facility management. Construction documents is a stage of its own, between design and procurement, in which the design is turned into the drawings and specifications needed for pricing, regulatory approvals, and construction. Design development is a phase within the design stage, not the next stage.

questions.question: How is a project distinguished from a facility?

options.A: Facility: buildings only; project: civil and infrastructure work
options.B: Project: the delivery process; facility: the completed entity
options.C: The terms are interchangeable once the building is occupied
options.D: Project: the completed entity; facility: the delivery process
options.E: Project: design and documents; facility: construction and use
options.F: Project: the owner's program; facility: the occupied building

questions.explanation: A project is the delivery process: planning, designing, procuring, contracting, and building a facility for its owner. The facility is the completed constructed entity, built for a specific purpose and function. Facility is a broad term that covers anything built, not only buildings, and the two terms do not become interchangeable once the building is occupied.

questions.question: Which format organizes preliminary project descriptions and early cost data by systems rather than products, and what is its Level 1 structure?

options.A: UniFormat, organized by functional elements A through G plus Z (General)
options.B: OmniClass Table 22, organized by procurement and contracting requirements
options.C: MasterFormat, organized into the 50 numbered divisions of work results
options.D: SectionFormat, organized by the three standard parts of a specification section
options.E: UniFormat, organized by work results in Divisions 00 through 49
options.F: MasterFormat, organized by functional elements A through G plus Z (General)

questions.explanation: UniFormat organizes construction information by functional elements, the systems and assemblies of a facility, described by what they do rather than by the products in them. Its Level 1 elements run from Element A, Substructure, through Element G, Building Sitework, plus Element Z, General, and they are used to arrange preliminary project descriptions and early cost estimates. MasterFormat organizes by work results in numbered divisions, and SectionFormat organizes the inside of a section.

questions.question: The architect resolved a locker/wall conflict in a written communication record, copied to the owner and contractor, stating that the resolution stands unless someone objects in writing within seven days. No one objected. The wall was later built where the original drawings showed it. Who is responsible?

options.A: The contractor, who received the recorded resolution
options.B: The specifier, whose section created the conflict
options.C: The owner, who approved the original drawings
options.D: The architect, who issued no change order
options.E: The architect and contractor, who share the blame
options.F: The owner, who was copied but did not object

questions.explanation: The architect documented the resolution in writing and distributed it, and since no one objected within the seven days the record allowed, the resolution stood. The contractor received it and still built the wall in the superseded location, so the responsibility is the contractor's. Had the architect not documented the resolution, the architect and the contractor would have shared the blame.

questions.question: An A/E project manager assigns document coordination to another team member. Who holds ultimate responsibility for coordinating the construction documents?

options.A: The assigned coordinator
options.B: The specifier preparing the project manual
options.C: The A/E's project manager
options.D: Each discipline lead for its own documents
options.E: The owner's project manager
options.F: The construction manager as advisor

questions.explanation: Ultimate responsibility for coordinating the construction documents rests with the A/E's project manager. The project manager may assign the coordination work to another design team member, who then reviews the drawings and the project manual for consistency, but handing off the task does not hand off the responsibility. The specifier, discipline leads, and owner contribute to coordination without owning it.

questions.question: When the design stage begins, the team meets on coordination procedures and prepares a preliminary project description or outline specification. That document is meant to serve as:

options.A: The final project manual table of contents
options.B: A coordination checklist
options.C: A precedence listing for bidding
options.D: A substitute for later coordination meetings
options.E: A basis-of-design product list
options.F: A list of catalog references

questions.explanation: At the first coordination meeting of the design stage, attended by the A/E, consultants, drafters, and specifier, a preliminary project description or outline specification is prepared to serve as a coordination checklist, and further meetings follow as the design progresses. It does not replace those meetings, fix the final table of contents, or act as a product list.

questions.question: Designers keep a list of catalog references instead of putting detailed product notes on drawings. How should the list be organized for the specifier?

options.A: By the design discipline that prepared each referenced detail
options.B: By an outline keyed to the project manual table of contents
options.C: Alphabetically by manufacturer name across all the disciplines
options.D: By the drawing sheet number on which each detail appears
options.E: By UniFormat element, matching the preliminary project description
options.F: By the status of each product decision reviewed with the team

questions.explanation: Rather than crowd the drawings with detailed product notes, designers can keep a list of the catalog references they used for particular products and equipment and send it to the specifier as an outline that follows the project manual's table of contents. The specifier can then check the relevant part while writing each section; sorting by sheet, discipline, or manufacturer would scatter one section's products across the list.

questions.question: An owner furnishes Division 01. What should the A/E do?

options.A: Replace the owner's sections with the A/E's own Division 01
options.B: Use the owner's Division 01 as is and add nothing
options.C: Move its procedural requirements into Divisions 02-49
options.D: Prepare added sections as needed for its own contract duties
options.E: Include the owner's Division 01 in the manual by reference only
options.F: Have each consultant write its own general requirements

questions.explanation: When the owner provides Division 01, the A/E keeps the owner's sections and prepares whatever additional sections it needs to carry out its own contractual responsibilities, coordinated with the owner's requirements and the rest of the project manual. Replacing the owner's sections, adding nothing, or moving procedural requirements into the technical sections would all break that coordination.

questions.question: A drawing is correct by itself but inconsistent with the specifications. This illustrates that:

options.A: The drawing should take precedence over the specifications
options.B: Checking documents is not the same as coordinating them
options.C: The level of specification detail is too high
options.D: Terminology control belongs to the contractor
options.E: A precedence listing should be added for bidding
options.F: Coordination is best left to the final check before issue

questions.explanation: Checking a document confirms it is correct in itself; coordinating compares the separate parts of the construction documents with one another. A drawing can pass a check and still conflict with the specifications, which is why coordination is a task of its own, started early with enough time. Making one document take precedence only decides which error wins; it does not remove the inconsistency.

questions.question: A drawing set's abbreviation list defines 'WT.' as both WEIGHT and WINDOW. Which of the following are recommended practices for the abbreviations?

options.A: Keep both meanings and rely on context on each sheet
options.B: Move the abbreviation list into the specifications
options.C: Make sure each abbreviation stands for only one item
options.D: Use an edited list tailored to the project, shown on the drawings
options.E: Abbreviate short words of five letters or less freely
options.F: Let each discipline keep its own meaning for the abbreviation

questions.explanation: Each abbreviation should stand for only one item, so WT. cannot mean both weight and window, and it should not mean something different on another discipline's drawings. The documents should carry an edited list of abbreviations tailored to the project, shown on the drawings rather than in the specifications. Abbreviations are best avoided altogether for short words of five letters or less.

questions.question: A roof curb detail calls for 'RIGID INSULATION.' Section 07 21 00 specifies extruded polystyrene, polyisocyanurate, and mineral-wool insulation. Which product does the detail require?

options.A: Polyisocyanurate, the only foil-faced board
options.B: Extruded polystyrene, the first product listed
options.C: Mineral wool, the only noncombustible product
options.D: Cannot be determined; the terms need coordinating
options.E: Any of the three, at the contractor's option
options.F: Polyisocyanurate, the board used in the roof assembly

questions.explanation: 'Rigid insulation' does not match any one of the three products the section specifies, so the drawing cannot tell anyone which one is required. Drawings and specifications should use the same terminology, so the note must be coordinated with the section and revised to use the section's term for the intended product. Picking the first-listed, foil-faced, or noncombustible product is a guess, not a requirement.

questions.question: The architect writes Section 07 84 13, Penetration Firestopping. The plumbing engineer wants to add Section 22 00 05, Firestopping for Plumbing. Best practice is to:

options.A: Coordinate all firestopping into the Division 07 section
options.B: Keep both so each discipline controls its own firestopping
options.C: Move all firestopping into Division 22
options.D: Keep both and add a precedence note to Division 01
options.E: Cover plumbing firestopping with notes on the plumbing drawings
options.F: Move all firestopping into Division 01 as a general requirement

questions.explanation: Two sections covering the same work, often in different ways, are exactly what early coordination policies should prevent. The plumbing engineer's firestopping requirements should be coordinated into the architect's Division 07 section, with one lead professional preparing it and the other disciplines reviewing the draft. Keeping both sections, even with a precedence note, would leave conflicting requirements in the documents.

questions.question: Why are deviations from the listed products in a fire-resistance-rated assembly generally not permitted?

options.A: Listed products carry a single-source manufacturer warranty
options.B: Prescriptive code tables assign the products for each rating
options.C: The fire marshal approves the product list at plan review
options.D: The rating depends on tests of those specific products together
options.E: The specifier is the sole decision-maker on rated products
options.F: The listed products are the project's basis-of-design products

questions.explanation: A fire-resistance rating comes from testing an assembly made of specifically listed products and materials. Swap one of those products and the tested rating no longer covers what is built, so deviations from the approved lists are generally not permitted and the specifier must make sure the specified products match the indicated tested assemblies. Prescriptive code requirements are a separate kind of product coordination.

questions.question: An owner-furnished article lists only 'soap dispenser, paper towel dispenser, toilet paper dispenser' for the contractor to install. Is that enough to bid?

options.A: Yes; owner-furnished items carry no installation cost
options.B: No; the products must be identified to price the installation
options.C: Yes; the drawing schedule shows the install method
options.D: No; only the manufacturer brand names are missing
options.E: Yes; the owner supplies the fasteners and backing
options.F: No; owner-furnished items need a separate contract

questions.explanation: To price the installation, the contractor has to know which products the owner will actually provide, because the products decide the labor, the type of fasteners, and any backing the walls need. Generic item names do not identify them, and the fix is to identify the actual products, which takes more than adding brand names. Installing owner-furnished items is still contract work with a cost.

questions.question: The owner keeps failing to give the contractor's required insurance limits and tells the architect to 'use whatever you usually use.' The architect should:

options.A: Use the limits from a similar project the architect did for another client
options.B: Leave the insurance limits out of the documents
options.C: Have the owner confirm limits with its counsel and insurance agent
options.D: Use the highest limits from the architect's past projects
options.E: Ask the contractor to propose limits with its bid
options.F: Set the limits from the architect's own judgment and note it

questions.explanation: Decisions on the types and amounts of insurance belong to the owner, made with its legal counsel and insurance adviser; the A/E should not act as an insurance adviser or set or recommend limits. The architect should ask the owner to confirm the limits with its counsel and insurance agent. Borrowing another client's limits, using the architect's own judgment, or leaving the limits out would each fail that rule.

questions.question: The owner's geotechnical report should be included or referenced in:

options.A: Division 01, as a general requirement
options.B: The agreement, as an attachment to it
options.C: Division 00, as available project information
options.D: The earthwork section, as a reference standard
options.E: Section 01 64 00, as owner-furnished information
options.F: The supplementary conditions, as a contract document

questions.explanation: The owner typically provides the geotechnical report, and since the A/E, its consultants, and the contractor all rely on it, it is included or referenced in Division 00 as available project information. It is information for bidders to use, not a Division 01 requirement, a reference standard in the earthwork section, or an attachment to the agreement.

questions.question: The owner has already signed a contract with its chosen contractor. After reviewing that contract and its conditions, the specifier may need to:

options.A: Rewrite the contract to match the office master Division 01
options.B: Have the contractor prepare Division 01
options.C: Replace the conditions with the A/E's standard forms
options.D: Revise Division 01 sections to conform to those documents
options.E: Prepare new procurement requirements for the contractor
options.F: Include the owner's contract by reference only

questions.explanation: The specifier should find out whether the owner already has a contract with a contractor, ask to review it and any conditions of the contract, and check who is preparing the procurement requirements. Some Division 01 sections may then need revising to conform to those documents, because the specifications adapt to the executed contract, not the other way around.

questions.question: An owner's design manual does not directly prescribe a product the project needs. The A/E should:

options.A: Follow the owner's process for approving products
options.B: Select it from the A/E's office master specification
options.C: Specify it by performance so no approval is needed
options.D: Leave the selection to the contractor's bid
options.E: Name a basis-of-design product and accept comparables
options.F: Apply the nearest prescriptive item in the design manual

questions.explanation: Owner design manuals may be performance-based or prescriptive, and some owners have a process for approving materials and products the manual does not directly prescribe. That process must be followed to prevent costly problems later; choosing from the office master, specifying by performance, or applying the nearest prescriptive item would all bypass the owner's approval.

questions.question: During bidding, a product representative complains to the owner that proprietary language was edited out of a section. Contacting the owner was:

options.A: Appropriate, because the owner funds the project
options.B: Inappropriate; the A/E is responsible for the specifications
options.C: Appropriate, since the rep wrote the guide specification
options.D: Inappropriate only on a publicly funded project
options.E: Appropriate, because bids had not yet been opened
options.F: Inappropriate; the contractor selects the products

questions.explanation: The A/E of record is responsible for the specifications, and it may edit a manufacturer's guide specification to remove proprietary language. A product representative with a concern about the specifications should take it to the architect, not go around the A/E to the owner, and that holds on private and public projects alike and whether or not bids have been opened.

questions.question: When the contractor is involved early in design, as with CMAR or IPD, which of the following apply?

options.A: The contractor is given precedence over the A/E in resolving conflicts
options.B: The contractor is asked to write the Division 01 sections
options.C: The contractor is included in the project manual coordinating group
options.D: The contractor is limited to reviewing the drawings
options.E: The contractor brings constructability and cost efficiencies to design
options.F: The contractor takes over coordinating the construction documents

questions.explanation: Early contractor involvement, as under CMAR or IPD, puts the contractor's skills to work during design to bring constructability and cost efficiencies, and a contractor involved that early should be part of the project manual coordinating group. The contractor does not take over coordinating the construction documents, which stays with the A/E's project manager, and it gains no precedence over the A/E.

questions.question: During design, a curtain wall installer provides framing and glazing calculations and installation details to help develop the documents. This is a:

options.A: Delegated design
options.B: Design-assist role
options.C: Value analysis proposal
options.D: Substitution request
options.E: Shop drawing submittal
options.F: Constructability review

questions.explanation: In a design-assist role, a subcontractor such as a curtain wall installer gives the design team its expertise on one element during design, for example calculations for framing and glazing sizes and installation details, to help develop the construction documents. Delegated design is different: it is design the contract documents require the contractor to provide during construction, and a shop drawing is a construction-phase submittal.

questions.question: On a multiple-prime project, which Division 01 section states which contractor installs each owner-furnished item?
questions.explanation: Section 01 12 00, Multiple Contract Summary, is used when the work is split among more than one contract; it defines each contract's extent, including the owner-furnished items to be installed and which contractor installs them. Section 01 11 00 summarizes a single contract, 01 31 00 assigns coordination duties among contractors, and 01 73 00 sets basic installation requirements, not who installs.

questions.question: For which of the following does the specifier coordinate mainly with the owner?

options.A: Verifying whether a contractor has been selected and a contract is in place
options.B: Identifying cost savings from alternative design or construction technology
options.C: Verifying who will prepare the procurement requirements
options.D: Coordinating terminology used on the drawings and in the specifications
options.E: Checking the status of outstanding product decisions
options.F: Verifying comparable products to ensure equitable specifications

questions.explanation: Two coordination checks are made with the owner: whether a contractor has already been selected and a contract is in place, so it and its conditions can be reviewed, and who will prepare the procurement requirements. Cost-saving alternatives and comparable products for equitable specifications are worked out with product representatives, and terminology and the status of product decisions with the A/E team.

questions.question: To identify cost savings from alternative design or construction technology, the specifier coordinates mainly with the:

options.A: Product representative
options.B: Consultants
options.C: Architect/engineer
options.D: Owner's facility staff
options.E: Commissioning agent
options.F: Security adviser

questions.explanation: During design, product representatives help the team find cost savings by proposing alternative design or construction technology that lowers cost without giving up quality or performance. They can also point out comparable competing products so sections stay equitable. Consultants and the A/E coordinate their own design work and terminology rather than supplying this product knowledge.

questions.question: Two designers pick interfacing products that turn out to be incompatible, and no one notices before construction. What gets built into the building is a(n):

options.A: Latent defect
options.B: Discrepancy
options.C: Omission
options.D: Nonconforming work
options.E: Duplication
options.F: Terminology difference

questions.explanation: When products chosen by different designers meet in the building but are not compatible, and nobody catches it before construction, a latent defect is built in: a hidden flaw that shows up later, such as an adhesive that gradually loses its bond. A discrepancy is conflicting information shown in two or more places in the documents, and an omission is something left out; here the documents can agree and still produce a defect.

questions.question: A specified air barrier adhesive may not keep its bond with the adjacent PVC roof membrane. Besides finding a compatible adhesive with the architect, the specifier should:

options.A: Leave both sections unchanged pending a field bond test
options.B: Route the issue to the contractor as a substitution request
options.C: Change the roofing from PVC to another membrane
options.D: Have the drawing note revised once a new adhesive is chosen
options.E: Add a note that the specifications govern over the drawings
options.F: Leave the adhesive choice to the installer's shop drawings

questions.explanation: Once the incompatibility is found, the specifier works with the architect to choose a more compatible adhesive and then has the drawing notation revised to match, so the drawings and specifications agree. Changing the roofing goes beyond fixing the problem, a field test or precedence note leaves the bad pairing in the documents, and a substitution request or shop drawing would push a design decision onto the contractor during construction.

questions.question: A UL fire-resistance design lists specific sprayed fire-resistive manufacturers. The specification's list adds Carboline, which the design does not name. Is a Carboline product acceptable for that assembly?

options.A: Yes, because the specification lists the manufacturer
options.B: No, because it is not listed in the tested design
options.C: Yes, if its hourly rating matches the design
options.D: No, because a rated assembly allows only one manufacturer
options.E: Yes, if the architect accepts it as a comparable product
options.F: Yes, because the specification governs over the UL design

questions.explanation: A rated assembly's fire rating covers only the products listed in its tested design. A manufacturer the design does not name has not been tested in that assembly, so its product does not comply even though the specification lists it; the mismatch between the specification and the design is a coordination error to correct. Matching the hourly rating or being accepted as comparable does not replace the listing.

questions.question: During construction, the contractor proposes a substitute fire-resistive product that is listed in a different tested assembly. What should the specifier do?

options.A: Reject it because the maker is not in the specified design
options.B: Approve it if the assembly gives the same rating
options.C: Refer it to the building official for a decision
options.D: Help the architect evaluate the proposed assembly
options.E: Issue an addendum adding the product to the list
options.F: Return it, since substitutions end once bidding closes

questions.explanation: A product listed in a different tested assembly may still be acceptable if that assembly as a whole meets the project's requirements, so the specifier helps the architect evaluate the proposed assembly. The specifier does not approve substitutions alone, and rejecting the product only because its maker is not in the specified design skips that evaluation. An addendum is a bidding-phase tool, not a way to handle a construction-phase substitution.

questions.question: Glazing for a climate zone 4 project is not yet selected, and the architect asks for language that meets the state energy code. The specifier should:

options.A: Require glazing to meet or exceed the energy code minimums
options.B: Require the architect to select a specific glazing product
options.C: State the maximum SHGC the code requires for that condition
options.D: Leave glazing performance for the contractor to determine
options.E: State the minimum SHGC the code requires for that condition
options.F: Cite the energy code glazing table in a drawing general note

questions.explanation: Specifications should state measurable requirements, so the specifier finds the energy code's limit for that climate zone and condition and writes it into the section, as a maximum solar heat gain coefficient such as 'SHGC no greater than 0.40.' SHGC limits are maximums, because a lower value admits less solar heat, so a minimum gets it backward. A general 'meet or exceed the code' clause leaves bidders to find the number, and no product choice is needed first.

questions.question: Which statements about coordination on a project issued in multiple packages are correct?

options.A: Changes made in earlier packages carry forward into later packages
options.B: A change in a later package is settled by a precedence statement
options.C: A change in a later package must be back-coordinated with earlier packages
options.D: Changes in later packages are deferred to change orders after award
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: When a project is issued in multiple packages, coordination between them is critical: changes made in earlier packages must be carried into later ones, and a change made in a later package must be back-coordinated with the earlier packages so the documents stay consistent. That makes {E} correct. A precedence statement does not resolve inconsistent documents, and coordination happens in the documents, not later by change order.

questions.question: Engineers add their own 'Submittal Procedures' sections to their divisions. Whoever prepares Division 01 should:

options.A: Let each division keep its own submittal procedures
options.B: Delete the engineers' sections without discussion
options.C: Fold their unique requirements into the Division 01 section
options.D: Move submittal procedures into the supplementary conditions
options.E: Add a note that Division 01 governs over their sections
options.F: Ask the owner to decide which procedures should apply

questions.explanation: Division 01 applies to all the other sections, and separate submittal procedures sections in each division often conflict with it. Whoever prepares Division 01 should find out what unique requirements led the engineers to write their own sections and work with them to fold those into the Division 01 section. Keeping both, or adding a note that Division 01 governs, leaves the conflict in place.

questions.question: An abatement consultant's section directs both the 'Abatement Contractor' and the 'window replacement contractor' to do parts of the work. Is this appropriate?

options.A: Yes, because it clarifies the interface between trades
options.B: Yes, if both contractors are named in the agreement
options.C: No; specifications address the contractor, who assigns the work
options.D: No, unless the owner self-performs the windows
options.E: No; only the drawings may assign work to particular trades
options.F: Yes, because the specification's organization sets trade scope

questions.explanation: Specifications are directed to the contractor, who alone decides how the work is divided among subcontractors and trades; under A201 §1.2.2, the way the specifications and drawings are organized does not control that division. A section that tells an 'Abatement Contractor' or a 'window replacement contractor' to do parts of the work assigns scope to trades, which neither the specifications nor the drawings should do.

questions.question: How is the contract sum adjusted to reflect the actual cost of a cash allowance?

options.A: By construction change directive
options.B: By field order
options.C: By change order
options.D: By addendum
options.E: By order for a minor change in the Work
options.F: By the final Certificate for Payment

questions.explanation: Under the standard general conditions, the difference between a cash allowance and the actual cost is settled by change order, which adjusts the contract sum; EJCDC C-700 calls for that change order before final payment. A construction change directive is for a change not yet agreed, a field order or minor change does not change the price, and an addendum is issued before the contract exists.

questions.question: When may a precedence listing among the contract documents be prepared?

options.A: For warranty enforcement after closeout
options.B: For bidding purposes only
options.C: When the owner furnishes the general conditions
options.D: On multiple-prime contracts only
options.E: For resolving conflicts during construction
options.F: When the project is issued in multiple packages

questions.explanation: Statements setting an order of precedence among the contract documents are not recommended, because the documents are complementary; the conditions should say only that the A/E makes a documented interpretation when the drawings and specifications conflict. If one is needed, a precedence listing may be prepared for bidding purposes only, never as the way to resolve conflicts during construction.

questions.question: An abatement article calls for a 'fine spray mist' until the material is 'sufficiently saturated, without causing excess dripping.' Is it clear how the contractor is to proceed?

options.A: Yes, because the article cites OSHA and NESHAP
options.B: Yes, because the spray equipment is specified
options.C: No, because the terms cannot be measured
options.D: No, because the asbestos material type is omitted
options.E: No, because it conflicts with the inventory sheets
options.F: Yes, because the contractor controls the means and methods

questions.explanation: 'Fine spray mist,' 'sufficiently saturated,' and 'excess dripping' cannot be measured, so neither the contractor nor the inspector can tell when the work complies. Citing OSHA and NESHAP or specifying the equipment does not cure vague execution language, and leaving it to the contractor's means and methods is not a requirement at all; the article needs measurable terms.

questions.question: In an abatement section, 3.01 says to remove all ACM shown on the material inventory sheets and floor plans. 3.02 says to remove Transite panels 'where specified on the approved plans and specifications.' These statements are:

options.A: In conflict, because they point to different sources
options.B: Complementary, since one sets scope and one sets method
options.C: Redundant, so 3.02 should be deleted
options.D: Complementary, since both rely on the floor plans
options.E: Vague, since neither statement can be measured
options.F: Acceptable, since the more specific 3.02 governs

questions.explanation: The two articles point to different sources for the same scope: one ties removal to the material inventory sheets and floor plans, the other to the 'approved plans and specifications.' A reader cannot tell which source controls, so the statements conflict and should be rewritten to point to one source. They are not redundant, since they do not say the same thing, and being more specific does not make one govern.

questions.question: A demolition section directs the contractor to remove hazardous materials as described in Document 00 31 26, Existing Hazardous Material Information. Why is that inappropriate?

options.A: The demolition section supersedes Division 00
options.B: Division 00 documents cannot govern Division 02 work
options.C: Abatement must be priced as an allowance
options.D: It is information for bidders, not a contract document
options.E: The hazardous material report must be attached to the agreement
options.F: Hazardous material data belongs in Document 00 31 19 instead

questions.explanation: Document 00 31 26 passes the owner's information to bidders for their convenience, and it states that it is not part of the contract documents. A reference to it therefore cannot make abatement part of the contract work; the removal requirements belong in remediation sections of the specifications, such as asbestos or lead remediation in Division 02.

questions.question: Which statements about liquidated damages are correct?

options.A: They are usually deducted for failure to substantially complete the work on time
options.B: An excessive amount not based on financial loss may be an unenforceable penalty
options.C: They are useful because actual damages are easy to calculate after the delay
options.D: They are recalculated to equal the owner's actual loss once it is known
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: Liquidated damages are usually deducted from money due the contractor when it fails to reach substantial completion within the stated time, and an excessive or arbitrary amount not based on financial loss may be treated as a penalty and become unenforceable, so {E} is correct. They exist because actual damages are hard to determine precisely after a delay, so the amount is agreed in advance and not recalculated to the actual loss.

questions.question: A contract sets liquidated damages at $750 per calendar day. Substantial completion was due April 10 and was achieved April 25, with damages running the day after the deadline through the date achieved. The amount assessed is:
questions.explanation: Damages run from April 11, the day after the deadline, through April 25, the day substantial completion was achieved: 15 days counted inclusively, and 15 x $750 = $11,250. Starting the count on April 10 gives 16 days ($12,000), and stopping at April 24 gives 14 days ($10,500).

questions.question: An invitation to bid requires performance and payment bonds, each for 100 percent of the contract price, and says nothing else about bonds. For a $4 million bid, what bid security must accompany the bid?

options.A: $4 million
options.B: $8 million
options.D: None

questions.explanation: Performance and payment bonds secure the contract after award: one backs completion of the work, the other payment of subcontractors and suppliers. Bid security is a separate requirement, and since this invitation asks for no bid bond or other bid security, none has to accompany the bid. Amounts such as 5 or 10 percent of the bid apply only when the documents call for bid security.

questions.question: A pre-bid meeting notice states that attendance is mandatory for prime bidders who intend to submit a bid. Must a tile subcontractor who will bid to the primes attend?

options.A: Yes, like all interested bidders
options.B: No, it applies only to prime bidders
options.C: Yes, if no prime will cover the tile scope
options.D: No, unless the meeting is held on site
options.E: Yes, if it bids to more than one prime
options.F: No, unless a prime names it on its bid form

questions.explanation: The mandatory attendance applies only to prime bidders, the firms bidding directly to the owner. A tile subcontractor bidding to the primes is not a prime bidder, so it may attend but is not required to, whether or not it bids to several primes, the meeting is on site, or a prime names it on its bid.

questions.question: Section 01 21 00 lists the costs an allowance does NOT cover, such as installation, overhead, and profit, so that those costs are:

options.A: Included in the contract sum
options.B: Deducted from the allowance at closeout
options.C: Priced as unit prices on the bid form
options.D: Paid from the owner's contingency
options.E: Added by change order when the allowance is adjusted
options.F: Billed separately at the contractor's standard rates

questions.explanation: Section 01 21 00 identifies what each allowance covers, such as the product's cost and taxes, and also the costs it does not cover, such as handling at the site, installation, overhead, and profit. Naming the excluded costs makes sure bidders carry them in the contract sum, so they are not taken out of the allowance, added later by change order, or billed separately.

questions.question: A tenant corridor entrance is fully specified, but the number to be installed is not yet known. In Division 01 this is best handled as:

options.A: A cash allowance (01 21 13)
options.B: A quantity allowance (01 21 29)
options.C: A contingency allowance (01 21 16)
options.D: An alternate (01 23 00)
options.E: A product allowance (01 21 26)
options.F: A time allowance (01 21 43)

questions.explanation: When an item is fully specified but the number needed is unknown, a quantity allowance states an estimated quantity for equitable bidding, and unit prices adjust the contract sum to the actual quantity installed. A cash allowance carries a dollar amount for an item whose selection has not been made, a contingency allowance covers unforeseen costs, and an alternate prices a change in scope.

questions.question: Earthwork paid by unit price is usually measured in which of the following ways?

options.A: Measured in the finished work
options.B: Measured by truckload as it is hauled
options.C: Measured as loose volume when stockpiled
options.D: Measured separately as excavate, stockpile, and place quantities
options.E: Measured from the estimated quantity on the bid form
options.F: Measured at the borrow pit
