Between them there is only an administrative relationship, not an implied or direct contract.

questions.question: Why is CMAR increasingly acceptable for public work despite the constructor's early design involvement?

options.A: Public competitive-bidding laws are fully waived the moment any construction manager is retained
options.B: The CM competed to become the CMAR and subcontractors competed for work, preserving competition
options.C: The CMAR contractually guarantees the absolute lowest first cost obtainable on every subcontract
options.D: The architect/engineer assumes the construction risk, so the public agency carries none of it
options.E: The public owner itself awards every trade subcontract after a public low-bid opening
options.F: The CMAR's guaranteed maximum price is fixed before any design work has begun

questions.explanation: CMAR keeps the spirit of competition: the construction manager competed to be selected, and the subcontractors compete for the trade work, so the public agency still meets its duty to spend taxpayer money with care. Public bidding laws are not simply waived, and the CMAR's guaranteed maximum price comes once design is well along, not before it starts.

questions.question: Negotiated design-bid-build contracts are rarely used for publicly funded projects mainly because:

options.A: Public owners rarely have staff able to negotiate
options.B: Negotiated contracts cannot include a GMP
options.C: Bidding laws bar starting before the final cost is known
options.D: The A/E cannot administer a negotiated public contract
options.E: Negotiation is allowed only when many bidders qualify
options.F: Negotiated contracts suit only renovation or remodeling

questions.explanation: Public competitive bidding laws exist to protect the public interest, and they do not let construction start before the final construction cost is known, which a negotiated contract would allow. An exception may be made when a project is so complex that only a few bidders are qualified, not when many qualify.

questions.question: Which statement best captures how integrated project delivery (IPD) manages risk, distinct from traditional methods?

options.A: The owner retains essentially all risk and indemnifies the other parties
options.B: A multi-party agreement focuses risk management at the project level
options.C: Risk is allocated to each participant so each bears only its own scope
options.D: Risk is transferred to a surety through a three-party guaranty bond set
options.E: The constructor carries cost risk above a not-to-exceed GMP it proposes
options.F: Risk is held by a single-purpose entity that owns the project's assets

questions.explanation: In IPD the owner, A/E and contractor sign a multi-party agreement that manages risk for the project as a whole rather than for each participant, supported by a no-blame approach, waivers of claims against one another, and risk and reward shared according to the project outcome. Allocating risk so that each party bears only its own scope is the traditional approach that IPD moves away from.

questions.question: The MacLeamy Curve is most often cited to support which premise underlying IPD?

options.A: Design decisions should shift earlier, when impact is high and change cost low
options.B: Construction waste can be minimized only by extending the construction time
options.C: The cost of design changes reaches its lowest point during construction
options.D: The architect/engineer's fee should be weighted toward construction administration
options.E: Design effort should stay concentrated in the construction documents phase
options.F: Design decisions should be deferred until bids confirm the construction cost

questions.explanation: The MacLeamy Curve shows the ability to affect cost and function is greatest early in design and falls over time, while the cost of design changes keeps rising, so design decisions should be moved as early as possible. IPD builds on that by involving the key participants early; concentrating effort in construction documents or waiting for bids does the opposite.

questions.question: Which statements about a single-purpose entity (SPE) created for a construction project are correct?

options.A: It has no assets of its own
options.B: It is dissolved when the project is completed
options.C: It can be used for design-build and IPD
options.D: It holds legal title to the project property
options.E: {A}, {B} and {C}
options.F: Both {A} and {B}

questions.explanation: An SPE formed for a construction project is created for that project and dissolved when it is complete, and unlike a real estate SPE it holds no assets of its own; it can be used for design-build or integrated project delivery, so {E} is right. Holding title to a property describes a real estate SPE, not a construction one.

questions.question: An IPD single-purpose entity typically involves which membership, distinguishing it from a design-build SPE?

options.A: Only the contractor and the architect/engineer serving as its owner-managers
options.B: The owner paired with a surety acting as the guarantor of all performance
options.C: A tri-party agreement among owner, contractor, and architect/engineer
options.D: The owner acting alone, who later assigns membership to selected subs
options.E: Consultants and subcontractors only, with the owner kept outside it
options.F: The owner and contractor, with the architect/engineer as their consultant

questions.explanation: An SPE for integrated project delivery usually rests on a tri-party agreement among the owner, contractor and A/E, and consultants and subcontractors may also join. A design-build SPE, like a design-build joint venture, usually has only the contractor and the A/E as its owners or managers.

questions.question: Under the CM-Agent method, which statements about the construction manager's position are correct?

options.A: It guarantees and is directly responsible for delays and cost overruns
options.B: It acts as the owner's agent, with authority defined by the owner agreement
options.C: It enters into agreements only with the owner, not with any contractors
options.D: It makes and renders decisions binding on the owner within delegated limits
options.E: {B}, {C} and {D}
options.F: Both {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: A CM-Agent acts as the owner's agent with authority set by its agreement with the owner, can make decisions that bind the owner within that authority, and contracts only with the owner, not with contractors or suppliers, so {E} is right. It carries no guarantee and no direct responsibility for schedule delays, cost overruns or construction defects.

questions.question: In design-build delivery, the owner's single-point responsibility comes at the cost of which trade-off relative to design-bid-build?

options.A: The owner gains an enforceable contractual relationship directly between the A/E and contractor
options.B: The owner must personally coordinate among several separate prime construction contracts
options.C: The owner gives up the independent A/E whose design loyalty in DBB runs solely to the owner
options.D: The owner forfeits any ability to use a guaranteed maximum price on the construction work
options.E: The owner takes on the liability for design errors and omissions found during construction
options.F: The owner must sign a multi-party agreement that shares project risk and reward with all

questions.explanation: In design-bid-build the owner hires an independent A/E whose duty runs to the owner. In design-build the A/E works for the design-builder, so the owner loses that direct relationship and independent advocate, which some owners replace by hiring their own A/E as a representative. Coordinating several prime contracts is a multiple-prime burden, not a design-build one.

questions.question: Which arrangement lets a contractor give design-assist services and present a GMP before the documents are complete?

options.A: Design-bid-build, competitive bid option
options.B: Design-bid-build, competitive proposal option
options.C: Design-bid-build, negotiation option
options.D: Owner-build with multiple prime contracts
options.E: CM as advisor with multiple prime contracts
options.F: Owner-build using the owner's own forces

questions.explanation: Under the negotiation option of design-bid-build, the owner selects a contractor early; the contractor works with the A/E during design, may give design-assist services, prices incomplete documents and submits a GMP. Under the competitive bid and competitive proposal options the A/E completes the documents before pricing, so there is no contractor input during design.

questions.question: A design-bid-build project switches from the competitive bid option to the competitive proposal option. How does Division 00 most accurately change?

options.A: Equivalent proposal forms and documents replace the bidding forms and documents
options.B: Many of the forms and documents in the procurement requirements become needless
options.C: Division 00 does not change in any significant way under these circumstances
options.D: Division 00 is replaced entirely by the Division 01 general-requirements set
options.E: The negotiating contractor prepares the contracting forms, bonds and certificates
options.F: The conditions of the contract are left out until the final price is negotiated

questions.explanation: Moving from competitive bids to competitive proposals changes Division 00 mainly by swapping the bidding forms and documents for matching proposal forms and documents, such as a request for proposals, instructions to proposers and a proposal form. Dropping many procurement forms is what happens under the negotiated option, not the proposal option.

questions.question: Under the design-bid-build competitive proposal option, after a proposer is selected, may the owner and contractor negotiate the contract's final price?

options.A: No, the proposed price becomes the fixed contract sum and may not afterward be negotiated
options.B: Yes, the owner and the selected contractor may negotiate the final price after selection
options.C: No, applicable public-bidding law forbids any negotiation once a proposer is selected
options.D: Only the architect/engineer, not the owner, may negotiate the final price after selection
options.E: No, price negotiation belongs only to the negotiated option of design-bid-build
options.F: Only when the proposal was priced as a guaranteed maximum price (GMP) agreement

questions.explanation: The competitive proposal option picks the proposal that best serves the owner rather than the lowest price, and once a proposer is chosen the two parties can still bargain over the final price. Negotiation is therefore not reserved for the negotiated option or for GMP proposals, and the A/E does not negotiate in the owner's place.

questions.question: For a CMAR project, which statements about project-manual preparation, compared with traditional design-bid-build, are correct?

options.A: Decisions normally the A/E's alone may be shared with the owner and the CM
options.B: The CM, not the A/E, prepares the procurement documents for its subcontracts
options.C: Conditions of the contract are omitted, being established before the manual
options.D: Division 00 calls for more A/E preparation effort than it does under DBB
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: On CMAR projects, decisions that would normally be the A/E's alone are often shared with the owner and construction manager, and the CM, not the A/E, prepares the procurement documents for its subcontracts, so {E} is right. The general conditions are set before the manual is prepared but are still included because subcontractors are bound by them, and Division 00 takes little A/E effort.

questions.question: For a design-build project, who prepares the procurement and contracting requirements used to obtain bids from the trades?

options.A: The owner, who issues the procurement requirements directly to the trade bidders
options.B: The authority having jurisdiction, as part of its review of the procurement package
options.C: The design-builder, who controls both the design and the construction procurement
options.D: A specifier the owner engages separately to prepare procurement requirements
options.E: A general contractor the owner hires separately once the design is complete
options.F: A construction manager, who issues a procurement package for each subcontract

questions.explanation: On a design-build project the owner prepares the procurement requirements used to select the design-builder, but the design-builder prepares the procurement and contracting requirements, including instructions to bidders, for getting bids or proposals from its subcontractors. A construction manager does this on CMAR projects, not on design-build.

questions.question: On an owner-build project, are procurement requirements still developed?

options.A: No, because the owner's own forces build the project
options.B: Yes, depending on what contractors will perform
options.C: No, because the A/E acts as the design-builder
options.D: Yes, the same set that design-bid-build requires
options.E: Yes, but only for multiple-prime contracts
options.F: No, the owner's purchase orders replace them

questions.explanation: Procurement requirements for an owner-build project vary with what the owner's own forces will do and what is bought from contractors; they are developed much as for other methods, and the owner may write its own for specialty contractor packages. So they are still needed wherever work is contracted out, though not necessarily the full design-bid-build set.

questions.question: In most standard owner/design-builder agreements, how are the conditions of the contract handled?

options.A: They are issued as stand-alone documents bound into Division 00 of the manual
options.B: They are omitted entirely, since design-build requires no general conditions
options.C: They are prepared by the architect/engineer apart from the design-builder
options.D: They are incorporated into the agreement, so they do not appear separately
options.E: They are written as two separate sets, one for each phase of the agreement
options.F: They are bound into Division 01 as the project's administrative requirements

questions.explanation: Most standard owner/design-builder agreements, such as those from AIA, EJCDC, DBIA and ConsensusDocs, build the conditions of the contract into the agreement form itself, so no separate general conditions appear. These agreements are often written in two phases, preliminary design and documents/construction, but that does not create two sets of conditions.

questions.question: Which statements about Division 01 on an IPD project issued in multiple work packages are correct?

options.A: It may be issued once as a stand-alone package that later packages reference
options.B: A revision to it can be issued with a later work package
options.C: It must be published again with each work package
options.D: IPD projects are not subject to Division 01 requirements
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: Both {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: IPD specifications follow the same Division 01 requirements as other methods. When work is issued in several packages, Division 01 can be issued once as a stand-alone package that the later packages reference, so it need not be republished each time, and any revision it needs can go out with a later package; {E} is right.

questions.question: Seven exit-device models are evaluated for a school gymnasium. Only Model 2 and Model 4 fit the doors and meet the required 5-lb maximum operating force, and both are hurricane rated. Model 3 is hurricane rated but needs more than 5 lb to operate. If a hurricane rating is also required, how many models comply?

options.A: One
options.B: None
options.C: Two
options.D: Three, adding Model 3
options.E: Four
options.F: Five

questions.explanation: Adding a requirement can only keep the set of compliant models the same or shrink it. Model 3's hurricane rating does not help, because it still fails the 5-lb operating-force limit, and the two models that already complied are both hurricane rated, so two models still comply.

questions.question: As a general principle of product-evaluation counting, adding one more required criterion to an evaluation matrix has which possible effect on the number of compliant products?

options.A: It has no effect on the number of compliant products under any circumstances
options.B: It can only hold the count steady or decrease it; it can never increase it
options.C: It always lowers the count by at least one product
options.D: It can only increase the count, since more criteria capture more candidates
options.E: It can hold the count steady, decrease it, or increase it
options.F: It always lowers the count unless the owner waives the criterion

questions.explanation: Each added required criterion is one more test a product must pass: products that already failed stay out, and some that passed may now fail. The number of compliant products can therefore stay the same or drop, but it can never rise, and it drops only if a product that qualified fails the new test.

questions.question: A state's adopted accessibility requirements limit the operating force of panic hardware to 5 lb, while the model code allows up to 15 lb. Why does the 5-lb limit govern?

options.A: Local codes always take precedence over ICC codes
options.B: The ICC limit does not apply to educational buildings
options.C: The 5-lb limit is the more stringent one
options.D: The architect chose it to meet the owner's accessibility goals
options.E: The ICC limit applies only to doors in hazardous areas
options.F: The 5-lb limit is the more recently adopted one

questions.explanation: When two applicable requirements differ, the project must satisfy both, so the more stringent 5-lb limit controls; hardware that operates at 5 lb also meets a 15-lb limit. Local codes do not automatically override model-code requirements, and the choice is not left to the architect's discretion.

questions.question: Which of the following are major product-selection considerations for an indoor swimming pool room?

options.A: Noise control
options.B: Resistance to fading
options.C: Humidity control
options.D: Safety
options.E: {A}, {C} and {D}
options.F: Both {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: An indoor pool room combines constant moisture, hard reflective surfaces and wet floors, so humidity control, noise control and safety all drive product choices there, which makes {E} right. Resistance to fading matters where sunlight strikes finishes and is not one of the major concerns for a pool room.

questions.question: What is the most important product-selection consideration for a sauna?

options.A: Sunlight
options.B: Humidity control
options.C: Lighting
options.D: Noise control
options.E: Resistance to fading
options.F: Infection prevention and control

questions.explanation: A sauna's intense heat and moisture break down materials that are not made for that environment, so humidity control is the most important consideration in choosing its products. Lighting, noise, sunlight and fading are minor issues in a small enclosed hot room, and infection control drives choices in health care spaces.

questions.question: In a weight room, which building element is the most important product-selection consideration?

options.A: Ceiling
options.B: Windows
options.C: Flooring
options.D: Wall paint
options.E: Lighting
options.F: Acoustical wall panels

questions.explanation: In a weight room the flooring matters most, because weights are often dropped rather than set down, putting heavy impact loads on the floor; durability matters most for materials that take a lot of wear. Ceilings, windows, paint and lighting are chosen much as in other rooms, and acoustical panels help with noise but not with impact.

questions.question: In a hospital, which interior product strategy supports infection prevention and control?

options.A: Hard surfaces where touched often, for cleaning
options.B: Ultraviolet window tints along busy corridors
options.C: Sound-absorbing surfaces in high-touch areas
options.D: Acoustical batts and high-performance glazing
options.E: Insulation meeting the code's minimum R-values
options.F: Soft acoustical wall panels in patient areas

questions.explanation: Because infection control is critical in hospitals, hard surfaces should be used where people touch surfaces often, so they can be cleaned frequently. Ultraviolet window tints address fading, sound-absorbing surfaces, acoustical batts and high-performance glazing address noise, and insulation R-values address energy use and comfort.

questions.question: Where wall finishes and floor coverings risk fading from sunlight through windows, the recommended product strategy is to:

options.A: Specify hard, easily cleaned surfaces throughout the sunlight-exposed locations
options.B: Specify acoustical batts within the exterior walls of the sunlit areas
options.C: Specify single monolithic glazing to admit more daylight to those areas
options.D: Specify ultraviolet window tints where sunlight may fade the finishes
options.E: Specify soft, sound-absorbing surfaces for the walls of the sunlit areas
options.F: Specify envelope insulation to the code's minimum R-values in those areas

questions.explanation: Where sunlight through windows may fade wall finishes and floor coverings, ultraviolet window tints are the recommended product strategy. Hard, cleanable surfaces serve infection control, acoustical batts and soft surfaces serve noise control, and insulation R-values serve energy use and comfort, none of which stops fading.

questions.question: What can happen when an interior product is not suited to the building's interior climate?

options.A: It deteriorates and shortens the building's useful life
options.B: It voids the manufacturer's warranty automatically
options.C: It fails the code's energy provisions
options.D: It must be replaced through a substitution request
options.E: It must be corrected within the one-year correction period
options.F: It loses its third-party code compliance listing

questions.explanation: A product that does not suit the interior climate can deteriorate and shorten the useful life of the building, so the A/E should check durability under interior conditions, especially for heavily worn materials such as flooring. Warranties, code listings and correction periods do not change how the material holds up in that environment.

questions.question: A two-story office building near the Gulf Coast will have brick masonry and glass walls on cold-formed metal framing and a low-slope roof. What should be the contractor's first sequencing priority?

options.A: Construct the brick masonry exterior walls fully before any roofing is set
options.B: Perform some activities out of sequence to finish the project as fast as possible
options.C: Finish the second-floor mechanical and electrical work before any roofing
options.D: Get framing, sheathing, and roof membrane in place to dry-in for interior work
options.E: Set the glass in the exterior walls before any of the framing is erected
options.F: Start first-floor interior finishes before the roof membrane is installed

questions.explanation: The first priority is to get the building dried-in, with the framing up, the sheathing on and the roof membrane down at the earliest point the schedule permits, so interior work can start out of the weather. Building out the masonry or finishing overhead mechanical work before roofing delays dry-in, and starting finishes before the roof is on exposes them to damage.

questions.question: For a two-story office building near the Gulf Coast in the southeastern United States, which considerations are necessary for product selection?

options.A: Severity of the winter months
options.B: Risk of storm surges
options.C: Hurricanes
options.D: Both {B} and {C}
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: A Gulf Coast site is exposed to hurricanes and to the risk of storm surge, and both bear directly on product choices for the walls and roof, so {D} is right. Winters there are mild, so the severity of the winter months is not a necessary consideration for this building.

questions.question: Which group lists only exterior conditions to assess when choosing products for the site?

options.A: Groundwater levels, seismic activity, risk of storm surges
options.B: Humidity control, safety, resistance to wear
options.C: Weather severity, sunlight through windows, noise control
options.D: Proximity to water, infection control, ventilation
options.E: Hurricanes, groundwater levels, resistance to fading
options.F: Regional cultural conditions, product durability, lighting

questions.explanation: Exterior conditions include weather severity, major weather events such as hurricanes, groundwater levels, seismic activity, nearness to water, storm-surge risk, product durability and regional cultural and aesthetic conditions. Humidity control, safety, wear, sunlight through windows, noise, infection control, ventilation, lighting and fading are interior conditions, and every other group includes at least one of them.

questions.question: Building a southwestern-style stucco, flat-roof house in the Midwest ignores which factors?

options.A: Interior climate conditions
options.B: Code-required energy and insulation provisions
options.C: The colder regional climate
options.D: Constructability and sequencing
options.E: Regional seismic activity and groundwater levels
options.F: Local cultural and aesthetic conditions

questions.explanation: Materials and methods have to suit the local climate and fit regional and local cultural and aesthetic conditions. A stucco, flat-roofed house common in the Southwest ignores the Midwest's colder climate and its building traditions, where wood framing, vinyl siding and pitched roofs are the norm. Seismic activity and groundwater are real exterior conditions, but this example does not turn on them.

questions.question: In law, how does a guaranty differ from a warranty?

options.A: A guaranty covers products, a warranty covers workmanship
options.B: A guaranty is the principal's promise, a warranty a third party's
options.C: A guaranty is a third party's promise, a warranty the principal's
options.D: A guaranty lasts one year, a warranty lasts longer
options.E: A guaranty covers wear and tear, a warranty covers defects
options.F: A guaranty is implied by law, a warranty must be written

questions.explanation: In legal usage, a guaranty is a separate contract in which a third party, much like a surety, takes on responsibility if the principal fails to perform, while a warranty is the principal's own promise to take on stated responsibilities for its work. The pairing that makes the guaranty the principal's promise reverses the two.

questions.question: A manufacturer warrants its roofing material. Using the legal meanings of the terms, what does the contractor provide for the same roof?

options.A: A warranty of the materials and a guaranty of its workmanship
options.B: A guaranty of the materials and a warranty of its workmanship
options.C: A warranty of both the materials and its workmanship
options.D: A guaranty of both the materials and its workmanship
options.E: A warranty of its workmanship only, not of the materials
options.F: A guaranty of the materials only, not of its workmanship

questions.explanation: A party warrants its own product or work and guarantees someone else's. The manufacturer warrants the roofing material it makes, so the contractor gives a third-party guaranty for that same material and a warranty for its own workmanship in installing it.

questions.question: Warranties specified for materials and equipment run in what relationship to the contractor's general warranty and the correction period?

options.A: They begin only after the one-year correction period ends
options.B: They replace the general warranty for those items
options.C: They are in addition to it and run concurrently
options.D: They are valid only if the general warranty is waived
options.E: They begin at final completion, after the general warranty
options.F: They supersede the correction period for those items

questions.explanation: Warranties specified for particular materials and equipment add to the contractor's general warranty and to the contract's correction-period obligations, and they run at the same time as them. They do not replace or supersede those obligations, and they do not wait for the one-year correction period to end before starting.

questions.question: Which statements about the one-year correction period in standard general conditions are correct?

options.A: It is a specific contractor obligation and an owner remedy
options.B: It is not intended to limit other warranties in the contract
options.C: It sets the time limit on the contractor's general warranty
options.D: Manufacturers' warranties are usually as broad as it is
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: The one-year correction period is a specific contractual duty of the contractor and a remedy for the owner, and it is not meant to limit other warranties in the contract, so {E} is right. The standard general warranty has no stated time limit, and a manufacturer's warranty as broad as the contractor's correction-period duties is practically impossible to get.

questions.question: Regarding time limitation, which statements about the warranty provisions in standard AIA, EJCDC, and ConsensusDocs general conditions are correct?

options.A: The general warranty is always limited to exactly one year, as in FAR contracts
options.B: The general warranty carries a fixed two-year time limit in each of these docs
options.C: None of these documents states a time limit for the general warranty
options.D: The general warranty expires automatically on the date of substantial completion
options.E: The time limit varies with the project's location and the governing law
options.F: The general warranty lasts as long as the extended warranties in PART 1

questions.explanation: The general warranties in AIA, EJCDC and ConsensusDocs general conditions state no time limit; how long the contractor stays liable depends on where the project is and on the law governing the contract. Federal contracts using FAR warranty language are the exception that caps the warranty at one year, and extended warranties must be specified separately in PART 1.

questions.question: A federal construction contract using FAR warranty language differs from standard private general conditions in that it:

options.A: Actually limits the contractor's warranty obligations to a period of just one year
options.B: Requires a third-party guarantor to stand behind all of the project's installed materials
options.C: Eliminates the contractual correction period that the private general conditions provide
options.D: Imposes an unlimited contractor warranty obligation that never expires by its terms
options.E: Makes it unnecessary to specify extended product warranties in PART 1 of each section
options.F: Excludes defects caused by improper maintenance, which the private conditions cover

questions.explanation: Federal construction contracts that use the Federal Acquisition Regulation's warranty language actually limit the contractor's warranty obligations to one year. Standard AIA, EJCDC and ConsensusDocs general conditions, by contrast, state no time limit for the contractor's general warranty; how long it lasts depends on the governing law.

questions.question: In warranty terms, the key difference between an exclusion and a condition is that:

options.A: An exclusion makes the warranty effective, whereas a condition merely limits its scope
options.B: A condition applies only to product warranties and an exclusion only to construction ones
options.C: The two terms are legally identical and may be used interchangeably without any effect
options.D: An exclusion limits applicability, while a condition must be met or the warranty is void
options.E: An exclusion is imposed by the UCC, while a condition is written in by the A/E
options.F: A condition limits the warranty's duration, while an exclusion limits its remedies

questions.explanation: An exclusion narrows what a warranty covers, while a condition is something that must be satisfied for the warranty to take effect at all; if it is not met, the warranty is void. The difference matters because an unmet condition can cancel coverage even for failures that have nothing to do with it.

questions.question: A roofing warranty lists proper use and adequate maintenance as conditions rather than exclusions. The practical risk to the owner is that:

options.A: The manufacturer becomes obligated to repair even a roof that was never kept up
options.B: The stated condition automatically extends the roofing warranty by one full year
options.C: The stated condition converts the manufacturer's warranty into a surety guaranty
options.D: The manufacturer may disclaim liability even when failure is unrelated to it
options.E: The manufacturer may disclaim only those failures caused by poor maintenance
options.F: The warranty becomes enforceable only by the original purchaser of the roof

questions.explanation: When proper use and adequate maintenance are written as conditions instead of exclusions, failing either one can void the warranty, so the manufacturer may refuse a claim even when the roof failed for reasons unrelated to use or maintenance. Written as exclusions, they would only remove failures actually caused by misuse or poor upkeep.

questions.question: When a reference standard's workmanship statements duplicate but differ in wording from the conditions of the contract or Division 01, the most reliable A/E response is to:

options.A: Rely on a blanket most-stringent-shall-apply clause to handle every conflict
options.B: Identify the duplications and modify the references to remove the conflicts
options.C: Leave the apparent conflict for the contractor to resolve in the field later
options.D: Delete Division 01 from the manual to avoid any overlap with the standard
options.E: State that the general conditions govern over any referenced standard
options.F: Cite only the standard's number, so its workmanship statements do not apply

questions.explanation: When a referenced standard repeats workmanship or administrative requirements in words that differ from the conditions of the contract or Division 01, those statements become part of the specifications and can conflict. The A/E should find the duplications and modify the references to remove the conflicts; a blanket 'more stringent requirement governs' clause cannot be relied on to settle every one.

questions.question: Which of the following are reasons a manufacturer's limited warranty often gives owners less protection than they expect?

options.A: It cuts the rights a full warranty would give
options.B: It starts only when the contractor's warranty ends
options.C: It must be negotiated anew for every project
options.D: It shifts liability for defects to the installer
options.E: It can exclude labor and consequential damages
options.F: It begins only at substantial completion

questions.explanation: Most product warranties are limited warranties, which take away rights the owner would otherwise have by statute under a full warranty, and they commonly exclude labor and consequential and incidental damages. Their terms are seldom negotiated at all, and a warranty that starts at substantial completion protects the owner more, not less, than one that starts at purchase or installation.

questions.question: An owner requires a force-main system to withstand at least 250 psi. Because the seals cannot be judged by looking at them during design, the owner's assurance of compliance depends on:

options.A: The manufacturer's marketing literature describing the product line capabilities
options.B: A post-bid substitution request submitted by the contractor for the seal parts
options.C: Testing and code-required certifications, consistent from product to product
options.D: The architect/engineer's visual examination of a representative design sample
options.E: A manufacturer's warranty to replace any seals that fail after installation
options.F: The architect/engineer's field observation of the seals as they are installed

questions.explanation: Features critical to safe operation, such as a seal that must hold a set pressure, cannot be judged by inspecting the product during design; they have to be evaluated and tested, and the owner relies on the product meeting code requirements consistently from one unit to the next. Marketing literature, a warranty or field observation does not prove the rating in advance.

questions.question: When little time is allowed for product evaluation or value analysis, which downstream consequences are likely?

options.A: Long-term maintenance cost is reduced over the building life
options.B: Substitution requests become more frequent
options.C: The lowest-first-cost product is selected with no downstream effect
options.D: Construction prices often increase
options.E: Product lead times grow, delaying the project schedule
options.F: More expensive manufacturers must be used to shorten the schedule

questions.explanation: A short evaluation period limits how many options the A/E can consider, which tends to bring more substitution requests and often raises construction prices. Long lead times and paying more for faster manufacturers are separate schedule issues, and a rushed evaluation does nothing to cut long-term maintenance cost.

questions.question: A mock-up requirement for a brick veneer assembly goes under:

options.A: QUALITY ASSURANCE in PART 1—GENERAL
options.B: FIELD [OR] SITE QUALITY CONTROL in PART 3—EXECUTION
options.C: SOURCE QUALITY CONTROL in PART 2—PRODUCTS
options.D: EXAMINATION in PART 3—EXECUTION
options.E: ADMINISTRATIVE REQUIREMENTS in PART 1—GENERAL
options.F: ACTION SUBMITTALS in PART 1—GENERAL

questions.explanation: In SectionFormat, mock-ups and field samples are subordinate titles under the Quality Assurance article in PART 1—GENERAL, even though the mock-up is built at the site, because they set the standard by which workmanship will be judged. Field or Site Quality Control in PART 3 covers tests and inspections of the installed work.

questions.question: Which subordinate titles does SectionFormat list under QUALITY ASSURANCE in PART 1—GENERAL?

options.A: Preinstallation Meetings
options.B: Field [or] Site Samples
options.C: Preinstallation Testing
options.D: Manufacturer Services
options.E: Preconstruction Testing
options.F: Delegated Design Submittals

questions.explanation: Under Quality Assurance, SectionFormat lists qualifications, certifications, preconstruction testing, field or site samples and mock-ups, among others. Preinstallation meetings fall under Administrative Requirements, preinstallation testing under Examination in PART 3, manufacturer services under the source and field quality control articles, and delegated design submittals under the submittal articles.

questions.question: When a printed project manual is split into volumes, where should the number and content of each volume be identified?

options.A: In Section 01 10 00—Summary
options.B: In the invitation to bid
options.C: On the spine label of each volume
options.D: On the cover pages
options.E: In the table of contents
options.F: In the instructions to bidders

questions.explanation: The number of volumes and what each one contains should be shown on the cover page or pages and in the table of contents, so anyone holding one volume can tell where the rest of the manual is. Spine labels, the summary section and the procurement documents are not where this is identified.

questions.question: Besides a high page count, which of the following are reasons to issue separate project manual volumes?

options.A: Addenda and modifications
options.B: Design-build projects
options.C: Projects using both MasterFormat and UniFormat
options.D: Projects with owner-furnished products
options.E: Multiple-prime contract projects
options.F: Construction manager at risk projects

questions.explanation: A printed manual is usually split once it passes about 700 pages, and separate volumes are also used for addenda and modifications and for multiple-prime contract projects, where each contract may get its own set of documents. A delivery method alone, such as design-build or CM at risk, is not a reason for separate volumes.

questions.question: Besides the owner and each project team member, who should receive copies of the approved project manual?

options.A: Regulatory agencies, for permits and approvals
options.B: Bonding companies, for surety underwriting
options.C: The owner's insurer, for builder's risk coverage
options.D: Adjacent property owners, for public notice
options.E: Product representatives, for product review
options.F: The commissioning agent, for the OPR

questions.explanation: Once approved, the project manual is reproduced in enough copies for procurement and for lenders' funding approvals, and distributed to each project team member and to regulatory agencies for the building permit and other approvals. Sureties, insurers, neighbors and product representatives are not part of that distribution.

questions.question: Which party typically performs the final review of the project manual before publication?

options.A: Architect/engineer
options.B: Authorities having jurisdiction
options.C: Owner
options.D: Contractor
options.E: Construction manager
options.F: Commissioning agent

questions.explanation: The processed specification text is sent to the owner, who gives the last review and comments; if the owner wants changes the text is revised, and if not it becomes the final copy for reproduction. The A/E prepares and coordinates the project manual, but it is the owner who signs off on it before publication.

questions.question: A revision log should capture the project name and number, the section number and title, and:

options.A: The names of all of the bidders on the project
options.B: The successful contractor's lump-sum bid amount
options.C: The reference standards cited within the section
options.D: A brief description of the changes made
options.E: The name of the person who made each change
options.F: The contractor's submittal register numbers

questions.explanation: A revision log records the project name, the owner's or A/E's project number, the section number and title, and a short description of what was changed, and it is archived so lessons learned can be used to update the office master guide specifications. Bidder names, bid amounts and submittal numbers belong to other records.

questions.question: A primary purpose of archiving the revision log is to:

options.A: Satisfy a code requirement that the AHJ imposes for permits
options.B: Update office master guide specifications and capture lessons learned
options.C: Track the contractor's monthly payment applications during construction
options.D: Replace the project manual table of contents after publication
options.E: Prevent unauthorized modification of the contract documents
options.F: Record the AHJ's plan review comments for the permit file

questions.explanation: The revision log is archived so the office can update its master guide specifications and capture lessons learned from the project. Preventing unauthorized changes to the contract documents is the job of security features on the issued files, and payment applications and permit comments are tracked in other records.

questions.question: In the preferred PageFormat addressing scheme, the paragraphs under an article such as 2.01 are numbered:

options.A: Uppercase letters: A., B., C.
options.B: Numbers: 1., 2., 3.
options.C: Period first: .1, .2, .3
options.D: Lowercase letters: a., b., c.
options.E: Numbers and parenthesis: 1), 2), 3)
options.F: Article style: 2.1, 2.2, 2.3

questions.explanation: PageFormat's preferred scheme addresses paragraphs with uppercase letters followed by a period (A., B., C.), with subparagraphs then numbered 1., a., 1) and a) at successive levels. The all-numeric scheme with a leading period (.1, .2) is the alternative used in Canada, and numbers such as 2.01 identify articles, not paragraphs.

questions.question: Under PageFormat, how are the pages of a specification section numbered?

options.A: Sequentially through the whole project manual, front to back
options.B: From 1 in each section, with the section number (04 05 13 - 1)
options.C: From 1 in each division, with the division number added
options.D: From 1 in each PART, with the PART number
options.E: From 1 in each volume, with the volume number added
options.F: From 1 in each article, with the article number

questions.explanation: PageFormat starts numbering at 1 on the first page of every section and writes the page number as the section number, a hyphen and the page (04 05 13 - 1), so any page can be cited exactly. Numbering straight through the whole project manual is discouraged because adding or removing pages during production would force renumbering everything after them.

questions.question: Which of the following are objectives of a standard page format?

options.A: Provide a flexible format compatible with most production software
options.B: Fix one typeface and point size for the industry
options.C: Match the title block and sheet layout of the National CAD Standard
options.D: Keep every section to an even number of pages
options.E: Present text at a density best suited for easy reading
options.F: Number the pages straight through the whole project manual

questions.explanation: A standard page format aims to present text clearly, at a density that makes reading easy and reference quick; to serve as an accepted standard across the construction industry; and to work with most production methods and software. PageFormat deliberately leaves the typeface and point size to the user, and it starts page numbering at 1 in each section instead of running it through the manual.

questions.question: When a specification section is displayed as a continuous-page (scrolling) electronic document, its headers and footers are meant to:

options.A: Insert top and bottom margins between every paragraph as the reader scrolls
options.B: Identify the project and the section number and title
options.C: Display the full list of reference standards used throughout the project manual
options.D: Replace the project-manual table of contents on screens that cannot display it
options.E: Show the running page number of the whole project manual
options.F: Carry the revision log for each change made to the section

questions.explanation: Headers and footers identify the document as belonging to a particular project and state its subject, the section number and title. On a scrolling screen they should stay fixed at the top and bottom while the text scrolls, or else appear at the start and end of the document. A running page number for the whole manual is wrong twice over: pages are numbered within each section, and a continuous document has no real pages.

questions.question: When a specification is displayed on a small screen and blank space has to be reduced, which kind of blank space should be reduced last?

options.A: Line spacing
options.B: Paragraph indentation
options.C: Page margins
options.D: Gutters between side-by-side text columns
options.E: Header and footer zones
options.F: Space before article titles

questions.explanation: On a small screen, blank space is given up in order: page margins first (the screen frame can act as a margin), then line spacing, and paragraph indentation last, because indentation shows the hierarchy of paragraphs and helps the reader navigate. Even then indentation should be cut back to a minimum of about two ems rather than removed. Side-by-side columns are discouraged on screens altogether.

questions.question: On screens where scrolling is NOT available, how should specification sections be displayed?

options.A: Noncontinuous pages, the same as if printed
options.B: A single continuous page that the reader scrolls
options.C: Horizontally scrolling tables of section text
options.D: Multiple side-by-side columns of running text
options.E: A continuous page with headers repeated at breaks
options.F: One separate screen for each PART of the section

questions.explanation: Without scrolling the reader can only move page by page, so sections should be shown as noncontinuous pages laid out just like printed ones. The continuous-page (scrolling) style is an option only where scrolling is available, and it is preferred there when the screen cannot show a full page readably. Multiple columns and horizontal scrolling are discouraged on any screen.

questions.question: Which of the following does PageFormat recommend AGAINST when specifications are displayed on screens wider than a printed page?

options.A: Widening the print area to fill the wider screen
options.B: Using high contrast between the page text and its background
options.C: Placing a sequential page number on each printed page
options.D: Using sans-serif fonts for on-screen viewing
options.E: Using multiple columns that force horizontal scrolling
options.F: Using uppercase for emphasis where bold cannot display

questions.explanation: On a screen larger than a printed page, the print area should not be widened to fill it, because longer lines are harder to read, and multiple columns should be avoided because they mix vertical and horizontal scrolling. High contrast between text and background, sans-serif fonts, and uppercase for emphasis where bold cannot display are all recommended for screens, and sequential page numbers remain part of PageFormat.

questions.question: For on-screen viewing, which fonts are preferred, and what is the recommended means of emphasis when a device cannot display bold?

options.A: Serif fonts; underlining text for emphasis
options.B: Monospaced fonts; color shading for emphasis
options.C: Sans-serif fonts; uppercase for emphasis
options.D: Decorative fonts; italics for emphasis
options.E: Serif fonts; color highlighting for emphasis
options.F: Sans-serif fonts; underlining for emphasis

questions.explanation: Sans-serif fonts read better on screens, and some fonts have been designed specifically for screen display. When a device cannot show bold, uppercase is the recommended way to emphasize text. Serif fonts are the usual choice for printed body text rather than screens, and underlining, italics or color are not the recommended stand-in for bold.

questions.question: Which of the following are purposes of specifying a mock-up?

options.A: Document the closeout submittals required at completion of the project
options.B: Replace the field quality-control tests otherwise required after install
options.C: Establish the standard by which the workmanship will be judged
options.D: Verify product properties through testing during manufacture
options.E: Ensure understanding and coordination of the required construction
options.F: State the minimum expertise required of the installer

questions.explanation: A mock-up is a full-size erected assembly that makes sure everyone understands and coordinates the required construction; it can also be tested and observed, and it becomes the standard against which workmanship is judged. Testing products while they are manufactured is source quality control, the installer's minimum expertise belongs under qualifications, and a mock-up does not take the place of required field tests.

questions.question: General requirements for placing the facility and its systems into service, including the commissioning agent's responsibilities, are specified in which Division 01 section?

options.A: Section 01 78 00 - Closeout Submittals
options.B: Section 01 92 00 - Facility Operation
options.C: Section 01 77 00 - Closeout Procedures
options.D: Section 01 91 00 - Commissioning
options.E: Section 01 75 00 - Starting and Adjusting
options.F: Section 01 79 00 - Demonstration and Training

questions.explanation: Section 01 91 00 - Commissioning covers commissioning the facility and its systems: the duties of the commissioning agent and the contractors, evaluation of system performance, and testing, adjusting and balancing as part of commissioning. Starting and Adjusting (01 75 00) covers equipment startup before commissioning, and Facility Operation (01 92 00) covers running the facility as part of a contract.

questions.question: Section 01 91 00 - Commissioning should be coordinated with the section that covers starting and adjusting equipment before commissioning begins. Which section is that?

options.A: Section 01 75 00
options.B: Section 01 33 00
options.C: Section 01 94 00
options.D: Section 01 42 00
options.E: Section 01 79 00
options.F: Section 01 77 00

questions.explanation: Equipment is started and adjusted under Section 01 75 00 - Starting and Adjusting, and that work comes before the commissioning process in 01 91 00, so the two must be coordinated. Section 01 79 00 covers demonstration and training, 01 77 00 closeout procedures, and 01 94 00 facility decommissioning, which takes systems out of service rather than starting them.

questions.question: In SectionFormat, where does the Systems Startup article of a technical specification section belong?

options.A: PART 1 - GENERAL
options.B: Division 00 documents
options.C: PART 3 - EXECUTION
options.D: PART 2 - PRODUCTS
options.E: Section 01 75 00 - Starting and Adjusting
options.F: Section 01 91 00 - Commissioning

questions.explanation: Systems Startup is a PART 3 - EXECUTION article, following Field [or] Site Quality Control and ahead of Adjusting, because it lists the actions for starting up the section's installed operating systems and equipment. It is coordinated with Division 01 Sections 01 75 00 - Starting and Adjusting and 01 91 00 - Commissioning, which hold the project-wide requirements, but the article itself sits in PART 3 of the technical section.

questions.question: A specifier requires the contractor to update the building information model periodically to show as-built conditions. In SectionFormat this is a:

options.A: Record Documentation closeout submittal in PART 1
options.B: Source Quality Control requirement in PART 2
options.C: Field [or] Site Quality Control requirement in PART 3
options.D: Product Data action submittal in PART 1
options.E: Closeout Activities requirement in PART 3
options.F: Delegated Design action submittal in PART 1

questions.explanation: Record documentation, such as marked-up drawings and project manuals showing what was actually built, is a closeout submittal in PART 1, and SectionFormat notes it can include periodic or final updates of the building information model by the contractor. Product data is an action submittal reviewed before the work, and Closeout Activities in PART 3 covers demonstration and training, not record submittals.

questions.question: The same software that produces specifications can also provide tools to:

options.A: Coordinate specifications and drawings, reducing errors and omissions
options.B: Choose the right specifying method for each product automatically
options.C: Replace the prime A/E's review of the consultants' sections
options.D: Eliminate the need for Division 01
options.E: Certify code compliance in place of the AHJ's plan review process
options.F: Price every specified product to update the cost estimate

questions.explanation: Specification software can link sections internally, keep a section's choices from contradicting each other, generate tables of contents and submittal lists, and provide tools for coordinating the specifications with the drawings, which reduces errors and omissions. These tools support the design professional's judgment; they do not pick the specifying method, replace the prime A/E's review of consultants' work, or stand in for the authority having jurisdiction.

questions.question: Providing product samples, CAD drawings and BIM objects to the design team is a typical service of:

options.A: The contractor's BIM coordinator
options.B: Product representatives
options.C: The commissioning agent
options.D: The authorities having jurisdiction
options.E: Reference standards organizations
options.F: Trade associations

questions.explanation: Product representatives supply information about their products: guide specifications, code information, help in obtaining approval from the authority having jurisdiction, product samples, CAD drawings and BIM objects. The design professional still reviews that material and decides what goes into the specifications. Samples and product models are manufacturer-side material, not something a contractor's BIM coordinator or a commissioning agent produces.

questions.question: Drawing details and BIM objects are among the information generally available from:

options.A: Reference standards organizations
options.B: Manufacturer websites
options.C: Section 01 42 00 - References
options.D: The AHJ's plan review office
options.E: Trade association handbooks
options.F: Commercial master guide specifications

questions.explanation: Manufacturer websites typically offer catalogs, product data sheets, installation instructions, test and evaluation reports, environmental product declarations, guide specifications, and drawing details and BIM objects for their products. Reference standards organizations publish the standards themselves, and Section 01 42 00 - References only lists the standards cited in the project, so neither supplies product models.

questions.question: Which statement uses the terms 'observe' and 'supervise' correctly?

options.A: The A/E supervises the Work; the Contractor observes it
options.B: The A/E observes the Work; the Contractor supervises it
options.C: The A/E observes the Work and directs its methods
options.D: Both terms mean watching the Work without control
options.E: The Owner observes the Work; the A/E supervises it
options.F: The Contractor observes the Work; the Owner supervises it

questions.explanation: To observe is to watch or view the work being performed; to supervise is to oversee it with control and direction. Control and direction of the work rest with the contractor, so the contractor supervises and the A/E observes. Saying the A/E supervises, or that it directs the methods, implies a responsibility the A/E does not have.

questions.question: Sending header, footer, and other formatting information to consultants before they write their sections mainly:

options.A: Transfers responsibility for overall coordination to the consultants
options.B: Eliminates the need for the prime A/E to review the returned sections
options.C: Lessens the time needed for final production of the project manual
options.D: Allows consultants to renumber sections using their own office system
options.E: Gives consultants the Division 01 requirements they must not repeat
options.F: Removes the need for final proofreading of the assembled manual

questions.explanation: Giving consultants the project's header, footer and other formatting before they write lets their sections arrive already matching the rest of the project manual, which shortens final production. It does not shift coordination to the consultants or remove the prime A/E's review of their sections, and the assembled manual still needs a final check before it is issued.

questions.question: Manufacturer guide specifications obtained for a project should be:

options.A: Used only on private projects
options.B: Reviewed carefully for bias and accuracy
options.C: Cited in the PART 1 References article
options.D: Inserted verbatim as accurate text
options.E: Placed in Division 00 as available information
options.F: Accepted once the product representative signs off

questions.explanation: Manufacturers' guide specifications save research and writing time, but they must be reviewed carefully because they may favor the maker's product or not state accurately what the project needs. Treat them as a starting point to edit, not finished text: copying them verbatim, or accepting them because the product representative approves, leaves any bias in place.

questions.question: To open a proprietary specification while still defining the desired quality, the preferred approach is to name a basis-of-design product and:

options.A: State the salient characteristics any comparable product must meet
options.B: Prohibit all substitutions so only the named product may be used
options.C: Append the phrase 'or equal' without stating any comparison criteria
options.D: Reference only the MasterFormat division number for that product
options.E: Name at least three products and close the list to substitutions
options.F: Copy the named product's literature verbatim as the requirements

questions.explanation: A basis-of-design product sets the type, function, dimension, appearance and quality wanted, and stating its salient characteristics gives a measurable basis for judging whether a comparable product is acceptable. A bare 'or equal' supplies no criteria for equality, prohibiting substitutions keeps the specification closed, and copying the maker's literature verbatim with no ranges still yields a closed proprietary specification.

questions.question: Procurement requirements such as the invitation to bid and instructions to bidders are located in:

options.A: Division 00 - Procurement and Contracting Requirements
options.B: PART 1 of each individual technical procurement section
options.C: The supplementary conditions to the contract documents only
options.D: Division 01 - General Requirements sections
options.E: Section 01 10 00 - Summary, in the general requirements
options.F: Section 01 25 00 - Substitution Procedures in Division 01

questions.explanation: Procurement requirements, such as the advertisement or invitation to bid, instructions to bidders and bid forms, are placed in Division 00 - Procurement and Contracting Requirements, which is separate from the specifications in Divisions 01 through 49. Division 01 sections such as 01 10 00 - Summary and 01 25 00 - Substitution Procedures hold general requirements of the work, not the solicitation or the bidding instructions.

questions.question: In Division 00, geotechnical data and existing conditions reports are grouped under:

options.A: Available Information
options.B: Supplementary Conditions
options.C: Instructions for Procurement
options.D: Project Forms
options.E: Contracting Forms and Supplements
options.F: Conditions of the Contract

questions.explanation: Available Information (00 30 00) holds information given to bidders for reference, such as preliminary schedules (00 31 13), existing condition information (00 31 19) and geotechnical data (00 31 32). The supplementary conditions modify the general conditions of the contract, and Instructions for Procurement (00 20 00) tell bidders how to prepare and submit bids, so reports belong in neither.

questions.question: Cross-references go to section numbers rather than article or page numbers because article and page numbers:

options.A: Are assigned only when the manual is printed
options.B: Are reserved for Division 01 references
options.C: Can change with later revisions
options.D: Differ between printed and PDF copies
options.E: Are defined only in Section 01 42 00
options.F: Are fixed by SectionFormat for every section

questions.explanation: Cross-references should cite section numbers only, because article and page numbers can shift whenever a section is revised. A MasterFormat section always keeps the same number and title, so a reference to it stays correct as text and pages change. Article and page numbers are not reserved for Division 01 and are not fixed by SectionFormat.

questions.question: Outline specifications prepared during early design should be organized using:

options.A: UniFormat element numbers and titles
options.B: MasterFormat numbers and section titles
options.C: Alphabetical product and material names
options.D: The PageFormat page layout and margins
options.E: UDS drawing sheet numbers and titles
options.F: Trade contract bid package numbers

questions.explanation: Outline specifications use MasterFormat numbers and titles so they stay as close as possible to the organization of the final project manual. UniFormat elements organize the preliminary project description, which comes earlier and describes the project by systems and assemblies rather than by work results.

questions.question: A small, straightforward project needs a condensed but legally enforceable specification. The most appropriate type is:

options.A: Outline specification
options.B: Preliminary project description (PPD)
options.C: Shortform specification
options.D: Performance specification for the entire project
options.E: Full-length specification
options.F: Outline master guide specification

questions.explanation: A shortform specification condenses full-length specifications for projects of limited scope, yet it remains a complete, legally enforceable contract document with at least a code-compliant level of detail. Outline specifications and preliminary project descriptions are early design documents that convey intent for review and estimating; they are not meant to serve as the contract specifications.

questions.question: Rather than include a precedence statement, the conditions of the contract should state that a conflict between the drawings and the specifications is resolved by:

options.A: Following the more stringent requirement
options.B: Following the A/E's documented interpretation
options.C: Following the specifications over the drawings
options.D: Following the larger-scale drawing
options.E: Following the owner's written determination
options.F: Following the precedence list in the agreement

questions.explanation: Drawings and specifications are complementary, so a statement ranking one over the other is not recommended. The conditions should say only that when the two conflict, the A/E makes a documented interpretation. A precedence list may be prepared for bidding purposes only; rules such as 'specifications govern' or 'the more stringent requirement governs' are exactly the precedence statements this approach avoids.

questions.question: In MasterFormat, the supplementary conditions are numbered:
questions.explanation: Supplementary conditions are 00 73 00, immediately after the general conditions at 00 72 00; both fall within the Conditions of the Contract group (00 70 00). Agreement forms are 00 52 00 under Contracting Forms and Supplements, and 00 22 13 is Supplementary Instructions to Bidders, a procurement document whose name is easy to confuse with it.

questions.question: Naming a single manufacturer followed by 'or equal' is generally:

options.A: Discouraged as awkward and redundant
options.B: The recommended open proprietary technique
options.C: Required on all federal projects
options.D: A form of descriptive specifying
options.E: The preferred method for public work
options.F: A form of closed proprietary specifying

questions.explanation: Tacking 'or equal' onto a manufacturer's name is awkward and redundant; one substitution paragraph in Division 01, backed by the instructions to bidders, does the job once and in the right place. Public agencies that do require 'or equal' usually also require at least three brand names plus the salient characteristics needed to judge equality, so a single name with 'or equal' is not the recommended open technique.

questions.question: Rather than reusing a prior project's sections, the preferred basis for new specification sections is:

options.A: The contractor's own preferred product and specification list
options.B: The conditions of the contract from a prior project
options.C: The general notes carried on the contract drawings
options.D: An office master guide specification, edited per project
options.E: A manufacturer's guide specification, inserted verbatim
options.F: The cited reference standards, copied into each section

questions.explanation: New sections should be edited from an office or commercial master guide specification, which is kept current and records lessons learned on past projects. A prior project's sections should be used only for reference: they may lack needed options, cite outdated standards or products no longer made, and miss changes made by addenda. Inserting a manufacturer's guide specification verbatim carries its bias into the project.

questions.question: Which sentences are written in the imperative mood?

options.A: Spread adhesive with notched trowel.
options.B: Adhesive is to be spread with a notched trowel.
options.C: Install equipment plumb and level.
options.D: The Contractor shall spread adhesive with a notched trowel.
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: In the imperative mood the action verb comes first, as in 'Spread adhesive with notched trowel' and 'Install equipment plumb and level.' 'The Contractor shall spread adhesive...' is the indicative mood, which relies on 'shall' and tends to be wordy, though it can help when several parties are named in one paragraph. 'Is to' is not recommended in specifications at all.

questions.question: Which words are capitalized when used in their specific contractual sense?

options.A: ‘subparagraph,’ when it refers to a specific numbered item within a section
options.B: ‘northwest,’ when it is used as a compass direction within the text
options.C: ‘subcontractor,’ when referring to a trade performing part of the work
options.D: ‘owner,’ when it means the specific owner bound by the owner-contractor agreement
options.E: ‘paragraph,’ when it refers to a paragraph in the specifications
options.F: ‘clause,’ when it refers to a clause of the general conditions

questions.explanation: Words defined in the contract are capitalized when used in that specific sense: Owner for the owner who is party to the agreement, and Paragraph when it points to a paragraph of the specifications or other contract documents. Subparagraph and clause are usually left lowercase, subcontractor is not capitalized because a subcontractor is not a party defined in the agreement, and compass directions are capitalized only as part of a proper noun.

questions.question: When a closed proprietary specification names at least three products, the A/E must still ensure that:

options.A: Each named product is stocked by a local supplier
options.B: Substitutions are processed under Section 01 25 13
options.C: The bid form includes a substitution page
options.D: The named products are comparable and acceptable
options.E: One named product is designated basis of design
options.F: The products are listed in order of preference

questions.explanation: Naming at least three products can create competition, but only if the named products really are comparable and acceptable, and the A/E must confirm that. A closed specification allows no substitutions, so processing substitutions under Section 01 25 13 or adding a substitution page to the bid form belongs to the open methods, and nothing requires one product to be designated basis of design or the list to show preference.

questions.question: Reference standard specifying differs from the other three methods because it:

options.A: Always names a single manufacturer and product
options.B: Cannot be combined with any other method in the same section
options.C: Can be used only for prescriptive specifications
options.D: Can serve both prescriptive and performance specifications
options.E: Places the full burden of performance on the specifying A/E
options.F: Requires naming at least three comparable products to compete

questions.explanation: Descriptive and proprietary specifying are prescriptive: they specify the products and processes, not the results. Performance specifying states the results and leaves the means to the contractor. Reference standards can be written either way, so reference standard specifying can serve both prescriptive and performance specifications, and it can share a section with the other methods.

questions.question: Even with no manufacturer named, a specification is still proprietary if:

options.A: It cites a consensus reference standard
options.B: It specifies a special warranty
options.C: It states performance criteria with ranges
options.D: The product is available from only one source
options.E: It lists requirements several makers can meet
options.F: It cites a federal commercial item description

questions.explanation: A specification is proprietary when the product it describes can come from only one source, whether or not a manufacturer is named. Requirements that several makers can meet keep it open, while requirements only one product can satisfy make it restrictive even without a brand name. Citing a consensus standard or stating performance with ranges does not make a specification proprietary.

questions.question: Which statements about 'shall' and 'will' in specifications are correct?

options.A: 'Shall' is used for work required to be done by the contractor.
options.B: 'Will' is used for acts required of the owner or the A/E.
options.C: 'Will' has no legal force, so it binds neither the owner nor the A/E.
options.D: 'Must' is the recommended substitute for 'will' in owner duties.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: 'Shall' is the imperative used for work the contractor is required to do, and 'will' is used for acts required of the owner or the A/E. 'Will' carries the same legal meaning as 'shall' but is treated as the less obligatory variant, so it is wrong to say it has no legal force. 'Must' is not recommended in specifications at all.

questions.question: Under SectionFormat, the 'Warranty [or] Bond' article, with its Manufacturer Warranty and Special Warranty subtitles, is located in:

options.A: CLOSEOUT SUBMITTALS only
options.B: PART 2—PRODUCTS
options.C: PART 1—GENERAL
options.D: PART 3—EXECUTION
options.E: Section 01 78 00 only
options.F: Division 00 bond forms

questions.explanation: WARRANTY [OR] BOND is a PART 1 - GENERAL article, with subordinate titles for Manufacturer Warranty, Special Warranty and Extended Correction Period. The warranty papers the contractor hands over at the end are a separate item, Warranty Documentation, under Closeout Submittals, and Division 00 bond forms are contract forms rather than requirements of a section.

questions.question: Elemental (systems and assemblies) performance specifications included in a project manual can be located in which MasterFormat section, arranged in an order taken from UniFormat categories?

options.A: Section 01 80 00 - Performance Requirements
options.B: Section 01 33 00 - Submittal Procedures
options.C: Section 01 42 00 - References
options.D: Section 00 01 10 - Table of Contents
options.E: Section 01 41 00 - Regulatory Requirements
options.F: Section 01 10 00 - Summary

questions.explanation: Section 01 80 00 - Performance Requirements can hold elemental performance specifications, ordered by UniFormat's categories; its subsections from 01 82 00 to 01 89 00 follow the building elements, such as substructure, shell and interiors. Section 01 41 00 covers regulatory requirements, 01 42 00 lists cited standards and 01 10 00 summarizes the work; none of them organizes performance criteria by element.

questions.question: Version control of the specifications covers revisions made during:

options.A: Schematic design and design development
options.B: Procurement and construction
options.C: AHJ plan review, procurement, and construction
options.D: Bidding, construction, and project closeout
options.E: Design development and AHJ plan review only
options.F: Procurement, construction, and facility operation

questions.explanation: Version control means tracking revisions so the whole team works from the latest specifications and can see what changed. It applies once the project team formally accepts the specifications, including changes made during the AHJ's plan review, not only those made during procurement and construction. Drafts during schematic design and design development come before that formal acceptance.

questions.question: In SectionFormat, which of the following are subordinate titles under CLOSEOUT SUBMITTALS in PART 1?

options.A: Maintenance Contracts
options.B: Tools
options.C: Manufacturer Reports
options.D: Warranty Documentation
options.E: Demonstration
options.F: Training

questions.explanation: Closeout Submittals covers what is handed over at completion: warranty documentation, maintenance contracts, bonds, record documentation, operation and maintenance data, and sustainable design closeout documentation. Tools are a Maintenance Material Submittal, Manufacturer Reports are an action or informational submittal, and Demonstration and Training are Closeout Activities in PART 3, not PART 1 submittals.

questions.question: In SectionFormat, 'Product Data,' 'Shop Drawings' and 'Samples' are subordinate titles under which PART 1 article?

options.A: CLOSEOUT SUBMITTALS at the end of PART 1
options.B: QUALITY ASSURANCE qualifications in PART 1
options.C: ACTION/INFORMATIONAL SUBMITTALS in PART 1
options.D: MAINTENANCE MATERIAL SUBMITTALS in PART 1
options.E: ADMINISTRATIVE REQUIREMENTS in PART 1
options.F: WARRANTY [OR] BOND near the end of PART 1

questions.explanation: Product Data, Shop Drawings, Samples, Certificates, Delegated Design Submittals and similar items fall under ACTION SUBMITTALS/INFORMATIONAL SUBMITTALS in PART 1; they are submitted for review or information while the work proceeds. Closeout Submittals cover items handed over at completion, such as warranty documents and record documents, and Maintenance Material Submittals cover spare parts, extra stock and tools.

questions.question: Which formats are recommended for distributing and archiving specification revisions?

options.A: Native CAD drawing files
options.B: PDF
options.C: Printed paper copies only
options.D: Editable word-processing files
options.E: Internet-based posting
options.F: Files with tracked changes

questions.explanation: Distribute and archive revisions in a neutral format like PDF or an internet posting, which everyone can open and which can carry security features so only the designated means can change the documents. Editable word-processing files, native CAD files and files with tracked changes invite unauthorized edits, and printed paper alone is not what is called for.

questions.question: An A/E must locate the specification for door hardware. Using MasterFormat, the correct division is:

options.A: Division 05—Metals
options.B: Division 06—Wood, Plastics, and Composites
options.C: Division 08—Openings
options.D: Division 10—Specialties
options.E: Division 28—Electronic Safety and Security
options.F: Division 12—Furnishings

questions.explanation: Division 08 - Openings covers doors, frames, windows, glazing and the hardware that goes with them, and door hardware has its own section, 08 71 00 - Door Hardware. Division 05 - Metals covers structural and fabricated metal work rather than hardware for openings, Division 10 - Specialties covers items such as signage and toilet compartments, and Division 28 covers electronic safety and security systems.
