questions.question: An accepted field or site sample of a finish may serve to:

options.A: Eliminate the need for the manufacturer's shop drawings
options.B: Establish a minimum standard of workmanship
options.C: Define and fix the contract sum for that work
options.D: Replace the manufacturer's product warranty
options.E: Serve as the field quality-control test report
options.F: Certify equivalence to the manufacturer's tested units

questions.explanation: Field or site samples are trial applications of finishes, such as paint or coatings, made at the project; once accepted, they can set a minimum standard of workmanship for the rest of that work. They do not take the place of shop drawings, warranties or field tests, and verifying equivalence to tested units is the job of a certification, not a sample.

questions.question: 'PART' is capitalized in specifications when it refers to:

options.A: A subcontractor's portion of the scope of work
options.B: One of the three parts of SectionFormat
options.C: Any general portion of the work of the contract
options.D: A clause within a cited reference standard
options.E: A numbered paragraph within an article
options.F: A bound volume of the project manual

questions.explanation: PART is written in capitals when it refers to one of SectionFormat's three parts: PART 1 - GENERAL, PART 2 - PRODUCTS and PART 3 - EXECUTION. Used in a general sense, such as a portion of the work, the word stays lowercase. A numbered paragraph is a Paragraph, and the bound volume is the Project Manual.

questions.question: When preparing a descriptive specification, combining the best features of several manufacturers' products risks:

options.A: Turning the specification into a closed proprietary one
options.B: Shifting the burden of performance to the contractor
options.C: Violating federal rules on non-restrictive specifications
options.D: Describing a product that does not exist
options.E: Requiring tests where a product certification would suffice
options.F: Specifying features that are better shown on the drawings

questions.explanation: Descriptive specifying means stating the requirements and confirming that real products can meet them. Picking the unique or best features of several manufacturers' products can add up to a description that no product satisfies. The specification does not become closed proprietary, since no product is named, and the burden of performance does not shift to the contractor: under a descriptive specification it stays with the A/E.

questions.question: When an open proprietary specification permits an unlimited number of substitutions, a likely consequence is that:

options.A: Competition among the bidders is effectively eliminated
options.B: The specification is automatically converted to the descriptive method
options.C: No A/E review of any proposed substitution is then required
options.D: The task of evaluating and analyzing the bids becomes quite large
options.E: Substitutions must then be considered after the contract award
options.F: Proof of comparability shifts from the bidders to the A/E

questions.explanation: When bidders may propose any number of substitutions, the A/E has to weigh every one, so reviewing and comparing the bids can become a very large job. A substitution page on the bid form and instructions that make bidders prove comparability help keep the listings to ones worth considering. Competition is not removed, and the proof of comparability stays with the bidder.

questions.question: In specification sentences, the articles 'the', 'a', and 'an' should generally be:

options.A: Replaced with the imperative verb 'shall' placed before the noun
options.B: Retained within every sentence for the sake of grammatical clarity
options.C: Omitted in most instances, as in 'Install gypsum board on framing'
options.D: Capitalized in order to emphasize the products being specified
options.E: Replaced with 'all' so that each requirement is fully inclusive
options.F: Retained wherever the sentence uses the indicative mood

questions.explanation: The articles 'the', 'a' and 'an' can be left out of most specification sentences, which keeps the streamlined imperative style: 'Apply oil paint with brush to walls' reads better than the same sentence with 'an', 'a' and 'the' in front of each noun. The word 'all' is usually unnecessary too, and 'shall' never takes the place of an article.

questions.question: The 'Examination' article, which verifies that conditions are acceptable to receive the specified products, is located in:

options.A: PART 2 - PRODUCTS
options.B: PART 3 - EXECUTION
options.C: Division 01 sections
options.D: PART 1 - GENERAL
options.E: Section 01 71 00 only
options.F: Division 00 documents

questions.explanation: EXAMINATION comes early in PART 3 - EXECUTION, right after Installers. It is a quality assurance step: before installing, the contractor confirms that conditions are acceptable to receive the section's primary products. Section 01 71 00 - Examination and Preparation sets general procedures for the project, but the article for each section's own checks sits in that section's PART 3.

questions.question: HVAC work results are organized in MasterFormat under:

options.A: Division 23 - Heating, Ventilating, and Air-Conditioning
options.B: Division 21 - Fire Suppression
options.C: Division 22 - Plumbing
options.D: Division 25 - Integrated Automation
options.E: Division 26 - Electrical
options.F: Division 28 - Electronic Safety and Security

questions.explanation: Division 23 - Heating, Ventilating, and Air-Conditioning holds HVAC work results in the Facility Services Subgroup, alongside Fire Suppression (21), Plumbing (22), Integrated Automation (25) and Electrical (26). Division 25 can look tempting because it covers automation that ties building systems together, but the HVAC equipment, ductwork and piping themselves are Division 23.

questions.question: Archived electronic specification files should include security features to:

options.A: Prevent any future editing of the files by the originating design firm
options.B: Block the owner from viewing the archived section files
options.C: Prevent modification of the contract documents by undesignated means
options.D: Encrypt all of the reference standards cited in the sections
options.E: Lock every file name to the ISO 8601 date convention
options.F: Limit file access to the firm's own specification staff

questions.explanation: Specifications distributed and archived in a neutral format should carry security features so the contract documents cannot be changed except through the means expressly designated for changes. The aim is to protect the record from unauthorized edits, not to keep the owner from viewing it, lock file names to a date convention, or restrict access to the firm's own staff.

questions.question: MasterFormat allows an additional, optional pair of digits beyond the standard three pairs. Its purpose is to:

options.A: Identify the contractor's trade for the section
options.B: Allow for expansion to greater specificity
options.C: Designate the PART of SectionFormat in use
options.D: Record the issue date of the cited standard
options.E: Number the articles within each PART
options.F: Show which MasterFormat edition is used

questions.explanation: MasterFormat numbers use three pairs of digits: the first pair is the Level 1 division, the second Level 2 and the third Level 3, as in 03 20 00 - Concrete Reinforcing. An optional fourth pair can be added to expand to greater specificity where a project needs it. The extra pair has nothing to do with trades, SectionFormat PARTs or the edition of a standard.

questions.question: Preinstallation meetings for complex installations that need coordination among several participants are specified under which PART 1 article?

options.A: Submittals article for action items
options.B: Summary of work article in PART 1
options.C: Quality Assurance qualifications article
options.D: Administrative Requirements article
options.E: Field [or] Site Conditions article
options.F: Delivery, Storage, and Handling article

questions.explanation: The Administrative Requirements article in PART 1 covers coordination, preinstallation meetings, sequencing and scheduling, so meetings before complex installations that need several parties to coordinate go there. Quality Assurance covers qualifications, certifications, field samples and mock-ups, and Field [or] Site Conditions covers ambient and existing conditions rather than meetings.

questions.question: Standard designations such as 'ASTM C270' and MasterFormat numbers such as 'Section 01 42 19' are kept on one line by using:

options.A: An em-dash between the number and title
options.B: A left-aligned tab stop placed after the number
options.C: A non-breaking space between the elements
options.D: A hard page break before the designation
options.E: A soft hyphen between the number elements
options.F: Quotation marks around the whole designation

questions.explanation: Designations such as ASTM C270 and MasterFormat numbers such as Section 01 42 19 should not be split by a line break, so a non-breaking space is placed between their parts to hold them together. A soft hyphen does the opposite by marking where a word may break, and tabs, page breaks and quotation marks do nothing to keep the elements on one line.

questions.question: A complete reference standard designation includes the issuing organization's name, the number, the title, and which of the following?

options.A: A proprietary product name that conforms to the cited standard
options.B: The current purchase price of the standard from the issuing body
options.C: Citation of the applicable requirements, unless all are required
options.D: The name of the testing laboratory that verifies the compliance
options.E: The date of issue of the standard
options.F: A statement that the edition in effect at bid date governs

questions.explanation: A complete designation names the issuing organization and gives the standard's number, title and date of issue, plus a citation of the applicable requirements unless the entire standard applies. Product names, prices and testing laboratories are not part of a designation, and the edition date for standards not otherwise dated is set once in Division 01 (Section 01 42 19 - Reference Standards), not in each designation.

questions.question: An A/E names one manufacturer's product and states that bids are to use that product and that no other product will be accepted in its place. This is which form of proprietary specification?

options.A: Open proprietary
options.B: Closed proprietary
options.C: Proposed substitutions
options.D: Reference standard
options.E: Controlled substitutions
options.F: Requested alternates

questions.explanation: A closed proprietary specification allows no substitutions: it names one product, or several as options, and bids must be based on a named product. Open forms such as requested alternates, proposed substitutions and controlled substitutions all leave some route for another product to be priced or accepted. Reference standard specifying names a standard, not a manufacturer.

questions.question: The four Cs of effective specification communication are clear, concise, complete, and:

options.A: Correct
options.B: Comprehensive
options.C: Competitive
options.D: Compliant
options.E: Consistent
options.F: Coordinated

questions.explanation: The four Cs of effective specification writing are clear, concise, correct and complete. Correct means presenting the information accurately and precisely, with words that convey exact meanings. Coordinated and consistent are good qualities too, and being complete already includes coordinating with related sections, but neither is one of the four Cs.

questions.question: 'Ambient Conditions' and 'Existing Conditions' are subordinate titles under which PART 1 article?

options.A: FIELD [OR] SITE CONDITIONS
options.B: DELIVERY, STORAGE, AND HANDLING
options.C: QUALITY ASSURANCE qualifications
options.D: ADMINISTRATIVE REQUIREMENTS
options.E: SUMMARY
options.F: PRICE AND PAYMENT PROCEDURES

questions.explanation: FIELD [OR] SITE CONDITIONS in PART 1 has two subordinate titles: Ambient Conditions, the temperature, humidity, lighting and similar conditions under which the work must be done, and Existing Conditions. Delivery, Storage, and Handling covers getting products to the site and protecting them before installation, and Administrative Requirements covers coordination, meetings, sequencing and scheduling.

questions.question: Because the same MasterFormat numbers and titles organize both specifications and filed product data, the chief benefit is that:

options.A: Each section can correspond to exactly one subcontractor's trade scope
options.B: Cited reference standards no longer need their dates of issue
options.C: The project manual is guaranteed never to exceed one volume
options.D: Filed technical data can be quickly related to the section written
options.E: Manufacturers' guide specifications no longer need the A/E's review
options.F: Section numbers then match the UniFormat element designations

questions.explanation: Because one numbering system organizes both the specifications and the office's filed technical data and product literature, material filed by work result can be related at once to the section being written, and many manufacturers number their literature the same way. Shared numbering does not tie a section to a single trade, change how standards are cited, or line sections up with UniFormat element designations.

questions.question: Excavation, grading, and soil work are organized under which MasterFormat division of the Site and Infrastructure Subgroup?

options.A: Division 33 - Utilities
options.B: Division 02 - Existing Conditions
options.C: Division 31 - Earthwork
options.D: Division 32 - Exterior Improvements
options.E: Division 34 - Transportation
options.F: Division 35 - Waterway and Marine Construction

questions.explanation: Division 31 - Earthwork, in the Site and Infrastructure Subgroup, covers excavation, grading and other soil work. Division 32 - Exterior Improvements covers paving, planting and other improvements built on the prepared ground, Division 33 - Utilities covers site utility services, and Division 02 - Existing Conditions covers assessment, demolition and remediation of what is already there.

questions.question: Where in SectionFormat are 'Spare Parts,' 'Extra Stock Materials,' and 'Tools' specified?

options.A: MAINTENANCE article in PART 3 - EXECUTION
options.B: ACCESSORIES article in PART 2 - PRODUCTS
options.C: CLOSEOUT ACTIVITIES in PART 3 - EXECUTION
options.D: MAINTENANCE MATERIAL SUBMITTALS in PART 1
options.E: CLOSEOUT SUBMITTALS in PART 1 - GENERAL
options.F: OWNER-FURNISHED PRODUCTS in PART 2

questions.explanation: Spare parts, extra stock materials and tools are supplies furnished to the owner, so SectionFormat lists them under MAINTENANCE MATERIAL SUBMITTALS in PART 1. CLOSEOUT SUBMITTALS covers documents such as warranties, bonds, record documents and operation and maintenance data, and the MAINTENANCE article in PART 3 covers maintenance services after installation rather than supplies handed over.

questions.question: Which usage of 'party' and 'entity' is correct?

options.A: Use 'party' for subcontractors and others not signing the contract.
options.B: Use 'party' for a contract signer and 'entity' for a non-signer.
options.C: Use 'entity' only when referring to the owner who signs the contract.
options.D: The two terms are fully interchangeable throughout the specifications.
options.E: Use 'entity' for a contract signer and 'party' for a non-signer.
options.F: Use 'party' only for the A/E, who is not a signer of the agreement.

questions.explanation: A party is a signer of the contract, such as the owner and the contractor in the owner-contractor agreement. When the meaning must take in people or companies who did not sign, such as subcontractors and others involved in construction, the generic word 'entity' is used. The terms are not interchangeable, and swapping them gets the distinction backwards.

questions.question: Which of the following are disadvantages of closed proprietary specifications?

options.A: The sole-source supplier may exploit its position and raise prices
options.B: Product selection can be closely controlled by the design team
options.C: The contractor may be forced to use a product it has had trouble with
options.D: More detailed drawings can be prepared from precise product data
options.E: Bidding is simplified by removing product pricing as a variable
options.F: The A/E assumes the full burden of performance for the product

questions.explanation: A closed proprietary specification offers no protection against higher costs, because a sole-source supplier can take unfair advantage and raise its price, and it may force the contractor to use a product it has had bad experience with, such as slow delivery or poor technical service. Close control of selection, more detailed drawings and simpler bidding are advantages, and the A/E carrying the burden of performance describes descriptive specifying.

questions.question: Which statements about combining specifying methods are correct?

options.A: A single specification section may use all four specifying methods.
options.B: Combining methods for a single product can create a conflict that cannot be resolved.
options.C: Project specifications should use only one specifying method.
options.D: Reference standards can be used only for prescriptive specifications.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: Project specifications usually use more than one specifying method, and one section may use all four. The caution concerns a single product: describing it by two methods at once can create redundancy or a conflict that cannot be resolved. Reference standards are not limited to prescriptive specifying; they can serve performance specifications too, which is why the three-statement combination is wrong.

questions.question: Which line follows the recommended rules for both symbols and numerals in specifications?

options.A: Wood studs: 2 by 4
options.B: Wood studs: 2×4
options.C: Wood studs: 2"x4"
options.D: Wood studs: two by four
options.E: Wood studs: 2 by 4 @ 16 inches
options.F: Wood studs: 2 inch × 4 inch

questions.explanation: Symbols such as × for 'by' and @ for 'at' should not be used in specifications, and sizes should be written with numerals, so '2 by 4' is the right form. 'Two by four' breaks the numerals rule, and every other line uses a symbol. The written word is used only for a quantity placed next to a size, as in 'five 2 by 4s.'

questions.question: Tests and inspections of variable conditions performed after the product is installed fall under which SectionFormat article and PART?

options.A: FIELD [OR] SITE QUALITY CONTROL in PART 3
options.B: PREPARATION in PART 3 - EXECUTION
options.C: QUALITY ASSURANCE in PART 1 - GENERAL
options.D: SOURCE QUALITY CONTROL in PART 2 - PRODUCTS
options.E: EXAMINATION in PART 3 - EXECUTION
options.F: ADJUSTING in PART 3 - EXECUTION

questions.explanation: FIELD [OR] SITE QUALITY CONTROL in PART 3 is the final form of verification: tests and inspections of installed work, which usually deal with variable conditions and can identify defective work during or after installation. SOURCE QUALITY CONTROL in PART 2 covers tests before products reach the site, and EXAMINATION and PREPARATION check conditions before installation begins.

questions.question: UniFormat is best suited to which of the following?

options.A: The final contract specifications throughout Divisions 02 through 49
options.B: Preliminary project descriptions in schematic design
options.C: The project manual's Division 00 table of contents
options.D: Reference-standard citations within the PART 1 article
options.E: Preliminary cost estimates before assemblies are detailed
options.F: Filing manufacturers' product literature by work result

questions.explanation: UniFormat is best suited to work done before the details of construction assemblies are known: it organizes preliminary project descriptions in schematic design and preliminary cost estimates, and offices also use it to file drawing details. Final contract specifications and filing product literature by work result are MasterFormat uses, and Division 00 is part of MasterFormat as well.

questions.question: SectionFormat was developed for Divisions 02 through 49, but its principles also apply to sections in:

options.A: Division 01—General Requirements
options.B: Division 00—Procurement and Contracting Requirements
options.C: The drawings
options.D: The conditions of the contract
options.E: The agreement forms
options.F: The bid form and its supplements

questions.explanation: SectionFormat's three-part structure was created for the sections in Divisions 02 through 49, but its principles apply equally to the sections of Division 01 - General Requirements, which are specifications too. Division 00 holds procurement and contracting documents, such as the bid form, the agreement and the conditions of the contract, which are documents rather than specification sections.

questions.question: The 'Qualifications' requirement stating the minimum expertise of a manufacturer, fabricator, or installer is placed under which PART 1 article?

options.A: Administrative Requirements
options.B: Delivery, Storage, and Handling
options.C: Submittals
options.D: Quality Assurance
options.E: Field [or] Site Conditions
options.F: Warranty [or] Bond

questions.explanation: Qualifications state the minimum expertise required of manufacturers, suppliers, fabricators, installers and similar parties, including testing agencies and design professionals the contractor employs, and they belong in the Quality Assurance article of PART 1. The qualification statements the contractor turns in are listed under Submittals, but the requirement itself sits under Quality Assurance.

questions.question: Which is the preferred form in specification language?

options.A: Top of platform
options.B: The platform top
options.C: Platform top
options.D: Top of the platform
options.E: Top surface of the platform
options.F: The top of platform

questions.explanation: Specification sentences are shortened by using a modifier in place of a prepositional phrase, so 'platform top' is preferred. 'Top of platform' is correct but longer, and versions that add 'the' or 'surface' only add words. The same rule turns 'within the time recommended by manufacturer' into 'within manufacturer's recommended time limit.'

questions.question: Of the four specifying methods, the two classified as prescriptive are:

options.A: Descriptive and proprietary
options.B: Reference standard and proprietary
options.C: Descriptive and performance
options.D: Performance and reference standard
options.E: Performance and proprietary
options.F: Descriptive and reference standard

questions.explanation: Descriptive and proprietary specifying are both prescriptive: they specify the products and processes, not the results. Performance specifying states the required results and leaves the means open. Reference standard specifying does not belong to either camp alone, because a cited standard can be prescriptive or performance-based, which is why the pairs that include it are wrong.

questions.question: On the scale of performance specifying levels, which runs from fully descriptive specifying to specifying by determinates, the requirement '10-gage galvanized annealed steel wire hangers spaced 4 feet on center both ways' falls at which level?

options.A: Descriptive specifying with performance criteria
options.B: A total project specified in descriptive terms
options.C: A reference standard specification
options.D: A total project specified in performance terms
options.E: Descriptive specifying with overall performance criteria
options.F: A major assembly specified as a self-contained component

questions.explanation: The requirement fixes material, gage and spacing and states no result to achieve, so it sits at the fully descriptive end of the scale: the total project specified in descriptive terms. The next level, descriptive with performance criteria, would add a result, such as hangers sized and attached to support 60 lb each. A self-contained assembly or a whole project specified by performance comes much further along.

questions.question: Which is the preferred revision of 'Contractor shall lay brick in common bond'?

options.A: Brick shall be laid in common bond by the Contractor.
options.B: The Contractor is to lay brick in common bond.
options.C: Brick must be laid in common bond.
options.D: Lay brick in common bond.
options.E: Contractor will lay brick in common bond.
options.F: All brick shall be laid in common bond.

questions.explanation: The preferred revision is the imperative 'Lay brick in common bond': the verb comes first and the contractor is not made the subject. 'Brick must be laid in common bond' improves on the original but relies on 'must', which is not recommended in specifications, and neither is 'is to'. Passive 'shall be laid' versions and adding 'all' only add words.

questions.question: A manufacturer's representative must visit the site to instruct the installer and verify compliance with installation instructions. These manufacturer services go under:

options.A: SOURCE QUALITY CONTROL in PART 2 - PRODUCTS
options.B: DELIVERY, STORAGE, AND HANDLING in PART 1
options.C: QUALITY ASSURANCE qualifications in PART 1
options.D: FIELD [OR] SITE QUALITY CONTROL in PART 3
options.E: CLOSEOUT ACTIVITIES, demonstration, in PART 3
options.F: INSTALLERS in PART 3 - EXECUTION

questions.explanation: When a manufacturer's representative has to come to the site to instruct the installer or verify that installation follows the manufacturer's instructions, the requirement goes under Manufacturer Services in FIELD [OR] SITE QUALITY CONTROL in PART 3, and a field report is the matching submittal. Manufacturer services under SOURCE QUALITY CONTROL in PART 2 cover coordination at the factory during manufacture, not site visits.

questions.question: A major advantage of MasterFormat's fixed numbering is that a section can be added:

options.A: Without renumbering the other sections
options.B: Without listing it in the table of contents
options.C: Without issuing an addendum during bidding
options.D: Without coordinating it with related sections
options.E: Without assigning it to a MasterFormat division
options.F: Without the prime A/E's coordination review

questions.explanation: Because each section always keeps the same MasterFormat number and title, sections can be written or added at any time without renumbering the others, and assembling the manual in numerical order keeps related sections grouped. A new section still needs its table of contents entry and coordination with related sections, and adding one during bidding still takes an addendum.

questions.question: When the project manual's table of contents is prepared, each section's number and title are recorded carefully. What do some firms record for each section as well?

options.A: The PART numbers used
options.B: The author's initials for each section
options.C: The number of pages of each section
options.D: The reference standards in each section
options.E: The date each section was last revised
options.F: The consultant who wrote each section

questions.explanation: The table of contents lists each section's number and title, and some firms also record how many pages each section has. Another common practice is to start the table of contents early in design and keep it current through production, then cross-check it against the assembled manual as part of quality control. Author initials, revision dates and consultants' names are not standard entries.

questions.question: Before reproduction, the processed specification text should first be:

options.A: Posted publicly to invite competitive bidding
options.B: Bound and shipped to all of the subcontractors
options.C: Transmitted to the owner for review and comment
options.D: Sent directly to the AHJ in order to obtain a permit
options.E: Returned to the consultants for final coordination
options.F: Archived as a PDF for version control purposes

questions.explanation: The processed text goes to the owner for a final review and comment. If the owner requires changes, the text is returned for revision; if not, the draft becomes the final copy, which is then reproduced for procurement, financing approvals, the project team and the permitting agencies. Permit submission and distribution to bidders follow reproduction rather than come before it.

questions.question: 'Manufacturer List,' 'Substitution Limitations' and 'Product Options' are subordinate titles of the Manufacturers article in which PART of SectionFormat?

options.A: Division 01
options.B: PART 3—EXECUTION
options.C: PART 1—GENERAL
options.D: PART 2—PRODUCTS
options.E: Section 01 60 00—Product Requirements
options.F: Division 00 instructions to bidders

questions.explanation: The Manufacturers article, with Manufacturer List, Substitution Limitations and Product Options, sits in PART 2 - PRODUCTS under the product heading, since it governs which products may be used. PART 3 has a similar Installers article, with Installer List and Substitution Limitations, which is the tempting mix-up. Division 01 and the instructions to bidders set substitution procedures, not a section's manufacturer list.

questions.question: During cleanup after installation, collecting the recyclable packaging and construction waste generated by a section's work result is specified in:

options.A: PART 2, Accessories
options.B: Division 00 procurement documents
options.C: PART 3, Cleaning
options.D: PART 2, Description (sustainability requirements)
options.E: PART 3, Adjusting
options.F: PART 3, Protection

questions.explanation: Collecting recyclable packaging and construction waste produced by the section's own work result belongs under Cleaning in PART 3, which can also call for flush-out of specific products. If Section 01 74 00 - Cleaning and Waste Management already covers that waste adequately, the section need not repeat it. Adjusting prepares installed products to perform, and Protection guards completed work, so neither deals with waste.

questions.question: When the contractor and the owner are mentioned in the same paragraph, the acceptable usage is:

options.A: 'Contractor shall' and 'Owner shall'
options.B: Imperative mood for both with no subjects
options.C: 'Contractor will' and 'Owner shall'
options.D: 'Contractor shall' and 'Owner will'
options.E: 'Contractor must' and 'Owner will'
options.F: 'Contractor is to' and 'Owner is to'

questions.explanation: Instructions are normally addressed to the contractor in the imperative, but when the contractor and the owner (or the A/E) appear in the same paragraph, 'The Contractor shall' and 'Owner will' may be used for clarity. 'Shall' marks the contractor's duty and 'will' the less obligatory acts of the owner or A/E. 'Must' and 'is to' are not recommended, and dropping the subjects would hide who does what.

questions.question: Which of the following are drawbacks of the descriptive method?

options.A: It is prohibited on public projects because it uses brand names
options.B: It cannot be enforced through submittals or observation
options.C: Writing a full descriptive specification takes a long, tedious effort
options.D: It reduces competition to a single source and invites collusion claims
options.E: The A/E assumes the burden of performance when it is used
options.F: It cannot be used where proprietary names are prohibited by law

questions.explanation: Descriptive specifications take a long and tedious effort to write, and the A/E assumes the burden of performance: if a product meeting the description fails, the contractor cannot be held responsible. Sole sources and collusion claims are drawbacks of closed proprietary specifying, and because descriptive specifications use no brand names, they are often the logical choice where proprietary names are prohibited by law.

questions.question: A ceiling hanger specified as 'non-sag' rather than 'straightened No. 11 wire, tightly wrapped two times' is an example of:

options.A: A reference standard specification citing an industry test method for sag
options.B: Simple performance criteria added to an otherwise descriptive spec
options.C: A purely descriptive specification with no performance content
options.D: A closed proprietary specification naming one hanger maker
options.E: Specifying by determinates, based on human requirements alone
options.F: A design-build statement of a ceiling system based on UniFormat

questions.explanation: Performance specifying has two applications. The first and narrowest is adding simple performance criteria to any specification, even one that otherwise describes what is wanted: 'non-sag' states the result, while 'straightened No. 11 wire, tightly wrapped two times' describes the means. No standard or maker is named, and specifying by determinates or a design-build systems statement lies at the broad end of performance specifying.

questions.question: Which statements match the recommended rules for dimensions in specification text?

options.A: Spell out feet when no inches are used, as in 8 feet.
options.B: Use symbols when both feet and inches are used, as in 8'-8".
options.C: Write fractions as single characters such as ¼.
options.D: A dimension may break across two lines when space is tight.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: Spell out feet when no inches are used (8 feet) and inches when no feet are used, but use symbols when both appear, as in 8'-8". A complete dimension should stay on one line rather than break across two, and fractions are typed with individual keys, as 1/4, rather than converted to special characters such as ¼.

questions.question: Which of the following are articles in PART 3 - EXECUTION of SectionFormat?

options.A: Source Quality Control
options.B: Field [or] Site Conditions
options.C: Systems Startup
options.D: Delivery, Storage, and Handling
options.E: Adjusting
options.F: Accessories

questions.explanation: SYSTEMS STARTUP and ADJUSTING are PART 3 articles, following Field [or] Site Quality Control and coming before Cleaning, since they deal with installed work at the site. Source Quality Control and Accessories are PART 2 - PRODUCTS articles, while Field [or] Site Conditions and Delivery, Storage, and Handling are PART 1 - GENERAL articles.

questions.question: UniFormat's built-in cross-reference to MasterFormat goes to which levels?

options.A: Level 1 only
options.B: Levels 1 through 3
options.C: Levels 1 through 4
options.D: Levels 1 and 2
options.E: Levels 2 and 3
options.F: Level 3 only

questions.explanation: UniFormat includes a cross-reference to MasterFormat Level 1 and Level 2 numbers, which helps when information moves from the PPD to the outline specifications. The specifier still has to choose the Level 3 sections: a curtain wall system that the cross-reference points to 08 44 00 may end up in 08 44 13 - Glazed Aluminum Curtain Walls, with its entrances, hardware and glazing in other sections.

questions.question: During construction, a contractor asks in writing for an interpretation of a specification paragraph. Which standardized form applies, and where should a copy of it be?

options.A: A communication record; kept in the A/E's project file only
options.B: A substitution request log; posted on the project website
options.C: A substitution request form; distributed to every sub-bidder
options.D: A request for information (RFI) form; a copy placed in the project manual
options.E: A request for information (RFI) form; kept in the A/E's project file only
options.F: A communication log; a copy placed in the project manual

questions.explanation: A request for interpretation during construction goes on a standardized request for information (RFI) form, which has one space for the question and another for the A/E's response, and a copy of the blank form belongs in the project manual so the contractor uses it. Communication records and logs track questions during procurement, and substitution request forms and logs handle proposed product substitutions, not interpretations.

questions.question: Approval of a substitution hinges on what determination?

options.A: The A/E accepts it as equal to the specified item
options.B: The owner agrees to share any resulting cost savings
options.C: It appears on a preapproved list in Division 01
options.D: It was logged on a substitution request form before bids opened
options.E: The contractor shows it will save time, money or both
options.F: The specified product is no longer available

questions.explanation: Approval of a substitution turns on the A/E accepting it as equivalent to the specified material, product or assembly. Savings in time or money are often why owners welcome substitutions, but savings alone never make a proposed product acceptable, and neither does a log entry or a list. Unavailability of the specified product may justify a request, yet equivalence is still the test.

questions.question: Which software feature lets editing notes stay in master sections without being deleted for each project?

options.A: Embedded objects
options.B: Hidden text or nonprinting tags
options.C: Track changes
options.D: Neutral-format (PDF) publishing
options.E: Web-based hyperlinks
options.F: Security features against modification

questions.explanation: Master sections can keep editing notes and instructions as hidden text or tags that do not print unless wanted, so they never have to be deleted for each project. Track changes records insertions and deletions rather than hiding notes, and hyperlinks, embedded objects and PDF publishing serve other purposes, such as linking to resources or distributing a locked copy.

questions.question: Which are common methods of identifying revisions in the specifications?

options.A: Renumbering the section
options.B: A revised table of contents only
options.C: Delta symbols
options.D: Hyperlinks to the old version
options.E: Clouds
options.F: Hidden text tags that do not print

questions.explanation: Revisions made after the specifications are final, or after the procurement documents are issued, are commonly marked with revision numbers, delta symbols, clouds, or strikethrough, bold, underline or italic text. Renumbering a section, revising only the table of contents or linking to an old version do not show what changed, and hidden non-printing text is a master-specification feature for editing notes, not a revision mark.

questions.question: On a project issued in multiple work packages, what is a work package?

options.A: The Division 01 sections that govern every prime contract
options.B: A bid alternate the owner may accept or reject
options.C: The full project manual and drawings at 100% CDs
options.D: Specs, drawings and schedules for one portion of the work
options.E: The owner's program for one phase of a master plan
options.F: Specs and drawings for all the work at each milestone

questions.explanation: A work package is a group of specifications, drawings and schedules that the design team prepares to describe one portion of the work so it can be priced, permitted and built separately from the rest. A bid alternate is an optional change to the base bid, and a full set of 100% construction documents covers all of the work rather than one portion of it.

questions.question: Which OmniClass tables are based on MasterFormat and UniFormat?

options.A: MasterFormat: Table 23; UniFormat: Table 32
options.B: MasterFormat: Table 22; UniFormat: Table 21
options.C: MasterFormat: Table 11; UniFormat: Table 13
options.D: MasterFormat: Table 21; UniFormat: Table 22
options.E: MasterFormat: Table 23; UniFormat: Table 21
options.F: MasterFormat: Table 22; UniFormat: Table 12

questions.explanation: OmniClass Table 22, Work Results, is based on MasterFormat, and Table 21, Elements, is based on UniFormat; the two are easy to swap, so remember that elements come first at 21. Table 23 covers products and Table 32 services, while Tables 11 through 14 classify construction entities and spaces by function and by form.

questions.question: The specifier tracks every change made to the project manual once it has been published. Which set lists the kinds of modifications to record?

options.A: Bid alternates, unit prices, allowances, and value-engineering proposals received from the low bidder
options.B: Addenda, substitution requests, contract modifications, and requests for information (RFIs)
options.C: Schematic, design-development, construction-document, and as-built revisions tracked by design phase
options.D: Punch-list items, warranty claims, closeout submittals, and operation-and-maintenance manual updates
options.E: Addenda, shop drawing reviews, field observation reports, and certificates for payment
options.F: Prebid meeting minutes, bidder questions, bid tabulations, and the notice of award

questions.explanation: After publication, the specifier records addenda issued during procurement, substitution requests, contract modifications made after the agreement is signed, and requests for information answered during construction, since each one changes or interprets the documents. Shop drawing reviews, punch lists, bid tabulations and similar items are records of administering the project, not modifications of the project manual.

questions.question: When updating a master guide specification, what should the A/E do about a master section that caused a problem on a past project?

options.A: Permanently delete the offending paragraph from the master
options.B: Convert the section to performance specifying to shift risk
options.C: Wait for the publisher's next scheduled subscription update
options.D: Find out if the cause was project-specific or industry-wide
options.E: Update the section's text to the latest referenced standards
options.F: Exclude the section and keep it available for future use

questions.explanation: Text that caused trouble on a previous project is revised, but first the A/E investigates whether the problem was specific to that project or reflects a broader, industry-wide change. Bringing standards up to date is a separate routine update task, and permanently deleting the paragraph or waiting for a publisher's update skips the investigation that tells the A/E what to change.

questions.question: In the tripartite relationship, how are the A/E and the contractor related?

options.A: A contract formed when the A/E signs the owner's agreement
options.B: A statutory duty for the A/E to indemnify the contractor
options.C: No contractual relationship, only an administrative one
options.D: A direct contract created by flow-down clauses
options.E: A subcontract under the owner-contractor agreement
options.F: A purchase order for administration services

questions.explanation: The owner contracts separately with the A/E to design the project and with the contractor to build it, so the A/E and the contractor have no contract with each other, only an administrative relationship: the A/E administers the construction contract for the owner. Signing the owner's agreement, flow-down clauses or a subcontract would make them contracting parties, which they are not.

questions.question: Which stage begins the facility life cycle?

options.A: Project conception
options.B: Design
options.C: Facility management
options.D: Programming
options.E: Feasibility study
options.F: Due diligence

questions.explanation: The facility life cycle begins with project conception, when the owner identifies a need, verifies feasibility, secures financing, develops a facility program and identifies a site. Programming and feasibility studies are activities within conception rather than separate first stages, design follows conception, and facility management comes after construction, late in the cycle.

questions.question: Which statements about combining shortform and full-length sections in one project manual are correct?

options.A: Combining them should be avoided to keep consistency between sections
options.B: When they are combined, section titles and numbers must be coordinated
options.C: SectionFormat makes them read alike, so they may be combined freely
options.D: Combining them is acceptable only on projects for public owners
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: Mixing shortform and full-length sections in one project manual should be avoided so the sections stay consistent. When it cannot be avoided, for example when a product lacks enough information for a full-length section, the section titles and numbers must be coordinated, including with consultants whose content overlaps. A shared format does not make mixed sections consistent, and nothing limits the practice to public owners.

questions.question: An allowance must also cover installation, but the standard general conditions limit allowances to materials and equipment delivered to the site. Which of the following should be done?

options.A: State the expanded allowance only on the bid form for pricing
options.B: Describe the installation only in PART 3 of the affected section
options.C: Add the installation by change order after the contract is signed
options.D: Delete the limiting general conditions provisions through the supplementary conditions
options.E: State the modified allowance requirements in Division 01
options.F: Price the installation as a separate unit price item on the bid form

questions.explanation: Where an allowance must cover more than the general conditions permit, such as installation, quantities or time, the limiting provisions of the general conditions are deleted through the supplementary conditions, and the expanded allowance requirements are then written into Division 01. Stating it only on the bid form or in PART 3, or adding it later by change order or unit price, leaves the general conditions excluding installation.

questions.question: The documents that coordinate an allowance must state which of these?

options.A: Precisely what scope of work is included under the stated allowance
options.B: Who is to install the items that are covered by the allowance
options.C: How costs adjust if actual price, quantity, or time varies from the amount
options.D: Which single manufacturer's product the allowance amount must purchase
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: The coordinated documents must state precisely what the allowance includes, who authorizes the items it covers, and how the cost is adjusted when the real price, quantity or time turns out different from the stated amount. Who installs the items is not one of the required statements (who authorizes them is), and an allowance does not have to name a single manufacturer's product.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700, which statements about Unit Price Work are correct?

options.A: The engineer determines the actual quantities and classifications
options.B: The estimated quantities are guaranteed to the contractor
options.C: Payments for Unit Price Work are based on the estimated quantities
options.D: The contractor's overhead and profit are paid apart from the unit prices
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: Under C-700 the engineer determines the quantities and classifications of Unit Price Work actually performed, and payment is based on those actual quantities. The estimated quantities are not guaranteed; they serve only to compare bids and set the initial contract price. Each unit price is deemed to include the contractor's overhead and profit, so neither combination that adds another statement is right.

questions.question: When alternates are used, modifying the standard general conditions is:

options.A: Generally required to add alternate pricing and selection rules to the contract
options.B: Always required, since alternates change the parties' rights and remedies
options.C: Required only on public projects subject to competitive-bidding statutes
options.D: Generally not required, because selected alternates become part of the work
options.E: Required to record which alternates the owner has accepted
options.F: Required through the supplementary conditions, as for expanded allowances

questions.explanation: Standard general conditions generally need no changes for alternates, because once the owner selects them and the agreement lists them, they simply become part of the work and the contract sum reflects them. The special provisions go elsewhere: the solicitation and bid form in the procurement documents, the selection in the agreement, and the description of each alternate in Section 01 23 00 - Alternates.

questions.question: In a Division 02-49 technical section affected by an allowance, the paragraph calling attention to the allowance provisions belongs in:

options.A: PART 2, PRODUCTS
options.B: PART 3, EXECUTION
options.C: PART 1, GENERAL
options.D: An end-of-section schedule
options.E: Section 01 21 00 only, not the technical section
options.F: The section header, beside its number and title

questions.explanation: A technical section affected by an allowance includes an article in PART 1 - GENERAL that calls attention to the allowance provisions and cross-references the amount stated in Division 01. PART 2 and PART 3 still describe the product and its installation as completely as possible so bidders know exactly what the allowance covers, but they are not where the notice goes.

questions.question: For an item covered by an allowance, how fully should PART 2 and PART 3 of the section describe the product and its installation?

options.A: Generically, since the allowance amount controls selection
options.B: As completely as possible, so bidders know what is covered
options.C: Product only, since installation is set when the allowance is spent
options.D: Not at all, since Division 01 states the allowance
options.E: By performance only, so any product within the amount qualifies
options.F: Installation only, since the product is chosen later

questions.explanation: Bidders must know precisely what the allowance covers, so PART 2 and PART 3 should describe both the product and its installation as completely as possible. Division 01 states the allowance amount and PART 1 points to it, but neither replaces the technical requirements, and a generic or partial description would leave bidders guessing what to include.

questions.question: If the contractor measures unit price quantities, Section 01 22 00 must specify:

options.A: How the owner controls and verifies the measurements
options.B: A guaranteed minimum quantity for each unit price item
options.C: The contractor's markup on each measured quantity
options.D: That the bid-form quantities govern final payment
options.E: Administration procedures for the owner's measuring staff
options.F: That quantities be measured by truckload or loose volume

questions.explanation: Section 01 22 00 - Unit Prices must say who measures the unit price quantities. If the owner or its representative measures, procedures for administration and coordination are defined; if the contractor measures, the owner's methods for controlling and verifying the measurements must be specified. Unit prices already include overhead and profit, payment follows the measured quantities, and truckload or loose-volume measurement should be avoided.

questions.question: Specifying compliance with ACI 350 predicts that a concrete structure is suitable to:

options.A: Carry assembly-occupancy live loads
options.B: Resist ASCE 7 wind loads
options.C: Contain water and wastewater
options.D: Achieve a one-hour fire rating
options.E: Store hazardous solid wastes
options.F: Resist de-icing chemical exposure

questions.explanation: A specified reference standard predicts the result of the construction it governs. When a concrete structure's specifications call for compliance with ACI 350, the structure can be expected to be suitable for conveying, storing or treating environmental liquids such as water and wastewater. Wind loads come from ASCE 7 and fire ratings from fire tests such as ASTM E119, not from ACI 350.

questions.question: Which advantage of reference standards comes from their representing the consensus of a national network of manufacturers?

options.A: Quality assurance
options.B: Reduced work
options.C: Reduced conflict and duplication
options.D: Uniformity
options.E: Applicability
options.F: Availability

questions.explanation: Uniformity comes from the fact that a standard represents the consensus of a national network of manufacturers in its field. Quality assurance comes instead from the developers' expertise, research and experience, reduced conflict and duplication from ANSI coordinating standards development, and reduced work from citing a standard rather than writing the requirements out.

questions.question: Model building codes are typically updated about every:

options.A: Year
options.B: Three years
options.C: Five years
options.D: Ten years
options.E: Two years
options.F: Four years

questions.explanation: Model codes are revised periodically, usually about every three years, by committees that each maintain one part of the code. Because the jurisdiction decides when a new edition takes effect, specifiers must track which edition the AHJ has adopted and when the next one becomes effective rather than assume the latest one applies.

questions.question: ASCE/SEI 7 is titled:

options.A: Standard Practice for Assessing and Qualifying Inspectors of Firestop Systems
options.B: Safety Code for Elevators and Escalators in Buildings and Other Structures
options.C: Minimum Design Loads for Buildings and Other Structures
options.D: Accessible and Usable Buildings and Facilities for Persons with Disabilities
options.E: Standard Methods of Fire Testing for Building Assemblies and Materials
options.F: Building Construction and Safety Code

questions.explanation: ASCE/SEI 7 sets the minimum design loads, such as wind loads, for buildings and other structures, and building codes name it as the basis of their load requirements. The other titles are altered versions of other standards' titles: firestop inspector qualification (ASTM E3038), elevator safety (ASME A17.1), accessibility (ICC A117.1) and fire tests of building construction (ASTM E119).

questions.question: Code requires a skylight's insulating glass to have a safety-glass inboard lite. Which statements about the offered products are correct?

options.A: Single 1/4-in annealed glass complies.
options.B: An insulated unit with a laminated inboard lite and an annealed outboard lite complies.
options.C: An insulated unit with a heat-strengthened inboard lite and an annealed outboard lite complies.
options.D: Both {A} and {B}
options.E: Both {B} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: The code calls for an insulated unit whose inboard lite is safety glass. The unit with a laminated inboard lite meets that, because laminated glass is a safety glass. Single annealed glass is neither an insulated unit nor safety glass, and heat-strengthened glass, though stronger than annealed, is not classed as safety glass, so that unit fails as well.

questions.question: A spec requires roof SRI of at least 82 initial or 64 aged for low-sloped roofs, and 39 initial or 32 aged for steep-sloped roofs. Which product is unacceptable?

options.A: PVC membrane, 1/4 in per ft, initial SRI 50
options.B: Asphalt shingle, 3:12, aged SRI 75
options.C: Standing-seam metal, 6:12, initial SRI 82
options.D: Modified bitumen, 1/4 in per ft, aged SRI 66
options.E: Built-up roof, 1/4 in per ft, aged SRI 64
options.F: Clay tile, 6:12, aged SRI 32

questions.explanation: Slope sets the threshold. At 1/4 inch per foot a roof is low-sloped, so it needs an initial SRI of at least 82 or an aged SRI of at least 64, and the PVC's initial 50 fails. The modified bitumen (aged 66) and built-up roof (aged 64) meet the low-slope limit, the metal and clay tile roofs at 6:12 meet the steep-slope limit, and the shingle's aged 75 passes either way.

questions.question: Which is NOT among the information manufacturers' websites generally provide?

options.A: Evaluation service reports
options.B: Project-specific shop drawings
options.C: BIM objects and drawing details
options.D: Continuing education presentations
options.E: Health Product Declarations
options.F: Installation instructions

questions.explanation: Manufacturer websites typically post general product information: catalogs, data sheets, installation instructions, safety data sheets, EPDs and HPDs, test and evaluation service reports, drawing details and BIM objects, guide specifications and continuing education. Shop drawings are prepared for a specific project and submitted during construction, so they are not posted as general product information.

questions.question: A normally voluntary reference standard becomes mandatory when it is:

options.A: Listed in a manufacturer's guide specification
options.B: Kept in the A/E's office library of standards
options.C: Published by an ANSI-accredited organization
options.D: Cited by reference within an adopted code
options.E: Adopted by a consensus of manufacturers
options.F: Referenced in a product's evaluation report

questions.explanation: Reference standards are voluntary on their own, but when an adopted code references a standard, that portion of the standard becomes codified and is treated as part of the code's mandatory requirements. Being listed in a guide specification or an evaluation report, kept in an office library, or published by an ANSI-accredited developer does not make a standard mandatory.

questions.question: Codes set minimum requirements. A design team that wants stricter requirements:

options.A: May include them only with AHJ approval
options.B: Must match the code minimums exactly
options.C: May include them without AHJ approval
options.D: May exceed the code only for life safety
options.E: Must first request a code modification
options.F: Must first obtain a local interpretation

questions.explanation: Codes set minimum requirements and do not stop the design team from specifying stricter ones, so exceeding the code needs no AHJ approval. Approval, a code modification or an interpretation comes into play when a design departs from what the code requires or its meaning is unclear, not when the design goes beyond the minimum.

questions.question: A public owner wants to allow only one manufacturer's product. What is usually required?

options.A: An AHJ code modification
options.B: A model code evaluation report
options.C: A bid alternate for the product
options.D: Special sole-source permission
options.E: An open proprietary specification
options.F: Substitution procedures in Division 01

questions.explanation: Many owners, especially public ones, require competition among products, so limiting a project to one manufacturer usually takes special sole-source permission. Investigating several manufacturers, letting acceptable products compete and recording the selection criteria in the specifications can also save the owner money. An open proprietary specification or Division 01 substitution procedures would do the opposite by admitting other products.

questions.question: Which statements about product representatives as trusted advisors are correct?

options.A: Trusted advisors want their part of the project to succeed for the client, not just to see their product listed.
options.B: Good representatives know competing products as well as their own.
options.C: Consulting a trusted advisor replaces the specifier's need to do its own product research.
options.D: A trusted advisor is valuable because it specializes in every product in the project manual.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: Both {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: A representative becomes a trusted advisor through an ongoing working relationship. Such advisors care that their part of the project succeeds for the client, not just that their product gets listed, and the good ones know competing products as well as their own and can weigh strengths and weaknesses on evidence. They do not replace the specifier's own research, and their value comes from focusing on a narrow part of the project.

questions.question: A pharmacist will own a new building for more than 10 years. The team picks an insulation that costs much more than the others. What justifies it?

options.A: A lower first cost than the other insulations
options.B: A smaller HVAC unit and lower operating costs
options.C: An energy code mandate for that product
options.D: Elimination of all mechanical equipment
options.E: Greater durability in heavily used areas
options.F: Better availability than the other insulations

questions.explanation: Looking past first cost to the cost of owning and operating the building over 10 years, the better-insulated envelope allows a smaller HVAC unit that costs less, which offsets the insulation's premium, and the owner then saves notably on operating costs. A lower first cost is the opposite of this case, and no insulation removes the need for mechanical equipment.

questions.question: When told to select the 'best' product, the design team should judge 'best' by:

options.A: The product with the single highest durability rating available
options.B: The priorities the owner has established for the project
options.C: The lowest first cost among the otherwise comparable products
options.D: The option the product representative recommends most strongly
options.E: The minimum grade the adopted building code allows
options.F: The grade the A/E used successfully on previous projects

questions.explanation: 'Best' can mean many things: the most durable product may be hard to get or far more expensive. The design team judges what is best for this project by the priorities the owner has set, whether durability, cost, availability or something else. A single attribute, a representative's strongest recommendation or past habit does not define best on its own.

questions.question: For exposed railings at an oceanfront Florida condominium with an open parking deck, which material is the better choice?

options.A: Galvanized steel
options.B: Painted carbon steel
options.C: Aluminum
options.D: Weathering steel
options.E: Ductile iron
options.F: Shop-primed carbon steel

questions.explanation: Aluminum is the better choice than galvanized steel for exposed railings and components here, because it is less affected by corrosive conditions such as salt spray from the ocean. The steel and iron options, coated or not, are the ones the salt air threatens; knowing the basic weaknesses of commonly used materials is part of selecting products for a site.

questions.question: The AHJ over a project is normally determined by the project's location. Which projects are the usual exception?

options.A: State university projects
options.B: Design-build projects
options.C: Privately financed projects
options.D: Federal government projects
options.E: Projects in states with a statewide code
options.F: Projects in unincorporated county areas

questions.explanation: The authority having jurisdiction normally follows the project's location, but federal government projects are the exception: they are built in widely varying places and are subject to federal procurement and construction regulations, which can differ by the agency building or occupying the facility. Delivery method, financing and the kind of local government do not change the location rule.

questions.question: Besides knowing the codes that govern a project, specifiers must track:

options.A: When the next code version takes effect, per the AHJ
options.B: When the ICC publishes the next edition of the code
options.C: Which code variances the contractor is likely to request
options.D: The AHJ's current plan-review backlog
options.E: Which committee maintains each part of the model code
options.F: Which products the AHJ has placed on its approved list

questions.explanation: Besides knowing the codes that govern the project, specifiers must know when the next version of the code takes effect in that jurisdiction, as set by the AHJ. A model code is not enforceable until the local authority adopts it, so the date a code publisher releases a new edition is not the trigger, and adoption may come well after.

questions.question: Under design-build delivery, design errors that surface during construction are MOST directly the financial responsibility of:

options.A: The owner, because the owner accepted the design at the bridging-documents stage
options.B: The A/E of record, under a separate prime agreement held with the project owner
options.C: The surety, which steps in to fund any design-related rework once a claim is filed
options.D: The design-builder, who holds both the design and the construction obligations
options.E: The design-builder's A/E, under its own professional agreement with the owner
options.F: The owner's own A/E, engaged to act as the owner's representative on the project

questions.explanation: In design-build the owner holds a single contract, with the design-builder, for both design and construction. The design-builder has final responsibility for the design, so errors, omissions and contradictions in the documents become its liability, not the owner's. The design-builder's A/E works for the design-builder rather than under its own agreement with the owner.

questions.question: An owner planning several new buildings on its campus hires a firm to help with site selection, financing, design oversight, and construction, acting as an extension of its staff. What is this role?

options.A: Program manager
options.B: Construction manager as agent
options.C: Construction manager at risk
options.D: Design-builder
options.E: Construction manager as advisor
options.F: Owner's architect/engineer

questions.explanation: A program manager acts as an extension of the owner's staff, usually on multi-site or multi-building programs, and can help with everything from finding sites, feasibility and financing to overseeing design and construction. A construction manager as agent also works only for the owner, but its services center on managing design and construction, while a CM at risk or a design-builder takes on the construction itself.

questions.question: Two referenced workmanship standards for the same product impose differing tolerances. What is the MOST defensible action for the A/E?

options.A: Identify the conflict and modify the references so the specifications carry no contradiction
options.B: Insert a clause stating the more stringent of the two conflicting standards will always control
options.C: Direct the contractor to apply whichever of the two standards it finds easier to satisfy
options.D: Adopt the standard with the earlier publication date as the controlling requirement here
options.E: Cite both unchanged, since a product meeting either tolerance would be acceptable
options.F: Adopt the standard with the later publication date as the controlling requirement

questions.explanation: Conflicting standards open the door to a product that meets only the lesser requirement, so the A/E should identify the conflicting provisions and modify the references in the specifications until no contradiction remains. A blanket clause saying the more stringent requirement governs may be added, but it cannot be relied on to settle every conflict, and letting the contractor or a publication date decide gives up the A/E's responsibility.

questions.question: A manufacturer's warranty takes effect only when the owner signs it. What does this requirement suggest?

options.A: It likely limits the owner's rights
options.B: It is a guaranty rather than a warranty
options.C: It becomes the owner's exclusive remedy
options.D: It transfers if the building is sold
options.E: It begins only at substantial completion
options.F: It covers workmanship as well as materials

questions.explanation: A signature requirement is one of the warranty provisions to watch for: a warranty that does not take effect until the owner signs it probably includes wording that restricts the owner's rights. Exclusive-remedy wording, limits on coverage or assignment, deductibles and short time limits for legal action are other warning signs, and signing does not turn the warranty into a guaranty.

questions.question: An A/E specifies one window using a reference standard, a descriptive requirement and two named manufacturers. The main caution about this approach is that it:

options.A: Is not permitted within a single specification section
options.B: Can create redundancy or a conflict that cannot be resolved
options.C: Converts the window to a closed proprietary item
options.D: Shifts the burden of performance onto the named manufacturers
options.E: Turns the section into a performance specification
options.F: Requires naming at least a third comparable manufacturer

questions.explanation: Using all four specifying methods within one section is acceptable, but combining several methods to specify a single product calls for care, because the requirements can duplicate each other or conflict in a way that cannot be resolved. Mixing methods does not make the section a performance specification, and naming two manufacturers alongside other requirements does not by itself shift the burden of performance.

questions.question: The descriptive method is used less often today than it once was, mainly because:

options.A: Projects are more complex and better reference standards exist
options.B: Federal law now prohibits descriptive specifications
options.C: Descriptive requirements cannot be checked through any submittal
options.D: Manufacturers no longer publish product properties
options.E: Proprietary names are now prohibited on most projects
options.F: It shifts the burden of performance to the contractor

questions.explanation: Descriptive specifying, once widely preferred, is used less as projects grow more complex and better reference standards become available to cite. It remains the logical choice where proprietary names are prohibited and no adequate reference standard exists. With descriptive specifying the A/E, not the contractor, carries the burden of performance, so that distractor reverses the rule.

questions.question: Where should the requirements and procedures for requesting product substitutions be specified?

options.A: PART 1 of each technical section, next to its submittals
options.B: The instructions to bidders alone
options.C: Section 01 25 13 - Product Substitution Procedures
options.D: The supplementary conditions
options.E: Section 01 33 00 - Submittal Procedures
options.F: Section 01 60 00 - Product Requirements

questions.explanation: Substitution requirements and procedures are best stated once, in Section 01 25 13 - Product Substitution Procedures, which covers limits on substitutions, the contractor's representations, and how to request and submit them. The instructions to bidders give the deadline for requests during bidding and point to 01 25 13 for the rest, and repeating the rules in each technical section breaks the say-it-once principle.

questions.question: A brick-and-mortar sample panel is to be built at the site, left standing, and used as the benchmark for judging the rest of the masonry. In the masonry section, this requirement is specified under:

options.A: PART 3, Field [or] Site Quality Control
options.B: PART 1, Quality Assurance
options.C: PART 2, Source Quality Control
options.D: PART 3, Installation
options.E: PART 1, Administrative Requirements
options.F: PART 3, Examination

questions.explanation: A mock-up is a full-size assembly built to set the standard by which workmanship will be judged, and SectionFormat lists Mock-ups under the Quality Assurance article of PART 1, even though it is erected at the site. Field [or] Site Quality Control in PART 3 is for tests and inspections of the installed work, and Source Quality Control in PART 2 is for tests at the plant.

questions.question: In a continuous-page (scrolling) electronic specification, PageFormat recommends that the page number be:

options.A: Either not used or shown in the recommended format
options.B: Numbered straight through the whole project manual
options.C: Replaced by the article number on each screen
options.D: Shown only on the first screen of each section
options.E: Shown at the top and bottom of every screen
options.F: Replaced by the section number in the footer

questions.explanation: A scrolling document has just one top, at its beginning, and one bottom, at its end, so a number on every page means little. PageFormat therefore says to omit the page number, or to show it in its usual format when the display technology allows. The project and section identification still go in the header and footer, held at the top and bottom of the screen if possible.

questions.question: Which revision of 'The contractor shall install the gypsum board in a careful and workmanlike manner' best follows recommended specification language?

options.A: Install gypsum board in a workmanlike manner.
options.B: Gypsum board shall be installed in a workmanlike manner.
options.C: The Contractor shall install gypsum board carefully.
options.D: Install gypsum board.
options.E: Install gypsum board to the satisfaction of the Architect.
options.F: Carefully install all gypsum board.

questions.explanation: Specification sentences should be imperative, without 'the Contractor shall' as the subject, and 'in a workmanlike manner' and 'to the satisfaction of the Architect' are on the list of vague expressions to avoid. Quality comes from the referenced standards and stated requirements, so 'Install gypsum board.' is the best revision. Words like 'carefully' or 'all' add length without adding an enforceable requirement.

questions.question: On a project with formal commissioning, a section requires the contractor to start up the system and then support functional testing. The section's 'Systems Startup' activity and the overall commissioning requirements go, respectively, in:

options.A: PART 3 of the section, and Division 01 Section 01 91 00 - Commissioning
options.B: PART 2 of the section, and the supplementary conditions of the contract itself
options.C: Division 01 for both, since startup and commissioning are general requirements
options.D: PART 1 of the section, and Division 00 procurement and contracting documents
options.E: PART 3 of the section, and Division 01 Section 01 75 00 - Starting and Adjusting
options.F: PART 1 of the section, and Division 01 Section 01 91 00 - Commissioning

questions.explanation: Systems Startup is an article in PART 3 - EXECUTION of the section, describing the final actions that make installed products ready to perform. The general commissioning requirements, including the commissioning agent's responsibilities, belong in Division 01 under Section 01 91 00 - Commissioning. Section 01 75 00 - Starting and Adjusting is the tempting wrong pick: it covers the schedule and procedures for starting equipment, not the overall commissioning process.

questions.question: When it comes to controlling substitutions, a specification is considered weak when it:

options.A: Allows substitutions to be proposed after contract award
options.B: Names only one product for each requirement
options.C: Requires substitution requests in writing
options.D: Sets a firm deadline for requests at 10 days before the bid date
options.E: Does not consider requests from manufacturers and suppliers
options.F: Requires supporting data to be submitted with each request

questions.explanation: Letting the contractor propose substitutions after the contract is awarded makes a specification weak: it invites more bid shopping and puts pressure on the A/E to accept substitutes the owner did not plan for. Written requests, a firm deadline, refusing requests that come straight from manufacturers and suppliers, and requiring supporting data are all controls recommended for the instructions to bidders.

questions.question: During schematic and early design, requirements are organized by building element (e.g., 'B2010 Exterior Walls') and later restated as work-result sections for the contract documents. The two classification systems used, in that order, are:

options.A: OmniClass for the early element descriptions, then SectionFormat for the documents
options.B: MasterFormat for the early descriptions, then UniFormat for the work-result sections
options.C: UniFormat for the early element descriptions, then MasterFormat for the sections
options.D: PageFormat for the early descriptions, then MasterFormat for the contract documents
options.E: PPDFormat for the early element descriptions, then UniFormat for the sections
options.F: MasterFormat for the early descriptions, then SectionFormat for the sections

questions.explanation: UniFormat organizes information by building element and system without naming products, so it suits preliminary project descriptions and estimates in early design. At about design development, that information is translated into MasterFormat work-result sections for the contract documents. OmniClass is the broad umbrella classification, PPDFormat organizes the text of a preliminary project description, and SectionFormat and PageFormat govern how a section is arranged and laid out.

questions.question: A manufacturer's representative helps the design team develop a curtain wall. The product then often appears in the specifications as:

options.A: A basis-of-design product
options.B: A closed proprietary product
options.C: An owner-furnished product
options.D: A requested alternate
options.E: A proposed substitution
options.F: A cash allowance item

questions.explanation: When a manufacturer's representative helps the design team with a product, that product is often written into the specifications as the basis-of-design product. Division 01 should then define basis of design and say how comparable products, if permitted, will be accepted. The help does not make it a closed proprietary product, and alternates, substitutions and allowances are separate procedures that have nothing to do with how the product was developed.

questions.question: After a standard's complete designation is listed in the PART 1 References article, PARTS 2 and 3 cite it by:

options.A: Its complete designation, with date
options.B: Its number only
options.C: Its title only
options.D: Its issuing organization only
options.E: Its number and date of issue
options.F: Its abbreviation and title

questions.explanation: The References article in PART 1 gives each standard's complete designation, including its date, and PARTS 2 and 3 then cite the standard by its number alone, for example ASTM C33/C33M. The short references save time and space, and the single complete list in PART 1 makes the standards easy to gather. Repeating the full designation or the date in every later reference is unnecessary.

questions.question: MasterFormat is typically updated:

options.A: Every year
options.B: Every two years
options.C: Every five years
options.D: Every ten years
options.E: Every three years
options.F: Every four years
