questions.explanation: MasterFormat is typically revised on a biennial (two-year) cycle, so the specifier should keep up with changes to its numbers and titles and update office masters to match. An annual cycle is the common wrong guess, and the longer intervals are also wrong for current practice.

questions.question: A coating must be sampled and tested at the manufacturing plant before shipment, and the cured film must also be inspected on the wall after installation. Under SectionFormat, these two requirements are specified, respectively, in:

options.A: Field [or] Site Quality Control in PART 3, and Source Quality Control in PART 2
options.B: Quality Assurance in PART 1, and Examination of substrates in PART 3 of the section
options.C: Source Quality Control in PART 2, and Field [or] Site Quality Control in PART 3
options.D: Source Quality Control in PART 2, and Examination of substrates in PART 3 instead
options.E: Source Quality Control in PART 2, and Quality Assurance in PART 1 of the section
options.F: Quality Assurance in PART 1, and Field [or] Site Quality Control in PART 3

questions.explanation: Tests and inspections of a product during manufacture, before it ships, are Source Quality Control in PART 2 - PRODUCTS. Tests and inspections of the installed work at the site are Field [or] Site Quality Control in PART 3 - EXECUTION. Quality Assurance in PART 1 covers qualifications, mock-ups and other prerequisites, and Examination is the check of substrates before installation, not of the finished film.

questions.question: An office is archiving a finished project manual. Best practice is a neutral format, security against unauthorized changes, and file names that use:

options.A: A single sequential index number, assigned in the order the sections were written
options.B: A proprietary CAD job code that ties the file to the firm's drawing database alone
options.C: The contractor's 6-digit purchase-order number paired with the volume page count
options.D: The optional ISO 8601 date convention (yyyy-mm-dd) within a consistent protocol
options.E: The MasterFormat section number followed by a mm-dd-yyyy date of issue
options.F: The owner's project number followed by the printing sequence number

questions.explanation: Archived specifications should be kept in a neutral format such as PDF, protected from unauthorized changes, and named under one consistent protocol for version control, using the optional yyyy-mm-dd date convention of ISO 8601. A mm-dd-yyyy date is not the ISO form, and sequence numbers, CAD job codes or purchase-order numbers do not identify the version in a consistent, dated way.

questions.question: A facade's curtain wall, described in early design under UniFormat B2010.40, is being translated to MasterFormat. Which section is the home for the curtain wall assembly itself?

options.A: 08 41 00 - Entrances and Storefronts
options.B: 08 44 00 - Curtain Wall and Glazed Assemblies
options.C: 08 51 00 - Metal Windows
options.D: 08 80 00 - Glazing
options.E: 08 46 00 - Window Wall Assemblies
options.F: 08 45 00 - Translucent Wall and Roof Assemblies

questions.explanation: MasterFormat places curtain wall assemblies in 08 44 00 - Curtain Wall and Glazed Assemblies, for example 08 44 13 - Glazed Aluminum Curtain Walls. Entrances and storefronts are in 08 41 00, window walls in 08 46 00, metal windows in 08 51 00, and 08 80 00 - Glazing covers the glass, which may get its own section when other assemblies use the same glazing.

questions.question: A preliminary project description lists 'B3010 Roofing' for a membrane roof. When the information moves to MasterFormat, the membrane roofing belongs in:

options.A: Division 06—Wood, Plastics, and Composites
options.B: Division 07—Thermal and Moisture Protection
options.C: Division 09—Finishes
options.D: Division 05—Metals
options.E: Division 08—Openings
options.F: Division 13—Special Construction

questions.explanation: Membrane roofing is a thermal and moisture protection work result, so it goes in Division 07. The switch from UniFormat elements to MasterFormat sections usually happens in design development, when the preliminary project description becomes a resource for the outline specifications. The roof deck or framing may fall in Divisions 05 or 06, but the membrane itself does not.

questions.question: A contractor proposes a product equal in performance to the basis-of-design product, but its greater depth forces rework by another trade. If it is accepted, who pays for that rework?

options.A: The contractor that proposed it
options.B: The owner, as a change in the work
options.C: The A/E, as a design revision
options.D: No one, since it meets the salient characteristics
options.E: The trade whose work must be reworked
options.F: The product's manufacturer, under its warranty

questions.explanation: The designer chose the specified product and drew the project around its dimensions, so any coordination or rework a contractor-proposed substitute causes is the contractor's responsibility. Substitution request forms commonly have the requester certify that it will pay for resulting design changes and construction costs. Equal performance does not shift that cost to the owner, the A/E or the affected trade, and a warranty covers product defects, not coordination.

questions.question: A project has a geotechnical report, an environmental hazardous-materials survey, and a record drawing of existing utilities. In Division 00, they belong:

options.A: All three under 00 31 00, Available Project Information
options.B: All three in the supplementary conditions, since they modify the general conditions
options.C: Geotechnical under 00 31 32; the other two in Division 02 sections
options.D: All three in 00 73 00, since existing-condition data alters the contract
options.E: Hazardous survey under 02 26 00; the other two under 00 31 00
options.F: Geotechnical under 02 32 00; the other two under 00 31 00

questions.explanation: MasterFormat groups information the owner makes available to bidders under 00 31 00 - Available Project Information, including 00 31 19 Existing Condition Information, 00 31 26 Existing Hazardous Material Information and 00 31 32 Geotechnical Data. These documents are information for the bidders' use, not supplementary conditions that modify the contract, and not Division 02 work results such as remediation or subsurface investigation.

questions.question: A developer will conceive, finance and manage the design and construction of an apartment complex, then lease every unit and never occupy it. A bank provides the construction loan. Who is the owner, and why?

options.A: The tenants, because they will occupy and use the finished complex every day
options.B: The bank, because its construction loan supplies the money for the project
options.C: The developer, because it initiates, assumes the risk and controls the process
options.D: The developer and tenants jointly, since owner status requires occupancy
options.E: The developer, because it will occupy the complex it manages after completion
options.F: The project management company that represents the developer to the other teams

questions.explanation: The owner is the principal stakeholder who initiates the project, assumes the risk, provides the funding and controls the design and construction process. An owner need not occupy the facility: a developer building units for tenants to lease is a standard example. A bank that arranges financing is one of the owner's advisers, and the tenants are facility users, not the owner.

questions.question: A private nonprofit hospital system builds an outpatient clinic with bank loans and donations. The clinic will serve the public and must meet state health regulations. How is this owner classified, and on what basis?

options.A: Public, because the clinic will serve the general public
options.B: Private, because no funding comes from taxation or appropriation
options.C: Public, because a state agency regulates the clinic's design
options.D: Private, because the owner is an organization, not an individual
options.E: Public, because a nonprofit owner is exempt from taxation
options.F: Public, because part of the funding comes from donations

questions.explanation: Funding decides the classification: a private owner's funding includes no money from taxation or appropriation by a legislative body, so bank loans and donations make this a private owner. Serving the public or being regulated by the state does not make an owner public. Being an organization is not the test either, since companies, corporations and boards of trustees can all be private owners.

questions.question: An owner hires an independent party to evaluate, test and analyze newly installed mechanical and electrical systems to see whether they will function according to the design criteria. What is this party called?

options.A: Testing and inspection agency
options.B: Sustainability consultant
options.C: Commissioning agent or authority
options.D: Mechanical engineer of record
options.E: Facility manager
options.F: Environmental engineer

questions.explanation: The commissioning agent (or commissioning authority) is the party that evaluates, tests and analyzes newly built building services, such as mechanical and electrical systems and sometimes the envelope, to see whether they will function according to the design criteria. The testing and inspection agency is the close miss: it gives the owner quality assurance and control by verifying that specific elements comply with the contract documents and code.

questions.question: An office building owner contracts with an outside service company to run the maintenance and operations programs, and the company will also give input when an addition is planned. How is this company classified?

options.A: As a facility user, because its staff work in the building daily
options.B: As a design team consultant, because it gives input during planning
options.C: As an owner's adviser, because it is an outside firm hired by the owner
options.D: As the facility manager, even though it is not on the owner's staff
options.E: As a project management company, since it represents the owner
options.F: As a commissioning agent, since it keeps the building systems working

questions.explanation: A facility manager can be an individual, a staff member or an outside management and service company that runs the maintenance and operations programs so the facility keeps serving its purpose, and it may take part in planning later additions or renovations. Facility users are the people the facility was designed for, not the firm that maintains it, and giving planning input does not make it a design consultant.

questions.question: On a new distribution center, who arranges and enters agreements for electrical power, water, sewer and communications service to the completed facility?

options.A: The owner, with design and contractor teams then helping coordinate service
options.B: The contractor, since it installs the service connections during construction
options.C: The A/E, whose engineers contract with the utilities as design consultants
options.D: The construction manager, acting as owner's agent for all utility matters
options.E: The utility providers, as owner-team members for the facility's life
options.F: The design team, with the owner and contractor then helping coordinate service

questions.explanation: Owners arrange and contract with public and regulated private utility providers for power, gas, water, sewer, stormwater and communications service to the completed facility. Once those agreements are in place, the design and contractor teams help coordinate the services. Utility providers are not owner-team members in the usual sense, although the owner's relationship with them lasts for the life of the facility.

questions.question: Which of the following are NOT part of the management expertise that contractors typically bring to project delivery?

options.A: Knowledge of the factors that influence cost, time and quality
options.B: Helping the owner determine the design program and requirements
options.C: Experience managing a construction budget within a risk-based setting
options.D: Skill in bidding and awarding the contracts and subcontracts
options.E: Identifying the codes and regulations that apply to the design
options.F: Ability to manage cash flow and project accounting

questions.explanation: Helping the owner determine the design program and identifying the codes and regulations that apply to the design are design team services. The contractor's expertise is construction experience, knowledge of cost, time and quality factors, managing subcontractors and suppliers, managing cash flow and accounting, bidding and awarding contracts and subcontracts, and managing a budget in a risk-based setting.

questions.question: A building products manufacturer has a staff member who researches what buyers and decision makers value, helps set criteria for products that satisfy clients, supplies information for competitive pricing and forecasts future sales. Which type of manufacturer employee is this?

options.A: Sales employee
options.B: Technical employee
options.C: Marketing employee
options.D: Independent sales representative
options.E: Order-processing employee
options.F: Stocking distributor

questions.explanation: Market research, product criteria, competitive pricing information, advertising strategy and sales forecasting are the work of marketing employees. Sales employees also quote prices, but their job is sales appointments, quotes, purchase orders and shipments toward a quota. An independent sales representative works under an agreement with the manufacturer rather than on its staff.

questions.question: An independent sales representative in one region helps an A/E get a roof system specified. The building is constructed in another region, where a second independent rep handles the sale. How is the commission typically handled?

options.A: Paid to the first rep when the product is specified in the documents
options.B: Split between both reps, and paid only once the product is used
options.C: Paid to the second rep alone, since the sale occurs in that region
options.D: Replaced by a salary, since the reps act as manufacturer employees
options.E: Split between both reps, and paid once the product is specified
options.F: Paid to the first rep as a fee for writing the specification

questions.explanation: When design happens in one region and construction in another, the commission is often split between the independent reps of both areas. Being specified is not enough: no commission is paid until the product is actually used. A salary is typical of a manufacturer's own representatives, not independent reps, and a fee for writing specifications is a separate arrangement, not the sales commission.

questions.question: After a partnering session led by a managerial consultant, the team agrees on shared goals and pledges to resolve issues without conflict. What is the main weakness of this technique?

options.A: Participants may not follow the priorities and goals set in the session
options.B: Shared software raises questions of privacy and authority over data
options.C: It shifts the contractor's risk to the owner through the session pledge
options.D: It replaces the dispute provisions written into the contract documents
options.E: It requires a managerial consultant to lead the interactive session
options.F: It requires participants to give up their contractual rights

questions.explanation: Partnering usually brings the participants together in a session led by a managerial consultant to set shared priorities and goals and, often, a pledge to resolve issues without conflict. Its weakness shows when participants do not follow those priorities and goals afterward. Questions of privacy and authority over shared data belong to collaboration software, a related but different idea, and partnering does not replace the contract or its rights.

questions.question: In a team approach to project quality, which statements are accurate?

options.A: The A/E's documented design of the owner's requirements is critical to defining the quality
options.B: The testing agency defines the tolerances and standards the work is judged against
options.C: The contractor's quality control of its means and methods defines the quality required
options.D: The contractor's performance is evaluated against the requirements of the contract documents
options.E: Both {A} and {D}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: {E} is right. Turning the owner's requirements into a documented design is the A/E's critical contribution, because that design sets the quality and the yardsticks, such as tolerances and standards, used to judge the work; the contractor's work and the finished project are then measured against the contract documents. A testing agency checks compliance with those documents and codes but does not set the standard, and the contractor's quality control is how it meets the required quality, not what defines it.

questions.question: Beyond a cooperative atmosphere on the job, which of the following should partnering and collaboration ideally deliver?

options.A: Documents of higher quality, prepared with a higher standard of care
options.B: A contract sum fixed before the construction documents are complete
options.C: Design liability shared equally by the owner, A/E and contractor
options.D: Dispute provisions no longer needed in the conditions of the contract
options.E: Service to the practical needs of the design and construction participants
options.F: Pooled contingencies that cover unknown and unforeseeable problems

questions.explanation: Ideally, partnering and collaboration help the delivery process, lead to better documents prepared with a higher standard of care, and meet the practical needs of the people who design and build the project. They do not replace the contract: participants are expected to understand their contractual rights, so shared liability and dropping dispute provisions are wrong. Pooled contingencies and early pricing belong to other delivery approaches, not to partnering itself.

questions.question: On a design-bid-build project with competitive bidding, which of the following push the team toward adversarial relationships?

options.A: An owner contingency for scope gaps
options.B: Familiar roles and well-understood contract relationships
options.C: Emphasis on the low bid
options.D: Multi-party agreements with consensus decisions
options.E: No contractor involvement during the design phases
options.F: Pooled contingencies with early trade involvement

questions.explanation: Competitive design-bid-build can turn adversarial because of its emphasis on the low bid and because the contractor has no part in the design phases; a contractor who bid with little profit may then look to change orders. The lack of an owner contingency is a related limitation, not the cause named. Familiar roles and well-understood contracts are a benefit of design-bid-build, and multi-party agreements and pooled contingencies are features of integrated project delivery.

questions.question: Partnering is possible when participants meet certain conditions. Which is NOT one of them?

options.A: They understand their own and others' contractual rights and responsibilities
options.B: They set aside their contractual rights so team consensus decides disputes
options.C: They show a willingness to suppress short-term economic self-interest
options.D: They work swiftly to solve problems through effective communication
options.E: They systematically apply their professional or trade standards of practice
options.F: They consistently act in an ethical manner

questions.explanation: Partnering depends on participants understanding the extent of their own and others' contractual rights and responsibilities, not giving those rights up to team consensus. The other conditions are applying professional or trade standards of practice, working quickly to solve problems through good communication, being willing to put project success ahead of short-term economic self-interest, and acting ethically throughout.

questions.question: A fast-food chain wants the same building design used for restaurants on sites in several states. Which statement describes this design approach?

options.A: One design reused on different sites, with minor changes for site and AHJ needs
options.B: One design reused on different sites with no changes, so identity stays consistent
options.C: A large-scale design of complementary facilities on the same or contiguous sites
options.D: A design refined through full-scale prototypes and mock-ups before documents issue
options.E: One design reused on different sites, with each AHJ waiving its local requirements
options.F: Separate custom designs for each site that share only a consistent brand identity

questions.explanation: This is prototype design: a single design used for several projects on different sites, with minor changes to fit each site and the requirements of the authorities having jurisdiction, so users readily recognize the facility. Retail outlets and fast-food chains are the classic examples. Reusing it with no changes ignores site and code differences, and complementary buildings on the same or adjoining sites describe master planning.

questions.question: A university plans a 20-year campus of integrated, complementary buildings on contiguous parcels. Which statements about master planning are accurate?

options.A: It is the approach used when one design is repeated on scattered sites
options.B: The A/E may be hired to design the entire plan or only some of its facilities
options.C: Its requirements are best defined after the first building's schematic design
options.D: It may take longer than an equal number of individual designs of similar scope
options.E: Both {B} and {D}
options.F: {B}, {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: {E} is right. An owner may have all of a master plan designed at once or only part of it, so the A/E may be engaged for the whole plan or a portion, and master planning can take longer than the same number of separate designs because it needs thorough knowledge of present and future needs. Its requirements belong in the owner's program during project conception, not after a first schematic design, and one design repeated on scattered sites is prototype design.

questions.question: An owner has found a parcel it likes for a new headquarters. Which statements about due diligence investigations of the property are accurate?

options.A: They should begin as soon as the property is identified
options.B: They should wait until the purchase closes and the site is accessible
options.C: Programming may not be completed until they are complete
options.D: They are done during schematic design, when the A/E first needs site data
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: {E} is right. Due diligence on a property should start once the owner identifies it, before the owner is bound by contract to buy or lease, so problems surface while the owner can still walk away. The investigations are preparatory steps for programming, so programming may not be finished until they are done. Waiting for the closing or for schematic design reverses that order.

questions.question: An owner's financial study looks at the timing of funding. Which pairings of funding source and timing consideration are correct?

options.A: Government grants: apply once construction bids have been received
options.B: Bank loans: secure them when interest rates are relatively low
options.C: Philanthropic donations: solicit them as construction costs are incurred
options.D: Tax and bond issues: success depends mainly on the owner's credit rating
options.E: Private investment: success needs experienced marketing strategies
options.F: Venture capital: secure it when interest rates are relatively low

questions.explanation: Timing matters in securing funds: bank loans are best locked in while interest rates are relatively low, and private investment and venture capital depend on experienced marketing strategies to attract money. Grants and philanthropic donations must be sought well before the money is needed, not after bids or during construction. Tax and bond issues depend on the economy, public receptiveness and competing public issues, not mainly on a credit rating.

questions.question: A manufacturer weighing a move of its plant 300 miles away must consider whether key employees can move, whether a trained workforce exists there, and the effect of downtime on customers. Which community impact study category covers these concerns?

options.A: Operations
options.B: Public facilities and utilities impact
options.C: Economic impact
options.D: Relocation
options.E: Environmental impact
options.F: Noise pollution

questions.explanation: Relocation covers the effects of moving on users, employees, suppliers and customers, downtime during the move, the mobility of key employees, the cost of moving and whether a trained workforce exists at the new location. Operations is about how renovations or additions disrupt the owner's existing operations, and economic impact is about the facility's role in local taxes and employment.

questions.question: The site survey shows a recorded easement for overhead power lines crossing the parcel. Which statements about it are typically true?

options.A: The owner still owns the portion of the property within the easement
options.B: Paving is usually allowed within the easement
options.C: Low buildings may be built within the easement below a set height
options.D: The utility may legally enter the easement for maintenance and repairs
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: {F} is right. An easement gives another party, here the power company, right-of-way over part of the owner's property, but the owner still owns that land. Buildings and permanent structures cannot be built on the easement, though paving usually is allowed, and its width lets the utility legally enter for maintenance, repairs and replacement. No height allowance lets low buildings into the easement.

questions.question: An owner is considering a former industrial parcel that previous owners contaminated with chemicals. Which statements are accurate?

options.A: Lenders are often reluctant to finance it, so other financing may be needed
options.B: Federal cleanup grants are available, though applications usually involve long waits
options.C: The term brownfield also covers any building containing asbestos materials
options.D: The contamination affects project cost but not the schedule or site flexibility
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: {E} is right. Lenders are very reluctant to finance projects on contaminated sites, so other financing may be needed, and federal programs and grants for restoring such sites exist but usually come with long waits. A brownfield is land contaminated by earlier owners; it is not the same as a building that contains hazardous materials such as asbestos. Problem sites affect cost, schedule and how freely the owner can adapt the site.

questions.question: Before renovating, the owner wants to know whether water and air infiltration through the enclosure could cause corrosion, movement and loss of structural integrity in components. Which evaluation addresses this?

options.A: Structural evaluation
options.B: Facility systems evaluation
options.C: Hygrothermal analysis
options.D: Environmental and indoor air quality evaluation
options.E: Functional evaluation
options.F: Energy consumption evaluation

questions.explanation: A hygrothermal analysis studies how water and air leaking through the building envelope can damage components, both structurally and thermally, through effects such as corrosion and movement. A structural evaluation looks at the gravity and lateral components, foundations and superstructure, not at moisture moving through the envelope. Indoor air quality and energy evaluations look at other aspects of the building's performance.

questions.question: A remote parcel is offered at a very low price but does not meet all of the owner's requirements. Which statements are sound?

options.A: A site that misses some requirements may still be worthwhile if bought for less
options.B: Remote sites may need upgraded or new transportation, utility and communication infrastructure
options.C: Addressing a site's limitations seldom slows the acquisition process
options.D: A site that meets every criterion is the most economical choice for the project
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: {E} is right. A site that misses some requirements can still be worth buying if its lower price leaves enough money to deal with its limitations, and a remote site may need new or upgraded roads, utilities and communications, especially when it is very cheap. Working around a site's limitations takes time and money and slows acquisition, and a site that meets every criterion can be prohibitively expensive rather than the most economical choice.

questions.question: An owner's A/E is helping it search for, evaluate and acquire a site. Which statements about the timing of site studies are accurate?

options.A: The full range of site studies must be finished before any site is acquired
options.B: The studies needed to justify the acquisition should be done before it
options.C: More extensive studies can follow acquisition, before programming is completed
options.D: Buying a site before the project requirements are known may leave some objectives unmet
options.E: Both {B} and {C}
options.F: {B}, {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: {F} is right. Not every site study has to be finished before acquisition, but the studies that justify buying the site should be, and the more extensive studies can follow as long as they are done before programming is complete. Buying a site before the project's requirements are known risks a site on which some of the owner's objectives cannot be met, so requiring every study first is the wrong pick.

questions.question: A retailer wants a site near competing stores because they stimulate shopping activity. Under which key location attribute does proximity to competing businesses fall?

options.A: Human resources
options.B: Proximity to cultural magnets
options.C: Natural features
options.D: Economic resources
options.E: Public utilities and services
options.F: Access to transportation infrastructure

questions.explanation: Economic resources, as a location attribute, include nearness to complementary businesses, to natural and material resources, and even to competitors whose presence stimulates business activity. Human resources is the tempting pick because customers are people, but that attribute is about the population a facility draws on, such as skilled labor, customers and volunteers, not about neighboring businesses.

questions.question: A zoning code limits how much of a lot may be developed, paved or otherwise used, expressed as occupant density or building footprint. What is this limit called?

options.A: Setback restriction
options.B: Floor area restriction
options.C: Allowable site coverage
options.D: Height restriction
options.E: Conditional use restriction
options.F: Parking requirement

questions.explanation: A zoning limit on how much land may be developed, paved or otherwise used is the allowable site coverage, stated as occupant density or as the facility's footprint. Setback restrictions set how far the building must stay from property lines and other structures, while floor area and height restrictions limit the size and height of the building itself rather than the share of the lot used.

questions.question: A school district is offered an affordable parcel next to a large airport, where noise would affect classroom activities. Which site consideration most directly argues against it?

options.A: Height restrictions under land development regulations
options.B: Surrounding conditions and their effect on operations
options.C: Marketability of the facility for a later resale
options.D: Access to transportation as a location attribute
options.E: Natural features such as topography and climate
options.F: Parking and loading zone requirements

questions.explanation: Surrounding economic and social conditions affect the owner's operations now and over the long term. A site next to a large airport may suit a package-handling facility, but high noise makes it a poor fit for a school, laboratory or housing. Height restrictions near airports exist because tall buildings can be a hazard to aircraft; they say nothing about the noise a school would suffer.

questions.question: Marketability is a key factor in deciding whether to remodel an existing facility or relocate. Which statements about it are accurate?

options.A: Owners of highly specialized facilities may be financially unable to relocate
options.B: Rising land value at a site now "in town" may offset the cost of relocating
options.C: Marketability matters only to owners who lease rather than own their facilities
options.D: An "in town" site may be far from major highways and rail systems
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: {F} is right. Owners of highly specialized facilities may be financially unable to relocate. Land that was 'out of town' decades ago may now be 'in town' and worth enough to offset the cost of moving, yet that in-town site may be far from the highways and rail the owner needs for goods and raw materials. Nothing limits marketability to owners who lease.

questions.question: An owner makes an offer on a site. How do most site purchase agreements work?

options.A: The purchase closes first, and the owner may resell if a later evaluation is unfavorable
options.B: The seller must furnish a favorable evaluation before the buyer may submit an offer
options.C: The offer is conditioned on a site evaluation, and closing waits for a favorable one
options.D: The offer and closing happen together, with evaluations done during schematic design
options.E: The offer is unconditional, and the agreement sets a timeline for due diligence
options.F: The offer is conditioned on financing, and site evaluations follow the closing

questions.explanation: Most site purchase agreements work in two steps: the buyer makes an offer conditioned on an evaluation of the site that satisfies its requirements, and the purchase is completed only after a favorable evaluation comes in. The agreement may also set a deadline for finishing the due diligence. Closing first and evaluating later, or making an unconditional offer, leaves the buyer bound to a site it has not checked.

questions.question: Problem Seeking describes programming as two phases that run from general to specific and tie into the design phases. Which pairing is correct?

options.A: Schematic programming leads into schematic design, and program development into design development
options.B: Schematic programming leads into design development, and program development into construction documents
options.C: Both phases are finished before schematic design starts, since programming precedes design
options.D: Program development comes first, and schematic programming then adds the detailed data
options.E: Schematic programming leads into design development, and program development into schematic design
options.F: Schematic programming ends as design begins, and program development ends as bidding begins

questions.explanation: Schematic programming identifies the broad goals, user preferences, image, functions and adjacencies, and as it ends, schematic design begins. Program development then organizes the detailed data from the impact studies and site analysis, and as it ends, design development begins. So programming does not all finish before design starts; program development runs alongside schematic design.

questions.question: In Problem Seeking's Step 1, Establish Goals, corporate executives decide to build a new headquarters mainly as a catalyst for reorganizing the company's administration. Under which influence does this motivation fall?

options.A: Social considerations
options.B: Functional considerations
options.C: Existing conditions
options.D: Economics
options.E: Aesthetics
options.F: Regulations

questions.explanation: The economics influence covers the financial reasons projects get started, such as a growing market, a grant or subsidy, a tax incentive or a competitor's collapse, and it notes that executives often use a decision to build or renovate as a catalyst for organizational or administrative change. Social considerations are about public needs met by public facilities, such as schools and libraries, not about reorganizing a company.

questions.question: During Problem Seeking's Step 2, Collect and Analyze Facts, the owner's operations director insists that her views on staffing needs be recorded as facts. How should the programmer handle them?

options.A: Record them as facts, since the owner's staff know the operation best
options.B: Evaluate and test them as opinions, and avoid preconceptions
options.C: Discard them, since only measured data may enter the program
options.D: Hold them for Step 4, when needs are weighed against the budget
options.E: Treat them as goals and move them back to Step 1
options.F: Record them as concepts to be tested in Step 3

questions.explanation: In collecting facts, the programmer must present them clearly and objectively, avoid preconceptions, and evaluate and test opinions, keeping only information that bears directly on the defined goals. The director's views are opinions to be tested, not facts to record as given. Throwing them out is also wrong: measurable facts are easier to evaluate, but opinions are tested rather than discarded.

questions.question: Programming concepts address performance problems, while design concepts address design problems. Which item is a design concept rather than a programming concept?

options.A: Flexibility
options.B: Service grouping
options.C: Demountable partitions
options.D: Energy conservation
options.E: Convertibility
options.F: Phasing

questions.explanation: Programming concepts are abstract functional answers to performance problems with no physical form, while design concepts are physical answers to design problems. Flexibility, service grouping, energy conservation and phasing are recurring programming concepts. Convertibility is a programming concept too; the demountable partition is the design concept that responds to it.

questions.question: In Problem Seeking's Step 4, Determine Needs, when does a wants-versus-needs confrontation occur?

options.A: When the owner defines the problem as architectural solutions, not functional requirements
options.B: When the owner defines the problem as functional requirements, not architectural solutions
options.C: When the owner sets the budget before the space requirements have been determined
options.D: When the owner ranks economic goals above aesthetic, social and environmental ones
options.E: When the owner understands its functional needs but fails to relate them to its finances
options.F: When the programmer evaluates the owner's assumptions for feasibility

questions.explanation: A clash between wants and needs arises when the owner states the problem as architectural solutions, such as a particular building or room, instead of as functional requirements; the programmer must then find and test the assumptions behind those solutions. Stating the problem as functional requirements is the goal, not the cause. Determining needs is the first economic feasibility test, separating real needs from the wish list.

questions.question: A programmer is drafting the problem statements for a facility program in Problem Seeking's Step 5, State the Problem. Which practices are recommended?

options.A: Include universal aspects common to all facilities so that nothing is missed
options.B: Describe the preferred building forms so the A/E grasps the intended image
options.C: Limit the key issue statements to unique aspects of the problem
options.D: State the owner's goals only in quantitative terms so they can be measured
options.E: State the key issues in performance terms so form is not ruled out
options.F: Organize the key issues by building element rather than by category

questions.explanation: Key issue statements should cover only what is unique about this problem, not aspects common to every facility, and should ideally be written in performance terms so they do not rule out different expressions of form, which is the A/E's job. Describing preferred building forms does exactly that. Goals are stated in both quantitative and qualitative terms, and statements are grouped by category, such as function, form, economics, regulations, social, environmental and time.

questions.question: A clinic program lists three floor-finish requirements: (1) occupants should sense cleanliness and order, (2) the finish must resist repeated scrubbing without degrading, and (3) the finish must be easy to clean. In order, which performance factor groups do these fall under?

options.A: Amenity/comfort, durability, operational/maintenance
options.B: Health/safety, durability, operational/maintenance
options.C: Amenity/comfort, operational/maintenance, durability
options.D: Operational/maintenance, durability, amenity/comfort
options.E: Amenity/comfort, durability, health/safety
options.F: Health/safety, operational/maintenance, durability

questions.explanation: A sense of cleanliness and order affects the occupants' comfort and pleasure, so it is an amenity/comfort factor. Resisting repeated scrubbing is about the material holding up against a degrading influence, which makes it durability. Ease of cleaning is operational/maintenance, because operational factors describe how easy something is to do, while what happens to the material when it is done is a durability factor.

questions.question: An owner's project budget is being split into hard and soft costs. Which items are hard costs?

options.A: Utility connection fees
options.B: Furniture, fixtures and equipment
options.C: Due diligence costs, including site surveys
options.D: Cost of extending utilities to the site
options.E: Demolition costs
options.F: Hazardous material abatement costs

questions.explanation: Hard costs are the tangible parts of the finished project: extending utilities to the site, demolition, construction, and permanent fixtures and equipment. Utility connection fees, due diligence such as surveys, furniture, fixtures and equipment, and hazardous material abatement are all soft costs. The site purchase price itself is often treated as a separate cost that is neither hard nor soft.

questions.question: Before programming, a state agency's construction budget for a new office building is fixed by a legislative act. What is this construction budget method called?

options.A: Available funds
options.B: Authorized funds
options.C: Estimated funds by cost per measured unit
options.D: Component cost
options.E: Bond issue funds
options.F: Owner's contingency

questions.explanation: Authorized funds are construction funds approved by a public agency or a legislative act for a public project, which is what a state agency's budget fixed by statute is. Available funds is simply the amount a private owner wants to spend, and the cost-per-measured-unit method multiplies a count of units, such as square feet or hotel rooms, by a unit cost.

questions.question: During project conception, the owner's consultant drafts a project schedule with broad time blocks for programming, site acquisition and design. The owner's CFO objects that these tasks are not construction. Which statements about this schedule are accurate?

options.A: It is substantially broader than the construction schedule
options.B: Precise milestone dates must be fixed now so that approvals can proceed
options.C: Programming and site acquisition belong in the construction schedule instead
options.D: More detail is added as project conception tasks are completed
options.E: Both {A} and {D}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: {E} is right. The project schedule drafted during conception is much broader than the construction schedule: it covers programming, site studies and acquisition, design and more, with construction as just one part. Precise milestone dates often cannot be set that early, so it starts as broad time blocks and gains detail as conception tasks are completed. Programming and site acquisition do not belong in the contractor's construction schedule.

questions.question: A specifier is sorting the evaluation criteria for a resilient flooring product into attribute categories. Which criteria are sustainability attributes rather than physical properties, performance, or safety and protection?

options.A: Dimensional stability
options.B: Moisture vapor transmission rate
options.C: Smoke propagation
options.D: Low embodied energy
options.E: Recycled content
options.F: Thermal resistance

questions.explanation: Low embodied energy and recycled content are sustainability attributes, along with criteria such as regional production, recyclability and good indoor air quality; a project may also require products that meet a chosen green building rating system. Dimensional stability and thermal resistance are measurable physical properties, moisture vapor transmission rate is a performance criterion, and smoke propagation falls under fire safety.

questions.question: What has been the primary motivation behind the evolution of project delivery methods beyond the traditional sequence of design, bid and build?

options.A: Shifting design liability from the A/E to the contractor's side of the team
options.B: Delivering projects as fast as possible while keeping the design's quality
options.C: Increasing price competition so owners always get the lowest construction cost
options.D: Reducing the number of specialized participants needed to deliver a facility
options.E: Replacing architects and engineers as the designers of most projects
options.F: Giving owners a way to avoid competitive bidding by contractors

questions.explanation: Delivery methods have evolved mainly to deliver projects as quickly as possible while keeping the quality of the design. Owners pay a financial cost for every day the facility is not available, so they want it built fast in order to start recouping their investment. Every method still relies on many specialized designers, contractors and subcontractors, so reducing participants or replacing the A/E is not the aim.

questions.question: A school board member says 'project delivery' just means the construction schedule. Which description matches how project delivery is defined?

options.A: The overlapping of design and construction phases to shorten the time from concept to occupancy of the facility
options.B: The procurement process by which the owner obtains a price and then awards the contract for construction
options.C: The sequence of design phases that carries a project from programming through the construction documents
options.D: The contractual relationships that engage design and construction to deliver a completed, occupied facility
options.E: The sequence of life cycle stages that runs from project conception through facility management
options.F: The management option an owner adds to oversee one or more phases of the project life cycle

questions.explanation: Project delivery means the contractual relationships needed to engage design and construction so that a conceptual idea becomes a completed, occupied facility; it is the whole assembly of people and services involved. Overlapping design and construction to save time is fast-track scheduling, a scheduling technique used within delivery methods. Bidding and award is the procurement step, and design phases or life cycle stages are parts of the process, not its definition.

questions.question: An owner's next facility will be several times larger and more complex than anything it has built before. What should the owner expect?

options.A: More participants and a more intensive construction process, with a direct bearing on the delivery method
options.B: The same participants as before, since extent affects only the cost and time needed for the work
options.C: Fewer participants per unit of floor area, since larger projects gain economies of scale in staffing
options.D: No effect on the delivery method, since the extent of work is defined only after a method is chosen
options.E: More participants, though the project's extent has no bearing on the choice of delivery method
options.F: The same delivery method as before, since the owner's past experience alone decides the method

questions.explanation: A project's size and complexity bear directly on how it is delivered: the type of project, its extent, cost and required speed are among the factors that decide the delivery method. A much larger, more complex facility draws in more participants and a more demanding construction process. Extent is therefore not just a matter of cost and time, and past experience alone does not settle the method.

questions.question: Who generally establishes the time needed for a project's design and construction, and in what document?

options.A: The contractor, in the progress schedule it submits after contract award
options.B: The A/E, in the design schedule it prepares during schematic design
options.C: The owner, in the project schedule prepared during project conception
options.D: The construction manager, in a master schedule made in preconstruction
options.E: The A/E, in the schedule of services in the Owner-A/E Agreement
options.F: The owner's lender, in the construction loan agreement for the project

questions.explanation: The owner generally sets the time for design and construction, in the project schedule it develops during project conception, because that time is a significant cost to the owner. The contractor's progress schedule comes much later and must fit the contract time, which runs from the notice to proceed to substantial completion. The A/E and construction manager help refine the schedule but do not set the overall time.

questions.question: An owner wants a $3,000-per-day penalty for late completion in the agreement and offers nothing for early completion. What is the risk?

options.A: The penalty is unenforceable unless paired with a bonus
options.B: The penalty must be deducted from each progress payment
options.C: The penalty automatically doubles as liquidated damages
options.D: The penalty voids the contractor's right to time extensions
options.E: The penalty must equal the owner's documented financial loss
options.F: The penalty is enforceable only on single-prime contracts

questions.explanation: A daily penalty for late completion is best paired with a bonus for early completion, usually at the same daily amount, and courts have held that a delay penalty is unenforceable without such a bonus. Liquidated damages are a different tool: an agreed amount that estimates the owner's real loss from delay, and an arbitrary amount not tied to loss can itself be struck down as a penalty.

questions.question: An owner adds a shared-savings clause to a cost-plus contract with a GMP. What should the A/E anticipate?

options.A: More substitutions to review, possibly justifying added A/E fees
options.B: Less submittal review, since the contractor carries overrun risk
options.C: Design responsibility for substituted items shifting to the contractor
options.D: A savings split fixed by law, whatever the agreement says
options.E: A GMP set below estimated cost to leave room for savings
options.F: Shorter review times, since the contractor pre-checks substitutions

questions.explanation: A shared-savings clause gives the contractor an agreed share of the difference between the GMP and the actual cost, so the contractor looks hard for cheaper materials, products and systems. The A/E should expect many substitutions to review, which can take longer than normal and may justify additional A/E fees. The incentive increases review work rather than reducing it, and the GMP is usually set somewhat above the estimate, not below it.

questions.question: During bidding on a design-bid-build project, which activities are legitimate ways for a product representative to help?

options.A: Selecting which certified installer the contractor must hire to install the specified product
options.B: Prequalifying the general contractor bidders on the owner's behalf for this product's installation
options.C: Helping subcontractors and suppliers make sure their bids are based on the specified products
options.D: Issuing written clarifications of the specified product's requirements directly to all bidders
options.E: Identifying which installers are certified or approved to install the specified product
options.F: Accepting competing products as equals for bidders who ask before the bid date

questions.explanation: A product representative supplies accurate technical information, can identify which installers are certified or approved for the product, and can help subcontractors and suppliers make sure their bids are based on the specified products. Identifying qualified installers is not choosing one, which stays the contractor's decision. Clarifications to bidders go out from the A/E by addendum, and the A/E, not the rep, decides whether a competing product is acceptable.

questions.question: Which of the following are NOT benefits of the design-bid-build delivery method?

options.A: Roles and contract relationships that are familiar and well understood by all
options.B: A shorter total duration, because design and construction phases can overlap
options.C: Schedules that are easier to establish, because the phases do not overlap
options.D: Suitability for owners that lack staff with construction or bidding expertise
options.E: The owner may expect the project to be built for the bid or proposed price
options.F: Contractor input on constructability throughout the design phases

questions.explanation: Design-bid-build is valued for its familiar roles and well-understood contracts, the owner's right to expect the work built for the bid or proposed price, easier scheduling because phases do not overlap, and its suitability for owners without construction staff. Overlapping phases to save time is the opposite of its linear sequence, and the lack of contractor input during design is a known weakness of the competitive bid option, not a benefit.

questions.question: A contractor won a competitively bid design-bid-build project at a very tight price, then finds an omission in the documents. Why is this especially likely to become a change order or claim under this option?

options.A: The contractor priced partially complete documents and must fill in the blanks during construction
options.B: The A/E has no duty to interpret the documents once the bid has become the contract sum for the work
options.C: The owner usually carries no contingency for scope inconsistencies, and low bids leave little margin
options.D: The owner's GMP contingency belongs to the contractor and is drawn down first to cover any omissions
options.E: The contractor reviewed the design during the design phases and so accepted the omission as its own
options.F: Low-bid contractors are barred from seeking change orders, so a claim is the only remedy for omissions

questions.explanation: Under the competitive bid option, the contractor usually cannot count on the owner carrying a contingency for scope-of-work inconsistencies, and a low bid leaves little margin for error, so every error or omission tends to become a change order, claim or dispute. Pricing partially complete documents is a problem of the negotiation option, not the bid option, and low-bid contractors are not barred from requesting change orders.

questions.question: Under which design-bid-build options may the owner choose to take part in evaluating and selecting subcontractors and suppliers?

options.A: The competitive bid option and the negotiation option
options.B: The negotiation option only, because no bids are taken
options.C: All three, including the competitive bid and proposal options
options.D: The competitive proposal option and the negotiation option
options.E: The competitive bid option only, since bidders list their subcontractors
options.F: None of them, since the contractor alone selects its subcontractors

questions.explanation: Under the competitive proposal and negotiation options, the owner may take part in evaluating and selecting subcontractors and suppliers, just as it may prefer certain contractors. Under the competitive bid option, choosing the low bidder also means accepting whatever subcontractors and suppliers that bidder plans to use, and the owner has no say in how the contractor buys out the work.

questions.question: A hospital system that negotiates all its work with one trusted contractor is weighing a flooring product well suited to its operations. What added value can the product representative offer this owner?

options.A: A negotiated unit price that binds the contractor's flooring subcontractor on future projects
options.B: Data on features, budget pricing and availability that can become part of the owner's standards
options.C: Approval of the flooring as an equal, so later projects need no further product evaluation
options.D: A sole-source warranty that replaces the contractor's correction-period obligations
options.E: A guaranteed maximum price for the flooring that the owner carries into negotiation
options.F: A design-assist role that lets the owner make flooring selections without its A/E

questions.explanation: A product with lasting benefits or a close fit with the owner's operations can open an ongoing relationship, and the rep can supply data on features, budget pricing and availability that may become part of the owner's standards. A rep cannot bind a subcontractor's future prices, approve its own product as an equal, or replace the contractor's correction obligations; those decisions belong to the parties to the contracts.

questions.question: Under the design-bid-build negotiation option, which results does early cooperation among the A/E, contractor and subcontractors produce?

options.A: Ambiguities are cleared up before documents and agreements are prepared, so costs are more accurate
options.B: Price competition among several qualified bidders keeps the negotiated contract sum as low as possible
options.C: The owner knows the final construction cost before it commits financially to the project
options.D: The contract sum is fixed early, so later design development cannot affect the time or cost
options.E: Mutual product selections and choices of construction technique become possible
options.F: The contractor takes over the A/E's responsibility for the design's constructability

questions.explanation: When the contractor joins early in a negotiated project, cooperation among the A/E, contractor and subcontractors makes joint product selections and choices of construction technique possible, and it clears up ambiguities before the documents and agreements are written, which gives more accurate costs. The owner does not know the final cost before committing; that is a known drawback of negotiating. The contractor advises on constructability but does not take over the design.

questions.question: A negotiated price was set on partially complete documents. As the construction documents are finished, the contractor asks for more money for detailed work that was implied but not shown when it priced. How should the team view this request?

options.A: As barred outright, since a negotiated price covers all work reasonably inferable from any of the drawings
options.B: As a substitution request, to be handled under the Division 01 product substitution procedures
options.C: As a bid-day surprise, to be resolved by redesigning and rebidding the remaining scope of work
options.D: As a known risk, since without a record of what the price covered, assuming it was included may be unfair
options.E: As included work, since the A/E may expect any contractor to anticipate and price the implied scope
options.F: As an allowance adjustment, to be settled against the cash allowances specified in Division 01

questions.explanation: When a negotiated price is set on partially complete documents, the contractor may ask for adjustments as the design is finished, and what the price covered is not always obvious. The A/E may expect the contractor to have priced work that was implied but not shown, but without documentation of what was included, assuming it was covered may be unfair. That is why it is a known risk, not work automatically included or automatically barred.

questions.question: Negotiated contracts aim for the shortest time at the lowest cost while keeping the specified quality, but normally not all three can be achieved. Which are usually the primary considerations?

options.A: Construction cost
options.B: Construction quality
options.C: Construction time
options.D: Project extent
options.E: Ultimate project cost
options.F: Interim financing charges

questions.explanation: Negotiated contracts try for the shortest time and lowest cost at the specified quality, but usually only two of the three can be had, and quality and time are normally the primary considerations. Construction cost is therefore what typically gives way and rises. The ultimate project cost may still fall, through savings in interim financing charges and income from earlier use of the facility.

questions.question: How does the product representative's role on a construction manager at risk project compare with design-bid-build?

options.A: Reps work only through the A/E, since the CMAR has no role until the construction phase begins
options.B: The CMAR, involved during design, may bring reps in for product decisions and design-assist
options.C: Reps contract directly with the owner, since CMAR procurement is conducted open book
options.D: Reps prepare the bid packages, since the CMAR issues several separate work packages
options.E: Reps take over product selection from the A/E, since the CMAR holds the design contract
options.F: Reps become prime contractors to the owner for their products under the CMAR

questions.explanation: Product reps are a resource under CMAR just as under design-bid-build, but because the CMAR is involved during design, it may bring reps in for their expertise on material, product and equipment decisions, and reps may take part in design-assist. Open-book procurement means the owner sees how the CMAR selects subcontractors and suppliers; the owner still contracts only with the CMAR, not with reps or suppliers.

questions.question: On a design-build project, the owner's project requirements say nothing about roofing, and a roofing rep wants its premium membrane used. Whom should the rep mainly work with, and why?

options.A: The design-builder and its A/E, since unstated material choices are usually left to the design-builder
options.B: The owner directly, since the owner selects all materials under a design-build agreement
options.C: The owner's bridging A/E, since it remains the architect/engineer of record through construction
options.D: The authority having jurisdiction, since it approves the material selections on design-build work
options.E: The owner, by change order, since unstated material choices default to the owner
options.F: The owner's facility manager, since the owner's standards fill any gaps in its requirements

questions.explanation: Unless the owner's project requirements say otherwise, material selections are usually left to the design-builder, so the rep should work closely with the design-builder and its A/E to offer products that meet those requirements. The owner does not select every material under design-build; if it later wants to change or upgrade a material, a change order will likely be needed. A bridging A/E is not the architect/engineer of record.

questions.question: An owner's design-build requirements say nothing about shop drawings, samples, testing or extended warranties. Which statements are accurate?

options.A: The design-builder typically performs no services outside the owner's project requirements
options.B: The design-builder's A/E protects the owner's interest just as on a conventional project
options.C: These items may not be provided unless codes, regulations or the requirements call for them
options.D: The general conditions supply these items automatically, as on design-bid-build
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: {E} is right. A design-builder typically does nothing beyond the owner's project requirements, so items usually taken for granted, such as shop drawings, samples, testing and inspection and extended warranties, might never reach the owner unless codes, regulations or the requirements call for them. The design-builder's A/E works for the design-builder, so the owner should not expect the protection it gets when it contracts with the designer directly.

questions.question: Which of the following does an owner-builder need in order to realize the cost savings of owner-build?

options.A: In-house experience and expertise to perform all of a contractor's duties
options.B: Financial backing to absorb the risk of problems or losses in construction
options.C: An independent A/E retained for full construction contract administration
options.D: Performance and payment bonds that cover the entire project
options.E: In-house architects so that design errors stay under the owner's control
options.F: A single general contractor to hold all of the specialty trade contracts

questions.explanation: Owner-build saves money only if the owner has the in-house experience and expertise to perform all of a contractor's duties and the financial backing to absorb problems or losses during construction, along with good working relationships with its specialty contractors. Owner-builders often limit or drop A/E construction administration, bonding each contractor does not bond the whole project, and designing in-house leaves no recourse for errors in the documents.

questions.question: A retail chain designs its stores with in-house architects and builds them as owner-builder. A detailing omission causes roof leaks. Which limitation of owner-build does this illustrate?

options.A: The specialty prime contractors become liable for the design once they install the work
options.B: There is no outside party to hold responsible for errors or omissions in the documents
options.C: The building permit shifts responsibility for the omission to the authority having jurisdiction
options.D: The performance bonds on each prime contract will cover the cost of correcting design errors
options.E: The in-house architects' professional insurance covers the owner for the design omission
options.F: Each specialty contractor must correct the omission at its own cost under its warranty

questions.explanation: When an owner-builder also designs in-house, it has no one to hold responsible for errors, discrepancies or omissions in the construction documents; an owner who hires an independent A/E gets an experienced, licensed and insured designer. The specialty contractors are not liable for a design they only built. Bonding each contractor covers that contractor's own performance, not design errors, and still does not bond the whole project.

questions.question: Which statements about selecting the project delivery method are accurate?

options.A: It should be set early because design and construction may occur concurrently
options.B: Most owners rely on advice from an A/E, CM or contractor to choose it
options.C: The applicable building codes depend on which method is selected
options.D: The A/E's fee cannot be negotiated until the contractor has been chosen
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: {E} is right. The delivery method should be settled early in design because some methods overlap design and construction, and most owners rely on an experienced A/E, construction manager or contractor to help choose it, weighing cost, complexity, time and market conditions. The building codes that apply do not depend on the method, and the A/E is usually selected independently of the construction team, so its fee does not wait on the contractor.

questions.question: When assembling the project team, which owner action enhances successful, harmonious relations among the participants?

options.A: Issuing a clear, concise project schedule that allows everyone adequate time
options.B: Selecting every participant through the same competitive low-fee process
options.C: Making the A/E the sole decision-maker over every participant's work
options.D: Requiring all participants to have worked together on an earlier project
options.E: Letting the contractor set the design schedule for all of the participants
options.F: Compressing each participant's time so that the schedule stays aggressive

questions.explanation: A clear, concise project schedule that gives every participant adequate time to do the job properly is what promotes successful, harmonious relations on the team. Compressing everyone's time works against that. Good teams also need participants with the education, experience and skills to work in concert, which a uniform low-fee process or a past history together does not guarantee.

questions.question: Under which delivery method is the owner not involved in selecting the A/E of record?

options.A: Construction manager at risk
options.B: Design-bid-build negotiation option
options.C: Design-build
options.D: Owner-build
options.E: Integrated project delivery
options.F: Construction manager as advisor

questions.explanation: The owner selects the A/E under every delivery method except design-build, where the design-builder picks the A/E (when it has none in-house) and the owner is not involved. Under construction manager at risk, the owner still selects the A/E, although it may hire the construction manager first and ask for its help in choosing.

questions.question: An owner that has built several facilities sends a request for proposal to only one A/E firm. What does this signal, and what does the owner save?

options.A: A closed competition, which saves the cost of seating an independent jury
options.B: Direct selection, which saves research, interviews and documentation
options.C: Qualifications-based selection, which saves the owner a fee negotiation
options.D: Fee-based selection, which saves the owner from checking firm references
options.E: An open competition, which saves the owner a shortlisting step
options.F: Direct selection, which saves the owner marketing and presentation costs

questions.explanation: Sending a request for proposal to just one A/E means the owner intends to negotiate the design agreement directly, a common route for owners with design and construction experience. Direct selection saves the owner research, interviews and detailed documentation of requirements. The A/E is the one that saves marketing and presentation costs, so that version names the wrong party's savings.

questions.question: A county reviews A/E proposals with special attention to the qualifications of each firm and its key people, treating the proposed fee as secondary. Which method is this, and what follows?

options.A: Qualifications-based, so the firm chosen may not have the lowest fee
options.B: Fee-based, so the firm chosen must have the lowest responsive fee
options.C: Best-value, so the firm chosen must have the lowest total project cost
options.D: Direct selection, so the firm chosen needs no interview or shortlist
options.E: Qualifications-based, so no fee proposal is requested in the RFP
options.F: Fee-based, so the firms' qualifications are not considered at all

questions.explanation: In qualifications-based selection, the owner decides mainly on the qualifications of the firm and its key people, with the proposed fee as a secondary consideration, so the firm chosen may not have the lowest fee. A fee proposal can still be part of the request for proposal. Fee-based selection reverses the priority, making the fee the deciding factor while still considering qualifications.

questions.question: A city seeking a landmark library invites four preselected firms to submit design solutions, to be judged by a panel of architects. What kind of selection is this?

options.A: An open design competition, since an independent jury judges all of the entries
options.B: Qualifications-based selection, since the firms were screened before submitting
options.C: Hybrid fee-based selection, since only a shortlist of firms is allowed to compete
options.D: A closed design competition, aimed at the best aesthetic and technical solution
options.E: A design-build competition, since the firms submit proposed design solutions
options.F: Direct selection, since the city negotiates with a small group of firms

questions.explanation: When only a preselected group of firms may submit designs, it is a closed design competition; an open competition accepts proposals from any A/E. Both aim to choose the best aesthetic and technical solution for a high-profile project, often with a jury of peers judging the entries. Screening firms first does not make it qualifications-based selection, because the designs themselves are what is judged.

questions.question: A bidder qualification form covers physical and financial capability. Which inquiry does NOT belong on it?

options.A: Trade, bank and surety references for the bidder's company
options.B: Claims, suits and any failures to complete earlier projects
options.C: The markup the bidder plans to add to subcontractor prices
options.D: Licenses the company holds to perform the work requested
options.E: A financial statement showing the company's financial standing
options.F: Completed and ongoing projects and key individuals' experience

questions.explanation: A bidder qualification form asks about the company's background and principals, licenses, experience including claims, suits and failures to complete work, trade, bank and surety references, financial statements, and references for past projects. Those show physical and financial capability. How much the bidder plans to mark up subcontractor prices is its own pricing strategy, not a qualification item.

questions.question: When a general contractor prepares a competitive bid, how do subcontractors compete?

options.A: Subcontractors compete with general contractors for the whole project by bidding to the owner
options.B: Each unit of specialized work has its own price competition among subcontractors in that trade
options.C: The owner holds one competition across all trades and awards each unit of work to the low bidder
options.D: Subcontractors compete on qualifications only, while price competition is left to the contractors
options.E: Subcontractors compete only after award, when the contractor buys out each trade's work
options.F: One subcontractor per trade is named in the specifications, so its price is set by negotiation

questions.explanation: Most construction contracts break down into units of specialized work, and within each one subcontractors in that trade compete on price; the general contractor's bid is built from those prices. Subcontractors do not bid the whole project to the owner, and an owner awarding each trade's work directly describes multiple-prime contracting, not subcontracting under a general contractor.

questions.question: An owner using design-build hires its own architect to prepare bridging documents before engaging a design-builder. Which statements about that architect are correct?

options.A: It is not the architect of record and the design-builder cannot retain it
options.B: It becomes the architect of record once the design-build contract is signed
options.C: It is assigned to the design-builder to finish the construction documents
options.D: It must be the design-builder's in-house architect to avoid split liability
options.E: The owner may keep it on to oversee quality assurance and control
options.F: It prepares the bridging documents from the design-builder's criteria

questions.explanation: Under the bridging option, the owner's design A/E prepares the bridging documents from the owner's criteria or program; it is not the architect/engineer of record, and the design-builder may not hire it. The owner may keep it on to oversee quality assurance and quality control during design, construction or contract administration. The design-builder's own A/E picks up where the bridging documents stop and completes the construction documents.

questions.question: Which would schematic design drawings NOT be expected to begin describing?

options.A: Code and life-safety requirements for the design
options.B: Major building systems such as structure and HVAC
options.C: Spatial relationships and functional characteristics
options.D: Fabrication and installation details for components
options.E: Size, shape and volume of the project
options.F: Materials proposed for the project

questions.explanation: Schematic design drawings give the concept an organized form and begin to describe its aesthetics, size, shape and volume, spatial relationships, functions, code and life-safety needs, materials and major building systems. They are not technical drawings, so fabrication and installation details for components come much later, in the construction documents and shop drawings.

questions.question: The contractor's quality assurance and quality control processes start from different points. Which pairing is correct?

options.A: QA starts with inspecting installed work, and QC starts with preparing and reviewing the submittals
options.B: QA starts with the notice to proceed, and QC starts with the first test by an independent agency
options.C: QA starts with visiting the site to learn its conditions, and QC starts with supervising and directing the work
options.D: QA starts with supervising and directing the work, and QC starts with visiting the site to learn its conditions
options.E: QA starts with taking field measurements, and QC starts with scheduling and coordinating the trades
options.F: QA starts with documenting design decisions, and QC starts with verifying the constructability

questions.explanation: The contractor's quality assurance begins when it visits the site to learn the conditions it will work under, and continues through field measurements, coordination, scheduling, inspection of installed work before later work covers it, and submittals. Its quality control comes from its duty to supervise and direct the work, including control of means, methods, techniques and sequences. The reversed pairing is the common trap.

questions.question: A slump test is run on concrete still in the mixer truck before it is placed. Under the idea that quality processes run concurrently, how is this test classified?

options.A: Quality assurance only, because it happens before the concrete becomes part of the work
