options.A: Work, Drawings, and Project Manual
options.B: Drawings only, not work or project manual
options.C: Drawings and Project Manual, not work
options.D: None of them, as all are general terms
options.E: Work and Drawings, not project manual
options.F: Project Manual only, as a bound volume

questions.explanation: Work is capitalized when it means the work of this specific contract, Drawings when it means the graphic portion of the contract documents, and Project Manual when it means the bound volume of this set of construction documents. All three refer to this contract here, so all three take capitals; they stay lowercase only in the general sense.

questions.question: In specification text, 'Specifications' is capitalized when it refers to:

options.A: Every document bound in the project manual
options.B: The sections in Divisions 01–49
options.C: Only the technical sections in Divisions 02–49
options.D: A manufacturer's published product specifications
options.E: The sections in Divisions 00 and 01 only
options.F: The project manual and the Drawings together

questions.explanation: Capitalized, Specifications means the sections in Divisions 01 through 49, the Specifications Group. Division 00 procurement and contracting documents are bound in the project manual but are documents, not specifications. Division 01 is included even though only Divisions 02 through 49 are called technical specifications.

questions.question: In specification text, 'Government' is capitalized when:

options.A: A government agency is a party to the contract
options.B: A government agency has enforcement authority over the project
options.C: It refers to federal laws and regulations
options.D: It appears in a defined term in Division 01
options.E: It refers to the employees of any public owner
options.F: A public agency reviews the documents for a permit

questions.explanation: Government takes a capital only when a government agency is one of the parties to the contract, such as a public owner. An agency that merely enforces regulations over the project is an authority having jurisdiction, a separate term with its own capitalization, and federal laws or permit reviews in general do not make the word capitalized.

questions.question: Which phrase follows standard specification rules for numbers?

options.A: 2 3-inch screws
options.B: two three-inch screws
options.C: two 3-inch screws
options.D: 2 three-inch screws
options.E: two (2) 3-inch screws
options.F: two 3-in. screws

questions.explanation: When one number states a quantity and the next states a size, the quantity is written as a word and the size in numerals, as in 'three 1/2-inch holes', so 'two 3-inch screws' is correct. Dimensions always take numerals, so 'three-inch' is wrong, and repeating a number in parentheses, as in 'two (2)', is unnecessary.

questions.question: Which temperature is written correctly for a specification?

options.B: ten degrees C (fifty degrees F)
options.C: 10 deg C (50 deg F)
options.D: 10 degrees C (50 degrees F)
options.E: ten degrees C (50 degrees F)
options.F: 10 degrees C (50°F)

questions.explanation: Temperatures always take numerals, and the degree symbol is one of the symbols not to use in specifications, so the form is '10 degrees C (50 degrees F).' 'Degrees F' is an accepted abbreviation exception, but 'deg' is not, and spelling the numbers out as words breaks the numerals rule.

questions.question: Which time and date is written correctly for a specification?

options.B: 2:10 p.m. on June 15th, 2021
options.C: 2:10 PM on June 15, 2021
options.D: 2:10 PM on June 15th, 2021
options.E: two-ten p.m. on June 15, 2021
options.F: 2:10 p.m. on June fifteenth, 2021

questions.explanation: Clock times and dates are written in numerals, the 'th' is left off the day, and time is abbreviated a.m. or p.m. in lowercase with periods, giving '2:10 p.m. on June 15, 2021.' Each of the other choices breaks one of those rules: 'June 15th', capital PM, or a time or day spelled out in words.

questions.question: Which work-hours phrase follows recommended specification style?

options.A: between 7:00 a.m. and 12:00 p.m.
options.B: between 7 a.m. and noon
options.C: between 7:00 a.m. and noon
options.D: between 7 a.m. and 12 p.m.
options.E: between seven a.m. and noon
options.F: between 7 AM and noon

questions.explanation: Unneeded zeroes are left out of time and money references, so 7 a.m. rather than 7:00 a.m. (and $200 rather than $200.00). Clock times are otherwise written in numerals, but noon and midnight are the stated exceptions and are written as words. The accepted abbreviation for time is a.m. or p.m., not AM, so 'between 7 a.m. and noon' is the correct form.

questions.question: Fractions in specification text are written:

options.A: As single characters, such as ¼
options.B: As decimals, such as 0.25
options.C: In words, such as one-quarter inch
options.D: With individual keys, such as 1/4
options.E: In superscript and subscript fonts
options.F: As decimals without a zero, such as .25

questions.explanation: Fractions are typed with individual keys, such as 1/4 and 1/2, and not converted to superscript or subscript fonts or single special characters such as ¼. Special characters can garble when files move between software programs and blur in poor printing. Decimals are for decimal values, and a decimal under one takes a leading zero.

questions.question: Which statements are recommended rules for numbers in specifications?

options.A: Use numerals whenever possible.
options.B: When numbers give both size and quantity, write the quantity as a word.
options.C: Spell out numbers from one to nine.
options.D: Write percentages in words, such as twenty percent.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: Arabic numerals are used whenever possible because they are easy to identify, and the quantity is written as a word only when numbers give both size and quantity, as in 'three 1/2-inch holes.' Percentages always take numerals, as in '20 percent', and spelling out one to nine is a general-writing convention that specifications do not follow.

questions.question: Which is written correctly for a specification?

options.A: Limit moisture content to 19 percent.
options.B: Limit moisture content to nineteen percent.
options.C: Limit moisture content to 19%.
options.D: Limit moisture content to 19 pct.
options.E: Limit moisture content to 19 percent (19%).
options.F: Limit moisture content to nineteen (19) percent.

questions.explanation: Percentages always take numerals, and the % symbol is one of the symbols not to use in specifications, so the numeral is followed by the word: '19 percent.' 'Pct.' is not an accepted abbreviation exception, spelling the number out breaks the numerals rule, and repeating the value in parentheses adds marks that should be minimized.

questions.question: Which statements reflect recommended practice for abbreviations in specifications?

options.A: Use abbreviations only on drawings and schedules where space is limited.
options.B: Limit abbreviations to five or fewer letters.
options.C: Spell out a term once in each section and abbreviate it afterward.
options.D: Prefer abbreviations even when they save only one or two characters.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: Abbreviations belong only on drawings and schedules where space is limited, and they should be five letters or fewer. Abbreviating a short word to save only one or two characters should be avoided, and when in doubt, spell it out. Spelling a term out once and abbreviating it afterward is a common habit, but it is not the recommended rule.

questions.question: Which line follows the accepted exceptions for abbreviations in specifications?

options.A: Start at 8 AM E.S.T. Test to 150 p.s.i.
options.B: Start at 8 a.m. E.S.T. Test to 150 psi.
options.C: Start at 8 a.m. EST. Test to 150 psi.
options.D: Start at 8 AM EST. Test to 150 p.s.i.
options.E: Start at 8 a.m. EST. Test to 150 p.s.i.
options.F: Start at 8 AM EST. Test to 150 psi.

questions.explanation: The accepted abbreviation exceptions write time as a.m. and p.m., time zones as EST without periods, and units of measure such as psi without periods, so 'Start at 8 a.m. EST. Test to 150 psi.' is correct. Periods inside EST or psi, or a capitalized AM, depart from those accepted forms.

questions.question: Specification writers should avoid abbreviations that:

options.A: Save only one or two characters
options.B: Name organizations, such as ASTM
options.C: Have five or fewer letters
options.D: Are defined in Division 01
options.E: Are units of measure, such as psi
options.F: Are part of a company's legal name

questions.explanation: An abbreviation of a short word that saves only one or two characters should be avoided; when in doubt, spell it out. Five or fewer letters is the recommended maximum length for an abbreviation, not a reason to avoid one, and organization names such as ASTM, units such as psi and parts of legal company names are accepted exceptions.

questions.question: Abbreviations with more than one meaning should be avoided unless they are:

options.A: Defined once in the supplementary conditions or in Division 01
options.B: Used in different disciplines where context makes the meaning clear
options.C: Listed in the US National CAD Standard
options.D: Written in capital letters with no periods, as for ASTM
options.E: Defined on each drawing sheet where they appear in the set
options.F: Limited to five or fewer letters and written without periods

questions.explanation: An abbreviation that has several meanings is acceptable only when it is used in different disciplines where the context makes its meaning clear. Defining it, listing it in the National CAD Standard or keeping it short does not remove the ambiguity, so otherwise it should be avoided, and when in doubt, spell it out.

questions.question: Which of the following should not be used in specifications?

options.A: Relative pronouns such as 'which'
options.B: Pronouns of every kind
options.C: Demonstrative pronouns such as 'this'
options.D: Personal pronouns
options.E: The word 'same' used as a pronoun
options.F: The word 'provide' for furnish and install

questions.explanation: Personal pronouns should not be used at all, and 'same' should never stand in as a pronoun; repeating the noun avoids misunderstanding. Pronouns in general are to be minimized or avoided, and relative pronouns such as 'which' used sparingly if at all, so those are cautions rather than outright bans. 'Provide' is an accepted term meaning furnish and install.

questions.question: Which sentences follow recommended pronoun practice for specifications?

options.A: Remove rejected units and replace them with new units.
options.B: Remove rejected units and replace same at no cost.
options.C: Remove rejected units and provide acceptable units.
options.D: Install toilet accessories purchased under allowances in Section 01 21 00.
options.E: Both {C} and {D}
options.F: {A}, {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: 'Them' is a personal pronoun, which should not be used, and 'same' should never be used as a pronoun, so both of those sentences fail. Repeating the noun, as in 'provide acceptable units', avoids any doubt. The accessories sentence is also preferred: it avoids the relative pronoun in 'accessories which are to be purchased' and the needless 'Contractor shall.'

questions.question: A section says 'Furnish fire extinguishers.' Under the standard definitions of these terms, the Contractor must:

options.A: Supply and deliver them to the site, ready for installation
options.B: Install extinguishers the Owner supplies
options.C: Supply, deliver, and install them, complete and ready for use
options.D: Supply them, and install only those shown on the Drawings
options.E: Select models and submit them for the Owner to purchase
options.F: Pay for them from a cash allowance only

questions.explanation: Furnish means to supply the item and deliver it to the site, ready to be installed; it does not include installing it. Install means to put in position for service or use, and provide means furnish and install, complete and ready for use. The project states these definitions in the supplementary conditions or Division 01.

questions.question: A door needs a glass sidelight at each jamb, left and right. Which wording states that intent?

options.A: Provide glass sidelights on either side of the door.
options.B: Provide glass sidelights on both sides of the door.
options.C: Provide a glass sidelight at either jamb of the door.
options.D: Provide glass sidelights on any side of the door.
options.E: Provide glass sidelights on one or both sides of the door.
options.F: Provide glass sidelights at all sides of the door.

questions.explanation: 'Either' implies a choice between two options, while 'both' is all-inclusive. 'Glass sidelights on either side of the door' could be read as allowing a sidelight on just one side, so 'both sides' states the intent of one at each jamb. 'Any side' and 'all sides' are vague for a door that has only two jambs.

questions.question: 'Repair any cracks' differs from 'Repair cracks' because 'any':

options.A: Changes nothing; the two mean the same
options.B: Extends the requirement to every crack, however small
options.C: Limits the repair to visible cracks
options.D: Could mean only the cracks the Contractor selects
options.E: Requires the A/E to identify the cracks to repair
options.F: Turns the requirement into a performance criterion

questions.explanation: 'Any' is imprecise in number and leaves discretion to the reader, so 'repair any cracks' could be read as only the cracks the contractor chooses. 'Repair cracks' means all cracks. That is why 'any', along with 'all' and 'such', appears among words to avoid in specifications; it does not broaden the requirement.

questions.question: A draft reads 'Seal joints and/or penetrations,' and both are to be sealed. Which revision follows good specification practice?

options.A: Seal joints or penetrations.
options.B: Seal joints and/or penetrations, both required.
options.C: Seal joints and penetrations.
options.D: Seal any joints and penetrations.
options.E: Seal joints, and penetrations as required.
options.F: Seal all joints and penetrations.

questions.explanation: 'And/or' is not recommended because it lets the contractor decide whether it means 'and' or 'or', so the intent should be stated with one word. Since both joints and penetrations must be sealed, 'and' is correct. Adding 'any' brings back the reader's discretion, 'all' is usually unnecessary, and 'as required' leaves out who requires it.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'amount' and 'quantity' correctly in a specification?

options.A: Record the amount of fill placed and the quantity paid.
options.B: Record the quantity of fill placed and the amount paid.
options.C: Record the amount of fill placed and the amount paid.
options.D: Record the quantity of fill placed and the quantity paid.
options.E: Record the amount of fill placed and the balance paid.
options.F: Record the quantity of fill placed and the remainder paid.

questions.explanation: 'Amount' is for money, and 'quantity' is for numbers, linear measure, area or volume. Fill is measured by volume, so it takes 'quantity', and the payment is money, so it takes 'amount.' Swapping them, or using one word for both, misuses the terms, and 'balance' or 'remainder' does not state what was paid.

questions.question: Which statement reflects recommended specification usage of 'flammable' and 'inflammable'?

options.A: Use 'flammable'; the two mean the same thing
options.B: Use 'flammable'; 'inflammable' means not combustible
options.C: Use 'inflammable'; it is the legal term
options.D: Use either; neither is preferred
options.E: Use 'inflammable'; 'flammable' means not combustible
options.F: Use neither; write 'combustible' instead

questions.explanation: Flammable and inflammable mean exactly the same thing, even though 'inflammable' sounds like the opposite, and 'flammable' is the preferred word. Saying either one means not combustible is wrong, and treating them as an open choice misses the stated preference for 'flammable.'

questions.question: Which sentence uses insure, assure, and ensure correctly?

options.A: Ensure the Work against fire. Insure joints are watertight.
options.B: Insure the Work against fire. Assure joints are watertight.
options.C: Assure the Work against fire. Ensure joints are watertight.
options.D: Insure the Work against fire. Ensure joints are watertight.
options.E: Assure the Work against fire. Insure joints are watertight.
options.F: Ensure the Work against fire. Assure joints are watertight.

questions.explanation: To insure means to issue or obtain an insurance policy, so the Work is insured against fire. To ensure means to make certain in a way that rules out error, so the Contractor ensures joints are watertight. To assure means to give a person confidence or convince them of something, which fits neither instruction.

questions.question: Specification writers avoid 'as required', as in 'Install blocking as required', because it:

options.A: Should be written 'as per requirements' instead
options.B: Must be set off by commas
options.C: Leaves out who or what does the requiring
options.D: Puts the sentence in the indicative mood
options.E: Is a foreign-language expression
options.F: Uses an article that should be omitted

questions.explanation: 'As required' is a phrase with a missing object, like 'as indicated', 'as directed' and 'as necessary': it never says required by whom or by what, so the requirement is unclear. Rewriting it as 'as per requirements' does not help, because 'as per' is itself an expression to avoid, and the phrase has nothing to do with mood or commas.

questions.question: Which sentences follow recommended practice on unnecessary words?

options.A: Protect finished surfaces from damage.
options.B: Store millwork under shelter.
options.C: Protect all finished surfaces from damage.
options.D: Spread an adhesive with a trowel on the floor.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: The word 'all' is usually unnecessary, and the articles 'the', 'a' and 'an' can be left out in most specification sentences. 'Protect finished surfaces from damage' and 'Store millwork under shelter' follow that. 'Protect all finished surfaces' adds a needless 'all', and the adhesive sentence is padded with articles; 'Spread adhesive with trowel on floors' says the same thing.

questions.question: Which expressions are on the standard list of words and expressions to avoid in specifications?

options.A: At no additional cost
options.B: When ambient temperature is above 40 degrees F
options.C: Within manufacturer's recommended time limit
options.D: To the satisfaction of the Architect
options.E: In a workmanlike manner
options.F: Furnish and install

questions.explanation: 'To the satisfaction of the architect/engineer' and 'in a workmanlike manner' are on the list of expressions to avoid, along with 'etc.', 'as per', 'also' and 'shall function as intended.' The other phrases are acceptable and appear in recommended wording, and furnish and install are defined terms.

questions.question: 'Also provide blocking as necessary.' How many of the words and phrases that specifiers are advised to avoid does it contain?

options.A: None
options.B: One
options.C: Two
options.D: Three
options.E: Four
options.F: Five

questions.explanation: The sentence has two: 'also' is on the list of words and expressions to avoid, and 'as necessary' is a phrase with a missing object, since it never says necessary to whom or for what. 'Provide' is an accepted term meaning furnish and install, and 'blocking' is just the item being specified, so the count is two.

questions.question: Which sentences use the parallel structure recommended for specifications, with the same grammatical form in both parts of the compound?

options.A: Inspect welds to verify size and to confirm placement.
options.B: Perform tests to determine strength and to establish quality.
options.C: Inspect welds to verify size and confirm placement.
options.D: Inspect welds verifying size and to confirm placement.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: Both parts of a compound should have the identical grammatical structure, so each infinitive keeps its own 'to': 'to verify size and to confirm placement', 'to determine strength and to establish quality.' Dropping the second 'to' is treated as incorrect in specification writing, and mixing a participle such as 'verifying' with an infinitive breaks the parallel.

questions.question: Which version is preferred for a specification?

options.A: Each of the anchors are to be set in grout.
options.B: Set each anchor in grout.
options.C: Each of the anchors shall be set in grout.
options.D: Each of the anchors is to be set in grout.
options.E: Each of the anchors must be set in grout.
options.F: All of the anchors are to be set in grout.

questions.explanation: 'Each of the anchors are' pairs a singular subject with a plural verb. 'Is to' fixes the agreement but is not recommended, and 'shall be set' gives a duty to anchors, which cannot have one. The preferred form is a short, direct imperative with correct agreement: 'Set each anchor in grout.'

questions.question: Which spelling choices follow recommended practice for contract documents?

options.A: Facia rather than fascia
options.B: Gauge rather than gage
options.C: Catalog rather than catalogue
options.D: Thru rather than through
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: When two spellings are equally correct, the shorter is preferred in contract documents: facia, gage, molding and catalog. That makes 'gauge rather than gage' backwards. Shortcuts invented for brevity, such as 'thru', are not acceptable spellings, so 'through' is written in full.

questions.question: A section says 'Provide door hardware.' Using the standard specification definitions, the Contractor must:

options.A: Supply and deliver it to the site, ready for installation
options.B: Install hardware that the Owner supplies
options.C: Furnish and install it, complete and ready for the intended use
options.D: Coordinate the hardware supplier's own installation crew on site
options.E: Furnish it only, with the installation by the Owner's forces
options.F: Select the hardware and submit it for the Owner's purchase

questions.explanation: 'Provide' is the accepted specification shorthand for furnish and install, so the Contractor supplies the hardware, delivers it and installs it, complete and ready for its intended use. Supplying and delivering only is 'furnish', and placing items someone else supplies is 'install.' These definitions are stated in the supplementary conditions or Division 01.

questions.question: In specifications, what does 'furnish' mean?

options.A: Supply, deliver, and install, complete and ready for use
options.B: Place in position for service or use
options.C: Make available at the factory for the installer to collect
options.D: Supply and deliver to the site, ready for installation
options.E: Purchase and hold off site until installation is scheduled
options.F: Select and submit the product for the A/E's approval

questions.explanation: To furnish is to supply an item and deliver it to the project site, ready to be installed; it stops short of installation. Supplying, delivering and installing, complete and ready for use, is 'provide', and placing an item in position for service or use is 'install.' EJCDC C-700 1.02.E gives the same meaning to furnish.

questions.question: The Owner buys lockers and has them delivered to the site. Which verb states the Contractor's duty for them?

options.A: Install
options.B: Provide
options.C: Furnish
options.D: Supply
options.E: Perform
options.F: Coordinate

questions.explanation: 'Install' means to put an item in position for service or use, which is all that is left once the Owner has bought and delivered the lockers. 'Provide' means furnish and install, so it would make the Contractor buy them as well, and 'furnish' covers only supplying and delivering, which the Owner has already done.

questions.question: A section says 'Provide fire extinguishers.' What must the Contractor do?

options.A: Deliver them to the site for the Owner's staff to mount
options.B: Install extinguishers that the Owner supplies
options.C: Furnish and install them, complete and ready for use
options.D: Select models for the Owner to purchase
options.E: Pay for them out of a cash allowance only
options.F: Inspect and certify existing extinguishers

questions.explanation: 'Provide' means furnish and install: the Contractor supplies the extinguishers, delivers them and mounts them, complete and ready for their intended use. Delivering them only would be 'furnish', and mounting extinguishers the Owner supplies would be 'install.' Nothing in 'provide' limits payment to an allowance.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700, the documents give the Contractor a duty for some equipment but never say furnish, install, perform, or provide. What must the Contractor do?

options.A: Furnish it only, since installation is not stated
options.B: Install it only, if the Owner supplies it
options.C: Request an interpretation, since the duty is undefined
options.D: Furnish and install it, complete and ready for use
options.E: Perform services for it only, without supplying it
options.F: Provide it only where it is shown on the Drawings

questions.explanation: C-700 says that when the documents set a Contractor duty for services, materials or equipment without using any of those four words, the Contractor furnishes and installs them complete and ready for intended use. The silence is not read as a furnish-only or install-only duty, and it does not make the requirement undefined.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700, what do terms such as 'as directed' and 'as approved' in the Contract Documents do?

options.A: Authorize the Engineer's professional judgment on the Work
options.B: Give the Engineer authority to direct the Contractor's methods
options.C: Let the Contractor choose methods, subject to later review
options.D: Make the Engineer's decision final and binding on both parties
options.E: Require the Owner's written approval before work proceeds
options.F: Make the Engineer responsible for supervising the Work

questions.explanation: C-700 1.02.B says these terms authorize the Engineer's professional judgment, used to evaluate the Work for compliance with the Contract Documents and the design concept. It states they give the Engineer no duty or authority to supervise or direct the Work, which rules out directing the Contractor's methods or supervising the Work.

questions.question: Which expressions are phrases with a missing object, to be avoided in specifications?

options.A: In lieu of
options.B: Hereinafter
options.C: As directed
options.D: Such
options.E: As required
options.F: Etc.

questions.explanation: 'As directed', 'as required', 'as approved', 'as indicated' and similar phrases have missing objects: directed by whom, required by what. The other choices are also avoided, but for other reasons: 'in lieu of' is a foreign expression, 'hereinafter' is an adverb to avoid, 'such' is an article to avoid, and 'etc.' is a word to avoid.

questions.question: In SectionFormat terms, what is a section?

options.A: One of the three groups of information in a Division
options.B: A subject within a Part made up of related paragraphs
options.C: One of the 50 standard categories in MasterFormat
options.D: A portion of a Division that specifies work results
options.E: A subdivision of a Group made up of related Divisions
options.F: The written documents prepared for a construction contract

questions.explanation: SectionFormat defines a section as a portion of a Division that specifies work results, identified by a MasterFormat number and title and included in the project manual as the project needs. One of the 50 standard categories is a Division, one of the three groups of information in a section is a Part, and a subject within a Part is an Article.

questions.question: Within a section, what is SectionFormat's hierarchy from highest to lowest?

options.A: Article, Part, paragraph, subparagraph
options.B: Part, Article, paragraph, subparagraph
options.C: Part, paragraph, Article, subparagraph
options.D: Part, Article, subparagraph, paragraph
options.E: Article, paragraph, Part, subparagraph
options.F: Paragraph, Article, Part, subparagraph

questions.explanation: Each section has three Parts, each Part has one or more Articles, each Article has one or more paragraphs, and a paragraph may have subparagraphs. PageFormat uses the same order for its outline levels, with the Part as the highest level, so any order that puts the Article or paragraph above the Part is wrong.

questions.question: In PageFormat, which level does an item addressed 'a.' occupy?

options.A: A paragraph, at the 2nd level
options.B: A subparagraph, at the 3rd level
options.C: A subparagraph, at the 4th level
options.D: A subparagraph, at the 5th level
options.E: A subparagraph, at the 6th level
options.F: An Article, at the 1st level

questions.explanation: PageFormat addresses the Article as 1.01 (1st level) and the paragraph as A. (2nd level), then subparagraphs as 1. (3rd), a. (4th), 1) (5th) and a) (6th). The numbered '1.' subparagraph sits just above 'a.', which is the usual mix-up, and 'a)' with a parenthesis is the 6th level.

questions.question: In PageFormat, what is a paragraph's 'address'?

options.A: The section number and title repeated in the page header
options.B: The Article title under which the paragraph is placed
options.C: The cross-reference that sends a reader to the paragraph
options.D: The characters, such as 'A.', that precede its first line
options.E: The page number combined with the section number
options.F: The temporary left margin set for the paragraph's lines

questions.explanation: PageFormat uses 'address' for the characters immediately before the first line of an Article, paragraph or subparagraph, such as 1.01, A. or 1. These addresses let a reader refer precisely to an item, as in 2.03.B.1. The page header carries the section number and title, which is a different item.

questions.question: A paragraph's last line ends up alone at the top of the next page. What does PageFormat call that line?

options.A: A widow
options.B: An orphan
options.C: A runover
options.D: A hanging line
options.E: A footer
options.F: An indent

questions.explanation: PageFormat defines a widow as the last line of a paragraph or subparagraph left alone at the top of a page. An orphan is the reverse: the first line of an Article, paragraph or subparagraph left alone at the bottom of a page. Good page layout avoids both.

questions.question: SectionFormat defines a work result as an aspect of construction achieved how?

options.A: By combining elements that together serve a common function
options.B: By purchasing products from a single manufacturer
options.C: Through a skill or trade applied to construction resources
options.D: By one subcontract awarded to a single trade
options.E: By testing products at the plant during manufacture
options.F: By stating a required end result and how it is verified

questions.explanation: A work result is a permanent or temporary part of a construction project produced by applying a particular skill or trade to construction resources, whether during construction or later through alteration, maintenance or demolition. Grouping elements that serve a common function describes UniFormat's functional elements, and a work result is not defined by a subcontract or a single manufacturer.

questions.question: Which statements about the Related Requirements list in a section's Summary article are correct?

options.A: It helps the reader find requirements specified elsewhere.
options.B: It is for information only and does not define the section's scope.
options.C: It assigns the listed work to the proper trade or subcontract.
options.D: It makes the listed sections part of this section's scope of work.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: SectionFormat says the Related Requirements cross-references are for information only, to help the reader find requirements specified elsewhere that might be expected in this section. They do not define the scope of the section, of contracts or of subcontracts, and they do not assign work to a trade.

questions.question: In SectionFormat, products to be installed 'by others' outside the contract are treated as installed by whom?

options.A: The Contractor, under another section
options.B: The supplier that furnished them
options.C: A separate prime contractor named in Division 01
options.D: The Owner
options.E: A subcontractor named in the Summary
options.F: The manufacturer's own installer

questions.explanation: Under SectionFormat, a product that 'others' will install outside the contract, or an installation marked 'not in contract', is treated as installed by the Owner. The same rule treats products furnished or supplied 'by others' as furnished by the Owner, so 'by others' never points to an unnamed separate contractor or supplier.

questions.question: A standard appears in a section's References article but is never cited in PART 2 or PART 3. What is its effect?

options.A: Its listing does not by itself require compliance
options.B: Compliance with the standard becomes mandatory
options.C: It applies to the products described in PART 2
options.D: It overrides conflicting Division 01 requirements
options.E: It applies to every section of the project manual
options.F: It governs only if Section 01 42 00 also lists it

questions.explanation: The References article fully identifies standards that are cited elsewhere in the section by an abbreviated designation, with their dates and titles. Merely listing a standard there does not necessarily require compliance with it; the requirement comes from where PART 2 or PART 3 actually cites the standard.

questions.question: Which term belongs in a section's Definitions article?

options.A: A term common to the work results that the section covers
options.B: A contract term such as Contractor or Owner
options.C: A term unique to the section and not defined elsewhere
options.D: An abbreviation used in several sections
options.E: A term already defined in Section 01 42 16
options.F: An acronym specific to this section's work

questions.explanation: A section's Definitions article is for terms unique to that section that the contract documents do not define anywhere else, not for terms common to the work results it covers. Contract terms such as Owner and Contractor come from the conditions of the contract, general definitions go in Section 01 42 16, and abbreviations and acronyms have their own article.

questions.question: A section needs only an Allowances paragraph under Price and Payment Procedures. What does SectionFormat permit?

options.A: Keep all four subordinate titles and mark the unused ones Not Used
options.B: Omit the parent Article and use Allowances as the primary Article
options.C: Move the allowance text into PART 2 with the products
options.D: State the allowance amount in this section instead of Division 01
options.E: Move the Allowances paragraph into the Summary article
options.F: Add a fourth Part titled Allowances after PART 3

questions.explanation: When only one of the subordinate titles under Price and Payment Procedures is needed, SectionFormat lets the specifier omit the parent Article and use that subordinate title, here Allowances, as a primary Article; Article titles may be raised or lowered as needed. The 'Not Used' convention is for unused Parts, and allowance amounts still belong in Division 01.

questions.question: On a unit-price project, where does SectionFormat place a section's measurement and payment requirements?

options.A: In a fourth Part titled Measurement and Payment
options.B: In PART 3, after Field Quality Control
options.C: Only in the schedule of prices on the bid form
options.D: In PART 1, under Price and Payment Procedures
options.E: In PART 2, with the product descriptions
options.F: In the supplementary conditions

questions.explanation: SectionFormat's Measurement and Payment Article sits in PART 1 under Price and Payment Procedures, and unit-price projects are told to use that Article rather than invent a non-standard fourth Part. Long or complex unit-price lists may be appended as attachments, while the technical requirements for the products and work stay in PART 2 and PART 3.

questions.question: A table in a section has a title and two columns. By SectionFormat's definition, what is it?

options.A: A list or legend that may sit in line with text
options.B: A schedule, to be placed at the end of PART 3—EXECUTION
options.C: A schedule, to be placed after END OF SECTION
options.D: A form that must be attached in Division 01
options.E: An attachment that must follow END OF SECTION
options.F: An illustration to be placed in PART 2—PRODUCTS

questions.explanation: Following the Uniform Drawing System, SectionFormat defines a schedule as a table of related items with a heading and at least three columns of related information. A table with fewer than three columns is a legend, key, index or list, and it may be placed in line with the text; schedules are often better placed at the end of the section.

questions.question: A section has a door hardware schedule as an attachment. Where does 'END OF SECTION' go?

options.A: After the attachment, as the very last line of text
options.B: Before PART 3, so the schedule ends the section
options.C: After PART 3 and before the attachment
options.D: At the end of PART 1, before the products
options.E: After PART 3, with the schedule moved into PART 1
options.F: Nowhere, since an attachment ends the section

questions.explanation: END OF SECTION comes right after PART 3 and before any attachments, and the related Part refers the reader to them. Attachments are schedules, tables, illustrations or forms that follow the end of the section for convenience or clarity, so putting END OF SECTION after the attachment, or leaving it out, is wrong.

questions.question: A project carries a cash allowance for door hardware. Where is the dollar amount stated?

options.A: In PART 1 of the door hardware section
options.B: In the Division 01 allowances section
options.C: In PART 2 of the door hardware section
options.D: In the supplementary conditions
options.E: In the Division 01 unit prices section
options.F: In the Division 01 alternates section

questions.explanation: The dollar amounts or quantities of allowances, and the procedures for handling them, are stated in Section 01 21 00 Allowances or its subordinate sections. The door hardware section has a PART 1 article that calls attention to the allowance and cross-references that Division 01 amount, while PART 2 and PART 3 describe exactly what the allowance covers.

questions.question: The standard general conditions do not fully define 'alternate.' Where does SectionFormat say the definition should go?

options.A: In Section 01 23 00 Alternates
options.B: In the instructions for procurement
options.C: In each affected section's Definitions article
options.D: In the Supplementary Conditions
options.E: In Section 01 42 16 Definitions
options.F: In the Agreement form

questions.explanation: SectionFormat notes that the meaning and use of 'alternate' and 'alternative' vary by region and between standard contracts. If the standard contract does not fully define them, the specifier puts the definitions in the Supplementary Conditions, where they modify the general conditions; Section 01 23 00 then describes the work of each alternate.

questions.question: The term 'office master specification' distinguishes an A/E's own master specification from what?

options.A: A project specification edited from it
options.B: A manufacturer-furnished guide specification
options.C: A commercially published guide specification
options.D: A government guide specification, such as HUD's
options.E: A previous project's specification kept for reference
options.F: An outline master guide specification

questions.explanation: 'Office master specification' separates an A/E's in-house master from commercially published master guide specifications, even though the office master is often built from a commercial one. The Department of Defense and HUD call their masters 'guide specifications', a separate usage, and a project specification is what gets edited from either kind of master.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, what sets Shop Drawings apart from Product Data?

options.A: Shop Drawings are specially prepared for the Work
options.B: Shop Drawings are prepared by the Architect
options.C: Shop Drawings become Contract Documents when approved
options.D: Shop Drawings show only standard catalog products
options.E: Shop Drawings are prepared only by the manufacturer
options.F: Shop Drawings require the Owner's written approval

questions.explanation: A201 3.12.1 defines Shop Drawings as drawings, schedules and other data specially prepared for the Work by the Contractor or a subcontractor, manufacturer, supplier or distributor. Product Data are standard illustrations, schedules, performance charts and brochures. Under 3.12.4 neither becomes a Contract Document, even after the Architect's review.

questions.question: A pump manufacturer's standard catalog sheet and performance curve are submitted. Under AIA A201, what is this submittal?

options.A: A Shop Drawing
options.B: A Sample
options.C: A Delegated Design Submittal
options.D: Product Data
options.E: A Certificate
options.F: A Qualification Statement

questions.explanation: A201 3.12.2 defines Product Data as illustrations, standard schedules, performance charts, instructions, brochures and similar information that show materials or equipment for part of the Work. Standard catalog information is Product Data; Shop Drawings are drawings specially prepared for this Work, and Samples are physical examples.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700, what does the word 'day' mean?

options.A: A working day, excluding weekends and legal holidays
options.B: A calendar day of 24 hours, midnight to midnight
options.C: Any 24-hour period starting when notice is received
options.D: A calendar day, excluding legal holidays
options.E: A business day from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. local time
options.F: A calendar day ending at noon on the next day

questions.explanation: C-700 1.02.C defines 'day' as a calendar day of 24 hours measured from one midnight to the next. Weekends and legal holidays are not excluded, there is no business-hours limit, and the count does not start at the hour a notice happens to arrive.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700, Work built exactly to the Contract Documents can still be 'defective' in which cases?

options.A: It shows normal wear and tear once the Owner begins using it
options.B: It uses a substitute the Engineer accepted
options.C: It is damaged before the Engineer recommends final payment
options.D: It differs from what the Owner now prefers
options.E: It fails a test or approval the Contract Documents refer to
options.F: It was installed before the Engineer's site visit

questions.explanation: C-700 1.02.D calls Work defective if it does not conform to the Contract Documents, does not meet a required inspection, reference standard, test or approval, or was damaged before the Engineer recommends final payment. The last two can apply even to Work built as drawn. Normal wear from the Owner's use and a substitute the Engineer accepted do not make Work defective.

questions.question: When 'Specifications' is capitalized in the contract documents, what does the word refer to?

options.A: The sections in Divisions 02 through 49
options.B: Every document in Divisions 00 through 49
options.C: The entire bound project manual
options.D: The sections in Divisions 01 through 49
options.E: The Division 01 General Requirements only
options.F: The sections and the Drawings together

questions.explanation: Capitalized, Specifications refers to the sections in Divisions 01 through 49. Division 01 General Requirements is included, while the Division 00 procurement and contracting documents are not specifications. The whole bound volume is the Project Manual, and only Divisions 02 through 49 are called the technical specifications.

questions.question: Which sentences follow standard specification capitalization?

options.A: Refer to Section 09 91 23 for primers.
options.B: Coordinate with the work of other Sections.
options.C: Refer to the Drawings for access panel locations.
options.D: Protect the Northwest corner of the building.
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: Section is capitalized when it refers to a specific section, such as Section 09 91 23, and Drawings when it refers to the graphic portion of the contract documents. In the general sense, as in 'other sections', the word stays lowercase, and compass directions such as northwest are not capitalized unless they form part of a proper noun.

questions.question: How should 'flammable' and 'inflammable' be treated in specifications?

options.A: They are opposites; 'inflammable' means will not burn
options.B: They mean the same thing; 'flammable' is preferred
options.C: They mean the same thing; 'inflammable' is preferred
options.D: 'Flammable' is for liquids, 'inflammable' for solids
options.E: They are opposites; 'flammable' means will not burn
options.F: They mean the same thing; neither should be used

questions.explanation: The two words have exactly the same meaning, even though 'inflammable' sounds like the opposite, and 'flammable' is the preferred word. Reading 'inflammable' as 'will not burn' is the very error the preference guards against, and neither word is reserved for liquids or solids.

questions.question: On a unit-price pipeline, fittings are paid within the linear-foot price of the pipe instead of being measured. What are such items called?

options.A: Allowance items
options.B: Lump-sum items
options.C: Subsidiary obligations
options.D: Incidental alternate items
options.E: Directly measured items
options.F: Quantity allowance items

questions.explanation: In unit-price work some items are measured directly, while others are subsidiary obligations whose cost is carried in the price of a measured item, as fittings are carried in the price per foot of pipe. Ideally the measured quantities follow how the work is performed. Allowances and lump sums are separate pricing devices, not items folded into a unit price.

questions.question: Under PageFormat, where do MasterFormat Division titles appear in a project manual?

options.A: In the heading of every section within that Division
options.B: In the page header of every specification page
options.C: On labeled dividers only, never in the contents
options.D: In the table of contents, not in section headings
options.E: On the cover page of each volume only
options.F: In the page footer of each section

questions.explanation: Division titles appear in the project manual's table of contents as an organizing device, and they should not be repeated in the section headings or in the body of the specifications. MasterFormat Subgroups, not Divisions, are what may be marked by labeled dividers or separate volumes, and Groups are not identified in the project manual at all.

questions.question: Which participants may work together to judge whether a product suits the conditions of a particular project?

options.A: The A/E, owner, and product representative
options.B: The A/E, contractor, and building official
options.C: The owner, general contractor, and installer
options.D: The A/E, AHJ, and independent testing agency
options.E: The A/E, owner, and contractor
options.F: The owner, AHJ, and product representative

questions.explanation: Few products can withstand every project's conditions, but many perform well within reasonable limits, so the A/E, the owner and the manufacturer's product representative may work together to decide whether a product fits this project. When the conditions are unusual, a custom or special product designed for them may be needed. Each other grouping leaves out the A/E or the product representative, the two parties at the center of this judgment.

questions.question: Before starting Division 00 documents and Division 01 sections, the specifier must first review:

options.A: The owner-provided conditions of the contract and agreement
options.B: The A/E's office master Division 01 sections
options.C: The consultants' draft technical sections
options.D: The front-end documents from the last similar project
options.E: The geotechnical data and existing condition information
options.F: The preliminary schedules in Section 00 31 13

questions.explanation: A specifier should never begin Division 00 documents or Division 01 sections without first carefully reviewing the owner-provided conditions of the contract and the proposed owner-contractor agreement, because those documents govern what Division 00 and Division 01 must say. The term 'front end' should be avoided in favor of 'Division 00' and 'Division 01.'

questions.question: Why are the application chapters of the Uniform Drawing System (UDS) organized by facility life-cycle stage?

options.A: So each discipline issues its own separate drawing set
options.B: So earlier graphics can be retrieved and reused later
options.C: So each stage starts with a fresh drawing set
options.D: So sheets can be numbered by MasterFormat division
options.E: So each stage follows its own CAD layer guidelines
options.F: So sheets are grouped by contractor bid package

questions.explanation: UDS presents drawings and project information in a standard form that serves planning, design, construction and operation, the stages of a facility's life. Its application chapters follow those stages so that, as a facility moves from one stage to the next, graphics made earlier can be retrieved and reused, pulling out only the information needed. Starting each stage with a fresh set defeats that aim.

questions.question: Which of the following can be inserted into the open structure of the UDS application chapters?

options.A: Line widths and their gray-scale screening
options.B: BIM exchange requirements between disciplines
options.C: Layer status fields and minor group codes
options.D: Keynotes and specifications
options.E: MasterFormat and UniFormat
options.F: Each firm's own office drawing standards

questions.explanation: UDS is built as an open structure of application chapters, so other systems can be plugged into it: MasterFormat and UniFormat, keynotes, specifications and similar special applications. Gray-scale screening of line widths belongs to the Plotting Guidelines, layer status and minor group fields to the AIA CAD Layer Guidelines, and model data exchanges to the BIM side of the National CAD Standard.

questions.question: For construction drawings, the Uniform Drawing System (UDS) establishes which of the following?

options.A: Model data exchanges between design disciplines
options.B: Specification section numbers and titles
options.C: Set content and order
options.D: Layer names, plot colors and gray-scale screening
options.E: Sheet identification and file naming
options.F: Drawing scales for each type of scaled view

questions.explanation: For a set of construction drawings, UDS sets the content and order of the set, how sheets are identified and how files are named. Layer names come from the AIA CAD Layer Guidelines, plot colors and gray-scale screening from the Plotting Guidelines, model exchanges from the BIM side of the National CAD Standard, and section numbers and titles from MasterFormat.

questions.question: The U.S. National CAD Standard combines several industry publications. Which part of it was developed by the AIA?

options.A: CAD Layer Guidelines
options.B: Uniform Drawing System
options.C: Plotting Guidelines
options.D: BIM Implementation
options.E: Foreword, Introduction, and Administration
options.F: NBIMS-US exchange standards

questions.explanation: The National CAD Standard is a consensus standard made of the National Institute of Building Sciences' foreword, introduction and administration, the AIA CAD Layer Guidelines, the Uniform Drawing System, BIM Implementation and the Plotting Guidelines. The AIA's part is the CAD Layer Guidelines, which name layers with discipline, major group, minor group and status fields. NBIMS-US is a separate BIM standard, not a part of the NCS.

questions.question: Which UDS module covers door and window reference identifiers and north arrows?

options.A: Module 3, Schedules
options.B: Module 6, Symbols
options.C: Module 7, Notations
options.D: Module 5, Terms and Abbreviations
options.E: Module 1, Drawing Set Organization
options.F: Module 2, Sheet Organization

questions.explanation: A symbol is a scaled or non-scaled graphic, drawn with little detail, that stands for a product or material. Symbols serve as reference identifiers for doors, windows and equipment and show abstract conditions such as north arrows and direction-of-view indicators, and the standard ones are in UDS Module 6, Symbols. Module 3 covers schedules, Module 5 terms and abbreviations, and Module 7 notes and keynotes.

questions.question: Which part of UDS covers sheet keynotes, where a note is replaced on the drawing by an identifying symbol?

options.A: Module 6, Symbols
options.B: Module 3, Schedules
options.C: Module 1, Drawing Set Organization
options.D: Module 7, Notations
options.E: Module 5, Terms and Abbreviations
options.F: Module 2, Sheet Organization

questions.explanation: A sheet keynote, or reference keynote, is a note that applies only to one sheet or drawing; the text is replaced by a short identifying symbol that points to the full note written elsewhere on the same sheet. It is still a note, so it falls under UDS Module 7, Notations. Module 6 covers standard symbols such as door identifiers and north arrows, and Module 3 schedules.

questions.question: Which UDS module offers a typical drawing set organization, slightly different from the traditional set?

options.A: Module 3
options.B: Module 7
options.C: Module 1
options.D: Module 6
options.E: Module 2
options.F: Module 5

questions.explanation: A traditional drawing set groups sheets by discipline and then by drawing type, such as plans, elevations and sections. UDS Module 1, Drawing Set Organization, offers a typical set organization that differs slightly from that traditional arrangement. Modules 3, 6 and 7 are Schedules, Symbols and Notations, and Module 2 covers the organization of individual sheets.

questions.question: The UDS portion of the National CAD Standard describes naming library files of standard details and schedules by:

options.A: UniFormat numbers and titles
options.B: OmniClass space numbers and titles
options.C: AIA CAD layer names and fields
options.D: Project sheet numbers and titles
options.E: MasterFormat numbers and titles
options.F: UDS sheet type designators

questions.explanation: UniFormat numbers and titles can serve as the file-naming convention for library files of standard details and schedules, as UDS describes. Library files are named differently from project files and grouped by building system, assembly or use, since that is how people search for them, and UniFormat classifies exactly those functional elements. Sheet numbers identify sheets in one project, and layer names organize data inside a CAD file.

questions.question: In the standard organization of the project manual, Solicitation belongs to which group?

options.A: Specifications, Division 01
options.B: Procurement Requirements
options.C: Revisions, Clarifications & Modifications
options.D: Contracting Requirements
options.E: Contracting Forms
options.F: Conditions of the Contract

questions.explanation: Solicitation (00 10 00), the advertisement or invitation that asks for bids or proposals, is the first heading of the Procurement Requirements, ahead of Instructions for Procurement, Available Information, and Procurement Forms and Supplements. The Contracting Requirements start at 00 50 00 with Contracting Forms, and Conditions of the Contract is one of their headings, not a group of its own.

questions.question: In the standard organization of the project manual, Instructions for Procurement belongs to which group?

options.A: Contracting Requirements
options.B: Procurement Requirements
options.C: Specifications, Division 01
options.D: Conditions of the Contract
options.E: Pre-Contract Revisions (Addenda)
options.F: Contracting Forms

questions.explanation: Instructions for Procurement (00 20 00) tell bidders or proposers how to prepare and submit their pricing, so they sit in the Procurement Requirements with Solicitation, Available Information, and Procurement Forms and Supplements. Instructions to Bidders (00 21 13) is one document under this heading. The Contracting Requirements hold the Agreement, bonds, certificates and the Conditions of the Contract that govern the work once a contract exists.

questions.question: Which of the following are headings within the Procurement Requirements of Division 00?

options.A: Available Information
options.B: Contracting Forms
options.C: Project Forms
options.D: Procurement Forms & Supplements
options.E: Supplementary Conditions
options.F: Certificates

questions.explanation: The Procurement Requirements have four headings: Solicitation, Instructions for Procurement, Available Information, and Procurement Forms and Supplements (00 10 00 to 00 40 00). Contracting Forms, Project Forms (which hold the bonds and certificates) and the Supplementary Conditions all belong to the Contracting Requirements, which start at 00 50 00.

questions.question: In Division 00, Procurement Forms and Supplements belongs to which group?

options.A: Project Forms
options.B: Contracting Requirements
options.C: Procurement Requirements
options.D: Revisions, Clarifications & Modifications
options.E: Contracting Forms
options.F: Specifications, Division 01

questions.explanation: Procurement Forms and Supplements (00 40 00) holds the bid or proposal forms and their supplements, such as the bid security form, and it is the last heading of the Procurement Requirements. Do not confuse it with Contracting Forms (the Agreement) or Project Forms (the bonds and certificates), which open the Contracting Requirements at 00 50 00 and 00 60 00.

questions.question: Which statements about the Agreement in the standard organization of construction documents are correct?

options.A: It is filed under Contracting Forms.
options.B: It is filed under Project Forms, with the bonds.
options.C: It incorporates all other contract documents by reference.
options.D: It is executed by the owner and the architect/engineer.
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: Both {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: The Agreement is the document under Contracting Forms (00 50 00); the bonds and certificates are Project Forms. It is the legal instrument signed by the owner and the contractor, not the architect/engineer, that binds them to its terms, and it brings all the other contract documents into the contract by reference, so {E} is correct.

questions.question: In Division 00, the performance bond is filed under which heading?

options.A: Procurement Forms & Supplements
options.B: Project Forms
options.C: Contracting Forms
options.D: Conditions of the Contract
options.E: Instructions for Procurement
options.F: Revisions, Clarifications & Modifications

questions.explanation: Project Forms (00 60 00) hold the performance bond, the payment bond and certificates: forms that guarantee the contractor's performance, certify compliance and help administer the contract. The bid bond is different: it is bid security, filed with the Procurement Forms and Supplements. Contracting Forms hold the Agreement.

questions.question: In Division 00, certificates (such as certificates of insurance) are filed under which heading?

options.A: Contracting Forms
options.B: Conditions of the Contract
options.C: Project Forms
options.D: Procurement Forms & Supplements
options.E: Div. 01 General Requirements
options.F: Revisions, Clarifications & Modifications

questions.explanation: Certificates are Project Forms (00 60 00), listed after the performance and payment bonds. They include certificates of insurance and certificates showing compliance with the laws and regulations that apply. Contracting Forms hold the Agreement, and Procurement Forms and Supplements hold the bid forms and bid security used before award.

questions.question: In Division 00, the General Conditions are filed under which heading?

options.A: Contracting Forms
options.B: Conditions of the Contract
options.C: Project Forms
options.D: Specifications, Division 01
options.E: Revisions, Clarifications & Modifications
options.F: Procurement Forms & Supplements

questions.explanation: The Conditions of the Contract (00 70 00) are made up of the General Conditions and the Supplementary Conditions, which define the rights, responsibilities and relationships of the parties. Division 01 General Requirements is a different document despite the similar name: it is the first division of the Specifications and holds administrative and procedural requirements.

questions.question: In the standard organization of the project manual, the Supplementary Conditions sit under which heading, in which group?

options.A: Conditions of the Contract, in Contracting Requirements
options.B: Conditions of the Contract, in Procurement Requirements
options.C: Project Forms, in Contracting Requirements
options.D: Division 01, in Specifications
options.E: Contracting Forms, in Contracting Requirements
options.F: Procurement Forms & Supplements, in Procurement Requirements

questions.explanation: The Supplementary Conditions modify the General Conditions to suit a specific project, and both are filed under Conditions of the Contract (00 70 00), the third heading of the Contracting Requirements. They are not in the Procurement Requirements, which end at 00 40 00, and they are not Project Forms, which hold the bonds and certificates.

questions.question: The heading Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications is the last heading of which group?

options.A: Procurement Requirements
options.B: Contract Drawings
options.C: Contracting Requirements
options.D: Specifications
options.E: Conditions of the Contract
options.F: Div. 01 General Requirements

questions.explanation: The Contracting Requirements run Contracting Forms, Project Forms, Conditions of the Contract, and finally Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications (00 90 00), which holds addenda, clarifications and proposals, and contract modifications. Conditions of the Contract is the heading just before it, not a group, and Division 01 opens the Specifications that follow Division 00.

questions.question: Which group or groups of the project manual are numbered in Division 00?

options.A: Procurement Requirements only
options.B: Procurement and Contracting Requirements
options.C: Contracting Requirements only
options.D: Contracting Requirements and Specifications
options.E: Procurement Requirements and Specifications
options.F: All three project manual groups

questions.explanation: Division 00, Procurement and Contracting Requirements, holds both: the Procurement Requirements at 00 10 00 to 00 40 00 and the Contracting Requirements at 00 50 00 to 00 90 00. These are documents rather than specifications, so the Specifications Group begins at Division 01 and runs through Division 49.

questions.question: Which list gives the four headings of the Procurement Requirements?

options.A: Solicitation, Instructions for Procurement, Available Information, Procurement Forms & Supplements
options.B: Instructions for Procurement, Available Information, Procurement Forms & Supplements, Project Forms
options.C: Solicitation, Instructions for Procurement, Available Information, Contracting Forms
options.D: Solicitation, Instructions for Procurement, Procurement Forms & Supplements, Addenda
options.E: Solicitation, Instructions for Procurement, Available Information, Resource Drawings
options.F: Advertisement for Bids, Instructions for Procurement, Available Information, Procurement Forms & Supplements

questions.explanation: The Procurement Requirements are Solicitation, Instructions for Procurement, Available Information, and Procurement Forms and Supplements (00 10 00 through 00 40 00): solicit, instruct, inform, then the forms. Advertisement for Bids is one document under Solicitation, Contracting Forms open the Contracting Requirements, and addenda are filed under Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications.

questions.question: Which list gives the four headings of the Contracting Requirements, in order?

options.A: Contracting Forms, Project Forms, Conditions of the Contract, Revisions/Clarifications/Modifications
options.B: Contracting Forms, Conditions of the Contract, Project Forms, Revisions/Clarifications/Modifications
options.C: Contracting Forms, Project Forms, Revisions/Clarifications/Modifications, Conditions of the Contract
options.D: Project Forms, Contracting Forms, Conditions of the Contract, Revisions/Clarifications/Modifications
options.E: Contracting Forms, Conditions of the Contract, Revisions/Clarifications/Modifications, Project Forms
options.F: Project Forms, Contracting Forms, Revisions/Clarifications/Modifications, Conditions of the Contract

questions.explanation: The order follows the Division 00 numbers: Contracting Forms (00 50 00), Project Forms (00 60 00), Conditions of the Contract (00 70 00), then Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications (00 90 00). A memory aid: sign it, secure it, govern it, change it. The bonds and certificates in Project Forms come before the Conditions, not after them.

questions.question: Which list contains only items filed under Project Forms?

options.A: Agreement, Performance Bond, Payment Bond
options.B: Performance Bond, Payment Bond, Certificates
options.C: Performance Bond, Payment Bond, Supplementary Conditions
options.D: Bid Bond, Performance Bond, Payment Bond
options.E: Performance Bond, Payment Bond, Certificates, Agreement
options.F: Payment Bond, Certificates, General Conditions

questions.explanation: Project Forms include the performance bond, the payment bond, and certificates such as insurance certificates. The Agreement has its own heading, Contracting Forms; the bid bond is bid security, filed with the Procurement Forms and Supplements; and the General and Supplementary Conditions belong under Conditions of the Contract.

questions.question: The Agreement, the performance and payment bonds, the certificates, the General and Supplementary Conditions, and the bid form all appear in Division 00. Which of them are filed under Contracting Forms?

options.A: The Agreement and both bonds
options.B: The Agreement and the General Conditions
options.C: The Agreement and the Certificates
options.D: Only the Agreement
options.E: The Agreement and the bid form
options.F: The Agreement and the Supplementary Conditions

questions.explanation: Of these documents, only the Agreement is filed under Contracting Forms (00 50 00); it is the legal instrument that binds the owner and contractor. The bonds and certificates have their own heading, Project Forms; the General and Supplementary Conditions are Conditions of the Contract; and the bid form is a procurement form used before award.

questions.question: In the standard organization of Division 00, the Conditions of the Contract consist of which documents?

options.A: General Conditions and Supplementary Conditions
options.B: General Conditions, Supplementary Conditions, and Division 01
options.C: General Conditions and the Agreement
options.D: General Conditions, Supplementary Conditions, and the bonds
options.E: General Conditions only
options.F: General Conditions, Supplementary Conditions, and Addenda

questions.explanation: The Conditions of the Contract are the General Conditions, standard provisions that apply to almost any project, and the Supplementary Conditions, which modify them for the specific project. Division 01 belongs to the Specifications, the Agreement to Contracting Forms, the bonds to Project Forms, and addenda to Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications.

questions.question: Which of the following are NOT part of the Procurement Requirements?

options.A: Solicitation
options.B: Procurement Forms & Supplements
options.C: Available Information
options.D: Project Forms
options.E: Instructions for Procurement
options.F: Contracting Forms

questions.explanation: The Procurement Requirements hold Solicitation, Instructions for Procurement, Available Information, and Procurement Forms and Supplements (00 10 00 to 00 40 00). Contracting Forms (the Agreement) and Project Forms (the bonds and certificates) are the first two headings of the Contracting Requirements, at 00 50 00 and 00 60 00.

questions.question: Which of the following are NOT part of the Contracting Requirements?

options.A: Contracting Forms
options.B: Available Information
options.C: Project Forms
options.D: Conditions of the Contract
options.E: Revisions, Clarifications & Modifications
options.F: Div. 01 General Requirements

questions.explanation: The Contracting Requirements have four headings: Contracting Forms (00 50 00), Project Forms (00 60 00), Conditions of the Contract (00 70 00), and Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications (00 90 00). Available Information, such as geotechnical data, belongs to the Procurement Requirements, and Division 01 General Requirements opens the Specifications.

questions.question: Which statements about the Project Forms heading are correct?

options.A: The Performance Bond is listed under it.
options.B: The Agreement is listed under it.
options.C: Certificates are listed under it.
options.D: The Payment Bond is listed under it.
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: Project Forms include the performance bond, the payment bond and certificates, the forms that guarantee the contractor's performance, certify compliance and help administer the contract, so {F} is correct. {E} leaves out the payment bond. The Agreement is filed separately, under Contracting Forms.

questions.question: Which list gives the subgroups of MasterFormat's Specifications Group in numerical order?

options.A: Facility Construction, General Requirements, Facility Services, Process Equipment, Site & Infrastructure
options.B: General Requirements, Facility Construction, Facility Services, Site & Infrastructure, Process Equipment
options.C: General Requirements, Facility Services, Facility Construction, Site & Infrastructure, Process Equipment
options.D: General Requirements, Facility Construction, Site & Infrastructure, Facility Services, Process Equipment
options.E: General Requirements, Facility Construction, Facility Services, Process Equipment, Site & Infrastructure
options.F: General Requirements, Site & Infrastructure, Facility Construction, Facility Services, Process Equipment

questions.explanation: In division order: General Requirements (Division 01), Facility Construction (02-19), Facility Services (20-29), Site and Infrastructure (30-39), and Process Equipment (40-49). A memory aid: set the rules, build the building, service it, work the site, then equip the process plant. Site work comes after the building services, not before them.

questions.question: Counting the General Requirements Subgroup (Division 01), how many subgroups make up MasterFormat's Specifications Group?
questions.explanation: There are five: General Requirements (Division 01), Facility Construction (02-19), Facility Services (20-29), Site and Infrastructure (30-39), and Process Equipment (40-49). Four is the count only if Division 01 is left out. Sixteen and fifty count divisions, not subgroups: the Specifications Group alone spans division numbers 01 through 49.

questions.question: The Division 00 heading Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications covers three kinds of documents. Which list gives them in their Division 00 order, which is also the order in which they arise on a project?

options.A: Precontract revisions (addenda), clarifications and proposals, contract modifications
options.B: Contract modifications, clarifications and proposals, precontract revisions (addenda)
options.C: Precontract revisions (addenda), contract modifications, clarifications and proposals
options.D: Clarifications and proposals, precontract revisions (addenda), contract modifications
options.E: Clarifications and proposals, contract modifications, precontract revisions (addenda)
options.F: Contract modifications, precontract revisions (addenda), clarifications and proposals

questions.explanation: Precontract revisions come first (00 91 00): addenda made before the agreement is signed, usually before bids or proposals are received. Clarifications and proposals (00 93 00), such as requests for information and proposal requests, start changes not yet made part of the contract. Contract modifications (00 94 00), such as change orders, change directives and minor changes, then formally change it.

questions.question: Which heading comes first in the Procurement Requirements?

options.A: Solicitation
options.B: Instructions for Procurement
options.C: Available Information
options.D: Procurement Forms & Supplements
options.E: Introductory Information
options.F: Contracting Forms

questions.explanation: Solicitation (00 10 00), the advertisement or invitation to bid, comes first, then Instructions for Procurement, Available Information, and Procurement Forms and Supplements: solicit, instruct, inform, then the forms. Introductory Information, such as the title page and table of contents, comes ahead of the Procurement Requirements and is not one of their headings.

questions.question: In the Procurement Requirements, which heading comes directly after Instructions for Procurement?

options.A: Contracting Forms
options.B: Available Information
options.C: Solicitation
options.D: Procurement Forms & Supplements
options.E: Resource Drawings
options.F: Conditions of the Contract

questions.explanation: The order is Solicitation (00 10 00), Instructions for Procurement (00 20 00), Available Information (00 30 00), then Procurement Forms and Supplements (00 40 00): solicit, instruct, inform, then the forms. Available Information, such as geotechnical data and existing condition information, comes before the bid forms that bidders fill in.

questions.question: Which heading comes last in the Procurement Requirements?

options.A: Procurement Forms & Supplements
options.B: Solicitation
options.C: Instructions for Procurement
options.D: Available Information
options.E: Contracting Forms
options.F: Pre-Contract Revisions (Addenda)

questions.explanation: Procurement Forms and Supplements (00 40 00), with the bid forms and bid security form, closes the Procurement Requirements; Contracting Forms (00 50 00) then opens the Contracting Requirements. Addenda are not a Procurement Requirements heading: they are filed under Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications at the end of the Contracting Requirements.

questions.question: Which order of the Procurement Requirements headings is correct?

options.A: Solicitation, Instructions, Procurement Forms & Supplements, Available Information
options.B: Solicitation, Available Information, Instructions, Procurement Forms & Supplements
options.C: Solicitation, Instructions, Available Information, Procurement Forms & Supplements
options.D: Instructions, Solicitation, Procurement Forms & Supplements, Available Information
options.E: Instructions, Solicitation, Available Information, Procurement Forms & Supplements
options.F: Solicitation, Available Information, Procurement Forms & Supplements, Instructions

questions.explanation: The headings run Solicitation (00 10 00), Instructions for Procurement (00 20 00), Available Information (00 30 00), and Procurement Forms and Supplements (00 40 00). A memory aid: solicit, instruct, inform, then the forms. The forms that bidders fill in come last, after the information they need to price the work.

questions.question: Which of the following are main headings of the Contracting Requirements, rather than documents filed under one of those headings?

options.A: Contracting Forms
options.B: Agreement
options.C: Certificates
options.D: Revisions, Clarifications & Modifications
options.E: General Conditions
options.F: Performance Bond

questions.explanation: The four main headings are Contracting Forms (00 50 00), Project Forms (00 60 00), Conditions of the Contract (00 70 00), and Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications (00 90 00). The Agreement, the performance bond, certificates and the General Conditions are documents filed under those headings, at numbers such as 00 52 00, 00 61 00, 00 62 00 and 00 72 00.

questions.question: In the Contracting Requirements, which heading comes directly after Contracting Forms?

options.A: Conditions of the Contract
options.B: Procurement Forms & Supplements
options.C: Revisions, Clarifications & Modifications
options.D: Project Forms
options.E: Solicitation
options.F: Div. 01 General Requirements

questions.explanation: The order is Contracting Forms (00 50 00), Project Forms (00 60 00), Conditions of the Contract (00 70 00), then Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications (00 90 00). So the bonds and certificates in Project Forms come right after the Agreement, ahead of the General and Supplementary Conditions.

questions.question: Which heading comes last in the Contracting Requirements?

options.A: Revisions, Clarifications & Modifications
options.B: Project Forms
options.C: Conditions of the Contract
options.D: Contracting Forms
options.E: Supplementary Conditions
options.F: Div. 01 General Requirements

questions.explanation: Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications (00 90 00) comes last, after Conditions of the Contract (00 70 00). It holds the documents that change the others: addenda, clarifications and proposals, and contract modifications. The Supplementary Conditions are a document under Conditions of the Contract, and Division 01 begins the Specifications.

questions.question: Within Project Forms, which order is correct?

options.A: Payment Bond, Performance Bond, Certificates
options.B: Performance Bond, Payment Bond, Certificates
options.C: Performance Bond, Certificates, Payment Bond
options.D: Certificates, Performance Bond, Payment Bond
options.E: Payment Bond, Certificates, Performance Bond
options.F: Certificates, Payment Bond, Performance Bond

questions.explanation: Bond forms (00 61 00) come before certificates and other forms (00 62 00), and within the bonds the performance bond form (00 61 13.13) comes before the payment bond form (00 61 13.16). A memory aid: the contractor performs the work, then gets paid, and the certificates come last.

questions.question: In Division 00, which heading comes directly after Procurement Forms and Supplements?

options.A: Available Information
