options.B: Project Forms
options.C: Contracting Forms
options.D: Agreement
options.E: Conditions of the Contract
options.F: Instructions for Procurement

questions.explanation: Procurement Forms and Supplements (00 40 00) ends the Procurement Requirements, and Contracting Forms (00 50 00) opens the Contracting Requirements. The Agreement is a document filed under Contracting Forms, not the heading itself, and Project Forms (00 60 00) comes after Contracting Forms.

questions.question: In Division 00, which heading comes directly after the Supplementary Conditions?

options.A: Contract Modifications
options.B: Div. 01 General Requirements
options.C: Certificates
options.D: Revisions, Clarifications & Modifications
options.E: General Conditions
options.F: Contract Drawings

questions.explanation: The Supplementary Conditions (00 73 00) end the Conditions of the Contract, and Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications (00 90 00) follows as the last heading of the Contracting Requirements. Division 01 General Requirements is the tempting choice, but it comes only after all of Division 00 ends. Contract modifications are one category inside 00 90 00, not the heading itself.

questions.question: In the project manual, which group comes directly after the last Division 00 heading, Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications?

options.A: Div. 02-19 Facility Construction
options.B: Supplementary Conditions
options.C: Contract Drawings
options.D: Div. 01 General Requirements
options.E: Procurement Requirements
options.F: Project Forms

questions.explanation: Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications (00 90 00) ends Division 00, and the Specifications Group then begins with Division 01 General Requirements. Facility Construction starts only at Division 02, and the contract drawings are a separate set that is not bound in the project manual.

questions.question: Of the following, which is listed last under Project Forms?

options.A: Agreement
options.B: General Conditions
options.C: Payment Bond
options.D: Certificates
options.E: Performance Bond
options.F: Supplementary Conditions

questions.explanation: Under Project Forms, the bond forms (00 61 00: performance bond, then payment bond) come first and certificates (00 62 00) follow them. The Agreement belongs to Contracting Forms, and the General and Supplementary Conditions belong to the Conditions of the Contract, which come after Project Forms.

questions.question: In the standard arrangement of construction documents, the three written groups of the project manual come first in Division order, followed by the drawings that become part of the contract and then the drawings furnished for reference only. Which order is correct?

options.A: Procurement requirements, contracting requirements, specifications, resource drawings, contract drawings
options.B: Procurement requirements, contracting requirements, specifications, contract drawings, resource drawings
options.C: Contracting requirements, procurement requirements, specifications, contract drawings, resource drawings
options.D: Procurement requirements, specifications, contracting requirements, contract drawings, resource drawings
options.E: Procurement requirements, contracting requirements, contract drawings, specifications, resource drawings
options.F: Contracting requirements, procurement requirements, specifications, resource drawings, contract drawings

questions.explanation: The project manual holds the procurement requirements and contracting requirements (both Division 00) and then the specifications (Divisions 01-49). The contract drawings come next because they become contract documents, and the resource drawings, which show existing conditions for reference and are not part of the contract, come last.

questions.question: Leaving aside introductory information such as the title page and table of contents, which group comes first in the project manual?

options.A: Specifications
options.B: Contracting Requirements
options.C: Procurement Requirements
options.D: Contract Drawings
options.E: Resource Drawings
options.F: Div. 01 General Requirements

questions.explanation: The Procurement Requirements (00 10 00 to 00 40 00) come first, telling bidders or proposers how pricing is solicited and submitted. The Contracting Requirements follow (00 50 00 to 00 90 00), then the Specifications starting with Division 01. The drawings are not bound in the project manual at all.

questions.question: In Division 00, which group follows the Procurement Requirements?

options.A: Contracting Requirements
options.B: Specifications
options.C: Contract Drawings
options.D: Resource Drawings
options.E: Pre-Contract Revisions (Addenda)
options.F: Div. 01 General Requirements

questions.explanation: Division 00 holds two groups: the Procurement Requirements (00 10 00 to 00 40 00) and then the Contracting Requirements (00 50 00 to 00 90 00). The Specifications, starting with Division 01, come only after both, and addenda are filed under the last Contracting Requirements heading rather than forming a group of their own.

questions.question: When the written documents of the project manual are placed ahead of the drawings, which group comes directly before the contract drawings?

options.A: Resource Drawings
options.B: Specifications
options.C: Contracting Requirements
options.D: Procurement Requirements
options.E: Pre-Contract Revisions (Addenda)
options.F: Contract Modifications

questions.explanation: The project manual ends with the Specifications (Divisions 01-49), after the procurement and contracting requirements of Division 00, so the Specifications sit right before the contract drawings. Resource drawings are reference material listed after the contract drawings, and addenda and contract modifications are revisions, not one of the groups in this sequence.

questions.question: Drawings furnished to bidders to show existing conditions, such as record drawings of an existing structure, are provided for reference and are not part of the contract. Which group of construction documents are they?

options.A: Contracting Requirements
options.B: Specifications
options.C: Resource Drawings
options.D: Contract Drawings
options.E: Shop Drawings
options.F: Addenda

questions.explanation: Resource drawings depict existing conditions or nearby construction, for example record drawings of a building already standing; they are issued with the procurement documents for reference but never become part of the contract. Contract drawings show the new work and become contract documents. Shop drawings are contractor submittals prepared during construction, and they are not contract documents either.

questions.question: Which group of construction documents shows graphically what the project will look like when complete, including the extent of its elements and how they relate, and becomes part of the contract?

options.A: Procurement Requirements
options.B: Specifications
options.C: Contract Drawings
options.D: Contracting Requirements
options.E: Resource Drawings
options.F: Revisions, Clarifications & Modifications

questions.explanation: Contract drawings are the graphic part of the contract documents: they illustrate the completed work and show the quantities, extent and relationships of its elements. Resource drawings are also drawings, but they show existing conditions for reference only and do not become part of the contract. The specifications describe the work in words, not graphically.

questions.question: Which range of divisions, including reserved numbers, makes up MasterFormat's Facility Construction Subgroup?

options.A: Divisions 20 through 29
options.B: Divisions 01 through 19
options.C: Divisions 02 through 19
options.D: Divisions 02 through 14
options.E: Divisions 02 through 49
options.F: Divisions 00 through 19

questions.explanation: Facility Construction spans Divisions 02 through 19: Division 02 Existing Conditions through Division 14 Conveying Equipment are in use, and 15 through 19 are reserved. Division 01 is not part of it, since it forms the General Requirements Subgroup by itself, and Division 20 begins Facility Services.

questions.question: Which range of divisions, including reserved numbers, makes up MasterFormat's Facility Services Subgroup?

options.A: Divisions 21 through 28
options.B: Divisions 30 through 39
options.C: Divisions 20 through 29
options.D: Divisions 20 through 39
options.E: Divisions 20 through 28
options.F: Divisions 02 through 19

questions.explanation: Facility Services spans Divisions 20 through 29: Fire Suppression (21), Plumbing (22), HVAC (23), Integrated Automation (25), Electrical (26), Communications (27), and Electronic Safety and Security (28), with 20, 24 and 29 reserved. Ranges that start at 21 or stop at 28 count only the divisions in use, and Divisions 30 through 39 are Site and Infrastructure.

questions.question: Which range of divisions, including reserved numbers, makes up MasterFormat's Site and Infrastructure Subgroup?

options.A: Divisions 40 through 49
options.B: Divisions 30 through 39
options.C: Divisions 31 through 35
options.D: Divisions 20 through 29
options.E: Divisions 31 through 39
options.F: Divisions 30 through 35

questions.explanation: Site and Infrastructure spans Divisions 30 through 39: Earthwork (31), Exterior Improvements (32), Utilities (33), Transportation (34), and Waterway and Marine Construction (35), with 30 and 36 through 39 reserved. Ranges that start at 31 or stop at 35 count only the divisions in use.

questions.question: Which range of divisions, including reserved numbers, makes up MasterFormat's Process Equipment Subgroup?

options.A: Divisions 41 through 48
options.B: Divisions 40 through 49
options.C: Divisions 30 through 39
options.D: Divisions 40 through 50
options.E: Divisions 40 through 48
options.F: Divisions 41 through 49

questions.explanation: Process Equipment is the last subgroup, Divisions 40 through 49: from Process Interconnections (40) and Material Processing and Handling Equipment (41) to Electrical Power Generation (48), with 47 and 49 reserved. Stopping at 48 counts only the divisions in use, and MasterFormat has no Division 50.

questions.question: Which statements about Division 01 are correct?

options.A: It is the first division of the Specifications Group.
options.B: It forms the General Requirements Subgroup by itself.
options.C: It is part of the Procurement and Contracting Requirements Group (Division 00).
options.D: It is the first division of the Facility Construction Subgroup.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: Both {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: Division 01 General Requirements opens the Specifications Group, and it makes up the General Requirements Subgroup on its own, so {E} is correct. It is not in Division 00, which holds the procurement and contracting documents, and the Facility Construction Subgroup begins at Division 02 Existing Conditions.

questions.question: In MasterFormat's Specifications Group, which subgroup comes directly after Facility Construction, and what division range does it cover?

options.A: Process Equipment, Div. 40-49
options.B: Facility Services, Div. 20-29
options.C: Site & Infrastructure, Div. 30-39
options.D: General Requirements, Div. 01
options.E: Facility Services, Div. 20-39
options.F: Site & Infrastructure, Div. 20-29

questions.explanation: After Facility Construction (02-19) comes Facility Services, Divisions 20 through 29. Site and Infrastructure (30-39) follows it, then Process Equipment (40-49). Facility Services stops at 29, so a 20-39 range wrongly takes in the site divisions.

questions.question: Which subgroup comes last in MasterFormat's Specifications Group?

options.A: Facility Services
options.B: Site & Infrastructure
options.C: Facility Construction
options.D: Process Equipment
options.E: General Requirements
options.F: Electrical Power Generation

questions.explanation: Process Equipment (Divisions 40-49) is the last subgroup, after General Requirements (01), Facility Construction (02-19), Facility Services (20-29), and Site and Infrastructure (30-39). Electrical Power Generation is Division 48, one division inside Process Equipment, not a subgroup of its own.

questions.question: Which of the following divisions fall in MasterFormat's Facility Services Subgroup?

options.A: Division 23 Heating, Ventilating, and Air Conditioning (HVAC)
options.B: Division 14 Conveying Equipment
options.C: Division 33 Utilities
options.D: Division 27 Communications
options.E: Division 13 Special Construction
options.F: Division 48 Electrical Power Generation

questions.explanation: Facility Services covers Divisions 20 through 29, which includes Division 23 HVAC and Division 27 Communications. Divisions 13 and 14 are Facility Construction (02-19), Division 33 Utilities is Site and Infrastructure (30-39), and Division 48 Electrical Power Generation is Process Equipment (40-49).

questions.question: Which statements about MasterFormat's Specifications subgroups are correct?

options.A: Division 08 Openings is in Facility Construction.
options.B: Division 25 Integrated Automation is in Facility Services.
options.C: Division 35 Waterway and Marine Construction is in Site & Infrastructure.
options.D: Division 14 Conveying Equipment is in Process Equipment.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: Divisions 02-19 are Facility Construction (Division 08 Openings, and also Division 14 Conveying Equipment), 20-29 are Facility Services (Division 25 Integrated Automation), and 30-39 are Site and Infrastructure (Division 35 Waterway and Marine Construction), so {F} is correct. Conveying equipment is not process equipment: Process Equipment starts at Division 40.

questions.question: Which of the following divisions fall in MasterFormat's Site and Infrastructure Subgroup?

options.A: Division 31 Earthwork
options.B: Division 02 Existing Conditions
options.C: Division 28 Electronic Safety and Security
options.D: Division 40 Process Interconnections
options.E: Division 34 Transportation
options.F: Division 22 Plumbing

questions.explanation: Site and Infrastructure is Divisions 30 through 39, so Division 31 Earthwork and Division 34 Transportation are in it. Division 02 Existing Conditions is Facility Construction, Divisions 22 and 28 are Facility Services, and Division 40 opens Process Equipment.

questions.question: Division 02 Existing Conditions falls in which MasterFormat subgroup?

options.A: Facility Services
options.B: Facility Construction
options.C: General Requirements
options.D: Site & Infrastructure
options.E: Procurement Requirements
options.F: Process Equipment

questions.explanation: Division 02 Existing Conditions opens the Facility Construction Subgroup (02-19), even though it covers surveys, demolition and site remediation; it is not in Site and Infrastructure (30-39). The existing condition information given to bidders (00 31 19, under Available Information) is a separate Procurement Requirements document, not Division 02.

questions.question: Which of the following divisions fall in MasterFormat's Facility Construction Subgroup?

options.A: Division 11 Equipment
options.B: Division 21 Fire Suppression
options.C: Division 41 Material Processing and Handling Equipment
options.D: Division 33 Utilities
options.E: Division 10 Specialties
options.F: Division 01 General Requirements

questions.explanation: Facility Construction runs from Division 02 through 19, so it includes Division 10 Specialties and Division 11 Equipment. Division 41 is Process Equipment (40-49) despite its 'Equipment' title, Division 21 is Facility Services, Division 33 is Site and Infrastructure, and Division 01 is its own General Requirements Subgroup.

questions.question: Which statements about where these MasterFormat divisions fall are correct?

options.A: Division 26 Electrical is in Facility Services.
options.B: Division 48 Electrical Power Generation is in Facility Services.
options.C: Division 28 Electronic Safety and Security is in Facility Services.
options.D: Division 33 Utilities is in Site & Infrastructure.
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: Facility Services is Divisions 20-29, so it holds Division 26 Electrical and Division 28 Electronic Safety and Security, and Division 33 Utilities is in Site and Infrastructure (30-39), so {F} is correct. Division 48 Electrical Power Generation is in Process Equipment (40-49), not with Division 26.

questions.question: Which statements about MasterFormat's Facility Construction Subgroup are correct?

options.A: Division 14 Conveying Equipment is in it.
options.B: Division 21 Fire Suppression is in it.
options.C: Division 41 Material Processing and Handling Equipment is in it.
options.D: Division 01 General Requirements is in it.
options.E: Both {A} and {D}
options.F: {A}, {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: Of these, only Division 14 Conveying Equipment is in Facility Construction (02-19). Division 21 is Facility Services (20-29), Division 41 is Process Equipment (40-49), and Division 01 is its own General Requirements Subgroup, so no combination is right.

questions.question: Which statements about MasterFormat's Site and Infrastructure Subgroup are correct?

options.A: Division 33 Utilities is in it.
options.B: Division 22 Plumbing is in it.
options.C: Division 35 Waterway and Marine Construction is in it.
options.D: Division 46 Water and Wastewater Equipment is in it.
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: Both {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: Site and Infrastructure is Divisions 30 through 39, which takes in Division 33 Utilities and Division 35 Waterway and Marine Construction, so {E} is correct. Division 22 Plumbing is Facility Services (20-29) and Division 46 Water and Wastewater Equipment is Process Equipment (40-49), even though both deal with water.

questions.question: Division 21 Fire Suppression falls in which MasterFormat subgroup, and what division range does that subgroup cover?

options.A: Site & Infrastructure, Div. 30-39
options.B: General Requirements, Div. 01
options.C: Facility Services, Div. 20-29
options.D: Facility Construction, Div. 02-19
options.E: Facility Services, Div. 20-39
options.F: Process Equipment, Div. 40-49

questions.explanation: Division 21 Fire Suppression is the first active division of Facility Services, a subgroup that covers Divisions 20 through 29 (Division 20 is reserved but still inside the range). Divisions 30-39 are Site and Infrastructure, so a 20-39 range is too wide, and Facility Construction stops at 19.

questions.question: Which of the following divisions fall in MasterFormat's Process Equipment Subgroup?

options.A: Division 14 Conveying Equipment
options.B: Division 11 Equipment
options.C: Division 33 Utilities
options.D: Division 41 Material Processing and Handling Equipment
options.E: Division 35 Waterway and Marine Construction
options.F: Division 46 Water and Wastewater Equipment

questions.explanation: Process Equipment is Divisions 40 through 49, including Division 41 Material Processing and Handling Equipment and Division 46 Water and Wastewater Equipment. Divisions 11 Equipment and 14 Conveying Equipment are Facility Construction despite their titles, and Divisions 33 and 35 are Site and Infrastructure.

questions.question: The procurement requirements belong to which of these sets: the procurement documents, the project manual, the contract documents?

options.A: Procurement documents and project manual only
options.B: Procurement documents only
options.C: All three
options.D: Procurement documents and contract documents only
options.E: Project manual only
options.F: Project manual and contract documents only

questions.explanation: Procurement requirements are bound in the project manual and issued as part of the procurement documents, but they are not contract documents: the contract documents begin with the contracting requirements and add the specifications, contract drawings and addenda. Items such as the invitation to bid and the instructions to bidders serve pricing, not the contract.

questions.question: Which statements about Available Information (such as geotechnical data) are correct?

options.A: It is part of the procurement documents.
options.B: It is bound in the project manual.
options.C: It becomes part of the contract documents.
options.D: Both {A} and {B}
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: Available Information (00 30 00) is a procurement requirement, so it is bound in the project manual and issued with the procurement documents, making {D} correct. Like the other procurement requirements, it informs bidders but is not a contract document: information the owner furnishes in anticipation of bids stays out of the contract unless the agreement specifically lists it.

questions.question: The Agreement belongs to which of these sets: the procurement documents, the project manual, the contract documents?

options.A: Contract documents only
options.B: Procurement documents and project manual only
options.C: Project manual and contract documents only
options.D: All three
options.E: Procurement documents and contract documents only
options.F: Project manual only

questions.explanation: The Agreement is a contracting requirement, and contracting requirements are in all three sets: the agreement form is bound in the project manual, issued with the procurement documents so bidders know the terms, and becomes a contract document once signed. It is the procurement requirements and any resource drawings that stay out of the contract.

questions.question: Which statements about the Supplementary Conditions are correct?

options.A: They are part of the procurement documents.
options.B: They are bound in the project manual.
options.C: They are part of the contract documents.
options.D: Both {A} and {C}
options.E: Both {B} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: The Supplementary Conditions are part of the contracting requirements, which belong to all three sets: they are issued to bidders for pricing, bound in the project manual, and become part of the contract, so {F} is correct. {E} misses that bidders receive them as part of the procurement documents.

questions.question: Specification sections in Divisions 20-29 (Facility Services) belong to which of these sets: the procurement documents, the project manual, the contract documents?

options.A: Project manual only
options.B: Procurement documents and project manual only
options.C: All three
options.D: Project manual and contract documents only
options.E: Contract documents only
options.F: Procurement documents and contract documents only

questions.explanation: All of the specifications, Divisions 01 through 49, are bound in the project manual, issued with the procurement documents for pricing, and become contract documents at the agreement. Bidders need the specifications to price the work, so they are procurement documents as well as contract documents.

questions.question: Which statements about the contract drawings are correct?

options.A: They are part of the procurement documents.
options.B: They are bound in the project manual.
options.C: They are part of the contract documents.
options.D: Both {A} and {C}
options.E: Both {B} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: Contract drawings are issued to bidders and become contract documents, so {D} is correct. They are not part of the project manual, which is the bound set of written documents (procurement requirements, contracting requirements and specifications) that accompanies the drawings.

questions.question: Which statements about resource drawings are correct?

options.A: They are part of the procurement documents.
options.B: They are bound in the project manual.
options.C: They become contract documents at the agreement.
options.D: Both {A} and {B}
options.E: Both {A} and {C}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: Resource drawings, such as record drawings of existing construction, go out with the procurement documents for reference only. They are drawings, so they are not part of the bound project manual, and unlike the contract drawings they do not become contract documents when the owner and contractor reach agreement.

questions.question: Which statements about addenda are correct?

options.A: They are part of the procurement documents.
options.B: They become part of the contract documents.
options.C: They are typically issued after the agreement is signed.
options.D: They are filed under Record Clarifications and Proposals (00 93 00).
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: Both {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: Addenda are precontract revisions issued during procurement, so they are procurement documents, and they carry into the contract, so {E} is correct. They are typically issued before bids or proposals are received, not after the agreement, and they are filed under Precontract Revisions (00 91 00), not with clarifications and proposals.

questions.question: Which of the following arise only after the owner and contractor sign the agreement, so they are never part of the procurement documents?

options.A: Addenda
options.B: Clarifications and proposals
options.C: Contract modifications
options.D: Contract drawings
options.E: Resource drawings
options.F: Supplementary Conditions

questions.explanation: Clarifications and proposals start changes or clarifications to an existing contract that no formal modification has yet made part of it, and contract modifications (change orders, change directives, minor changes) are issued after the agreement is signed. Addenda are the revisions issued during procurement. Contract drawings and the Supplementary Conditions go out to bidders, and resource drawings are procurement documents only.

questions.question: Of the three kinds of documents under Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications, which is part of the procurement documents?

options.A: Only contract modifications
options.B: Only precontract revisions (addenda)
options.C: None of the three
options.D: Only clarifications and proposals
options.E: All three
options.F: Both precontract revisions and clarifications and proposals

questions.explanation: Only precontract revisions such as addenda exist while pricing is under way; they revise the procurement documents before bids or proposals are received and are listed among them. Clarifications and proposals and contract modifications deal with a contract that already exists, so they come after the procurement documents have done their job.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes how the procurement documents, the project manual and the contract documents relate?

options.A: The contract documents include everything in the procurement documents, resource drawings included.
options.B: The project manual includes the contract drawings and any resource drawings.
options.C: The project manual and the contract documents are the same set of documents.
options.D: The procurement documents are the widest set issued for pricing: the whole project manual plus the contract drawings, any resource drawings, and addenda.
options.E: The procurement documents are a subset of the contract documents.
options.F: The contract documents are the project manual alone, with the drawings for reference only.

questions.explanation: The procurement documents take in everything issued for pricing: the project manual (procurement requirements, contracting requirements, specifications), the contract drawings, any resource drawings, and addenda. The contract documents are a subset of the procurement documents, not the other way around. The project manual holds no drawings, the contract drawings are contract documents in their own right, and resource drawings never become contract documents.

questions.question: Which groups make up the project manual?

options.A: Contracting Requirements, Specifications, Contract Drawings
options.B: Procurement Requirements, Contracting Requirements, Specifications
options.C: Procurement Requirements, Contracting Requirements, Specifications, Contract Drawings
options.D: Contracting Requirements and Specifications only
options.E: Procurement Requirements and Contracting Requirements only
options.F: Procurement Requirements, Contracting Requirements, Specifications, Resource Drawings

questions.explanation: The project manual is the bound volume of written documents: the procurement requirements and contracting requirements of Division 00, followed by the specifications in Divisions 01 through 49. It contains no drawings of either kind; the contract drawings are a separate set that the project manual accompanies.

questions.question: Apart from addenda and later modifications, which groups make up the contract documents?

options.A: Contracting Requirements, Specifications, Contract Drawings
options.B: Contracting Requirements, Specifications, Contract Drawings, Resource Drawings
options.C: Specifications and Contract Drawings only
options.D: Procurement Requirements, Contracting Requirements, Specifications
options.E: Contracting Requirements and Specifications only
options.F: Procurement Requirements, Contracting Requirements, Specifications, Contract Drawings

questions.explanation: The contract documents are the contracting requirements (00 50 00 to 00 90 00), the specifications, and the contract drawings, plus addenda issued before the agreement and modifications issued after it. The procurement requirements and any resource drawings help bidders price the work but do not become part of the contract.

questions.question: Construction documents fall into five groups (procurement requirements, contracting requirements, specifications, contract drawings, and resource drawings) and three kinds of revisions (addenda, clarifications and proposals, and contract modifications). Which of these make up the procurement documents?

options.A: All five groups and all three kinds of revisions
options.B: All five groups plus addenda
options.C: All groups except the resource drawings
options.D: The three project manual groups only
options.E: All five groups, but none of the revisions
options.F: All groups except the resource drawings, plus addenda

questions.explanation: The procurement documents are everything issued for pricing: procurement requirements, contracting requirements, specifications, contract drawings, any resource drawings, and addenda. Resource drawings are included even though they never become contract documents. Clarifications and proposals and contract modifications come only after a contract exists.

questions.question: Which of the following are in the project manual but not in the contract documents?

options.A: Instructions for Procurement
options.B: Contract Drawings
options.C: Agreement
options.D: Available Information
options.E: Resource Drawings
options.F: Div. 01 General Requirements

questions.explanation: The procurement requirements (Solicitation, Instructions for Procurement, Available Information, Procurement Forms and Supplements) are bound in the project manual but do not become contract documents. The Agreement and Division 01 are in both. Contract drawings are the reverse case, contract documents outside the project manual, and resource drawings are in neither.

questions.question: Which group is in the contract documents but not in the project manual?

options.A: Resource Drawings
options.B: Procurement Requirements
options.C: Contracting Requirements
options.D: Contract Drawings
options.E: Specifications
options.F: Available Information

questions.explanation: Contract drawings become contract documents, but they are issued as a separate set, not bound in the project manual with the written documents. Contracting requirements and specifications are in both, and resource drawings are in neither, since they are reference material that never enters the contract.

questions.question: Which group is a procurement document but is in neither the project manual nor the contract documents?

options.A: Resource Drawings
options.B: Contracting Requirements
options.C: Contract Drawings
options.D: Procurement Requirements
options.E: Specifications
options.F: Contract Modifications

questions.explanation: Resource drawings, such as record drawings of existing construction, are issued with the procurement documents for reference only: they are drawings, so they are not bound in the project manual, and they do not become contract documents at the agreement. Contract drawings, by contrast, become contract documents, and contract modifications are never procurement documents at all.

questions.question: Which of the following belong to all three sets: the procurement documents, the project manual, and the contract documents?

options.A: Contracting Requirements
options.B: Procurement Requirements
options.C: Contract Drawings
options.D: Specifications
options.E: Resource Drawings
options.F: Contract Modifications

questions.explanation: Only the contracting requirements and the specifications are in all three: bound in the project manual, issued for pricing, and part of the contract. Procurement requirements are not contract documents, contract drawings are not in the project manual, resource drawings are procurement documents only, and contract modifications come after procurement has ended.

questions.question: Reading the construction documents in their standard order, which is the first group that becomes part of the contract documents?

options.A: Specifications
options.B: Contract Drawings
options.C: Procurement Requirements
options.D: Contracting Requirements
options.E: Resource Drawings
options.F: Div. 01 General Requirements

questions.explanation: The contract documents start with the contracting requirements (00 50 00 to 00 90 00): the Agreement, bonds, certificates and conditions. The procurement requirements ahead of them (00 10 00 to 00 40 00) are used to obtain pricing and are not contract documents.

questions.question: Which group is the last one bound in the project manual?

options.A: Contract Drawings
options.B: Resource Drawings
options.C: Specifications
options.D: Contracting Requirements
options.E: Procurement Requirements
options.F: Div. 01 General Requirements

questions.explanation: The project manual ends with the specifications, which follow Division 00 and run from Division 01 through Division 49 (Process Equipment). Neither the contract drawings nor the resource drawings are bound in it, and Division 01 is the first part of the specifications, not the last.

questions.question: The contract drawings and the resource drawings are both issued to bidders. Which of them become part of the contract documents?

options.A: The contract drawings only
options.B: Both the contract drawings and the resource drawings
options.C: The resource drawings only
options.D: Neither; all drawings are reference material
options.E: The resource drawings, once an addendum revises them
options.F: Both, but only after the contractor accepts them

questions.explanation: Contract drawings illustrate the completed work and become contract documents when the owner and contractor reach agreement. Resource drawings, such as record drawings of an existing structure, show existing conditions for reference and stay outside the contract; they are the one kind of drawing in the procurement documents that does not carry over.

questions.question: Which of the following becomes part of the contract documents but is never part of the procurement documents?

options.A: Addenda
options.B: Contract Modifications
options.C: Contract Drawings
options.D: Resource Drawings
options.E: Supplementary Conditions
options.F: Agreement

questions.explanation: Contract modifications, such as change orders, construction change directives and minor changes, are issued after the agreement is signed and become part of the contract documents, but they did not exist when the work was priced. Addenda are issued during procurement and carry into the contract, and resource drawings are procurement documents only.

questions.question: Which of the following are contract documents?

options.A: Instructions for Procurement
options.B: Resource Drawings
options.C: Supplementary Conditions
options.D: Available Information
options.E: Addenda
options.F: Procurement Forms & Supplements

questions.explanation: The Supplementary Conditions are a contracting requirement and addenda are precontract revisions, and both become contract documents. Instructions for Procurement, Available Information, and Procurement Forms and Supplements are procurement requirements, used to obtain pricing but not part of the contract, and resource drawings are for reference only.

questions.question: Which of the following are NOT contract documents?

options.A: Payment Bond
options.B: Resource Drawings
options.C: Addenda
options.D: Contract Modifications
options.E: Solicitation
options.F: Certificates

questions.explanation: Resource drawings are reference material that never becomes part of the contract, and the Solicitation is a procurement requirement used only to obtain pricing. The payment bond and certificates are project forms within the contracting requirements, addenda carry into the contract, and contract modifications become part of it after the agreement.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT part of the project manual?

options.A: Contract Drawings
options.B: Solicitation
options.C: Certificates
options.D: Div. 40-49 Process Equipment
options.E: Supplementary Conditions
options.F: Available Information

questions.explanation: The project manual is the bound set of written documents, from the Solicitation in Division 00 through the specifications in Division 49, and it holds no drawings. The contract drawings are a separate set that the project manual accompanies, even though both are contract documents.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a procurement document?

options.A: Available Information
options.B: Addenda
options.C: Resource Drawings
options.D: Contract Modifications
options.E: Contract Drawings
options.F: Supplementary Conditions

questions.explanation: Contract modifications are issued after the agreement is signed, during the contract period, so they are never part of the documents used for pricing. Available Information, addenda, resource drawings, contract drawings and the Supplementary Conditions are all issued to bidders or proposers as procurement documents.

questions.question: Construction documents are made up of which two major groups?

options.A: Contract documents and record documents
options.B: Procurement requirements and contracting requirements
options.C: Procurement documents and contract documents
options.D: Bidding requirements and contract forms
options.E: Contract documents and pre-contract revisions
options.F: Project manual and resource drawings

questions.explanation: Construction documents divide into procurement documents, used to obtain pricing, and contract documents, which govern the work once the agreement is signed. Procurement requirements and contracting requirements are only the Division 00 parts of those sets, and record documents are produced during and after construction rather than issued to bidders.

questions.question: Which statements about how contract documents relate to procurement documents are correct?

options.A: Contract documents are a subset of the procurement documents.
options.B: Except for resource drawings, procurement documents become contract documents at agreement.
options.C: Resource drawings become contract documents once the agreement is signed.
options.D: Contract documents are prepared by the contractor after award.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: Both {A} and {C}

questions.explanation: Contract documents form a subset of the procurement documents, and the architect/engineer and design team prepare them, not the contractor. Once the owner and contractor sign the agreement, the procurement documents turn into contract documents, except for any resource drawings, which remain reference material only. So {E} is correct.

questions.question: Which statements about what each kind of revision can change are correct?

options.A: Addenda can change the procurement requirements, such as the instructions for procurement.
options.B: Addenda may be issued at any point while the contract is in force.
options.C: Contract modifications can change the procurement requirements after the agreement is signed.
options.D: Clarifications and proposals are typically issued before bids or proposals are received.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: {A}, {C} and {D}

questions.explanation: Addenda are issued during procurement and can revise any of the procurement documents, including the procurement requirements. They are typically issued before bids or proposals are received; it is contract modifications that can be issued at any time during the contract, and those change the contract and the work, not the procurement requirements. Clarifications and proposals also deal with a contract already in place.

questions.question: After the agreement is signed, clarifications, proposals and contract modifications can affect which documents?

options.A: Specifications, contract drawings and resource drawings
options.B: Procurement requirements, contracting requirements, specifications and contract drawings
options.C: Contracting requirements and specifications only
options.D: Contracting requirements, specifications and contract drawings
options.E: Contracting requirements, specifications, contract drawings and resource drawings
options.F: Procurement requirements, contracting requirements and specifications

questions.explanation: Clarifications, proposals and contract modifications deal with the contract, so they reach every contract document: the contracting requirements, the specifications and the contract drawings. The procurement requirements have done their job once pricing ends, and resource drawings were never part of the contract.

questions.question: Of the three kinds of revisions (addenda, clarifications and proposals, and contract modifications), which can change the procurement requirements, such as the instructions to bidders or the bid form?

options.A: None of the three kinds
options.B: Only addenda (precontract revisions)
options.C: All three kinds
options.D: Only contract modifications
options.E: Only clarifications and proposals
options.F: Both addenda and clarifications and proposals

questions.explanation: Only addenda can, because they are issued while pricing is open and may revise any of the procurement documents, including the procurement requirements. Clarifications and proposals and contract modifications deal with the contract after the agreement, when the procurement requirements no longer apply.

questions.question: On a renovation, the owner gives bidders record drawings of the existing building as resource drawings. How are they treated once the agreement is signed?

options.A: They remain reference material and do not become contract documents.
options.B: They become contract documents along with the contract drawings.
options.C: They are bound into the project manual under Division 01.
options.D: They replace the contract drawings for the existing work.
options.E: They are reissued as contract modifications.
options.F: They are filed under Record Modifications (00 94 00).

questions.explanation: Resource drawings show existing conditions or related construction for reference. They go out with the procurement documents, but they are not included in the contract and do not become contract documents when the agreement is signed. Contract modifications change the work after the agreement; they do not turn reference drawings into contract documents.

questions.question: Which Division 00 heading covers addenda, clarifications and proposals, and contract modifications?

options.A: Div. 01 General Requirements
options.B: Conditions of the Contract
options.C: Procurement Forms & Supplements
options.D: Revisions, Clarifications & Modifications
options.E: Supplementary Conditions
options.F: Contracting Forms

questions.explanation: Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications (00 90 00), the last Contracting Requirements heading, holds all three: Precontract Revisions (00 91 00), Record Clarifications and Proposals (00 93 00), and Record Modifications (00 94 00). Division 01 holds the procedures for contract modifications, but the revision documents themselves are filed in Division 00.

questions.question: Addenda are the main example of which category of revisions?

options.A: Clarifications & Proposals
options.B: Procurement Forms & Supplements
options.C: Contract Modifications
options.D: Pre-Contract Revisions
options.E: Supplementary Instructions to Bidders
options.F: Bid or Proposal Revisions

questions.explanation: Addenda are precontract revisions (00 91 00): written or graphic changes made before the agreement is signed, typically before bids or proposals are received. Bid or proposal revisions, when permitted, are the other kind of precontract revision, not a category that contains addenda. Clarifications and proposals and contract modifications come after the agreement.

questions.question: When is an addendum typically issued?

options.A: Before bids or proposals are received
options.B: After the agreement is signed
options.C: During construction, with a change order
options.D: Between bid opening and award only
options.E: At any time during the contract period
options.F: Together with the notice of award

questions.explanation: An addendum is a precontract revision: it clarifies, revises, adds to or deletes information in the procurement documents, and it is typically issued before bids or proposals are received so that every bidder prices the same documents. Changes after the agreement is signed are contract modifications, such as change orders.

questions.question: Which of the following are precontract revisions?

options.A: Change orders issued before mobilization
options.B: Requests for information
options.C: Minor changes in the work
options.D: Bid or proposal revisions
options.E: Addenda
options.F: Proposal requests

questions.explanation: Precontract revisions are made before the agreement is signed: written addenda and, when permitted, bid or proposal revisions, all filed under 00 91 00. Requests for information and proposal requests are clarifications and proposals, and change orders and minor changes in the work are contract modifications, made after the agreement.

questions.question: Which statements about clarifications and proposals are correct?

options.A: Requests for information belong in them.
options.B: Proposal requests belong in them.
options.C: Change orders belong in them.
options.D: They are part of the procurement documents.
options.E: Both {A} and {B}
options.F: Both {B} and {D}

questions.explanation: Clarifications and proposals are documents that start changes or clarifications not yet made part of the contract by a formal modification, such as requests for information and proposal requests (00 93 00), so {E} is correct. Change orders are contract modifications, and these documents arise after the agreement, so they are not procurement documents.

questions.question: Which of the following are contract modifications?

options.A: Addenda
options.B: Change orders
options.C: Requests for information
options.D: Proposal requests
options.E: Minor changes in the work
options.F: Change order requests

questions.explanation: Contract modifications are issued after the agreement, at any time during the contract, and change the work through change orders, change directives and minor changes in the work. Requests for information, proposal requests and change order requests only start or clarify changes, so they are clarifications and proposals (00 93 00), and addenda are precontract revisions.

questions.question: When are contract modifications made?

options.A: Before bids or proposals are received
options.B: Between bid opening and signing the agreement
options.C: After the agreement is signed
options.D: Only after substantial completion
options.E: When the owner accepts a bid or proposal revision
options.F: When an addendum is issued

questions.explanation: Contract modifications come after the construction agreement is signed and may be issued at any time during the contract period. Changes made before signing are precontract revisions, such as addenda or permitted bid revisions, and the owner accepting a revised bid is part of procurement, not a contract modification.

questions.question: Which statements about what project forms do are correct?

options.A: They guarantee contractor performance.
options.B: They certify compliance.
options.C: They define the basic rights and relationships of the parties.
options.D: They assist in the administration of the contract.
options.E: {A}, {B} and {D}
options.F: {A}, {B} and {C}

questions.explanation: Project forms, such as the bonds and certificates, back up the contractor's performance, certify compliance, and help in administering the contract, so {E} is correct. Setting out the basic rights, responsibilities and relationships of the parties is the job of the Conditions of the Contract, and binding the parties to their terms is the job of the Agreement.

questions.question: Besides the performance and payment bonds, the project forms include certificates. Which two kinds of certificates are meant?

options.A: Bid security certificates
options.B: Manufacturers' product certifications
options.C: Insurance certificates
options.D: Certificates of occupancy
options.E: Legal-compliance certificates
options.F: Material certificates for structural steel

questions.explanation: The certificates in the project forms are certificates of insurance, showing the contractor carries the required coverage, and certificates showing compliance with the laws and regulations that apply. Bid security belongs with the procurement forms, a certificate of occupancy comes from the building official, and product and material certificates are submittals required by the specifications.

questions.question: Which document incorporates all the other contract documents by reference?

options.A: The Supplementary Conditions
options.B: Division 01 General Requirements
options.C: The Agreement
options.D: The General Conditions
options.E: The Table of Contents
options.F: The Bid Form

questions.explanation: The Agreement is the legal instrument the owner and contractor sign; it sets out their relationship and obligations and makes every other contract document part of the contract by reference. The General and Supplementary Conditions define the parties' rights and responsibilities, and Division 01 sets administrative requirements, but none of them is the document that ties the set together.

questions.question: What does a payment bond guarantee?

options.A: That subcontractors and suppliers will be paid
options.B: That the bidder will sign the agreement if awarded
options.C: That the surety will complete the work if the contractor defaults
options.D: That the owner will pay the contractor on time
options.E: That the contractor carries the required insurance
options.F: That the work complies with applicable laws

questions.explanation: A payment bond guarantees that subcontractors, material suppliers and others who furnish labor, materials or services to the project get paid. Finishing the work if the contractor defaults is the job of the performance bond, and a promise that the bidder will sign the agreement if awarded is bid security.

questions.question: In Division 00, which number range holds the Procurement Requirements?
questions.explanation: The Procurement Requirements run from 00 10 00 Solicitation through 00 40 00 Procurement Forms and Supplements, and the Contracting Requirements follow at 00 50 00 through 00 90 00. Numbers starting at 00 01 00 take in the introductory information, such as the title page and table of contents, which is not a procurement requirement.

questions.question: In Division 00, which number range holds the Contracting Requirements?
questions.explanation: The Contracting Requirements run from 00 50 00 Contracting Forms and Supplements through 00 90 00 Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications, taking in Project Forms (00 60 00) and Conditions of the Contract (00 70 00). Stopping at 00 70 00 or 00 80 00 leaves out the revisions, and 00 40 00 is the last Procurement Requirements heading.

questions.question: In Division 00, what is 00 60 00?

options.A: Procurement Forms and Supplements
options.B: Project Forms
options.C: Conditions of the Contract
options.D: Contracting Forms and Supplements
options.E: Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications
options.F: Available Information

questions.explanation: 00 60 00 is Project Forms, which holds the bond forms, certificates and other forms. It sits between 00 50 00 Contracting Forms and Supplements (the Agreement) and 00 70 00 Conditions of the Contract, while Procurement Forms and Supplements is 00 40 00.

questions.question: In Division 00, addenda are filed under which heading?

options.A: 00 91 00 Precontract Revisions
options.B: 00 94 00 Record Modifications
options.C: 00 70 00 Conditions of the Contract
options.D: 00 40 00 Procurement Forms and Supplements
options.E: 00 93 00 Record Clarifications and Proposals
options.F: 00 63 00 Clarification and Modification Forms

questions.explanation: Addenda (00 91 13) fall under 00 91 00 Precontract Revisions, the first of three headings within 00 90 00 Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications. Record Clarifications and Proposals (00 93 00) holds items such as requests for information, Record Modifications (00 94 00) holds change orders, and Clarification and Modification Forms (00 63 00) are blank project forms.

questions.question: AIA document B201 defines the Bidding Documents as the bidding requirements plus the proposed contract documents. What broader term covers this set when the work may be bid, negotiated or purchased?

options.A: Construction Documents
options.B: Contract Documents
options.C: Procurement Documents
options.D: Project Manual
options.E: Procurement Requirements
options.F: Contracting Requirements

questions.explanation: Procurement documents is the broader term, because procurement covers bidding, negotiating and purchasing; the set includes the procurement requirements, contracting requirements, specifications, contract drawings, any resource drawings and addenda. Procurement requirements are only the Division 00 part of that set, and construction documents is the umbrella that also takes in the contract documents.

questions.question: The Agreement, the performance and payment bonds, and the certificates are all forms used to contract the work, but Division 00 files them under two different headings. How are they divided?

options.A: Contracting Forms (the Agreement) and Project Forms (bonds and certificates)
options.B: Contracting Forms (Agreement and bonds) and Project Forms (certificates)
options.C: Procurement Forms (bonds) and Contracting Forms (Agreement and certificates)
options.D: Project Forms (Agreement) and Contracting Forms (bonds and certificates)
options.E: Contracting Forms (Agreement and certificates) and Project Forms (bonds)
options.F: Contracting Forms (the Agreement) and Conditions of the Contract (bonds and certificates)

questions.explanation: Contracting Forms (00 50 00) hold the Agreement, and Project Forms (00 60 00) hold the performance bond, payment bond and certificates; both headings are part of the Contracting Requirements. The bonds are not filed with the Agreement, no procurement form holds them, and the Conditions of the Contract hold only the General and Supplementary Conditions.

questions.question: How is MasterFormat's Specifications Group (Divisions 01 through 49) organized?

options.A: Three subgroups: building, services, and site
options.B: Fifty divisions listed one by one, with no subgroups
options.C: Sixteen divisions numbered 01 through 16
options.D: Division 01 as its own subgroup, plus four division-range subgroups
options.E: Division 01 plus three subgroups
options.F: Four subgroups, with Division 01 inside Facility Construction

questions.explanation: Division 01 forms the General Requirements Subgroup on its own, and four subgroups follow by division range: Facility Construction (02-19), Facility Services (20-29), Site and Infrastructure (30-39), and Process Equipment (40-49). Leaving out Process Equipment gives only three range subgroups, and Facility Construction starts at Division 02, not 01.

questions.question: Besides precontract revisions such as addenda, which two categories make up Revisions, Clarifications, and Modifications in Division 00?

options.A: Contract Modifications and Construction Change Directives
options.B: Change Orders and Minor Changes
options.C: Contract Modifications and Requests for Information
options.D: Contract Modifications and Clarifications & Proposals
options.E: Clarifications & Proposals and Change Orders
options.F: Clarifications & Proposals and Bid Revisions

questions.explanation: The heading has three categories: precontract revisions (addenda), clarifications and proposals (00 93 00), and contract modifications (00 94 00). Change orders, construction change directives and minor changes are documents within contract modifications, requests for information fall under clarifications and proposals, and bid revisions are precontract revisions, so none of them is a category of its own.

questions.question: On a hospital project, the A/E's specifier is assembling sections prepared by the structural, mechanical, and electrical consultants while holding to the production schedule. Industry guidance gives which tasks as examples of the management proficiency needed to incorporate information from multiple consultants?

options.A: Confirming that every consultant edited its sections from the A/E's own office master
options.B: Comparing each consultant's sections with the latest cost estimate and the owner budget
options.C: Checking specification format and verifying content has no duplication or omission
options.D: Approving each consultant's product selections before design development has begun
options.E: Sealing each consultant's sections under the A/E's own professional registration
options.F: Holding consultant sections until all drawings are final so none need revision

questions.explanation: Industry guidance ties schedule management to organizational skill, and its examples for folding in consultant work are checking that the specification format is consistent and confirming that no content is duplicated or omitted. Requiring consultants to use the office master, reconciling their sections to cost estimates, and pre-approving their product choices are not the examples industry guidance gives for this proficiency.

questions.question: The electrical consultant's Division 26 sections arrive after the project manual has gone to the owner, and one lighting section is missing entirely. Which practice is meant to prevent exactly this outcome?

options.A: Making each consultant aware of the schedule, including specification delivery dates
options.B: Having the A/E's specifier write every consultant section in-house from their drawings
options.C: Issuing the late and missing consultant sections afterward by addendum during bidding
options.D: Having the owner set consultant delivery dates in each owner-consultant agreement form
options.E: Reviewing each consultant's sections for format only after the manual is issued
options.F: Letting the contractor obtain any missing sections later through its RFIs

questions.explanation: Most design consultants write the sections for their own part of the work, so each one must know the production schedule and the dates its specification documents are due; that is what lets the A/E collect every section on time with nothing missing at submission. Writing every consultant section in-house ignores that consultants prepare their own, an addendum changes documents during bidding rather than preventing late delivery, and a review after issue or a contractor's RFI comes far too late.
questions.source: coordinating the production schedule with consultants

questions.question: At what point does the A/E begin developing the project manual?

options.A: Once the drawings are complete and fully coordinated among all of the design consultants
options.B: Once the outline specification is approved and the cost estimate has been reconciled
options.C: Once the owner-A/E agreement is executed and the delivery method has been confirmed
options.D: Once a plan is established and the scope of work is understood from the design documents
options.E: Once the authorities having jurisdiction have completed their plan review
options.F: Once bids are received and the low bidder's proposed products are known

questions.explanation: The A/E begins developing the project manual once a plan is in place and the scope of work is thoroughly understood from the design documents, and it stays organized so information can be managed and retrieved quickly. Completed drawings, an approved outline specification, an executed agreement, plan review and bids are not the triggers; plan review and bidding need a project manual already, and waiting for finished drawings would defeat producing drawings and specifications concurrently.

questions.question: Before editing any sections, a specifier drafts a plan for gathering project information systematically and comprehensively. Which set consists entirely of items industry guidance specifically names as things that plan must help the specifier fully understand?

options.A: Delivery method, the contractor's proposed schedule, and specifications format
options.B: Delivery method, insurance and bonding requirements, and specifications format
options.C: Owner-builder agreement form, AHJ review comments, and insurance requirements
options.D: Scope of the work, the subcontractor list, and the owner-builder agreement form
options.E: Scope of the work, bonding requirements, and the contractor's schedule of values
options.F: Owner-builder agreement form, specifications format, and the shop drawing log

questions.explanation: The production plan must give the specifier a full understanding of the scope of work, the project delivery method, the form of owner-builder agreement, insurance and bonding requirements, and the specification format, among other project characteristics. Each wrong set slips in one item that is not on that list: the contractor's schedule, subcontractor list, schedule of values, and shop drawings are contractor-generated during construction, and AHJ review comments are not a planning input.
questions.source: developing a detailed document production plan

questions.question: After the owner formally accepts the specifications, the building department's plan review requires changes to two sections before any bids are solicited. How does industry guidance treat these changes for version control purposes?

options.A: They need no tracking, since version control begins when procurement documents issue
options.B: They should wait for a change order, since only the executed contract can be revised
options.C: They must be identified as revisions, since version control extends to AHJ plan review
options.D: They should be logged for internal review only, since no contractor has been selected
options.E: They should be issued by addendum, since the owner has already accepted the set
options.F: They should be noted only in the AHJ's permit file, since the AHJ required them

questions.explanation: Version control is not limited to procurement and construction: it includes identifying revisions made after the project team formally accepts the specifications and during plan review by the authorities having jurisdiction, so the whole team works from the latest version and can see what changed. An addendum modifies documents already issued to bidders, and deferring tracking, waiting for a change order, or keeping the record internal or in the permit file hides the change from the team.

questions.question: While bids are being prepared, a roofing subcontractor wants the prime bidder to propose an alternative membrane to the one specified. What kind of standardized form should the bidder use for this request?

options.A: A substitution request form meant for use during bidding or negotiating
options.B: A substitution request form meant for use after bidding or negotiating ends
options.C: A substitution request log that tracks each request as it is made
options.D: A request for information form with a space for the A/E's response
options.E: A change order request form signed by both the owner and the contractor
options.F: A bid form that lists the membrane as an owner-requested alternate

questions.explanation: During procurement, a request to use an unspecified product goes on the substitution request form meant for the bidding or negotiating phase, submitted before or with the bid as the procurement documents require. A separate form serves requests made after that phase, the log only tracks requests, and an RFI asks for an interpretation. A change order cannot exist before the agreement is signed, and alternates are requested by the owner, not proposed by bidders.

questions.question: An addendum changes a door hardware set that is described in Section 08 71 00 and also shown on four drawing sheets. Using the narrative method, how should the specifier handle this repetitive change?

options.A: Repeat the full change instructions under each affected sheet and section for clarity
options.B: Describe only the specification change and let bidders infer the drawing revisions
options.C: Reissue only the four sheets with clouds, omitting any written narrative of the change
options.D: State all related revisions once, then point readers back to that statement elsewhere
options.E: Defer the drawing revisions to a change order after the contract is awarded
options.F: Explain the change orally at the prebid meeting and confirm it later in writing

questions.explanation: Under the narrative method's cross-reference criterion, a change is stated once; when a specification change also affects the drawings, all related changes are explained in the addendum and readers are referred to that statement instead of being given repeated instructions. Repeating instructions everywhere breaks that rule, leaving drawing changes unstated fails the clarity criterion, reissuing clouded sheets is the revised-page method, and oral explanations should be avoided even when a written change will follow.

questions.question: After Change Order No. 1, the specifier reissues Section 07 92 00 in full using the revised-page method. What may the reissued section carry to show its status?

options.A: A new MasterFormat number distinguishing it from the originally issued section
options.B: The revision date and an identifier such as CO-01 in its header or footer
options.C: A narrative summary of every change placed at the start of PART 1—GENERAL
options.D: The original issue date only, with the change noted in the table of contents
options.E: The contractor's signed acknowledgment on the section's first page
options.F: The addendum number under which the section was first issued

questions.explanation: In the revised-page method the change is made in the section or sheet using one of the revision methods and the item is reissued; each reissued section may show the revision date and an identifier such as CO-01 in its header or footer. Renumbering the section is not part of the method, a narrative summary belongs to the narrative method, and an old issue date or addendum number would hide which version the reader has.

questions.question: A firm does most of its work for one university system and wants a master guide specification tailored to that client's standards. How does this fit the usual description of office master guide specifications?

options.A: It does not; office masters capture only information common to the firm's own practice
options.B: It does not; owner standards go only in project manuals, never in a master guide
options.C: It fits; office masters capture what is common to an office, owner, or building type
options.D: It fits only if the university itself develops and maintains the master guide
options.E: It does not; a master must remain generic text, never tailored to a client
options.F: It fits only for public owners, since private owners do not set standards

questions.explanation: Office master guide specifications exist to hold whatever is common to an office, an owner, or a building type, so a master tailored to one university client's standards fits that purpose. Limiting masters to the firm's own practice, barring owner standards, or insisting a master stay generic contradicts this, and nothing requires the owner itself, public or private, to author an owner-focused master.
questions.source: developing and organizing office master guide specifications

questions.question: A firm's master guide specification system currently consists of nothing but the master sections themselves. Which additional element does industry guidance include to flag the principal choices that must be made for an individual project?

options.A: A list of frequently specified products
options.B: A section title list noting related work
options.C: Provisions for drawing-spec coordination
options.D: A checklist prepared for each section
options.E: Evaluations of products and standards
options.F: A library of past project manuals

questions.explanation: Among the elements of a complete master guide specification system, the checklist for each section is the one that identifies the principal decisions needed for an individual project. The frequently specified products list, the drawing-specification coordination provisions, and the evaluations of products, codes, and standards are also system elements but serve other purposes, while a section title list or a library of old project manuals is not one of the listed elements.

questions.question: A firm principal wants specifications produced alongside the drawings rather than in a rush at the end of the documents phase. Which benefit of a master guide specification does industry guidance tie directly to this outcome?

options.A: Reduced delays in project development
options.B: Improved efficiency in specifying
options.C: Standardized office policies and procedures
options.D: Expanded decision-making capability
options.E: Reduced exposure to liability
options.F: Easier updating of specification data

questions.explanation: The reduced-delays benefit rests on a master guide letting specification production run concurrently with the drawings, avoiding the delay, confusion, and misuse that last-minute preparation causes. Improved efficiency concerns no longer redeveloping the same specifications, standardized policies concern terminology and office procedures, expanded decision-making concerns a wide range of standard options, reduced liability follows from fewer errors, and easier updating concerns keeping product data current.
questions.source: reasons for using a master guide specification

questions.question: A school district mandates its own guide specifications on all of its work, and several of them differ from the A/E firm's standard approach. What course of action does industry guidance call for?

options.A: Substitute the firm's office master wherever the district's text conflicts with it
options.B: Verify conflicts with the firm's practice and resolve them before project completion
options.C: Leave the conflicts for the contractor to raise through RFIs during construction
options.D: Bind in both documents and let the order-of-precedence clause settle any conflict
options.E: Ask the district to waive its guide specifications in favor of the firm's master
options.F: Follow the firm's practice and ask the district to accept the deviations at closeout

questions.explanation: When an owner requires its own guide specifications, the A/E must check for conflicts between the owner's specifications and the firm's standard practice and get them resolved and clarified before the project is complete. Overriding the owner's text, asking for a waiver, or seeking acceptance of deviations at closeout ignores the owner's requirement, while pushing conflicts to RFIs or an order-of-precedence clause leaves contradictions in the documents.
questions.source: reasons for using a master guide specification

questions.question: A firm's three offices each use an office master built on the same commercial master guide specification, but the offices are working from different releases of it. What does industry guidance direct the A/E to do?

options.A: Let each office keep its own release provided that office edits are logged centrally
options.B: Freeze the office master at the release in use when the firm first adopted the product
options.C: Update an office's release only after a project problem shows the older one is deficient
options.D: Ensure all users have the latest release and that the office master has current updates
options.E: Update only the commercial base text and drop each office's own edits
options.F: Move each office to a different commercial master so releases never clash

questions.explanation: When a commercial master guide serves as the office master, the A/E should make sure every user has the latest release, and the office master should carry the latest updates to both the office edits and the commercial base text. Mixed releases, a frozen old release, updates only after a failure, or offices on different products leave users on outdated or inconsistent text, and dropping office edits loses the firm's own improvements.

questions.question: In an office master section, an editing note applies to an entire article covering fire-rated door assemblies. Where does industry guidance say such a note is usually located?

options.A: At the end of the article, following the last paragraph it affects
options.B: At the beginning of the section, ahead of the PART 1—GENERAL heading
options.C: Immediately after the article title, ahead of the text it affects
options.D: In a block of end-of-section notes placed after PART 3—EXECUTION
options.E: Just before whichever paragraph in the article it most affects
options.F: In a separate notes file kept apart from the master section

questions.explanation: An editing note that governs a whole article usually goes right after the article title, ahead of the text it affects, while a note for a single paragraph goes just before that paragraph. Putting the article note after the text, at the head of the section, beside one paragraph, in an end-of-section block, or in a separate file separates it from the article it governs.

questions.question: A specifier is developing an office master section for porcelain tile. Which content should be left out of the master guide specification section itself?

options.A: The color, pattern, and texture choices for the tile
options.B: Editing notes that point out drawing coordination
options.C: Permanent decisions, separately listed and identified
options.D: Bracketed options for alternative setting methods
options.E: Blank spaces where project information will be inserted
options.F: Designations of the referenced tile and setting standards

questions.explanation: Some options a project needs stay out of the master, either because there are too many of them, such as color, pattern, and texture, or because they are project-specific, such as engineering design data. Editing notes, separately listed permanent decisions, bracketed options, blanks for project information, and the designations of referenced standards all belong in a master section; only the full text of those standards is kept outside it.

questions.question: A sealant joint failed on a recently completed project, and the firm wants to revise the corresponding office master section. What does industry guidance say should happen as part of revising that text?

options.A: Withdraw the section from project use until the manufacturer issues revised product data
options.B: Investigate whether the failure was project-specific or reflects an industry-wide change
options.C: Wait for the next commercial release and adopt whatever revision that release contains
options.D: Add the failed sealant product to a prohibited-products list within the master section
options.E: Have the sealant manufacturer rewrite the section from its own guide specification
options.F: Record the failure in that project's closeout file and leave the master text as is

questions.explanation: Updating a master includes revising text that caused problems on a previous project, after investigating whether the problem was specific to that project or reflects a broader, industry-wide change. Withdrawing the section, waiting for a commercial release, blacklisting the product, handing the rewrite to the manufacturer, or simply filing the failure all skip that investigation and leave the master's text unexamined.

questions.question: A firm designs many tenant improvement projects and wants to begin issuing shortform specifications for them. Which approach does industry guidance recommend for creating those shortform specifications?

options.A: Expand each project's description into shortform sections as design proceeds
options.B: Edit a previous tenant improvement project's specifications for each new job
options.C: Write each shortform section from the applicable industry reference standards
options.D: Develop them from a master guide specification prepared for that project type
options.E: Adopt each manufacturer's guide specification for the products selected
options.F: Write each section from scratch once the tenant's design is complete

questions.explanation: Shortform specifications can be produced other ways, such as expanding a project description, editing an earlier specification, working from reference standards, or writing from scratch, but the recommended route is to develop them from a master guide specification. A firm can keep a separate shortform master for each project type it designs often, such as tenant improvements. Manufacturer guide specifications need careful review and are not a master.

questions.question: A firm is evaluating a newer master guide specification product. Which statement reflects how master guide specifications have changed in recent years?

options.A: Fewer, broader sections that are simpler to integrate into design practice
options.B: Consolidation under one publisher, which raises new licensing issues to weigh
options.C: More sections and better editing tools, which raise new issues to weigh
options.D: Shorter publisher release cycles, which simplify integration into practice
options.E: Built-in cost data, which removes the need for separate estimates
options.F: Simplified formats, which remove the need to follow SectionFormat

questions.explanation: Master guide specifications have improved through an expanded number of available sections and more sophisticated editing technology, and those improvements bring other issues users must weigh when bringing them into practice.
