Fewer sections contradicts the expanded coverage; publisher consolidation and faster releases are not among the improvements named; and masters neither carry detailed cost data nor drop the three-part SectionFormat.

questions.question: After issuing the project manual electronically, a specifier wants to ensure that no one other than expressly designated persons can alter the contract documents. Which technology feature does industry guidance list specifically for this purpose?

options.A: Security features restricting modification
options.B: Publishing to a neutral format such as PDF
options.C: Tracking or recording insertions and deletions
options.D: Shared linkages to CAD and BIM software
options.E: Notes kept as hidden text that does not print
options.F: Hyperlinks to manufacturer and standards websites

questions.explanation: Among the technology features listed for master guide specifications, security features that stop anyone but expressly designated persons from modifying the contract documents serve this purpose. Publishing to a neutral format such as PDF is listed for accessibility and usability, even though such files can carry security settings; change tracking records insertions and deletions, hidden-text notes and hyperlinks aid editing, and software linkages connect to CAD and BIM.

questions.question: A firm asks how much supplemental material its specifiers will need beyond the master guide specification. The answer depends partly on which factor?

options.A: How many consultants contribute to the project
options.B: How comprehensive the master is meant to be
options.C: Which delivery method the owner has selected
options.D: How often the publisher issues master updates
options.E: How large the owner's construction budget is
options.F: How many prime bidders the owner expects

questions.explanation: A master guide specification is not a complete system by itself; how much more information is needed depends partly on how comprehensive the master is intended to be. Users still turn to manufacturers' product data, the project's design information, codes, and referenced standards. The number of consultants, the delivery method, the publisher's update cycle, the budget, and the number of bidders are not the factors named.

questions.question: A project architect opens a publisher's master guide specification section in a cloud-based specification system and tries to edit that master text directly. What typically happens in such systems?

options.A: Edits are saved to the master text and pushed automatically to every active project file
options.B: The master is locked until the publisher issues its next scheduled release of the section
options.C: The architect must first download the section and edit the master text on an office server
options.D: The master sections are not editable; selected sections are copied into the project file
options.E: The edits go to the publisher for review before its next release of the section
options.F: The section becomes an office master that only that architect may revise

questions.explanation: Industry guidance explains that cloud-based master systems typically do not allow the master guide sections to be edited; the specifier selects the sections needed and copies are added to the project file automatically, leaving the masters intact. Edits that propagate to every project, waiting on a publisher release, or downloading to edit the master would all undermine the protected master industry guidance describes; only office masters built from those sections may be revised, and then only by authorized users.

questions.question: The architect's specifier is compiling a design development submission that includes sections prepared by the mechanical, electrical, and civil consultants. The A/E's proficiency in managing the specifications production schedule specifically includes which task when bringing the consultants' material together?

options.A: Confirming that each consultant's fee proposal covers all specification work assigned
options.B: Sealing every consultant section under the architect's own professional license
options.C: Rewriting each consultant's sections into the architect's preferred writing style
options.D: Checking the format and confirming the content has no duplications or omissions
options.E: Renumbering consultant sections to match the architect's own office system
options.F: Binding each discipline's sections as a separate volume of the manual

questions.explanation: Schedule-management proficiency includes folding in information from multiple consultants, which means checking specification format and making sure nothing is duplicated or left out. Consultants typically prepare the sections for their own part of the work and must meet the delivery dates so nothing is missing at submission; fees, sealing, restyling, renumbering, and separate binding are not part of the task described.

questions.question: A design firm is drafting a project management procedure and wants its stated purpose for the coordination process to match industry guidance. Which statement should it adopt?

options.A: To establish which contract document governs when requirements conflict
options.B: To assign each consultant sole responsibility for its discipline's documents
options.C: To manage dependencies between tasks and parties, adding value to delivery
options.D: To limit which stakeholders may supply information to the design team
options.E: To shift design risk from the A/E to the contractor and its suppliers
options.F: To fix the owner's budget before design development begins

questions.explanation: The coordination process exists to add value to project delivery and make it more efficient by handling how project tasks and parties depend on one another, summed up as managing dependencies between activities. Deciding which document governs is a precedence question that is handled separately and discouraged. Coordination integrates the parties rather than isolating disciplines or restricting who may supply information, and it is not a means of shifting risk or fixing a budget.

questions.question: After a claim arises from inconsistencies between the drawings and the project manual, the A/E firm's principal asks where ultimate responsibility for coordinating the construction documents should have rested. It should have rested with:

options.A: the specifier, whether in-house or independent, who prepared the project manual
options.B: the A/E's project manager, who may delegate coordination to a team member
options.C: the owner's project manager, who reviews the documents before issue
options.D: the general contractor, who must report discrepancies it discovers
options.E: the principal-in-charge, who signs the agreements that commit the firm
options.F: each consultant, for the drawings and sections of its own discipline

questions.explanation: Ultimate responsibility for coordinating the construction documents belongs to the A/E's project manager, who may assign the task to another design team member. The specifier works with the design team but is not the party ultimately responsible; the principal-in-charge commits the firm but is not involved in day-to-day document work; consultants work within the prime A/E's overall coordination; and the owner and contractor are outside the design team.

questions.question: To limit rework as the design changes, an A/E's project manager asks when the specifier should start preparing the project manual. What is the recommended approach?

options.A: Start as design begins, and keep it coordinated continuously as the design develops
options.B: Start once the owner approves the design development drawings and product selections
options.C: Start when the drawings are substantially complete, then hold a coordination review
options.D: Start midway through construction documents, once most product selections are settled
options.E: Start after schematic design, once the outline specifications are approved
options.F: Start once the cost estimate has been reconciled with the final drawings

questions.explanation: Preparing the project manual should run alongside design, with coordination carried on continuously from the start of the project; a preliminary project description or outline specifications act as a checklist as design begins. Each wrong choice waits for a later milestone, which turns coordination into a late check and invites the rework that design changes, errors, and omissions cause.

questions.question: The owner's counsel asks the specifier to add a clause stating that the specifications govern over the drawings whenever the two conflict. How should the specifier respond?

options.A: Add the clause to Division 01 so that it governs throughout construction
options.B: Add an order-of-precedence listing to the supplementary conditions
options.C: Have the conditions state that the more stringent requirement governs
options.D: Have the conditions state that the A/E makes a documented interpretation
options.E: Add a note on the drawing cover sheet that the specifications govern
options.F: Have the agreement state that the drawings govern over the specifications

questions.explanation: Precedence statements in the project manual are not recommended because drawings and specifications complement each other; the conditions of the contract should say only that the A/E makes a documented interpretation when the two conflict. A precedence list may be prepared for bidding purposes only. A Division 01 clause, a supplementary conditions listing, a cover-sheet note, an agreement clause, or a "more stringent governs" rule each sets up the precedence that guidance discourages.

questions.question: An independent specifier receives product selections from several designers on the prime A/E's team, and some selections contradict each other. Which communication method best addresses the problem?

options.A: Have product representatives send product data directly to the specifier for each section
options.B: Have all product information reach the specifier only from designated individuals
options.C: Have each designer keep sending selections directly to the specifier, who reconciles them
options.D: Have the specifier select products and send the selections to the designers for approval
options.E: Have the contractor resolve conflicting selections later through submittals
options.F: Have each designer write the product paragraphs for the sections it selected

questions.explanation: Set up a protocol so that product information reaches the specifier only from one or more designated people, typically the project manager, the project A/E, or both. Letting product representatives or each designer keep sending selections leaves several sources that may conflict; having the specifier choose products inverts the process; and leaving conflicts to submittals risks incompatible products reaching construction as a latent defect.

questions.question: A prime A/E adopts a cloud-based collaboration tool that lets the design team access the specifications while they are being developed. What is the main benefit to the specifier?

options.A: Automatic reconciliation of terminology between the drawings and the specifications
options.B: Direct editing of sections by designers, reducing the specifier's drafting workload
options.C: Timely, accurate feedback that reduces section-by-section specification review meetings
options.D: Documented design team approval of each section before the project manual is issued
options.E: Removal of the need to coordinate the drawings with the specifications
options.F: Transfer of responsibility for the project manual to the design team

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says cloud-based tools that let the design team access the specifications during development give the specifier timely and accurate feedback, which minimizes time-consuming section-by-section review meetings. Coordinating terminology between drawings and specifications remains part of the specifier's regular reviews with the design team; the tool does not do it automatically. Industry guidance describes the design team accessing the specifications, not editing them in the specifier's place, and does not present the tool as a formal approval step.

questions.question: A prime A/E retains mechanical and electrical consultants to write their own sections. When should the prime A/E request the consultants' input for Division 01 sections?

options.A: When it gives them the project, contract, and Division 01 information, before they write
options.B: After the consultants submit first drafts, so Division 01 can be reconciled with them
options.C: At the construction documents review, when the A/E checks for duplications and omissions
options.D: During bidding, when bidders' questions reveal gaps between the disciplines' requirements
options.E: Once the drawings are complete, when the consultants seal their sections
options.F: Only if a consultant's sections are found to conflict with the general conditions

questions.explanation: Before consultants write any sections, the prime A/E should give them the project type, contract, specification formats, general conditions, and above all the Division 01 requirements, and should ask for their Division 01 input at that same time. Waiting for drafts, a late review, completed drawings, bidders' questions, or a discovered conflict invites the duplicated or conflicting discipline requirements this early exchange prevents.

questions.question: An electrical consultant's drawings include general notes on submittal procedures, warranties, and payment terms for the electrical work. What should the prime A/E direct?

options.A: Keep the notes on the drawings, since the consultant seals its own documents
options.B: Move the notes into a separate general requirements section for electrical work
options.C: Keep the notes, and add a statement that the drawings take precedence for electrical work
options.D: Move the requirements into Division 01 and the other appropriate contract documents
options.E: Keep the notes and repeat them in each Division 26 specification section
options.F: Leave them as notes and cite them by sheet from the Division 26 sections

questions.explanation: Consultants should not put general notes on administrative matters and terms and conditions on their drawings; those belong in Division 01 and the other contract documents, which also keeps consultants from writing separate general requirements for their disciplines. Sealing explains why consultants write their own sections, not why administrative notes stay on drawings, and a precedence statement, repetition, or cross-reference leaves the requirements in the wrong place.

questions.question: A specifier is placing the team's value-analysis (value-engineering) requirements. Without relying on the section title, which Division 01 section NUMBER is correct?
questions.explanation: Value Analysis is Section 01 24 00, where the general requirements and procedures for conducting value analysis are specified. The 01 2x family runs 01 21 00 Allowances, 01 22 00 Unit Prices, 01 23 00 Alternates, 01 24 00 Value Analysis, 01 25 00 Substitution Procedures, and 01 26 00 Contract Modification Procedures.

questions.question: A specifier is sorting draft Division 01 content into the categories industry guidance uses to describe the General Requirements. Procedures for eventually taking the completed facility out of service belong in which category?

options.A: Performance requirements
options.B: Temporary facilities and controls
options.C: Life cycle activities
options.D: Administrative and procedural requirements
options.E: Execution and closeout requirements
options.F: Quality requirements

questions.explanation: Life cycle activities relate to commissioning, facility operation, facility maintenance, and facility decommissioning, so procedures for taking the facility out of service fall there. Performance requirements concern facility and system performance, temporary facilities and controls exist only during construction, administrative and procedural requirements concern contract administration, and execution and closeout or quality requirements are Division 01 titles about the construction work, not about retiring the facility.

questions.question: The fire protection engineer asks the specifier to add a special submittal review step that applies only to the fire-suppression sprinkler section. Where should this requirement be written?

options.A: In Section 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures, in a paragraph naming the sprinkler section
options.B: In the supplementary conditions, modifying the submittals article
options.C: In a Basic Requirements section at the start of that division
options.D: In the affected section itself, as a section-specific procedure
options.E: In a general note on the fire protection drawings for that system
options.F: In the instructions to bidders, under the submittal requirements

questions.explanation: An administrative or procedural requirement peculiar to one section belongs in that section, while Division 01 carries requirements broad enough to apply across Divisions 02 through 49. Section 01 33 00 and the supplementary conditions are the wrong documents for a one-section procedure, Basic Requirements sections within a division are discouraged because they may conflict with Division 01, drawing notes are no place for procedures, and instructions to bidders are not contract documents.

questions.question: The section titles for Division 01 come from ____, and the arrangement of Division 01 numbers and titles approximates ____.

options.A: MasterFormat; the sequence of SectionFormat's three parts
options.B: SectionFormat; the order of the MasterFormat divisions
options.C: MasterFormat; the order of the general conditions articles
options.D: UniFormat; the sequence of SectionFormat's three parts
options.E: MasterFormat; the order of the UniFormat elements
options.F: UniFormat; the order of the general conditions articles

questions.explanation: MasterFormat provides the section titles for Division 01, and the Division 01 numbers and titles are arranged to approximate the sequence of information in SectionFormat's three parts: PART 1, PART 2, and PART 3. SectionFormat does not supply titles, UniFormat is neither the source of the titles nor the model for their order, and the general conditions articles are not the organizing basis.

questions.question: While reviewing a construction project manual, the owner's facility manager asks why Section 01 93 00—Facility Maintenance was not included in Division 01. Which response is consistent with industry guidance?

options.A: Facility life cycle activities fall outside Division 01 by definition
options.B: That title better suits a later stage, such as facility management
options.C: MasterFormat reserves that number solely for future expansion of Division 01
options.D: Maintenance topics belong in the general conditions instead
options.E: That title applies only to renovation work in existing buildings
options.F: That section may be issued only with design-build agreements

questions.explanation: Some MasterFormat titles, such as Section 01 93 00—Facility Maintenance, may never appear in a construction project manual, because specifications are written for the construction stage and those titles fit a later stage such as facility management. Life cycle activities are in fact one of the Division 01 categories, and nothing reserves the number, moves maintenance into the general conditions, or ties the title to renovation or design-build work.

questions.question: Industry guidance names two MasterFormat sections as examples of titles that are especially relevant to project manuals because they address construction activities directly. Which pair does it name?

options.A: 01 14 00—Work Restrictions and 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures
options.B: 01 50 00—Temporary Facilities and Controls and 01 93 00—Facility Maintenance
options.C: 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures and 01 93 00—Facility Maintenance
options.D: 01 14 00—Work Restrictions and 01 50 00—Temporary Facilities and Controls
options.E: 01 50 00—Temporary Facilities and Controls and 01 70 00—Execution and Closeout Requirements
options.F: 01 14 00—Work Restrictions and 01 93 00—Facility Maintenance

questions.explanation: Work Restrictions (01 14 00) and Temporary Facilities and Controls (01 50 00) are the two examples given of MasterFormat titles with particular relevance to project manuals, since both deal directly with construction activities. Facility Maintenance (01 93 00) is the example of a title that may never appear in a construction project manual, and Submittal Procedures (01 33 00) and Execution and Closeout Requirements (01 70 00) are not among the examples, so each wrong pair has at least one wrong title.

questions.question: Industry guidance aligns each Division 01 grouping with one of SectionFormat's three parts. Quality Control (Source) is aligned with the same part as which other grouping?

options.A: Quality Assurance
options.B: Performance Requirements
options.C: Quality Control (Field)
options.D: Temporary Facilities and Controls
options.E: Life Cycle Activities
options.F: Price and Payment Procedures

questions.explanation: Product Requirements, Performance Requirements, and Quality Control (Source) are the groupings aligned with PART 2—PRODUCTS. Quality Assurance, Temporary Facilities and Controls, and Price and Payment Procedures align with PART 1—GENERAL, while Quality Control (Field) and Life Cycle Activities align with PART 3—EXECUTION, so the three quality groupings fall in three different parts.

questions.question: Which Division 01 grouping does industry guidance align with PART 1—GENERAL of SectionFormat?

options.A: Temporary Facilities and Controls
options.B: Performance Requirements
options.C: Execution and Closeout Requirements
options.D: Life Cycle Activities
options.E: Product Requirements
options.F: Quality Control (Field)

questions.explanation: The Division 01 groupings aligned with PART 1—GENERAL are Summary, Price and Payment Procedures, Administrative Requirements, Quality Assurance, and Temporary Facilities and Controls. Performance Requirements and Product Requirements align with PART 2—PRODUCTS, while Quality Control (Field), Execution and Closeout Requirements, and Life Cycle Activities align with PART 3—EXECUTION.

questions.question: For a small tenant fit-out, a specifier wants to combine the Division 01 procedural requirements into three sections instead of issuing a separate section for every applicable Level 2 title. This approach is:

options.A: Not acceptable, since every MasterFormat Level 2 title must be its own section
options.B: Acceptable only if the supplementary conditions list each omitted title
options.C: Acceptable; sections may be combined or divided to suit project complexity
options.D: Acceptable only for PART 1 sections; PART 3 sections must remain separate
options.E: Not acceptable, since each SectionFormat part needs its own Division 01 section
options.F: Acceptable only if the agreement names each of the combined sections

questions.explanation: Tying Division 01 to SectionFormat gives an organizing logic flexible enough to combine procedural requirements into a few sections or divide them among many, depending on how complex the project is; a simple project may even combine Division 01 into one section. Nothing requires one section per Level 2 title or per SectionFormat part, a list of omitted titles, naming in the agreement, or keeping PART 3 groupings separate.

questions.question: The instructions to bidders state that the successful bidder must provide weekly drone photographs of progress. The requirement appears nowhere else in the project manual or drawings. During construction, the contractor declines to provide the photographs. The requirement is:

options.A: Enforceable, since the agreement incorporates the bidding documents by reference
options.B: Not enforceable, since procurement requirements are not contract documents
options.C: Not enforceable, since only the general conditions may impose documentation requirements
options.D: Enforceable, if the bid form acknowledged receipt of the instructions to bidders
options.E: Enforceable, since the low bidder's bid accepted all of its stated terms
options.F: Not enforceable, since only the agreement may require construction photographs

questions.explanation: Under the AIA, EJCDC, and ConsensusDocs general conditions, procurement requirements are not contract documents, so a requirement stated only in the instructions to bidders cannot be enforced during construction. Submitting a bid or acknowledging the instructions does not make them part of the contract. Neither the general conditions nor the agreement is the only place for such a requirement: photographic documentation belongs in Division 01, Section 01 32 00—Construction Progress Documentation.

questions.question: Bidders need to know before pricing that the project has detailed substitution procedures in Division 01. How should the instructions to bidders address this?

options.A: Refer to the applicable Division 01 section by its number and title
options.B: Restate the substitution procedures in full so bidders cannot miss them
options.C: Summarize the procedures and state that the summary governs during bidding
options.D: Omit any mention, since procurement requirements cannot address Division 01
options.E: Attach a copy of the Division 01 section to the bid form for signature
options.F: Move the substitution procedures out of Division 01 into the instructions

questions.explanation: Procurement requirements should point bidders to the relevant Division 01 section, identified by number and title, rather than repeat it; the instructions may state the deadline for substitution requests during bidding but cross-reference the section for the procedures. Restating, summarizing, attaching, or relocating the procedures creates duplication and room for conflict, and saying nothing leaves bidders without a pointer to the governing section.

questions.question: The owner-contractor agreement notes that the owner will occupy completed portions of the building during construction. Which Division 01 section specifies the need to accommodate the owner's occupancy in more detail?

options.A: Section 01 20 00—Price and Payment Procedures
options.B: Section 01 50 00—Temporary Facilities and Controls
options.C: Section 01 10 00—Summary
options.D: Section 01 30 00—Administrative Requirements
options.E: Section 01 70 00—Execution and Closeout Requirements
options.F: Section 01 40 00—Quality Requirements

questions.explanation: The Summary section, 01 10 00, sets out administrative details and what the owner and the contractor are each responsible for: a summary of the work, other contracts, work restrictions, and the need to make room for the owner's occupancy during construction. Section 01 20 00 expands on allowances, alternates, and unit prices, and the administrative, temporary facilities, quality, and execution and closeout groupings are not where owner occupancy is addressed.

questions.question: An owner-contractor agreement includes stipulated unit prices and a list of alternates, and the project also carries several allowances. Which Division 01 section expands on these agreement provisions?

options.A: Section 01 10 00—Summary
options.B: Section 01 30 00—Administrative Requirements
options.C: Section 01 70 00—Execution and Closeout Requirements
options.D: Section 01 20 00—Price and Payment Procedures
options.E: Section 01 40 00—Quality Requirements
options.F: Section 01 60 00—Product Requirements

questions.explanation: Section 01 20 00—Price and Payment Procedures is the Division 01 section that details the agreement's pricing provisions, such as allowances, alternates, and unit prices. Section 01 10 00—Summary covers the summary of work, other contracts, work restrictions, and owner occupancy, and the administrative, quality, product, and execution and closeout groupings do not carry these pricing mechanisms.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between the owner-contractor agreement and Division 01?

options.A: Division 01 supersedes the agreement wherever the two documents address the same topic
options.B: The agreement includes all contract documents by reference; Division 01 details some provisions
options.C: The agreement includes only the conditions of the contract; Division 01 restates its payment terms
options.D: The agreement includes the procurement requirements by reference; Division 01 then modifies them
options.E: The agreement and Division 01 are independent; neither relies on the other
options.F: Division 01 includes the agreement by reference and then adds details to it

questions.explanation: The owner-contractor agreement incorporates every other contract document by reference, and some of its provisions are supplemented by Division 01 sections that set out the parties' responsibilities in more detail. Division 01 neither supersedes the agreement nor incorporates it, the two are linked rather than independent, the agreement is not limited to the conditions of the contract, and procurement requirements are not contract documents.

questions.question: A peer reviewer notes that cutting and patching is addressed in both the general conditions and Division 01 and calls this a violation of the 'say it once and in the right place' principle. The best response is:

options.A: Disagree; the two state it at different levels of detail, without conflict
options.B: Agree; delete the Division 01 provisions and rely on the general conditions
options.C: Agree; move the general conditions text into the supplementary conditions
options.D: Disagree; Division 01 takes precedence over the general conditions in any case
options.E: Agree; keep only a bare reference to the general conditions in Division 01
options.F: Disagree; the principle applies only within one section, not across documents

questions.explanation: The general conditions cover cutting and patching only in broad terms, and Division 01 then details it for the specific project. Because the two state the requirement at different levels of detail, without duplication or conflict, the principle is not violated, so deleting, relocating, or reducing either text to a bare reference is unwarranted. The principle does apply across documents, and the answer does not rest on Division 01 taking precedence.

questions.question: Which set consists entirely of topics that industry guidance lists as usually covered, in broad terms, by the general conditions and then detailed in Division 01?

options.A: Property surveys, cutting and patching, cleaning, record documents
options.B: Bid security, warranties, submittals, progress schedules
options.C: Mock-ups, schedule of values, applications for payment, closeout procedures
options.D: Pest control, temporary utilities and services, warranties, cleaning
options.E: Record documents, submittals, cleaning, value analysis
options.F: Schedule of values, warranties, cleaning, alternates

questions.explanation: The topics the general conditions usually cover in broad terms, for Division 01 to detail, include property surveys, record documents, cutting and patching, and cleaning, along with warranties, submittals, progress schedules, temporary utilities and services, the schedule of values, applications for payment, and closeout procedures. Each other set contains one item from elsewhere: bid security is a procurement item, mock-ups belong to quality requirements, pest control to temporary controls, and value analysis and alternates to their own Division 01 sections.

questions.question: The general conditions broadly permit the owner to use separate contractors and to coordinate them. When separate contractors are in fact used, what does Division 01 add?

options.A: The bid security amount and bid opening date for each contract
options.B: The owner's legal right to award separate contracts and provide coordination
options.C: The contracts, the scope of work in each, and each party's coordination role
options.D: The insurance limits and bond amounts required of each separate contractor
options.E: The bidding procedures that each separate contractor must follow
options.F: The dispute-resolution terms between the owner and each contractor

questions.explanation: The general conditions only broadly allow the owner to use separate contractors and coordinate them; when separate contractors are used, Division 01 (for instance, Section 01 12 00—Multiple Contract Summary) identifies each contract and its scope and defines how the owner, the A/E, and each contractor take part in coordination. Bid security, opening dates, and bidding procedures are procurement items, the owner's right is already in the general conditions, and insurance, bonds, and dispute terms are contract conditions.

questions.question: The only general reference to Division 01 that belongs in the supplementary conditions is:

options.A: A list of every Division 01 section number and title
options.B: A summary restating the key provisions of each Division 01 section
options.C: A statement that Division 01 applies only where the general conditions are silent
options.D: A statement establishing the authority of Division 01
options.E: A statement that Division 01 governs wherever it conflicts with the general conditions
options.F: A statement that Division 01 is advisory and not one of the contract documents

questions.explanation: The one general reference to Division 01 that belongs in the supplementary conditions is a statement establishing Division 01's authority, which the standard general conditions do not state outright. A list or summary of Division 01 content invites duplication and conflict, a statement confining Division 01 to gaps or making it govern over the general conditions sets up precedence instead of authority, and calling it advisory would strip that authority away.

questions.question: A specifier adds a statement to the supplementary conditions that shop drawings, product data, and samples shall be prepared and submitted according to Section 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures. The owner's attorney asks whether the statement is required. It is:

options.A: Required, because Division 01 is unenforceable unless the supplementary conditions cite it
options.B: Improper, because the supplementary conditions may never cite a specific Division 01 section
options.C: Unnecessary, but it may help the user of the documents
options.D: Permitted, but only if it also summarizes the Section 01 33 00 requirements
options.E: Required, because the general conditions say nothing about submittals at all
options.F: Improper, because submittal requirements belong only in the agreement

questions.explanation: Statements in the supplementary conditions that point to specific Division 01 sections are unnecessary but may help the user, and this submittal statement is the standard example. Such a reference is neither required for enforceability nor prohibited; the general conditions do address submittals (A201 §3.12), the agreement is not where submittal procedures go, and summarizing Section 01 33 00 would repeat Division 01 content.

questions.question: A draft of the supplementary conditions includes detailed procedures for locating the contractor's field office and sanitation facilities. What should the specifier do?

options.A: Keep them there, since supplementary conditions take precedence over Division 01
options.B: Relocate them to the general conditions, which govern temporary facilities
options.C: Relocate them to the instructions to bidders, so bidders can price them
options.D: Relocate them to Division 01, where construction facilities are specified
options.E: Relocate them to the agreement, which states the contractor's obligations
options.F: Delete them, since field offices are left to the contractor's means and methods

questions.explanation: Supplementary conditions should neither repeat the general conditions nor take over subjects that belong in Division 01; field offices and sanitation facilities, including who installs and pays for them and where they may go, are specified in Section 01 52 00—Construction Facilities. Precedence is no reason to leave them where they are, the general and agreement texts are not the place for such detail, the instructions to bidders are not contract documents, and the requirements should be specified rather than dropped.

questions.question: Which pair of Division 01 subjects does industry guidance say usually requires extensive delineation on the drawings and close coordination with Division 01?

options.A: Submittals and quality requirements
options.B: Use of the site and phased construction
options.C: Use of the site and submittals
options.D: Phased construction and quality requirements
options.E: Multiple prime contracts and closeout procedures
options.F: Closeout procedures and submittals

questions.explanation: Division 01 sections on use of the site, phased construction, and multiple prime contracts usually have to be shown at length on the drawings, so the drawings and those sections must be closely coordinated. Submittals, quality requirements, and closeout procedures are purely procedural subjects that need no coordination with the drawings, so any pair that includes one of them is wrong.

questions.question: On a multiple-prime project, the specifier has limited time to cross-check Division 01 against the drawings. Which section needs no coordination with the drawings?

options.A: Section 01 12 00—Multiple Contract Summary
options.B: Section 01 14 00—Work Restrictions
options.C: Section 01 40 00—Quality Requirements
options.D: Section 01 11 00—Summary of Work
options.E: Section 01 14 19—Use of Site
options.F: Section 01 12 16—Work Sequence

questions.explanation: Purely procedural Division 01 sections, such as those for submittals, quality requirements, and closeout, need no checking against the drawings. Sections on multiple prime contracts, use of the site, and the sequence or phasing of the work usually need extensive delineation on the drawings, and the drawings graphically define the extent of work that the summary describes.

questions.question: The site plan for a single-contract project shows a future parking structure to be built later under a separate contract. A reviewer argues the drawings should show only work of this contract. Showing the parking structure is:

options.A: Appropriate, since drawings may define related work outside the contract
options.B: Improper, since drawings may depict only work included in this contract
options.C: Improper, since related work may be described only in Division 01 text
options.D: Appropriate only if the supplementary conditions expressly authorize it
options.E: Appropriate only if the parking structure is listed as a bid alternate
options.F: Improper unless the separate contract has already been awarded

questions.explanation: Drawings graphically define Division 01 subjects such as the extent of work, and they may also show related work whether or not it is part of the contract. Drawings are therefore not limited to this contract's work, and nothing confines related work to Division 01 text, requires authorization in the supplementary conditions, or makes it depend on an alternate or on the other contract's award.

questions.question: In the recommended sequence of Division 01 coordination activities, the specifier first distributes an early draft to contributors and then prepares a list of requirements solicited from consultants. Which activity comes next?

options.A: Resolve overlapping requirements, omissions, and conflicts
options.B: Determine which requirements belong in Division 01 and which are section-specific
options.C: Compare the list of requirements with the Division 01 draft
options.D: Revise the Division 01 draft for review by specification contributors
options.E: Issue the Division 01 draft to prospective bidders for their comment
options.F: Assign each Division 01 section to the consultant with the most related work

questions.explanation: The Division 01 coordination effort runs in order: distribute a Division 01 draft early, prepare a list of requirements solicited from consultants and contributors, compare that list with the draft, determine which requirements belong in Division 01 and which in individual sections, resolve overlaps, omissions, and conflicts, and revise the draft for review. Determining, resolving, and revising all follow the comparison, and bidders and section assignments are not part of the sequence.

questions.question: For an occupied hospital renovation, a specifier finds restrictions on the contractor's operations in occupied areas written in both Section 01 14 00—Work Restrictions and Section 01 35 00—Special Procedures. The specifier should:

options.A: Keep both so each section is complete when read on its own
options.B: Verify the requirement is stated in one location that provides its basis
options.C: Move both into the supplementary conditions to give them contractual force
options.D: Add a Basic Requirements section to each affected technical division instead
options.E: Restate the restrictions on the drawings so that they govern in the field
options.F: Add a precedence clause stating which of the two sections governs

questions.explanation: Section 01 14 00 restricts the contractor's operations in a building the owner occupies, while Section 01 35 00 may set similar restrictions by activity or project type, so the specifier should make sure each requirement sits in one location that gives the basis for imposing it. Keeping duplicates invites conflict, precedence clauses and drawing notes add more places for it, and division-level Basic Requirements sections are discouraged because they may conflict with Division 01.

questions.question: On a small retail project, the owner's representative asks the specifier to add extensive Division 01 requirements: daily reports, weekly coordination meetings, multiple photo sets, and elaborate temporary facilities. Which consideration from industry guidance should guide the specifier's response?

options.A: These items carry only direct costs, which bidders will identify and price
options.B: Detailed procedures reduce disputes, which lowers overall construction cost
options.C: Added requirements shift all administrative obligations from the A/E to the contractor
options.D: Overspecifying may raise costs and burden whoever administers the contract
options.E: Small projects need more Division 01 detail, since their contractors are smaller
options.F: Division 01 requirements cost the owner nothing, since the A/E administers them

questions.explanation: The administrative and procedural requirements and the temporary facilities and controls in Division 01 carry both direct and indirect costs, so overspecifying can raise construction costs unnecessarily and impose excessive obligations on whoever administers the construction contract. The costs are not only direct, added procedures are not a cost saving, they do not shift A/E duties to the contractor, and a small project calls for scaling requirements to fit rather than adding more.

questions.question: For detailed examples of Division 01 sections, specifiers are referred to master guide specification systems. Which system-and-publisher pairing is correct?

options.A: MASTERSPEC, an AIA product published by Deltek
options.B: SpecLink, published by the AIA
options.C: SPECTEXT, published by Building Systems Design
options.D: Unified Facilities Guide Specifications, published by GSA
options.E: SPECTEXT, published by the AIA
options.F: Unified Facilities Guide Specifications, published by Deltek

questions.explanation: Commonly cited master guide specification systems with detailed Division 01 examples are MASTERSPEC, the AIA's system published by Deltek; SPECTEXT, also from Deltek; SpecLink, from Building Systems Design (BSD); and the Unified Facilities Guide Specifications, from DoD and NASA. SpecLink is not an AIA product, SPECTEXT is not from BSD or the AIA, and the UFGS come from DoD and NASA, not GSA or Deltek.

questions.question: The owner wants daily reports of site activity and recorded video of the work as it proceeds. The requirements for these belong in:

options.A: Section 01 31 00—Project Management and Coordination
options.B: Section 01 32 00—Construction Progress Documentation
options.C: Section 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures
options.D: Section 01 78 00—Closeout Submittals
options.E: Section 01 35 00—Special Procedures
options.F: Section 01 45 00—Quality Control

questions.explanation: Section 01 32 00—Construction Progress Documentation covers the progress schedule, daily construction reports, and the kind of photographic record required, whether prints, digital images, or video. Section 01 31 00 covers coordination and meetings, Section 01 33 00 shop drawings, product data, and samples, Section 01 35 00 special procedures for particular facility types, Section 01 45 00 testing and inspection, and Section 01 78 00 closeout submittals.

questions.question: On a multiple-prime project, Section 01 31 00—Project Management and Coordination must address who is responsible for project meetings. The specifier determines whether that responsibility lies with:

options.A: the owner or the architect/engineer
options.B: the architect/engineer or the commissioning agent
options.C: the owner's project manager or the A/E's field representative
options.D: one of the contractors or the construction manager
options.E: the owner or the construction manager
options.F: the architect/engineer or one of the contractors

questions.explanation: On a multiple-prime project, Section 01 31 00 assigns responsibility for project meetings to either one of the prime contractors or the construction manager, and it also sets how often and where the meetings are held. Pairs that bring in the owner, the A/E, its field representative, or the commissioning agent are not the alternatives this decision weighs, even when one half of the pair is right.

questions.question: A specifier must state the testing laboratory's qualifications, the limits on its authority, the contractor's cooperation duties, and who pays for tests, along with site mock-ups that will serve as standards for installed work. These belong in:

options.A: Section 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures
options.B: Section 01 60 00—Product Requirements
options.C: Section 01 40 00—Quality Requirements
options.D: Section 01 75 00—Starting and Adjusting
options.E: Section 01 50 00—Temporary Facilities and Controls
options.F: Section 01 70 00—Execution and Closeout Requirements

questions.explanation: Section 01 40 00—Quality Requirements specifies site mock-ups and field samples used as quality standards for installed work, plus testing laboratory qualifications, limits on the laboratory's authority, contractor cooperation, payment responsibilities, and references to required tests. Section 01 33 00 governs shop drawings, product data, and samples, Section 01 60 00 product options, delivery, and storage, Section 01 75 00 starting and adjusting, and Sections 01 50 00 and 01 70 00 temporary facilities and execution.

questions.question: A project needs temporary lots where construction workers can leave their cars, plus temporary drives into the site. Which section specifies these facilities?

options.A: Section 01 55 00—Vehicular Access and Parking
options.B: Section 01 53 00—Temporary Construction
options.C: Section 01 56 00—Temporary Barriers and Enclosures
options.D: Section 01 14 00—Work Restrictions
options.E: Section 01 52 00—Construction Facilities
options.F: Section 01 51 00—Temporary Utilities

questions.explanation: Temporary access and parking facilities are specified in Section 01 55 00—Vehicular Access and Parking. Section 01 53 00—Temporary Construction is limited to the structural parts of temporary structures, Section 01 56 00 covers fences and noise and dust barriers, Section 01 52 00 covers field offices and sanitary facilities, Section 01 51 00 covers temporary water, power, and similar services, and Section 01 14 00 holds special restrictions on the contractor's access rather than the facilities themselves.

questions.question: The owner will let the contractor's delivery trucks onto the operating campus only through the north gate and only between 9:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. Where should this limitation on the contractor's access be specified?

options.A: Section 01 55 00—Vehicular Access and Parking
options.B: Section 01 14 00—Work Restrictions
options.C: Section 01 57 00—Temporary Controls
options.D: Section 01 56 00—Temporary Barriers and Enclosures
options.E: Section 01 31 00—Project Management and Coordination
options.F: Section 01 52 00—Construction Facilities

questions.explanation: Section 01 55 00—Vehicular Access and Parking is limited to maintaining and controlling access, and special restrictions on the contractor's access go in Section 01 14 00—Work Restrictions, which also carries limits on access to and use of the site. Sections 01 56 00 and 01 57 00 cover barriers, enclosures, and temporary controls, Section 01 31 00 covers coordination and meetings, and Section 01 52 00 covers field offices and sanitary facilities.

questions.question: Which pairing of requirement and Division 01 section is correct for temporary facilities and controls?

options.A: Noise barriers—01 57 00 Temporary Controls
options.B: Temporary signs—01 52 00 Construction Facilities
options.C: Swing staging and scaffolding—01 53 00 Temporary Construction
options.D: Dust barriers—01 56 00 Temporary Barriers and Enclosures
options.E: Temporary fencing—01 52 00 Construction Facilities
options.F: Erosion and sediment control—01 51 00 Temporary Utilities

questions.explanation: Fences, noise barriers, and dust barriers are specified in Section 01 56 00—Temporary Barriers and Enclosures, so the dust barrier pairing is correct and the fencing pairing is not. Section 01 57 00—Temporary Controls covers controls such as erosion and sediment, storm water, and pest control rather than noise barriers or utilities; temporary signs belong in Section 01 58 00—Project Identification; and swing staging and scaffolding belong in Section 01 54 00—Construction Aids.

questions.question: On a multiple-prime project, the tower crane and personnel hoists furnished by one prime contractor will also be used by the other prime contractors. The requirements for sharing this equipment are indicated in:

options.A: Section 01 54 00—Construction Aids
options.B: Section 01 51 00—Temporary Utilities
options.C: Section 01 53 00—Temporary Construction
options.D: Section 01 52 00—Construction Facilities
options.E: Section 01 56 00—Temporary Barriers and Enclosures
options.F: Section 01 55 00—Vehicular Access and Parking

questions.explanation: Section 01 54 00—Construction Aids specifies temporary elevators, hoists, cranes, scaffolding, platforms, and swing staging, and on a project with multiple contracts it states how those aids are to be shared. Section 01 51 00 covers temporary utilities, Section 01 52 00 field offices and sanitary facilities, Section 01 53 00 the structural parts of temporary structures, Section 01 55 00 access and parking, and Section 01 56 00 barriers and enclosures.

questions.question: The owner will purchase kitchen equipment for installation by the contractor, and Section 01 64 00 will be used. Where should the owner's list of these items be located, and where should it be cross-referenced?

options.A: Listed in 01 10 00—Summary; cross-referenced in 01 64 00
options.B: Listed in 01 64 00—Owner-Furnished Products; cross-referenced in 01 10 00
options.C: Listed in 01 73 00—Execution; cross-referenced in 01 64 00—Owner-Furnished Products
options.D: Listed in 01 65 00—Product Delivery Requirements; cross-referenced in 01 10 00
options.E: Listed in 01 62 00—Product Options; cross-referenced in 01 10 00
options.F: Listed in 01 66 00—Product Storage and Handling; cross-referenced in 01 64 00

questions.explanation: Owner-furnished items may be listed in the Summary section or in the Owner-Furnished Products section, but when Section 01 64 00 is used, the list goes there and Section 01 10 00 refers to it. Reversing the two contradicts that, Section 01 73 00 covers installing owner-furnished products while referring to 01 64 00 for their characteristics, and Sections 01 62 00, 01 65 00, and 01 66 00 cover product options, delivery, and storage.

questions.question: A specifier needs to state the basic rules the contractor follows when choosing among specified products, including the general procedure for deciding whether products are equivalent. This belongs in:

options.A: Section 01 64 00—Owner-Furnished Products
options.B: Section 01 65 00—Product Delivery Requirements
options.C: Section 01 62 00—Product Options
options.D: Section 01 66 00—Product Storage and Handling Requirements
options.E: Section 01 25 00—Substitution Procedures
options.F: Section 01 73 00—Execution

questions.explanation: Section 01 62 00—Product Options sets the basic rules for the contractor's choices among the products specified, including how to judge whether products are equivalent. Section 01 25 00 uses similar rules but for the contractor's proposals to substitute products that were not specified, Section 01 64 00 covers owner-furnished products, Sections 01 65 00 and 01 66 00 cover delivery and storage, and Section 01 73 00 covers installation.

questions.question: In Section 01 73 00—Execution, industry guidance distinguishes among three possibilities for existing material and equipment. Which of the following is one of them?

options.A: Salvaged and retained by the contractor, with salvage value accruing to the contractor
options.B: Abandoned in place and concealed behind new construction
options.C: Salvaged and sold by the contractor, with proceeds shared equally with the owner
options.D: Salvaged and retained by the contractor, with salvage value accruing to the owner
options.E: Demolished and hauled off site by the contractor as construction waste
options.F: Left in place for the owner to remove after substantial completion

questions.explanation: Section 01 73 00—Execution distinguishes three cases for existing material and equipment: salvaged and reinstalled in the work; salvaged and kept by the contractor, with the salvage value going to the owner; and salvaged and delivered to the owner. Value going to the contractor, a split of sale proceeds, abandonment in place, hauling it away as waste, and leaving it for the owner to remove are not among the three.

questions.question: The mechanical engineer wants the HVAC systems run and adjusted again in the opposite season after initial start-up, with a defined method for reporting compliance. The basic requirement belongs in:

options.A: Section 01 75 00—Starting and Adjusting
options.B: Section 01 79 00—Demonstration and Training
options.C: Section 01 78 00—Closeout Submittals
options.D: Section 01 76 00—Protecting Installed Construction
options.E: Section 01 77 00—Closeout Procedures
options.F: Section 01 74 00—Cleaning and Waste Management

questions.explanation: Section 01 75 00—Starting and Adjusting sets the schedule for starting and adjusting equipment and systems, the requirements for seasonal operation, and the method for reporting compliance. Demonstration and Training covers instructing the owner's staff, Closeout Submittals covers record documents and operation and maintenance data, Closeout Procedures covers substantial and final completion, Cleaning covers cleaning and recycling, and Protecting Installed Construction covers protecting finished work.

questions.question: While other trades keep working, newly completed wall and floor work must be guarded, and the documents must state how damaged completed work will be remedied or replaced. These basic requirements belong in:

options.A: Section 01 56 00—Temporary Barriers and Enclosures
options.B: Section 01 76 00—Protecting Installed Construction
options.C: Section 01 74 00—Cleaning and Waste Management
options.D: Section 01 77 00—Closeout Procedures
options.E: Section 01 73 00—Execution
options.F: Section 01 78 00—Closeout Submittals

questions.explanation: Section 01 76 00—Protecting Installed Construction includes the basic requirements for protecting finished work while construction continues and states how damaged work is to be remedied or replaced. Section 01 56 00 covers barriers that protect facility users and existing spaces, Section 01 73 00 covers installing products, Section 01 74 00 covers cleaning and recycling, Section 01 77 00 covers completion and punch lists, and Section 01 78 00 covers closeout submittals.

questions.question: An owner requires that the building earn particular, owner-selected credits (specific points) under a named green building rating system. Where in Division 01 should the specifier locate these requirements?

options.A: Section 01 81 00—Facility Performance Requirements
options.B: Section 01 81 13—Sustainable Design Requirements
options.C: A section in the range 01 82 00 through 01 89 00
options.D: Section 01 35 00—Special Procedures
options.E: Section 01 78 53—Sustainable Design Closeout Documentation
options.F: Section 01 57 19—Temporary Environmental Controls

questions.explanation: When a project must earn specific points in a particular rating system, the requirements go in Section 01 35 00 or its subordinate sections, such as 01 35 63 for sustainability certification requirements. Section 01 81 00 covers facility-wide performance such as sustainability and energy goals, 01 81 13 is for a target rating whose means are left to the contractor, 01 82 00 to 01 89 00 cover performance shared across sections, and the closeout and temporary controls sections serve other purposes.

questions.question: The design team wants interior partitions, doors, and joint sealants, which are specified in several different sections, to jointly meet a minimum sound isolation rating. Where should this requirement be specified, and who is responsible for how it is achieved?

options.A: Section 01 81 00; the A/E details the assemblies that achieve the rating
options.B: Section 01 81 00; the contractor develops the means and methods
options.C: A section within 01 82 00 to 01 89 00; the contractor develops the means and methods
options.D: A section within 01 82 00 to 01 89 00; the A/E details the assemblies in each section
options.E: Section 01 35 00; the contractor develops the means and methods
options.F: Section 01 81 13; the A/E details the assemblies in each section

questions.explanation: Sections 01 82 00 through 01 89 00 hold the facility's overall performance requirements when work results in several sections must perform together to reach a minimum level, and the contractor is responsible for developing the means and methods to reach it. Section 01 81 00 and its subsection 01 81 13 are for general facility-wide goals such as sustainability and energy, Section 01 35 00 is for special procedures such as rating-system points, and having the A/E detail the solution contradicts the contractor's responsibility.

questions.question: A specifier is drafting Section 01 21 00—Allowances for a door hardware cash allowance. Which other documents typically also carry allowance provisions that must be coordinated with that section?

options.A: The procurement requirements, the conditions of the contract, and Section 08 71 00—Door Hardware
options.B: The procurement requirements, the conditions of the contract, and the door hardware product submittals
options.C: The procurement requirements, Section 01 22 00—Unit Prices, and the door hardware product submittals
options.D: The schedule of values, the conditions of the contract, and the door hardware product submittals
options.E: The procurement requirements, Section 01 23 00—Alternates, and Section 08 71 00—Door Hardware
options.F: The conditions of the contract, the schedule of values, and Section 08 71 00—Door Hardware

questions.explanation: Allowance requirements typically appear in four coordinated places: the procurement requirements, the conditions of the contract, Division 01, and the specification section for the item the allowance covers, here 08 71 00. Submittals are not contract documents and do not carry allowance provisions, and the unit price and alternates sections and the schedule of values are not among the documents that state the allowance.

questions.question: A school project is bid as a stipulated sum with just two unit prices, for rock excavation and unsuitable soil replacement. The project manager suggests skipping formal unit-price procedures because the contract is not unit-price based. How should the specifier respond?

options.A: Agree; formal unit price procedures are needed only for contracts based entirely on unit prices
options.B: Agree; the general conditions alone adequately govern a few unit prices in a stipulated sum contract
options.C: Disagree; unit price requirements and procedures must be defined in the procurement documents either way
options.D: Disagree; the two unit prices should instead be converted into allowances under Section 01 21 00
options.E: Disagree; the two unit prices should be bid as alternates under Section 01 23 00
options.F: Agree; a few unit prices in a stipulated sum contract are set later by change order

questions.explanation: Unit price requirements and procedures must be defined in the procurement documents, and the rule applies equally to a stipulated sum contract with a few unit prices and to a contract priced entirely by unit prices. The share of unit-price work does not change that, the general conditions alone are not enough, and converting the unit prices to allowances or alternates, or pricing them later by change order, defeats their purpose.

questions.question: The requirements and procedures for handling unit prices involve which two components, both of which must then be coordinated with the applicable technical specifications?

options.A: The agreement form and the supplementary conditions
options.B: The bid or proposal form and Division 01 sections
options.C: The instructions to bidders and the drawing schedules
options.D: The bid security form and the schedule of values
options.E: The bid or proposal form and the agreement form
options.F: The schedule of values and Division 01 sections

questions.explanation: Unit price requirements rely on the bid or proposal form together with carefully written Division 01 sections, and both have to be coordinated with the related technical sections in Divisions 02 through 49. The agreement, supplementary conditions, instructions to bidders, bid security, and schedule of values are not that pair, so each half-right pairing is still wrong.

questions.question: While writing Section 01 22 00—Unit Prices, a specifier plans to copy the unit-price paragraphs of the project's standard general conditions into the section word for word so all requirements sit in one place. What does industry guidance recommend instead?

options.A: Coordinate with the general conditions and expand on them without duplicating them
options.B: Delete the unit price paragraphs from the general conditions so Division 01 governs alone
options.C: Restate the general conditions in Division 01 and let the agreement resolve any conflict
options.D: Leave unit prices out of Division 01 since the general conditions already address them
options.E: Copy them, but label the copied paragraphs as informational only
options.F: Move unit prices to the bid form only, with no Division 01 provisions

questions.explanation: Unit price requirements must be coordinated with the conditions of the contract to prevent conflicts, duplication, or omission; most standard general conditions already address unit prices, and Division 01 usually expands on them. Copying the clauses, even labeled as informational, creates the duplication to avoid, deleting general-condition text is not the remedy, and leaving unit prices out of Division 01 or putting them only on the bid form omits essential requirements.

questions.question: On an EJCDC C-700 project, the bid form listed an estimated quantity of 2,000 cubic yards of rock excavation, but only 1,400 cubic yards were actually excavated. The contractor argues the owner guaranteed the 2,000 cubic yard quantity. Under C-700, which statement is correct?

options.A: The quantity is guaranteed because the bid is attached to the signed agreement
options.B: The quantity is guaranteed unless the owner issued a field order reducing it
options.C: Estimated quantities become guaranteed once the engineer accepts the bid form
options.D: Estimated quantities are not guaranteed; they serve to compare bids
options.E: The quantity is guaranteed because the engineer prepared the estimate
options.F: Payment is based on the estimated quantity, not the quantity excavated

questions.explanation: Under C-700, estimated quantities of unit price work are not guaranteed; they serve only to compare bids and set an initial contract price, and payment is based on the actual quantities, which the engineer determines. Attaching the bid to the agreement, a field order, the engineer's estimate, or acceptance of the bid form does not turn an estimate into a guarantee; a large variance can at most support a claim to adjust the unit price.

questions.question: On a project using EJCDC C-700, the contractor and owner disagree about how much excavated material should be paid as rock rather than common excavation under the unit price schedule. Under C-700, who has the authority to determine the actual quantities and classifications?

options.A: The owner's representative
options.B: The contractor's licensed surveyor
options.C: The engineer
options.D: The independent testing agency
options.E: The owner and the contractor jointly, by agreement
options.F: A dispute review board named in the contract

questions.explanation: C-700 gives the engineer the authority to decide the actual quantities and classifications of unit price work, after reviewing its preliminary determinations with the contractor; the engineer's written decision is final and binding on owner and contractor, subject to later correction. The owner's representative, a surveyor, or a testing agency may supply information, and the parties or a dispute board do not make that determination.

questions.question: Under an EJCDC C-700 contract, a contractor's pay application bills unit-priced pipe bedding at the bid unit price and then adds a separate 15 percent markup for overhead and profit. Under C-700, how should the engineer view the markup?

options.A: Acceptable, because unit prices are understood to cover only direct labor, materials, and equipment
options.B: Not acceptable, because unit price bids already include overhead and profit
options.C: Acceptable, provided the engineer has approved the contractor's schedule of values
options.D: Not acceptable, because overhead and profit on unit price work require a field order
options.E: Acceptable, because overhead and profit are paid on every change in quantity
options.F: Not acceptable, because unit price work carries no overhead or profit at all

questions.explanation: Under C-700, each unit price is deemed to include an amount the contractor considers adequate for its overhead and profit on that item, so an added markup would count those costs twice. The claim that unit prices cover only direct costs, or carry no overhead and profit at all, contradicts that provision, and neither an approved schedule of values, a change in quantity, nor a field order changes what the unit price already includes.

questions.question: When the A/E assists the owner in planning how the construction work will be procured, which factors are weighed in evaluating a general contractor, multiple contractors, or a particular project delivery method?

options.A: Owner financing sources, the contractors' bonding capacity, and the local insurance market
options.B: Applicable building codes, zoning restrictions, and the AHJ's permitting schedule
options.C: Design fee limits, consultant availability, and the A/E's documentation schedule
options.D: Local practices, the local labor market, and likely unfavorable site conditions
options.E: Bid bond rates, retainage practice, and the owner's payment terms
options.F: The building's occupancy type, height, and construction classification

questions.explanation: The procurement plan the A/E helps the owner build weighs local practices, the local labor market, and the likelihood of unfavorable site conditions when choosing among a general contractor, multiple contractors, and delivery methods. Financing, bonding, retainage, codes, zoning, building classification, design fees, and A/E staffing are not the factors listed for that evaluation.

questions.question: The A/E's production schedule has slipped. The project manager proposes releasing the bid documents on time despite several known coordination gaps, intending to fix them through addenda during bidding and change orders after award. What is the best course of action?

options.A: Release on time and correct the gaps through addenda issued early in the bidding period
options.B: Release on time and correct the gaps by change orders once the agreement is executed
options.C: Correct the gaps first; addenda and change orders should not be relied on to fix them
options.D: Correct the gaps first; addenda may not be issued after the bidding period begins
options.E: Release on time and explain the gaps orally at the prebid conference
options.F: Correct the gaps first; change orders cannot be used after the agreement is executed

questions.explanation: Nothing replaces clear, complete, and carefully coordinated contract documents, and relying on addenda and change orders to repair poorly prepared drawings and project manuals should be avoided. Both release-on-time choices knowingly issue deficient documents, and oral explanations should be avoided. The other correct-first choices give false reasons: addenda are issued before bids are received, so during bidding, and change orders are the instruments issued after the agreement is executed.

questions.question: A state agency owner requires the A/E to use the agency's own addendum and change order forms and procedures, which differ slightly from the commonly recommended ones. How should such differences be viewed?

options.A: They override the recommended principles, so agency procedures replace them entirely
options.B: They are procedural only and do not affect the underlying principles
options.C: They are acceptable only if the agency also adopts the AIA document forms
options.D: They must be reconciled by the specifier in the supplementary conditions
options.E: They must be replaced by the A/E's standard forms before bidding
options.F: They apply only to addenda; change orders must still use federal forms

questions.explanation: Many public agencies have their own addendum and change order forms and procedures that vary somewhat from the usual recommendations, but the variations are procedural and leave the underlying principles intact. Agency procedures do not override those principles, need not adopt AIA or federal forms or be replaced by the A/E's forms, and do not have to be reconciled in the supplementary conditions.

questions.question: During bidding, the A/E accepts a bidder's request to use a different manufacturer's roof membrane. How should this acceptance be made part of the procurement documents?

options.A: Issue an addendum to all bidders listing the approved substitution
options.B: Issue a field order to all bidders identifying the approved product
options.C: Send a letter only to the requesting bidder confirming the approval
options.D: Defer the approval and process it by change order after award
options.E: Approve it at the prebid meeting and record it only in the meeting minutes
options.F: Issue a construction change directive naming the approved product

questions.explanation: Addenda are used whenever the procurement documents must change, including to add approved substitutions, so an accepted substitution goes to all bidders by addendum and can be bid as an equal to the specified product. A letter to one bidder or meeting minutes do not modify the documents everyone is bidding on, field orders and construction change directives are construction-phase instruments, and a post-award change order is too late.

questions.question: Besides the instructions for procurement and the bid/proposal form, which documents does industry guidance identify as containing references to addenda, their method of issue, and related facts?

options.A: Sections 01 25 00 and 01 26 00 in Division 01
options.B: The advertisement for bids and the bid bond form
options.C: The drawing index and the project manual table of contents
options.D: The agreement and the conditions of the contract
options.E: The invitation to bid and the qualification statement
options.F: The submittal procedures and the project schedule

questions.explanation: References to addenda, how they are issued, and related facts appear in four places: the procurement instructions, the bid or proposal form, the owner-contractor agreement, and the conditions of the contract. Division 01 sections, the advertisement or invitation, the bid bond, the qualification statement, the schedule, and the drawing index or table of contents are not among them.

questions.question: After award and signing of the agreement, the contractor claims that Addendum No. 3, which revised a paragraph in Section 07 54 23, is not binding because addenda are only procurement documents. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The addendum lapsed at bid opening and binds no one unless it is reissued
options.B: The revision is binding only if it is reissued later as a change order
options.C: The revision became a contract document when the agreement was executed
options.D: The addendum remains a procurement document superseded by the agreement
options.E: The revision binds only the subcontractor that bid Section 07 54 23
options.F: The revision binds only if the contractor signed a receipt for it

questions.explanation: An addendum joins the procurement documents when issued, and once the agreement is executed, the parts of it that affect the contract documents become contract documents; AIA's contract documents expressly include addenda issued before the agreement is executed. The revision does not need to be reissued as a change order, did not lapse at bid opening, is not superseded, and binds the contractor rather than one subcontractor.

questions.question: A public owner will award three prime contracts (general, mechanical, and electrical) that are bid at the same time. How does industry guidance recommend numbering the addenda?

options.A: Use one consecutive series of addenda numbers shared by all the contracts
options.B: Use a separate consecutive series of addenda numbers for each contract
options.C: Number addenda by their issue date rather than in consecutive sequence
options.D: Number addenda by the specification Division that each one affects
options.E: Number addenda by the drawing sheet that each one revises
options.F: Restart the numbering at 1 for each week of the bidding period

questions.explanation: Addenda should be numbered consecutively, and where separate contracts will be awarded, each contract gets its own series of addenda numbers. A single shared series, date-based numbering, numbering by Division or drawing sheet, or restarting the count each week does not follow that practice; a simple numbering system for items within each addendum is a separate aid to cross-referencing.

questions.question: Five days before bid opening, the A/E finds that the structural framing for an entire wing must be redesigned, a significant change. What is the best course of action?

options.A: Advise the owner, issue a complete addendum, and if possible delay the bid date
options.B: Issue a short addendum with a few brief statements describing the change
options.C: Hold the change and issue it by change order after the agreement is executed
options.D: Issue a minor addendum, since four days' notice is the recommended minimum
options.E: Issue the addendum on the day before bids are due without telling the owner
options.F: Explain the redesign orally to bidders and confirm it after bids are opened

questions.explanation: For a significant change late in bidding, a hastily prepared addendum of a few inadequate statements should be avoided; the owner should be advised and, where possible, the bid opening postponed. The four-day lead time applies only to minor addenda, oral explanations should be avoided, and holding a change until after the agreement is executed suits only minor changes with no effect on cost or time, which a wing redesign is not.

questions.question: An addendum will include four items: a revision to Sheet A-201, a correction to an item in Addendum No. 1, a change to the instructions to bidders, and a change to Section 09 21 16. In what order should these items appear in the standard addendum format?

options.A: Instructions to bidders, Addendum No. 1 correction, Section 09 21 16, Sheet A-201
options.B: Addendum No. 1 correction, instructions to bidders, Section 09 21 16, Sheet A-201
options.C: Addendum No. 1 correction, Section 09 21 16, Sheet A-201, instructions to bidders
options.D: Instructions to bidders, Section 09 21 16, Sheet A-201, Addendum No. 1 correction
options.E: Sheet A-201, Section 09 21 16, instructions to bidders, Addendum No. 1 correction
options.F: Addendum No. 1 correction, Sheet A-201, instructions to bidders, Section 09 21 16

questions.explanation: The standard addendum format places changes to prior addenda first, then changes to procurement requirements such as the instructions to bidders, then contracting requirements, then specifications in sequence, and finally drawings. Each other sequence moves the prior-addendum correction, the procurement change, or the drawing revision out of that order.

questions.question: In a typical addendum, a correction to a prior addendum, a bidding-requirements change, a contracting-requirements change, and specification changes appear under separate headings. How are the individual items numbered?

options.A: Restarting at 1 under each heading
options.B: By the affected section or sheet number
options.C: With a letter per heading and a number per item
options.D: Consecutively from the first item to the last
options.E: By the date each item was approved
options.F: By the page number of the changed text

questions.explanation: Each item in an addendum is numbered consecutively for ease of reference, so the numbers run straight through the prior-addenda, procurement, contracting, specification, and drawing headings rather than starting over under each one. Restarting at each heading, using section, sheet, or page numbers, approval dates, or a letter-number scheme makes items harder to cite later.

questions.question: Which part of the standard AIA, EJCDC, ConsensusDocs, and DBIA document families spells out the procedures for issuing interpretations and for ordering minor modifications consistent with them?

options.A: Their contractor-subcontractor agreements
options.B: Their instructions to bidders
options.C: Their conditions of the contract
