Under the UCC the parties may settle on a limited warranty with fewer remedies, so no rule requires labor or consequential damages, and the correction period is a one-year obligation, not a 15-year one. Warranty forms are reviewed along with other submittals, so they are within the A/E's review.

questions.question: An owner needs a concealed below-slab vapor retarder to perform for the life of the building. A newly introduced product carries a 30-year warranty; an established product carries 15 years. What should the A/E do before specifying?

options.A: Specify the established product only if its manufacturer will extend to 30 years
options.B: Select the 30-year product, since its warranty covers the longer performance period
options.C: Verify each product's performance history and the testing that supports its term
options.D: Specify either product, since warranty duration reflects expected service life
options.E: Require each manufacturer's standard warranty to be submitted for approval
options.F: Specify both products and let the contractor choose between them on price

questions.explanation: Warranty time limits often bear no direct relation to expected service life, so where performance duration is critical the A/E should check the product's performance history and the testing the manufacturer did to support the stated period; a long warranty on a new product is itself questionable. Choosing by warranty length or price, relying on submitted standard warranties, or treating duration as service life all skip that verification.

questions.question: An owner directs the specifier to name a single brand of submersible pump, overriding the supplier's recommendation for the application. Under the UCC as industry guidance explains it, which warranty does the buyer give up by demanding one named brand?

options.A: Express warranty created by the product description
options.B: Implied warranty of merchantability
options.C: Warranty of clear title free of any security interests
options.D: Implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose
options.E: Express warranty based on a sample or model
options.F: Full warranty covering labor and consequential damages

questions.explanation: A fitness-for-a-particular-purpose warranty is implied only when the buyer relies on the seller's skill and judgment to choose suitable goods. A buyer who demands one brand is relying on its own judgment, so no fitness warranty arises. Merchantability, title, express warranties from a description or sample, and a full warranty's remedies do not depend on that reliance, so naming a brand does not give them up.

questions.question: One specification calls for a pump; another calls for a submersible pump. The assurance that the second pump will operate under water comes from which warranty?

options.A: Express warranty based on a sample or model of the pump
options.B: Implied warranty of merchantability
options.C: Warranty of clear title to the goods
options.D: Implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose
options.E: Full warranty covering both labor and materials
options.F: Third-party guaranty from the supplier's surety

questions.explanation: A seller of a generic pump impliedly warrants that it is merchantable, fit for the ordinary purposes pumps serve; a seller of a submersible pump may also warrant fitness for the particular purpose of working under water. Merchantability covers only ordinary uses, title concerns ownership free of liens, no sample or model is involved, and a full warranty or a surety's guaranty describes remedies or backing, not fitness for a stated purpose.

questions.question: A manufacturer's product data sheet makes a written performance claim, while fine print elsewhere in the same document disclaims that claim. Under the UCC, how is the conflict resolved?

options.A: Warranty language takes precedence over the conflicting disclaimer
options.B: The disclaimer controls, because it is the more specific language
options.C: Both are void, so only the implied warranties remain in effect
options.D: The disclaimer controls if it uses the words as is, with all faults
options.E: The disclaimer controls if it is printed in conspicuous type
options.F: The claim binds only if it is repeated in the specifications

questions.explanation: Express warranties can be disclaimed the same way they are created, but where warranty and disclaimer language conflict, the warranty language takes precedence. A conspicuous written disclaimer or the words as is, with all faults are ways to disclaim implied warranties, not to override a conflicting express claim. The UCC does not void both, favor the more specific clause, or require the claim to be restated in the specifications, since an affirmation of performance is itself an express warranty.

questions.question: Industry guidance, citing a business law text, explains what the term merchantable means under the implied warranty of merchantability. Which quality level does it give?

options.A: Goods of fair, average, medium quality
options.B: Highest commercially available quality
options.C: Quality matching the approved sample
options.D: Quality suited to the buyer's specific use
options.E: Goods free of any defect for the life of the product
options.F: Quality approved by the A/E during submittal review

questions.explanation: A business law text quoted in industry guidance defines merchantable as fair, average, medium quality, meaning goods that are reasonably suited to the general purpose they are sold for. Fitness for a buyer's specific use is the separate implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose, and conformance to a sample is an express warranty. The definition calls for neither the highest quality, freedom from every defect, nor A/E approval.

questions.question: Before starting the project manual, an A/E needs the owner's decisions on the construction contract and bidding procedures. Which document does industry guidance identify for obtaining this information?

options.A: AIA Document B101, Owner-Architect Agreement
options.B: AIA Document A701, Instructions to Bidders
options.C: AIA Document G612, Owner's Instructions to the Architect
options.D: AIA A201, General Conditions of the Contract for Construction
options.E: AIA Document A101, Owner-Contractor Agreement
options.F: EJCDC C-052, Owner's Instructions Concerning Bonds and Insurance

questions.explanation: The owner usually supplies the information on contract procedures, and AIA G612, Owner's Instructions to the Architect, has parts for the construction contract and for bidding procedures. A701, A101 and A201 are documents those decisions later feed into, B101 sets out the architect's services, and EJCDC C-052 records the owner's bonds and insurance decisions rather than its contract and bidding choices.

questions.question: A specifier preparing documents for a multiple-prime project with no construction manager looks for guidance. Under which delivery method or option are multiple-prime contracts normally discussed?

options.A: The construction manager as advisor/agent option
options.B: The negotiated option of the design-bid-build method
options.C: The construction manager at risk method
options.D: The design-build project delivery method
options.E: The integrated project delivery method
options.F: The competitive proposal option of design-bid-build

questions.explanation: Multiple-prime contracts can be used without construction management, but they are normally discussed under the construction manager as advisor/agent option, which suits projects with several prime contractors whose documents may be released at different times. The negotiated and competitive proposal options, CMAR, design-build and integrated project delivery are not where multiple-prime contracting is taken up.

questions.question: An A/E moving from competitive-bid work to a project delivered under a different method asks what will shape the documents. Which factor may decide both what kinds of documents are needed and how the work is specified?

options.A: The A/E's office master specification system
options.B: The procurement and contracting procedures used
options.C: The size and complexity of the drawing set
options.D: The permit process of the authority having jurisdiction
options.E: The construction cost estimate for each design phase
options.F: The number of consultants on the A/E's design team

questions.explanation: Procurement and contracting procedures may decide which documents are needed and how the work is specified, which is why the owner's input on contract procedures is gathered early. Office masters, drawing size, permitting, cost estimates and the size of the design team affect content and effort, but they are not what determines the type of documents or the specifying method.

questions.question: Which three options fall under the design-bid-build delivery method, and which one is treated as the baseline?

options.A: Competitive bid, competitive proposal, and negotiation; negotiation is the baseline
options.B: Competitive bid, qualifications-based selection, and negotiation; competitive bid is the baseline
options.C: Competitive bid, competitive proposal, and negotiation; competitive bid is the baseline
options.D: Competitive bid, qualifications-based selection, and negotiation; negotiation is the baseline
options.E: Competitive bid, competitive proposal, and fast-track; competitive bid is the baseline
options.F: Competitive proposal, negotiation, and CM at risk; competitive proposal is the baseline

questions.explanation: Design-bid-build has three options, competitive bid, competitive proposal and negotiation, and the competitive bid option is treated as the baseline, so discussion of variations centers on the other two. Qualifications-based selection is not one of the three, fast-track is a scheduling technique, CM at risk is a separate delivery method, and the negotiated option is a variation from the baseline rather than the baseline itself.

questions.question: A public owner uses the competitive proposal option of design-bid-build. What chiefly distinguishes it from the competitive bid option?

options.A: Proposers submit added documents used to evaluate the best-qualified contractor
options.B: The project manual is completed after negotiations begin during the early design phases
options.C: Pricing is based on outline specifications leading toward a guaranteed maximum price
options.D: The A/E shares project manual decisions with the owner and the selected contractor
options.E: The construction manager prepares the procurement documents for each package
options.F: Sealed prices are opened and the lowest responsible bidder wins the award

questions.explanation: The competitive proposal option resembles competitive bidding except that proposers submit added documents, which the owner uses to evaluate them and pick the best-qualified contractor; the final price may still be negotiated after selection. Completing the project manual after negotiations start, outline-specification pricing toward a GMP and shared decision-making mark the negotiated option, construction manager procurement belongs to CM methods, and low-bid award describes competitive bidding.

questions.question: An owner selects a contractor early in design under the negotiated option of design-bid-build. What are the negotiations frequently based on?

options.A: Schematic design drawings and a preliminary description leading to unit prices
options.B: Bidding documents and a complete project manual leading to a stipulated sum
options.C: Outline specifications and design development documents leading to a GMP
options.D: Construction documents and addenda leading to cost-plus-fee without a maximum
options.E: A design-builder's proposal and the owner's program leading to a lump sum
options.F: Final construction documents and a schedule of values leading to a stipulated sum

questions.explanation: Under the negotiated option, negotiations often rest on outline specifications and design development documents and lead to a cost-of-the-work agreement with a guaranteed maximum price. The project manual is completed afterward to finish the design, get permits and obtain actual prices, so final construction documents, a complete project manual or addenda are not the basis, and unit prices, stipulated or lump sums and an open-ended fee are not the usual outcome.

questions.question: On a design-bid-build project using the negotiated option, the A/E may not make every decision that normally falls to it alone. With whom are those decisions often shared?

options.A: The owner and the construction manager
options.B: The owner and the contractor
options.C: The contractor and its major subcontractors
options.D: The owner and its cost consultant
options.E: The owner and the authority having jurisdiction
options.F: The contractor and the product manufacturers

questions.explanation: Under the negotiated option, other team members, especially the owner and the contractor, often share decisions the A/E would usually make alone. Sharing them with the owner and a construction manager is the parallel point for CMAR projects, and subcontractors, cost consultants, manufacturers and the AHJ are not the parties named for the negotiated option.

questions.question: A design-bid-build project is switched from the competitive bid option to the negotiated option. Which portion of the project manual is expected to change the most?

options.A: Division 01
options.B: Division 00
options.C: Divisions 02 through 49
options.D: PART 1 of each product section
options.E: PART 2 of each product section
options.F: The Division 01 warranty and closeout sections

questions.explanation: Division 00 changes the most when a design-bid-build project moves to the competitive proposal or negotiated option, because bidding forms are replaced with proposal forms or dropped. Division 01 needs coordination of negotiated procedures such as payments, submittals, warranties and closeout, but product sections in Divisions 02 through 49, including their PART 1 and PART 2 articles, are not significantly different.

questions.question: An owner intends to negotiate a design-bid-build contract directly with one contractor it trusts. The specifier is adapting the office's competitive-bid Division 00 master. What does industry guidance indicate about the procurement portion?

options.A: Each bid form should be replaced with a proposal form
options.B: The full set of bidding documents should be retained
options.C: Its requirements should be relocated into Division 01
options.D: Many of its forms and documents will be unnecessary
options.E: It should be prepared by a construction manager
options.F: It should be replaced by a request for qualifications

questions.explanation: Under the negotiated option, much of the procurement requirements' usual content is unnecessary, because the price is reached by negotiation with one contractor rather than through competition. Swapping bid forms for equivalent proposal forms, or adding a request for qualifications, fits the competitive proposal option; a construction manager prepares procurement documents under CMAR, and nothing calls for keeping the full bid package or moving it into Division 01.

questions.question: A specifier preparing Division 00 for a design-bid-build project procured by competitive proposal deletes most procurement documents, reasoning that no bids will be received. What is wrong with this approach?

options.A: The set should resemble the bid documents, with proposal forms replacing bid forms
options.B: Nothing; most procurement documents are unnecessary under the competitive proposal option
options.C: The deleted documents belong in Division 01 rather than being removed from the manual
options.D: Only the bid form should have been removed; other bidding documents stay as written
options.E: The documents should be kept, but moved into the owner-contractor agreement
options.F: The full set should be replaced by a single request for qualifications

questions.explanation: Under the competitive proposal option, Division 00 looks much like the competitive bid version, with equivalent proposal forms and documents in place of the bidding forms. Dropping most procurement documents is the pattern for the negotiated option, a request for qualifications is only one of the optional proposal titles, and nothing supports moving the documents into Division 01 or the agreement, or keeping the bid documents unchanged.

questions.question: For a design-bid-build project procured under the competitive proposal option, which group of optional MasterFormat titles does industry guidance identify as applicable to that process?

options.A: Advertisement for Bids, Instructions to Bidders, and Bid Security Form
options.B: Request for Proposal, Instructions to Bidders, and Bid Form
options.C: Request for Proposal, Request for Qualifications, and Instructions to Proposers
options.D: Request for Proposal, Instructions to Proposers, and Notice of Award
options.E: Request for Qualifications, Instructions to Bidders, and Bid Form
options.F: Request for Proposal, Request for Qualifications, and Notice to Proceed

questions.explanation: MasterFormat includes optional titles suited to the competitive proposal process: Request for Proposal, Request for Qualifications and Instructions to Proposers. The other sets mix in bid-oriented titles such as Advertisement for Bids, Instructions to Bidders, Bid Form and Bid Security Form, or contracting forms such as Notice of Award and Notice to Proceed, which are not among the proposal-process titles.

questions.question: An owner questions why the project manual for a competitive proposal procurement should include Instructions to Proposers when no formal bid opening will occur. Which benefit does industry guidance cite for including such documents?

options.A: They set procedures for clarifications, addenda, and a structured proposal form
options.B: They set the contract sum, retainage, and the payment application procedures
options.C: They stand in for the conditions of the contract during the negotiation period
options.D: They remove the need to issue any addenda during the proposal period
options.E: They require the award to go to the lowest-priced proposal
options.F: They set the warranty and closeout procedures for the work

questions.explanation: Instructions to Proposers and similar documents improve the proposal process by setting procedures for clarifications and addenda and by providing a structured proposal form. The contract sum and retainage are agreement matters, warranty and closeout procedures are Division 01 matters, the instructions do not stand in for the conditions of the contract, they make addenda orderly rather than unnecessary, and proposers are evaluated for the best-qualified contractor, not on price alone.

questions.question: While drafting Instructions to Proposers for a competitive proposal project, a specifier considers requiring each proposer to affirm that it visited the site and accounted for local conditions. What does industry guidance indicate?

options.A: Such a requirement is inappropriate, since site affirmations apply only to competitive bids
options.B: Such a requirement belongs only in the owner-contractor agreement after negotiations end
options.C: Such a requirement is appropriate, since it can mirror a traditional bid requirement
options.D: Such a requirement belongs in the Division 01 summary of work rather than in procurement
options.E: Such a requirement is unnecessary, since proposers are already prequalified
options.F: Such a requirement is valid only when a mandatory prebid meeting is held

questions.explanation: Procurement requirements for the proposal process can resemble those of a traditional bid, and having the proposer affirm that it visited the site and accounted for local conditions is the usual example. The affirmation is therefore neither limited to competitive bids nor unnecessary for proposers, it is a procurement requirement rather than an agreement or Division 01 provision, and nothing makes it depend on a mandatory prebid meeting.

questions.question: On a design-bid-build project using the negotiated option, the owner negotiates the contract sum directly with the contractor and the A/E does not take part. What should the A/E do regarding the owner-contractor agreement form?

options.A: Prepare the agreement form and insert the negotiated amount once the owner reports it
options.B: Exclude the agreement from review, since the A/E was not a party to the negotiations
options.C: Wait until after award and then revise the conditions of the contract to match it
options.D: Request a copy to confirm it does not conflict with the conditions or Division 01
options.E: Draft supplementary conditions that override the agreement's terms
options.F: Ask the contractor to certify that the agreement matches Division 01

questions.explanation: Even when the A/E takes no part in negotiating the agreement, it should ask for a copy of the agreement form to check for conflicts with the conditions of the contract and Division 01. Preparing the form or inserting the amount is not the A/E's task, ignoring the agreement or waiting until after award leaves conflicts undetected, and neither a contractor's certification nor overriding supplementary conditions replaces the A/E's own review.

questions.question: Under the negotiated option, the negotiating contractor prepares the contracting forms, bonds, and certificates instead of the A/E. When the A/E reviews these forms, what does industry guidance identify as the focus of that review?

options.A: Confirming the forms are standard AIA or EJCDC documents
options.B: Confirming the forms add no A/E duties beyond the A/E agreement
options.C: Confirming the forms follow the A/E's office master format
options.D: Confirming the named surety is acceptable to the owner's insurer
options.E: Confirming the bonds name the A/E as an obligee
options.F: Confirming the forms repeat the insurance limits of the general conditions

questions.explanation: When the negotiating contractor prepares the contracting forms, bonds and certificates, the A/E reviews them to make sure they give it no responsibilities beyond its own agreement, and tells the owner if the proposed agreement omits required responses to the A/E's duties. The forms need not be AIA or EJCDC documents or follow the office format, and surety acceptability, obligees and insurance limits are not the focus of the A/E's review.

questions.question: Reviewing a proposed owner-contractor agreement for a negotiated project, the A/E finds that it says nothing about the contractor's required responses to the A/E's contract administration responsibilities. What is the A/E's best course of action?

options.A: Revise the agreement directly to add the missing obligations
options.B: Take no action, since the A/E agreement alone defines those duties
options.C: Notify the owner that the agreement leaves out those obligations
options.D: Ask the contractor directly to add the obligations to the agreement
options.E: Decline to provide contract administration services for the project
options.F: Delete the A/E's administration duties from the general conditions

questions.explanation: The A/E is not a party to the owner-contractor agreement, so when a proposed agreement leaves out the contractor's required responses to the A/E's duties, the A/E should tell the owner. Editing the agreement or negotiating with the contractor goes around the owner, while taking no action, declining administration services or deleting the A/E's duties from the general conditions leaves the A/E's role unsupported instead of fixing the gap.

questions.question: During negotiations on a design-bid-build project, the owner and contractor modify several provisions of the general conditions. What does industry guidance direct the A/E to do?

options.A: Review the changes to see whether Division 01 needs revision
options.B: Remove the conditions of the contract from the project manual as superseded
options.C: Leave Division 01 unchanged, since negotiated changes do not affect it
options.D: Rewrite Part 1 of each Divisions 02-49 section to restate the new provisions
options.E: Have the contractor revise Division 01 to suit the new provisions
options.F: Restate the changed provisions in the instructions to bidders

questions.explanation: The conditions of the contract are the basis for Division 01, so when negotiation changes those provisions the A/E reviews the changes to see whether Division 01 must be revised. The conditions stay in the project manual to establish that basis, negotiated changes can affect Division 01, restating them in every section only duplicates them, and the instructions to bidders are procurement documents, not part of the contract.

questions.question: On a negotiated design-bid-build project, the contractor submits conditions of the contract that it drafted itself. Whose review should those conditions receive?

options.A: The contractor's legal counsel
options.B: The owner's legal counsel
options.C: The owner's insurance consultant
options.D: The contractor's bonding surety
options.E: The authority having jurisdiction
options.F: The contractor's insurance agent

questions.explanation: When a negotiating contractor proposes conditions of the contract it wrote itself, the owner's legal counsel should review them, because those terms set the owner's rights and risks. The contractor's counsel or insurance agent works for the party that drafted the document, and an insurance consultant, a surety or the authority having jurisdiction does not review contract terms on the owner's behalf.

questions.question: On a negotiated project, the owner-contractor agreement already sets out the payment application process and retainage. The owner's draft supplementary conditions restate the same retainage terms. What does industry guidance recommend?

options.A: Keep the terms in both documents to reinforce them for the contractor
options.B: Move the terms into the conditions and delete them from the agreement
options.C: Move the terms to Division 01 and delete them from the other two documents
options.D: Keep the terms in the agreement and do not repeat them in the conditions
options.E: Move the terms to the bid form and delete them from the other documents
options.F: Keep the terms in the conditions and restate them again in Division 01

questions.explanation: When the owner-contractor agreement already sets out payment applications and retainage, those terms belong there and are not restated in the conditions of the contract; one location avoids two versions that can drift into conflict. Keeping them in both documents, or adding them to Division 01 as well, invites conflict, and nothing calls for stripping them from the agreement or moving them to Division 01 or a procurement form.

questions.question: On a negotiated project, the owner declines to share the owner-contractor agreement with the A/E, citing confidentiality. How does industry guidance say the conditions of the contract for the project manual should then be handled?

options.A: The A/E should publish unmodified standard AIA conditions as a placeholder
options.B: The A/E should leave the conditions of the contract out of the project manual
options.C: The contractor's counsel should expand Division 01 to replace the conditions
options.D: The owner and contractor should prepare suitable conditions for publication
options.E: The A/E should draft the conditions on its own, without the agreement
options.F: The contractor alone should prepare conditions for publication

questions.explanation: When the A/E cannot see the owner-contractor agreement, the owner and contractor, who know what they agreed, should prepare suitable conditions of the contract for the project manual. Unmodified standard conditions or conditions the A/E drafts blind risk conflicting with an agreement it has not seen, the contractor alone does not speak for the owner, leaving the conditions out removes the basis for Division 01, and Division 01 cannot replace them.

questions.question: On a negotiated design-bid-build project, the specifier is coordinating Division 01 with the conditions of the contract. Which group of procedures does industry guidance name as possibly needing special coordination because they may be negotiated?

options.A: Progress schedules, substitutions, and warranties
options.B: Temporary facilities, field engineering, and cutting
options.C: Quality control, regulatory requirements, and mockups
options.D: Selective demolition, alterations, and protection
options.E: Site use, security, and personnel identification
options.F: Testing laboratory services, allowances, and alternates

questions.explanation: On a negotiated project, the procedures the owner and contractor may bargain over (payments, progress schedules, submittals, substitutions, warranties and closeout) are the ones that can need special coordination between Division 01 and the conditions of the contract. Site use, security and personnel identification are concerns for owner-build work at existing facilities, and temporary facilities, testing services, allowances, quality control or demolition are not named for this coordination.

questions.question: During negotiations on a design-bid-build project, the owner and contractor agree on a specific roofing system and price it accordingly. How does industry guidance suggest the specifier write the roofing section?

options.A: As a performance specification so that competing systems can still be offered
options.B: As a descriptive specification with more detail than for a bid project
options.C: As a proprietary specification, with some level of detail eliminated
options.D: As a reference to the negotiated price list in the owner-contractor agreement
options.E: As a reference standard specification citing only the roofing standard
options.F: As an or-equal specification naming the system only as a basis of design

questions.explanation: When negotiation and pricing have already fixed a specific product, the section can be written as proprietary, which lets some descriptive detail drop out. Performance, reference standard or or-equal approaches would reopen choices the negotiation already settled, negotiated specifications are otherwise like bid specifications rather than more detailed, and a price list in the agreement does not replace the specification section.

questions.question: An A/E is scoping its services for a construction manager at risk (CMAR) project. Which task belongs to the construction manager rather than the A/E?

options.A: Preparing the Division 01 sections that all packages reference
options.B: Preparing the procurement documents for each subcontract
options.C: Preparing the Divisions 02 through 49 sections for each package
options.D: Preparing the drawings that are issued with each work package
options.E: Preparing the design development drawings and outline specifications
options.F: Organizing section numbers so the packages can later be conformed

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that with CMAR the A/E does not prepare procurement documents; the construction manager prepares them for each subcontract it intends to issue. Industry guidance does not shift Division 01, the Divisions 02 through 49 sections, or the package drawings to the construction manager; it directs the A/E to prepare specifications that secure accurate pricing and to work with the CM on package drawings and specifications.

questions.question: A CMAR job will use fast-track scheduling. Industry guidance says the construction manager may then furnish procurement documents for each work package issued, comparable to the work packages of which method?

options.A: Design-build with bridging documents
options.B: Integrated project delivery (IPD)
options.C: Multiple-prime with CM as advisor
options.D: Negotiated design-bid-build
options.E: Owner-build with multiple contracts
options.F: Design-bid-build, competitive bid option

questions.explanation: When a CMAR construction manager fast-tracks the job, it may issue procurement documents with each work package, much like the staggered work packages of integrated project delivery; IPD in turn is described as working like fast-track CMAR. Design-build, owner-build, multiple-prime with a CM as advisor and the design-bid-build options are not the comparison drawn.

questions.question: An owner wants a contractor-side manager's input on cost and constructability while drawings are still being developed. How does industry guidance characterize CMAR in relation to that goal?

options.A: It does not fit; CMAR expertise begins only after design is complete
options.B: It does not fit; CMAR expertise is confined to the construction phase
options.C: It fits only when fast-track scheduling divides design into packages
options.D: It fits; CMAR provides professional management expertise during design
options.E: It fits only if the CM also holds the design contract
options.F: It does not fit; CMAR input is limited to pricing bid packages

questions.explanation: CMAR brings the construction manager onto the team early to provide professional management expertise during design, including input on budget, cost estimates, schedule and constructability, which is what this owner wants. That expertise is not limited to construction, to pricing bid packages or to the period after design, does not depend on fast-tracking, and does not require the CM to hold the design contract, which would make it design-build.

questions.question: A specifier accustomed to design-bid-build starts a CMAR project. Regarding items normally within the A/E's responsibility in preparing the project manual, what should the specifier expect?

options.A: Decisions will often be shared with the owner and construction manager
options.B: The A/E will remain the sole decision-maker on all such items
options.C: The construction manager will become the sole decision-maker on them
options.D: The owner's attorney will make those decisions for the project manual
options.E: The owner will become the sole decision-maker on them
options.F: The subcontractors will decide them during bidding

questions.explanation: Under CMAR, the A/E is not always the only party deciding matters it would control in a design-bid-build project manual; the owner and construction manager often share those decisions. The guidance describes shared decisions, not continued sole control by the A/E and not a full handover to the construction manager, the owner, its attorney or the subcontractors.

questions.question: In Division 00 for a CMAR project, which item is given as an example of a procurement form rather than a contract form or an owner-provided document?

options.A: Substitution request form
options.B: RFI form
options.C: Wage rates
options.D: Geotechnical data
options.E: Hazardous materials survey
options.F: Subcontract agreement form

questions.explanation: In Division 00 for a CMAR project, wage rates are the example of a procurement form, while the substitution request and RFI forms are contract forms and a subcontract agreement is a contracting form the CM usually supplies. Geotechnical data and existing hazardous material information are owner-provided documents.

questions.question: On a CMAR project, the construction manager adds its own subcontractor bid forms and subcontract documents to Division 00 of the project manual. What does industry guidance say should accompany that addition?

options.A: The table of contents should list each added item
options.B: The A/E should reformat each added item to its office standard
options.C: The added items should be bound as a separate volume
options.D: The owner should execute each added item before issue
options.E: The added items should be moved into Division 01
options.F: The A/E should certify each added item for accuracy

questions.explanation: The construction manager may supplement Division 00 with its own forms and documents for subcontractors, and when they are included the table of contents should list them so readers know they are there. Nothing calls for the A/E to reformat or certify them, for binding them separately or moving them to Division 01, or for the owner to execute them before issue.

questions.question: An A/E is estimating its specification effort for Division 00 on a CMAR project. Which expectation is consistent with industry guidance?

options.A: Heavy effort: the A/E prepares bid forms and instructions for every subcontract
options.B: Moderate effort: the A/E drafts the CM's standard subcontract agreement forms
options.C: Light effort: owner-provided data and a few forms, possibly added to by the CM
options.D: No effort: Division 00 is omitted entirely from CMAR project manuals
options.E: Heavy effort: the A/E rewrites the general conditions for each package
options.F: Moderate effort: the A/E prepares the geotechnical and hazmat reports

questions.explanation: The A/E expects little Division 00 effort on a CMAR project: mainly owner-provided documents such as geotechnical and hazardous material data, a few procurement and contract forms, and whatever the CM adds. The CM prepares subcontract procurement documents and its standard agreement forms, the owner furnishes the site data, the general conditions are already established, and Division 00 is not omitted.

questions.question: On a CMAR project, the owner decides to prepare the procurement requirements for an early site-utilities package itself instead of the construction manager. How does this affect the A/E's coordination?

options.A: The A/E now coordinates that package with the owner only, not with the CM
options.B: The A/E is relieved of coordinating because the CM did not prepare them
options.C: The A/E must now prepare procurement requirements for the other packages
options.D: The A/E still works with the CM on the drawings and specifications
options.E: The A/E must stop work on that package until the CM takes it back
options.F: The A/E coordinates that package directly with the bidding subcontractors

questions.explanation: The A/E's coordination with the construction manager does not depend on who writes the procurement requirements: the A/E and CM work together on the drawings and specifications each package needs. A different preparer does not redirect that coordination to the owner or the bidders, end or pause it, or make the A/E responsible for procurement requirements on the other packages.

questions.question: What is the stated purpose of the A/E working with the construction manager on the drawings and specifications to be included in CMAR work packages?

options.A: To ensure each package carries its own copy of Division 01
options.B: To ensure each package contains the required information
options.C: To ensure each package uses the CM's standard subcontract forms
options.D: To ensure each package is priced within the owner's budget
options.E: To ensure each package is issued on the fast-track schedule
options.F: To ensure each package is reviewed by the owner's legal counsel

questions.explanation: The A/E works with the construction manager on the drawings and specifications so that each work package contains the information it needs. Division 01 may be issued once as a stand-alone package rather than in every package, the CM's subcontract forms are a separate Division 00 matter, and budget control, schedule and legal review are not the stated purpose.

questions.question: Midway through design, a CMAR team decides to issue one complete set of construction documents rather than a series of work packages. How does industry guidance treat the A/E's collaboration with the construction manager on drawings and specifications?

options.A: It ends, because it is required only when work packages are issued
options.B: It shifts to the owner, who coordinates single-set documents with the CM
options.C: It still applies, whether the work is issued as one set or as packages
options.D: It is replaced by a Division 01 section that defines single-set content
options.E: It passes to the CM alone, who then edits the single set
options.F: It is limited to Division 00, since the set needs no packaging

questions.explanation: The A/E and construction manager collaborate on the drawings and specifications for a CMAR project whether the documents are issued as one complete set or as a series of work packages. That collaboration is not limited to packaged work, does not pass to the owner or to the CM alone, does not shrink to Division 00, and is not replaced by a Division 01 section.

questions.question: Who usually prepares the agreement forms for subcontracts on a CMAR project, and what are they typically based on?

options.A: The A/E, adapting the standard owner-contractor agreement form
options.B: The construction manager, using its standard subcontract forms
options.C: The owner's attorney, using the owner's in-house legal forms
options.D: The construction manager, matching an owner-CM advisor agreement
options.E: Each subcontractor, using its own proposal form
options.F: The owner, adapting its owner-CM agreement form

questions.explanation: On CMAR projects the construction manager usually prepares the subcontract agreement forms, typically its own standard subcontract forms, because it holds the subcontracts. Compatibility with an owner-CM agreement form is the point for the CM as advisor/agent option, and the A/E, the owner, the owner's attorney and the subcontractors are not the usual preparers here.

questions.question: A specifier preparing the project manual for a CMAR project notes that the general conditions were settled in the owner-CM contract long before. Should a copy of the conditions of the contract be included?

options.A: No, because they were established before the project manual was prepared
options.B: No, because the CM's subcontract forms replace the general conditions
options.C: Yes, but only as a summary restated within Division 01 requirements
options.D: Yes, because subcontractors are bound to the same provisions as the CM
options.E: No, because subcontractors are not bound by those provisions
options.F: Yes, but only after the owner's attorney rewrites them

questions.explanation: For CMAR the general conditions are already in place when the project manual is prepared, but a copy should still be included because subcontractors are bound by the same provisions as the construction manager. Their earlier establishment is not a reason to omit them, the CM's subcontract forms do not replace them, and neither a Division 01 summary nor a rewrite by the owner's attorney is called for.

questions.question: A CMAR project will be issued in six work packages. Which approach to Division 01 does industry guidance describe for multiple work package projects?

options.A: Issue it once as a stand-alone package referenced by each later package
options.B: Publish the complete Division 01 again with every work package issued
options.C: Write a separate Division 01 tailored to the scope of each package
options.D: Omit Division 01 and rely on the CM's subcontract general conditions
options.E: Issue it only with the last work package of the project
options.F: Place its requirements in the first package's Division 00

questions.explanation: For projects with multiple work packages, Division 01 may be issued as a stand-alone package that each later package references, so it need not be published again with every package. Writing a different Division 01 for each package conflicts with every package being subject to the same Division 01 requirements, issuing it last leaves earlier packages without it, and Division 00 is not where general requirements go.

questions.question: Division 01 for a multi-package CMAR project was issued as a stand-alone package. Work package 4 now needs a revision to a Division 01 section. How does industry guidance indicate the change can be issued?

options.A: By reissuing every earlier work package with the revision
options.B: Only in the conformed documents after all packages are out
options.C: Through a separate Division 01 revision package after award
options.D: Along with work package 4 when that package is released
options.E: Only as an amendment to the owner-CM agreement
options.F: By a CM field directive to the affected subcontractors

questions.explanation: When a later work package needs a revision to the stand-alone Division 01, the change can be issued with that work package. Reissuing every earlier package, waiting for the conformed documents, or using a separate post-award package, an agreement amendment or a field directive is not the method described.

questions.question: The CM on a CMAR project suggests that the early site work package follow lighter general requirements than the later building packages. How does this compare with industry guidance?

options.A: It aligns; each work package may carry its own Division 01 requirements
options.B: It conflicts; every package is subject to the same Division 01 requirements
options.C: It aligns, provided the owner approves the reduced requirements in writing
options.D: It conflicts; site packages must follow the conditions of the contract alone
options.E: It aligns, if the lighter requirements are listed in Division 00
options.F: It aligns; site packages fall outside Division 01 entirely

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says CMAR specifications are subject to the same Division 01 requirements whether issued as one set or as multiple work packages, so lighter general requirements for one package conflict with that guidance. Industry guidance lets a needed Division 01 revision travel with a later package, but that revises the common Division 01 rather than creating package-specific requirements; owner approval is not an exception industry guidance offers, and site packages are not limited to the conditions of the contract.

questions.question: On a CMAR project, the A/E is deciding how to approach the Divisions 02 through 49 sections. Which objective does industry guidance state the A/E's specifications should achieve?

options.A: Minimizing document length so packages can be released sooner
options.B: Transferring design responsibility to the trade subcontractors
options.C: Securing accurate pricing for each set or package
options.D: Limiting each work package to sections not previously issued
options.E: Shifting product selection to the construction manager
options.F: Matching the detail of the design development outline

questions.explanation: On a CMAR project the A/E prepares specifications that secure accurate pricing, whether the work goes out as one complete set or in several packages. The stated aim is not shortening documents, handing design responsibility or product selection to others, or holding to outline-level detail, and later packages may in fact reuse sections that were issued earlier.

questions.question: Under CMAR delivery, which parties or factors does industry guidance say may influence the level of detail in the A/E's specifications?

options.A: The construction manager or the owner's project requirements
options.B: The trade subcontractors or the authority having jurisdiction
options.C: The bonding surety or the owner's insurance carrier
options.D: The low bidders' pricing or the product manufacturers
options.E: The testing agency or the commissioning authority
options.F: The design-builder or the owner's project description

questions.explanation: On a CMAR project, either the construction manager or the owner's project requirements may shape how detailed the A/E's specifications are. The design-builder and the owner's project description are the influences named for design-build, and subcontractors, building officials, sureties, insurers, testing agencies, bidders' prices and manufacturers are not the parties named.

questions.question: A later CMAR work package needs the same cast-in-place concrete section that was issued with the foundation package. What does industry guidance indicate?

options.A: The section may not appear in any package after the one that first issued it
options.B: The section may be reused only after it is renumbered for the later package
options.C: The same section may be reused in the later package, under version control
options.D: The section may be reused only after the earlier package is withdrawn
options.E: The section may be reused only if the CM approves a substitution
options.F: The section must be rewritten from scratch for the later package

questions.explanation: Some work packages may use the same sections as packages issued earlier, with version control used to keep track of each issue. Reuse is not prohibited, and nothing requires the section to be renumbered, rewritten, approved as a substitution, or the earlier package to be withdrawn.

questions.question: After all work packages for a CMAR project are issued, who might require that they be combined into one project manual, and for what reason?

options.A: The owner or construction manager, for convenience
options.B: The authority having jurisdiction, for permit records
options.C: The A/E, to satisfy its professional liability insurer
options.D: The contractor's surety, to define the bonded work
options.E: The owner's lender, to document the financed work
options.F: The trade subcontractors, to coordinate their scopes

questions.explanation: After every work package has gone out, the owner or the construction manager may ask for them to be combined into one project manual for convenience. Permit records, the A/E's insurer, the surety, a lender or the subcontractors are not the parties or reasons identified, although the A/E should plan for a possible combination from the start.

questions.question: When should the A/E on a multi-package CMAR project become aware that the packages may later be combined into a single project manual?

options.A: When the final work package is about to be issued
options.B: At the outset, before the first package is prepared
options.C: When the owner formally requests a combined manual
options.D: At substantial completion, as record documents begin
options.E: After bids on the first package have been received
options.F: When the conformed set is being compiled for the owner

questions.explanation: The A/E should be aware from the beginning that all work packages may later be combined, so sections and drawings can be organized for it. Learning of it after the first bids, when the last package goes out, when the owner asks, while the conformed set is compiled or at substantial completion is too late to number and title sections consistently.

questions.question: Anticipating that the owner may later want all CMAR work packages merged into one project manual and drawing set, what should the A/E do from the start?

options.A: Issue each package with its own complete Division 01 so that packages can stand alone
options.B: Number each package's sections independently, restarting in every package
options.C: Defer assigning any section numbers until every package has been issued and priced
options.D: Organize similar sections by suitable numbers and titles; number drawings logically
options.E: Number sections by the CM's subcontract codes instead of MasterFormat numbers
options.F: Title every section after its work package rather than after its content

questions.explanation: Knowing combination may be required, the A/E organizes similar specification sections with appropriate numbers and titles and gives the drawings a logical numbering system from the beginning. A full Division 01 in every package is unnecessary, and restarting numbers per package, deferring numbering, using subcontract codes or titling sections by package all work against a clean merge.

questions.question: An owner retains a construction manager who will not perform work as a contractor. The owner's agreement authorizes the CM to make decisions on the owner's behalf instead of only offering recommendations. Which designation fits this arrangement?

options.A: Construction manager as advisor (CMa)
options.B: Construction manager at risk (CMAR)
options.C: Construction manager as agent
options.D: Construction manager as constructor
options.E: General contractor with preconstruction services
options.F: Design-builder

questions.explanation: The two non-contractor CM roles differ in authority: the CM as agent is delegated authority to make binding decisions for the owner, while the CM as advisor only advises the owner. CMAR, CM as constructor, a general contractor and a design-builder all put the firm in the contractor role, which this owner excluded.

questions.question: An owner asks whether the construction manager as advisor/agent option is tied to a particular project delivery method and what kind of project it fits best. Which response matches industry guidance?

options.A: It applies with any delivery method and is best suited to single-prime projects
options.B: It applies only with design-bid-build and is best suited to multiple-prime projects
options.C: It applies with any delivery method and is best suited to multiple-prime projects
options.D: It applies only with design-bid-build and is best suited to single-prime projects
options.E: It applies only with CMAR and is best suited to multiple-prime projects
options.F: It applies only with design-build and is best suited to single-prime projects

questions.explanation: CM as advisor/agent provides management services to the owner and can be used with any project delivery method, and it is particularly well suited to projects with multiple prime contractors. Answers that tie it to one delivery method (design-bid-build, CMAR or design-build) or name single-prime projects as its best fit contradict that guidance.

questions.question: An owner using a construction manager as advisor elects fast-track scheduling with a single-prime contract and expects the A/E's document effort to shrink because the overall schedule will be shorter. What does industry guidance indicate is likely?

options.A: The A/E's document preparation time will likely decrease in step with the reduced overall schedule
options.B: The A/E's document preparation time is unaffected because fast-track applies only to multiple-prime work
options.C: The A/E's document preparation time will likely increase while the overall schedule is reduced
options.D: The A/E's document preparation time will likely decrease because the CM produces the document packages
options.E: The A/E's document preparation time will likely decrease because a single prime contract needs no packages
options.F: The A/E's document preparation time is unaffected because the CM as advisor absorbs the added work

questions.explanation: With fast-track scheduling, under either a single-prime or a multiple-prime contract, the A/E should expect to spend more time preparing documents even though the overall schedule gets shorter, because the documentation is staggered into separate bid or proposal packages. The CM as advisor does not absorb that work: the A/E usually produces the document packages the CM identifies.

questions.question: An A/E has two projects that both use a construction manager as advisor/agent: Project 1 is a single-prime competitive bid project, and Project 2 is divided into multiple prime contracts. Where should the A/E expect differences in project manual preparation?

options.A: Mainly on Project 1, since the CM option there replaces the single prime contractor
options.B: Equally on both projects, since CM involvement alters the manual whether contracts are single or multiple
options.C: On neither project, since the CM handles procurement outside the project manual
options.D: Mainly on Project 2, since the CM option there implements multiple-prime contracts
options.E: Mainly on Project 1, since single-prime work always requires work packages
options.F: On neither project, since the CM as advisor uses the A/E's standard manual unchanged

questions.explanation: Project manual differences under the CM as advisor/agent option come from using it to carry out a multiple-prime project. For a single-prime project the manual may differ little or not at all from a typical bid or proposal project, so CM involvement alone does not drive the change, and the multiple-prime project does need adjusted documents.

questions.question: On a multiple-prime project using a construction manager as advisor/agent, the specifier assumes the A/E will have the final word on every item that is normally its responsibility. What does industry guidance indicate?

options.A: Those decisions are often shared with team members such as the owner and the CM
options.B: Those decisions stay with the A/E, since the CM's role is limited to advising the owner
options.C: Those decisions shift to the CM, since it acts as the owner's agent on the project
options.D: Those decisions wait until the prime contractors' bids reveal the cost impacts
options.E: Those decisions pass to the prime contractors, who carry the cost risk
options.F: Those decisions move to the owner's attorney for final approval

questions.explanation: As with other delivery methods, the A/E is not necessarily the only decision-maker under this option; the owner and CM commonly share in decisions the A/E would normally make. Sharing is not a transfer to the CM, the prime contractors or the owner's attorney, the A/E does not keep sole control, and the decisions are not deferred until bids are in.

questions.question: For a single-prime project that uses the construction manager as advisor/agent option, the project manual may differ little or not at all from which baseline?

options.A: A typical construction manager at risk project
options.B: A typical negotiated-contract project
options.C: A typical integrated project delivery project
options.D: A typical competitive bid or proposal project
options.E: A typical design-build project
options.F: A typical multiple-prime project

questions.explanation: For a single-prime project, the CM as advisor/agent option may leave the project manual little or no different from that of a typical competitive bid or proposal project; the differences arise when the option is used for multiple-prime contracts. The negotiated option, CMAR, IPD and design-build each bring their own project manual differences, so none of them is the baseline.

questions.question: An owner will hire a firm to manage a multiple-prime project as the owner's advisor or agent, without the firm acting as a contractor. Besides the AIA, EJCDC, and the ConsensusDocs Coalition, which organization does industry guidance name as a publisher of specialized standard contract documents for this option?

options.A: Design-Build Institute of America (DBIA)
options.B: Project Management Institute (PMI)
options.C: National Institute of Building Sciences (NIBS)
options.D: Construction Management Association of America (CMAA)
options.E: International Code Council (ICC)
options.F: ASTM International (ASTM)

questions.explanation: Specialized standard contract documents for the CM as advisor/agent option come from the AIA, EJCDC, ConsensusDocs and the Construction Management Association of America (CMAA). DBIA's documents address design-build, PMI publishes general project management standards, NIBS is known for building science resources and design guides, the ICC publishes model building codes, and ASTM publishes material and testing standards rather than contract forms.

questions.question: For a multiple-prime project managed by a construction manager as advisor/agent, what does each bid/proposal package usually contain in Division 00?

options.A: Procurement requirements with a form fitted to the package's scope, with the conditions of the contract issued after all packages are awarded
options.B: Procurement requirements with a form fitted to the package's scope, plus contracting requirements including the conditions of the contract
options.C: Contracting requirements only, with a single bid form covering the entire project issued with the first package
options.D: A bid form covering the entire project, plus the construction manager's standard subcontract forms as the agreement
options.E: Procurement requirements with a form fitted to the package's scope, plus a Division 01 summary in place of the conditions of the contract
options.F: Procurement requirements only, with the agreement and conditions of the contract kept in the owner-CM agreement

questions.explanation: Each multiple-prime package carries both procurement requirements, with a bid or proposal form matched to that package's scope, and contracting requirements that include the conditions of the contract, issued identically with every package. Deferring the conditions, using one project-wide bid form, relying on the CM's subcontract forms or the owner-CM agreement, or substituting a Division 01 summary all depart from that.

questions.question: A specifier proposes reusing the firm's standard design-bid-build Division 00 documents without change on a multiple-prime project where the owner has engaged a construction manager as agent. What is the best course of action?

options.A: Modify the procurement and contracting requirements to conform to this management option
options.B: Reuse them unchanged, since obtaining separate prime bids differs little from design-bid-build
options.C: Replace the agreement and conditions with the construction manager's standard subcontract forms
options.D: Keep them, but issue one bid form covering the combined scope of all the prime contracts
options.E: Reuse them unchanged, but have the CM add its own subcontract bid forms
options.F: Replace Division 00 with a Section 01 12 00 summary of all the contracts

questions.explanation: The procurement and contracting requirements must be modified to suit the CM as advisor/agent option, and specialized standard documents exist for it. Obtaining separate prime bids resembles design-bid-build, but the documents still need adjustment. CM subcontract forms are the CMAR approach, each prime package needs a bid form for its own scope, and Section 01 12 00 summarizes the contracts without replacing Division 00.

questions.question: A construction manager as agent wants to start procuring the early prime contracts while design of later work is still underway and also wants to hold down reproduction costs. Which issuing approach does industry guidance associate with those advantages?

options.A: Issue full sets of procurement documents with every package
options.B: Issue full sets after design completion with scopes in Section 01 12 00
options.C: Issue partial documents describing only the package being procured
options.D: Issue the drawings in full sets and the specifications only in part
options.E: Issue one combined package for all primes after design is complete
options.F: Issue full sets, but only to prequalified prime bidders

questions.explanation: Partial packages that describe only the work being procured let bidding start while design continues and usually cost less to reproduce, at the price of bidders not seeing all related documents. Full sets, whether to every bidder or only prequalified ones, and a single combined package all require a completed design, which defeats the CM's goal.

questions.question: A construction manager decides to issue full sets of procurement documents with every bid package on a multiple-prime project. Which pairing of advantage and disadvantage does industry guidance give for this approach?

options.A: Bidders can review all requirements affecting their price; the design must be complete
options.B: Packages can be issued while design continues; bidders may not see all related documents
options.C: Reproduction costs are usually lower; the design must be complete
options.D: Bidders can review all requirements affecting their price; scope gaps between the primes increase
options.E: Each prime's scope is limited to its own documents; the design must be complete
options.F: Bidders can review all requirements affecting their price; bid prices usually rise

questions.explanation: Full sets let each bidder examine every requirement that might affect its price, and their drawback is that the design has to be finished first. Issuing during design and lower reproduction cost are benefits of partial packages, a full set does not limit a prime to its own documents, and scope gaps or higher bid prices are not the drawback named.

questions.question: When full sets of procurement documents go to every bidder on a multiple-prime project, industry guidance says the scope of work for each contract should be indicated where?

options.A: In the bid/proposal form or in Section 01 12 00
options.B: In the instructions to bidders or in Section 01 11 00
options.C: In the agreement form or in Section 01 31 00
options.D: In the supplementary conditions or in Section 01 14 00
options.E: In the advertisement for bids or in Section 01 23 00
options.F: In the general conditions or in Section 01 32 00

questions.explanation: Because every bidder receives the full set, each contract's scope is stated on the bid/proposal form or in Section 01 12 00, Multiple Contract Summary. Section 01 11 00 describes work under a single contract, Section 01 31 00 covers coordination and meetings, Section 01 32 00 covers progress schedules, and the instructions, agreement, conditions, advertisement and alternates are not where the per-contract scope goes.

questions.question: On a multiple-prime project using the construction manager as advisor/agent option, who usually prepares the agreement form for each bid package, and with what should it be compatible?

options.A: The CM; it should be the CM's own standard subcontract form for each trade
options.B: The A/E; it should be compatible with the owner-A/E agreement form
options.C: The CM; it should be compatible with the owner-CM agreement form
options.D: Each prime contractor; it should match that contractor's standard subcontract form
options.E: The owner's attorney; it should match the owner's in-house legal forms
options.F: The CM; it should be compatible with the A/E's standard bid form

questions.explanation: Under the CM as advisor/agent option, the CM usually prepares the agreement form for each bid package, and that form should be compatible with the owner-CM agreement. The CM's own standard subcontract forms describe CMAR, contractor-prepared subcontract forms describe IPD, and neither the owner's attorney nor a bid form sets the standard here.

questions.question: General conditions for a multiple-prime project under the construction manager as advisor/agent option need special provisions for cooperation and mutual responsibility among the primes. Which CM service does industry guidance give as an example such provisions may require?

options.A: Reviewing and approving shop drawings for the primes in place of the A/E
options.B: Consolidating the primes' payment applications into one for the A/E to review
options.C: Certifying substantial completion for the primes on the owner's behalf
options.D: Guaranteeing a maximum price for the combined work of all of the prime contracts
options.E: Performing the work of any prime contractor that falls behind schedule
options.F: Issuing change orders to the primes without the owner's signature

questions.explanation: A typical special provision has the CM combine the multiple payment applications into a single application that the A/E reviews. Shop drawing approval and completion certification do not move to the CM, a guaranteed maximum price belongs to an at-risk arrangement, and a CM in an advisory or agency role neither performs a prime's work nor issues change orders without the owner.

questions.question: A specifier is drafting supplementary conditions for a multiple-prime project managed by a construction manager as agent. Which modifications do these supplementary conditions typically include?

options.A: The usual design-bid-build ones, such as insurance, bonds, payment applications, and retainage
options.B: Provisions coordinating the primes, with insurance and bond requirements relocated to Division 01
options.C: Provisions unique to CM delivery, since design-bid-build modifications do not carry over
options.D: Each prime's scope of work, with payment terms left to the individual agreement forms
options.E: Only the CM's fee and reimbursable expenses, since the primes are separate
options.F: Provisions restating each prime's bid price and contract time

questions.explanation: Supplementary conditions for this option carry the customary design-bid-build modifications: insurance and bond requirements and the process for payment applications and retainage. Moving insurance and bonds to Division 01, dropping the usual modifications, or filling the conditions with each prime's scope, price, time or the CM's fee confuses them with the agreements and Division 01.

questions.question: The first of five prime-contract bid packages must be issued in three weeks, but the general conditions are still in draft. The CM suggests releasing the first package now and tailoring the conditions of the contract to each later package. What is the best course of action?

options.A: Release the first package without conditions and publish one set with the last package
options.B: Complete them early for the first package, then issue identical conditions with every package
options.C: Tailor the conditions of the contract to each package's scope, just as is done for Division 01 sections
options.D: Issue the conditions only with packages whose scope carries insurance or bond requirements
options.E: Let each prime contractor propose its own conditions with its bid
options.F: Substitute Division 01 sections for the conditions until they are final

questions.explanation: The conditions of the contract go out with the first bid package, so they must be finished early, and every multiple-prime package must carry the identical conditions. Division 01 sections may vary by package, but the conditions may not; withholding them, tailoring them, letting each prime propose its own or using Division 01 in their place contradicts that.

questions.question: The construction manager is assembling a multiple-prime bid package for interior painting only. Which Division 01 requirement does industry guidance say should be included with every package, including this one?

options.A: Temporary facilities and controls
options.B: Product substitution procedures
options.C: Alternates
options.D: Field engineering
options.E: Testing laboratory services
options.F: Operation and maintenance data

questions.explanation: Submittal procedures, product substitution procedures and cleaning are common to all packages, so they go out with every multiple-prime package. Temporary facilities and controls, alternates, field engineering, testing laboratory services and operation and maintenance data are examples of sections issued only with the packages they apply to.

questions.question: On a project with several prime contracts under a construction manager as advisor/agent, which Division 01 section should identify the participants' responsibilities, the construction documents packages, and site use?

options.A: Section 01 11 00, Summary of Work
options.B: Section 01 31 00, Project Management and Coordination
options.C: Section 01 14 00, Work Restrictions
options.D: Section 01 12 00, Multiple Contract Summary
options.E: Section 01 32 00, Construction Progress Documentation
options.F: Section 01 50 00, Temporary Facilities and Controls

questions.explanation: On multiple-prime projects, Section 01 12 00, Multiple Contract Summary, identifies the participants' responsibilities, long-lead items, the construction documents packages and site use. Section 01 11 00 is for work under a single contract, and the coordination, work restrictions, progress schedule and temporary facilities sections each cover narrower subjects rather than this summary of the contracts.

questions.question: A prime contractor on a multiple-prime project managed by a construction manager as agent submits shop drawings missing required information. Under Section 01 33 00, what normally happens?

options.A: The A/E checks it for completeness and returns it through the CM to the contractor
options.B: The CM checks it for completeness and returns it to the contractor to resubmit
options.C: The CM forwards it unchanged to the A/E, which then checks it for completeness
options.D: The owner checks it for completeness and returns it to the A/E for resubmittal
options.E: The CM approves it for construction and notes the missing data
options.F: The A/E rejects it and tells the owner to withhold the payment

questions.explanation: Under this option the CM receives shop drawings, product data and samples, checks them for completeness, and either forwards them to the A/E or returns them to the contractor to resubmit. The A/E is not the completeness gatekeeper, the owner has no role in that check, and the CM checks completeness without approving the submittal for construction.

questions.question: After the CM and the A/E inspect a multiple-prime project for substantial completion, how does Section 01 70 00 typically handle the inspection results?

options.A: Given to the owner for corrective action and to each responsible contractor for information
options.B: Given to the A/E for certification and to the CM for adjustment of the final payment
options.C: Given to each responsible contractor for corrective action and to the owner for information
options.D: Given to the CM alone, which decides whether the owner needs to be informed
options.E: Given to the sureties of each prime for consent to final payment
options.F: Given to the building official to support a certificate of occupancy

questions.explanation: Results of the substantial completion inspection go to the respective contractors so they can correct deficiencies, and to the owner so it is informed. Reversing those roles, routing results only to the CM, or treating them as a payment, surety or permit matter is not how the closeout section handles them.

questions.question: Two bid packages on a multiple-prime project each need miscellaneous metal, and their Metal Fabrications sections differ in content. How can the two sections be numbered and titled?

options.A: With Level 3 numbers such as 05 51 00 and 05 52 00, each with its own distinct title
options.B: With letter suffixes such as 05 50 00A and 05 50 00B, sharing a single title
options.C: With Level 2 numbers such as 05 50 00 and 05 60 00, sharing a single title
options.D: With Level 4 numbers such as 05 50 00.10 and 05 50 00.20, each with its own title
options.E: With the same number 05 50 00 and the package name added to each title
options.F: With package prefixes such as P1-05 50 00 and P2-05 50 00, sharing one title

questions.explanation: Each package-specific metal fabrications section can get its own Level 4 number and title, such as 05 50 00.10 for building envelope and 05 50 00.20 for interior construction. Level 3 numbers already denote other MasterFormat subjects, and letter suffixes, package prefixes, another Level 2 number or one number shared by two different sections would not identify each section clearly.

questions.question: The construction manager on a multiple-prime project prefers that one Metal Fabrications section be issued with every bid package. How does industry guidance indicate the portion belonging to each package should then be defined?

options.A: Keep the single section and describe each package's scope in Section 01 11 00
options.B: Keep the single section and describe each package's scope in Section 01 12 00
options.C: Keep the single section and define each package's portion as an alternate in Section 01 23 00
options.D: Keep the single section and describe each package's scope in the supplementary conditions
options.E: Keep the single section and describe each package's scope in Section 01 31 00
options.F: Keep the single section and list each package's scope in the instructions to bidders

questions.explanation: Some construction managers use the same section for all packages and rely on Section 01 12 00, Multiple Contract Summary, to state what each package includes. Section 01 11 00 covers single-contract work, Section 01 31 00 covers coordination and meetings, alternates serve another purpose, the instructions to bidders are not contract documents, and identical conditions cannot carry package scope.

questions.question: On a multiple-prime project, the construction manager as agent asks the specifier to revise several technical sections so each prime contractor's responsibilities are unmistakable. How does industry guidance view the CM's involvement?

options.A: As appropriate, though the level of specification detail remains the A/E's decision alone
options.B: As appropriate; the CM may seek such changes and may influence specification detail
options.C: As misplaced; each prime's responsibilities belong in its agreement form, not the specifications
options.D: As premature; responsibilities are clarified by addendum only after bids are received
options.E: As misplaced; a CM as agent may not communicate with the specifier
options.F: As appropriate only if every prime contractor first agrees to the changes

questions.explanation: On multiple-prime contracts the CM may request changes so the various contractors' responsibilities are clearly defined, and the CM or the owner's project requirements may shape how detailed the specifications are. Keeping detail solely with the A/E, moving responsibilities into agreement forms, deferring them to post-bid addenda or requiring the primes' consent does not match that.

questions.question: Under the CM as advisor/agent option, which parties does industry guidance identify as possibly requiring that all document packages be combined into one project manual and one set of drawings?

options.A: The owner or the A/E
options.B: The A/E or the prime contractors
options.C: The owner or the CM
options.D: The CM or the prime contractors
options.E: The A/E or the CM
options.F: The owner or the prime contractors

questions.explanation: The owner or the CM might call for combining every package into a single project manual and drawing set, for convenience. The A/E is expected to anticipate that possibility rather than impose it, and the prime contractors are not named, so any pairing that includes the A/E or the primes is wrong.

questions.question: At the start of the construction documents stage on a multiple-prime project, the CM mentions the packages might later be merged into one project manual. What should the A/E do about specification section numbering?

options.A: Wait until all packages are issued, then renumber similar sections in the merged manual
options.B: Number each package's sections independently and add a cross-reference table later
options.C: Give every package identical Level 2 numbers and rely on the package name to distinguish them
options.D: Organize similar sections now using the appropriate level of numbers and titles
options.E: Let the CM assign section numbers as each package goes out for bids
options.F: Number each package's sections in order of issue instead of by MasterFormat

questions.explanation: The A/E should anticipate combination from the outset, organizing similar sections with suitable number levels and titles.
