questions.explanation: The local construction community's likely response is a critical factor: enough bidders must be able and willing to respond to performance criteria, and too few participants can cancel out the method's advantages, so the level must be set to match local capabilities. Requiring in-house design ignores that services can be retained per project, jumping to the broadest levels or leaning on manufacturers sidesteps the capability problem, and the level cannot wait until bids are opened.

questions.question: A general contractor with no engineers on staff asks whether it can respond to a performance-based solicitation that requires design of the specified systems. How may bidders or proposers furnish the necessary services?

options.A: In-house, because design responsibility cannot be delegated to outside firms
options.B: Through the A/E of record, under an amendment to its agreement with the owner
options.C: In-house, or by retaining them on a project-by-project basis as needed
options.D: Through the system manufacturer, as part of its standard product warranty
options.E: Through the owner's CM-advisor/agent, as part of its coordination role
options.F: Through the owner's independent testing agency, under a separate agreement

questions.explanation: Responding to performance criteria takes design and engineering, but bidders or proposers may supply those services with their own staff or bring them in project by project as needed, so a contractor without engineers can still take part. Design can be obtained from outside firms, and the A/E of record, the owner's CM or testing agency, and a product warranty are not how a bidder obtains these services.

questions.question: Which set of activities does a performance-based solicitation require of participating bidders or proposers?

options.A: Administering contracts, designing items, acquiring systems products, coordinating installation
options.B: Writing performance criteria, selecting test methods, evaluating proposals, awarding contracts
options.C: Preparing the program, securing financing, approving the budget, obtaining the building permit
options.D: Reviewing submittals, certifying payments, issuing change orders, accepting the completed work
options.E: Administering contracts, designing items, writing performance criteria, issuing permits
options.F: Defining owner needs, designing items, acquiring systems products, coordinating installation

questions.explanation: A performance-based solicitation expects bidders or proposers to administer contracts, design and engineer the performance-specified items, acquire suitable systems products, and coordinate installation as needed, using in-house or retained services. Writing criteria and defining needs fall to the owner and A/E, permits come from AHJs, and evaluating proposals, financing, submittal review and payment certification are owner or A/E tasks.

questions.question: A state agency's procurement rules require that every proposal be judged strictly on a complies/does-not-comply basis, with no negotiation. Which level of performance specifying may be best?

options.A: A broader level, because objective evaluation reduces the A/E's design effort
options.B: The broadest levels, H and J, because objective scoring suits systems proposals
options.C: Any level, because the evaluation method does not affect the level chosen
options.D: A narrower level, because absolute objectivity in evaluation is demanded
options.E: A broader level, because negotiation can resolve any noncompliance
options.F: A broader level, because public agencies favor design-build delivery

questions.explanation: When evaluation must be absolutely objective, judged only as complying or not complying, a narrower performance level is likely the better fit, because broader levels depend on subjective judgment and the freedom to accept, reject or negotiate. A rule against negotiation removes that latitude, so the evaluation method does affect the level, and objective scoring favors neither broader levels nor the broadest levels used mainly for design-build.

questions.question: An owner's representative argues against broad-level performance specifying because it will necessarily lengthen proposal development and complicate evaluation. Which statement is accurate?

options.A: Both effects necessarily follow, so broad levels suit only negotiated procurements
options.B: Neither necessarily follows, though the broad level does demand more A/E design time
options.C: Neither necessarily follows, and the broad level also reduces the A/E's design time
options.D: Only longer development follows, since evaluation time is fixed by the owner's rules
options.E: Only a more involved evaluation follows, since broad proposals vary widely
options.F: Both effects follow, but the broad level reduces the A/E's design time

questions.explanation: Choosing a broad level does not by itself lengthen the time to develop proposals or make their evaluation more complicated. It does, however, add A/E time to design the solutions that rely on the performance specification to meet the design intent. Claims that either effect must follow are wrong, and so is any claim that the broad level saves the A/E design time.

questions.question: A contractor that regularly uses systems building components is reviewing two solicitations, one with broad-level and one with narrow-level performance specifications. What risk does the narrow-level approach carry?

options.A: It may demand highly developed design and manufacturing capability
options.B: It may permit only a subjective evaluation of each proposal
options.C: It may serve only to exclude otherwise acceptable options
options.D: It may require drawings that are diagrammatic in content
options.E: It may give manufacturers too much latitude to innovate
options.F: It may invite proposals for most elements of the project

questions.explanation: A contractor that regularly uses systems building components can respond readily to broad-level performance specifications, but narrow-level specifications may only shut out options that would otherwise be acceptable. Narrow levels restrict innovation rather than widen it, while demanding design capability, subjective evaluation, diagrammatic drawings and proposals for most of the project are traits of broad levels.

questions.question: A specifier's performance section for cast-in-place concrete states required mix proportions and also a minimum 28-day compressive strength. What problem may result?

options.A: The bidder may be able to comply with just the less demanding requirement
options.B: The bidder must comply with whichever requirement is more stringent in each case
options.C: The mix proportions automatically govern, and the strength becomes advisory only
options.D: The section converts to a reference standard specification by default
options.E: The strength requirement governs, and the mix proportions become advisory only
options.F: The concrete supplier takes on the burden of performance for the mix

questions.explanation: Specifying the same item in both descriptive and performance terms, such as a concrete mix by proportions and also by strength, sets up a possible conflict between the stated criteria and how the described mix actually performs, and the bidder might satisfy only the less demanding of the two. No rule makes the stricter, the descriptive or the performance requirement govern automatically, the section does not become a reference standard specification, and the supplier does not take on the burden of performance.

questions.question: A specifier wants to cite a test method that was originally developed for one material to evaluate a different material in a performance specification. Which statement is correct?

options.A: It should not be used, since tests developed for one material never apply to others
options.B: It may have valid application, but its validity and applicability must be verified
options.C: It may be cited for information only, since criteria cannot rely on material-specific tests
options.D: It may be used as is, since any published standard test is inherently performance oriented
options.E: It may be cited only if a trade association for the new material has endorsed it
options.F: It must be replaced by a test of a mock-up or prototype built for the project

questions.explanation: Many tests were written for one material under particular conditions and do not carry over, yet some material-oriented tests remain valid for other materials, so the specifier must know the test well enough to confirm it is valid, applicable and useful for the end result. Its origin neither bars it nor makes it acceptable as is, since referenced tests must be performance oriented, and no trade-association endorsement or mock-up substitute is required.

questions.question: To appear thorough, a specifier adds several referenced standards to a performance specification that have no real utility for the project conditions. What is the effect of this overspecifying?

options.A: It lowers the owner's risk by expanding the basis for rejecting proposals
options.B: It shifts design liability from the A/E to the referenced testing agency
options.C: It turns the performance specification into a reference standard method
options.D: It raises costs by putting a needless burden on bidders or proposers
options.E: It broadens competition by giving proposers more ways to show compliance
options.F: It reduces the test reports and design data that proposers must submit

questions.explanation: Specified standards and tests should reflect the project's conditions. Requiring compliance with standards that have no real use for the project achieves nothing and adds cost, because every bidder or proposer must carry the extra burden of meeting them. Overspecifying does not lower the owner's risk, shift design liability, change the specifying method, broaden competition, or cut the submittals required.

questions.question: Midway through design, the A/E decides to narrow the level of performance specifying for an exterior wall system from broad to narrow. How should the accompanying drawings change?

options.A: They should become more diagrammatic in composition and content
options.B: They should be omitted, leaving the written criteria to govern
options.C: They should become more definitive in composition and content
options.D: They should be reduced to existing condition drawings only
options.E: They should be limited to a location plan with a blank footprint
options.F: They should be limited to site drawings and schematic plans

questions.explanation: Drawings that accompany performance criteria follow the level of specifying: a broad level calls for diagrammatic drawings, and a narrower level calls for more definitive ones. Omitting drawings, or limiting them to existing conditions, a location plan with a blank footprint, or site drawings with schematic plans, fits the broad levels where the proposer develops the design, the opposite of narrowing.

questions.question: Drawings for a performance-specified sunshade system show an illustrative blade layout, but the A/E does not intend to require strict adherence to that configuration. What should the A/E do?

options.A: Note that the layout represents only a suggested definition
options.B: Delete the layout, since drawings cannot accompany performance criteria
options.C: Leave the layout un-noted, since written criteria always govern graphics
options.D: Restate the layout as a descriptive requirement in the section text
options.E: Show the layout as a mandatory configuration that admits no alternatives
options.F: Move the layout into the available information issued to bidders

questions.explanation: A drawing meant only as a suggested definition, with no requirement to follow its configuration exactly, should carry a note saying so, and written and graphic material must not contradict each other. Deleting the layout, leaving it unmarked, or making it mandatory misstates the intent; restating it in the text describes the item twice; and available information is not part of the contract documents.

questions.question: On a project with several performance-specified systems, the owner asks where it will be made clear which party is responsible for coordinating the design once the final performance product characteristics are known. Which documents clarify this?

options.A: The design development drawings
options.B: The procurement documents
options.C: The project record documents
options.D: The preliminary project description
options.E: The shop drawing submittals
options.F: The schedule of values

questions.explanation: The procurement documents state which party coordinates the design once the final characteristics of the performance products are known, so proposers know the responsibility before they respond. Design development drawings and the preliminary project description are earlier design tools, while shop drawings, the schedule of values and record documents come from the contractor after award, too late to assign it.

questions.question: A turnkey project is procured at the broadest level of performance specifying. What do the drawings furnished to proposers consist of?

options.A: Structural layout and foundation drawings fixed by the A/E
options.B: Definitive drawings with blanks at performance-specified items
options.C: Site drawings plus fully detailed elevations and sections
options.D: Existing condition drawings only
options.E: Site drawings with schematic plans, elevations, and sections
options.F: Definitive site drawings, with plans left for the proposer

questions.explanation: At the broadest level of performance specifying, as in a turnkey or design-build project, the drawings consist only of existing condition drawings; design direction comes from the design criteria, and the proposer develops the rest. Site drawings with schematic plans, definitive site drawings, A/E-fixed structural layouts and definitive drawings with blanks belong to narrower levels, where the A/E still draws part of the work.

questions.question: Separate prime contracts are awarded for a performance-specified curtain wall and a performance-specified skylight system that meet at a common edge. When are the details at that interface coordinated?

options.A: Before bidding, by the A/E on its definitive construction drawings
options.B: During bidding, as each bidder details its interface with the other system
options.C: After each of the interfacing systems has been selected
options.D: After the first system is selected, by that system's successful bidder
options.E: During bidding, through addenda issued by the A/E to all bidders
options.F: After construction, as each contractor prepares its record drawings

questions.explanation: With multiple-prime contracts for performance-specified systems, the A/E draws the descriptive items definitively and shows the performance-specified items only generically, and each successful proposer develops its own system. Where two such systems meet, their interface can only be detailed once every interfacing system has been chosen; before or during bidding the solutions are unknown, one selection is not enough, and record drawings come far too late.

questions.question: A performance-specified rooftop mechanical system appears on the bid drawings only as an outline without detail. What must the A/E still show definitively?

options.A: The elements with which the system must interface
options.B: The configuration and dimensions of the system itself
options.C: The manufacturer and model the design is based on
options.D: The routing of every duct and pipe within the system
options.E: The nominal dimensions of each component within the system
options.F: The detailed drawings of the proposer's chosen solution

questions.explanation: A performance-specified element may appear as an outline without detail, but the A/E must still show definitively the elements it has to interface with, because bidders and proposers need that to develop solutions. The proposer then prepares detailed drawings of its solution and how it relates to other work, so the system's configuration, components, internal routing and product selection are left to the proposer.

questions.question: An owner awards a separate prime contract for each of several systems that will be assembled before delivery. When does the A/E begin developing definitive construction drawings that integrate those systems?

options.A: Before bidding, so each bidder can price against fixed details
options.B: Only after the final choice of every system has been made
options.C: During bidding, as addenda answering bidders' questions
options.D: After the first system is selected, ahead of the others
options.E: During schematic design, as part of the design given to bidders
options.F: Never, since each system's bidder furnishes all definitive drawings

questions.explanation: When a separate prime contract covers each of several systems assembled before delivery, the performance specifications come with no definitive drawings: the A/E gives each bidder a schematic project design, and bidders submit definitive drawings of their own systems. Only after every system has been finally chosen does the A/E start the definitive construction drawings that integrate the systems with each other and with the descriptive work.

questions.question: A broad-level performance specification uses UniFormat as the organizational format for the project manual. How is each section titled?

options.A: With the MasterFormat number and title, adding the UniFormat number in the footer
options.B: With both MasterFormat and UniFormat numbers, separated by a slash in the title
options.C: With a descriptive title only, numbering being assigned in the table of contents
options.D: With the UniFormat number and title instead of MasterFormat's number and title
options.E: With the Section 01 80 00 Level 3 number and title for each element
options.F: With the OmniClass table number and title for each element

questions.explanation: When broad-level performance specifying uses UniFormat to organize the project manual, each section title carries the applicable UniFormat number and title where a MasterFormat number and title would otherwise go. Keeping MasterFormat numbers, dual numbering, or unnumbered titles is not the approach; Section 01 80 00 numbers serve narrow-level performance specifying, and OmniClass tables classify information rather than title project manual sections.

questions.question: A specifier preparing a broad-level performance specification organized by UniFormat assumes PageFormat no longer applies to the page layout. Which statement is correct?

options.A: PageFormat can be used for narrow-level performance specifying only
options.B: PageFormat applies only when sections carry MasterFormat numbers and titles
options.C: PageFormat suits both narrow-level and broad-level performance specifying
options.D: PageFormat is replaced by a UniFormat page layout for broad-level work
options.E: PageFormat governs only the order of articles within each section
options.F: PageFormat applies only to sections written by the descriptive method

questions.explanation: PageFormat, which sets an orderly, uniform arrangement of text on each page, serves narrow-level and broad-level performance specifying alike. When UniFormat organizes the manual, only the section number and title change; there is no separate UniFormat page layout, and PageFormat is not limited to narrow-level, descriptive or MasterFormat-numbered sections. Arranging articles within a section is SectionFormat's job.

questions.question: When the three-part SectionFormat is adapted for use in performance specifications, how are its article headings typically changed?

options.A: It omits some article headings, adds one broad article title, and adds several narrow ones
options.B: It keeps every standard heading unchanged and adds a separate fourth part for performance criteria
options.C: It omits PART 3—EXECUTION, since the contractor determines the installation methods
options.D: It adds several broad article titles and omits all of the narrow article titles
options.E: It replaces the three parts with Section 01 80 00 Level 2 and 3 titles
options.F: It keeps the standard headings and moves all criteria into PART 1 Summary

questions.explanation: The three-part SectionFormat is kept for performance specifying, for consistency and flexibility. The adapted version leaves out article headings that usually do not apply to performance work, adds one broad article title, and adds several narrow ones, in keeping with the idea that every article title is optional. PART 3 stays, no fourth part is added, and the criteria go in PART 2, not the Summary or Division 01.

questions.question: In a performance specification for a curtain wall, the specifier must define how the system interfaces with the structural frame and roofing specified in other sections. Which PART 1 article should be used?

options.A: References
options.B: Summary
options.C: Quality Assurance
options.D: Project or Site Conditions
options.E: Submittals
options.F: Warranty

questions.explanation: In PART 1 of a performance section, the Summary article defines how the specified system interfaces with systems or products specified in other sections. References carries definitions and cited standards, Quality Assurance carries qualifications, Project or Site Conditions covers environmental and existing conditions and field measurements, Submittals lists documents to be furnished, and Warranty covers guarantees, so none of them is the place for interface requirements.

questions.question: A specifier wants test reports and design data for a performance-specified skylight system submitted with the proposal, and a colleague insists submittals cannot be required before award. At which points in time may performance submittals be requested?

options.A: With bid, after award, before fabrication, during installation, at substantial completion
options.B: After award, before delivery, before installation, after installation, at final payment
options.C: Before bid, after award, before fabrication, after installation, after final acceptance
options.D: Before bid, with bid, before fabrication, before installation, before final acceptance
options.E: Before bid, with bid, after award, before delivery, after final payment
options.F: With bid, before fabrication, before delivery, before installation, at closeout

questions.explanation: Performance submittals may be called for at five points: before the bid or proposal, with it, before fabrication, before installation, and before final acceptance. Requiring test reports and design data with the proposal is therefore allowed. Every other list adds a point that is not among the five, such as after award, before delivery, after installation, at substantial completion, at closeout or after final payment.

questions.question: The submittals required in a performance specification can be separated into which two groups, and with provisions intended to ensure what?

options.A: Action and informational, ensuring timely and consistent review by the A/E
options.B: Prebid and postbid, ensuring fair and open competition among all proposers
options.C: Quality assurance and quality control, ensuring correct design liability
options.D: Product and closeout, ensuring complete and accurate project record documents
options.E: Shop drawings and product data, ensuring the work matches the design
options.F: Design data and test reports, ensuring compliance with the criteria

questions.explanation: Performance submittals fall into two groups, quality assurance and quality control, and the provisions for them are meant to place design liability with the correct party. Some submittals also need review and approval while others are only documentation or information, but that is not the grouping tied to design liability. Shop drawings, product data, design data and test reports are individual submittal types, not the two groups.

questions.question: For a performance-specified precast cladding system, the qualification requirements in the Quality Assurance article must set credentials, possibly including engineering licensure by AHJs, for which entities?

options.A: Manufacturer, contractor, designer, installer, and testing agency
options.B: Owner, A/E of record, contractor, installer, and testing agency
options.C: Manufacturer, supplier, installer, surety, and building official
options.D: Contractor, subcontractors, installer, inspector, and A/E of record
options.E: Owner, manufacturer, designer, surety, and testing agency
options.F: Fabricator, supplier, A/E of record, installer, and inspector

questions.explanation: Under the broad Quality Assurance article of a performance section, qualification requirements must set credentials for the entities involved: manufacturer, contractor, designer, installer, and testing agency. Those credentials may call for engineering expertise and licensure by authorities having jurisdiction. The owner, the A/E of record, the surety, suppliers, inspectors and the building official are not entities whose credentials the section sets.

questions.question: Within the Performance/Design Criteria article of a performance specification, attributes, requirements, criteria, and tests work together. Which describes the role of a criterion?

options.A: A statement of the discrete need or expected result for an attribute
options.B: A statement that sets limits or gives standards bounding a requirement
options.C: The procedure by which the element's performance is evaluated
options.D: A characteristic of the element, such as fire resistance or deflection
options.E: A category, such as safety and protection, that groups related attributes
options.F: A list of the components that together make up the specified system

questions.explanation: In the Performance/Design Criteria article, each element's attributes are listed, requirements state the discrete needs or expected results for them, and criteria bound those requirements by setting limits or giving standards in measurable or observable terms. A test tied to each criterion is how performance is evaluated. The other options describe a requirement, a test, an attribute, an attribute category, and a component list.

questions.question: A specifier is converting a descriptive section to a performance specification. Which group of PART 2 article titles is seldom used, because those decisions are typically left to the manufacturer, fabricator, supplier, or contractor?

options.A: Performance/Design Criteria, Components, and Finishes
options.B: Components, Finishes, and Source Quality Control
options.C: Manufacturers, Performance/Design Criteria, and Mixes
options.D: Materials, Mixes, and Fabrication
options.E: Performance/Design Criteria, Finishes, and Source Quality Control
options.F: Manufacturers, Components, and Finishes

questions.explanation: Because a performance specification states end results rather than the means of reaching them, article titles such as Manufacturers, Materials, Manufactured Units, Equipment, Mixes, and Fabrication are seldom used, though they can still narrow the field to acceptable or unacceptable products. Performance/Design Criteria, Components, Finishes, and Source Quality Control remain among the PART 2 articles, so any group that includes one of them is wrong.

questions.question: On a small clinic, the A/E's performance criteria for a daylighting system would require advancing the current state-of-the-art technology. What response should the A/E anticipate?

options.A: A limited response unless the volume of work supports research and development costs
options.B: A broad response, because performance criteria invite innovation from many suppliers
options.C: A broad response, because state-of-the-art requirements lower proposers' design costs
options.D: A limited response unless the criteria are restated as proprietary product requirements
options.E: A broad response, because no standard solution yet exists on the market
options.F: A broad response, because subjective evaluation of proposals is allowed

questions.explanation: A requirement that pushes an element beyond the current state of the art tends to draw few responses unless the volume of work is large enough to pay for the research and development. Performance specifying does suit elements that lack a standard solution, and subjective evaluation allows a broader level, but neither creates interest when the cost barrier remains; restating the criteria as proprietary requirements is not the remedy either.

questions.question: A performance specification for an integrated ceiling needs distinct attributes, requirements, criteria, and tests for the grid, the acoustical panels, and the light fixtures. How should PART 2 be organized?

options.A: List all of them together within a single Performance/Design Criteria article
options.B: Provide a separate article for each one, which may carry that item's actual name
options.C: Specify each one under a Manufactured Units article with its own model number
options.D: Move each one into its own section and cross-reference it under the Summary
options.E: Group all of them under Accessories, since they support the main system
options.F: Place them in a schedule that follows the end of the section

questions.explanation: Complex systems may need attributes defined for major components as well as for the whole system. The generic Components article, or an article named for the component itself, such as Suspension Grid, Acoustical Panels, or Luminaires, can be repeated so each component has its own attributes, requirements, criteria, and tests. One combined criteria article, Manufactured Units or Accessories articles, separate sections, or a schedule would not organize them that way.

questions.question: A specifier drafting a performance specification section for an exterior wall system states the required air-infiltration rate in PART 2. A consultant then adds a PART 3 paragraph prescribing the sealant sequence and anchor spacing the installer must use to reach that rate. What is the main concern with this draft?

options.A: PART 3 of a performance section may not contain an installation article of any kind
options.B: Specifying the PART 2 result and a PART 3 method to achieve it can cause conflicts
options.C: The prescribed method belongs in Section 01 80 00 rather than in PART 3 of the section
options.D: Installation methods for performance sections belong in PART 1 under Quality Assurance
options.E: The air-infiltration rate belongs in Section 01 80 00 rather than in PART 2
options.F: The prescribed method should be moved to the PART 3 Field Quality Control article

questions.explanation: Stating the performance result in PART 2 and also prescribing in PART 3 a way to reach it can create conflicts, so extra care is needed to avoid doing both. A performance section may still include an installation article, so a ban overstates the rule. Section 01 80 00 holds element numbers and titles for narrow-level performance requirements, not installation methods, and moving the method to PART 1 or to Field Quality Control leaves the conflict in place.

questions.question: A performance specification section for a roofing system will accept several manufacturers' systems, each with its own application, and the installer may choose among options. What may be all that is necessary in the PART 3 installation article?

options.A: A detailed installation procedure written around the basis-of-design system
options.B: A cross-reference to Section 01 80 00 for each element's installation method
options.C: No PART 3 content, because execution articles do not apply to performance sections
options.D: A statement requiring compliance with the manufacturer's installation instructions
options.E: A requirement for a mock-up of each proposed system before installation
options.F: A full installation method for each system that might be proposed

questions.explanation: Several products may satisfy a performance specification, each installed its own way, or the installer may be allowed other options, so sometimes a single statement requiring compliance with the manufacturer's installation instructions is all the article needs. Writing procedures around one system, or for every possible system, ignores that installation depends on the product developed. PART 3 articles still apply, Section 01 80 00 covers performance requirements, and a mock-up is a quality measure.

questions.question: A design-build owner wants the project manual to establish end-result requirements for broad-scope building elements without referencing specific products. Which numbering approach suits this broad level of performance specifying?

options.A: UniFormat Level 1 and 2 numbers and titles for the element sections
options.B: Section 01 80 00 Level 2 and 3 numbers and titles for each element
options.C: UniFormat Level 3 and 4 numbers and titles for each specific product
options.D: Section 01 80 00 and UniFormat numbers combined in one project manual
options.E: MasterFormat Level 2 and 3 numbers and titles for each product section
options.F: OmniClass product table numbers and titles for each product

questions.explanation: For broad performance specifying with UniFormat, its Level 1 and 2 numbers and titles can head sections that set end-result requirements for broad-scope building elements without naming products. Section 01 80 00 Level 2 and 3 titles suit narrow-level performance specifying; 01 80 00 and UniFormat both suit design-build but not together in one manual; and product-level UniFormat, MasterFormat or OmniClass numbering contradicts the no-specific-products approach.

questions.question: A specifier's section title list will be distributed to the owner and other design team members early in design. What is it preferable to add to the list, and what can the list ultimately become?

options.A: Article and page numbers for each section; the master for all cross-references
options.B: Cost estimates for each section's scope; the basis for the schedule of values
options.C: Other documents and forms in the project manual; the manual's table of contents
options.D: Names of the consultants writing each section; the drawing coordination checklist
options.E: Proposed manufacturers for each section; the basis-of-design product list
options.F: Revision dates for each section; the project manual revision log

questions.explanation: The section title list usually goes to the owner and other design team members, so it is better to include the other documents and forms that will be bound into the project manual; in its final form the list can serve as the manual's table of contents. Cross-references use section numbers only, never article or page numbers, and cost estimates, consultant names, manufacturers and revision dates are not what the list adds.

questions.question: Working from an office master guide specification, a specifier renumbers several master sections to suit a project. Why should this be done with care?

options.A: MasterFormat does not permit project-specific changes to section numbers
options.B: Renumbered sections lose their SectionFormat article structure
options.C: Cross-references to the original numbers may exist in other sections
options.D: The owner must approve each change made to the section title list
options.E: Each new number must first be recorded in the office master's revision log
options.F: Section numbers must stay matched to the drawing sheet numbers

questions.explanation: Sections drawn from a master guide specification may be cross-referenced by other sections of the master, so changing their numbers can leave references pointing to the wrong place. MasterFormat does not forbid project-specific numbering, SectionFormat structure is unaffected, and neither owner approval, a revision-log entry, nor drawing sheet numbering governs the change. A related rule is to cross-reference section numbers only, never article or page numbers.

questions.question: When a master guide specification system is used, the proposed section title list should be compared with the master system's contents. What should that comparison identify?

options.A: Sections that can be edited from guide text versus those to be custom-prepared
options.B: Sections to be prepared by consultants versus those prepared by the A/E
options.C: Sections belonging in Division 01 versus those in Divisions 02 through 49
options.D: Sections to be specified descriptively versus those to be specified by performance
options.E: Sections using proprietary methods versus those using reference standards
options.F: Sections needed for the bid set versus those to be issued by addendum

questions.explanation: Comparing the proposed section titles with the master's contents shows which sections can be developed or edited from existing master text and which must be written from scratch for the project. The comparison should also flag products or work that could end up specified in more than one section. Consultant assignments, Division placement, specifying method and addendum timing are not what it sorts out.

questions.question: A specifier includes product illustrations within several specification sections. Where may text that clarifies the status of the graphics within the documents be included?

options.A: In the instructions to bidders, under the bidders' representations
options.B: In the supplementary conditions, under definitions of contract documents
options.C: In Division 01, under the submittal procedures for product data sheets
options.D: In the owner-contractor agreement, under the enumeration of documents
options.E: In the general notes on the cover sheet of the drawings
options.F: In the closeout section, under project record document requirements

questions.explanation: Graphics belong in specifications only after careful thought and with text that makes their status within the documents clear. That text may go in the supplementary conditions, where the contract documents are defined. The instructions to bidders, Division 01 submittal or closeout sections, the agreement's list of documents and drawing notes are not where that clarifying statement is placed.

questions.question: A specifier wants to include a manufacturer's data sheet to illustrate the basis-of-design product in a section. Besides referencing the data sheet in the section, where does SectionFormat suggest inserting it?

options.A: In an appendix placed after the last section of Division 49
options.B: On a supplementary sheet issued with the contract drawings
options.C: In PART 2 of the section, under the article naming manufacturers
options.D: In the project manual immediately following the individual section
options.E: In Division 01, within the general product requirements section
options.F: In the procurement requirements, as information available to bidders

questions.explanation: Manufacturers' data sheets that illustrate basis-of-design products can be referenced in the individual section or, as SectionFormat suggests, bound into the project manual right after that section. An appendix at the end of the manual, a drawing sheet, a PART 2 article, the Division 01 product requirements section, and the available information documents are not the placement SectionFormat suggests.

questions.question: A specifier plans to paste a photograph of a lighting fixture, copied from a manufacturer's catalog, into a lighting section. What should the specifier consider before doing so?

options.A: Photographs belong only on the contract drawings, so the photograph must be moved there
options.B: Copyright release may be needed, and a patented design may imply added requirements
options.C: Only isometric views are permitted, so the photograph must be redrawn as one
options.D: A photograph makes the section a closed proprietary specification requiring owner approval
options.E: Photographs are allowed only for items carried as allowances
options.F: The photograph must be reviewed by the AHJ before the section is issued

questions.explanation: Using another party's illustrations, graphics or photographs may require permission or a copyright release from their owner or originator, and an image of a proprietary or patented design could imply requirements beyond those written. Illustrations, including photographs and isometric views, are allowed in specifications, and lighting fixtures are a typical item that benefits from them. Nothing limits them to allowance items, requires AHJ review, or makes the section closed proprietary.

questions.question: A firm's specification style guide must state the three qualities that characterize good specification writing style. Which three should it list?

options.A: Clarity, correctness, and completeness
options.B: Accuracy, brevity, and clarity
options.C: Brevity, consistency, and precision
options.D: Accuracy, conciseness, and completeness
options.E: Accuracy, simplicity, and consistency
options.F: Brevity, clarity, and completeness

questions.explanation: A good specification writing style is marked by accuracy, brevity, and clarity, supported by simple sentences and plain, clearly understood terms. Clear, concise, complete, and correct are the separate four Cs of effective communication, so lists built from completeness, correctness or conciseness mix the two ideas, and consistency, precision and simplicity are not among the three named qualities.

questions.question: A consultant's section is written in long sentences that attach several qualifying clauses to each requirement. Under recommended specification writing style, in what form should sentence structure be maintained?

options.A: Simple statements in declarative or imperative form
options.B: Narrative statements explaining each requirement's intent
options.C: Compound statements that group related requirements
options.D: Conditional statements that state any exceptions first
options.E: Streamlined statements with a colon in place of every verb
options.F: Passive statements that name the item before the action

questions.explanation: One of the basic writing style rules is to keep sentence structure to simple declarative or imperative statements, alongside using simple sentences. Narrative explanations of intent, compound groupings, exception-first conditionals and passive constructions all add length or weaken the instruction. Streamlining with colons suits lists of products, materials and standards, not the sentence structure of requirements in general.

questions.question: A draft section contains one long sentence that combines products, installation locations, and exceptions in several clauses. Under recommended specification writing style, what is the specific risk of such complicated sentences?

options.A: The sentence cannot be converted to the imperative mood without rewriting
options.B: Reviewers outside the design team may not understand trade terminology
options.C: Complex sentences increase page count and reproduction costs of the manual
options.D: Accidentally dropping or adding punctuation could alter the meaning
options.E: Each clause would then have to be restated in the indicative mood
options.F: Bidders could treat the exceptions as alternates to be priced separately

questions.explanation: The writing style rules warn against complicated sentences because accidentally leaving out or adding a punctuation mark could change their meaning or make them ambiguous. Converting to the imperative, unfamiliar trade terms, page count, the indicative mood and the pricing of exceptions are not the risk named; word choice is a separate rule that calls for simple, clearly understood terms.

questions.question: Applying the rule that the shorter of two equally correct spellings is preferred, a specifier changes every 'through' in the project manual to 'thru.' How does recommended spelling practice treat this change?

options.A: Acceptable, because shorter spellings are preferred in contract documents
options.B: Acceptable, if the change is applied consistently in every section
options.C: Unacceptable, because spellings created for brevity should be avoided
options.D: Unacceptable, unless 'thru' appears in the office supplemental term list
options.E: Acceptable, if 'thru' is defined in the Division 01 abbreviations list
options.F: Unacceptable, because only the longer spelling is allowed in contract documents

questions.explanation: When two spellings are equally correct, the shorter is preferred in contract documents, as with facia, gage, molding, and catalog. That preference does not cover spellings invented to save letters: thru is not an accepted spelling of through and should be avoided. Using it consistently, adding it to a supplemental list or defining it in Division 01 does not make it acceptable, and the longer spelling is not mandatory.

questions.question: Two specifiers in the same firm disagree on how to spell several words. What should spelling in the specifications be based on?

options.A: The spellings used in the reference standards cited in each section
options.B: An office-standard dictionary, with a supplemental list of technical terms
options.C: The spellings preferred by the manufacturer of each basis-of-design product
options.D: The MasterFormat titles and keywords index published for each section
options.E: The spellings used in the general conditions of the contract
options.F: The spellings each consultant uses in its own office master

questions.explanation: Spelling should be correct and consistent, based on one dictionary that the office designates as its standard, plus a supplemental list of technical terms that dictionary lacks. Reference standards, manufacturers' literature, MasterFormat titles, the general conditions and consultants' own masters are not the basis named, and following several such sources would produce inconsistent spellings across the manual.

questions.question: Compare 'Install equipment plumb and level' with 'The Contractor shall install equipment plumb and level.' These illustrate the two basic grammatical moods for specification sentences. Which moods are they, in order?

options.A: Indicative mood, then imperative mood
options.B: Imperative mood, then indicative mood
options.C: Imperative mood, then subjunctive mood
options.D: Declarative mood, then indicative mood
options.E: Imperative mood, then passive voice
options.F: Indicative mood, then subjunctive mood

questions.explanation: The two basic moods for specification requirements are imperative and indicative. The imperative puts the action verb first, as in 'Install equipment plumb and level,' while the indicative typically uses shall or will, as in 'The Contractor shall install.' Reversing the order mislabels them, the second sentence is in the active voice, and subjunctive and declarative are not the two moods used.

questions.question: A paragraph reads 'Provide the following accessories' and is followed by three subparagraphs that list the items. How should that introductory paragraph end?

options.A: With a semicolon, showing that the list continues the sentence
options.B: With no punctuation, since the subparagraphs complete it
options.C: With a period, since every paragraph must end in a period
options.D: With a colon, so that the subparagraphs are linked to it
options.E: With a comma, since the list completes the sentence
options.F: With a dash, introducing the items that follow

questions.explanation: Every paragraph ends with either a period or a colon, and a parent paragraph ends with a colon when its subparagraphs must be linked to it, as with a list of accessories. A period suits a paragraph that stands on its own, and semicolons, commas, dashes, or no punctuation are not endings the rules allow. Each listed item then ends with a period to show nothing is missing.

questions.question: A draft sentence reads 'One of the long anchor bolts are to be set in the base plate.' What grammatical error does it contain?

options.A: The singular subject 'one' is paired with the plural verb 'are'
options.B: The plural subject 'bolts' is paired with a singular verb
options.C: The modifier 'long anchor' has no noun for it to modify
options.D: The passive verb 'to be set' does not name the responsible party
options.E: The pronoun 'one' has no clear noun for it to refer to
options.F: The sentence mixes the indicative and the imperative moods

questions.explanation: Subject and verb must agree in number. The subject here is the singular 'one,' so it needs a singular verb; 'bolts' belongs to the plural modifier 'of the long anchor bolts,' which is easily mistaken for the subject in a long sentence. 'Long anchor' does modify 'bolts,' 'one' plainly refers to one of the bolts, and the sentence uses only the indicative mood, so none of those is the error.

questions.question: A draft reads 'One of the two stainless steel clips are to be placed over the rail and fastened.' Which revision best follows recommended specification grammar and style?

options.A: Place one stainless steel clip over the rail, and it should be fastened.
options.B: One of the stainless steel clips is to be placed over the rail and fastened.
options.C: Fasten one stainless steel clip to the rail.
options.D: Rail shall receive one fastened stainless steel clip.
options.E: The Contractor shall place one stainless steel clip over the rail and fasten it.
options.F: One of the stainless steel clips are to be fastened to the rail.

questions.explanation: The best revision fixes the number error and is a short, direct imperative: the action verb comes first and one verb carries the whole instruction. The 'place... and it should be fastened' version drifts from the imperative into a weak 'should' clause, the 'is to be placed' version keeps a phrase not recommended in specifications, the 'shall' versions add words or give a duty to an object, and the last version still pairs 'one' with 'are.'

questions.question: A mechanical section's scope paragraph lists 'Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning.' Applying the rules of parallel construction and punctuation, how should this series read?

options.A: Heat, ventilation, and air-conditioning
options.B: Heating, ventilation and air-conditioning
options.C: Heating, ventilating, and air-conditioning
options.D: Heating, ventilating and air-conditioning
options.E: Heating; ventilating; and air-conditioning
options.F: Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioners

questions.explanation: Items in a series should share the same grammatical form, so 'ventilation' must become 'ventilating' to match 'heating' and 'air-conditioning,' and the formal punctuation rules call for a comma after each item, including the one before 'and.' Versions without that final comma, with semicolons, or mixing forms such as 'heat,' 'ventilation' or 'air-conditioners' each break one rule or the other.

questions.question: Good grammar calls for parallel form in the two halves of a compound subject or predicate. For which other construction is the same identical grammatical structure recommended?

options.A: A parent paragraph and each of its subparagraphs
options.B: A series of nouns, adverbs, or prepositional phrases
options.C: A section title and each of its article titles
options.D: A reference standard designation and its edition date
options.E: A requirement and the reference standard that governs it
options.F: A product name and its manufacturer's model number

questions.explanation: Parallel construction applies to compound subjects and predicates and also to a series of nouns, adverbs, or prepositional phrases, as in 'heating, ventilating, and air-conditioning.' The relationship between a parent paragraph and its subparagraphs is a punctuation matter, and section or article titles, standard designations and product names are not what this grammar rule addresses.

questions.question: A draft reads 'Spray sealer from the tank onto the slab when it is above 50 degrees F.' Applying the rules of pronoun reference, what is the best revision approach?

options.A: Replace 'it' with 'same' so that it clearly refers back to the tank
options.B: Add a 'which' clause identifying the item that must exceed 50 degrees F
options.C: Retain 'it', because only personal pronouns are to be avoided
options.D: Repeat the intended noun, such as ambient temperature, in place of 'it'
options.E: Replace 'it' with 'this' so that the reference stays short
options.F: Move the 'when it is above 50 degrees F' clause to the start

questions.explanation: Pronouns should be kept to a minimum, because repeating the noun is better than risking a misreading; the fix is to name what must be above 50 degrees F, such as the ambient temperature or the slab. 'Same' should not be used as a pronoun, relative pronouns such as 'which' are best avoided, 'this' is still a pronoun, and moving the clause leaves 'it' unclear. The rule covers all pronouns, not only personal ones.

questions.question: A firm's quality manager asks what should govern how much detail goes into each job's specifications. Specification detail should be commensurate with which of the following?

options.A: The requirements of the project and the method of project delivery
options.B: The scale of the drawing details and the number of drawing sheets
options.C: The size of the design firm and the extent of its office master system
options.D: The experience of likely bidders and the number of bids expected
options.E: The number of consultants and the length of the design schedule
options.F: The owner's familiarity with construction and its stated preferences

questions.explanation: The amount of detail in a project's specifications should match the requirements of the project and its method of delivery. Drawing scale, firm size, bidder experience, the number of consultants, the design schedule and the owner's familiarity with construction are not the measures used. How much detail to include remains a judgment call, often tempered by economic considerations.

questions.question: A firm is specifying both a large housing project and a small vacation cottage. Which statement about the two sets of specifications is accurate?

options.A: The cottage specs may use a looser language style because their level of detail is lower
options.B: Both need identical detail, because detail and language style are the same thing
options.C: Housing specs may be more complex, but the same clarity and conciseness rules apply
options.D: The housing specs must use performance methods because of their greater complexity
options.E: The cottage specs should be written in the indicative mood for clarity
options.F: The housing specs must use streamlining because of their greater length

questions.explanation: A large housing project may need more complex specifications than a small vacation cottage, yet both are held to the same general rules of clarity and conciseness. Language style is not the same thing as specification detail, so less detail does not permit a looser style. Project size does not call for the indicative mood, performance methods or streamlining.

questions.question: A project manager asks the specifier to add explanatory paragraphs to every section so that 'nothing could possibly be left out.' Which response best reflects when a specification is complete?

options.A: It is complete when every product and step is described in full narrative detail
options.B: It is complete when each Division 01 requirement is restated in every section
options.C: It is complete when the owner's attorney has reviewed it for legal sufficiency
options.D: It is complete when it covers important details without elaborate language
options.E: It is complete when every referenced standard is quoted in full
options.F: It is complete when no addenda are needed during the bidding period

questions.explanation: A specification is complete when it covers the important details without elaborate or needless wording, and how much detail to include is a judgment often tempered by economics. Full narrative, restating Division 01 in each section, or quoting referenced standards adds exactly the unnecessary language to avoid, and legal review or the absence of addenda does not measure completeness.

questions.question: Where are quality assurance and quality control requirements that are specific to one work result addressed?

options.A: In Section 01 40 00—Quality Requirements, organized by work result
options.B: In the supplementary conditions, under the contractor's general duties
options.C: Within the individual section for that work result in Divisions 02-49
options.D: In the owner-contractor agreement, under the description of the work
options.E: In the general conditions, under the article on tests and inspections
options.F: In a separate quality section placed at the end of each Division

questions.explanation: Divisions 02 through 49 are made up of individual sections, each covering a distinct subject or work result, and the quality assurance and quality control requirements specific to a section are written in that section. Gathering work-result quality requirements in a Division 01 section, the general or supplementary conditions, the agreement, or a separate quality section per Division contradicts that arrangement.

questions.question: While editing Division 01 quality sections, a specifier checks what those sections rely on. Division 01 requirements depend on provisions in which document?

options.A: The Divisions 02 through 49 sections
options.B: The conditions of the contract
options.C: The instructions to bidders
options.D: The cited reference standards
options.E: The general notes on the drawings
options.F: The office master guide specification

questions.explanation: Division 01 requirements depend on, and expand on, provisions in the conditions of the contract, because the contract documents are so closely linked that no one of them stands on its own. Division 01 governs the Divisions 02-49 sections rather than depending on them, and the instructions to bidders, reference standards, drawing notes and office masters are not what it builds on.

questions.question: A newly hired specifier is unsure how the quality articles in a Division 08 section relate to the Division 01 quality sections. Examining which document helps clarify these interrelationships?

options.A: MasterFormat, which assigns numbers and titles to sections
options.B: UniFormat, which arranges information by building elements
options.C: PageFormat, which governs the arrangement of text on a page
options.D: SectionFormat, which organizes each section's three parts
options.E: OmniClass, which classifies information in a set of tables
options.F: The National CAD Standard, which organizes drawing sets

questions.explanation: Examining SectionFormat helps clarify how article requirements in individual Divisions 02-49 sections relate to the Division 01 sections, since it organizes every section into the same three parts and articles. MasterFormat numbers and titles sections, UniFormat arranges by building element, PageFormat sets page layout, OmniClass classifies information, and the National CAD Standard covers drawings, so none maps article requirements to Division 01.

questions.question: An owner requires a specific sustainability certification level but lets the contractor decide which points to pursue. Where are the performance requirements for this approach established?

options.A: Section 01 35 63—Sustainability Certification Project Requirements
options.B: Section 01 81 13—Sustainable Design Requirements
options.C: Section 01 35 66—Sustainability Certification Project Procedures
options.D: Section 01 33 29—Sustainable Design Reporting
options.E: Section 01 81 19—Indoor Air Quality Requirements
options.F: Section 01 35 00—Special Procedures

questions.explanation: When the contractor may choose which points to pursue toward a required certification level, the specifying is performance based, and the performance requirements go in Section 01 81 13—Sustainable Design Requirements. Section 01 35 63 is used when the level rests on specific point targets, 01 35 66 and 01 33 29 cover certification procedures and reporting, 01 35 00 suits projects with no certification, and 01 81 19 covers indoor air quality.

questions.question: On a certification project, the design team fixes the certification level through a select group of specific point targets (descriptive specifying). Where are the general sustainability product requirements and the particular product requirements specified?

options.A: Section 01 35 63, with particular requirements in the affected sections
options.B: Section 01 81 13, with particular requirements in Section 01 35 63
options.C: Section 01 35 66, with particular requirements in Section 01 33 29
options.D: The affected sections, with particular requirements in Section 01 35 63
options.E: Section 01 35 00, with particular requirements in the affected sections
options.F: Section 01 81 13, with particular requirements in the affected sections

questions.explanation: When a certification level rests on a chosen group of specific point targets, the specifying is descriptive: general sustainability product requirements go in Section 01 35 63—Sustainability Certification Project Requirements, while the affected sections hold the particular product requirements. The reversed arrangement inverts that, 01 81 13 serves the performance approach, 01 35 00 serves projects with no certification, and 01 35 66 and 01 33 29 cover procedures and reporting.

questions.question: Regardless of whether the certification is specified by performance or descriptively, the owner wants the contractor to track, record, and submit sustainability information throughout the project. Which section could establish these requirements?

options.A: Section 01 35 66—Sustainability Certification Project Procedures
options.B: Section 01 35 63—Sustainability Certification Project Requirements
options.C: Section 01 33 29—Sustainable Design Reporting
options.D: Section 01 78 00—Closeout Submittals
options.E: Section 01 81 13—Sustainable Design Requirements
options.F: Section 01 32 00—Construction Progress Documentation

questions.explanation: With either the performance or the descriptive method, Section 01 33 29—Sustainable Design Reporting can set up the tracking, recording, and submitting of sustainability information. Section 01 35 66 covers the procedures for managing certification, 01 35 63 the general product requirements of descriptive specifying, 01 81 13 the performance requirements, 01 32 00 progress schedules and reports, and 01 78 00 closeout submittals.

questions.question: A project is not pursuing any sustainability certification, but the A/E and client treat sustainability as a matter of practice. Where can the general sustainability requirements be specified?

options.A: Section 01 33 29—Sustainable Design Reporting
options.B: Section 01 35 63—Sustainability Certification Project Requirements
options.C: Section 01 35 66—Sustainability Certification Project Procedures
options.D: Section 01 35 00—Special Procedures or a suitable Level 3 section
options.E: Section 01 74 00—Cleaning and Waste Management
options.F: Section 01 57 00—Temporary Controls

questions.explanation: When a project is not pursuing certification but the A/E, the client, or both pursue sustainability as a routine practice, the general requirements can go in Section 01 35 00—Special Procedures or a fitting Level 3 section, with particular product requirements in the affected sections. Sections 01 33 29, 01 35 63 and 01 35 66 serve certification projects, 01 74 00 covers cleaning and recycling waste, and 01 57 00 covers temporary controls.

questions.question: The authority having jurisdiction must issue a specific approval of the emissions control procedures for a coating installation. Under which PART 1 article heading does this requirement belong in the coating section?

options.A: Quality Assurance—Sustainability Standards Certifications
options.B: Submittals—Sustainable Design Closeout Documentation
options.C: Quality Assurance—Regulatory Agency Sustainability Approvals
options.D: Submittals—Sustainable Design Submittals, under Action Submittals
options.E: Quality Assurance—Preconstruction Testing
options.F: Field Conditions—Ambient Conditions

questions.explanation: Specific approvals by authorities having jurisdiction that relate to sustainability, such as emissions control, recycling procedures or the posting of bonds, go under Quality Assurance as Regulatory Agency Sustainability Approvals. Sustainability Standards Certifications document that items comply with a certification program such as FSC chain of custody, the two submittal headings cover product submittals and the certification package, and preconstruction testing and ambient conditions are not approvals.

questions.question: PART 1 'Submittals' of a section with sustainability requirements can include two types of sustainable design submittals. Which describes Sustainable Design Closeout Documentation?

options.A: Information included in the package submitted for certification
options.B: Product submittals that specifically address the sustainable requirements
options.C: Documentation of AHJ approvals for emissions control or recycling
options.D: The contractor's procedures for managing the certification process
options.E: Operation and maintenance data for the section's products
options.F: Spare parts and extra stock materials for the owner's use

questions.explanation: Sustainable Design Closeout Documentation is the information that goes into the package submitted for certification. Product submittals that address sustainable requirements are the other type, Sustainable Design Submittals; AHJ approvals sit under Quality Assurance; procedures for managing certification belong in Division 01; and operation and maintenance data and spare parts or extra stock are separate closeout and maintenance material submittals.

questions.question: In PART 1 'Summary' of a section subject to sustainability requirements, what may the 'Related Requirements' paragraph include?

options.A: VOC content limits that apply to each of the section's products
options.B: Documentation that items meet sustainability certification requirements
options.C: Procedures for collecting recyclable packaging from this work result
options.D: References to the general sustainability requirements in Division 01
options.E: Approvals by authorities having jurisdiction for emissions control
options.F: Adjustments that bring installed products to the required performance

questions.explanation: The Summary article's Related Requirements paragraph may point to the general sustainability requirements in Division 01. VOC limits are product requirements for the PART 2 Description article, certification documentation and AHJ approvals for emissions control belong under PART 1 Quality Assurance, and collecting recyclable packaging and adjusting installed products are PART 3 Cleaning and Adjusting matters.

questions.question: A specifier is deciding where to place Sustainable Design Submittals within PART 1 of a resilient flooring section. Where may this type of submittal be located?

options.A: Under Closeout Submittals, with the certification package
options.B: Under Quality Assurance, with the standards certifications
options.C: Under Action or Informational Submittals, or a separate article
options.D: Under Informational Submittals only, since no A/E action is needed
options.E: Under Delivery, Storage, and Handling, with packaging
options.F: Under Maintenance Material Submittals, with extra stock

questions.explanation: Sustainable Design Submittals, the product submittals that address sustainable requirements, may sit under Action Submittals or Informational Submittals, or in a submittal article of their own. Information for the certification package is the separate closeout documentation type, standards certifications fall under Quality Assurance, limiting placement to Informational Submittals ignores the action option, and delivery or maintenance material articles are not submittal locations for them.

questions.question: Most of a section's sustainability requirements are written in PART 2, yet only one PART 2 article explicitly includes them. Which article is it?

options.A: Manufacturers
options.B: Materials
options.C: Source Quality Control
options.D: Description
options.E: Performance/Design Criteria
options.F: Assembly or Fabrication

questions.explanation: The Description article is the one PART 2 article that explicitly carries sustainability requirements, under its own sustainability heading. Materials, Mixes, Finishes and Accessories can hold item-specific requirements only when that umbrella heading is too limiting for the items, and Manufacturers, Source Quality Control, Performance/Design Criteria and Assembly or Fabrication are not set aside for them.

questions.question: Division 01 establishes a VOC content limit that applies to all sealants on the project. While editing PART 2 of a joint sealants section, what is the best course of action?

options.A: Reference the Division 01 section in Description rather than repeat the limit
options.B: Restate the VOC limit in the Description article so the section stands alone
options.C: Move the VOC limit out of Division 01 and into each sealant item in Materials
options.D: State the VOC limit under PART 1 Quality Assurance as a certification item
options.E: List the VOC limit under PART 1 Sustainable Design Submittals as a requirement
options.F: Place the VOC limit in PART 3 Application, where odors are controlled

questions.explanation: When products fall under a general sustainability requirement in Division 01, such as a VOC limit for all sealants, the PART 2 Description article can reference that section instead of repeating the limit. Restating it duplicates Division 01 and moving it fragments a project-wide rule. Submittal articles describe submittals without restating requirements, Quality Assurance covers approvals and certifications, and PART 3 Application covers actions during installation, not product content.

questions.question: A section specifies several dissimilar items (panels, adhesives, and trim), each with different recycled-content criteria, and a single umbrella paragraph would be too limiting. How should these sustainability requirements be specified?

options.A: In separate sections, one for each item's sustainability criteria
options.B: In Section 01 35 63, listed by item and cross-referenced in the section
options.C: With each item, under the Materials/Mixes/Finishes/Accessories articles
options.D: In PART 1 Summary, under the Related Requirements paragraph
options.E: Under PART 1 Sustainable Design Submittals, one paragraph per item
options.F: In the PART 2 Source Quality Control article, as tests for each item

questions.explanation: When the umbrella sustainability heading in the Description article is too limiting for the items, each item's own sustainability requirements can be written with that item under Materials, Mixes, Finishes or Accessories. Separate sections or a Division 01 listing scatter what belongs to this work result, Related Requirements only points to general Division 01 requirements, submittal articles describe submittals rather than state requirements, and source quality control covers tests and inspections.

questions.question: Low-flow faucets must have their flow controls set after installation so the fixtures achieve the water-use performance required by a sustainability requirement. Which PART 3 article covers this?

options.A: Installation
options.B: Field Quality Control
options.C: Adjusting
options.D: Cleaning
options.E: Examination
options.F: Protection

questions.explanation: Once installation is complete, products may need adjusting to reach the performance a sustainability requirement calls for, such as setting flow-control faucets, and that belongs in the Adjusting article. Installation covers actions during execution such as controlling odors or runoff, Cleaning covers waste and flush-out, Field Quality Control covers tests and inspections, and Examination and Protection deal with conditions before the work and with guarding it afterward.

questions.question: Division 01 has no building flush-out requirement, but the A/E wants a flush-out after installation of one specific product. Which PART 3 article of that product's section can provide this requirement?

options.A: Installation
options.B: Adjusting
options.C: Protection
options.D: Cleaning
options.E: Preparation
options.F: Field Quality Control

questions.explanation: When Division 01 calls for no building flush-out, the Cleaning article of an individual section can require flush-out of specific materials or products; the same article handles recyclable packaging and waste from that work. Installation covers odors, runoff and discharge during execution, Adjusting covers tuning installed products, Preparation readies the substrate before the work, and Field Quality Control and Protection are not the articles that carry flush-out.

questions.question: A floor coating releases chemical odors and runoff while it is being put in place, and these must be controlled to meet sustainability goals. Which PART 3 article could address these actions?

options.A: Application
options.B: Cleaning
options.C: Adjusting
options.D: Field Quality Control
options.E: Examination
options.F: Protection

questions.explanation: Actions taken while a product is being installed or applied, such as controlling chemical odors, runoff or discharge, belong in the Installation/Application article of PART 3. Cleaning covers packaging, waste and flush-out, Adjusting brings installed products to the required performance, Examination checks conditions before work starts, Protection guards completed work, and Field Quality Control covers tests and inspections.

questions.question: A casework section must specify shop joinery tolerances and the tolerances for scribing installed casework to walls. Where should these workmanship requirements be placed?

options.A: Both in PART 1 under Quality Assurance, as workmanship standards
options.B: Shop tolerances in PART 2 and installation tolerances in PART 3
options.C: Both in PART 3, since tolerances are verified at the project site
options.D: Shop tolerances in PART 1 and installation tolerances in PART 3
options.E: Both in PART 2, since tolerances are product characteristics
options.F: Shop tolerances in PART 3 and installation tolerances in PART 2

questions.explanation: Workmanship requirements must keep product items apart from installation items: fabrication workmanship, such as shop joinery tolerances, goes in PART 2—PRODUCTS, while installation workmanship, such as scribing tolerances, goes in PART 3—EXECUTION. SectionFormat reflects this with fabrication tolerances under PART 2 and installation tolerances under PART 3. Putting both in one part, reversing them, or moving either to PART 1 Quality Assurance ignores that split.

questions.question: NAAWS, jointly published by AWMAC and the Woodwork Institute, establishes measurable tolerances for joinery, surfaces, and clearances. Which grades does it establish that must be selected and specified?

options.A: Premium, standard, and economy
options.B: Custom, standard, and utility
options.C: Premium, custom, and economy
options.D: Premium, custom, and standard
options.E: Premium, custom, and utility
options.F: Custom, standard, and economy

questions.explanation: NAAWS is a standard example of controlling workmanship: it sets measurable tolerances for joinery, surfaces and clearances, and three grades, premium, custom and economy, one of which must be selected and specified. 'Standard' and 'utility' are not NAAWS grades, so every set that includes either of them, or leaves out one of the three real grades, is wrong.

questions.question: A draft installation article states 'Install panels with the best possible workmanship.' Which revision approach best controls workmanship?

options.A: Replace 'best possible' with 'highest quality' to raise the standard
options.B: Require workmanship satisfactory to the A/E in its sole judgment
options.C: Require installers to follow recognized industry best practices
options.D: Specify measurable tolerances and a mock-up as the acceptance basis
options.E: Delete the statement, since workmanship cannot be specified or verified
options.F: Require that panels be installed in a workmanlike manner

questions.explanation: Workmanship requirements should be measurable, and generalities such as 'best possible workmanship' fail because 'best' can be read many ways. Measurable tolerances, with a mock-up to set an acceptable level and a basis for judging later work, are among the recommended methods. 'Highest quality,' the A/E's sole judgment, 'best practices' and 'workmanlike manner' remain unmeasurable, and workmanship can be specified and verified, so deleting it is wrong.

questions.question: An owner upgrades a fabricated handrail from carbon steel to stainless steel, and the specifier assumes the fabrication workmanship requirements must be rewritten. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Workmanship differs from material; both metals may be worked the same way
options.B: Stainless steel requires a higher grade of fabrication workmanship
options.C: Workmanship is set by the material, so the PART 2 material article governs
options.D: Changing materials converts fabrication workmanship into a PART 3 requirement
options.E: Workmanship requirements move into PART 1 Quality Assurance when the metal changes
options.F: Stainless steel calls for tighter tolerances, since it is the costlier material

questions.explanation: Fabrication workmanship is not the same thing as the material: making a product from copper or stainless steel may involve exactly the same fabrication as making it from carbon steel, so the workmanship requirements need not change with the metal. A costlier material does not by itself call for a higher grade or tighter tolerances, and fabrication workmanship stays in PART 2 whatever the material.

questions.question: A specifier is outlining where a project's closeout documentation requirements will be stated. Closeout documentation is broadly covered in which documents?

options.A: The owner-contractor agreement and Section 01 77 00—Closeout Procedures
options.B: The contract conditions and Section 01 78 00—Closeout Submittals
options.C: The supplementary conditions and Section 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures
options.D: The procurement requirements and Section 01 78 00—Closeout Submittals
options.E: The general conditions and Section 01 74 00—Cleaning and Waste Management
options.F: The instructions to bidders and Section 01 79 00—Demonstration and Training

questions.explanation: Closeout documentation is covered broadly by the conditions of the contract together with Section 01 78 00—Closeout Submittals, which sets the submittals the contractor furnishes at project close, such as warranties, operation and maintenance data and record documents. Section 01 77 00 covers closeout procedures, 01 33 00 general submittal procedures, 01 74 00 cleaning and waste, and 01 79 00 demonstration and training, and procurement documents do not govern closeout.
